-- The typecheck stage: Hindley-Milner inference, interface/impl constraint solving,
-- and dict-passing elaboration.  Architecture doc, including the component model this
-- file is being decomposed towards: `compiler/TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md`.
--
-- The HM core is monotypes over Ref-based union-find tyvars, level-based
-- generalization, unification (occurs-check + level adjust), and instantiation.  On
-- top of it, and NOT deferred elsewhere, this file also carries: interfaces, impls,
-- superclasses and coherence; constraint solving and the dict-passing elaboration the
-- backends consume; effect rows; records; explicit signatures; and operator inference.
-- Exhaustiveness is the one part that lives elsewhere and is still called from here --
-- `checkMatchExhaustive` (`compiler/frontend/exhaust.mdk`), once per `EMatch`
-- ([P-EXHAUST-IN-TYPECHECK]).
--
-- ONE GRAPH DRIVER, TWO OUTPUT SELECTIONS.  `driveGraphK` is the single whole-graph
-- driver: `GOutDiags` (per-module diagnostics and schemes) is what `medaka check`,
-- `check --json`, the LSP, MCP, the playground and `medaka test`'s gate consume, and
-- `GOutTrees` (the same diagnostics plus the elaborated, dict-passed trees, the
-- residual and the evidence table) is what `run`, `build`'s child, `medaka test`'s
-- phases and the emit entries consume.  They share one preamble, one per-module
-- worker and one graph-end drain, so a module is checked against the same universe,
-- the same seed and the same mark sets on both.  Every whole-graph entry point in this
-- file is a projection of that function.  A keyed diagnostics drive
-- (`checkModulesDiagsChain (Some …)`) hands the one fold a serve policy (`diagsServe`),
-- which serves each unchanged module before the entry from its recorded interface
-- (`types/module_interface.mdk`) instead of checking it.
--
-- One thing the selections still differ on by construction, and it is observable:
-- `GOutTrees` promotes (inferred-constraint user fns join the dict-name set).  So
-- acceptance under one selection is still not proof about the other for a program that
-- promotes an inferred-constraint fn across modules; its consequence for the gate over
-- this compiler's own source is #1811.  `renameAliasedMethods` is NOT a second such
-- difference: it runs on both selections, because half (b) of it decides which
-- declaration a bare method name binds to, so skipping it on one selection would make
-- that selection typecheck a different program
-- (`test/run_check_agreement_fixtures/reject_1812_alias_import_order.mdk` and its
-- permuted accepting twin).
--
-- Single-file consumers are one-module projections of the same graph driver. There
-- is no second checking mode or second stamper order; `checkOne*` and `elaborateOne`
-- supply the one-module entry surface.
--
-- History: this began as a prelude-less HM engine validated against the (since removed)
-- OCaml reference compiler.  Both that reference and its `dev/tc_probe.exe` harness are
-- gone; native is the sole compiler.  The remaining probe is
-- `compiler/entries/selfproc_tc_probe.mdk`.

-- ── effect-label DOMAIN registry ───────────────────────────────────────────
-- Maps a label's identity key (`labelKey`) to the ⊤-param of its declared
-- domain.  A `PPrefix None` entry means "Prefix-domain (carries a pattern)";
-- a `PPath None` entry is a Prefix domain whose runtime confines by canonical
-- path, so its order compares canonical paths (`FileRead`, `FileWrite`: the
-- labels of the file externs that take a grant); absence ⇒ atomic (Unit).
-- Seeded with the builtin labels and extended per program from `effect Net
-- Prefix` decls, each under its declaration's own identity, so two modules'
-- same-spelled labels own separate schemas.  An assoc-list Ref (the label set
-- is tiny).

-- ── v2 Stage 3: the `IO` widening union alias (design §3.2) ─────────────────
-- `IO` is the coarse security alias: in a BOUND/annotation row it stands for
-- the join of the narrow security labels the selected profile grants, every one
-- at ⊤ when none is selected.  `hostLabels` lists them (every minted security
-- label EXCEPT IO itself); internal labels (Mut/Panic) are NOT members, so they
-- are tracked independently of IO.
-- NOTE: `FFI` is deliberately NOT a member. #2071/#2070 (epic, Layer 1, R1):
-- an `<IO>` bound must NOT subsume an `<FFI>`-performing body — FFI crosses a
-- trust boundary the IO alias is not meant to paper over. Do not "complete"
-- this list by adding FFI.

-- What `IO` joins in this drive: the selected profile's grants of the alias
-- labels, each at the parameter granted, in `hostLabels` order.  With no
-- profile that is all eleven at their tops.  Every module of the program is
-- judged against the one join, the shipped stdlib included.
export
ioJoinAtoms : List (String, Param) -> List (String, EffParamTy) -> List Atom
ioJoinAtoms domains grants =
  filterMap
    (l =>
      map
        (granted =>
          atomWith
            (builtinLabel l)
            (writtenParam (dtopIn domains (builtinLabel l)) granted))
        (lookupAssoc l grants))
    hostLabels

-- ── global inference state ────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- sorted + deduplicated string set (canonical effect-label order, matching the
-- OCaml `List.sort_uniq String.compare` so multi-label rows render identically)
-- sortUniqS / sortUniqSGo / sortInsertS moved to support/util.mdk (imported above).

-- ── effect propagation (Phase 79) ─────────────────────────────────────────
-- the latent effect of the function body currently being inferred: application
-- arms widen it; entering a lambda saves+reopens it, and the accumulated row
-- becomes the lambda's arrow effect. The accumulator begins at the empty row;
-- a closed row is an effect value, never a switch for discarding effects.

-- The site a binding performed a label at that the report is about: the
-- first, in source order, whose authority does not lie within the bound
-- the label was admitted at, else the first site.  Two reads under
-- `<FileRead "config/*">`, the second of `/etc/passwd`, report the second.
effectSiteOf : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  Option String ->
  Option Authority ->
  Option Loc
effectSiteOf mctx _ None _ = None
effectSiteOf mctx fn (Some label) bound =
  match omLookup (effectSiteKey fn label) mctx.mcCells.effectSitesRef.value
    Some sites =>
      let ordered = reverseL sites
      let offending = match bound
        Some hi => filterList (site => not (authSub (fst site) hi)) ordered
        None => []
      match offending ++ ordered
        site :: _ => snd site
        [] => None
    None => None

beginEffectSummaryScope : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> Unit
beginEffectSummaryScope mctx _ =
  mctx.mcCells.fileValueScopes :=
    wSnapshot mctx.mcCells.fileValueFlows :: mctx.mcCells.fileValueScopes.value
  EffectSolver.openSummaryScope
    mctx.mcCells.effectSummaries
    (newEffvarId mctx.mcGraph ())
    mctx.mcCells.currentLevel.value

freshEffectSummary : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> EffRow
freshEffectSummary mctx _ =
  EffectSolver.newSummary
    mctx.mcCells.effectSummaries
    (newEffvarId mctx.mcGraph ())

recordEffectBody : ModuleCtx -> EffRow -> EffRow -> Unit
recordEffectBody mctx summary lower =
  EffectSolver.recordBodyLower mctx.mcCells.effectSummaries summary lower

summaryEscape : GraphCtx -> Bool -> List Atom -> List Atom -> List Atom
summaryEscape gctx True lower upper = atomsDiff lower upper
summaryEscape gctx False lower upper = atomsEscape gctx lower upper

finishEffectSummaryScope : ModuleCtx ->
  Map Int Unit ->
  Map Int (Ref Effvar) ->
  Unit
finishEffectSummaryScope mctx retained borrowed =
  let _ = finishEffectSummaryScopeKeeping mctx noScopeRoles retained borrowed
  ()

-- Close the scope, keeping as residuals the unproven obligations over the
-- authorities [roles] quantifies at a member (`rlQuantified`, see
-- `closeSummaryScope`); each comes back with its member index.
finishEffectSummaryScopeKeeping : ModuleCtx ->
  ScopeRoles ->
  Map Int Unit ->
  Map Int (Ref Effvar) ->
  List (Int, AuthResidual)
finishEffectSummaryScopeKeeping mctx roles retained borrowed =
  let outcome =
    EffectSolver.closeSummaryScope
      mctx.mcCells.effectSummaries
      mctx.mcCells.rigidEffvarsRef.value
      mctx.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef.value
      roles
      retained
      borrowed
      (summaryEscape mctx.mcGraph)
      (joinCellOf mctx.mcGraph)
      (freshEffvarAt mctx.mcGraph)
      (widenOpenedFor mctx)
  let _ = reportEffectSummaryFailures mctx outcome.esoFailures
  let _ = finishFileValueScope mctx ()
  map
    ((member, w) => (
      member,
      AuthResidual {
        arLower = w.awLower,
        arUpper = w.awUpper,
        arExact = w.awExact,
      },
    ))
    outcome.esoResiduals

reportEffectSummaryFailures : ModuleCtx ->
  List (SummaryFailure ObligationSite) ->
  Unit
reportEffectSummaryFailures mctx [] = ()
reportEffectSummaryFailures outer (failure :: rest) =
  let fn = failure.esfContext.osFn
  let mctx =
    mctxAt
      (orElseLoc
        (effectSiteOf outer fn failure.esfLabel (failureBound failure))
        failure.esfContext.osLoc)
      outer
  let _ = match failure.esfAuthority
    Some (lo, hi) =>
      if mentionsEscaped mctx lo || mentionsEscaped mctx hi then
        ()
      else if failure.esfExact then
        reportIndexFailure mctx failure.esfContext.osCovering mctx.mcLoc lo hi
      else
        pushTypeErrorAt
          mctx
          "T-AUTHORITY"
          mctx.mcLoc
          (authorityFailureMsg
            mctx
            fn
            failure.esfLabel
            failure.esfResidualOf
            lo
            hi
            failure.esfWrittenUpper)
    None =>
      mctx.mcCells.rowFailureReportedRef :=
        omInsert fn () mctx.mcCells.rowFailureReportedRef.value
      reportRowFailure mctx failure
  reportEffectSummaryFailures outer rest

-- The authority the failing label was admitted at: the obligation's upper
-- term, or the upper row's atom of that label.
failureBound : SummaryFailure ObligationSite -> Option Authority
failureBound failure = match failure.esfAuthority
  Some (_, hi) => Some hi
  None => match failure.esfLabel
    Some label => map atomAuth (findAtom label (fst (rowFlat failure.esfUpper)))
    None => None

reportRowFailure : ModuleCtx -> SummaryFailure ObligationSite -> Unit
reportRowFailure mctx failure =
  let (upper, upperCells) = rowFlat failure.esfUpper
  let escaping = atomsEscape mctx.mcGraph (fst (rowFlat failure.esfLower)) upper
  let _ =
    if failure.esfExact then
      let rows = ppEachShared (Ref []) (Ref 0) [
        TEff failure.esfLower,
        TEff failure.esfUpper,
      ]
      pushTypeError
        mctx
        "T-EFFECT-INDEX-MISMATCH"
        ("effect index mismatch: "
          ++ joinWith " vs " rows
          ++ "; an effect row in a type argument is invariant, so write the same row on both sides")
    else if isNonEmptyL escaping && isEmptyL upperCells then
      effectLeakCheck mctx escaping upper
    else
      pushTypeError
        mctx
        "T-EFFECT-LAUNDER"
        (effectInclusionMsg
          failure.esfContext.osFn
          escaping
          (ppEachShared (Ref []) (Ref 0) [
            TEff failure.esfLower,
            TEff failure.esfUpper,
          ]))
  ()

-- Close a local binding scope over [members]: whether each generalizes, and
-- its type.  Joins recorded in the scope are decided first when a member
-- generalizes, since its type must not generalize over an undecided join;
-- otherwise they belong to the enclosing scope, where later uses of the
-- alternatives can still shape them.  Everything the close reads (roots,
-- quantifiable authorities) is taken after that.
finishValueEffectsKeeping : DynCtx ->
  List (Bool, Mono) ->
  List (Int, AuthResidual)
finishValueEffectsKeeping dyn generalizing =
  let members =
    map ((generalizes, mono) => (localRole generalizes, mono)) generalizing
  let level = dyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value
  let _ =
    if anyList fst generalizing then
      settlePendingJoins dyn level
    else
      postponePendingJoins dyn.dcModule level
  let monos = map snd members
  finishEffectSummaryScopeKeeping
    dyn.dcModule
    (scopeRolesOf members)
    (fold (acc mono => effectRoots mono acc) Tip monos)
    (fold (acc mono => borrowedEffectCells dyn.dcModule mono acc) Tip monos)

borrowedEffectCells : ModuleCtx ->
  Mono ->
  Map Int (Ref Effvar) ->
  Map Int (Ref Effvar)
borrowedEffectCells mctx mono cells =
  fold
    (acc input => effectCells input acc)
    cells
    (producedInputTypes (producedSlotCovariants mctx) mono)

-- A contract's effect variables are universal throughout its body judgment.
-- The same boundary is used for supplied methods and generic default bodies.
beginEffectContract : ModuleCtx ->
  EffRow ->
  Mono ->
  (Map Int Unit, Map Int Unit)
beginEffectContract mctx force value =
  let saved = mctx.mcCells.rigidEffvarsRef.value
  let savedAuths = mctx.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef.value
  let _ = beginEffectSummaryScope mctx ()
  mctx.mcCells.rigidEffvarsRef := effectRoots value (effectRowRoots force saved)
  mctx.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef :=
    authRoots value (authRowRoots force savedAuths)
  (saved, savedAuths)

finishEffectContract : DynCtx -> (Map Int Unit, Map Int Unit) -> Unit
finishEffectContract dyn (saved, savedAuths) =
  let _ = resolvePendingJoins dyn dyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value
  let _ = finishEffectSummaryScope dyn.dcModule Tip Tip
  dyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidEffvarsRef := saved
  dyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef := savedAuths

-- #784 (Option A): reject an interface method whose signature has a free effect
-- tail var in RETURN position but in NO ROW-KINDED argument position — it is
-- under-determined, so a caller can instantiate it to `<>` and LAUNDER the
-- dispatched impl's real effect (a pure-typed wrapper silently performs it).
-- SCOPED to interface methods (the ratified scope); a top-level return-only
-- effect var is #797's separate territory.
--
-- ⚠️ This runs as a SEPARATE pass from checkEffectParams, deliberately AFTER
-- registerAllData has populated `dataParamKindsRef` (see the call site in
-- checkBodyImpl). The predicate's kind-awareness (rowArgNames) consults that
-- table to tell a row-kinded ctor arg (`Async e a`) from a type-kinded one
-- (`List e`); running it in the early checkEffectParams pre-pass — before data
-- registration — would leave the table empty and spuriously reject `Async e a`.
checkUndeterminedRetEffVars : ModuleCtx -> List Decl -> Unit
checkUndeterminedRetEffVars mctx [] = ()
checkUndeterminedRetEffVars mctx (d :: rest) =
  let _ = checkUndeterminedRetEffVarsDecl mctx d
  checkUndeterminedRetEffVars mctx rest

checkUndeterminedRetEffVarsDecl : ModuleCtx -> Decl -> Unit
checkUndeterminedRetEffVarsDecl mctx (DInterface { name, typarams, typaramKinds, methods, ... }) =
  checkIfaceMethodEffs
    mctx
    name
    (declGradedScope mctx.mcGraph typarams typaramKinds methods)
    methods
-- #1103: the ARGUMENT-COVERAGE half of the rule is NOT method-only.  Its own
-- comment (below) says post-unify inspection cannot catch these shapes because
-- `unifyRowN`'s same-tail arm (`<e>` ~ `<Stdout | e>`) succeeds without
-- recording the atom anywhere — and that arm is reached from an ORDINARY
-- top-level arrow just as readily as from a method.  `launderArrow : (Unit ->
-- <Stdout | e> Unit) -> (Unit -> <e> Unit)` was accepted, and applying it to an
-- effectful callback produced a `Unit -> Unit` scheme that prints.  So the
-- coverage check runs over plain `DTypeSig` signatures too, with an EMPTY graded
-- scope (a non-interface signature has no graded typaram table — `scope` is the
-- only channel by which an abstract head can be row-kinded, see `rowArgNamesIn`).
-- ⚠️ Deliberately NOT widened alongside it: `undeterminedRetEffVars` (#784's
-- RETURN-only rule) stays interface-scoped — a top-level return-only effect var
-- is #797's separate territory, and the comment above says so.
checkUndeterminedRetEffVarsDecl mctx (DTypeSig _ n t _) =
  checkArgEffVarCoverage mctx None [] n t
checkUndeterminedRetEffVarsDecl mctx (DAttrib _ d) =
  checkUndeterminedRetEffVarsDecl mctx d
checkUndeterminedRetEffVarsDecl mctx _ = ()

checkIfaceMethodEffs : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  List IfaceMethod ->
  Unit
checkIfaceMethodEffs mctx _ _ [] = ()
checkIfaceMethodEffs mctx iface scope ((IfaceMethod mname mty _ _) :: rest) =
  let _ = match undeterminedRetEffVars mctx scope mty
    [] => ()
    bad =>
      pushTypeErrorOnceAt
        mctx
        "T-EFFECT-UNDETERMINED"
        (firstTyLoc mty)
        (effectUndeterminedMsg iface mname bad)
  let _ = checkArgEffVarCoverage mctx (Some iface) scope mname mty
  checkIfaceMethodEffs mctx iface scope rest

-- The DUAL of the #784 rule, closing the adversarial review's break 4 (and the
-- argument-only variant): an effect var's ARGUMENT-position occurrences are
-- rows an impl can PERFORM by using that argument, so the method's own rows
-- must account for them.  Two ill-formed shapes, both rejected at the
-- interface declaration:
--   * argument-only — `use : a -> (Unit -> <e> Unit) -> Int`: e rides an
--     argument but no non-argument row, so an impl applying the callback
--     performs e with no row charging it (verified launder: a pure-typed
--     wrapper prints);
--   * uncovered atoms — `act1 : a -> (Unit -> <Stdout | e> Unit) -> <e> Unit`:
--     the callback's concrete <Stdout> pours into a row declared bare <e>,
--     which a caller instantiates to <> (verified launder).  Sound iff every
--     non-argument occurrence of e covers the union of its argument-side
--     atoms, IO-expanded (`<Stdout | e>` callback with `<Stdout | e>` return
--     is accepted; so is an `<IO | e>` return).
-- Post-unify inspection CANNOT catch these: the same-tail row-unification arm
-- (`<e>` ~ `<Stdout | e>`) succeeds without recording the atom anywhere, so
-- the declaration is the only seam with the information intact.
-- [iface] is `Some` the enclosing interface for a method signature and `None`
-- for an ordinary top-level `DTypeSig` (#1103); it selects the diagnostic's
-- wording and nothing else — the RULE is identical either way.
checkArgEffVarCoverage : ModuleCtx ->
  Option String ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  String ->
  Ty ->
  Unit
checkArgEffVarCoverage mctx iface scope mname mty =
  checkArgEffVars
    mctx
    iface
    mname
    mty
    (methodEffArgOccs mctx scope mty)
    (methodEffRetOccs mctx scope mty)
    (dedup (map fst (methodEffArgOccs mctx scope mty)))

-- 🚨 THE TWO ARMS HAVE DIFFERENT SCOPES, and [iface] is what selects between
-- them.  Both arms apply to an interface method (`Some iface`); only the
-- UNCOVERED-ATOMS arm applies to an ordinary top-level signature (`None`).
--
-- Why the ARGUMENT-ONLY arm is method-only.  Its hazard is "an impl uses the
-- argument and performs <e> with no row charging it", and at an INTERFACE
-- declaration the declaration really is the only seam — the impl arrives later,
-- and #1100's `gtake : f e a -> a` launders for exactly that reason.  A
-- DIRECT call to a top-level function does not get there: the CALL SITE rejects
-- it.  MEASURED, both shapes, on this build — the reason is the call site, NOT
-- the callee's body (a first pass at this comment claimed the body check caught
-- it and that was falsified: `use : (Unit -> <e> Unit) -> Int` with a body that
-- calls `f ()` checks CLEAN, reported as `use : (Unit -> Unit) -> Int`):
--   * callback arg — `use : (Unit -> <e> Unit) -> Int`, body `let _ = f ()`,
--     applied to an effectful `shout`: "Effectful value used where <> is
--     allowed, but it performs <Stdout>", at `use shout`;
--   * row-kinded ctor arg — `force : Box e a -> a` forcing its `Susp` thunk,
--     applied to `Susp loud`: the same diagnostic, at `force (Susp loud)`.
-- Applying the arm to top-level signatures anyway buys no soundness and rejects
-- every honest INSPECTOR of a row-kinded value — also measured: 34 declarations
-- in this compiler's own sources (`unInt : Value e -> Int`, `isPartial : Value e
-- -> Bool`, … which pattern-match a `Value e` and never invoke the closure
-- inside it) plus `stdlib/async.mdk`'s `isDone`/`forceVal`.  Nothing at a
-- declaration tells an inspector from a forcer; for a method that uncertainty IS
-- the hazard, for a directly-called function the call site settles it.
--
-- Why the UNCOVERED-ATOMS arm is NOT method-only (#1103).  Its hazard survives
-- the body check: `launderArrow : (Unit -> <Stdout | e> Unit) -> (Unit -> <e>
-- Unit)` with body `launderArrow f = f` type-checks, because `unifyRowN`'s
-- same-tail arm accepts `<Stdout | e>` against `<e>` without recording <Stdout>
-- anywhere (see this function's header comment).  Effect inference therefore
-- CANNOT catch it, and the declaration is the only seam here too.
checkArgEffVars : ModuleCtx ->
  Option String ->
  String ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, List Atom) ->
  List (String, List Atom) ->
  List String ->
  Unit
checkArgEffVars mctx _ _ _ _ _ [] = ()
checkArgEffVars mctx iface mname mty argOccs retOccs (v :: rest) =
  let vrets = filterList (o => fst o == v) retOccs
  let vatoms = flatMap snd (filterList (o => fst o == v) argOccs)
  let _ =
    if isEmptyL vrets then match iface
      Some i =>
        pushTypeErrorOnceAt
          mctx
          "T-EFFECT-ARG-UNCOVERED"
          (firstTyLoc mty)
          (argOnlyEffVarMsg i mname v)
      None => ()
    else match retOccsEscape mctx.mcGraph vatoms vrets
      [] => ()
      esc =>
        pushTypeErrorOnceAt
          mctx
          "T-EFFECT-ARG-UNCOVERED"
          (firstTyLoc mty)
          (argAtomsMsgFor iface mname v esc)
  checkArgEffVars mctx iface mname mty argOccs retOccs rest

-- first non-empty escape of the argument-side atoms against a non-argument
-- occurrence's declared atoms (IO-expanded via atomsEscape)
retOccsEscape : GraphCtx -> List Atom -> List (String, List Atom) -> List Atom
retOccsEscape gctx _ [] = []
retOccsEscape gctx vatoms ((_, declAtoms) :: rest) =
  if isNonEmptyL (atomsEscape gctx vatoms declAtoms) then
    atomsEscape gctx vatoms declAtoms
  else
    retOccsEscape gctx vatoms rest

-- effect-var occurrences (name, written atoms) inside ARGUMENT positions of a
-- method signature that an impl can PERFORM: rows of functions the impl can
-- CALL (odd contravariant depth) and row-kinded values it can RUN.  The
-- arrow's own row is NOT an argument position, and — round-2 adversarial
-- FP 7 — a row at EVEN depth (`((Unit -> <e> Unit) -> Int)` argument: the
-- impl receives a CONSUMER of e-callbacks and can only SUPPLY callbacks) is
-- excluded: the impl cannot perform e there, and a malicious effectful supply
-- pours its atoms into e's own cell where the post-unify atom check reads
-- them.
-- [scope] mirrors `methodEffRetOccs`' parameter of the same name exactly: the
-- graded typaram map of the interface whose method signature this type IS
-- (`declGradedScope`), and `[]` for every non-method signature.  Before #1100 the
-- ARGUMENT half took no scope at all, so an abstract head (`gtake : f e a -> a`)
-- resolved no row-kinded slot and raised no obligation, while the RETURN half —
-- which has had the scope channel since #822 — did.
methodEffArgOccs : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, List Atom)
methodEffArgOccs mctx scope (TyConstrained _ t) = methodEffArgOccs mctx scope t
methodEffArgOccs mctx scope (TyEffect _ _ t) = methodEffArgOccs mctx scope t
methodEffArgOccs mctx scope (TyFun a b) =
  argPerformableOccs mctx scope True a ++ methodEffArgOccs mctx scope b
methodEffArgOccs mctx _ _ = []

-- One `(tail var, the row's written atoms)` occurrence per tail variable.  A
-- row is a JOIN when it names several (#821, `<Stdout | e | e2>`), and every
-- collector below reports them all: a caller reads the row at each var
-- independently, so a var left out would be a var nothing constrains.
occsOfTails : GraphCtx ->
  List String ->
  List EffAtomTy ->
  List (String, List Atom)
occsOfTails gctx tails labels =
  let atoms = atomsOfWritten gctx labels
  map (n => (n, atoms)) tails

-- rows in an argument subtree, collected only where [perf] (the impl can call
-- or run the value at this position); each arrow-LHS descent flips it.
argPerformableOccs : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  Bool ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, List Atom)
argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf (TyEffect labels tails t) =
  (if perf then occsOfTails mctx.mcGraph tails labels else [])
    ++ argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf t
-- A bare row atom (#997) carries its own tail var + labels directly (no
-- wrapped type to recurse into) — same treatment as the `TyEffect` arms
-- above.  Without this, a KRow ctor-arg written as `Box <Stdout | e> Int`
-- (as opposed to a bare `Box e Int`) was invisible to this collector, which
-- made the impl-body T-EFFECT-LAUNDER check over-fire on it (see
-- `effVarOccAtoms` below, which shares this gap).
argPerformableOccs mctx _ perf (TyRow labels tails _) =
  if perf then occsOfTails mctx.mcGraph tails labels else []
argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf (TyFun a b) =
  argPerformableOccs mctx scope (not perf) a
    ++ argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf b
argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf (TyTuple ts) =
  flatMap (argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf) ts
argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf (TyApp a b) = match tyAppSpine (TyApp a b)
  -- OCCURRENCE MINT (#1110/#1111 A-2.3): the head's acquired identity, read off
  -- the same record pattern as its name so the two cannot drift apart.
  (TyCon { tyConName = n, tyConOrigin = o }, args) =>
    krowSlotOccs mctx scope perf o n args
  -- #1100, the abstract-head half — symmetric with `rowArgNamesVarApp` on the
  -- RETURN side.  An interface typaram of graded kind, in scope, is row-kinded
  -- in exactly the same way a registered ctor's KRow slot is; without this arm
  -- `gtake : f e a -> a` collected NOTHING and the coverage rule never fired.
  (TyVar h, args) => krowSlotVarOccs mctx scope perf h args
  _ =>
    argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf a ++ argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf b
argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf (TyConstrained _ t) =
  argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf t
argPerformableOccs mctx _ _ _ = []

-- one ctor node: its bare row-kinded slots (if performable) + recurse the args
--
-- 🚨 THE SLOT'S ATOMS COME FROM THE HEAD'S DECLARATION, not from the use site.
-- This used to pad every performable KRow slot to `(e, [])` — "the impl can
-- perform `e` here and nothing else is guaranteed" — the ARGUMENT-side twin of
-- the blind pad #2110 removed from `methodEffRetOccs`.  On this side the pad is
-- not an over-rejection but a LAUNDER: for
--   `data Slot e = Slot (Unit -> <Stdout | e> Unit)`
-- a `Slot e` ARGUMENT lets the callee run a field the declaration guarantees
-- performs <Stdout> at EVERY instantiation, `Slot <>` included, so
--   `unslot : Slot e -> (Unit -> <e> Unit)`
-- under-claims: it hands back a function typed `<e>` that really performs
-- <Stdout>, and at `e := <>` the caller gets a pure-typed printer (measured —
-- `check` and `run` both exited 0 and the program printed).  Reading the
-- guarantee out of `dataParamRowAtomsRef` through `krowArgVarAtoms` — the same
-- table and the same walker the RETURN side already consults — makes those
-- <Stdout> atoms argument-side evidence, and the coverage rule ("every
-- non-argument occurrence of `e` covers the union of its argument-side atoms")
-- then rejects `unslot` while still accepting `widen : Slot e -> Slot e`, whose
-- return occurrence carries the same atoms.  Both halves are pinned:
-- `test/typecheck_error_fixtures/effect_arg_slot_launder.mdk` and its
-- `effect_arg_slot_unrelated_ok.mdk` accept-side twin.
-- ⚠️ A written-row slot (`Slot <Log | e>`) has its WRITTEN labels reported
-- twice — once here by `krowArgVarAtoms`, once by the `flatMap` below through
-- `argPerformableOccs`' `TyRow` arm.  Harmless, and NOT the return side's
-- double-count hazard: `checkArgEffVars` UNIONS the argument-side atoms
-- (`flatMap snd`), where the return side takes a first-non-empty escape and so
-- lets an atom-less copy veto a faithful one.
krowSlotOccs : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  Bool ->
  TyConOrigin ->
  String ->
  List Ty ->
  List (String, List Atom)
krowSlotOccs mctx scope perf o n args =
  match lookupTab (tyTabKey o n) mctx.mcCells.dataParamKindsRef.value
    Some kinds if listLen kinds == listLen args =>
      (if perf then
          krowArgVarAtoms
            mctx.mcGraph
            kinds
            (optionOr [] (paramRowAtomsOf mctx (tyTabKey o n)))
            args
        else
          [])
        ++ flatMap (argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf) args
    _ => flatMap (argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf) args

-- the ABSTRACT-HEAD sibling of `krowSlotOccs` (#1100): same shape, but the
-- kinds come from the graded typaram [scope] instead of `dataParamKindsRef`.
-- This is `rowArgNamesVarApp`'s counterpart on the argument side; a miss falls
-- through to the args exactly as `krowSlotOccs`' miss does.
-- An abstract head has no declaration to read, so its guarantee list is `[]`
-- and every slot still reports `(e, [])` — `krowArgVarAtoms kinds []` is the
-- old blind pad, occurrence for occurrence.  It is written this way rather than
-- left as the `map`, so the two arms stay ONE walker: the next atom fact an
-- abstract head can offer (a graded typaram's declared row, #820) lands in one
-- place instead of two.
krowSlotVarOccs : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  Bool ->
  String ->
  List Ty ->
  List (String, List Atom)
krowSlotVarOccs mctx scope perf h args = match lookupAssoc h scope
  Some kinds if listLen kinds == listLen args =>
    (if perf then krowArgVarAtoms mctx.mcGraph kinds [] args else [])
      ++ flatMap (argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf) args
  _ => flatMap (argPerformableOccs mctx scope perf) args

-- effect-var occurrences in NON-argument positions: each spine arrow's own row,
-- plus every occurrence inside the final return type (nested rows and bare
-- row-kinded ctor-arg slots).
--
-- 🚨 THE TWO TERMS OF THE LAST ARM CAN DESCRIBE THE SAME OCCURRENCE, and only
-- one of them carries its atoms.  For a return `Box <Stdout | e> Unit`,
-- `effVarOccAtoms` descends into the KRow slot's written row and reports
-- `(e, [Stdout])`; `rowArgAtomsIn` reports the same occurrence again, carrying
-- only what the HEAD'S DECLARATION guarantees at that slot (`(e, [])` for a
-- `Box` declared bare).  `retOccsEscape` takes the FIRST NON-EMPTY escape
-- over this list and does not dedupe, so the atom-less copy vetoes the faithful
-- one and an HONESTLY CHARGED declaration is rejected:
--   `widen : Box <Stdout | e> Unit -> Box <Stdout | e> Unit`
-- covers <Stdout> on both sides and must be ACCEPTED — it is the named
-- over-correction control in `test/typecheck_error_fixtures/
-- effect_index_unrelated_ok.mdk` (its header, "rejecting those instead would be
-- the obvious over-correction").  So a name `effVarOccAtoms` has already
-- reported is DROPPED from the padded term rather than added beside it.
-- ⚠️ This does NOT weaken any real rejection: the dropped entry is a strictly
-- less informative record of an occurrence still in the list, never an
-- occurrence the list would otherwise lose.  The rule stays "every non-argument
-- occurrence of e covers the union of its argument-side atoms"; this only stops
-- one occurrence from being counted twice, once with its labels erased.
-- Latent since the padded term was introduced — it mis-rejected interface
-- methods of this shape too, and #1103's widening to ordinary signatures is
-- merely what made it reachable from `effect_index_unrelated_ok.mdk`.
methodEffRetOccs : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, List Atom)
methodEffRetOccs mctx scope (TyConstrained _ t) = methodEffRetOccs mctx scope t
methodEffRetOccs mctx scope (TyEffect labels tails t) =
  occsOfTails mctx.mcGraph tails labels ++ methodEffRetOccs mctx scope t
methodEffRetOccs mctx scope (TyFun _ b) = methodEffRetOccs mctx scope b
methodEffRetOccs mctx scope t =
  let occs = effVarOccAtoms mctx.mcGraph t
  occs
    ++ filterList
      (o2 => not (anyList (o => fst o == fst o2) occs))
      (rowArgAtomsIn mctx scope t)

-- The predicate: return-position effect tail vars minus argument-carried ones.
-- An effect var is argument-carried — hence soundly pinned at every call site —
-- ONLY by a ROW-KINDED occurrence in an argument. The test is kind-aware, NOT
-- name-based: a Row-kinded effect var and a Type-kinded type var may share a
-- spelling yet be independent variables, so a Type-kinded `e` in `List e` /
-- `Box e` pins NOTHING about the return row `<e>` — counting it would relaunder
-- the effect (#784). The two sound argument-carriers:
--   * a callback's latent arrow effect (`(a -> <e> b)`) — a Row-kinded effect
--     row, captured by effTailNames over each arg;
--   * a row-kinded type-CONSTRUCTOR argument (`Async e a`, where Async's first
--     param has kind Row) — captured by rowArgNames, which consults the ctor's
--     recorded param kinds (dataParamKindsRef) and takes ONLY the tyvars sitting
--     in a KRow slot. `List e`/`Box e` (Type-kinded param) contribute nothing.
-- An effect tail var in the RETURN row and in no such Row-kinded argument slot
-- is the laundering hazard (map/fold/traverse/`Async e a` are pinned;
-- `speak : a -> <e> String` and `speak : a -> List e -> <e> String` are not).
-- An abstract row-ctor arg (`r e a`, `r` a type variable) is conservatively
-- rejected — no real interface method has that shape, and matching it soundly
-- would need per-argument kind inference we do not run here.
undeterminedRetEffVars : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  Ty ->
  List String
undeterminedRetEffVars mctx scope sig =
  let args = methodArgs sig
  let argCarried =
    dedup (flatMap effTailNames args ++ flatMap (rowArgNamesIn mctx scope) args)
  let retTail = dedup (effTailNames (methodRet sig))
  removeAllS argCarried retTail

-- return type of a method: strip leading constraint wrappers and arrows, but
-- KEEP a trailing effect row so its tail var is visible (unlike methodArgs,
-- which peels it).
methodRet : Ty -> Ty
methodRet (TyConstrained _ t) = methodRet t
methodRet (TyFun _ b) = methodRet b
methodRet t = t

-- #822 (graded interfaces): an instance head must have the KIND the interface's
-- corresponding type parameter has.  A graded interface binds the whole row-indexed
-- FAMILY — `impl GThenable Async`, never a fixed row like `impl GThenable (Async e)`
-- (EFFECTS-SEMANTICS §6, DICT-SEMANTICS §3) — so the head's REMAINING parameter
-- kinds (its declared kinds minus the ones the head already applied) must equal the
-- interface slot's kinds.
--
-- This is a soundness guard, not polish.  A kind-mismatched head elaborates the
-- method type's KRow slot to a `TEff` row while the constructor's own scheme has a
-- plain tyvar in that position, and `unify` binds a tyvar to a TEff without
-- complaint: the impl would be ACCEPTED and its grade would mean nothing — every
-- index a caller reads off the result would be a fabrication.
--
-- Only interfaces that actually HAVE a graded slot are JUDGED — the `anyKRow want`
-- guard below is what does that, not the table: every slot of every interface is
-- recorded (it always was, and `ceRowParamKinds` keeps doing so), and an all-`KType`
-- row falls into the same `_ => ()` arm an outright miss does.  ⚠️ This paragraph
-- read *"only interfaces that actually HAVE a graded slot are inspected
-- (ifaceParamKindsRef records nothing else)"* until #1557 A-3.5c, and the
-- parenthetical was false of the retired table too.  Runs on BOTH whole-program
-- paths: its one call site is in checkBodyImpl, shared by Flat and Module,
-- immediately after `dataEnv` has populated the head-constructor kind table.
--
-- 🚨 #1557 A-3.5c: IT STILL ITERATES `prog`, AND THAT IS THE UNIT'S DEFINING
-- CONDITION, not an implementation detail.  The owner ruling that split A-3.5c
-- out of the A-3b lane (issue #1557, 2026-08-12) is CONDITIONAL: this check
-- qualifies as CE-only *"only if the graded impl-head kind check keeps
-- iterating `prog` rather than `IE.ieRows`"*.  The impl HEADS come from the
-- decl list; only the interface's declared slot kinds come from stage K's `CE`.
-- Whoever re-points this walk at `IE.ieRows` has re-classified the unit as A-3b
-- by construction — that is a routing decision, not a refactor.
checkGradedImplHeads : ModuleCtx -> ClassEnv -> Int -> List Decl -> Unit
checkGradedImplHeads mctx _ _ [] = ()
checkGradedImplHeads mctx ce cur (d :: rest) =
  let _ = checkGradedImplHeadDecl mctx ce cur d
  checkGradedImplHeads mctx ce cur rest

-- OCCURRENCE MINT (#1110/#1111 A-2.4): `implOrigin` is the identity the
-- interface NAME in `impl <iface> …` acquired at resolve — read off the same record
-- pattern as the name itself so the two cannot drift apart, exactly as A-2.3 reads
-- `tyConOrigin` beside `tyConName`.
checkGradedImplHeadDecl : ModuleCtx -> ClassEnv -> Int -> Decl -> Unit
checkGradedImplHeadDecl mctx ce cur (DAttrib _ d) =
  checkGradedImplHeadDecl mctx ce cur d
checkGradedImplHeadDecl mctx ce cur (DImpl { iface, tys, implOrigin = o, ... }) =
  checkGradedImplTys mctx ce cur o iface 0 tys
checkGradedImplHeadDecl mctx _ _ _ = ()

-- The `CE` lookup via `ceSlotKindsAt` uses ordinal filtering — the key is a RegKey
-- (`ifaceTabKey o iface` + slot position), identity-based not bare-name, preserving
-- the identity mint from A-2.4. Ordinals are assigned in dependency-first order,
-- matching the order the accumulator is grown in, so ordinal filtering and the
-- previous marshalled population agree. See
-- compiler/TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md § "5. Decisions reopened, and decisions
-- deliberately kept" (A-3.5c) for the prior bare-name table this replaced and the
-- #1257 defect class it drains.
checkGradedImplTys : ModuleCtx ->
  ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  TyConOrigin ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List Ty ->
  Unit
checkGradedImplTys mctx _ _ _ _ _ [] = ()
checkGradedImplTys mctx ce cur o iface i (t :: rest) =
  let _ = match ceSlotKindsAt (regKeyOfTab (ifaceTabKey o iface)) cur i ce
    Some want if anyKRow want => checkGradedImplHead mctx iface t want
    _ => ()
  checkGradedImplTys mctx ce cur o iface (i + 1) rest

-- [want] is the interface slot's kind list.
--
-- Only a head whose kind is actually KNOWN is judged, and the two ways it can be
-- unknown are BOTH deliberate abstentions, not oversights:
--   * a type ALIAS head lives in aliasTableRef, never in dataParamKindsRef, and its
--     saturation is already policed by T-ALIAS-ARITY — a kind complaint here would be
--     a second, worse-worded report of the same defect;
--   * a head absent from dataParamKindsRef entirely — a builtin like `Int`, whose kinds
--     this compiler records nowhere.  Abstaining costs nothing real: a genuinely wrong
--     head still fails on its method bodies, where the mismatch is concrete and located.
--     ⚠️ An ABSTRACTLY-exported data type (`export data Asy e a`) USED to land here too,
--     cross-module, and the abstention was load-bearing for it: judging it reported a
--     correct program rejected and told the author to add a `Row` parameter the type
--     ALREADY HAD.  #804/#1028 fixed that at the source — an opaque type's kinds are
--     published cross-module (`kindPublicDataDecl`'s `VisAbstract` arm; it was
--     `registerOpaqueParamKinds` until A-3.2b retired the kind universe) — so an
--     abstract head is now judged on its REAL kinds like any other, and this arm no
--     longer covers for it.
-- A head that is not a TyCon spine at all is judged where it can be: a saturated
-- TUPLE is kind `Type`, which is never a graded slot's kind, so it is reported; a bare
-- tyvar head carries no kind and is left to the checks that already reject it.
checkGradedImplHead : ModuleCtx -> String -> Ty -> List Kind -> Unit
checkGradedImplHead mctx iface t want = match tyAppSpine t
  (TyCon { tyConName = n, tyConLoc = loc, tyConOrigin = o }, applied) =>
    checkGradedImplHeadCon mctx iface o n loc (listLen applied) want
  -- A saturated tuple is kind `Type`, which is never a graded slot's kind.  It gets its
  -- OWN remedy: the generic "give it a Row parameter" advice is nonsense for a tuple —
  -- you cannot add one.  ⚠️ The span is best-effort: `TyTuple` carries no loc of its own
  -- and `TyVar` carries none either, so `impl I (a, b)` genuinely has no span to point at
  -- and reports unlocated.  Fabricating a nearby one would be worse than saying nothing.
  (TyTuple ts, _) =>
    pushTypeErrorOncePerSite
      mctx
      "T-IMPL-KIND-MISMATCH"
      (firstTyLocList ts)
      (implTupleHeadKindMsg iface (listLen ts) want)
  _ => ()

checkGradedImplHeadCon : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  TyConOrigin ->
  String ->
  Option Loc ->
  Int ->
  List Kind ->
  Unit
checkGradedImplHeadCon mctx iface o n loc nApplied want =
  match headRemainingKinds mctx o n nApplied
    None => ()
    Some got => checkGradedImplHeadKinds mctx iface n loc nApplied want got

-- The head constructor's declared parameter kinds MINUS the ones the head already
-- applies (`impl I (Async e)` supplies one).  `None` = "this head's kind is not
-- knowable here" (an alias or a builtin), which the caller treats as an abstention.
-- ⚠️ An abstractly-exported type was in that bucket until #804/#1028 and is NOT any
-- more — `kindPublicDataDecl`'s `VisAbstract` arm gives it a real `dataParamKindsRef`
-- entry (via `declEnvSeedChain`), so it returns `Some` and is judged exactly like
-- a `public export` one.
-- `key` is minted ONCE and shared by both guard arms via the `where` (#1111
-- A-2.3 follow-up): the first guard ALWAYS evaluates it (Medaka is strict, and
-- a `where` scoping over guard arms lowers to `ELetGroup (..key..) (EGuards
-- arms)`, so the binding runs once before either arm is tested), so hoisting
-- adds nothing on the alias arm and removes the previously-redundant second
-- mint on the common `otherwise` arm.  A redundant-allocation removal, not a
-- measured perf win (`test/bench.sh` doesn't run on this box, #1187; the
-- perf-scaling gate grades a growth ratio, blind to a constant factor).
headRemainingKinds : ModuleCtx ->
  TyConOrigin ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Option (List Kind)
headRemainingKinds mctx o n nApplied
  | isSome (lookupTab key mctx.mcCells.aliasTableRef.value) = None
  | otherwise =
    map (drop nApplied) (lookupTab key mctx.mcCells.dataParamKindsRef.value)
  where
    key = tyTabKey o n

checkGradedImplHeadKinds : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Option Loc ->
  Int ->
  List Kind ->
  List Kind ->
  Unit
checkGradedImplHeadKinds mctx iface n loc nApplied want got
  | kindsEq got want = ()
  | otherwise =
    pushTypeErrorOncePerSite
      mctx
      "T-IMPL-KIND-MISMATCH"
      loc
      (implKindMismatchMsg iface n nApplied want got)

-- Closure construction is pure; only the source body's final application runs it.
arrowsWithLastEffect : List Mono -> EffRow -> Mono -> Mono
arrowsWithLastEffect params eff result = bodyArrows params eff result

-- The signature the declared-row walks below read: every alias on the return
-- spine expanded, so the declared row is the row `fromAstTypeE` elaborates.
-- `d : Tick` with `type Tick = Int -> <Stdout> Unit` declares `<Stdout>`, and
-- so do `v : S` and `f : Int -> S` with `type S = <Stdout> Int`
-- (`writtenBindingForce`, `returnRowE`).  An alias that expands to any other
-- type stays unexpanded, since it carries no row to read.
expandReturnSpine : ModuleCtx -> Ty -> Ty
expandReturnSpine mctx ty = match expandAliasHeadTy mctx ty
  TyFun a ret => TyFun a (expandReturnSpine mctx ret)
  TyConstrained cs t => TyConstrained cs (expandReturnSpine mctx t)
  row@(TyEffect _ _ _) => row
  _ => ty

-- the declared concrete effect set of a signature: labels on the first `<…>`
-- reached walking down the return side (Phase 79e escape check)
declaredEffects : GraphCtx -> Ty -> List Atom
declaredEffects gctx (TyFun _ ret) = declaredEffects gctx ret
declaredEffects gctx (TyEffect effs _ _) = atomsOfWritten gctx effs
declaredEffects gctx (TyConstrained _ t) = declaredEffects gctx t
declaredEffects gctx _ = []

-- #797: the TAIL of that same first `<…>` — the field `declaredEffects` drops.
-- No names is a genuinely CLOSED row (`<>`, `<Stdout>`); one or more is an OPEN
-- one (`<e>`, `<Stdout | e>`, `<Stdout | e | e2>`).  Arms mirror
-- `declaredEffects` exactly, stopping at the same node, so the two always
-- describe ONE row.
declaredEffectTail : Ty -> List String
declaredEffectTail (TyFun _ ret) = declaredEffectTail ret
declaredEffectTail (TyEffect _ tail _) = tail
declaredEffectTail (TyConstrained _ t) = declaredEffectTail t
declaredEffectTail _ = []

-- #797: effect-tail names occurring in ARGUMENT positions of the signature,
-- walking the same return spine `declaredEffects` walks and stopping at the same
-- node.  A name here is one the CALLER also constrains, so the declared return
-- row is not free even though it is syntactically open.
--
-- ⚠️ Deliberately BROADER than `methodEffArgOccs`: that collector answers "can
-- the BODY perform this row" and so excludes an even-contravariant-depth
-- occurrence (`((Unit -> <e> Unit) -> Int)`).  The question here is the
-- different one "does the caller pin this var", for which ANY argument-side
-- occurrence counts — an even-depth `e` is still unified with the caller's
-- chosen row.  `effTailNames`' documented name-based over-counting (`List <e>`)
-- is likewise conservative in the safe direction here: it can only make a row
-- read as argument-carried, i.e. keep the pre-#797 rejection, never widen.
declaredArgEffNames : ModuleCtx -> Ty -> List String
declaredArgEffNames mctx (TyFun a ret) =
  effTailNames a ++ rowArgNames mctx a ++ declaredArgEffNames mctx ret
declaredArgEffNames mctx (TyConstrained _ t) = declaredArgEffNames mctx t
declaredArgEffNames mctx _ = []

-- #797: is the declared return row genuinely OPEN — a free tail var that appears
-- NOWHERE on the argument side?  Such a var is chosen by nothing but the callee's
-- own body: `f : Int -> <e> String` means "f performs whatever it performs", so a
-- body performing <Stdout> is not an escape and must not be reported as one.
-- An argument-carried var (`g : (Int -> <e> Int) -> <e> Int`) is NOT open in this
-- sense — the caller instantiates it, so a body adding <Stdout> would launder,
-- and the pre-existing escape rejection stands unchanged.
-- A JOIN is open when SOME member is free of the argument side: that member
-- alone already admits whatever the body performs.
declaredEffectsOpen : ModuleCtx -> Ty -> Bool
declaredEffectsOpen mctx ty =
  let argNames = declaredArgEffNames mctx ty
  anyList (v => not (contains v argNames)) (declaredEffectTail ty)

-- Keyed indices — so the hot per-field-access read paths never walk a linear registry
-- (issue #149).  #415 item 3: `registerRecordInfoKeyed` is the sole REGISTRATION writer of
-- both; they are cleared together by `freshModuleCtx`; and the cross-module record floor is
-- loaded by `loadDataUniverse` from `universeRecordPop`.
--
-- 🚨 THE LOCKSTEP WAS "STRUCTURAL, NOT AN OBLIGATION" UNTIL #1111 A-2.12 (#1319 unit 2),
-- AND IT IS NOW AN OBLIGATION.  `applyRecordScopeOverrides` re-points `recordByNameRef`
-- for a collided key and does NOT touch `fieldOwnersRef`, so the two are no longer written
-- only in pairs and nothing enforces that they agree.  Re-pointing key `K` cannot change
-- which KEYS own a field name, but it does change which FIELDS `K` declares — so with two
-- same-named records having DISJOINT field sets, `fieldOwnersRef` can name `K` as the owner
-- of a field the newly-selected `K` does not declare.
-- ⚠️ THAT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS NOTE SAID IT WAS.  It called the
-- divergence "an obligation with no observed consequence" on the strength of one probe that
-- kept every projection inside the module which NAMED the record — where the overlay and the
-- floor agree by construction, so the probe could not have shown anything.  **#1377 was the
-- consequence**: a module naming one `Cfg` and holding a value of the other was refused.
-- 🚨 #1319 UNIT 3 DRAINED #1377, AND THE OBLIGATION SURVIVES IT.  Unit 3 did not reconcile
-- the two tables; it stopped ASKING the overlay a question the overlay could not answer —
-- `resolveFieldRecord`'s arm (a) now selects by the receiver's identity (see
-- `lookupRecordForReceiver`).  So the one observed consequence is gone and the write
-- asymmetry is not.  ⚠️ Do NOT restate this as "no observed consequence today": that exact
-- sentence has now been wrong twice here, and what is true is narrower — the consequence
-- that was found has been removed, and nobody has established that it was the only one.
-- Anything added here must state which of the two it writes and why the other is safe.
--   recordByNameRef : registry KEY → RecordInfo.  omInsert is last-write-wins and
--     the register site inserts in registration order, so it reproduces the old
--     prepend-list first-match (latest-registered wins) for lookupRecordByName.
--   fieldOwnersRef  : field name → the registry keys whose RecordInfo declares it
--     (a multimap).  fieldOwnerNames still `sortUniqS`es this so the owner-list
--     order that feeds ambiguousFieldMsg/head stays byte-identical.

-- Transparent type aliases (`type Foo = Int`, `type Pair a = (a, a)`).  Keyed by
-- alias name → (params, RHS surface type).  Populated in a pre-pass by
-- `registerData`'s DTypeAlias arm (mirrors `dataParamKindsRef`); consulted
-- on-demand at the `Ty→Mono` seam (`fromAstTypeE`) to expand an alias to its RHS.
-- The param list is stored even though stage 2 only expands the zero-param case,
-- so parameterized expansion (stage 3) can extend this without reshaping the table.

-- Names of record/named-field types exported ABSTRACTLY (`export data`/`export
-- record` without `public`).  Seeded ONCE (over EVERY module's decls, prelude
-- included) by the multi-module check drivers, BEFORE per-module checking, and
-- deliberately NOT cleared by `freshModuleCtx` — it is whole-program metadata, not a
-- per-module accumulator.  An abstract export brings the type NAME into scope but
-- never registers its fields (publicDataDecls drops VisAbstract decls, so they never
-- reach the record registry in an importer — its PARAM KINDS do travel, since #804/#1028, via
-- kindPublicDataDecl's VisAbstract arm, but a kind is not a field).  A dot-access on
-- such a type therefore lands at resolveFieldRecord's `head known but no record
-- info` branch with the type name still recoverable as the receiver's head tycon;
-- membership here distinguishes that case (clear abstract-export diagnostic) from a
-- genuinely-unknown field on an unbound receiver (the `<unknown>` message).  This
-- mirrors resolve's destructure-side AbstractFieldAccess signal (env.types ∋ owner
-- ∧ owner owns no field) without threading anything new through the import seed.

-- collect the names of all VisAbstract record-shaped (a DData whose variants
-- carry named fields) decls across the given decl list.  Only
-- record-shaped abstract types can be a dot-access receiver, but harvesting any
-- abstract DData name too is harmless (a positional ADT can't reach the abstract
-- branch with a field access — its fields never exist).
collectAbstractRecordTypes : List Decl -> List String
collectAbstractRecordTypes [] = []
collectAbstractRecordTypes ((DData { dataVis = VisAbstract, dataName = n }) :: rest) =
  n :: collectAbstractRecordTypes rest
collectAbstractRecordTypes (_ :: rest) = collectAbstractRecordTypes rest

-- seed abstractRecordTypesRef from every module's decls (the per-module progs plus
-- the prelude/core decls), once, before checking begins.  Keyed by the type
-- word (`typeTagOf`), so a program's own type that shares an abstract export's
-- name is not mistaken for it.
seedAbstractRecordTypes : GraphCtx ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  Unit
seedAbstractRecordTypes gctx coreDecls modules =
  let abstracts =
    collectAbstractRecordTypes coreDecls
      ++ flatMap (m => abstractTypeWords (fst m) (snd m)) modules
  gctx.abstractRecordTypesRef := namesToSet abstracts omEmpty

abstractTypeWords : String -> List Decl -> List String
abstractTypeWords mid decls =
  map (n => typeTagOf (OriginModule mid) n) (collectAbstractRecordTypes decls)

goalKindTag : GoalKind -> Int
goalKindTag GKReturnSite = 0
goalKindTag GKArgStamp = 1
goalKindTag GKRLocalSite = 2
goalKindTag GKBinopSite = 3
goalKindTag GKUnopSite = 4
goalKindTag GKArithSite = 5
goalKindTag GKDictApp = 6
goalKindTag GKMethodDict = 7
goalKindTag GKRecDictApp = 8

pushGoal : GraphCtx -> Obligation -> Unit
pushGoal gctx o =
  let g = gctx.graphRun
  g.goals := o :: g.goals.value
  g.goalsN := g.goalsN.value + 1

siteObligation : GoalKind -> Ref Inner -> PendingEntry -> Obligation
siteObligation k inner (PendingEntry name tagRef m encl site loc scope ev) = Obligation {
  oKind = k,
  oDest = EvRoute tagRef,
  oEv = ev,
  oEncl = encl,
  oLoc = loc,
  oScope = scope,
  oPayload = GPSite name m site,
  oInner = inner,
}

-- [inner] is the destination's summary: the method cell's `ecInner` when [e]'s route
-- ref is a cell's, a fresh one otherwise.
pushSiteGoal : GraphCtx -> GoalKind -> Ref Inner -> PendingEntry -> Unit
pushSiteGoal gctx k inner e = pushGoal gctx (siteObligation k inner e)

-- an arithmetic operator site: only its operand mono and its route cell
pushArithGoal : ModuleCtx -> Ref Route -> Mono -> EvId -> Unit
pushArithGoal mctx dref m ev = pushGoal mctx.mcGraph Obligation {
  oKind = GKArithSite,
  oDest = EvRoute dref,
  oEv = ev,
  oEncl = "",
  oLoc = None,
  oScope = captureScope mctx (),
  oPayload = GPArith m,
  oInner = Ref innerNone,
}

pushDictApp : GraphCtx -> PendingDictApp -> Unit
pushDictApp gctx app = pushGoal gctx Obligation {
  oKind = GKDictApp,
  oDest = EvRoutes app.pdaRoutesRef,
  oEv = app.pdaEv,
  oEncl = app.pdaEncl,
  oLoc = app.pdaLoc,
  oScope = app.pdaScope,
  oPayload = GPDictApp app,
  oInner = Ref innerNone,
}

pushMethodDictGoal : GraphCtx -> PendingMethodDict -> Unit
pushMethodDictGoal gctx pmd = pushGoal gctx Obligation {
  oKind = GKMethodDict,
  oDest = EvRoutes pmd.pmdRoutesRef,
  oEv = pmd.pmdEv,
  oEncl = pmd.pmdEncl,
  oLoc = None,
  oScope = pmd.pmdScope,
  oPayload = GPMethodDict pmd,
  oInner = pmd.pmdInner,
}

pushRecDictAppGoal : GraphCtx -> RecDictApp -> Unit
pushRecDictAppGoal gctx (r@(RecDictApp routesRef _ encl _ scope ev)) = pushGoal
  gctx
  Obligation {
    oKind = GKRecDictApp,
    oDest = EvRoutes routesRef,
    oEv = ev,
    oEncl = encl,
    oLoc = None,
    oScope = scope,
    oPayload = GPRecDictApp r,
    oInner = Ref innerNone,
  }

-- the goals recorded since `mark` (a length of the channel: a module's start mark
-- from `GraphMarks`, or a `let`/SCC bracket's own), newest first
goalsSince : GraphCtx -> Int -> List Obligation
goalsSince gctx mark =
  moduleWindow gctx.graphRun.goalsN.value mark gctx.graphRun.goals.value

goalsOfKindIn : GoalKind -> List Obligation -> List Obligation
goalsOfKindIn k gs = filterList (o => goalKindTag o.oKind == goalKindTag k) gs

siteEntry : Obligation -> List PendingEntry
siteEntry o = match o.oPayload
  GPSite name m site =>
    [PendingEntry name (evCell o.oDest) m o.oEncl site o.oLoc o.oScope o.oEv]
  _ => []

evCell : EvDest -> Ref Route
evCell (EvRoute r) = r
evCell (EvRoutes _) = Ref RNone

arithEntry : Obligation -> List (Ref Route, Mono)
arithEntry o = match o.oPayload
  GPArith m => [(evCell o.oDest, m)]
  _ => []

dictAppsSince : GraphCtx -> Int -> List PendingDictApp
dictAppsSince gctx mark = dictAppsIn (goalsSince gctx mark)

dictAppsIn : List Obligation -> List PendingDictApp
dictAppsIn gs = flatMap dictAppEntry gs

dictAppEntry : Obligation -> List PendingDictApp
dictAppEntry o = match o.oPayload
  GPDictApp a => [a]
  _ => []

methodDictEntry : Obligation -> List PendingMethodDict
methodDictEntry o = match o.oPayload
  GPMethodDict d => [d]
  _ => []

recDictAppEntry : Obligation -> List RecDictApp
recDictAppEntry o = match o.oPayload
  GPRecDictApp r => [r]
  _ => []

-- a bracket's mark: the channel's length now (what `wMark` was for `dictApps`)
goalsMark : GraphCtx -> Unit -> Int
goalsMark gctx _ = gctx.graphRun.goalsN.value

-- drop the goals of `kinds` recorded since `mark`, keeping every other goal
-- (`inferPropBodies`' bracket: a prop body's operator sites must not be stamped)
dropGoalsSince : GraphCtx -> Int -> List GoalKind -> Unit
dropGoalsSince gctx mark kinds =
  let g = gctx.graphRun
  let now = g.goals.value
  let n = g.goalsN.value - mark
  let tags = map goalKindTag kinds
  let kept =
    filterList (o => not (containsI (goalKindTag o.oKind) tags)) (take n now)
  g.goals := kept ++ drop n now
  g.goalsN := mark + listLen kept

-- return-position method sites discovered during inference: (method name, the
-- EMethodAt route ref to fill, the EMethodAt impl-dicts ref to fill, the method's
-- result mono).  After the whole program is inferred, each result mono's head
-- tycon is the concrete impl tag the site dispatches to (RKey) — or, when it is a
-- constrained function's constraint variable, that function's dict parameter
-- (RDict).  The impl-dicts ref is filled (single-module elaborate path only) when
-- the route is a parametric impl with a `requires` — one route per requires.
-- #156 S3a: entries are `PendingEntry`s of kind `SKReturn`.

-- Phase 151 / Gap G: comparison/equality OPERATOR sites discovered during
-- inference: (method name, the EBinOp route ref to fill, the operand mono).
-- After inference resolveBinopSites stamps each ref with the resolved Eq/Ord impl
-- route (RKey) — but ONLY when the operand grounds to a NON-primitive type; the
-- structural-builtin EBinOp eval path handles primitive / ungroundable operands
-- (so `eq a b = a == b` on Int never recurses).  dictPass then rewrites the
-- stamped node into the method application.
-- (method, route ref, operand mono, inImpl-flag, enclosing-fn name).  The 5th
-- field is currentFn at record time: for a TOP-LEVEL constrained fn an operator on
-- its own constraint var routes RDict $dict_<encl>_<slot> (via enclDictVarOf), the
-- operator analogue of the direct `eq x y` arg-stamp path.
-- #156 S3a: entries are `PendingEntry`s of kind `SKOp`.

-- Roadmap #18c: the EUnOp analogue of pendingBinopSites — `-` (Num's `negate`)
-- sites discovered during inference.  Same tuple shape/fields, same resolve/
-- rewrite seam (resolveUnopSites / rewriteUnopExpr), one operand instead of two.

-- Arithmetic EBinOp sites whose operand type may ground to a concrete primitive.
-- Recorded during inference (operand Mono + the node's route ref);
-- resolveArithSites reads each solved Mono after the whole module is inferred and
-- stamps its supported scalar tag so lowering carries the result type into
-- CBinPrim and the native emitter need not recover it from operand structure. A still-
-- polymorphic (Num a) operand never grounds → stays RNone → today's dict path
-- (mirrors resolveBinopSite's grounded-only guard, so dict-routed arithmetic is
-- untouched).

-- Error-path BLOCKER B4 (audit finding D3): missing-impl dispatch obligations.
-- `methodEntryHere` maps each interface method NAME → (iface, the iface's typarams,
-- the method's declared AST type), as the reading module's scope resolves it
-- (`methodScopeAt`).  At each EVar/EMethodAt occurrence of a
-- registered method, recordImplObligation captures the OCCURRENCE mono so that,
-- after inference, checkImplObligations can read what the interface params
-- resolved to (parallel-walking the declared type against the normalized
-- occurrence mono) and reject the call when those concrete head types have NO
-- matching impl in the program (the `No impl of … for …` reject).  Skips while a param is still a
-- polymorphic tyvar (deferred to the caller).
-- A bare-name collision between two unrelated interfaces is decided by the reading
-- module's scope, never by registration order (#1092) — see `MethodEnv`.

-- C5 (TYPECHECK-AUDIT / Phase 112): names that are BOTH an interface method AND a
-- cross-module-imported standalone top-level function (e.g. box's `toList`/`isEmpty`
-- shadowing Foldable's).  Populated per module by elabModuleStamp from the full graph
-- (a top-level funDef name that is also a method name and is NOT defined in the
-- current module).  resolveSite consults it: a method site at a concrete receiver
-- with NO impl, whose name is here, routes RLocal (eval reads the standalone) instead
-- of RKey<head> (which would panic with no impl).
-- `freshModuleCtx` starts it empty; `checkBodyImpl` rebuilds it per module.

-- DEFINER-shadow names (facet 2): the names THIS module declares as a top-level
-- funDef that ALSO name an interface method (buildDefinerShadows) — e.g. a user
-- `eq : List Int -> List Int -> Bool`.  A DIRECT call `eq [1] [2]` in user code
-- must resolve to the user's OWN definition (RLocal), NOT to a method impl, even
-- when the receiver's head HAS an impl of the interface (`List` has `Eq`).  The
-- arg-stamp pass would otherwise stamp `RKey:List` (the impl), making the eval path
-- dispatch to the prelude `Eq (List a)` impl (`[1] ≠ [2]` → False) instead of the
-- user's fn (True) — a run≠build divergence (the EMIT path already routes to the
-- user's def).  resolveRLocalSite stamps these RLocal unconditionally.  Populated
-- per-module in checkModuleFullImpl from buildDefinerShadows; reset by `freshModuleCtx`.

-- P0-19: the declared top-level SIGNATURES of definer-shadow standalones
-- (`size : Int -> Int`), keyed by name.  When a definer-shadow occurrence resolves
-- to the STANDALONE (no visible impl for the grounded receiver, or an ungrounded
-- receiver), inferDefinerShadowApp enforces this declared domain against the actual
-- argument — closing the S2/S5 "must then type against the standalone's domain" hole
-- that let `size "hi"` / a poly wrapper `useIt x = size x; useIt (Box 3)` type against
-- the permissive method scheme and reach codegen as garbage.  Set per-path from
-- `sigsOf prog`; empty for an unsignatured standalone (no domain to enforce → the old
-- permissive behavior, unchanged).

-- P0-19 d4b (S4): True while inferring the HEAD of a definer-shadow APPLICATION
-- (`size (Box 3)`) — set around the head-infer call in inferDefinerShadowVarApp /
-- inferDefinerShadowApp.  A shadow occurrence reaches inferVar / inferMethodAt in
-- two shapes: as an application head (dispatch-vs-standalone decided per-receiver by
-- the surrounding shadow-app machinery, so the head must keep the permissive METHOD
-- scheme `a -> Int`) OR in bare VALUE position (`map size xs`, `let f = size`), which
-- S4 says ALWAYS denotes the standalone.  This flag distinguishes the two so only the
-- value-position occurrence is pinned to the standalone scheme.  Default/reset False.

-- P0-18 (EMIT path only): the mangler (`mangleUnits`) renames a definer-shadow
-- standalone def + its call sites to `<mid>__name` BEFORE marking, but (correctly)
-- leaves the interface method name bare — so the mark pass's NAME-based shadow
-- detector (buildStandaloneShadowsGraph / buildDefinerShadows, keyed on
-- funDef-name ∩ iface-method-name) no longer sees a shadow and the occurrence never
-- becomes an `EMethodAt` dispatch site (→ a silent direct call to the standalone =
-- the build miscompile).  elaborateModules recovers the shadow post-mangle by
-- forward-constructing `mangledName mid method` for every (module, iface-method)
-- pair and checking it against the module's actual funDef names; each hit is a
-- `(mangledSymbol ↦ bareMethod)` entry recorded here.  The mark pass then (a) marks
-- the mangled occurrence `EMethodAt` with the BARE dispatch name (so `implFor` finds
-- the impl for a receiver that HAS one) and (b) carries the mangled symbol in the
-- route's `RLocal <symbol>` fallback for a receiver that does NOT.
-- #2809 RETIRED THE "EMPTY OFF THE EMIT PATH" INVARIANT.  Mangling now runs AFTER
-- elaboration, so NO path reaches this map with mangled funDefs and the rows every path
-- gets are the BARE ones `unitMangledShadows` adds: `(name ↦ name)` for a definer
-- shadow, in every module of the graph.  Both spellings are still recorded there, so
-- (a) and (b) above read the same way; what changed is that the SYMBOL half is now the
-- bare standalone name and the rename that moves it runs later.  A consumer must no
-- longer treat a non-empty map as "this is the emit path".
-- Set once at the top of elaborateModules;
-- deliberately NOT cleared by `freshModuleCtx` (checkModuleFullImpl's per-module `freshModuleCtx`
-- must not wipe it mid-graph) — the forward-construction membership check makes a
-- stale value inert (no funDef matches → no entry).

-- the MANGLED standalone symbol a route's RLocal fallback should call, or "" for
-- the bare-name (un-mangled) case.  Read off the marked EMethodAt route at record
-- time (before resolveArgStamps may overwrite the ref with an RKey) so the mangled
-- symbol survives into the pendingRLocalSites entry.
routeLocalSym : Route -> String
routeLocalSym (RLocal s _) = s
routeLocalSym _ = ""

-- ── #2809: the seed's ROUTE half and its TYPING half are different questions ──
-- `routeLocalSym` above is the ROUTE half: the symbol the emitter must call, which
-- `mangleRoute` renames once mangling runs.  Every reader below that instead asked
-- "is this occurrence a standalone shadow whose bare name no longer denotes the
-- standalone?" used a non-empty `routeLocalSym` as its answer, and that reading was
-- sound only while the seed was `<mid>__name` — a spelling that existed on the emit
-- path and nowhere else.  With mangling moved after elaboration the seed is the BARE
-- standalone name on EVERY path, so a seed equal to the occurrence's own method name
-- recovers nothing: the un-mangled classifiers (`definerShadowNamesRef`,
-- the standalone scheme carried by the env binding) already answer it, and reading
-- it as the old signal changed what `check` reports — measured on
-- `test/run_check_agreement_fixtures/s1_constrained_shadow_dispatch.mdk`, whose
-- specified `No impl of Num for Box` (clause S9's reject direction, named in the
-- fixture's own header) became `Type mismatch: Int literal vs Box` because the
-- standalone-domain enforcement below is gated on this test.
-- So: this is the RECOVERED-SYMBOL half — "" whenever the seed is just the bare name —
-- and every TYPING decision keys on it, while the route stamp keeps `routeLocalSym`.
recoveredShadowSym : String -> Ref Route -> String
recoveredShadowSym name tagRef =
  let s = routeLocalSym !tagRef
  if s == name then "" else s

-- ── A-3.2b (#1512) slices 2+3: THE DATA-UNIVERSE SEED, READ OUT OF K ─────────
-- `CrossRun.universeDataParamKinds` and `CrossRun.universeFieldOwners` are
-- RETIRED.  Both were the same machine: a cell grown one module at a time by
-- `appendDataUniverse` and copied into a per-run working ref by
-- `loadDataUniverse` at the top of every module's `checkBodyImpl` Module arm.
-- Neither carried a module id or an ordinal, so neither could answer "as seen by
-- WHOM" — the question §2 K exists to make askable.  The seed now comes from the
-- whole-graph envelope, projected at the reading module's own ordinal through the
-- SAME two predicates the overlay pool reads (`declEnvVisibleAt` /
-- `declEnvVisibleTo`).  ⚠️ This clause used to end "so A-3.6 keeps its one-body
-- deletion"; A-3.6 (#1558) SPLIT the predicate rather than deleting it, and this
-- seed — a NAME/data-scoping table — kept its ordinal filter unchanged.
--
-- 🚨 THE SEED EXCLUDES THE READER'S OWN ROW, AND THAT IS NOT AN ORDINAL
-- STATEMENT.  A module registers its own decls directly, immediately after this
-- seed, via `registerAllData … prog0` — which is also what the retired
-- accumulator did (`appendDataUniverse` runs at the END of a module's arm, so the
-- universe a module LOADS holds every EARLIER module and never itself).  Seeding
-- the own row a second time would not merely duplicate work: `addFieldOwners`
-- does not dedupe, so a doubled owner key would sit in the raw multimap; the one
-- reader, `fieldOwnerNames`, `sortUniqS`es it, so the exclusion is a work-and-shape
-- invariant of the seed that the `deSeedChainProbe` doctests assert, not a
-- correctness one.
--
-- 🚨 IT IS A CHAIN, NOT A PER-READ FOLD, AND THAT IS A MEASURED REQUIREMENT.  The
-- first cut of this unit folded the visible rows AT EVERY READ: O(universe) work
-- and allocation once per module, i.e. the "rebuild the whole thing once per
-- element" shape `compiler/AGENTS.md` opens with.  CI caught it —
-- `diff_compiler_perf_scaling`'s `modules` shape put `typecheck` TIME at
-- 0.299s/0.675s/1.872s over N=100/200/400 where the row's own note says the stage
-- has been UNDER the 200 ms floor since #154 PR-C, and the shape's climbing rule
-- (`r2 > r1 * 1.15 && r2 > 2.45`) failed it.  The ALLOC arm called the same run
-- `ok` at 2.24/2.42, which is exactly the second rule in `compiler/AGENTS.md`: a
-- quadratic that allocates little is invisible to the allocation arm.
--
-- So the seeds are built ONCE, in `buildDeclEnvs`, as a PREFIX CHAIN: reader k's
-- seed is reader (k-1)'s seed with row (k-1)'s public projection folded in, which
-- shares structure and costs O(whole graph) for the entire run.  The read is one
-- `omLookup` and allocates nothing.
--
-- 🚨 A-3.6 DID NOT EDIT HERE, AND THE INSTRUCTION THIS NOTE USED TO CARRY WAS A
-- LIVE REGRESSION.  It read: *"When A-3.6 makes `declEnvVisibleAt ≡ True`, every
-- reader must see the WHOLE chain instead of its own prefix: hand every row the
-- FINAL accumulator in `declEnvSeedChain` below."*  `test/registry_keying_ratchet.sh`
-- still says the same thing in its `declEnvsRef` and `deKindsBefore` rows.  **Do
-- not do it**, for two independent reasons:
--
--   1. THE FINAL ACCUMULATOR INCLUDES THE READER'S OWN ROW, and the own-row
--      exclusion is structural and mandatory — the 🚨 note above says so, and the
--      SAME ratchet row says so two sentences before instructing the edit that
--      destroys it.  A module re-registers its own decls immediately after this
--      seed via `registerAllData … prog0`, so seeding them here too doubles an
--      owner key in the raw multimap (`fieldOwnerNames` dedupes it on read, so
--      this is a shape invariant, not an answer change).  That is PINNED:
--      see the four `deSeedChainProbe` doctests below `deKindRow1`, which were
--      added by A-3.6 bite C-1 specifically as a tripwire on this edit and which
--      were confirmed to be the only assertions in this file that fire on it.
--   2. THE PREMISE IS FALSE ANYWAY.  A-3.6 (#1558) did not make
--      `declEnvVisibleAt ≡ True`; it split the predicate and flipped only the
--      instance axis (`ieCandidacyVisibleAt`).  These two seeds are name/data
--      scoping and keep the prefix rule.  Widening the field-owner half was in
--      fact the specific thing the owner ruling declined, because
--      `declEnvVisibleTo`'s MEASURED paragraph shows it NARROWS acceptance.
--
-- What the chain is, unchanged: it ENCODES `declEnvVisibleAt`'s prefix shape —
-- that is the whole source of the structure sharing — while each step still routes
-- its PROJECTION through `declEnvRowKindEntries`/`declEnvRowVisible`, hence through
-- `declEnvVisibleTo`'s two conjuncts.

-- ── #1597: FIELD-OWNER REACHABILITY ──────────────────────────────────────────
-- 🚨 WHY THIS IS A SECOND, NARROWER PREDICATE AND NOT A WIDENING OF
-- `declEnvVisibleAt`.  That predicate is shared by FOUR name-scoping tables plus a
-- decl-time existence query, and its own 🚨 note forbids widening its readers as a
-- side effect of anything: *"Widening any of this predicate's readers is a separate
-- unit with its own fixtures; it is not a side effect of anything."*  #1597 is the
-- opposite direction anyway — the ordinal prefix is too WIDE for the field-owner
-- reader, not too narrow.  So the prefix stays exactly as it is, the population stays
-- exactly as it is, and the FIELD-OWNER READER alone gets one extra conjunct.  No
-- other reader of `declEnvVisibleAt` sees any of this.
--
-- THE PREDICATE: an earlier module's record votes in `resolveFieldByOwners`'
-- ambiguity test only if that module is in the reading module's transitive `DUse`
-- closure.  "Earlier in the topological order" is not "reachable" — that conflation
-- is the whole of #1597, where a module importing NOTHING was rejected because an
-- unrelated module sorted first.
--
-- ⚠️ IT IS AN OVER-APPROXIMATION ON PURPOSE, IN THE SAFE DIRECTION.  The closure
-- walks every `DUse` edge regardless of publicity, selectivity or re-export, so it
-- only ever removes a module the reader has NO import path to at all.  A module the
-- reader can reach but may not legally name still votes, exactly as today.

-- The one and only way to add an obligation.  #991: this channel now stores the SAME
-- `UObligation` record the call channel does, with a real `Provenance` and an
-- `OpMethodOcc` projection carrying the (typarams, declared method type, occurrence
-- mono) triple the check-time `dispatchMonosOf` needs (see `OblProjection`).  The
-- pre-#838 5-tuple, and the `implOblToU` bridge that converted it, are gone.
pushPendingObl : ModuleCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List String ->
  Ty ->
  Mono ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Provenance ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
pushPendingObl mctx iface typarams mty occ omitted prov loc =
  wPush
    mctx.mcCells.implObls
    (mkMethodOccObl
      iface
      typarams
      mty
      occ
      omitted
      prov
      loc
      (captureScope mctx ()))

pushExactReturnObl : ModuleCtx -> MethodReturnRequest -> Unit
pushExactReturnObl mctx request = wPush mctx.mcCells.implObls UObligation {
  pred = Predicate { iface = request.mrrIface, args = [] },
  originId = 0,
  prov = PMethodOcc,
  loc = request.mrrLoc,
  uoScope = request.mrrScope,
  oblProj = OpExactReturn request,
}

methodReturnOrigin : ModuleCtx -> Option Loc -> GoalOrigin
methodReturnOrigin mctx loc =
  let moduleId = mctx.mcCells.currentModuleRef.value
  let binding =
    if mctx.mcCells.currentFn.value == "" then
      None
    else
      mkIdent NsValue (OriginModule moduleId) mctx.mcCells.currentFn.value
  GoalOrigin {
    location = loc,
    moduleId = moduleId,
    binding = binding,
  }

methodReturnInstantiation : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodReturnRequest ->
  Option Instantiation
methodReturnInstantiation mctx request = match (
  methodReturnPredicate mctx.mcGraph request,
  request.mrrGoalEv,
)
  (Some predicate, Some destination) => Some Instantiation {
    body = request.mrrQualifiedBody,
    force = pureRow,
    arguments = [
      InstantiationArgument {
        formal = Scopes.binderAt request.mrrScope 0,
        wanted = Wanted {
          id = goalIdForDestination destination,
          predicate = predicate,
          origin = methodReturnOrigin mctx request.mrrLoc,
          scope = request.mrrScope,
          destination = destination,
        },
      },
    ],
  }
  _ => None

methodReturnPredicate : GraphCtx -> MethodReturnRequest -> Option ClassPredicate
methodReturnPredicate gctx request =
  methodReturnPredicateFromTemplate
    gctx
    request.mrrPredicateTemplate
    request.mrrTyparams
    request.mrrOmitted
    request.mrrScope

-- A complete template is the goal.  An incomplete one is answered first by the
-- unique given matching its present positions; failing that, each absent position
-- is the occurrence's own [omitted] variable (DICT-SEMANTICS §5), for §3 to
-- determine or the boundary to reject.
methodReturnPredicateFromTemplate : GraphCtx ->
  MethodPredicateTemplate ->
  List String ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option ClassPredicate
methodReturnPredicateFromTemplate gctx template typarams omitted scope =
  match methodPredicateTemplateArgs template.mptArguments
    Some arguments => Some ClassPredicate {
      predicateInterface = template.mptInterface,
      predicateArguments = arguments,
    }
    None =>
      match (uniqueMethodTemplateGiven
        gctx
        template
        scope
        (givensForScope gctx scope))
        Some given => Some ClassPredicate {
          predicateInterface = template.mptInterface,
          predicateArguments = predicateSlotKnownArgs given.geSlot.psArgs,
        }
        None =>
          map
            (arguments => ClassPredicate {
              predicateInterface = template.mptInterface,
              predicateArguments = arguments,
            })
            (methodPredicateTemplateArgs
              (fillOmittedTemplateArgs typarams template.mptArguments omitted))

-- [arguments] with each absent position read from [omitted] by its typaram name.
fillOmittedTemplateArgs : List String ->
  List (Option Mono) ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List (Option Mono)
fillOmittedTemplateArgs (param :: params) (argument :: arguments) omitted =
  orElseOpt argument (lookupAssoc param omitted)
    :: fillOmittedTemplateArgs params arguments omitted
fillOmittedTemplateArgs _ arguments _ = arguments

methodReturnRequest : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  Mono ->
  MethodInstantiationSubst ->
  Option EvId ->
  MethodReturnRequest
methodReturnRequest mctx row occurrence subst goalEv =
  let loc = mctx.mcLoc
  let scope = captureScope mctx ()
  let qualifiedBody = match row.msrScheme
    Forall _ _ _ _ _ body =>
      substMono
        mctx.mcGraph
        subst.misTypeSubst
        subst.misEffectSubst
        subst.misAuthSubst
        body
  let omitted =
    if methodPredicateTemplateHasAbsent row.msrPredicateTemplate then
      omittedParamVars mctx row.msrTyparams row.msrType
    else
      []
  MethodReturnRequest {
    mrrIface = row.msrIface,
    mrrName = row.msrName,
    mrrTyparams = row.msrTyparams,
    mrrType = row.msrType,
    mrrOccurrence = occurrence,
    mrrEnclosing = mctx.mcCells.currentFn.value,
    mrrLoc = loc,
    mrrScope = scope,
    mrrGoalEv = goalEv,
    mrrQualifiedBody = qualifiedBody,
    mrrPredicateTemplate =
      instantiateMethodPredicateTemplate
        mctx.mcGraph
        row.msrPredicateTemplate
        subst,
    mrrOmitted = omitted,
    mrrResolution = Ref None,
  }

methodReturnArgs : GraphCtx -> MethodReturnRequest -> Option (List Mono)
methodReturnArgs gctx request =
  map
    (predicate => predicate.predicateArguments)
    (methodReturnPredicate gctx request)

methodReturnWanted : ModuleCtx -> MethodReturnRequest -> Option Wanted
methodReturnWanted mctx request = match methodReturnInstantiation mctx request
  Some (Instantiation { arguments = [argument], ... }) => Some argument.wanted
  _ => None

-- the mint for an impl-channel obligation.  `pred.args` is EMPTY and must stay so:
-- the dispatch vector is `OpMethodOcc`'s to project, at check time, via `uOblArgs`.
mkMethodOccObl : IfaceRef ->
  List String ->
  Ty ->
  Mono ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Provenance ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  UObligation
mkMethodOccObl iface typarams mty occ omitted prov loc scope = UObligation {
  pred = Predicate { iface = iface, args = [] },
  originId = 0,
  prov = prov,
  loc = loc,
  uoScope = scope,
  oblProj = OpMethodOcc typarams mty occ omitted,
}

pushNumLitObl : ModuleCtx ->
  ClassPredicate ->
  Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
pushNumLitObl mctx predicate occurrence loc scope = wPush
  mctx.mcCells.implObls
  UObligation {
    pred = Predicate {
