      iface = predicate.predicateInterface,
      args = predicate.predicateArguments,
    },
    originId = 0,
    prov = PNumLit,
    loc = loc,
    uoScope = scope,
    oblProj = OpNumLit occurrence,
  }

-- PLAN.md #11: one entry per source integer literal (ENumLit):
-- (litVar, fref, n, dref).  [litVar] is the literal's fresh Num-obligated type var;
-- [fref] is the node's own Option Float cell; [n] the int value; [dref] is the
-- node's `fromInt`-route cell (filled by resolveSites — the literal is modelled as a
-- `fromInt n` method occurrence).  After defaulting + grounding, the post-HM pass
-- setNumlitFloats decides the runtime rep: litVar ground Float ⇒ fref Some, dref cleared ⇒ ELit (LFloat f);
-- litVar ground Int ⇒ both cleared ⇒ ELit (LInt n); litVar still polymorphic `Num a`
-- (the soundness case — `1` in `inc x = x + 1`) ⇒ dref KEPT (RDictFwd onto the
-- enclosing Num dict) ⇒ dictPass emits `EApp (EMethodAt "fromInt" …) (ELit (LInt n))`.

-- Chunk A (error framing): the union-find root ids of every type var that took
-- part in a unification failure (`typeMismatch`).  Consulted ONLY by
-- `undeterminedGoalExempt` to SUPPRESS a secondary `ambiguous instance`
-- cascade on a var the primary mismatch already explained — never read on the
-- inference path, so a well-typed program (no mismatch) never poisons anything
-- and behaves identically.

-- Chunk D (Num mis-framing): (litVar, loc) for every numeric literal whose var
-- carried a Num obligation — captured at inferNumLit/inferNumLitBare record time
-- while the var is still unbound.  Lets checkOneImplObligation reframe a purely
-- literal Num obligation forced to a concrete non-Num type (`Type mismatch: Int vs
-- T`) while an OPERATOR-sourced one (`x + 1`) keeps `No impl of Num for T`.  Storing
-- the VAR (not just the loc) lets the operator-taint pass below share a root through
-- `normalize`, so `1 + x` and `x + 1` are both recognised as operator-sourced
-- regardless of unify direction.  Error-path only; reset per run.

-- PERF: the literals that are NOT YET operator-tainted.  `markNumlitOpTaint` scans
-- THIS instead of the full `numlitVarLocs` (which is never trimmed).  Sound because
-- tainting is idempotent: it appends a loc to `numlitOpLocs`, whose only reader
-- (`numlitReframeLoc`) does a membership test — so re-tainting an already-tainted
-- literal cannot change any outcome, and a tainted literal may leave the worklist.
-- Scanning EVERY literal ever recorded on EVERY arithmetic operand was O(N²), and
-- after the allocation fix (see `rootIdOf`) it was still the typecheck stage's
-- dominant remaining cost on a large file.
--
-- `numlitVarLocs` itself keeps every literal — `numlitReframeLoc` and
-- `tagLitLocsWithRoot` both still need the complete list.

-- Chunk D: locs of literals whose var was ALSO an operand of an arithmetic op
-- (recordIfaceObligation).  Such a literal keeps the Num message — the operator is the
-- real culprit — so the reframe skips it (it reframes `litLocs \ opLocs`).

-- Chunk D: (literalLoc, contextKind) recorded when inferIf / inferListLit / consOp
-- is about to force a still-unbound literal var against a concrete sibling type —
-- lets the reframe pick site-specific wording (if-branches / list elements / cons
-- head-vs-element) over the bare `Type mismatch: Int vs T`.

-- Every local binding (let-bound name, lambda param, function-clause param,
-- match-arm binder) flows through inferPat's PVar/PAs arms, which capture
-- (name, mono var) here.  The mono var is union-find-solved by the time inference
-- ends; the module checker then generalizes each into `localSchemesOut`, and
-- `captureEntryTables` freezes them into the drive's `PartialAnalysis`.  The seed
-- (runtime.mdk externs: putStrLn, readLine, …) stays in scope for inference but
-- is excluded from the returned env, so `seedSchemesOut` is frozen the same way.
-- Neither enters the returned env.

-- `loc` is the BINDER's own source span (#2092) — `None` only where the binding
-- site genuinely has none to give.  Discarding it is what made the hover tier
-- order unfixable: without a position there is no way to tell a local that is
-- in scope at the cursor from one bound in an unrelated declaration.
recordLocalBind : ModuleCtx -> String -> Option Loc -> BinderId -> Mono -> Unit
recordLocalBind mctx name loc bid v =
  let _ = recordBinderType mctx.mcGraph bid name v None False
  mctx.mcCells.localBindRefs :=
    (localSourceName name, loc, v) :: mctx.mcCells.localBindRefs.value

-- Queue binder [bid]'s type for the runtime-type table.  [arity] is `Some n` for
-- a function binder, whose return type is read after its n declared parameters;
-- [signed] is whether that function has a declared type signature.
-- A binder no minting pass visited (a node the typechecker or a later pass
-- synthesized) has no id to publish under and is skipped.
recordBinderType : GraphCtx ->
  BinderId ->
  String ->
  Mono ->
  Option Int ->
  Bool ->
  Unit
recordBinderType gctx bid name v arity signed = match bid
  BinderId _ i =>
    if i < 0 then
      ()
    else
      let g = gctx.graphRun
      g.binderPending :=
        PendingBinder bid (localSourceName name) v arity signed
          :: g.binderPending.value

-- an interface occurrence whose identity is not (yet) recoverable at the site.
--
-- ⚠️ U1b (#1482) RETIRED the two sites this comment used to name.
-- `recordCallObligations` and `recordSchemeCallObligations` now carry an `IfaceRef`
-- end to end (`funConstraintIfacesRef`'s payload is `List IfaceRef`,
-- `schemeObligationsRef`'s is `List VecObl`), so neither mints a bare goal any more.
-- What is LEFT — grep this name for the live worklist, do not trust this list:
--   * `recordImplObligation`'s METHOD-OCCURRENCE goal, which is a decl-layer /
--     occurrence-layer reconciliation and not a table widening.  Owned by #1507, and
--     it is the LAST condition on deleting the bare compatibility leg;
--   * `ifaceForInferredId`'s third fallback, which recovers a slot's interface from
--     `pendingDictApps` — a SPELLING-keyed routing channel (see `resolveDictApps` /
--     `dispHeadTab`) whose iface component must stay a route word, so the recovery is
--     bare by construction rather than by omission.
ifaceRefBare : String -> IfaceRef
ifaceRefBare n = IfaceRef { irName = n, irOrigin = OriginUnresolved }

-- U1b (#1482): the ABSENT-interface sentinel for the slot-parallel iface channels.
-- `funConstraintIfacesRef` has always used `""` to mean "this slot has no recoverable
-- interface" (see `ifaceForInferredId`), and every reader tests it and skips.  It is
-- deliberately NOT spelled `ifaceRefBare ""`: that name is the residual worklist for a
-- goal whose identity is UNRECOVERABLE, and "no interface at all" is a different fact
-- that must not pollute the grep.
ifaceRefNone : IfaceRef
ifaceRefNone = IfaceRef { irName = "", irOrigin = OriginUnresolved }

-- B-4 producer migration: pure legacy projections at reader seams.  Mutable state
-- stores only `PredicateSlot`; ids, ifaces and the known argument-vector prefix are
-- derived on demand so they cannot drift into separate authorities again.
predicateSlotIds : List PredicateSlot -> List Int
predicateSlotIds [] = []
predicateSlotIds (s :: rest) = match s.psBoundIds
  [] => predicateSlotIds rest
  id :: _ => id :: predicateSlotIds rest

predicateSlotView : PredicateSlot -> (CSlot, List Mono)
predicateSlotView s = match s.psBoundIds
  [] =>
    (CSlot { csIface = s.psIface, csId = 0 }, predicateSlotKnownArgs s.psArgs)
  id :: _ => (
    CSlot {
      csIface = s.psIface,
      csId = id,
    },
    predicateSlotKnownArgs s.psArgs,
  )

-- `idx` is the first-wins index `funPredicateSlotsIdxRef` mirrors from `funPredicateSlotsRef`.
lookupPredicateSlots : String ->
  OrdMap (List PredicateSlot) ->
  Option (List PredicateSlot)
lookupPredicateSlots k idx = omLookup k idx

hasPredicateSlots : String -> OrdMap (List PredicateSlot) -> Bool
hasPredicateSlots k idx = omHasKey k idx

predicateSlotIdsAt : String -> OrdMap (List PredicateSlot) -> List Int
predicateSlotIdsAt name idx = predicateSlotIds (optionOr [] (omLookup name idx))

predicateSlotWithoutArgs : PredicateSlot -> PredicateSlot
predicateSlotWithoutArgs s = PredicateSlot {
  psIface = s.psIface,
  psArgs = PSArgsUnknown,
  psBoundIds = s.psBoundIds,
}

predicateSlotsWithoutArgs : List PredicateSlot -> List PredicateSlot
predicateSlotsWithoutArgs slots = map predicateSlotWithoutArgs slots

predicateSlotTableWithoutArgs : List (a, List PredicateSlot) ->
  List (a, List PredicateSlot)
predicateSlotTableWithoutArgs entries =
  map (entry => (fst entry, predicateSlotsWithoutArgs (snd entry))) entries

-- #838 I1: project a ported UObligation back to the pre-#838 tuple shape
-- `(iface, argument vector, loc)`, for the many downstream consumers
-- (registerLocalScheme/registerSchemeObligations/checkSigConstraintCoverage/
-- checkMethodRigidityCore/numCallObls/…) that stay on the
-- old shape this increment — only the storage + its own checker move in I1 (#838 §5.2).
-- ⚠️ U1b (#1482): this used to project the interface back to its bare SPELLING, on
-- the stated ground that every consumer feeds `schemeObligationsRef` /
-- `funConstraintIfacesRef`, which were bare-name-keyed.  They are not any more, and
-- `forwardedVecObls` — an UNSIGNED constrained forwarder's whole scheme context —
-- reaches `schemeObligationsRef` through exactly this tuple.  Keeping the projection
-- would have left that one path minting bare goals inside a channel the rest of which
-- carries identity.  Consumers that ask a SPELLING question (`numCallObls`'s `"Num"`
-- test, the survivor-obligation diagnostics) read `.irName` at their own site.
oblAsTuple : GraphCtx -> UObligation -> (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc)
oblAsTuple gctx o = (o.pred.iface, uOblArgs gctx o, o.loc)

-- THE ONLY legal reader of an obligation's dispatch vector — total over both
-- `OblProjection` arms.  See `OblProjection` for why the impl channel's projection
-- cannot be hoisted to record time.
uOblArgs : GraphCtx -> UObligation -> List Mono
uOblArgs gctx o = match o.oblProj
  OpProjected => o.pred.args
  OpMethodOcc typarams mty occ omitted =>
    occurrenceDispatchMonos typarams mty occ omitted
  OpExactReturn request => optionOr [] (methodReturnArgs gctx request)
  OpNumLit _ => o.pred.args

-- the call channel's window, in the pre-#838 tuple shape (see oblAsTuple).
callOblsWindow : ModuleCtx -> Int -> List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc)
callOblsWindow mctx mark =
  map (oblAsTuple mctx.mcGraph) (wWindow mctx.mcCells.obls mark)

-- #1114 (DICT-SEMANTICS §4.2 D1): would `checkOneCallObligation` reach a VERDICT on this
-- recorded predicate right now?  That — not groundness — is the question the D1-preserving
-- window in `inferUserImplBodies` has to ask, and getting it wrong is silent by
-- construction (see the warning at the end of this comment).
--
-- The gate decides a goal now exactly when every argument has a constructed head
-- (`allConcreteHeads`), and that verdict cannot change later: grounding is monotone, so
-- a constructed head (a type constructor, a rigid, or an arrow) never becomes a variable.
-- A predicate this filter drops while the gate would decide it vanishes with no verdict
-- from any channel (D4 exempts the impl channel from D3), which is #792's three-verdict
-- signature (`check` 0 / `run` `intToString: not an Int` / `build` `arg-tag dispatch on
-- impl type that owns no constructors`).
-- `numUnimplementableHead`'s `TApp` arm (a spine head that is an unbound tyvar) is NOT
-- kept: that head can still bind, so its verdict is not stable and the predicate belongs
-- to D2's deferred population.  An EMPTY argument vector is inert at the gate
-- (`if isEmptyL args then ()`), so dropping it loses no verdict.
--
-- The set is closed, enumerated from the type rather than sampled.  `Mono` has six
-- constructors and `headMonoNode` peels `TApp`, so a head is one of `TVar`, `TCon`,
-- `TRigid`, `TFun`, `TEff`.  `TCon`/`TRigid`/`TFun` are the constructed heads
-- `headTyconMono` answers, so `allConcreteHeads` keeps them; `TVar` can still bind, so
-- gate and filter agree to defer it; and `TEff` is decided by neither (the gate reaches
-- its own `allConcreteHeads` arm and defers).  A vector mixing a constructed head with a
-- variable defers in both, whatever the constructed head is.
--
-- ⚠️ NO GATE CAN CATCH A REGRESSION HERE.  A predicate this filter drops is one no channel
-- ever reports, so it produces silence, and silence is what every golden in the corpus
-- already records for a program the compiler accepts.  If you narrow this predicate, the
-- suite stays green.  The obligation is on the reader: any arm added to
-- `checkOneCallObligation` ABOVE its `allConcreteHeads` test must be mirrored here, or it
-- becomes unreachable for every parametric impl body in the language.
uOblIsDecidableNow : GraphCtx -> UObligation -> Bool
uOblIsDecidableNow gctx o =
  let args = map normalize (uOblArgs gctx o)
  isNonEmptyL args && allConcreteHeads args

-- the top-level fn whose body is currently being inferred ("" = none); captured
-- into a deferred RecDictApp so its recursive calls forward the right dict param.

-- G4: True while inferring an impl method BODY (set around inferImplMethod).  A
-- comparison/equality OPERATOR site records this flag so resolveBinopSite consults
-- `activeDictVarOf` (→ route the impl's threaded element dict, RDict) ONLY for sites
-- genuinely inside an impl body.  A TOP-LEVEL `<=`/`==` must NOT — its operand could
-- normalize to an unsolved tyvar whose id collides with a stale activeDictVars entry
-- left by a previously-inferred impl, spuriously routing it RDict (which flipped the
-- repl's String-keyed `:browse` sort).  activeDictVars is global + uncleared, so the
-- flag is the scope gate the id-lookup alone cannot provide.

-- INFERRED (unsignatured) `=>`-constraint promotion (the reference's two-pass
-- Elaborate / Phase 83/84/115).  An unsignatured fn whose body uses a
-- return-position method — or calls a constrained fn — at one of its OWN
-- generalized tyvars carries a constraint only AFTER inference.  We discover this
-- by recording, per occurrence, the enclosing fn (currentFn) and the live mono,
-- then (post-generalization) intersecting with the fn's quantified ids.
--   methodSiteFns : (enclosing fn, a return-position method site's result mono)
--   dictAppFns    : (enclosing fn, a constrained-fn call's instantiated constraint
--                   monos) — propagates a constraint to an unsignatured CALLER
--   promotedRef   : fns discovered THIS pass to carry an inferred constraint; read
--                   by the retired promotion fixpoint to grow the dict-passed set
--   dictEligibleRef: the USER fn names eligible for promotion (the prelude's
--                   constrained fns stay arg-tag/RKey — out of scope).  Set by
--                   the old elaborator; NOT cleared by `freshModuleCtx` (constant per run).
--
-- PERF: both are INDEXED BY ENCLOSING FN rather than kept as flat (fn, mono) assoc
-- lists.  Their sole reader, `inferredConstraintIds`, selects the entries of ONE fn,
-- and it runs once per member of every top-level group — so scanning a flat list that
-- accumulates a site for every constrained occurrence in the whole file was O(N²).
-- Each key's list is built by consing, exactly like the flat lists were, so a fn's
-- sites keep the same most-recent-first order the old scan produced.

-- cons [x] onto the entry for [fn] (absent ⇒ a fresh single-element entry)
consSiteFn : String -> a -> OrdMap (List a) -> OrdMap (List a)
consSiteFn fn x idx = omInsert fn (x :: sitesFor fn idx) idx

-- the sites recorded for [fn], most-recent-first
sitesFor : String -> OrdMap (List a) -> List a
sitesFor fn idx = optionOr [] (omLookup fn idx)

-- The graph's promoted names so far, in load order.  `freshModuleCtx` clears
-- `promotedRef` per module, so `graphModuleWorker`'s `GOutTrees` arm unions each
-- module's `promotedRef.value` into here right after that module's check (before
-- the next module's `freshModuleCtx` wipes it).  Its reader is `beginModuleMarking`: a
-- module's dict-name set is the bare set plus THIS list, which is what lets one
-- sweep mark a promoted callee's cross-module call sites (ARCH §E).  Cleared at
-- every Module-arm driver entry (`elaborateModules`, `checkModulesPreambleK`) so an
-- earlier elaboration in the process cannot leak promoted names into a later mark
-- set; NOT touched by `freshModuleCtx`.  `elaborateModules` reads it once more at the
-- end, for the set `dictPass` prepends dict params over (`markDictNames`).

-- O(log n) membership index of dictEligibleRef.  #415 item 3: DERIVED from the list by
-- `setDictEligible`, the single writer of both — not mirrored at each set site, so the
-- two cannot drift.  maybeInferConstraint tests it per SCC member per discovery pass —
-- an O(members × eligible) scan over the whole program when it was a list.

-- Whether the retired single-program checker also inferred each parametric impl's
-- method bodies (instance-`requires` dict-passing, Phase 83/84 single-level).  ON
-- only for the old elaborate/dict path; off for the
-- `=== TYPES ===` golden path (checkProgram) and the multi-module path
-- (elaborateModules) so their scheme output stays byte-identical.  Deliberately
-- NOT reset by `freshModuleCtx` — the entrypoint that owns the path sets it.

-- ── D0.5 arg-position dispatch MEASUREMENT (probe-only) ─────────────────────
-- Classify every ARGUMENT-position interface-method occurrence (the bare-EVar
-- arg-tag population D0 counted, upper bound 1065) by the inferred type of its
-- DISCRIMINATING argument: concrete-primitive / concrete-ADT / type-variable.
-- Mirrors recordSite/resolveSites (which stamp RETURN-position sites) but for
-- arg-position sites it MEASURES, never stamps.  An arg-position method is exactly
-- one that reached inferVar (return-position + method-constrained methods were
-- already rewritten to EMethodAt/EDictAt by prePassDict, so they never arrive there).

-- method name → 0-based index of its first argument mentioning the interface
-- typaram (its dispatch position).  Set by the probe before elaboration; absence
-- of a name means "not an arg-position interface method" → not measured.

-- ── D3a arg-position dispatch STAMPING (Native backend, ALL elaboration paths) ──
-- The action analog of the D0.5 measurement: instead of classifying each
-- ARGUMENT-position interface-method occurrence, STAMP a static `RKey <head>` for
-- every one whose discriminating-argument type resolves to a concrete head (the
-- 903 concrete sites = 25 primitive + 878 ADT).  Type-variable occurrences (the
-- 110 D3b sites) stay RNone → the emitter falls back to runtime arg-tag dispatch.
-- Stamping is UNCONDITIONAL: emit, eval, and the `=== TYPES ===` / Core-IR golden +
-- ceval-oracle drivers all elaborate identically — one single elaboration mode
-- (#157).  Measured byte-identical across the 204/204 fixtures, so the unification
-- is representation-neutral, not a behaviour change.

-- the route refs awaiting an arg-position stamp + their discriminating-argument
-- mono (captured during inference, resolved by resolveArgStamps while the tyvar
-- cells are still bound).  Recorded as `GKArgStamp` goals on `GraphRun.goals`,
-- drained per module like the return-position sites.
-- D3b-1: also carries the method name + the EMethodAt impl-dicts ref, so a
-- concrete site whose head names a parametric `requires` impl can thread the
-- element dict (resolveArgStamp → argImplDictRoutesForEncl), exactly as the
-- return-position sites carry implRef for resolveSite.
-- #156 S3a: entries are `PendingEntry`s of kind `SKArg`.

-- the dispatch-index registry: each interface method → index of its first arg
-- mentioning the interface typaram.  Methods with NO such arg (return-position)
-- contribute nothing.  Computed structurally from interface decls.
argDispatchIndices : List Decl -> List (String, Int)
argDispatchIndices prog = flatMap argDispatchOfDecl prog

argDispatchOfDecl : Decl -> List (String, Int)
argDispatchOfDecl (DAttrib _ d) = argDispatchOfDecl d
argDispatchOfDecl (DInterface { typarams, methods, ... }) =
  flatMap (argDispatchOfMethod typarams) methods
argDispatchOfDecl _ = []

argDispatchOfMethod : List String -> IfaceMethod -> List (String, Int)
argDispatchOfMethod typarams (IfaceMethod mname mty _ _) =
  match firstDispatchIdx (dispatchTyparams typarams) 0 (methodArgs mty)
    Some i => [(mname, i)]
    None => []

-- #1351 L1 (EXPAND): the IDENTITY-CARRYING sibling of `argDispatchIndices` above.  Same
-- walk, same arms, same `firstDispatchIdx` classification — the ONLY difference is the
-- key: `(IfaceRef, method name)` instead of the bare method name.  `IfaceRef` is this
-- file's existing module-qualified interface identity (`irName` spelling + `irOrigin` I4
-- identity); it is already minted at the peer population site
-- `methodRowsInto` out of the SAME two `DInterface` fields, so this adds
-- no new notion of identity, only a second key-shape for an existing one.
--
-- Readers: its result is installed into `GraphCtx.argDispatchIdxByIdRef` by the
-- two drivers, and `argDispatchOf` reads that ref through `dispatchIdxScoped` (L3
-- MIGRATE, landed).  Derive the set — `grep -n argDispatchIdxByIdRef` — rather than
-- trusting a list here.
--
-- 🔒 Purity note, load-bearing for L1's zero-behaviour-change property:
-- `argDispatchIndices` and everything it reaches (`argDispatchOfDecl`,
-- `argDispatchOfMethod`, `dispatchTyparams`, `firstDispatchIdx`, `argMentions`,
-- `methodArgs`) is pure and structural, so running this second walk beside it advances
-- no counter, mints no id and registers nothing.  The scheme-bearing method-row walk is
-- intentionally effectful and therefore constructs identity and scheme together.
argDispatchIndicesById : List Decl -> List ((IfaceRef, String), Int)
argDispatchIndicesById prog = flatMap argDispatchOfDeclById prog

argDispatchOfDeclById : Decl -> List ((IfaceRef, String), Int)
argDispatchOfDeclById (DAttrib _ d) = argDispatchOfDeclById d
argDispatchOfDeclById (DInterface { name, typarams, methods, ifaceOrigin, ... }) =
  flatMap
    (argDispatchOfMethodById
      IfaceRef { irName = name, irOrigin = ifaceOrigin }
      typarams)
    methods
argDispatchOfDeclById _ = []

argDispatchOfMethodById : IfaceRef ->
  List String ->
  IfaceMethod ->
  List ((IfaceRef, String), Int)
argDispatchOfMethodById iface typarams (IfaceMethod mname mty _ _) =
  match firstDispatchIdx (dispatchTyparams typarams) 0 (methodArgs mty)
    Some i => [((iface, mname), i)]
    None => []

firstDispatchIdx : List String -> Int -> List Ty -> Option Int
firstDispatchIdx _ _ [] = None
firstDispatchIdx typarams i (ty :: rest)
  | argMentions typarams ty = Some i
  | otherwise = firstDispatchIdx typarams (i + 1) rest

-- D3a: queue an arg-position occurrence's route ref for stamping, keyed on the
-- inferred type of its discriminating argument (the dispatch-position arg mono).
-- The cell is read later (resolveArgStamps), once inference has solved it.  D3b-1:
-- also carry [name] + the impl-dicts ref so a concrete-head site can thread the
-- element dict for a parametric `requires` impl.  [suppressed] is the caller's
-- `dcSuppressArgStamp`: a definer-shadow application head records its argument
-- itself.
recordArgStamp : ModuleCtx ->
  Bool ->
  String ->
  Ref Route ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Ref Inner ->
  Int ->
  Mono ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Unit
recordArgStamp mctx suppressed name tagRef implRef innerRef idx mono omitted
  | suppressed = ()
  | otherwise = match nthArgMono idx mono
    Some am =>
      pushSiteGoal
        mctx.mcGraph
        GKArgStamp
        innerRef
        (PendingEntry
          name
          tagRef
          am
          mctx.mcCells.currentFn.value
          (SKArg implRef mono omitted)
          mctx.mcLoc
          (captureScope mctx ())
          (freshEvId mctx ()))
    None => ()

-- Cause-A prerequisite: an ARG-position method occurrence's discriminating-arg
-- mono, keyed by the enclosing fn (currentFn), pushed into methodSiteFns — the
-- arg-position analogue of recordSite's return-position push.  inferredConstraintIds
-- reads methodSiteFns to discover the enclosing fn's INFERRED constraint, so this
-- lets `f s = display s` promote `f` to a dict-passed fn (it had no signature, so
-- the constraint is inferred, not declared).  Idx-th arg mono = the receiver whose
-- (constraint) tyvar must be discovered.
recordArgSiteFn : ModuleCtx -> String -> Int -> Mono -> Unit
recordArgSiteFn mctx _ idx mono = match nthArgMono idx mono
  Some am =>
    mctx.mcCells.methodSiteFns :=
      consSiteFn
        mctx.mcCells.currentFn.value
        am
        mctx.mcCells.methodSiteFns.value
  None => ()

-- D3a/D3b-1: stamp each queued arg-position route from its now-resolved
-- discriminating arg mono.  D3b-1 first: a mono pinned to an impl's `requires`
-- element tyvar (registered in activeDictVars by registerImplRequires) → the
-- element dict param RDict $dict_<method>_<slot> — the ARGUMENT-position analogue
-- of resolveSite's return-position RDict.  Else (D3a): a concrete head
-- (Int/String/Float/… or any ADT tycon) → a static `RKey tag …`, and when that
-- head names a parametric impl WITH a requires, fill the impl-dicts ref so the
-- call threads the element dict (concrete element → RKey Int; a recursive element
-- of the SAME parametric type → RDict forwarding the in-scope dict param).  A
-- still-unsolved free type variable → left RNone (the emitter arg-tag-dispatches).
resolveArgStamps : SiteCtx -> List PendingEntry -> Unit
resolveArgStamps sx [] = ()
resolveArgStamps sx ((PendingEntry name tagRef am encl kind loc scope _) :: rest) =
  let sx = { sx | sxSite = loc }
  let _ = match kind
    SKArg implRef fullMono omitted =>
      resolveArgStamp sx name tagRef implRef am fullMono omitted encl loc scope
    _ => ()
  resolveArgStamps sx rest

-- #156 S3c: a thin adapter over `entail` (EKArg kind).  `entail` returns
-- `(primaryRoute, elementRoutes)`; stamp them into (tagRef, implRef).  Reproduces the
-- pre-S3c arm-by-arm body: assum → `(RDict dname, [])`, inst → `(RKey key [],
-- argImplDictRoutesForEncl …)`, fallback → `(RNone, [])`.
-- TYPECHECK-AUDIT C7 (arg-position): when ≥2 impls of this method share head tycon [tag]
-- but differ in type ARGS (e.g. `MyPair Int Bool` vs `MyPair Bool Int`), bare-head `RKey
-- tag` narrows to the FIRST impl (eval's hasTag matches the head `t`).  `keyForSite`
-- (inside entailInst) upgrades to the canonical full-type impl key so eval's hasTag
-- matches the right impl's `k`.  No collision → bare head, unchanged.
-- ⚠️ tagRef is NOT always RNone-seeded: rewriteArgScoped (~7438) seeds a standalone-shadow
-- arg site to `RLocal <sym> []`.  At an `EKArg` site, `resolveRLocalSites` leaves that
-- importer seed untouched only for an ungrounded receiver or a grounded receiver with a
-- visible impl; a no-impl grounded receiver is restamped `RLocal`.  So the pre-S3c None
-- arm's `()` was load-bearing: it PRESERVED the seed until that receiver decision.  For
-- EKArg `entail` yields RNone ONLY from its fallback (assum→RDict,
-- inst→RKey), so guarding the stamp on RNone reproduces that do-nothing None arm exactly
-- and never clobbers an RLocal seed.  implRef is []-seeded everywhere (every EMethodAt
-- construction — 7313/7355/7356/7438/7441/7443 — uses `(Ref [])`, and only this resolver
-- ever writes an arg-site's implRef), so []-over-[] needs no guard (matches resolveSite).
resolveArgStamp : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  Ref Route ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Mono ->
  Mono ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  String ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
resolveArgStamp sx name tagRef implRef am fullMono omitted encl origin scope =
  let (route, routes) = entail sx name am encl scope (EKArg fullMono omitted)
  let _ = match route
    RNone => ()
    _ => tagRef := route
  implRef := routes

-- Native Gap C (parametric default-method dict-synthesis, 2026-06-12): a BY-NAME
-- relational method (`lt`/`gt`/…) at a parametric Ord head (tuple/`List a`/`Box a`)
-- has NO own impl, so its element `requires` dicts must be keyed off the inner
-- `compare` (whose impl carries them).  emitDefaultDefine eta-prepends matching
-- dict params; emitDefaultRKey forwards these words.  Concrete head / a method
-- with its own impl ⇒ same key as before (empty for non-parametric), unchanged.

-- ── type-error accumulator ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Unification failures record diagnostics here instead of panicking, so
-- ill-typed programs emit matching `TYPE ERROR: …` lines.  occursCheckFailed
-- is a per-bindVar flag: occursAdjustUnbound sets it so bindVar can skip the
-- actual link (preventing a cyclic union-find entry).
-- Each accumulated error carries the span of the construct around its push site
-- (the record's `mcLoc`, see `mctxAt`) unless the push names one.  severity = 1.
--
-- issue 1146 — THE CHANNEL IS SPLIT BY ROLE.  "Which diagnostics are REPORTED"
-- is OUTPUT and lives in `ModuleCells.mcCells.typeErrors`, a `Windowed TcDiag` like its
-- obligation-channel siblings (see `Windowed` above — `wPush`/`wRestore` are
-- its sole WRITERS, so its list and its count cannot drift apart).  "An error
-- OCCURRED" is CONTROL and lives in `ModuleCells.mcCells.errorsDetected`, a monotone-per-module
-- occurrence counter that is not a diagnostics channel at all.
--
-- The counter counts errors DETECTED, not errors STORED (PR2).  The three dedup
-- helpers below still read the list by CONTENT to decide whether to store, but a
-- short-circuit bumps the counter anyway (`noteTypeErrorDetected`), so "was an error
-- detected here" and "is this diagnostic worth printing" are now independent
-- judgments.  That is the property the whole split exists for: NO diagnostics
-- decision — dedup key, rendering, ordering, loc selection, code selection — can
-- reach a control decision, because the only thing control reads is a count of
-- detections and none of those choices changes whether a detection happened.
--
-- PR1 stopped short of this: it bumped only on a real store, so the counter's delta
-- equalled `listLen typeErrors`'s delta exactly (which is what let PR1 land without
-- moving a golden), and a deduped push therefore answered `erredDuring` False and let
-- a gated `unify` run that a non-deduped push would have suppressed.  PR2 gives that
-- equality up on purpose; it is no longer an invariant and must not be restored.
--
-- See `recordTypeError` / `noteTypeErrorDetected` (the counter's sole writers) and
-- `erredDuring` (its sole reader) below.

-- G1 (SOUNDNESS): `GraphCtx.typeErrorsSticky` is a sticky mirror of typeErrors that
-- `freshModuleCtx` does not clear.  The multi-module elaborate path
-- (elaborateModules → checkModuleFullImpl) calls `freshModuleCtx` at the start of each
-- module, wiping `typeErrors`, so after the whole graph only the last module's errors
-- survive there.  build/run must abort on a type error in any module, so
-- `pushTypeError` also records into this accumulator, which the drive's mint
-- starts `False`.  Read via `hadTypeErrors` to gate the CLI exit code before
-- emit/eval.
--
-- #2089 / #2544 (M4): `GraphCtx.typeErrorsStickyDiags` holds the diagnostics behind
-- the flag, newest first, across every module of the graph.  `ModuleCells.mcCells.typeErrors` is
-- wiped per module, so this is the only place a caller with no per-module hook can
-- read what armed the sticky flag rather than merely that it was armed — it is what
-- `elaborateModules` returns as its residual, each entry with its own `Loc`.  Written
-- only by `recordTypeError`, started empty by the drive's mint, and rolled back
-- wherever the flag is (`checkGraphFinish`) — the same pairing obligation the
-- detection counter states.  Both are the drive's own.

-- #2544 (M4): every diagnostic that armed the sticky gate in the drive, each tagged
-- with the module it was recorded in, in push order, deduplicated PER GOAL —
-- module, code, location and text together — never by text alone (a text key would
-- re-introduce the suppressed-check shape OD5 forbids: two goals at two sites with
-- the same rendering are two findings).
export
stickyTypeErrorDiags : DriveOutputs -> List (String, TcDiag)
stickyTypeErrorDiags o = stickyDiagsInPushOrder o.doStickyDiags

-- True iff the drive recorded a type error, as the drive left it.
export
hadTypeErrors : DriveOutputs -> Bool
hadTypeErrors o = o.doHadTypeErrors

-- Whether the `main` binding recorded obligations remains inference-private; the
-- publication module receives its Boolean answer rather than this side table.
mainHasObligations : ModuleCtx -> Bool
mainHasObligations mctx =
  let id = optionOr 0 (omLookup "main" mctx.mcCells.schemeDefIdsRef.value)
  match lookupSchemeObls "main" id mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value
    Some (_ :: _) => True
    _ => False

-- ── non-exhaustive-match warning accumulator (the type-aware `check_match`) ──
-- `inferMatch` pushes a warning here for every `match` whose non-guarded arms
-- don't cover the scrutinee's type.  `matchOracle` is the ctor oracle the matrix
-- recursion consults; `checkOneMatchToLines` seeds it from the program's
-- data decls (so it sees the same user + builtin ctors check_match does) before
-- inference runs.  `freshModuleCtx` installs both from the `CheckRunSeed` and the driver
-- reads `matchWarnings` after the typecheck pass; runs that ignore match warnings
-- (the schemes/selfproc paths) simply never read it.
-- #159: element type is now `TcDiag` (severity 2), carrying the span (formerly the
-- parallel `matchWarningLocs`) and the actionable-fix help (formerly the message-
-- keyed `matchWarningHelp`) INLINE — no parallel lists, no lookup-by-message.  The
-- `TcDiag.msg` holds the FULL "Warning: …"-prefixed string exactly as the old
-- `List String` did, so the text-rendering paths (`checkOneMatchToLines`,
-- checkToLinesWithRuntime, checkModulesEntryReport) stay byte-identical; only the
-- prefix strip happens on the driver/diagnostics.mdk side.
--
-- ⚠️ THE `W-*` CODE IS AUTHORED AT THE PUSH SITE — write it into the `TcDiag`, never
-- leave it `""` for a downstream reader to guess.  `driver/diagnostics.mdk`'s
-- `diagOfTypeWarning` carries whatever code it finds here straight through to
-- `--json`; it used to re-derive one by prefix-matching this message text, which
-- silently relabelled any third warning `W-NONEXHAUSTIVE` (see that function's own
-- note, and DIAGNOSTIC-CODES-DESIGN.md — "*No chokepoint can infer these*").
-- Register the code in DIAGNOSTIC-CODES-DESIGN.md's warning table in the same change.
--
-- ⚠️ THE `W-` PREFIX IS LOAD-BEARING, not a naming convention.  The JSON `kind` is
-- DERIVED from the code's prefix (`codeKind`), so the code you write here decides
-- how every consumer classifies the diagnostic.  A demoted error that KEEPS its
-- `T-*` code is the trap: it reads as a type error to anything filtering the
-- per-stage taxonomy.  `diagKind` now stops that from rendering an incoherent
-- `{"kind":"type","severity":2}`, but it deliberately does NOT rewrite your code —
-- inventing `W-FOO` from `T-FOO` would be the same derive-identity-from-spelling
-- mistake in the other direction.  Author a `W-*` code; do not reuse the error's.
--
-- This is THE channel for a typecheck-stage warning — including one that used to be
-- an error.  Do NOT demote an error by pushing a severity-2 `TcDiag` through
-- `recordTypeError` instead: it arms `typeErrorsSticky` (aborts `build`/`run`) and
-- bumps `errorsDetected` (steers `erredDuring`-gated inference, issue 1146)
-- UNCONDITIONALLY, without reading severity at all — so the "warning" keeps both of
-- an error's side effects.  It does not even RENDER as a warning: `diagOfTypeError`
-- binds the severity field to `_` and prints severity 1.  (Removing that hardcode
-- would not rescue the idea — it would print severity 2 and still abort the build.
-- The side effects are the reason, not the rendering.)  `matchWarnings` has neither.

-- True iff the last typecheck pass pushed any match warning.  Read by the snapshot
-- runner (`tools/snapshot.mdk`) to decide whether a rendered `# TYPES` section carries
-- diagnostic prose — a `W-*` warning is graded by `compiler/ERROR-QUALITY.md` exactly
-- like an error is, so a `# TYPES` section holding one is NOT `--bless`-able.  Keyed on
-- the accumulator rather than sniffing the rendered text: the renderer must not have to
-- guess which of its own lines are diagnostics.
export
hadMatchWarnings : DriveOutputs -> Bool
hadMatchWarnings o = o.doHadMatchWarnings

-- `hadMatchWarnings` of the last module checked: the only read of a drive that returns no
-- outputs (the projections).
export
matchWarningsNow : ModuleCtx -> Bool
matchWarningsNow mctx = match mctx.mcCells.matchWarnings.value
  [] => False
  _ => True

-- The drive inputs of a driver that loads no stdlib ownership and selects no
-- profile: no module stdlib-owned, the flat entry not stdlib, every trace off, and
-- the `IO` join of no profile.  A pure value (it holds no `Ref`).
--
-- No ownership means every `extern` is stamped (#2072, `ffiStampModeOwned`), and that
-- direction is the safe one on purpose: a driver that passes no ownership suppresses
-- nothing, so the worst it can do is render an `FFI` atom on the stdlib catalog when
-- someone points it at stdlib source.  The inverse default would leave #2072's hole
-- (a user `extern f : Int -> <> Int` typing pure) open on every such path, which is
-- a soundness hole rather than a cosmetic one.
export
defaultDriveInputs : DriveInputs
defaultDriveInputs = DriveInputs {
  diExecutedMainDriver = None,
  diManifestRequests = [],
  diStdlibOwned = omEmpty,
  diFlatEntryIsStdlib = False,
  diTrace = None,
  diIoJoinGrants = ioJoinGrants None,
  diProfileName = "",
  diPreludeKey = None,
}

-- The drive inputs a driver builds from the profile it selected and the loader's
-- owning-root fact (`stdlibOwnership`, `driver/loader.mdk`): whether the flat entry
-- is a stdlib module, and the stdlib-owned module ids.  That fact is read by
-- `ffiStampMode`, which decides whether an `extern` DECLARATION in the program
-- under check is the stdlib's extern catalog (never stamped) or a user's FFI
-- declaration (always stamped).
--
-- Two ownership fields because graph checks carry different amounts of identity.
-- `Module mid _ _` has a module id, so the Module arm asks "is THIS module
-- stdlib-owned" of the set.  `Flat _` has no id at all (the flat driver has already
-- flattened the program into one anonymous decl list), so the entry's ownership
-- arrives as its own Bool.
--
-- NOT `projectTrustedMods` (`driver/loader.mdk`): that predicate answers a different
-- question (may module M *reference* an internal-only extern?) and is opt-in-able
-- from any `medaka.toml` via `allow-internal` (#1713).  Routing this through it would
-- let a user exempt their own externs from the stamp by writing one manifest line.
export
driveInputsFor : Option TargetProfile -> Bool -> List String -> DriveInputs
driveInputsFor profile flatEntry mods = { defaultDriveInputs |
  diStdlibOwned = namesToSet mods omEmpty,
  diFlatEntryIsStdlib = flatEntry,
  diIoJoinGrants = ioJoinGrants profile,
  diProfileName = match profile
    None => ""
    Some p => profileName p,
}

-- Each entry with the evidence its goal published in [evidence], the table of the
-- drive that recorded it.
export
finishMethodReturnTrace : TraceSink -> EvTable -> List MethodReturnTraceEntry
finishMethodReturnTrace sink evidence =
  map
    (publishMethodReturnTrace evidence)
    (reverseL sink.tsMethodReturnEntries.value)

publishMethodReturnTrace : EvTable ->
  MethodReturnTraceEntry ->
  MethodReturnTraceEntry
publishMethodReturnTrace evidence entry =
  let published = match entry.mrtGoal
    Some goal => lookupTraceEvidence goal evidence
    None => None
  MethodReturnTraceEntry {
    mrtStage = entry.mrtStage,
    mrtInterface = entry.mrtInterface,
    mrtMethod = entry.mrtMethod,
    mrtArguments = entry.mrtArguments,
    mrtScope = entry.mrtScope,
    mrtOrigin = entry.mrtOrigin,
    mrtGoal = entry.mrtGoal,
    mrtPublished = published,
    mrtQualifiedBody = entry.mrtQualifiedBody,
    mrtWanted = entry.mrtWanted,
    mrtOutcome = entry.mrtOutcome,
    mrtRoute = entry.mrtRoute,
    mrtPrerequisites = entry.mrtPrerequisites,
  }

lookupTraceEvidence : EvId -> EvTable -> Option EvVal
lookupTraceEvidence _ [] = None
lookupTraceEvidence goal ((EvEntry candidate value) :: rest) =
  if sameTraceEvId goal candidate then
    Some value
  else
    lookupTraceEvidence goal rest

sameTraceEvId : EvId -> EvId -> Bool
sameTraceEvId (EvId moduleA ordinalA) (EvId moduleB ordinalB) =
  moduleA == moduleB && ordinalA == ordinalB

noteMethodReturnTrace : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodReturnTraceStage ->
  MethodReturnRequest ->
  Option Route ->
  List Route ->
  Unit
noteMethodReturnTrace mctx stage request route prerequisites =
  match mctx.mcGraph.trace
    Some sink =>
      if sink.tsMethodReturnEnabled then
        let (qualifiedBody, wanted) =
          match methodReturnInstantiation mctx request
            Some (Instantiation { body = body, arguments = [InstantiationArgument { wanted = carried, ... }], ... }) =>
              (Some body, Some carried)
            _ => (None, None)
        sink.tsMethodReturnEntries :=
          MethodReturnTraceEntry {
              mrtStage = stage,
              mrtInterface = request.mrrIface,
              mrtMethod = request.mrrName,
              mrtArguments = methodReturnArgs mctx.mcGraph request,
              mrtScope = request.mrrScope,
              mrtOrigin = request.mrrLoc,
              mrtGoal = request.mrrGoalEv,
              mrtPublished = None,
              mrtQualifiedBody = qualifiedBody,
              mrtWanted = wanted,
              mrtOutcome =
                map
                  (resolution => resolution.mrrOutcome)
                  request.mrrResolution.value,
              mrtRoute = route,
              mrtPrerequisites = prerequisites,
            }
            :: sink.tsMethodReturnEntries.value
    None => ()

goalKindName : GoalKind -> String
goalKindName GKReturnSite = "GKReturnSite"
goalKindName GKArgStamp = "GKArgStamp"
goalKindName GKRLocalSite = "GKRLocalSite"
goalKindName GKBinopSite = "GKBinopSite"
goalKindName GKUnopSite = "GKUnopSite"
goalKindName GKArithSite = "GKArithSite"
goalKindName GKDictApp = "GKDictApp"
goalKindName GKMethodDict = "GKMethodDict"
goalKindName GKRecDictApp = "GKRecDictApp"

-- Test visibility (`typecheck_test.mdk`): each goal of [gctx]'s graph that writes a
-- method cell's route or dictionaries, by kind, with whether its `oInner` is that
-- cell's `ecInner`, so the stampers' notes reach the judgment (`judgeCells`).  Read
-- by writing a marker through the goal's refs and looking for it in the cells, then
-- restoring both.  A goal whose destination is no cell's (a throwaway) is skipped.
export
cellGoalInnerAliasing : GraphCtx -> List (String, Bool)
cellGoalInnerAliasing gctx =
  let g = gctx.graphRun
  let cells = cellsFrom g.evCells.value 0 []
  filterMap
    (o =>
      map (c => (goalKindName o.oKind, innerAliases o c)) (cellOfGoal cells o))
    g.goals.value

cellsFrom : Array (Option EvCell) -> Int -> List EvCell -> List EvCell
cellsFrom arr i acc
  | i >= arrayLength arr = reverseL acc
  | otherwise = match arrayGetUnsafe i arr
    Some c => cellsFrom arr (i + 1) (c :: acc)
    None => cellsFrom arr (i + 1) acc

cellOfGoal : List EvCell -> Obligation -> Option EvCell
cellOfGoal cells o = match o.oDest
  EvRoute r =>
    let saved = r.value
    r := RLocal aliasMarker []
    let hit = filterList (c => isAliasMarker c.ecTag.value) cells
    r := saved
    onlyCell hit
  EvRoutes rs =>
    let saved = rs.value
    rs := [RLocal aliasMarker []]
    let hit =
      filterList
        (c => anyList isAliasMarker (c.ecImpl.value ++ c.ecMeth.value))
        cells
    rs := saved
    onlyCell hit

onlyCell : List EvCell -> Option EvCell
onlyCell [c] = Some c
onlyCell _ = None

aliasMarker : String
aliasMarker = "<inner-alias-probe>"

isAliasMarker : Route -> Bool
isAliasMarker (RLocal sym _) = sym == aliasMarker
isAliasMarker _ = False

innerAliases : Obligation -> EvCell -> Bool
innerAliases o c =
  let savedGoal = o.oInner.value
  let savedCell = c.ecInner.value
  c.ecInner := innerNone
  o.oInner := Inner True True
  let hit = match c.ecInner.value
    Inner True True => True
    _ => False
  o.oInner := savedGoal
  c.ecInner := savedCell
  hit

-- Every route a goal carries, in slot order — one for a site, one per slot for
-- a dictionary application.
obligationRoutes : Obligation -> List Route
obligationRoutes o = match o.oDest
  EvRoute r => [r.value]
  EvRoutes rs => rs.value

-- The predicate mono behind each slot, aligned by position with
-- `obligationRoutes`'s answer for the SAME obligation. `GKMethodDict`'s slots
-- carry an `IfaceRef`/`PredicateSlotArgs` pair rather than a `Mono` (#8251), so
-- it answers `None` per slot rather than reconstructing one.
obligationPredicateMonos : Obligation -> List (Option Mono)
obligationPredicateMonos o = match o.oPayload
  GPSite _ m _ => [Some m]
  GPArith m => [Some m]
  GPDictApp app => map Some app.pdaMonos
  GPMethodDict pmd => map (_ => None) pmd.pmdSlots
  GPRecDictApp (RecDictApp _ _ _ m _ _) => [Some m]

routeOutcomeKind : Route -> EvidenceOutcomeKind
routeOutcomeKind RNone = EOKNone
routeOutcomeKind (RKey _ _ _) = EOKInstance
routeOutcomeKind (RDict _) = EOKGiven
routeOutcomeKind (RDictFwd _) = EOKGiven
routeOutcomeKind (RLocal _ _) = EOKLocal
routeOutcomeKind (RScalar _) = EOKScalar
routeOutcomeKind (RProj r _) = routeOutcomeKind r

routeGivenBinder : Route -> Option String
routeGivenBinder (RDict n) = Some n
routeGivenBinder (RDictFwd n) = Some n
routeGivenBinder (RProj r _) = routeGivenBinder r
routeGivenBinder _ = None

routeInstanceKey : Route -> Option String
routeInstanceKey (RKey k _ _) = Some k
routeInstanceKey _ = None

-- The nested route list an `RKey`/`RLocal` packs at this slot: the packed
-- `requires`, exactly as `entailInst` produces them.
routePrerequisiteRoutes : Route -> List Route
routePrerequisiteRoutes (RKey _ rs _) = rs
routePrerequisiteRoutes (RLocal _ rs) = rs
routePrerequisiteRoutes _ = []

renderRouteIdentity : Route -> String
renderRouteIdentity RNone = "RNone"
renderRouteIdentity (RKey k _ _) = "RKey " ++ k
renderRouteIdentity (RDict n) = "RDict " ++ n
renderRouteIdentity (RDictFwd n) = "RDictFwd " ++ n
renderRouteIdentity (RLocal n _) = "RLocal " ++ n
renderRouteIdentity (RScalar n) = "RScalar " ++ n
renderRouteIdentity (RProj r path) =
  "RProj (\{renderRouteIdentity r}) \{joinWith "." (map intToString path)}"

noteEvidenceObservation : GraphCtx -> Obligation -> Unit
noteEvidenceObservation gctx o = match gctx.trace
  Some sink =>
    if sink.tsEvidenceObservationEnabled then
      let routes = obligationRoutes o
      let predicates = obligationPredicateMonos o
      let arity = listLen routes
      sink.tsEvidenceObservationEntries :=
        evidenceObservationEntriesGo o routes predicates arity 0
          ++ sink.tsEvidenceObservationEntries.value
  None => ()

evidenceObservationEntriesGo : Obligation ->
  List Route ->
  List (Option Mono) ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List EvidenceObservationEntry
evidenceObservationEntriesGo _ [] _ _ _ = []
evidenceObservationEntriesGo o (r :: rs) preds arity slot =
  let (predHere, predsRest) = match preds
    p :: ptail => (p, ptail)
    [] => (None, [])
  EvidenceObservationEntry {
      eoeEv = o.oEv,
      eoeGoalKind = goalKindName o.oKind,
      eoeSlot = slot,
      eoeArity = arity,
      eoePredicate = map ppMono predHere,
      eoeOutcome = routeOutcomeKind r,
      eoeGivenBinder = routeGivenBinder r,
      eoeInstanceKey = routeInstanceKey r,
      eoePrerequisites = map renderRouteIdentity (routePrerequisiteRoutes r),
      eoeScope = o.oScope,
    }
    :: evidenceObservationEntriesGo o rs predsRest arity (slot + 1)

noteNumericPredicateTrace : GraphCtx ->
  NumericPredicateTraceStage ->
  ClassPredicate ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option Loc ->
  Option IfaceRef ->
  Option Route ->
  List Route ->
  Unit
noteNumericPredicateTrace gctx stage predicate scope origin selected route prereqs =
  match gctx.trace
    Some sink =>
      if sink.tsNumericPredicateEnabled then
        sink.tsNumericPredicateEntries :=
          NumericPredicateTraceEntry {
              nptStage = stage,
              nptPredicate = predicate,
              nptScope = scope,
              nptOrigin = origin,
              nptSelectedInterface = selected,
              nptRoute = route,
              nptPrerequisites = prereqs,
            }
            :: sink.tsNumericPredicateEntries.value
    None => ()

-- Whether this drive traces numeric predicates; reads the sink in place.
numericPredicateTraceOn : GraphCtx -> Unit -> Bool
numericPredicateTraceOn gctx _ = match gctx.trace
  Some sink => sink.tsNumericPredicateEnabled
  None => False

assumAnswerBinder : AssumAnswer -> EvidenceBinderId
assumAnswerBinder (SemanticGiven evidence) = givenEvidenceBinder evidence
assumAnswerBinder (LegacyScalar binder) = binder
assumAnswerBinder (LegacyPredicate binder) = binder
assumAnswerBinder (LegacyProjected binder _) = binder

-- The evidence an assumption answer denotes.  A legacy answer has no semantic evidence
-- beyond the binder it routes through.
assumAnswerEvidence : AssumAnswer -> SolverEvidence
assumAnswerEvidence (SemanticGiven evidence) = evidence
assumAnswerEvidence (LegacyScalar binder) = GivenEvidence binder
assumAnswerEvidence (LegacyPredicate binder) = GivenEvidence binder
assumAnswerEvidence (LegacyProjected binder path) =
  SuperclassEvidence binder path

assumAnswerKind : AssumAnswer -> AssumptionTraceKind
assumAnswerKind (SemanticGiven (SuperclassEvidence _ _)) =
  ATSuperclassProjection
assumAnswerKind (SemanticGiven _) = ATDirectPredicate
assumAnswerKind (LegacyScalar _) = ATLegacyScalar
assumAnswerKind (LegacyPredicate _) = ATLegacyPredicate
assumAnswerKind (LegacyProjected _ _) = ATLegacyPredicate

-- The dict parameter that carries given-rooted evidence.  A superclass projection of a
-- given reads its parent's parameter: the super is a field of that dictionary
-- (`givenEvidenceRoute`), never selected again.
givenEvidenceBinder : SolverEvidence -> EvidenceBinderId
givenEvidenceBinder (GivenEvidence binder) = binder
givenEvidenceBinder (SuperclassEvidence parent _) = parent
givenEvidenceBinder _ = panic "non-given assumption evidence"

-- The route an assumption answer lowers to, reading its binder's parameter as
-- [paramRoute] renders it: a projection answer projects the parameter's dictionary
-- onto the super.  A scalar answer (a tyvar-keyed rung, which cannot say which
-- predicate it answered) whose binder's own predicate is a SUB-interface of the
-- goal's [goalIface] is projected the same way, along the first superclass path from
-- the binder's interface to the goal's.
assumAnswerRoute : GraphCtx ->
  AssumAnswer ->
  Option IfaceRef ->
  ScopeId ->
  (String -> Route) ->
  Route
assumAnswerRoute gctx (SemanticGiven (SuperclassEvidence parent path)) _ _ paramRoute =
  RProj (paramRoute (renderEvidenceBinder gctx parent)) path
assumAnswerRoute gctx (LegacyProjected parent path) _ _ paramRoute =
  RProj (paramRoute (renderEvidenceBinder gctx parent)) path
assumAnswerRoute gctx (LegacyScalar binder) (Some goalIface) useScope paramRoute =
  let base = paramRoute (renderEvidenceBinder gctx binder)
  match scalarGivenProjection gctx binder goalIface useScope
    Some path => RProj base path
    None => base
assumAnswerRoute gctx answer _ _ paramRoute =
  paramRoute (renderEvidenceBinder gctx (assumAnswerBinder answer))

-- The direct-super path from the predicate [binder] declares to [goalIface], when the
-- two differ.  Matched by spelling: a goal from a bare-named producer carries no
-- origin, and within one interface's superclass closure a spelling names one node.
scalarGivenProjection : GraphCtx ->
  EvidenceBinderId ->
  IfaceRef ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option (List Int)
scalarGivenProjection gctx binder goalIface useScope =
  match directGivenIfaceOf binder (givensForScope gctx useScope)
    None => None
    Some declared =>
      if declared.irName == goalIface.irName then
        None
      else
        map
          (n => drop 1 n.superPath)
          (find
            (n => n.superIface.irName == goalIface.irName)
            (superClosure
              (superLookup gctx)
              (_ _ _ => Some ())
              (ir _ => regKeyRender (regKeyOfTab (oblIfaceKey ir)))
              [(declared, ())]))

-- Whether the tyvar-keyed binder [binder] can answer a goal of [goalIface]: its own
-- predicate is the goal's interface or has it as a superclass.  A binder with no
-- recorded direct given, or a goal with no interface, is not constrained here.  The
-- interfaces compare by declaration identity; a goal still carrying no origin (the
-- #1318 residual, #3534) can only be compared by spelling.
scalarGivenAnswers : GraphCtx -> EvidenceBinderId -> IfaceRef -> ScopeId -> Bool
scalarGivenAnswers gctx binder goalIface useScope =
  goalIface.irName == ""
    || (match directGivenIfaceOf binder (givensForScope gctx useScope)
      None => True
      Some declared =>
        sameIfaceOrUnresolved declared goalIface
          || isSome (scalarGivenProjection gctx binder goalIface useScope))

sameIfaceOrUnresolved : IfaceRef -> IfaceRef -> Bool
sameIfaceOrUnresolved a b = match (a.irOrigin, b.irOrigin)
  (OriginUnresolved, _) => a.irName == b.irName
  (_, OriginUnresolved) => a.irName == b.irName
  _ => sameIfaceDecl a b

directGivenIfaceOf : EvidenceBinderId -> List GivenEntry -> Option IfaceRef
directGivenIfaceOf _ [] = None
directGivenIfaceOf binder (g :: rest)
  | g.geBinder == binder && g.geProvenance == DirectGiven =
    Some g.geSlot.psIface
  | otherwise = directGivenIfaceOf binder rest

projectedGivenOf : GraphCtx -> EvidenceBinderId -> List Int -> Option GivenEntry
projectedGivenOf gctx parent path =
  find
    (g => g.geProvenance == ProjectedGiven parent path)
    (givensForScope gctx (Scopes.binderScope parent))

noteAssumption : GraphCtx -> ScopeId -> AssumAnswer -> Unit
noteAssumption gctx scope answer = match gctx.trace
  Some sink =>
    if sink.tsAssumptionEnabled then
      sink.tsAssumptionEntries :=
        AssumptionTraceEntry {
            atGoalScope = scope,
            atBinder = assumAnswerBinder answer,
            atKind = assumAnswerKind answer,
          }
          :: sink.tsAssumptionEntries.value
  None => ()

openScope : ModuleCtx -> ScopeId -> Unit
openScope mctx sid = mctx.mcCells.currentScope := Scopes.openScopeCursor sid

closeScope : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> Unit
closeScope mctx _ =
  mctx.mcCells.currentScope :=
    Scopes.closeScopeCursor
      (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
      mctx.mcCells.currentScope.value

-- #2705: mint the cells for one `EMethodAt` node and return the id the node
-- carries.  [seed] is the pre-pass seed (the mangled definer-shadow symbol, or
-- ""): a non-empty seed becomes the `RLocal <seed> []` fallback the stampers and
-- every seed reader (`routeLocalSym`) expect to find on the dispatch cell.
mintMethodCell : ModuleCtx -> String -> EvId
mintMethodCell mctx seed =
  mintMethodCellRaw
    mctx
    ""
    None
    (if seed == "" then RNone else RLocal seed [])
    []

-- The `dictPass` mints: a node constructed AFTER the drain, from a route another
-- node already solved, so its cells start at their final values.  The entry is
-- recorded in [pe] as well: the index the pass reads was taken before the node
-- existed.
mintMethodCellWith : ModuleCtx ->
  PassEvidence ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Route ->
  List Route ->
  EvId
mintMethodCellWith mctx (PassEvidence _ minted) iface arity tag impls =
  let ev = mintMethodCellRaw mctx iface (Some arity) tag impls
  minted :=
    omInsert
      (intToString (evOrdinal ev))
      (EvMethod iface arity tag impls [])
      minted.value
  ev

mintMethodCellRaw : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  Option Int ->
  Route ->
  List Route ->
  EvId
mintMethodCellRaw mctx iface arity tag impls =
  let ev = freshEvId mctx ()
  let g = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun
  let i = evOrdinal ev - g.evBase
  let arr = indexWithSlot g.evCells i
  -- An occupied slot would mean two nodes minted under one ordinal — the same
  -- collision `fillEvidence` refuses at publish time — and a memo restore that
  -- rewound the counter without rewinding this index is the one way to reach it.
  -- Fail closed here, where the second mint happens, rather than at publish.
  let _ = match arrayGetUnsafe i arr
    None => ()
    Some _ => panic "method cell #\{intToString (evOrdinal ev)} minted twice"
  let _ =
    arraySetUnsafe
      i
      (Some EvCell {
        ecId = ev,
        ecIface = Ref iface,
        ecArity = Ref arity,
        ecTag = Ref tag,
        ecImpl = Ref impls,
        ecMeth = Ref [],
        ecLoc = Ref None,
        ecName = Ref "",
        ecInner = Ref innerNone,
      })
      arr
  ev

evOrdinal : EvId -> Int
evOrdinal (EvId _ i) = i

-- The array [index] holds, grown by doubling until slot [i] exists.
indexWithSlot : Ref (Array (Option a)) -> Int -> Array (Option a)
indexWithSlot index i =
  let arr0 = index.value
  if i < arrayLength arr0 then
    arr0
  else
    let grown = arrayMake (max 16 (2 * (i + 1))) None
    let _ = arrayBlit arr0 0 grown 0 (arrayLength arr0)
    index := grown
    grown

-- Mint the cell for one operator site, starting unrouted, and return its id.
mintOpSite : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> EvId
mintOpSite mctx _ = mintSite mctx (OpSite (Ref RNone))

-- Mint the cells for one numeric literal site: an unset float and an unrouted
-- `fromInt` route.
mintLitSite : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> EvId
mintLitSite mctx _ = mintSite mctx (LitSite (Ref None) (Ref RNone))

-- Mint the cell for one field access or record update, starting with the unknown
-- head "".
mintHeadSite : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> EvId
mintHeadSite mctx _ = mintSite mctx (HeadSite (Ref ""))

-- [ev] if it already has a site, else a freshly minted one: a body re-marked after
-- inference keeps the ids inference wrote through.
mintedOr : (Unit -> EvId) -> EvId -> EvId
mintedOr mint ev = if isUnminted ev then mint () else ev

mintSite : ModuleCtx -> SiteCell -> EvId
mintSite mctx cell =
  let ev = freshEvId mctx ()
  let g = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun
  let i = evOrdinal ev - g.evBase
  let arr = indexWithSlot g.siteCells i
  let _ = match arrayGetUnsafe i arr
    None => arraySetUnsafe i (Some (ev, cell)) arr
    Some _ => panic "site cell #\{intToString (evOrdinal ev)} minted twice"
  ev

-- The cell minted for site [ev].  Inference reaching a site the mark pass never
-- visited is a gap in marking coverage, so it panics rather than writing a cell no
-- reader would find.
siteCellOf : GraphCtx -> EvId -> SiteCell
siteCellOf gctx ev = match siteCellLookup gctx ev
  Ok c => c
  Err message => panic message

-- `siteCellOf`'s answer, or the reason it has none.
siteCellLookup : GraphCtx -> EvId -> Result String SiteCell
siteCellLookup gctx ev =
  let (EvId m n) = ev
  let g = gctx.graphRun
  let i = n - g.evBase
  let arr = g.siteCells.value
  if isUnminted ev then
    Err "site reached inference unminted"
  else if i < 0 then
    Err "site cell \{m}#\{intToString n} is from an earlier graph"
  else if i >= arrayLength arr then
    Err "site cell \{m}#\{intToString n} was never minted"
  else match arrayGetUnsafe i arr
    Some (_, c) => Ok c
    None => Err "site cell \{m}#\{intToString n} was never minted"

-- The route cell of operator or literal site [ev].
siteRouteCell : GraphCtx -> EvId -> Ref Route
siteRouteCell gctx ev = match siteCellOf gctx ev
  OpSite r => r
  LitSite _ r => r
  HeadSite _ => notAnOpSite ev

-- The resolved-record-head cell of field access or record update site [ev].
siteHeadCell : GraphCtx -> EvId -> Ref String
siteHeadCell gctx ev = match siteCellOf gctx ev
  HeadSite h => h
  OpSite _ => notAnOpSite ev
  LitSite _ _ => notAnOpSite ev

-- The defaulted-float cell of numeric literal site [ev].
siteFloatCell : GraphCtx -> EvId -> Ref (Option Float)
siteFloatCell gctx ev = match siteCellOf gctx ev
  LitSite f _ => f
  OpSite _ => notAnOpSite ev
  HeadSite _ => notAnOpSite ev

notAnOpSite : EvId -> a
notAnOpSite ev =
  panic
    "site cell \{evIdModule ev}#\{intToString (evOrdinal ev)} is not an operator site"

-- The cells minted for [ev].  A miss is a bug in this file (every `EMethodAt` is
-- minted through `mintMethodCell`), so it panics rather than answering unrouted.
methodCellOf : GraphCtx -> EvId -> EvCell
methodCellOf gctx ev = match methodCellLookup gctx ev
  Ok c => c
  Err message => panic message

-- `methodCellOf`'s answer, or the reason it has none.
methodCellLookup : GraphCtx -> EvId -> Result String EvCell
methodCellLookup gctx (EvId m n) =
  let g = gctx.graphRun
  let i = n - g.evBase
  let arr = g.evCells.value
  if i < 0 then
    Err "method cell \{m}#\{intToString n} is from an earlier graph"
  else if i >= arrayLength arr then
    Err "method cell \{m}#\{intToString n} was never minted"
  else match arrayGetUnsafe i arr
    Some c => Ok c
    None => Err "method cell \{m}#\{intToString n} was never minted"

-- Test visibility (`typecheck_test.mdk`): why [gctx]'s site and method cell stores
-- hold no cell for [ev], each "" where one does.
export
cellStoreMisses : GraphCtx -> EvId -> (String, String)
cellStoreMisses gctx ev = (
  missText (siteCellLookup gctx ev),
  missText (methodCellLookup gctx ev),
)

missText : Result String a -> String
missText (Ok _) = ""
missText (Err message) = message

-- The whole evidence table of this graph: one entry per method occurrence and per
-- minted site, plus the per-goal entries the drain recorded and the entries of the
-- modules a tree drive served (`applyModuleTrees`).
drivenEvidence : GraphCtx -> Unit -> EvTable
drivenEvidence gctx _ =
  cellEntriesFrom gctx.graphRun gctx.graphRun.evBase
    ++ gctx.graphRun.evTable.value

-- #2549 M2: the next evidence id for the module currently being inferred.  The
-- module component comes from the module's record, which `checkBodyImpl` mints once per
-- module before any body of it is inferred; the ordinal is this run's counter.
-- `evCounter` is graph-global, and `graphLineageRun` carries it across every new
-- lineage, so the ordinal alone is what makes an id unique; the module half does not
-- scope it, and `evDictRoutesIn` indexes on the ordinal without consulting it.
-- The module half is a tripwire for that lookup (see `EvId` in `frontend/ast.mdk`):
-- do not make ordinals per-module in the belief that the pair still separates them.
freshEvId : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> EvId
freshEvId mctx _ =
  let g = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun
  let n = g.evCounter.value
  g.evCounter := n + 1
  EvId mctx.mcCells.currentModuleRef.value n

sealMethodReturnGoals : GraphCtx ->
  EvTable ->
  List Obligation ->
  (List Obligation, List MethodReturnMemoView)
sealMethodReturnGoals gctx evidence goals =
  sealMethodReturnGoalsFrom gctx evidence (reverseL goals) ([], [])

-- Walks the goals last to first so each result list is built in input order, with
-- no recursion before the cons: the goal list of a program that imports `async` is
-- long enough to overflow the baseline-tier wasm stack in a browser worker.
sealMethodReturnGoalsFrom : GraphCtx ->
  EvTable ->
  List Obligation ->
  (List Obligation, List MethodReturnMemoView) ->
  (List Obligation, List MethodReturnMemoView)
sealMethodReturnGoalsFrom gctx _ [] acc = acc
sealMethodReturnGoalsFrom gctx evidence (goal :: rest) (goals, views) =
  match exactReturnRequestOfGoal goal
    Some request => sealMethodReturnGoalsFrom gctx evidence rest (
      goals,
      methodReturnMemoView gctx evidence goal request :: views,
    )
    None => sealMethodReturnGoalsFrom gctx evidence rest (goal :: goals, views)

methodReturnMemoView : GraphCtx ->
  EvTable ->
  Obligation ->
  MethodReturnRequest ->
  MethodReturnMemoView
methodReturnMemoView gctx evidence goal request =
  let (outcome, prerequisites) = match request.mrrResolution.value
    None => ("legacy", [])
    Some resolution => (
      methodReturnMemoOutcome resolution.mrrOutcome,
      methodReturnMemoPrerequisites resolution.mrrOutcome,
    )
  MethodReturnMemoView {
    mrmvInterface = methodReturnMemoIface request.mrrIface,
    mrmvMethod = request.mrrName,
    mrmvArguments =
      map methodReturnMemoArguments (methodReturnArgs gctx request),
    mrmvOutcome = outcome,
    mrmvPrerequisites = prerequisites,
    mrmvEvidence = methodReturnMemoEvidence goal.oEv evidence,
  }

methodReturnMemoArguments : List Mono -> List String
methodReturnMemoArguments arguments = map ppMono arguments

methodReturnMemoIface : IfaceRef -> String
methodReturnMemoIface iface =
  let identity = ifaceIdentity iface.irOrigin iface.irName
  if identity == "" then iface.irName else identity

methodReturnMemoOutcome : SolverOutcome -> String
methodReturnMemoOutcome (Solved (GivenEvidence _)) = "given"
methodReturnMemoOutcome (Solved (InstanceEvidence _ _ _ _)) = "instance"
methodReturnMemoOutcome (Solved (SuperclassEvidence _ _)) = "superclass"
methodReturnMemoOutcome (Deferred _ _) = "deferred"
methodReturnMemoOutcome (Insoluble _ MissingInstance) = "missing"
methodReturnMemoOutcome (Insoluble _ (AmbiguousInstances _)) = "ambiguous"
methodReturnMemoOutcome (Insoluble _ (ResolutionCycle _)) = "cycle"

methodReturnMemoPrerequisites : SolverOutcome -> List (String, List String)
methodReturnMemoPrerequisites (Solved (InstanceEvidence _ _ prerequisites _)) =
  map
    (prerequisite => (
      methodReturnMemoIface prerequisite.prerequisiteInterface,
      map ppMono prerequisite.prerequisiteArguments,
    ))
    prerequisites
methodReturnMemoPrerequisites _ = []

methodReturnMemoEvidence : EvId -> EvTable -> String
methodReturnMemoEvidence goal evidence = match lookupTraceEvidence goal evidence
  Some (EvOne route) => methodReturnMemoRoute route
  Some (EvMany routes) => joinWith "," (map methodReturnMemoRoute routes)
  Some (EvLit _ route) => methodReturnMemoRoute route
  Some (EvHead head) => "head:\{head}"
  None => "unpublished"

methodReturnMemoRoute : Route -> String
methodReturnMemoRoute RNone = "none"
methodReturnMemoRoute (RKey key prerequisites supers) =
  "key:\{key}[\{joinWith "," (map methodReturnMemoRoute prerequisites)}]\{methodReturnMemoSupers supers}"
methodReturnMemoRoute (RDict name) = "given:\{name}"
methodReturnMemoRoute (RDictFwd name) = "forwarded:\{name}"
methodReturnMemoRoute (RLocal name _) = "local:\{name}"
methodReturnMemoRoute (RScalar name) = "scalar:\{name}"
methodReturnMemoRoute (RProj r path) =
  "projected:\{methodReturnMemoRoute r}.\{joinWith "." (map intToString path)}"

methodReturnMemoSupers : List Route -> String
methodReturnMemoSupers [] = ""
methodReturnMemoSupers supers =
  "{\{joinWith "," (map methodReturnMemoRoute supers)}}"

-- #2547 unit 3: the givens of [sid]'s module.  The module id is the scope frame's,
-- minted with the frame, so a replayed or restored scope keeps its key with it.
givensForScope : GraphCtx -> ScopeId -> List GivenEntry
givensForScope gctx sid =
  optionOr
    []
    (omLookup
      (Scopes.scopeFrame (currentScopeStore gctx ()) sid).sfModuleId
      gctx.graphRun.gGiven.value)

-- The ONE given write.  Newest first, as both retired tables were, so every reader's
-- first-match order is the write order it had before.
pushGiven : GraphCtx ->
  GivenMatch ->
  GivenProvenance ->
  PredicateSlot ->
  EvidenceBinderId ->
  Unit
pushGiven gctx gm provenance slot binder =
  let mid =
    (Scopes.scopeFrame
      (currentScopeStore gctx ())
      (Scopes.binderScope binder)).sfModuleId
  let entry = GivenEntry {
    geSlot = slot,
    geBinder = binder,
    geMatch = gm,
    geProvenance = provenance,
  }
  gctx.graphRun.gGiven :=
    omInsert
      mid
      (entry :: optionOr [] (omLookup mid gctx.graphRun.gGiven.value))
      gctx.graphRun.gGiven.value

givenInScope : GivenScope -> GivenEntry -> Bool
givenInScope GSPredicateOnly g = match g.geMatch
  GMPredicate => True
  GMIdWitnessed => False
givenInScope GSImplRequires g = match g.geMatch
  GMIdWitnessed => True
  GMPredicate => False

-- Each channel's length as this module begins.
graphMarksNow : GraphCtx -> Unit -> GraphMarks
graphMarksNow gctx _ = GraphMarks {
  mGoals = gctx.graphRun.goalsN.value,
  mNumlit = gctx.graphRun.numlitN.value,
}

recordModuleStart : GraphCtx -> String -> Unit
recordModuleStart gctx mid =
  gctx.graphRun.moduleRanges :=
    (mid, graphMarksNow gctx ()) :: gctx.graphRun.moduleRanges.value

-- The marks of the module being processed (the head of `moduleRanges`); all zeros
-- before any module started, which is the whole graph.
currentModuleMarks : GraphCtx -> Unit -> GraphMarks
currentModuleMarks gctx _ = match gctx.graphRun.moduleRanges.value
  (_, m) :: _ => m
  [] => GraphMarks { mGoals = 0, mNumlit = 0 }

-- the numeric-literal channel's window, the counterpart of `goalsSince`
numlitSince : GraphCtx -> Int -> List (Mono, Ref (Option Float), Int, Ref Route)
numlitSince gctx mark =
  moduleWindow gctx.graphRun.numlitN.value mark gctx.graphRun.numlitRefs.value

-- The ONE numlit write, so the channel and its counter cannot drift apart.
pushNumlit : GraphCtx -> (Mono, Ref (Option Float), Int, Ref Route) -> Unit
pushNumlit gctx e =
  let g = gctx.graphRun
  g.numlitRefs := e :: g.numlitRefs.value
  g.numlitN := g.numlitN.value + 1

idSetInsertAll : List Int -> Map Int Unit -> Map Int Unit
idSetInsertAll [] m = m
idSetInsertAll (i :: rest) m = idSetInsertAll rest (IdMap.set i () m)

-- How many non-shrinking `requires` steps one walk may take (DICT-SEMANTICS §3 W2).
-- Only a context that does not shrink its goal (`impl C (T a) requires C (T (T a))`)
-- spends this, so the constant bounds divergence without bounding the depth of a
-- shrinking chain.  It is named in `requiresDepthMsg`, so changing it changes
-- user-visible text.
requiresNonShrinkingFuel : Int
requiresNonShrinkingFuel = 32

newWalkMemo : Unit -> WalkMemo
newWalkMemo _ = WalkMemo {
  wmRoutes = Ref omEmpty,
  wmDischarged = Ref omEmpty,
  wmCuts = Ref 0,
  wmSolved = Ref omEmpty,
  wmFollowed = Ref omEmpty,
  wmStopped = Ref False,
}

-- A walk whose seed is the goal [iface] [args].
reqWalkSeed : IfaceRef -> List Mono -> ReqWalk
reqWalkSeed iface args =
  ReqWalk
    [(iface, args, monoSizes args)]
    requiresNonShrinkingFuel
    (newWalkMemo ())

-- A walk with no goal on it yet: the first goal entered is its seed.
reqWalkStart : Unit -> ReqWalk
reqWalkStart _ = ReqWalk [] requiresNonShrinkingFuel (newWalkMemo ())

reqWalkEnter : ReqWalk -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> ReqStep
reqWalkEnter (ReqWalk path fuel memo) iface args =
  let size = monoSizes args
  match path
    [] => ReqOn (ReqWalk [(iface, args, size)] fuel memo)
    (parentIface, parentArgs, parentSize) :: _ =>
      if anyListM (sameWalkGoal iface args size) path then
        ReqCycle parentIface parentArgs iface args
      else if size < parentSize then
        ReqOn (ReqWalk ((iface, args, size) :: path) fuel memo)
      else if fuel <= 0 then
        ReqDeep iface args
      else
        ReqOn (ReqWalk ((iface, args, size) :: path) (fuel - 1) memo)

-- The memo bucket of the goal [walk] has just entered, the head of its path: that
-- goal's interface spelling and size and the fuel left.  Goals that are one goal by
-- `sameWalkGoal` share a bucket; a bucket may also hold goals that are not, so every
-- hit is confirmed against the goal itself: `walkGoalSame` for the solved and followed
-- tables, `sameIfaceDecl` and `monoVecSameGiven` for the rest.
enteredGoalKey : ReqWalk -> String
enteredGoalKey (ReqWalk ((iface, _, size) :: _) fuel _) =
  let name = iface.irName
  "\{name}#\{intToString size}#\{intToString fuel}"
enteredGoalKey (ReqWalk [] fuel _) = "#\{intToString fuel}"

reqWalkMemo : ReqWalk -> WalkMemo
reqWalkMemo (ReqWalk _ _ memo) = memo

-- The route walk below the goal [row]'s `requires` discharge at [goals], which [walk]
-- has just entered: the recorded routes if this walk already built them, otherwise
-- [follow]'s, recorded when they came out clean.
routeWalkMemoized : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List Mono ->
  ImplRow ->
  ReqWalk ->
  (SiteCtx -> List Route) ->
  List Route
routeWalkMemoized sx encl useScope goals row walk follow =
  let memo = reqWalkMemo walk
  let iface = ieRowIface row
  let key = enteredGoalKey walk
  let entries = optionOr [] (omLookup key memo.wmRoutes.value)
  match routeWalkRecorded iface goals row encl useScope entries
    Some entry =>
      let _ = noteInner sx entry.rweInner
      entry.rweRoutes
    None =>
      let cutsBefore = memo.wmCuts.value
      let acc = Ref innerNone
      let (erred, routes) =
        erredDuring sx.sxModule (_ => follow { sx | sxInner = Some acc })
      let inner = acc.value
      let _ = noteInner sx inner
      let _ =
        if erred || memo.wmCuts.value /= cutsBefore then
          ()
        else
          let entry = RouteWalkEntry {
            rweIface = iface,
            rweGoals = goals,
            rweRow = row,
            rweEncl = encl,
            rweScope = useScope,
            rweRoutes = routes,
            rweInner = inner,
          }
          memo.wmRoutes :=
            omInsert
              key
              (entry :: optionOr [] (omLookup key memo.wmRoutes.value))
              memo.wmRoutes.value
      routes

routeWalkRecorded : IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  ImplRow ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List RouteWalkEntry ->
  Option RouteWalkEntry
routeWalkRecorded _ _ _ _ _ [] = None
routeWalkRecorded iface goals row encl useScope (entry :: rest) =
  if entry.rweEncl == encl
    && entry.rweScope == useScope
    && sameIfaceDecl entry.rweIface iface
    && monoVecSameGiven entry.rweGoals goals
    && rowRouteKey entry.rweRow == rowRouteKey row then
    Some entry
  else
    routeWalkRecorded iface goals row encl useScope rest

-- What the stamper running now has built below its destination's top level.  The
-- three producers of the routes inside a dictionary (`argReqRoute`, `superRouteAt`,
-- `undeterminedRowRoute`'s supers) note each route they return, so a sub-route the
-- solver shares between paths is noted once, where it is built.
noteInner : SiteCtx -> Inner -> Unit
noteInner sx inner = match sx.sxInner
  Some acc => acc := innerOr acc.value inner
  None => ()

-- [r], noted as a route inside a dictionary.
noteInnerRoute : SiteCtx -> Route -> Route
noteInnerRoute sx r =
  let _ = noteInner sx (innerOfRoute r)
  r

-- A route walk's cut, counted so no subtree containing one is recorded.
noteRouteWalkCut : ReqWalk -> Unit
noteRouteWalkCut walk =
  let memo = reqWalkMemo walk
  memo.wmCuts := memo.wmCuts.value + 1

-- Has the obligation walk [walk] already checked goal [iface] [args], entered with
-- the fuel [walk] has left, without an error?
walkGoalDischarged : ReqWalk -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Bool
walkGoalDischarged walk iface args =
  let memo = reqWalkMemo walk
  anyListM
    ((otherIface, otherArgs) =>
      sameIfaceDecl otherIface iface && monoVecSameGiven otherArgs args)
    (optionOr [] (omLookup (enteredGoalKey walk) memo.wmDischarged.value))

noteWalkGoalDischarged : ReqWalk -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Unit
noteWalkGoalDischarged walk iface args =
  let memo = reqWalkMemo walk
  let key = enteredGoalKey walk
  memo.wmDischarged :=
    omInsert
      key
      ((iface, args) :: optionOr [] (omLookup key memo.wmDischarged.value))
      memo.wmDischarged.value

-- The residuals [solve] finds below the goal [iface] [args], which [walk] has just
-- entered: the recorded ones if this walk already solved that goal, otherwise
-- [solve]'s, deduplicated and recorded when they came out clean.  Deduplicating
-- keeps the first occurrence of each goal, so a goal the walk reaches along many
-- paths is one residual and the result stays as large as the distinct goals.
solvedOnWalk : ModuleCtx ->
  ReqWalk ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  (Unit -> List (IfaceRef, List Mono)) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
solvedOnWalk mctx walk iface args solve =
  let memo = reqWalkMemo walk
  let key = enteredGoalKey walk
  let entries = optionOr [] (omLookup key memo.wmSolved.value)
  match filterList (e => walkGoalSame e.sgeIface e.sgeGoals iface args) entries
    entry :: _ => entry.sgeResiduals
    [] =>
      let (clean, found) = solvedCleanly mctx (goals => flatMap snd goals) solve
      let residuals = dedupWalkGoals found
      let _ =
        if clean then
          let entry = SolvedGoalEntry {
            sgeIface = iface,
            sgeGoals = args,
            sgeResiduals = residuals,
          }
          memo.wmSolved :=
            omInsert
              key
              (entry :: optionOr [] (omLookup key memo.wmSolved.value))
              memo.wmSolved.value
      residuals

-- Runs [act] and says whether its result can stand for running it again: it
-- detected no error (`erredDuring`), and no type or effect variable it minted is in
-- the types [monosOf] reads off the result.  A second run would mint fresh ones in
-- their place.  Variables minted only to test a unification do not reach the result.
solvedCleanly : ModuleCtx -> (a -> List Mono) -> (Unit -> a) -> (Bool, a)
solvedCleanly mctx monosOf act =
  let tyvars = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.tyvarCounter.value
  let effvars = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.effvarCounter.value
  let (erred, result) = erredDuring mctx act
  (
    not erred && allList (monoMintedBefore tyvars effvars) (monosOf result),
    result,
  )

-- [goals] with each goal kept at its first occurrence (`walkGoalSame`).
dedupWalkGoals : List (IfaceRef, List Mono) -> List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
dedupWalkGoals goals = dedupWalkGoalsGo goals omEmpty []

dedupWalkGoalsGo : List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  OrdMap (List (IfaceRef, List Mono)) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
dedupWalkGoalsGo [] _ acc = reverseL acc
dedupWalkGoalsGo ((iface, args) :: rest) seen acc =
  let key = "\{iface.irName}#\{intToString (monoSizes args)}"
  let bucket = optionOr [] (omLookup key seen)
  if anyListM (g => walkGoalSame (fst g) (snd g) iface args) bucket then
    dedupWalkGoalsGo rest seen acc
  else
    dedupWalkGoalsGo
      rest
      (omInsert key ((iface, args) :: bucket) seen)
      ((iface, args) :: acc)

-- Has the prerequisite walk [walk] already followed the goal [iface] [args] it has
-- just entered?
walkGoalFollowed : ReqWalk -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Bool
walkGoalFollowed walk iface args =
  let memo = reqWalkMemo walk
  anyListM
    ((otherIface, otherArgs) => walkGoalSame otherIface otherArgs iface args)
    (optionOr [] (omLookup (enteredGoalKey walk) memo.wmFollowed.value))

noteWalkGoalFollowed : ReqWalk -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Unit
noteWalkGoalFollowed walk iface args =
  let memo = reqWalkMemo walk
  let key = enteredGoalKey walk
  memo.wmFollowed :=
    omInsert
      key
      ((iface, args) :: optionOr [] (omLookup key memo.wmFollowed.value))
      memo.wmFollowed.value

-- Two goals are one entry of a solving walk's memo when they are one predicate
-- (`monoVecSameGiven`) with the same effect rows and authorities as well.  A recorded
-- residual is built from its goal's own types, and `monoSameGiven` equates every row,
-- so a goal that differs only in a row must not be answered by another's entry.
walkGoalSame : IfaceRef -> List Mono -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Bool
