walkGoalSame iface args otherIface otherArgs =
  sameIfaceDecl iface otherIface && walkMonosSame args otherArgs

-- Private probe for the memo's goal equality: two goals `C (Int -> Int)` whose arrows
-- carry different effect rows are one predicate to `monoVecSameGiven` and two to
-- `walkGoalSame`, in either order; the same row is one goal to both.
export
walkGoalSameProbe : Unit -> List Bool
walkGoalSameProbe _ =
  let iface = ifaceRefBare "C"
  let int = tconBuiltin "Int"
  let mctx = initialModuleCtx (probeGraphCtx ())
  let row1 = EffRow [] (Some (freshEffvar mctx ()))
  let row2 = EffRow [] (Some (freshEffvar mctx ()))
  let goal1 = [TFun int row1 int]
  let goal2 = [TFun int row2 int]
  [
    monoVecSameGiven goal1 goal2,
    monoVecSameGiven goal2 goal1,
    walkGoalSame iface goal1 iface goal2,
    walkGoalSame iface goal2 iface goal1,
    walkGoalSame iface goal1 iface [TFun int row1 int],
  ]

-- Two goals are one goal when their interface is the same declaration and their
-- argument vectors are pointwise identical (`monoVecSameGiven`); equal sizes are
-- necessary, so they are compared first.
sameWalkGoal : IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Int ->
  (IfaceRef, List Mono, Int) ->
  Bool
sameWalkGoal iface args size (otherIface, otherArgs, otherSize) =
  otherSize == size
    && sameIfaceDecl otherIface iface
    && monoVecSameGiven otherArgs args

-- A solving walk's step, reported at the goal's site when the walk cannot continue:
-- `T-REQUIRES-CYCLE` for a repeated goal, `T-REQUIRES-DEPTH` for spent fuel.
reqWalkReported : ModuleCtx -> Option Loc -> ReqStep -> Option ReqWalk
reqWalkReported mctx _ (ReqOn walk) = Some walk
reqWalkReported mctx loc (ReqCycle parentIface parentArgs iface args) =
  let _ =
    pushTypeErrorOncePerSite
      mctx
      "T-REQUIRES-CYCLE"
      loc
      (requiresCycleMsg mctx parentIface parentArgs iface args)
  None
reqWalkReported mctx loc (ReqDeep iface args) =
  let _ =
    pushTypeErrorOncePerSite
      mctx
      "T-REQUIRES-DEPTH"
      loc
      (requiresDepthMsg iface args)
  None

mentionsEscaped : ModuleCtx -> Authority -> Bool
mentionsEscaped mctx q =
  anyList
    (cell =>
      IdMap.has (authvarId cell) mctx.mcCells.escapedExistentialsRef.value)
    (authVars q)

-- The summary's operations over the view of the entry the drive [o] checked.  The
-- field instantiation runs in a graph record of its own, whose effect-variable
-- counter continues from the drive's (`doEffvarNext`).
export
lastInvocationOps : DriveOutputs -> InvocationOps
lastInvocationOps o = match o.doInvocationView
  InvocationView ctors pols kinds =>
    let byHead = ctorsByHead invocationHeadKey ctors
    let gctx = initialGraphCtx builtinCtors (freshGraphRun ())
    gctx.graphRun.effvarCounter := o.doEffvarNext
    InvocationOps {
      headVariances =
        h => match headTyconMono h
          Some (HkDecl key) =>
            slotVariances (paramPolaritiesIn pols key) (lookupTab key kinds)
          _ => None,
      appliedFields =
        applied =>
          let (h, args) = spineParts applied
          flatMap
            (c => instantiateFields gctx args c)
            (optionOr [] (omLookup (invocationHeadKey h) byHead)),
      headKey = invocationHeadKey,
    }

-- Generalize each captured local binding's (now-solved) mono into a Scheme for
-- the LSP hover fallback (see localBindRefs).  Runs at the end of inference when
-- currentLevel is back at the top, so a still-free local var quantifies cleanly
-- to `a`; a ground var (e.g. a `let` bound to a String) renders concretely.
mapLocalSchemes : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Option Loc, Mono) ->
  List (String, Option Loc, Scheme)
mapLocalSchemes mctx [] = []
mapLocalSchemes mctx ((n, l, m) :: rest) =
  (n, l, generalize mctx m) :: mapLocalSchemes mctx rest

-- ── value restriction (T1) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- A binding RHS is *non-expansive* (a syntactic value) iff it cannot allocate a
-- mutable cell: literals, variables and lambdas are values; annotations are
-- transparent; tuples/lists are values iff their elements are.  Constructor
-- applications of non-expansive arguments are non-expansive (SML value
-- restriction relaxation, Phase 66 extension) EXCEPT `Ref`, excluded by name in
-- `isCtorAppSpine` below: generalizing `Ref x` would be unsound (polymorphic
-- reference: write at one type, read at another).
--
-- 🔒 THE HEAD TEST IS AN ACTUAL CONSTRUCTOR LOOKUP, NOT A SPELLING TEST —
-- issue 1150 (S0, memory-safety), fixed 2026-08-26.  `isCtorAppSpine`'s head
-- arms ask `lookupCtor env name`, so the predicate now answers "is this name a
-- REAL, DECLARED constructor?" instead of "does this name start with a capital
-- letter?".  Threading the `TcEnv` this needs is why `isNonexpansive`,
-- `isCtorAppSpine`, `clausesAreValue`/`clauseIsValue`,
-- `memberClauseIsValue` and `sccSchemes` all take an env parameter.
--
-- What the old first-character heuristic (`ctorHeadShaped`, retained below
-- only as a cheap pre-filter) got wrong: a MODULE ALIAS is REQUIRED to be
-- uppercase (`aliasNameFor`, frontend/parser.mdk — lowercase is a hard parse
-- error) and an alias-qualified value desugars to a FLAT `EVar` carrying the
-- dotted name (`rewriteAliasQual`, frontend/desugar.mdk, via `qualifiedLocal`
-- in frontend/ast.mdk: `"\{alias}.\{n}"`).  So `ctorHeadIsUpper "H.new"` (its first form) read
-- `'H'` and said True: EVERY alias-qualified call in the language was
-- CLASSIFIED as a constructor application.  Classification is not the whole
-- test — `isCtorAppSpine (EApp f x) = isCtorAppSpine f && isNonexpansive x`
-- still rejects the spine if any argument is expansive, so `H.f (g 1)` was
-- classified but NOT generalized.  It was enough for the repro, whose argument
-- is a value: `let m = H.new ()` over `stdlib/hash_map.mdk` yielded a
-- polymorphic mutable table — `check` exit 0, `run` E-NOT-A-FUNCTION, built
-- binary SEGFAULT.  Under the lookup, `"H.new"` is absent from the ctor map and
-- the binding is value-restricted: `check` REJECTS the program.
--
-- Why the lookup is sound (i.e. why "present in the ctor map" implies "really a
-- constructor").  `lookupCtor` reads `TcEnv`'s 2nd `OrdMap`, and that map is
-- written in exactly TWO places — `addCtor` (sole call site, inside
-- `addVariants`, reached only from `registerVariants`, itself called only from
-- `registerData`'s `DData` and `DNewtype` arms) and the two prelude ctors
-- `True`/`False`, hand-seeded straight into the map by `builtinCtors`, bypassing
-- `addCtor` entirely.  Both writers are constructor-only.  ("Populated only by
-- `addCtor`", which this comment asserted until 2026-07-31, was false — hence
-- the second clause.)  Re-derive with
-- `grep -n 'addCtor\|builtinCtors' compiler/types/typecheck.mdk`.
--
-- The uppercase-mutable-cell-extern hazard this comment used to warn about is
-- retired BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by audit: the grammar still permits an
-- uppercase extern NAME (`externNameFor (TUpper x) = emit x`,
-- frontend/parser.mdk, vs `identNameFor`, which accepts only `TIdent`), but an
-- extern is never passed to `addCtor`, so no extern — uppercase or not — can
-- pass the head test any more.  `Ref` (`extern Ref : a -> Ref a`,
-- stdlib/runtime.mdk) is exactly such an extern; its by-name exclusion is kept
-- below purely as defense-in-depth, since the lookup alone already rejects it.
-- See issue 1150 and docs/spec/DICT-SEMANTICS.md §4.1 G2.
--
-- Record creates are non-expansive iff all field expressions are.
-- Note: this ignores the `mut` flag (like the oracle), so `let mut x = []`
-- generalizes — the separate `mut`-gen hole is a both-sides follow-up (T1b).
isNonexpansive : TcEnv -> Expr -> Bool
isNonexpansive env (ELoc _ e) = isNonexpansive env e
isNonexpansive env (EDoOrigin _ e) = isNonexpansive env e
isNonexpansive env (ELit _) = True
isNonexpansive env (EVar _) = True
isNonexpansive env (EVarId _ _) = True
-- `run`/`build` rewrite a method reference into a dictionary-marked node before
-- typechecking (`prePassDict`); the marked node is still a variable, so the value
-- predicate must answer as it does for the `EVar` that `check` sees — otherwise
-- `callMin = min` is a value under one verb and expansive under another
-- (check green, build panics on an unbound dictionary witness).
isNonexpansive env (EMethodAt _ _ _) = True
isNonexpansive env (EDictAt _ _) = True
isNonexpansive env (EMethodRef _) = True
isNonexpansive env (ELam _ _) = True
isNonexpansive env (EAnnot e _) = isNonexpansive env e
isNonexpansive env (EHeadAnnot e _) = isNonexpansive env e
isNonexpansive env (ETuple es) = allList (isNonexpansive env) es
isNonexpansive env (EListLit es) = allList (isNonexpansive env) es
-- Constructor application: non-expansive iff the spine head is an EVar naming a
-- REAL, DECLARED constructor (`lookupCtor env`, see the 🔒 above and issue
-- 1150) — that is NOT `Ref`, and every spine argument is itself non-expansive.
-- Partial ctor applications (e.g. `MkTwo []`) are also non-expansive — they are
-- closures, not mutable cells.  `isCtorAppSpine` strips ELoc/EDoOrigin wrappers
-- before testing.
isNonexpansive env (app@(EApp _ _)) = isCtorAppSpine env app
-- Record creation: non-expansive iff every field expression is non-expansive.
isNonexpansive env (ERecordCreate _ fs) =
  allList
    (fa => match fa
      FieldAssign _ e => isNonexpansive env e)
    fs
isNonexpansive env _ = False

-- Walk the left spine of an application to its head, testing EVERY argument met
-- on the way, and finally test whether the head IS a constructor that is safe to
-- generalize: an EVar naming a constructor DECLARED in this `TcEnv`, asked of
-- the environment via `lookupCtor` rather than guessed from the name's spelling
-- (issue 1150, fixed 2026-08-26 — see the 🔒 on `isNonexpansive` above for why
-- the ctor map's two writers make the lookup sound).  `Ref` stays excluded by
-- name as defense-in-depth: it is an extern FUNCTION, never passed to
-- `addCtor`, so `lookupCtor` already rejects it on its own.
--
-- `ctorHeadShaped` is retained as a pure FAST PATH in front of the lookup: an
-- ordinary function-application head — the overwhelmingly common `let` RHS —
-- fails on a character read instead of an `OrdMap` probe.  It can only ever
-- narrow, never widen.  It DID narrow on the emit path (#2089's census): the
-- emitter's tree carries constructors mangled to `<mid>__<Ctor>`
-- (`types/private_mangle.mdk`), so a first-character-uppercase test judged every
-- constructor CAF (`regEmpty = Registry omEmpty`) expansive there, narrowed it at
-- first use, and every later use at another element type was a type mismatch —
-- discarded, because nothing read them.  The fast path now accepts both spellings.
--
-- The arguments are tested HERE, on the single walk to the head, rather than by
-- re-entering `isNonexpansive` at each `EApp` level: re-entering would re-walk
-- the whole spine per level, i.e. quadratic in the constructor's arity.  Testing
-- only the LAST argument was issue 1139 — a `Ref` in any non-final position
-- escaped the exclusion entirely, so `let b = BR (Ref []) True` generalized and
-- a cell written at `Int` could be read at `Int -> Int`.
--
-- The head is tested BEFORE the argument: `&&` short-circuits, and the common
-- RHS at a `let` is an ordinary function application, whose head fails the test
-- immediately.  Testing the argument first would walk its whole subtree before
-- discovering the spine was never a constructor application at all.  Both
-- operands are pure `Bool`, so the order is semantically invisible.
isCtorAppSpine : TcEnv -> Expr -> Bool
isCtorAppSpine env (ELoc _ e) = isCtorAppSpine env e
isCtorAppSpine env (EDoOrigin _ e) = isCtorAppSpine env e
isCtorAppSpine env (EApp f x) = isCtorAppSpine env f && isNonexpansive env x
isCtorAppSpine env (EVar name) = isDeclaredCtorHead env name
isCtorAppSpine env (EVarId name _) = isDeclaredCtorHead env name
isCtorAppSpine env _ = False

-- The head test itself: `name` is a real, declared constructor and is not the
-- `Ref` extern.  See `isCtorAppSpine`'s docblock for why `lookupCtor` is the
-- authority, why `ctorHeadShaped` is only a fast path in front of it, and why
-- the `Ref` exclusion is redundant-but-kept.
isDeclaredCtorHead : TcEnv -> String -> Bool
isDeclaredCtorHead env name =
  name /= "Ref" && ctorHeadShaped name && isSome (lookupCtor env name)

-- Spelled like a data constructor: uppercase-initial, or a mangled `<mid>__<Ctor>`
-- whose segment after the FIRST `__` is uppercase-initial (`private_mangle` joins
-- with one `__`, and a module id never contains one).  A spelling pre-filter only;
-- `lookupCtor` decides.
ctorHeadShaped : String -> Bool
ctorHeadShaped name =
  let cs = stringToChars name
  let n = arrayLength cs
  n > 0 && (isUpper (arrayGetUnsafe 0 cs) || mangledCtorShaped cs n 0)

mangledCtorShaped : Array Char -> Int -> Int -> Bool
mangledCtorShaped cs n i
  | i + 2 >= n = False
  | arrayGetUnsafe i cs == '_'
    && arrayGetUnsafe (i + 1) cs == '_'
    && isUpper (arrayGetUnsafe (i + 2) cs) = True
  | otherwise = mangledCtorShaped cs n (i + 1)

-- Generalize a value RHS; value-restrict (monomorphize, lowering free vars)
-- otherwise.  monoScheme leaves the mono ungeneralized.
genBindingRestricted : DynCtx ->
  Map Int Unit ->
  List AuthResidual ->
  Bool ->
  EffRow ->
  Mono ->
  Scheme
genBindingRestricted dyn declared residual isValue force t
  | isValue = generalizeBindingDeclared dyn declared residual force t
  | otherwise =
    let _ = lowerToCurrent dyn.dcModule t
    let _ = lowerRowLevels dyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value force
    -- a binding that turns out monomorphic after its scope kept residuals
    -- (a local pinned for dictionary forwarding) owes them where it lives
    let _ =
      fold
        (_ r =>
          let _ =
            lowerAuthLevels dyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value r.arLower
          let _ =
            lowerAuthLevels dyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value r.arUpper
          wantAuthorityWith dyn.dcModule r.arExact r.arLower r.arUpper)
        ()
        residual
    Forall [] [] [] [] force t

-- A constructor in PATTERN position: its universals freshen as at any use,
-- but an existential binder (§4.1) is OPENED — a fresh RIGID authority the
-- arm may relate values by and never solve — and parked for the pattern
-- site (`takePatLits`/`settlePatLits`), which decides whether it may open one.
instantiateCtorPattern : ModuleCtx -> Scheme -> Mono
instantiateCtorPattern mctx (Forall ids evars avars _ _ t) =
  let (asub, opened) = freshAuthSubstOpening mctx avars t
  let _ = openExistentials mctx opened
  substMono mctx.mcGraph (freshSubst mctx ids) (freshEffSubst mctx evars) asub t

openExistentials : ModuleCtx -> List (Ref Authvar) -> Unit
openExistentials mctx [] = ()
openExistentials mctx cells =
  let _ = markSourceless mctx.mcGraph (map authvarId cells)
  mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsRef :=
    cells ++ mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsRef.value

-- The context the module last checked recorded for its binding [n].
ownContext : ModuleCtx -> String -> List VecObl
ownContext mctx n =
  -- #837: key the obligation lookup by (name, binding-id), exactly as the check-path
  -- reader does — recovering the id from schemeDefIdsRef (top-level binders of the
  -- module last checked).  With the leak-guard windows retired this is what stops a
  -- where-helper `g`'s obligation rendering on an unrelated top-level `g`; a binder
  -- absent from schemeDefIdsRef (id 0) falls to the bare-name scan (today's path).
  let id = optionOr 0 (omLookup n mctx.mcCells.schemeDefIdsRef.value)
  optionOr [] (lookupSchemeObls n id mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value)

-- A module's own schemes, each with its context, taken when the module closes:
-- [mctx] still holds that module's tables, and the next module's check
-- mints its own record.
publishOwn : ModuleCtx -> List (String, Scheme) -> List (String, PubScheme)
publishOwn mctx = publishWithContexts (ownContext mctx)

-- Core's own obligations, keyed by bare name (#837: the binding-id half of each
-- key is dropped, as every cross-module reader looks a prelude name up by name).
-- Read right after the core pass, from the record [mctx] core was checked in.
coreOwnContexts : ModuleCtx -> OrdMap (List VecObl)
coreOwnContexts mctx =
  omFromPairs
    (map (kv => (fst (fst kv), snd kv)) mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value)
    omEmpty

-- The context a seed name renders with, by three steps in order.  A name the
-- module last checked BINDS takes that module's own context, or none, and never
-- reaches the prelude store, so a buffer's own `isEven x = "s"` cannot pick up the
-- prelude `isEven`'s context (#2054's shape).  The prelude's contexts are consulted
-- ONLY for a name this module does not bind and whose per-run table has no entry
-- at all: on the module arm each module gets its own `freshModuleCtx`, so the
-- prelude's obligations are not in [mctx], and a prelude scheme would otherwise
-- render without its `=>`.
-- The third step reads [coreContexts], the prelude's contexts keyed by bare name.
seedContext : ModuleCtx -> OrdMap (List VecObl) -> String -> List VecObl
seedContext mctx coreContexts n =
  match omLookup n mctx.mcCells.schemeDefIdsRef.value
    Some _ => ownContext mctx n
    None => match lookupSchemeObls n 0 mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value
      Some obs => obs
      None => optionOr [] (omLookup n coreContexts)

-- The last module of [modules], checked in [mctx]: its locals and its import seed,
-- frozen with their contexts.  The seed's prelude contexts come from
-- [coreContexts], `graphPreamble`'s snapshot.
captureEntryTables : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap (List VecObl) ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  EntryTables
captureEntryTables mctx coreContexts modules = match last modules
  None => noEntryTables
  Some (mid, _) => EntryTables {
    etModule = mid,
    etLocals =
      map
        ((n, loc, s) => (n, freezePub s (ownContext mctx n), loc))
        mctx.mcCells.localSchemesOut.value,
    etSeed =
      map
        (b => (
          fst b,
          freezePub (snd b) (seedContext mctx coreContexts (fst b)),
        ))
        mctx.mcCells.seedSchemesOut.value,
  }

lookupImportedStandalone : TcEnv -> String -> Option Scheme
lookupImportedStandalone env name = match lookupBinding env name
  Some binding => match binding.ebStandalone
    Some (ImportedStandalone, value) => Some value.vsScheme
    _ => None
  None => None

bindingDeclaredAt : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  MethodTrackedInstantiation ->
  Option CDeclared
bindingDeclaredAt env name inst =
  declaredEffectsAt env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph inst (bindingDeclared env name)

-- Slot projection below applies the type substitution after superclass expansion;
-- effect-index arguments use the same occurrence's row substitution here.
declaredEffectsAt : GraphCtx ->
  MethodTrackedInstantiation ->
  Option CDeclared ->
  Option CDeclared
declaredEffectsAt gctx inst declared =
  map
    (dc => CDeclared {
      cdSlots = dc.cdSlots,
      cdPrefix = dc.cdPrefix,
      cdArgs =
        map
          (map
            (substMono
              gctx
              []
              inst.mtiSubstitution.misEffectSubst
              inst.mtiSubstitution.misAuthSubst))
          dc.cdArgs,
    })
    declared

recordDeclaredBindingCall : ModuleCtx -> CDeclared -> List (Int, Mono) -> Unit
recordDeclaredBindingCall mctx dc subst =
  let expanded = dedupSlotVecs (zipSlotVecs dc.cdSlots dc.cdArgs)
  recordCallObligations
    mctx
    (map fst expanded)
    (constraintMonosOf (map (pair => (fst pair).csId) expanded) subst)
    (callArgVecsV mctx.mcGraph expanded subst)

-- ── pattern inference: returns the pattern's type + the bindings it adds ───
inferPat : TcEnv -> Pat -> (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferPat env (PVar x xloc bid) =
  let v = freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let _ = recordLocalBind env.teDyn.dcModule x (Some xloc) bid v
  (v, [(x, monoScheme v)])
inferPat env PWild = (freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule (), [])
inferPat env (PLit (LInt n)) = inferIntLitPat env.teDyn.dcModule n
inferPat env (PLit (LU64 hi lo)) = inferU64LitPat env.teDyn.dcModule hi lo
inferPat env (PLit (LI64 hi lo)) =
  let _ =
    refuseBoxedLitPat
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      "I64"
      (i64HalvesLiteral hi lo)
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
  (tconBuiltin "I64", [])
inferPat env (PLit l) = (litType l, [])
inferPat env (PCon name pats) = inferPatCon env name pats
inferPat env (PTuple pats) = inferPatTuple env pats
inferPat env (PCons h t) = inferPatCons env h t
inferPat env (PList pats) = inferPatList env pats
inferPat env (PAs x xloc bid p) = inferPatAs env x xloc bid p
inferPat env (PRec name fields _) = inferPatRec env name fields
inferPat env (PRng lo hi _) = inferPatRng env.teDyn.dcModule lo hi
inferPat env _ = panic "typecheck: unsupported pattern"

-- range pattern `lo..hi` / `lo..=hi`: only Int and Char bounds are valid
-- binds no variables
inferPatRng : ModuleCtx -> Lit -> Lit -> (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferPatRng mctx (LInt _) (LInt _) = (tconBuiltin "Int", [])
inferPatRng mctx (LChar _) (LChar _) = (tconBuiltin "Char", [])
inferPatRng mctx lo hi =
  let _ =
    pushTypeError
      mctx
      "T-TYPE-MISMATCH"
      "type mismatch: \{ppMono (litType lo)} vs \{ppMono (litType hi)}"
  (tconBuiltin "Int", [])

inferPatRec : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  List RecPatField ->
  (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferPatRec env name fields = match lookupRecordByName env.teDyn.dcModule name
  None =>
    let _ =
      pushTypeError
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        "T-UNKNOWN-RECORD"
        (unknownRecordMsg name)
    (freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule (), bindRecPatFieldsFresh env fields)
  Some ri => inferPatRecWith env name ri fields
-- bind the field pattern vars with fresh types (no field-type info) so the
-- arm body still typechecks; the oracle fails fast on the unknown record, we
-- accumulate, so dropping the bindings would raise spurious unbound-var errors

-- bind a record pattern's fields against fresh types, NO unknown-field check
-- (the record itself is already-reported unknown; see inferPatRec error path)
bindRecPatFieldsFresh : TcEnv -> List RecPatField -> List (String, Scheme)
bindRecPatFieldsFresh env [] = []
bindRecPatFieldsFresh env ((RecPatField fname _ bid mp) :: rest) =
  inferRecPatFieldWith env (freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule ()) fname bid mp
    ++ bindRecPatFieldsFresh env rest

inferPatRecWith : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  RecordInfo ->
  List RecPatField ->
  (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferPatRecWith env rname ri fields =
  let (ir, opened) = instantiateRecordOpening env.teDyn.dcModule ri
  let _ = openExistentials env.teDyn.dcModule opened
  (fst ir, inferRecPatFields env rname (snd ir) fields)

inferRecPatFields : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List RecPatField ->
  List (String, Scheme)
inferRecPatFields env _ _ [] = []
inferRecPatFields env rname fieldTypes ((RecPatField fname _ bid mp) :: rest) =
  inferRecPatField env rname fieldTypes fname bid mp
    ++ inferRecPatFields env rname fieldTypes rest

inferRecPatField : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  String ->
  BinderId ->
  Option Pat ->
  List (String, Scheme)
inferRecPatField env rname fieldTypes fname bid mp =
  match lookupAssoc fname fieldTypes
    None =>
      let _ =
        pushTypeError
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          "T-UNKNOWN-FIELD"
          (unknownFieldMsg fname rname)
      inferRecPatFieldWith env (freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule ()) fname bid mp
    Some ft => inferRecPatFieldWith env ft fname bid mp
-- bind the field's pattern vars against a fresh type so the arm body still
-- typechecks (the oracle fails fast on the unknown field; we accumulate, so
-- skipping the binding would raise spurious downstream unbound-variable errors)

-- A pun binds the field's own type.  It is published to the runtime-type table
-- but not to the LSP hover list, which has never carried puns.
inferRecPatFieldWith : TcEnv ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  BinderId ->
  Option Pat ->
  List (String, Scheme)
inferRecPatFieldWith env ft fname bid None =
  let _ = recordBinderType env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph bid fname ft None False
  [(fname, monoScheme ft)]
inferRecPatFieldWith env ft _ _ (Some p) =
  let pr = inferPat env p
  let _ = bindFrom env.teDyn (fst pr) ft
  snd pr

-- INTEGER-TYPES-DESIGN §3.2 item 5: an integer literal PATTERN takes its type from
-- the scrutinee when that is a builtin integer head, and is `Int` otherwise.  It is
-- inferred as a fresh var and parked on `patLitPending`; the pattern site that
-- unifies the pattern with its scrutinee (or a signature's domain) then settles it
-- with `settlePatLits`, or defers it to `generalize` when the scrutinee's type is
-- not known yet.  Either way the var is settled before anything can quantify it,
-- so a literal pattern never makes a binding polymorphic.
inferIntLitPat : ModuleCtx -> Int -> (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferIntLitPat mctx n =
  let a = freshVar mctx ()
  mctx.mcCells.patLitPending :=
    (a, n, mctx.mcLoc) :: mctx.mcCells.patLitPending.value
  (a, [])

-- Open a pattern site: park the literals of any enclosing site and start
-- empty.  The existentials a pattern opens are parked the same way; a match
-- arm or a clause takes them (`takeOpenedExistentials`) before settling, every
-- other site finds them still parked at `settlePatLits` and refuses them,
-- since only an arm or a clause has a scope to close them in.
takePatLits : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> List (Mono, Int, Option Loc)
takePatLits mctx _ =
  let _ = parkOpenedExistentials mctx ()
  let saved = mctx.mcCells.patLitPending.value
  mctx.mcCells.patLitPending := []
  saved

-- Close a pattern site, after its pattern met its scrutinee.  A literal whose var
-- is now a fixed-width head keeps that type and joins the literal range check; one
-- whose var is any other type is `Int`, exactly as a literal pattern always was (a
-- non-integer scrutinee is the same `Int vs T` mismatch).  A var still unknown here
-- (a lambda's parameter, typed only by a later argument) is deferred: `generalize`
-- defaults it to `Int` before it could be quantified, and the module's end settles
-- whatever remains (`settleDeferredPatLits`).
settlePatLits : DynCtx -> List (Mono, Int, Option Loc) -> Unit
settlePatLits dyn saved =
  let _ = refuseOpenedExistentials dyn.dcModule ()
  settlePatLitsOnly dyn saved

parkOpenedExistentials : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> Unit
parkOpenedExistentials mctx _ =
  mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsStackRef :=
    mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsRef.value
      :: mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsStackRef.value
  mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsRef := []

-- The existentials the current pattern site opened, handed to the site that
-- may close them; the site's accumulator is left empty for `settlePatLits`.
takeOpenedExistentials : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> List (Ref Authvar)
takeOpenedExistentials mctx _ =
  let opened = mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsRef.value
  mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsRef := []
  opened

refuseOpenedExistentials : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> Unit
refuseOpenedExistentials mctx _ =
  let opened = mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsRef.value
  let _ = match opened
    [] => ()
    cell :: _ =>
      pushTypeErrorAt
        mctx
        "T-AUTHORITY-EXISTENTIAL-SCOPE"
        mctx.mcLoc
        (existentialScopeMsg (authvarName cell))
  match mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsStackRef.value
    outer :: rest =>
      mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsRef := outer
      mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsStackRef := rest
    [] => mctx.mcCells.openedExistentialsRef := []

settlePatLitsOnly : DynCtx -> List (Mono, Int, Option Loc) -> Unit
settlePatLitsOnly dyn saved =
  let _ = settlePatLitsGo dyn False dyn.dcModule.mcCells.patLitPending.value
  dyn.dcModule.mcCells.patLitPending := saved

-- [final]: the module is done, so an unknown var defaults instead of deferring.
settlePatLitsGo : DynCtx -> Bool -> List (Mono, Int, Option Loc) -> Unit
settlePatLitsGo dyn _ [] = ()
settlePatLitsGo dyn final ((a, n, loc) :: rest) =
  let _ = match normalize a
    TCon tag _ if isTaggedFixedHead tag =>
      dyn.dcModule.mcCells.numlitRanges :=
        (a, n, loc) :: dyn.dcModule.mcCells.numlitRanges.value
    TCon tag _ if isBoxed64Head tag =>
      refuseBoxedLitPat dyn.dcModule tag (intToString n) loc
    TVar _ if not final =>
      dyn.dcModule.mcCells.patLitDeferred :=
        (a, n, loc) :: dyn.dcModule.mcCells.patLitDeferred.value
    _ => unifyIn (dynAtIfSome loc dyn) (tconBuiltin "Int") a
  settlePatLitsGo dyn final rest

-- The module's inference is complete: every deferred literal pattern takes the
-- type its scrutinee finally got, or `Int`.
settleDeferredPatLits : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> Unit
settleDeferredPatLits mctx _ =
  let deferred = mctx.mcCells.patLitDeferred.value
  mctx.mcCells.patLitDeferred := []
  settlePatLitsGo (dynFor mctx) True deferred

-- A `U64` or `I64` is a boxed cell, and no engine's pattern matcher compares one
-- against a constant, so a literal pattern cannot match it (INTEGER-TYPES-DESIGN
-- §3.2 item 5 builds the tagged heads only).  Refused, never compiled to an arm
-- that silently never matches: an ordinary literal whose scrutinee grounded to
-- `U64` or `I64` (`settlePatLitsGo`), and a wide one wherever it is written
-- (`exprToPat` keeps it as `LU64`).
refuseBoxedLitPat : ModuleCtx -> String -> String -> Option Loc -> Unit
refuseBoxedLitPat mctx tag lit loc =
  recordTypeError
    mctx
    (TcDiag
      "T-TYPE-MISMATCH"
      1
      (orElseLoc loc mctx.mcLoc)
      "the literal pattern `\{lit}` cannot match \{if isI64Head tag then "an" else "a"} `\{tag}`; compare in a guard instead"
      (Some "compare in a guard instead: `x if x == \{lit}`")
      None)

inferU64LitPat : ModuleCtx -> Int -> Int -> (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferU64LitPat mctx hi lo =
  let _ = refuseBoxedLitPat mctx "U64" ("0x" ++ u64HalvesHex hi lo) mctx.mcLoc
  (tconBuiltin "U64", [])

inferPatCon : TcEnv -> String -> List Pat -> (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferPatCon env name pats = match lookupCtor env name
  None =>
    let _ =
      pushTypeError env.teDyn.dcModule "T-UNKNOWN-CTOR" (unknownCtorMsg name)
    let pr = inferPats env pats
    (freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule (), snd pr)
  Some scheme => inferPatConWith env scheme pats
-- still infer the sub-patterns so their bindings reach the arm body
-- (else the continued path raises spurious unbound-variable errors the
-- oracle never reaches — it fails fast on the unknown constructor)

inferPatConWith : TcEnv -> Scheme -> List Pat -> (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferPatConWith env scheme pats =
  let ctorType = instantiateCtorPattern env.teDyn.dcModule scheme
  let pr = inferPats env pats
  let resultVar = freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let _ = unifyIn env.teDyn ctorType (foldrFun (fst pr) resultVar)
  (resultVar, snd pr)

inferPats : TcEnv -> List Pat -> (List Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferPats env [] = ([], [])
inferPats env (p :: ps) =
  let pr = inferPat env p
  let rest = inferPats env ps
  (fst pr :: fst rest, snd pr ++ snd rest)

inferPatTuple : TcEnv -> List Pat -> (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferPatTuple env pats =
  let pr = inferPats env pats
  (tupleMono (fst pr), snd pr)

inferPatCons : TcEnv -> Pat -> Pat -> (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferPatCons env h t =
  let hr = inferPat env h
  let tr = inferPat env t
  let listTy = TApp (tconBuiltin "List") (fst hr)
  let _ = unifyIn env.teDyn (fst tr) listTy
  (listTy, snd hr ++ snd tr)

inferPatList : TcEnv -> List Pat -> (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferPatList env pats =
  let elem = freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let pr = inferPats env pats
  let _ = unifyAll env.teDyn elem (fst pr)
  (TApp (tconBuiltin "List") elem, snd pr)

inferPatAs : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  Loc ->
  BinderId ->
  Pat ->
  (Mono, List (String, Scheme))
inferPatAs env x xloc bid p =
  let pr = inferPat env p
  let _ = recordLocalBind env.teDyn.dcModule x (Some xloc) bid (fst pr)
  (fst pr, (x, monoScheme (fst pr)) :: snd pr)

-- ── expression inference ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
infer : TcEnv -> Expr -> Mono
infer env (ELit l) = litType l
-- PLAN.md #11: a source integer literal is `Num a` for a fresh `a`.  With the
-- prelude loaded (Num registered + `fromInt` in scope), model the literal exactly
-- as `fromInt n`.  inferMethodAt
-- "fromInt" records the Num impl obligation AND a pendingSite keyed on [dref] (the
-- node's route cell), so resolveSites later stamps [dref]: RKey when the literal's
-- type grounds to a concrete Num head, RDictFwd onto the enclosing `Num a` dict when
-- it stays polymorphic (the soundness case, `1` in `inc x = x + 1` — exactly the
-- route `fromInt 0` in `sum` gets).  Apply the `Int -> a` method type to an Int arg
-- (mirror OCaml's `unify from_int_ty (TFun t_int … a)`) to recover the result var
-- [a], and stash (a, fref, n, dref) in numlitRefs so the post-HM setNumlitFloats can
-- decide concrete-Float / concrete-Int / still-poly.  Recording the obligation here
-- AND (when under `+`) in numArithOp is harmless: both unify the same var, both
-- demand `Num`.  Without the prelude (bare-HM oracle, `builtinClassPresent BNum` False)
-- `fromInt` is unbound: fall back to a plain fresh var, dref stays RNone (⇒ Int).
infer env (ENumLit n ev _) = inferNumLit env n ev
infer env (EWideLit hi lo ev lx) = inferWideLit env hi lo ev lx
infer env (EVar x) = inferVar env x
-- #837: EVarId carries the resolve-minted binding id; thread it to
-- instantiateVarTracked so obligation lookup keys by (name, id).
infer env (EVarId x id) = inferVarId env x id
infer env (EApp f x) = inferAppExpr env f x
infer env (ELam pats body) = inferLam env pats body
infer env (ELet _ isFun pat e1 e2) = inferLet env isFun pat e1 e2
infer env (ELetGroup binds body) = inferLetGroup env binds body
infer env (EIf c t e) = inferIf env c t e
infer env (EMatch scrut arms) = inferMatch env (infer env scrut) arms
infer env (ETuple es) = tupleMono (inferEach env es)
infer env (EListLit es) = inferListLit env es
infer env (EAnnot e ty) = inferAnnot env e ty
infer env (EBinOp op l r ev) =
  inferBinopE env op l r (siteRouteCell env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ev)
-- An operator or a field access the parser leaves unwrapped names its own span
-- (its operand's: the operator and the field name carry none).
infer env (EUnOp op e ev) =
  inferUnopE
    (envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc e) env)
    op
    e
    (siteRouteCell env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ev)
infer env (EInfix op l r) = inferInfix env op l r
infer env (ERecordCreate name fields) = inferRecordCreate env name fields
infer env (EFieldAccess e fname ev) =
  inferFieldAccess (envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc e) env) e fname ev
infer env (ERecordUpdate base fields ev) = inferRecordUpdate env base fields ev
infer env (EVariantUpdate cname base fields) =
  inferVariantUpdate env cname base fields
infer env (EBlock stmts) = inferBlock env stmts
infer env (EMethodAt name _ ev) =
  inferMethodAtCell env name (methodCellOf env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ev)
infer env (EDictAt name ev) = inferGrantedAt env name ev
infer env (EArrayLit es) = inferArrayLit env es
infer env (ERangeList lo hi _) = inferIntRange env lo hi (tconBuiltin "List")
infer env (ERangeArray lo hi _) = inferIntRange env lo hi (tconBuiltin "Array")
-- EIndex is desugared to an `index` method call before typecheck (Phase #16b);
-- the built-in index-inference path is retired, so no `EIndex` arm here.  ESlice
-- is likewise desugared to a `slice` method call before typecheck (#670), so
-- no `ESlice` arm here -- a surviving one is a desugar-ordering bug and hits the
-- loud "unsupported expression" catch-all, and a non-container receiver becomes a
-- "no impl of Slice" constraint error via normal method dispatch.
infer env (EHeadAnnot e ty) = inferHeadAnnot env e ty
-- ELoc is transparent: the wrapped expression and every check inside it are
-- located at this span, until a nested construct names its own.
infer env (ELoc l e) = infer (envAt (Some l) env) e
-- Phase 150: a do-lowered chain.  Record the do-block loc so a monad-shape
-- mismatch during inference is retargeted to the tailored "do requires a monad"
-- error (see typeMismatch).  The chain's walk gets its own context; an inline
-- nested `do` block (`a <- (do ...)`) mints another, so its first report never
-- un-blames a LATER statement of the outer chain (#894 review finding 2).
infer env (EDoOrigin l e) =
  -- #824: the lowered chain's synthesized callee names the herald
  -- (`deferThen` for a `defer` block), so the "requires a monad" reframe can
  -- name the right interface.
  let doCtx = DoCtx {
    doLoc = l,
    doDeferred = doChainIsDeferred e,
    doReported = Ref False,
  }
  infer { env | teDyn = { env.teDyn | dcDo = Some doCtx } } e

infer env _ = panic "typecheck: unsupported expression"

-- is this lowered do-chain a `defer` block?  Its head callee is the tagged
-- `deferThen` (see `callAndThen` in desugar.mdk).
doChainIsDeferred : Expr -> Bool
doChainIsDeferred (EApp f _) = doChainIsDeferred f
doChainIsDeferred (ELoc _ e) = doChainIsDeferred e
doChainIsDeferred (EDoOrigin _ (EVar "deferThen")) = True
doChainIsDeferred (EDoOrigin _ (EVarId "deferThen" _)) = True
doChainIsDeferred _ = False

inferArrayLit : TcEnv -> List Expr -> Mono
inferArrayLit env es =
  let elem = joinValueTypes env.teDyn JoinArray (inferProduced env es)
  TApp (tconBuiltin "Array") elem

-- [lo..hi] : List Int, [|lo..hi|] : Array Int
inferIntRange : TcEnv -> Expr -> Expr -> Mono -> Mono
inferIntRange env lo hi container =
  let _ = unifyIn env.teDyn (infer env lo) (tconBuiltin "Int")
  let _ = unifyIn env.teDyn (infer env hi) (tconBuiltin "Int")
  TApp container (tconBuiltin "Int")

-- (ESlice's `inferSlice`/`indexKind` were retired with #670: `a.[lo..hi]` now
-- desugars to a `slice` method call before typecheck, so slicing infers
-- through normal interface dispatch on `Slice`, not a bespoke arm here.)

-- a method occurrence.  Return-position: record (routeRef, result mono) so
-- resolveSites can stamp RKey/RDict.  D3a arg-position (name in
-- argDispatchIdxByIdRef): the dispatch is decided by the DISCRIMINATING-ARGUMENT type,
-- not the result, so queue recordArgStamp on the arg-position mono instead — it is
-- NOT a pendingSites/methodSiteFns return-position site.
inferMethodAt : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  Ref String ->
  Ref (Option Int) ->
  Ref Route ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Ref Inner ->
  Mono
inferMethodAtCell : TcEnv -> String -> EvCell -> Mono
inferMethodAtCell env name c =
  let st = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph.graphRun.grants
  st.gsLastMethodInst := None
  st.gsLastStandalone := None
  c.ecLoc := env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
  c.ecName := name
  let t =
    inferMethodAt
      env
      name
      c.ecIface
      c.ecArity
      c.ecTag
      c.ecImpl
      c.ecMeth
      c.ecInner
  let _ = match (st.gsLastStandalone.value, st.gsLastMethodInst.value)
    (Some (scheme, subst), _) =>
      recordStandaloneGrantOcc
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        name
        c.ecId
        scheme
        subst
        (optionOr 0 c.ecArity.value)
    (None, Some (scheme, subst)) =>
      recordMethodGrantOcc env.teDyn.dcModule name c.ecId scheme subst
    (None, None) => ()
  t

-- #2705: a standalone-shadow occurrence (a user fn spelled like an interface
-- method — `add x y = x + y` beside `Num`'s `add`) DENOTES THE STANDALONE, whose
-- scheme may carry an inferred or declared context.  Instantiate that context as
-- call obligations exactly as the plain-`EVar` path does
-- (`instantiateVarTrackedId`), so the verdict — `No impl of Num for String` on
-- `add "a" "b"` — is the obligation channel's on every driver, not something the
-- check pass supplies for the emit pass.  The shadow-dict recorders beside this
-- carry SLOTS only; obligations were never theirs.  MEASURED: without this,
-- marking the check drivers let that program through at exit 0.
-- A non-shadow method occurrence records nothing here: `lookupSchemeObls` keys by
-- binding name and a method is not a binding, and the cross-module store is only
-- consulted behind the same shadow gate.
recordShadowStandaloneObls : TcEnv -> String -> List (Int, Mono) -> Unit
recordShadowStandaloneObls env name subst
  | isDefinerShadow env.teDyn.dcModule name
    || isShadowStandalone
      env
      name =
    match (lookupSchemeObls
      name
      0
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value)
      Some obs => recordSchemeCallObligations env.teDyn.dcModule 0 obs subst
      None => match declaredCrossModuleObls env.teDyn.dcModule name
        Some obs => recordSchemeCallObligations env.teDyn.dcModule 0 obs subst
        None => ()
  | otherwise = ()

inferMethodAt env name ifaceRef arityRef tagRef implRef methodRef innerRef =
  let selected = match standaloneValueBinding env name
    Some scheme => Some scheme
    None => standaloneValueBindingEmit env name tagRef
  match selected
    Some value =>
      let _ = rejectAdmittedValueOccurrence env.teDyn.dcModule name
      let sym = routeLocalSym !tagRef
      let occurrence =
        instantiateStandaloneOccurrence
          env
          name
          sym
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
          value
      let inst = occurrence.svoInstance
      let dicts = occurrence.svoDicts
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph.graphRun.grants.gsLastStandalone :=
        Some (occurrence.svoScheme, inst.mtiSubstitution.misAuthSubst)
      arityRef := Some (funArity inst.mtiBody)
      let receiver = match methodDispatchIdx env.teDyn.dcModule name
        Some idx => optionOr inst.mtiBody (nthArgMono idx inst.mtiBody)
        None => inst.mtiBody
      let _ =
        pushSiteGoal
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
          GKRLocalSite
          innerRef
          (PendingEntry
            name
            tagRef
            receiver
            env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn.value
            (SKRLocal sym True dicts.sdMonos dicts.sdIfaces dicts.sdArgVecs)
            env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
            (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
            (freshEvId env.teDyn.dcModule ()))
      inst.mtiBody
    None =>
      inferMethodCandidateAt
        env
        name
        ifaceRef
        arityRef
        tagRef
        implRef
        methodRef
        innerRef

-- Selection precedes instantiation: the returned value, forcing row, obligations,
-- and route slots above share one occurrence's substitution. A discarded method
-- candidate must not supply a standalone value's receiver or dictionary cells.
inferMethodCandidateAt : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  Ref String ->
  Ref (Option Int) ->
  Ref Route ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Ref Inner ->
  Mono
inferMethodCandidateAt env name ifaceRef arityRef tagRef implRef methodRef innerRef =
  match lookupVar env name
    -- Routed standalone recovery already ran before candidate selection.
    None => panic ("unbound method: " ++ name)
    Some s =>
      let inst = instantiateMethodTracked env.teDyn.dcModule s
      let occurrence = inst.mtiBody
      let subst = inst.mtiSubstitution
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph.graphRun.grants.gsLastMethodInst :=
        Some (s, subst.misAuthSubst)
      arityRef := Some (funArity occurrence)
      ifaceRef := admittedIfaceWord env.teDyn.dcModule name
      let _ = recordRLocalSite env name tagRef innerRef occurrence
      let ret = match argDispatchOf env.teDyn.dcModule name
        Some idx =>
          let _ =
            recordMethodDicts
              env.teDyn.dcModule
              name
              methodRef
              innerRef
              subst.misTypeSubst
          -- One variable per omitted typaram, shared by the goal and the route.
          let omitted = methodOmittedVars env.teDyn.dcModule name
          let _ = recordMethodObligationGuarded env name s occurrence omitted
          let _ =
            recordArgStamp
              env.teDyn.dcModule
              env.teDyn.dcSuppressArgStamp
              name
              tagRef
              implRef
              innerRef
              idx
              occurrence
              omitted
          let _ = recordArgSiteFn env.teDyn.dcModule name idx occurrence
          occurrence
        None =>
          recordSite
            env
            name
            s
            ifaceRef
            tagRef
            implRef
            methodRef
            innerRef
            occurrence
            subst
      let _ = forceInstantiation env.teDyn.dcModule name inst
      ret
-- C5: if [name] is a standalone-shadow method, record its discriminating-arg
-- mono cell UNGATED so resolveRLocalSites can route RLocal when the receiver
-- grounds to a no-impl head (the arg-stamp path would otherwise leave it RNone
-- → arg-tag panic on a receiver with no impl).

-- Cause-A prerequisite: ALSO record the discriminating-arg mono into
-- methodSiteFns keyed by currentFn (mirroring recordSite, which only fires
-- for return-position).  Without this, an unsignatured fn whose body
-- dispatches a method in ARGUMENT position (`f s = display s`) never
-- surfaces its inferred constraint to inferredConstraintIds → never gets
-- promoted → no leading dict param on the build path → dict word 0 (SIGSEGV/
-- silent).  Inert unless promotion (`registerInferredConstraints`, whose result the
-- schedule marks with) consumes it.

-- C5: queue a standalone-shadow method occurrence's discriminating-arg mono cell so
-- resolveRLocalSites can stamp RLocal once inference grounds the receiver.  Only
-- shadows (standaloneValuesRef) are recorded — every other method occurrence is
-- untouched (no entry → byte-identical).  The dispatch index comes from the method's
-- declared interface type (methodDispatchIdx).
-- S-1: this is the GENERAL shadow-occurrence recorder, and it is the path that a
-- VALUE-position shadow (`map size [1,2,3]`) and an IMPORTER shadow on an UNGROUNDED
-- receiver (`size 3`, where the Num literal is not yet grounded so inferShadowApp's
-- standalone arm is never reached) both take.  Both must carry the standalone's dicts or
-- they under-apply exactly like the headline bug.  Slots only — NOT obligations; see
-- shadowStandaloneDictSlotsAt.
recordRLocalSite : TcEnv -> String -> Ref Route -> Ref Inner -> Mono -> Unit
recordRLocalSite env name tagRef innerRef inst
  | env.teDyn.dcSuppressRLocalRecord = ()
  -- #1430 (S2, row 39): a RETURN-POSITION method has NO dispatch argument, so
  -- `methodDispatchIdx` answers None and every arm below declined — no pending site, no
  -- route stamp, and the occurrence kept the method's dispatching route while
  -- `maybeStandaloneValueMono` had already pinned its TYPE to the standalone.  That is
  -- exactly the invariant `standaloneValuePinned`'s header states in bold ("⭐ THE ROUTE
  -- MUST FOLLOW THE ARM"), violated at the one cell the dispatch-index gate hides.
  -- Measured at the parent commit on a two-verb split that cannot be read any other way:
  -- for `interface Zed a where zed : a` + `impl Zed Int` + a module-local `zed : Bool`,
  -- `check --types` reported `zed : Bool` (the standalone — the TYPE arm) at exit 0 while
  -- `run` E-PANICked `no matching impl for dispatch` (the ROUTE arm asked `Zed Bool`).
  -- With `zed : Int` the same split is SILENT: `run` printed the impl's 777.
  -- forceLocal (`True`) rather than a receiver query: under S4 there is no receiver to
  -- dispatch on, which is the same argument `standaloneValuePinned` already makes for the
  -- arg-position value cell.  Empty dict slots: `shadowStandaloneDictSlotsAt` resolves a
  -- constrained standalone's slots by unifying its scheme against `TFun receiver …`, and a
  -- return-position value standalone has no such arrow to match — an unconstrained one
  -- (the whole cell #1430 pins) short-circuits to `emptyShadowDicts` there anyway.
  | isNone (methodDispatchIdx env.teDyn.dcModule name)
    && standaloneValuePinned env name =
    pushSiteGoal
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
      GKRLocalSite
      innerRef
      (PendingEntry
        name
        tagRef
        inst
        env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn.value
        (SKRLocal (routeLocalSym !tagRef) True [] [] [])
        env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
        (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
        (freshEvId env.teDyn.dcModule ()))
  | not (omHasKey name env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.standaloneValuesRef.value) =
    ()
  | otherwise = match methodDispatchIdx env.teDyn.dcModule name
    None => ()
    Some idx => match nthArgMono idx inst
      Some am =>
        let sym = routeLocalSym !tagRef
        let dicts =
          shadowStandaloneDictSlotsAt
            env.teDyn
            (standaloneValueFor env name sym)
            name
            (if sym == "" then name else sym)
            am
        pushSiteGoal
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
          GKRLocalSite
          innerRef
          (PendingEntry
            name
            tagRef
            am
            env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn.value
            (SKRLocal
              sym
              (standaloneValuePinned env name)
              dicts.sdMonos
              dicts.sdIfaces
              dicts.sdArgVecs)
            env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
            (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
            (freshEvId env.teDyn.dcModule ()))
      None => ()

-- A method-layer binding retains the standalone scheme it masks. Recover that
-- exact scheme, including forcing effects, before trying a routed symbol.
standaloneSchemeFor : TcEnv -> String -> String -> Option Scheme
standaloneSchemeFor env name sym =
  map (value => value.vsScheme) (standaloneValueFor env name sym)

standaloneOccurrence : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Option Loc ->
  Option SelectedValueOccurrence
standaloneOccurrence env name sym origin =
  map
    (instantiateStandaloneOccurrence env name sym origin)
    (standaloneValueFor env name sym)

-- Phase 69.x-e: if [name] is a method with method-level constraints (foldMap's
-- `Monoid m`), map each constraint's scheme id through this occurrence's
-- instantiation subst to its concrete mono and record the (methodRef, monos) so
-- resolveMethodDicts can route them after inference.  A method with no method-level
-- constraint records nothing — methodRef stays [], eval's fold is a no-op.
recordMethodDicts : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Ref Inner ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  Unit
recordMethodDicts mctx name methodRef innerRef subst =
  match methodIfaceHere mctx name
    None => ()
    Some iface =>
      match (lookupMethodPredicateSlots
        (methodSlotKey iface (originMethodName mctx name))
        mctx.mcCells.methodPredicateSlotsRef.value)
        None => ()
        Some slots =>
          recordMethodDictsFromSlots mctx slots methodRef innerRef subst

recordMethodDictsFromSlots : ModuleCtx ->
  List MethodPredicateSlot ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Ref Inner ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  Unit
recordMethodDictsFromSlots mctx slots methodRef innerRef subst = pushMethodDictGoal
  mctx.mcGraph
  PendingMethodDict {
    pmdRoutesRef = methodRef,
    pmdEv = freshEvId mctx (),
    pmdSlots = instantiateMethodPredicateSlots mctx.mcGraph slots subst,
    pmdEncl = mctx.mcCells.currentFn.value,
    pmdScope = captureScope mctx (),
    pmdInner = innerRef,
  }

instantiateMethodPredicateSlots : GraphCtx ->
  List MethodPredicateSlot ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  List PredicateSlot
instantiateMethodPredicateSlots gctx [] _ = []
instantiateMethodPredicateSlots gctx (slot :: rest) subst =
  match instantiateMethodPredicateSlot gctx slot subst
    Some pred => pred :: instantiateMethodPredicateSlots gctx rest subst
    None => instantiateMethodPredicateSlots gctx rest subst

instantiateMethodPredicateSlot : GraphCtx ->
  MethodPredicateSlot ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  Option PredicateSlot
instantiateMethodPredicateSlot gctx slot subst =
  map
    (instantiatedMethodPredicate gctx slot subst)
    (methodSlotSubst slot.mpsPredicate.psBoundIds slot.mpsPositions subst)

instantiatedMethodPredicate : GraphCtx ->
  MethodPredicateSlot ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  PredicateSlot
instantiatedMethodPredicate gctx slot subst slotSubst =
  let args2 =
    instantiatedMethodPredicateArgs gctx slot.mpsPredicate.psArgs slotSubst
  PredicateSlot {
    psIface = slot.mpsPredicate.psIface,
    psArgs = args2,
    psBoundIds = map (p => nthInt p (map fst subst)) slot.mpsPositions,
  }

instantiatedMethodPredicateArgs : GraphCtx ->
  PredicateSlotArgs ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  PredicateSlotArgs
instantiatedMethodPredicateArgs gctx PSArgsUnknown _ = PSArgsUnknown
instantiatedMethodPredicateArgs gctx (PSArgsKnown args) subst =
  PSArgsKnown (map (substMono gctx subst [] []) args)

methodSlotSubst : List Int ->
  List Int ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  Option (List (Int, Mono))
methodSlotSubst ids positions subst =
  let vals = map snd subst
  let n = listLen subst
  if listLen ids == listLen positions && allInRange positions n then
    Some (zipMethodSlotSubst ids positions vals)
  else
    None

zipMethodSlotSubst : List Int -> List Int -> List Mono -> List (Int, Mono)
zipMethodSlotSubst [] _ _ = []
zipMethodSlotSubst _ [] _ = []
zipMethodSlotSubst (id :: ids) (pos :: positions) vals =
  (id, nthMethodMono pos vals) :: zipMethodSlotSubst ids positions vals

allInRange : List Int -> Int -> Bool
allInRange [] _ = True
allInRange (p :: rest) n = p >= 0 && p < n && allInRange rest n

nthInt : Int -> List Int -> Int
nthInt _ [] = 0 - 1
nthInt 0 (x :: _) = x
nthInt i (_ :: xs) = nthInt (i - 1) xs

nthMethodMono : Int -> List Mono -> Mono
nthMethodMono _ [] = tconUnresolved "__missing_method_slot__"
nthMethodMono 0 (x :: _) = x
nthMethodMono i (_ :: xs) = nthMethodMono (i - 1) xs

-- record a return-position method occurrence: resolveSite later stamps its route
-- (RKey/RDict) once inference grounds the result mono.  An admitted-set occurrence
-- (`admittedSetOccurrence`) records the set's obligation and a site its commit
-- stamps (`resolveAdmittedSite`), both decided by the one test here.
recordSite : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  Scheme ->
  Ref String ->
  Ref Route ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Ref Inner ->
  Mono ->
  MethodInstantiationSubst ->
  Mono
recordSite env name scheme ifaceRef tagRef implRef methodRef innerRef methodType subst =
  let stripped = stripArrows methodType
  let ev = freshEvId env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let exactRow = exactReturnRow env name scheme
  let admitted = isNone exactRow && admittedSetOccurrence env name scheme
  let exact =
    map
      (row =>
        methodReturnRequest env.teDyn.dcModule row methodType subst (Some ev))
      exactRow
  let _ = match (exact, exactRow)
    (Some request, Some row) =>
      let _ =
        recordMethodLevelSlotsOwned
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          row
          subst.misTypeSubst
          request.mrrLoc
          request.mrrScope
      let _ = recordExactMethodObligation env.teDyn.dcModule request
      if isEmptyL row.msrMethodSlots then
        ()
      else
        recordMethodDictsFromSlots
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          row.msrMethodSlots
          methodRef
          innerRef
          subst.misTypeSubst
    _ =>
      let _ =
        if admitted then
          pushAdmittedOccObl env.teDyn.dcModule name methodType
        else
          let _ = recordMethodObligationGuarded env name scheme methodType []
          ()
      recordMethodDicts
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        name
        methodRef
        innerRef
        subst.misTypeSubst
  let siteEv = match exact
    Some request => optionOr ev request.mrrGoalEv
    None => ev
  pushSiteGoal
    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
    GKReturnSite
    innerRef
    (PendingEntry
      name
      tagRef
      stripped
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn.value
      (match exact
        Some request => SKExactReturn implRef request
        None =>
          if admitted then
            SKAdmittedReturn ifaceRef implRef methodType
          else
            SKReturn implRef methodType)
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
      (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
      siteEv)
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.methodSiteFns :=
    consSiteFn
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn.value
      stripped
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.methodSiteFns.value
  methodType

recordNumLitSite : ModuleCtx ->
  ClassPredicate ->
  Ref Route ->
  Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Mono
recordNumLitSite mctx predicate tagRef occurrence origin scope =
  let stripped = stripArrows occurrence
  pushSiteGoal
    mctx.mcGraph
    GKReturnSite
    (Ref innerNone)
    (PendingEntry
      "fromInt"
      tagRef
      stripped
      mctx.mcCells.currentFn.value
      (SKNumReturn predicate occurrence)
      origin
      scope
      (freshEvId mctx ()))
  mctx.mcCells.methodSiteFns :=
    consSiteFn
      mctx.mcCells.currentFn.value
      stripped
      mctx.mcCells.methodSiteFns.value
  occurrence

freshLocalAbsName : GraphCtx -> String -> String
freshLocalAbsName gctx x =
  let st = gctx.graphRun.localAbs
  let (mid, k) = st.lasNext.value
  let name = "\{x}$\{mid}$\{intToString k}$lb"
  st.lasNext := (mid, k + 1)
  st.lasMinted := name :: st.lasMinted.value
  name

isLocalAbsName : String -> Bool
isLocalAbsName n = endsWith "$lb" n

-- The name a candidate local was written with (`f` for `f$m$3$lb`); `$` never occurs in
-- a source identifier.
localSourceName : String -> String
localSourceName name
  | isLocalAbsName name = match splitOnChar '$' name
    first :: _ => first
    [] => name
  | otherwise = name

localAbsFor : GraphCtx -> String -> Option LocalAbs
localAbsFor gctx name =
  match omLookup name gctx.graphRun.localAbs.lasBinders.value
    Some found => found
    None => None

-- Forget what a previous inference of the same binder left, before any member of
-- its group is inferred (a group member's body records its siblings' uses): an
-- earlier inference in this drive, or a check of the module id in an earlier one.
forgetLocalAbs : GraphCtx -> String -> Unit
forgetLocalAbs gctx name =
  forgetLocalRows gctx.graphRun.localAbs gctx.graphRun.grants name

-- Enter a candidate local binder's own scope before its right-hand side is
-- inferred.
openLocalScope : ModuleCtx -> String -> ScopeId
openLocalScope mctx name =
  let parent = captureScope mctx ()
  let sid =
    Scopes.freshScope
      (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
      (Some parent)
      mctx.mcCells.currentLevel.value
      (Scopes.scopeFrame (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ()) parent).sfModuleId
      (LocalBindingOwner name)
  let _ = openScope mctx sid
  sid

-- The candidate local's scope, opened when the binder is a candidate.
openLocalScopeIf : ModuleCtx -> String -> Option ScopeId
openLocalScopeIf mctx name
  | isLocalAbsName name =
    let _ = forgetLocalAbs mctx.mcGraph name
    Some (openLocalScope mctx name)
  | otherwise = None

closeLocalScope : ModuleCtx -> Option ScopeId -> Unit
closeLocalScope mctx (Some _) = closeScope mctx ()
closeLocalScope mctx None = ()

registerLocalAbsIf : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  Option ScopeId ->
  Scheme ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  Unit
registerLocalAbsIf mctx name lscope sch oblN0 callN0 =
  let _ = recordLocalQuantified mctx.mcGraph sch
  match lscope
    Some scope =>
      let _ = registerLocalGrants mctx.mcGraph name sch
      registerLocalAbs mctx name scope sch oblN0 callN0
    None => ()

-- A generalized local's quantified variables stay in the enclosing binding's
-- obligation window, but they are the scheme's now: each use instantiates them
-- afresh, and the enclosing boundary's defaulting must reach those instances,
-- never the scheme's own variables.  Grounding one would fix the local at one
-- type behind every use and select one dictionary for two predicates (#3516).
recordLocalQuantified : GraphCtx -> Scheme -> Unit
recordLocalQuantified gctx sch = match schemeIds sch
  [] => ()
  ids =>
    let st = gctx.graphRun.localAbs
    st.lasQuantified := omFromNames (map intToString ids) st.lasQuantified.value

-- After a candidate local generalized: the predicates its scheme quantifies become
-- its dictionary parameters, registered as givens of its own scope so the sites in
-- its body read them; occurrences inferred before generalization (recursive uses)
-- are applied to those same parameters.
registerLocalAbs : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Scheme ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  Unit
registerLocalAbs mctx name lscope sch oblN0 callN0 =
  let boundIds = schemeIds sch
  let slots =
    if isEmptyL boundIds then
      []
    else
      localAbsSlots mctx name boundIds oblN0 callN0
  let st = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.localAbs
  let recOccs = optionOr [] (omLookup name st.lasRecOccs.value)
  st.lasRecOccs := omDelete name st.lasRecOccs.value
  match slots
    [] => st.lasBinders := omInsert name None st.lasBinders.value
    _ =>
      let _ = registerSlotPredGivens mctx.mcGraph lscope 0 slots
      let _ = registerActiveDictVars mctx.mcGraph lscope 0 slots
      let la = LocalAbs {
        laScope = lscope,
        laSlots = slots,
        laParams = localAbsParams mctx.mcGraph lscope 0 slots,
      }
      st.lasBinders := omInsert name (Some la) st.lasBinders.value
      fold
        (_ occ => pushLocalDictApp mctx name (fst occ) la [] (snd occ))
        ()
        recOccs

localAbsSlots : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List Int ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List PredicateSlot
localAbsSlots mctx name boundIds oblN0 callN0 =
  let addedObls = wWindow mctx.mcCells.implObls oblN0
  let callObls = callOblsWindow mctx callN0
  let preds =
    flatMap (oblPredOf mctx.mcGraph) addedObls ++ flatMap callPredOf callObls
  let vecs =
    directInferredPreds boundIds preds
      ++ residualInferredPreds mctx boundIds preds
  inferredPredicateSlots mctx name (dedupI (map inferredPredLead vecs)) vecs

localAbsParams : GraphCtx -> ScopeId -> Int -> List PredicateSlot -> List String
localAbsParams gctx _ _ [] = []
localAbsParams gctx lscope i (_ :: rest) =
  renderEvidenceBinder gctx (Scopes.binderAt lscope i)
    :: localAbsParams gctx lscope (i + 1) rest

-- One dictionary application of a local: each slot's predicate at the occurrence's
-- instantiation [subst] (empty for a recursive use, whose predicate is the binder's
-- own), solved in the occurrence's scope.
pushLocalDictApp : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  EvId ->
  LocalAbs ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
pushLocalDictApp mctx name ev la subst useScope =
  let monos = map (localSlotLead mctx subst) la.laSlots
  let _ = pushDictApp mctx.mcGraph PendingDictApp {
    pdaRoutesRef = Ref [],
    pdaEv = ev,
    pdaMonos = monos,
    pdaIfaces = map (s => s.psIface) la.laSlots,
    pdaArgVecs = map (localSlotArgs mctx subst) la.laSlots,
    pdaEncl = mctx.mcCells.currentFn.value,
    pdaLoc = mctx.mcLoc,
    pdaScope = useScope,
    pdaCallee = localSourceName name,
  }
  mctx.mcCells.dictAppFns :=
    consSiteFn mctx.mcCells.currentFn.value monos mctx.mcCells.dictAppFns.value

localSlotArgs : ModuleCtx -> List (Int, Mono) -> PredicateSlot -> List Mono
localSlotArgs mctx subst slot = match slot.psArgs
  PSArgsKnown args => map (substMono mctx.mcGraph subst [] []) args
  PSArgsUnknown => [localSlotLead mctx subst slot]

localSlotLead : ModuleCtx -> List (Int, Mono) -> PredicateSlot -> Mono
localSlotLead mctx subst slot = match slot.psArgs
  PSArgsKnown (a :: _) => substMono mctx.mcGraph subst [] [] a
  _ => match slot.psBoundIds
    id :: _ => optionOr (freshVar mctx ()) (lookupAssocI id subst)
    [] => freshVar mctx ()

-- An occurrence of a candidate local.  Once its binder has generalized with
-- predicates the occurrence instantiates them; before that (a recursive use) it is
-- recorded for `registerLocalAbs`.
inferLocalDictAt : TcEnv -> String -> EvId -> Mono
inferLocalDictAt env name ev =
  match (omLookup
    name
    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph.graphRun.localAbs.lasBinders.value)
    Some (Some la) => match lookupVar env name
      Some s =>
        let inst = instantiateVarTrackedWithSubst env name 0 s
        let _ =
          pushLocalDictApp
            env.teDyn.dcModule
            name
            ev
            la
            inst.mtiSubstitution.misTypeSubst
            (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
        inst.mtiBody
      None => unboundVarFresh env.teDyn.dcModule name
    Some None => inferVarId env name 0
    None =>
      let _ = recordLocalRecOcc env.teDyn.dcModule name ev
      inferVarId env name 0

recordLocalRecOcc : ModuleCtx -> String -> EvId -> Unit
recordLocalRecOcc mctx name ev =
  let st = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.localAbs
  let occs =
    (ev, captureScope mctx ())
      :: optionOr [] (omLookup name st.lasRecOccs.value)
  st.lasRecOccs := omInsert name occs st.lasRecOccs.value

-- dict_pass for locals: an abstracted binder takes its dictionary parameters, and an
-- occurrence of a binder that abstracted nothing is a plain variable again.
rewriteLocalDictExpr : GraphCtx -> Expr -> Expr
rewriteLocalDictExpr gctx (EDictAt n ev)
  | isLocalAbsName n = match localAbsFor gctx n
    Some _ => EDictAt n ev
    None => EVar n
  | otherwise = EDictAt n ev
rewriteLocalDictExpr gctx (ELet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e1 e2) =
  match localAbsFor gctx x
    Some la => ELet m r (PVar x xloc bid) (prependLocalDicts la.laParams e1) e2
    None => ELet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e1 e2
rewriteLocalDictExpr gctx (ELetGroup binds body) =
  ELetGroup (map (rewriteLocalLetBind gctx) binds) body
rewriteLocalDictExpr gctx (EBlock stmts) =
  EBlock (map (rewriteLocalDoStmt gctx) stmts)
rewriteLocalDictExpr gctx e = e

rewriteLocalLetBind : GraphCtx -> LetBind -> LetBind
rewriteLocalLetBind gctx (LetBind n clauses site bid) = match localAbsFor gctx n
  Some la =>
    LetBind n (map (prependLocalDictClause la.laParams) clauses) site bid
  None => LetBind n clauses site bid

prependLocalDictClause : List String -> FunClause -> FunClause
prependLocalDictClause params (FunClause pats body) =
  FunClause (map localDictPat params ++ pats) body

rewriteLocalDoStmt : GraphCtx -> DoStmt -> DoStmt
rewriteLocalDoStmt gctx (DoLet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e site) =
  match localAbsFor gctx x
    Some la =>
      DoLet m r (PVar x xloc bid) (prependLocalDicts la.laParams e) site
    None => DoLet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e site
rewriteLocalDoStmt gctx stmt = stmt

prependLocalDicts : List String -> Expr -> Expr
prependLocalDicts params (ELoc l e) = ELoc l (prependLocalDicts params e)
prependLocalDicts params (ELam pats body) =
  ELam (map localDictPat params ++ pats) body
prependLocalDicts params e = ELam (map localDictPat params) e

localDictPat : String -> Pat
localDictPat n = PVar n (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId

inferDictAt : TcEnv -> String -> EvId -> Mono
inferDictAt env name ev
  | isLocalAbsName name = inferLocalDictAt env name ev
  | otherwise = inferGlobalDictAt env name ev

inferGlobalDictAt : TcEnv -> String -> EvId -> Mono
inferGlobalDictAt env name ev = match lookupVar env name
  None => panic ("unbound constrained fn: " ++ name)
  Some scheme =>
    let inst = instantiateValueTracked env.teDyn.dcModule name scheme
    let occurrence = (inst.mtiBody, inst.mtiSubstitution.misTypeSubst)
    match bindingDeclaredAt env name inst
      Some dc => inferDeclaredDictAt env.teDyn.dcModule name ev dc occurrence
      None => inferDictAtFound env.teDyn.dcModule name ev occurrence

-- The catalog externs whose authority parameter names a file path
-- (`stdlib/runtime.mdk`), each with its value arity and the number of paths it
-- names.  No other extern takes a grant: a foreign function is not a
-- parameterized file extern.
fileGrantExterns : OrdMap (Int, Int)
fileGrantExterns = RuntimeGrants.fileGrantExterns

-- A program lowered without elaboration (the prelude-free emitter probes) has no
-- inference to solve a grant from: each file extern it names is granted the
-- whole domain, and saturated as elaboration saturates it.  The parameter names
-- come from the process's grant counter (the interners' lineage), which the next
-- drive continues.
export
grantWholeDomain : List Decl -> List Decl
grantWholeDomain prog =
  map (mapDeclBodies (wholeDomainExpr interners.value.lineage.lnGrants)) prog

wholeDomainExpr : GrantState -> Expr -> Expr
wholeDomainExpr st (e@(EApp _ _)) = match grantSpine e []
  (EVar n, args) => match omLookup n fileGrantExterns
    Some (arity, paths) =>
      saturateGrants
        st
        (EVar n)
        arity
        (replicate paths (EListLit []))
        (map (wholeDomainExpr st) args)
    None => mapChildren (wholeDomainExpr st) e
  _ => mapChildren (wholeDomainExpr st) e
wholeDomainExpr st (EVar n) = match omLookup n fileGrantExterns
  Some (arity, paths) =>
    saturateGrants st (EVar n) arity (replicate paths (EListLit [])) []
  None => EVar n
-- every other node: its children, through the one traversal every pass shares
wholeDomainExpr st e = mapChildren (wholeDomainExpr st) e

-- Apply [f] once to the root of every expression a declaration holds.
export
mapDeclBodies : (Expr -> Expr) -> Decl -> Decl
mapDeclBodies f (DFunDef pub n ps e site bid) = DFunDef pub n ps (f e) site bid
mapDeclBodies f (DLetGroup pub binds) =
  DLetGroup
    pub
    (map
      (b => match b
        LetBind n clauses site bid =>
          LetBind
            n
            (map
              (c => match c
                FunClause ps e => FunClause ps (f e))
              clauses)
            site
            bid)
      binds)
mapDeclBodies f (d@(DInterface { methods, ... })) = DInterface { d |
  methods =
    map
      (m => match m
        IfaceMethod n ty def mloc =>
          IfaceMethod
            n
            ty
            (map
              (dm => match dm
                MethodDefault ps e => MethodDefault ps (f e))
              def)
            mloc)
      methods,
}
mapDeclBodies f (d@(DImpl { methods, ... })) = DImpl { d |
  methods =
    map
      (m => match m
        ImplMethod n ps e => ImplMethod n ps (f e))
      methods,
}
mapDeclBodies f (DProp pub name params body) = DProp pub name params (f body)
mapDeclBodies f (DTest pub name body) = DTest pub name (f body)
mapDeclBodies f (DAttrib attrs d) = DAttrib attrs (mapDeclBodies f d)
-- a declaration with no expression body (data, signatures, imports, externs)
mapDeclBodies _ d = d

-- Grants are passed only on a graph whose driver ran the marking preamble: a
-- driver that never marks has no use that could carry one.
grantsEnabled : GraphCtx -> Unit -> Bool
grantsEnabled gctx _ = isSome gctx.markSetsRef.value

-- What a use of [name] in the module being marked denotes.  An extern the module
-- declares or imports is a foreign declaration, and one spelled like a catalog
-- file extern binds that same runtime operation (a redeclaration must agree with
-- the catalog row); any other value the module defines or imports is a source
-- binding; a name the module neither defines nor imports is the catalog extern
-- when the catalog declares it.
grantCalleeOf : ModuleCtx -> String -> GrantCallee
grantCalleeOf mctx name
  | isLocalAbsName name = SourceCallee
  | otherwise = match mctx.mcCells.markingRef.value
    Some mm =>
      if omHasKey name mm.mmExterns then
        externCallee name
      else if omHasKey name mm.mmUserNames then
        SourceCallee
      else
        catalogCallee mctx.mcGraph name
    None => catalogCallee mctx.mcGraph name

catalogCallee : GraphCtx -> String -> GrantCallee
catalogCallee gctx name =
  if omHasKey name gctx.builtinExternNamesRef.value then
    externCallee name
  else
    SourceCallee

externCallee : String -> GrantCallee
externCallee name =
  if omHasKey name fileGrantExterns then FileExternCallee else NoGrantCallee

-- Whether the marker gives a use of [n] a grant identity: the binding [n] denotes
-- in [env] is a value, not an interface method (whose uses are method
-- occurrences), that takes grants, and its own scheme quantifies an authority.
grantNameIn : TcEnv -> String -> Bool
grantNameIn env n
  | not (grantsEnabled env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ()) = False
  | otherwise = match lookupBinding env n
    Some b => match b.ebMethodRow
      Some _ => False
      None =>
        calleeTakesGrants (grantCalleeOf env.teDyn.dcModule n)
          && isNonEmptyL (schemeAuthIds b.ebValue.vsScheme)
    None => False

calleeTakesGrants : GrantCallee -> Bool
calleeTakesGrants SourceCallee = True
calleeTakesGrants FileExternCallee = True
calleeTakesGrants NoGrantCallee = False

-- A scheme's quantified authorities in grant order: first occurrence in the
-- type read left to right (an arrow's domain, its row, its result), so a
-- scheme and every copy of it list them alike whatever ids they carry.
grantOrder : Scheme -> List Int
grantOrder (Forall _ _ [] _ _ _) = []
grantOrder (Forall _ _ avars _ force body) =
  let seen = reverseL (authOrderRow force (authOrderIn body []))
  let quantified = filterList (i => containsI i avars) seen
  quantified ++ filterList (i => not (containsI i quantified)) avars

-- How many grants a top-level binding with this scheme takes ahead of its value
-- arguments.
export
bindingGrantArity : DriveOutputs -> String -> Scheme -> Int
bindingGrantArity o _ sch =
  if o.doGrantsEnabled then listLen (grantOrder sch) else 0

-- Mint a use node for a name that takes no dictionary, so its grants have an
-- identity to be recorded under.
mintGrantOnly : ModuleCtx -> String -> Expr
mintGrantOnly mctx n =
  let ev = freshEvId mctx ()
  let st = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.grants
  st.gsGrantOnly := IdMap.set (evOrdinal ev) () st.gsGrantOnly.value
  EDictAt n ev

isGrantOnlyEv : GraphCtx -> EvId -> Bool
isGrantOnlyEv gctx ev =
  IdMap.has (evOrdinal ev) gctx.graphRun.grants.gsGrantOnly.value

-- A grant-only use that became a dictionary application (a recursive use of a
-- member its group just promoted).
unmarkGrantOnly : GraphCtx -> EvId -> Unit
unmarkGrantOnly gctx ev =
  let st = gctx.graphRun.grants
  st.gsGrantOnly := IdMap.delete (evOrdinal ev) st.gsGrantOnly.value

grantOccOf : GraphCtx -> EvId -> Option GrantOcc
grantOccOf gctx ev = IdMap.get (evOrdinal ev) gctx.graphRun.grants.gsOccs.value

setGrantOcc : GraphCtx -> EvId -> GrantOcc -> Unit
setGrantOcc gctx ev occ =
  let st = gctx.graphRun.grants
  st.gsOccs := IdMap.set (evOrdinal ev) occ st.gsOccs.value

-- An `EDictAt` use: a dictionary application, a grant-only use, or both.  The
-- instantiation inference makes for it is recorded for its grants; a grant-only
-- use is inferred exactly as the stamped variable it stands for.
inferGrantedAt : TcEnv -> String -> EvId -> Mono
inferGrantedAt env name ev =
  let st = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph.graphRun.grants
  st.gsLastInst := None
  let t =
    if isGrantOnlyEv env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ev then
      inferVarId env name (grantOnlyBindingId env.teDyn.dcModule name)
    else
      inferDictAt env name ev
  let _ = match st.gsLastInst.value
    Some (scheme, subst) =>
      recordGrantOcc env.teDyn.dcModule name ev scheme subst
    None => ()
  t

-- The binding id resolve's stamp would have given this use: its top-level
-- binder's, or 0 for an imported name.
grantOnlyBindingId : ModuleCtx -> String -> Int
grantOnlyBindingId mctx name = match mctx.mcCells.markingRef.value
  Some mm => optionOr 0 (omLookup name mm.mmTop)
  None => 0

recordGrantOcc : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  EvId ->
  Scheme ->
  List (Int, Authority) ->
  Unit
recordGrantOcc mctx name ev (scheme@(Forall _ _ _ _ _ body)) subst =
  match grantCalleeOf mctx name
    NoGrantCallee => ()
    SourceCallee => recordOccWith mctx name ev scheme subst None False
    FileExternCallee =>
      recordOccWith mctx name ev scheme subst (Some (arrowArity body)) False

-- A method candidate's use: its grants follow its value arguments.
recordMethodGrantOcc : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  EvId ->
  Scheme ->
  List (Int, Authority) ->
  Unit
recordMethodGrantOcc mctx name ev (scheme@(Forall _ _ _ _ _ body)) subst =
  recordOccWith mctx name ev scheme subst (Some (arrowArity body)) False

-- A method occurrence typed as the standalone binding its name shadows: that
-- binding's grants, leading its arguments.
recordStandaloneGrantOcc : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  EvId ->
  Scheme ->
  List (Int, Authority) ->
  Int ->
  Unit
recordStandaloneGrantOcc mctx name ev scheme subst arity =
  recordOccWith mctx name ev scheme subst (Some arity) True

recordOccWith : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  EvId ->
  Scheme ->
  List (Int, Authority) ->
  Option Int ->
  Bool ->
  Unit
recordOccWith mctx name ev scheme subst trailing standalone =
  match grantOrder scheme
    [] => ()
    ids => setGrantOcc mctx.mcGraph ev GrantOcc {
      goCallee = name,
      goCells = map (i => optionOr (AJoin []) (lookupAssocI i subst)) ids,
      goRecIds = [],
      goTrailing = trailing,
      goChain = grantChainAt mctx.mcGraph (captureScope mctx ()),
      goStandalone = standalone,
    }

-- The evidence id of the method occurrence heading an application spine.
spineHeadEv : Expr -> Option EvId
spineHeadEv (ELoc _ e) = spineHeadEv e
spineHeadEv (EApp f _) = spineHeadEv f
spineHeadEv (EMethodAt _ _ ev) = Some ev
-- any other head is not a method occurrence
spineHeadEv _ = None

-- A shadow application's head, typed as the standalone [occurrence] selected.
recordStandaloneAt : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  Expr ->
  SelectedValueOccurrence ->
  Unit
recordStandaloneAt mctx name hd occurrence = match spineHeadEv hd
  Some ev =>
    recordStandaloneGrantOcc
      mctx
      name
      ev
      occurrence.svoScheme
      occurrence.svoInstance.mtiSubstitution.misAuthSubst
      (funArity occurrence.svoInstance.mtiBody)
  None => ()

methodGrantOf : GraphCtx -> String -> String -> Option MethodGrant
methodGrantOf gctx ifaceWord method =
  omLookup
    (methodGrantKey ifaceWord method)
    gctx.graphRun.grants.gsMethods.value

-- The interface methods a module declares whose type quantifies authorities; any
-- other method it declares has no row, whatever an earlier check of the module id
-- left.  The grants follow the arrows the written type spells, since that declared
-- arity is what the backends read; a result an alias names a function stays the
-- result.
recordMethodGrants : GraphCtx -> List MethodSchemeRow -> Unit
recordMethodGrants gctx rows =
  let st = gctx.graphRun.grants
  st.gsMethods :=
    fold
      (acc row =>
        let key =
          methodGrantKey
            (ifaceWordOf row.msrIface.irOrigin row.msrIface.irName)
            row.msrName
        match methodGrantOfRow row
          Some mg => omInsert key mg acc
          None => omDelete key acc)
      st.gsMethods.value
      rows

methodGrantOfRow : MethodSchemeRow -> Option MethodGrant
methodGrantOfRow row = match row.msrScheme
  Forall _ _ _ _ force body => match grantOrder row.msrScheme
    [] => None
    ids =>
      let cells = authCellsIn body (authRowCells force Tip)
      Some MethodGrant {
        mgArity = tyArrowCount row.msrType,
        mgNames =
          map
            (i => match IdMap.get i cells
              Some cell => optionOr "" (authvarName cell)
              None => "")
            ids,
      }

-- A method body's own authority binders, bound by the body's grant parameters.
-- The instance head's cells are no caller's to supply.  Every other authority
-- variable of the instantiated type is the method's own, and they occur in the
-- order `grantOrder` reads the method's scheme in, since both are the one written
-- type read left to right: the k-th of them is the k-th grant, whatever it is
-- called.
registerMethodBodyGrants : GraphCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  String ->
  List Mono ->
  MethodBodyInstance ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
registerMethodBodyGrants gctx iface mname heads inst (ScopeId sid) =
