    mctx.mcCells.methodPredicateSlotsRef.value)
    Some (_ :: _) => Unroutable iface
    _ => answer
routableSelection mctx _ answer = answer

admittedDeclAnswer : SiteCtx ->
  ImplEnv ->
  List MethodRow ->
  Mono ->
  IfaceRef ->
  AdmittedAnswer
admittedDeclAnswer sx env visible mono ir =
  match filterList (r => ieRowIfaceMatches (methodRowIface r) ir) visible
    r :: _ => match r.mrEntry
      (iface, typarams, mty, _) => match matchTyMono mty mono
        Some subst =>
          let goals = map (paramMonoOf subst) typarams
          match goalHeadCon goals
            None => Undecided
            Some _ => match ieSelectRowByIface sx env iface goals
              Some row => Selects iface row goals
              None => SelectsNothing
        None => Undecided
    [] => Undecided

isUndecided : AdmittedAnswer -> Bool
isUndecided Undecided = True
isUndecided _ = False

isSelection : AdmittedAnswer -> Bool
isSelection (Selects _ _ _) = True
isSelection _ = False

-- The receiver named in the no-impl reject: the first admitted declaration's own
-- receiver argument.
admittedReceiverMono : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List IfaceRef ->
  Mono ->
  Option Mono
admittedReceiverMono mctx _ [] _ = None
admittedReceiverMono mctx name (ir :: _) mono = do
  k <- lookupIdxById ir name mctx.mcCells.methodDispatchIdxByIdRef.value
  nthArgMono k mono

-- An occurrence whose obligation is its admitted set's rather than one
-- declaration's: a spelling with two or more admitted declarations, written where
-- neither a local (`recordMethodObligationGuarded`) nor a standalone shadow
-- (`recordImplObligation`) binds it.
admittedSetOccurrence : TcEnv -> String -> Scheme -> Bool
admittedSetOccurrence env name s =
  not
      (lookupLocalFlag env name
        || isMonoScheme s
        || omHasKey name env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.definerShadowNamesRef.value
        || omHasKey name env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.standaloneValuesRef.value)
    && listLen (methodAdmittedHere env.teDyn.dcModule name) >= 2

recordMethodObligationGuarded : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  Scheme ->
  Mono ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Mono
recordMethodObligationGuarded env name s mono omitted =
  if lookupLocalFlag env name || isMonoScheme s then
    mono
  else
    recordImplObligation env.teDyn.dcModule name mono omitted

exactReturnRow : TcEnv -> String -> Scheme -> Option MethodSchemeRow
exactReturnRow env name scheme = match lookupMethodRow env name
  None => None
  Some row =>
    if lookupLocalFlag env name
      || isMonoScheme scheme
      || omHasKey name env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.definerShadowNamesRef.value
      || omHasKey name env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.standaloneValuesRef.value
      || isSome
        (Scopes.enclosingDefaultBody
          (currentScopeStore env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ())
          (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()))
      || listLen (methodAdmittedHere env.teDyn.dcModule name) >= 2 then
      None
    else
      Some row

recordMethodObligationOwned : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  Scheme ->
  Mono ->
  MethodInstantiationSubst ->
  Option EvId ->
  Mono
recordMethodObligationOwned env name scheme occurrence subst goalEv =
  match exactReturnRow env name scheme
    Some row =>
      let request =
        methodReturnRequest env.teDyn.dcModule row occurrence subst goalEv
      let _ =
        recordMethodLevelSlotsOwned
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          row
          subst.misTypeSubst
          request.mrrLoc
          request.mrrScope
      recordExactMethodObligation env.teDyn.dcModule request
    None => recordMethodObligationGuarded env name scheme occurrence []

recordExactMethodObligation : ModuleCtx -> MethodReturnRequest -> Mono
recordExactMethodObligation mctx request =
  let _ = noteMethodReturnTrace mctx MRTProduced request None []
  let _ = pushExactReturnObl mctx request
  request.mrrOccurrence

recordMethodLevelSlotsOwned : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
recordMethodLevelSlotsOwned mctx row subst loc scope =
  recordInstantiatedMethodLevelSlots
    mctx
    (instantiateMethodPredicateSlots mctx.mcGraph row.msrMethodSlots subst)
    loc
    scope

recordInstantiatedMethodLevelSlots : ModuleCtx ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
recordInstantiatedMethodLevelSlots mctx [] _ _ = ()
recordInstantiatedMethodLevelSlots mctx (slot :: rest) loc scope =
  let _ = match slot.psArgs
    PSArgsUnknown => ()
    PSArgsKnown args =>
      recordOblAt
        mctx
        Predicate { iface = slot.psIface, args = args }
        0
        PMethodLevel
        loc
        scope
  recordInstantiatedMethodLevelSlots mctx rest loc scope

-- A numeric literal's checking obligation and method-level slots come from its
-- identity-selected method row; no bare-name table reconstructs the class and no
-- binding's spelling suppresses it.
recordNumLitObligationGuarded : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  ClassPredicate ->
  Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Mono
recordNumLitObligationGuarded mctx anchor predicate occurrence origin scope =
  if isMonoScheme anchor.msrScheme then
    occurrence
  else
    recordNumLitImplObligation mctx anchor predicate occurrence origin scope

recordNumLitImplObligation : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  ClassPredicate ->
  Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Mono
recordNumLitImplObligation mctx anchor predicate occurrence origin scope =
  let _ = pushNumLitObl mctx predicate occurrence origin scope
  let _ =
    recordMethodLevelObls mctx anchor.msrTyparams anchor.msrType occurrence
  occurrence

-- #818 (#838 I3): record one PMethodLevel obligation per method-level `=>` constraint
-- slot of a method occurrence.  [mty] is the method's DECLARED type (with its `=>`);
-- [occMono] is THIS occurrence's instantiated (constraint-free) type.  Align the
-- declared function spine (constraints/effects stripped) against [occMono] with
-- matchTyMono to recover each constraint var's concrete mono, then record the
-- constraint's whole argument vector under that substitution (`Show2 (f Int)` at
-- `f := Box` poses `Show2 (Box Int)`, not `Show2 Box`).  matchTyMono captures the
-- live tyvar cell, so a slot still a fresh var at record time normalizes to its
-- solved head at check time — a ground head (`NoOrd`) with no impl is rejected
-- `T-NO-IMPL`; a still-generalized var defers into the scheme
-- (`undeterminedGoalExempt`), uniform with every other obligation.  No slots ⇒ nothing
-- recorded (the receiver-only-method common case), and a shape mismatch (matchTyMono
-- None) records nothing — never a false reject.
recordMethodLevelObls : ModuleCtx -> List String -> Ty -> Mono -> Unit
recordMethodLevelObls mctx typarams mty occMono =
  let slots = methodLevelConstraintSlots typarams mty
  if isEmptyL slots then
    ()
  else match matchTyMono (stripLeadingMethodConstraints mty) occMono
    None => ()
    Some subst => recordMethodLevelSlotObls mctx slots subst

recordMethodLevelSlotObls : ModuleCtx ->
  List Constraint ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Unit
recordMethodLevelSlotObls mctx [] _ = ()
recordMethodLevelSlotObls mctx (c :: rest) subst =
  let _ =
    if allList (v => isSome (lookupAssoc v subst)) (constraintVarNames c) then
      recordObl
        mctx
        Predicate {
          iface = IfaceRef {
            irName = constraintIface c,
            irOrigin = c.constraintOrigin,
          },
          args = map (fromAstType mctx subst) c.constraintArgs,
        }
        0
        PMethodLevel
        mctx.mcLoc
  recordMethodLevelSlotObls mctx rest subst

-- Expected-type propagation for an application whose argument is a lambda.
-- Inferring `andThen e (stream => Ok [JArray stream])` naively infers the lambda
-- BODY first with `stream : freshVar`, so a downstream conflicting use inside the
-- body (`JArray stream` wants `Array Json`) pins `stream` to the WRONG type before
-- the function's declared param type (`List Json`) is ever reconciled — the later
-- reconciliation then fails at the application with no good site, and the hover
-- side-channel records the wrong `stream` type.  Fix (bidirectional "checking"
-- mode, the do-bind/higher-order case): infer `f` first, peel its parameter type,
-- and unify it onto the lambda's parameter BEFORE inferring the body.  Then the
-- body sees `stream : List Json` and the type error localizes to the `JArray`
-- USE, and recordLocalBind captures the right hover type.  Purely additive: the
-- final `unify ft (TFun xt …)` in inferApp imposes the same equality regardless,
-- so the solution is unchanged — we only make it available earlier.
exprLoc : Expr -> Option Loc
exprLoc (ELoc l _) = Some l
exprLoc (EDoOrigin l _) = Some l
exprLoc _ = None

-- The span of an application's outermost argument (Bite 3): peel any ELoc
-- wrapper on the `EApp` head, then read the argument Expr's span (an unwrapped
-- argument included).  Non-EApp shapes (never passed as `appExpr`) return None.
appArgLoc : Expr -> Option Loc
appArgLoc (ELoc _ e) = appArgLoc e
appArgLoc (EApp _ x) = exprSpanLoc x
appArgLoc _ = None

-- The span of a check about the application [app] itself: its own span, head
-- through last argument, or the [enclosing] construct's when that construct
-- begins with the application (at its first column, or one before it: an
-- opening bracket), so it does not start on unrelated code.
appSpanLoc : Option Loc -> Expr -> Option Loc
appSpanLoc enclosing app = match exprSpanLoc app
  None => enclosing
  Some own => if beginsWithSpan enclosing own then enclosing else Some own

-- Does [outer] start where [inner] starts, or one column before it, and reach
-- at least as far?
beginsWithSpan : Option Loc -> Loc -> Bool
beginsWithSpan (Some (Loc _ sl sc el ec)) (Loc _ isl isc iel iec) =
  sl == isl
    && isc - sc >= 0
    && isc - sc <= 1
    && (el > iel || el == iel && ec >= iec)
beginsWithSpan None _ = False

-- ── #1815: application spines ───────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The ultimate head of an application spine, ELoc wrappers peeled.  A non-application
-- expression is its own head (so `appSpineNodes` below answers [] for it, which is what
-- makes every spine-keyed predicate decline at dispatch index 0 and leave the existing
-- bare-head paths byte-unchanged).
appSpineHead : Expr -> Expr
appSpineHead (ELoc _ e) = appSpineHead e
appSpineHead (EApp f _) = appSpineHead f
appSpineHead e = e

-- The type/route classifier strips locations from the head. Its occurrence
-- obligations still belong to that head, including at a later dispatch argument.
appSpineHeadLoc : Expr -> Option Loc
appSpineHeadLoc (ELoc loc e) = orElseLoc (appSpineHeadLoc e) (Some loc)
appSpineHeadLoc (EApp f _) = appSpineHeadLoc f
appSpineHeadLoc e = exprLoc e

-- The `EApp` nodes of a spine in APPLICATION ORDER — node i is the one supplying
-- argument i.  ELoc wrappers are peeled off the nodes themselves (the argument keeps
-- its own, which is what `appArgLoc` reads for the error span).
appSpineNodes : Expr -> List Expr
appSpineNodes e = appSpineNodesGo e []

-- Walks from the outermost node inward, prepending, so the list comes out in
-- application order with no reverse.
appSpineNodesGo : Expr -> List Expr -> List Expr
appSpineNodesGo (ELoc _ e) acc = appSpineNodesGo e acc
appSpineNodesGo (EApp f x) acc = appSpineNodesGo f (EApp f x :: acc)
appSpineNodesGo _ acc = acc

-- the argument an application node supplies.  Total only over nodes `appSpineNodes`
-- returned; anything else has no argument and yields itself, which cannot happen.
appNodeArg : Expr -> Expr
appNodeArg (ELoc _ e) = appNodeArg e
appNodeArg (EApp _ x) = x
appNodeArg e = e

-- infer a spine's already-applied arguments, LEFT TO RIGHT (source order — the same
-- order the recursive `infer env f` walk used to visit them), pairing each with the
-- node that supplies it so `inferApp` can still localize its own error span.
inferSpineArgs : TcEnv -> List Expr -> List (Expr, Mono)
inferSpineArgs env [] = []
inferSpineArgs env (n :: rest) =
  let t = infer env (appNodeArg n)
  (n, t) :: inferSpineArgs env rest

-- fold `inferApp` over a spine's (node, argument-type) pairs, left to right.  One
-- pair is exactly the single `inferApp` call the bare-head paths make.
inferAppNodes : TcEnv -> Mono -> List (Expr, Mono) -> Mono
inferAppNodes env ft [] = ft
inferAppNodes env ft ((node, at) :: rest) =
  inferAppNodes env (inferApp env node ft at) rest

-- Apply [ft] to the spine's argument nodes in order and return the residual
-- result.  `[]` is the identity.  Each argument flows in through
-- `applicationRow` with its own syntax, so a standalone selected in place of a
-- method is proved exactly like any other callee.
unifySpineResult : TcEnv -> Expr -> Mono -> List (Expr, Mono) -> Mono
unifySpineResult env _ ft [] = ft
unifySpineResult env f ft ((node, at) :: rest) =
  let r = freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let eff = applicationRow env (EApp f node) ft at r
  let _ =
    performEffect env.teDyn.dcModule env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.curEffect eff
  let _ = notePerformSite env eff
  unifySpineResult env f r rest

-- ── #2109: RESULT-FIRST inference against a known expected type ───────────
-- `paramVarianceGuard` (the D-2 variance gate) fires only when BOTH rows at a
-- non-covariant slot are closed, and abstains while either is still a
-- metavariable.  That is the whole lever here.  Inferring an application
-- ARGUMENT-FIRST (`Ref noop`: `noop`'s closed `<>` row is pinned into `Ref ?a`
-- before the result ever meets the declaration) presents two closed rows and
-- the safe write-side narrowing is rejected; inferring it RESULT-FIRST
-- (`Ref ?a` meets `Ref (String -> <Stdout> Unit)` while `?a` is fresh) lets
-- the declaration pin the slot, and the argument is then checked against the
-- DECLARED field type by the ordinary arrow-row rule, which accepts a purer
-- function where a more effectful one is allowed.
--
-- Why this is sound for ANY callee, not only a constructor: the guard still
-- fires exactly when the callee's result at the slot is CLOSED independently
-- of the expectation — `idr : Ref a -> Ref a` applied to an already-typed cell
-- (`alias = idr box`, the #1098 launder) unifies its result first, which pins
-- `a := String -> <Stdout> Unit`, and the argument `box : Ref (String -> <>
-- Unit)` then meets that as closed~closed and is rejected as before.  A callee
-- whose result slot is a metavariable cannot have aliased the cell at any
-- particular row (parametricity), so nothing but a fresh value ever reaches
-- the accepting order.  The value this admits therefore has no other alias
-- yet, which is the one condition under which narrowing at a write is safe.
--
-- Scope, deliberately narrow: the expected type must contain a non-covariant
-- slot at all (`monoHasNonCovariantSlot`), the expression must be a plain
-- application spine (no lambda-argument or shadow-head special case, which
-- keep `inferAppExpr`'s arms), and only then does the order change.  Every
-- other program is inferred exactly as before, so no diagnostic moves.
inferExpected : TcEnv -> Expr -> Mono -> Mono
inferExpected env (ELoc l e) expected =
  inferExpected (envAt (Some l) env) e expected
-- A lambda meeting a known arrow takes the arrow's domains as its parameters
-- before its body is inferred, so a signed `f = p => …` sees `String @κ` the
-- way a clause `f p = …` does.
inferExpected env (ELam pats body) expected = match normalize expected
  TFun _ _ _ =>
    inferLamChecked
      (envAtIfSome (exprLoc body) env)
      (Some (normalize expected))
      pats
      body
  _ => infer env (ELam pats body)
inferExpected env e expected =
  -- The order only matters when an ARROW ROW sits inside a type-constructor
  -- slot (that is the only thing the variance gate compares), so a purely
  -- structural pre-check (`monoHasArrowInSlot`) runs first; the polarity
  -- table (a list, scanned per lookup) is consulted only for the rare
  -- expected types that have such a slot.  Measured: the unconditional table
  -- walk per signed clause cost ~1% Ir on hello-world `check`.
  if monoHasArrowInSlot expected
    && monoHasNonCovariantSlot
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      expected then match appSpineExpr e
    (hd, args) =>
      if isEmptyL args || not (plainAppHead env hd) then
        infer env e
      else
        inferAppResultFirst env hd args expected
  else
    infer env e

-- the application spine of [e]: its head and its arguments in order, looking
-- through the location wrappers that sit between one application node and
-- the next.  A non-application returns itself with no arguments.
appSpineExpr : Expr -> (Expr, List Expr)
appSpineExpr e = appSpineExprGo e []

-- Outermost node first, so each argument is prepended as it is met and the list
-- is already in application order.
appSpineExprGo : Expr -> List Expr -> (Expr, List Expr)
appSpineExprGo (EApp f x) args = appSpineExprGo f (x :: args)
appSpineExprGo (ELoc _ (EApp f x)) args = appSpineExprGo (EApp f x) args
appSpineExprGo e args = (e, args)

-- a head `inferAppExpr` would take through its plain arm: an ordinary variable
-- that is neither a standalone shadow nor a definer shadow.  Anything else
-- keeps its dedicated arm and the argument-first order.
plainAppHead : TcEnv -> Expr -> Bool
plainAppHead env (ELoc _ inner) = plainAppHead env inner
plainAppHead env (hd@(EVar _)) = plainAppHeadVar env hd
plainAppHead env (hd@(EVarId _ _)) = plainAppHeadVar env hd
plainAppHead env (EDictAt _ _) = True
plainAppHead env _ = False

plainAppHeadVar : TcEnv -> Expr -> Bool
plainAppHeadVar env hd = match shadowStandaloneHead env hd
  Some _ => False
  None => match definerShadowArgHead env.teDyn.dcModule hd
    Some _ => False
    None => match definerShadowVarHead env.teDyn.dcModule hd
      Some _ => False
      None => True

-- the arrows of [ft] peeled [n] deep, then the result unified with [expected]
-- BEFORE any argument is looked at; each argument is then inferred against
-- the (now pinned) domain and applied through the ordinary `inferApp`, so the
-- effect bookkeeping and every diagnostic of the plain path are unchanged.
-- A callee with fewer than [n] arrows skips the pre-unification (the arity
-- error surfaces from `inferApp` exactly as before).
inferAppResultFirst : TcEnv -> Expr -> List Expr -> Mono -> Mono
inferAppResultFirst env hd args expected =
  let ft = infer env hd
  let _ = match resultAfterArrows (listLen args) ft
    Some res => unifyIn env.teDyn res expected
    None => ()
  inferAppArgsAgainst env hd ft args

inferAppArgsAgainst : TcEnv -> Expr -> Mono -> List Expr -> Mono
inferAppArgsAgainst env _ ft [] = ft
inferAppArgsAgainst env appSoFar ft (x :: rest) =
  let xt = match lamUnderLoc x
    Some (loc, pats, body) =>
      inferLamChecked
        (envAtIfSome loc env)
        (Some (funDomain env.teDyn.dcModule (normalize ft)))
        pats
        body
    None => inferExpected env x (funDomain env.teDyn.dcModule (normalize ft))
  let res = inferApp env (EApp appSoFar x) ft xt
  inferAppArgsAgainst env (EApp appSoFar x) res rest

inferAppExpr : TcEnv -> Expr -> Expr -> Mono
inferAppExpr env f x = match lamUnderLoc x
  Some (loc, pats, body) =>
    let ft = infer env f
    -- ft is `(lamType) -> result`; its FIRST domain is the lambda's expected
    -- type.  Peel that, then peel the lambda type itself for its per-param types.
    let lamExpected = funDomain env.teDyn.dcModule (normalize ft)
    let xt = inferLamChecked (envAtIfSome loc env) (Some lamExpected) pats body
    inferApp env (EApp f x) ft xt
  None => match shadowStandaloneSpineHeadAt env f
    -- #2154: the IMPORTER-side spine arm, mirroring #1815's definer spine arms — it
    -- must run BEFORE the bare-head shadowStandaloneHead/inferShadowApp arm below for
    -- the same reason: an importer shadow whose interface dispatches at index k > 0
    -- has its receiver at the OUTER spine node, not the inner node the bare-head arm
    -- would otherwise ask about.  Declines (None) at k == 0, so the bare-head arm
    -- stays byte-identical.
    Some (mname, arityRefs, tagRefs, hd, nodes) =>
      inferShadowAppAt env mname arityRefs tagRefs hd nodes f x
    None => match shadowStandaloneHead env f
      Some (mname, arityRefs, tagRefs) =>
        inferShadowApp env mname arityRefs tagRefs f x
      -- #1815: the SPINE arms come FIRST, and they are the same two definer-shadow arms
      -- one node further out.  A definer shadow whose interface dispatches on argument
      -- k > 0 (`mth : Int -> b -> Int`) reaches its dispatch argument at the OUTER node
      -- of `EApp (EApp mth n) x` — the inner node supplies argument 0, which is not the
      -- receiver at all.  Without these arms the inner node fired the index-0 arms, asked
      -- the dispatch question about argument 0, and imposed the standalone's whole
      -- declared type on the enclosing annotated function.  They decline at k == 0 (a
      -- bare head has no applied nodes), so the index-0 path below is byte-unchanged.
      None => match definerShadowSpineArgAt env.teDyn.dcModule f
        Some (dname, darityRef, dtagRef, dimplRef, dinnerRef, dhd, dnodes) =>
          inferDefinerShadowAppAt
            env
            dname
            darityRef
            dtagRef
            dimplRef
            dinnerRef
            dhd
            dnodes
            f
            x
        None => match definerShadowSpineVarAt env.teDyn.dcModule f
          Some (dname, dhd, dnodes) =>
            inferDefinerShadowVarAppAt env dname dhd dnodes f x
          None => match definerShadowArgHead env.teDyn.dcModule f
            Some (dname, darityRef, dtagRef, dimplRef, dinnerRef) =>
              inferDefinerShadowApp
                env
                dname
                darityRef
                dtagRef
                dimplRef
                dinnerRef
                f
                x
            None => match definerShadowVarHead env.teDyn.dcModule f
              Some dname => inferDefinerShadowVarApp env dname f x
              None =>
                let ft = infer env f
                let xt = infer env x
                -- P0-16: detect `f(1, 2)` on the PRISTINE ft (before inferApp unifies
                -- its domain with the tuple), then record the residual result so a
                -- downstream no-impl / mismatch can surface the tailored hint.
                let pend = tupleCallShapeHint f x ft
                let res = inferApp env (EApp f x) ft xt
                let _ = match pend
                  Some (help, fix) =>
                    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.tupleCallCandidates :=
                      (res, help, fix)
                        :: env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.tupleCallCandidates.value
                  None => ()
                res

-- @Impl: if [x] is an `@Name` disambiguation hint (a bare `EVar "@Name"`, possibly
-- under an ELoc wrapper), return the name with the leading `@` stripped.  Mirrors
-- the two oracle arms `EApp(f, EVar h)` and `EApp(f, ELoc(_, EVar h))` with
-- `h.[0]='@'`.  Anything else → None → the ordinary application path.

-- Bug C: peel a single-argument application's
-- head to a standalone-shadow interface-method reference (`size b` where `size`
-- is BOTH a `Sizeable` method AND an imported standalone —
-- `test/shadow_fixtures/i7_importer_value_pos_liveimpl/`).  Handles BOTH the
-- MARKED form (`EMethodAt`, the eval/build path — carries a route ref to stamp RLocal)
-- and the UNMARKED form (`EVar`, the `check` path — no route ref; the empty list).
-- Only fires for a SINGLE-param interface method whose name is a registered importer
-- shadow with a stashed standalone scheme — exactly the oracle's guard.  Everything
-- else (no shadow, multi-param iface, non-method head) returns None → the ordinary path.
shadowStandaloneHead : TcEnv ->
  Expr ->
  Option (String, List (Ref (Option Int)), List (Ref Route, Ref Inner))
shadowStandaloneHead env (ELoc _ f) = shadowStandaloneHead env f
shadowStandaloneHead env (EMethodAt name _ ev)
  | isShadowStandalone env name =
    let c = methodCellOf env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ev
    Some (name, [c.ecArity], [(c.ecTag, c.ecInner)])
  | otherwise = None
shadowStandaloneHead env (EVar name)
  | isShadowStandalone env name = Some (name, [], [])
  | otherwise = None
shadowStandaloneHead env (EVarId name _)
  | isShadowStandalone env name = Some (name, [], [])
  | otherwise = None
shadowStandaloneHead env _ = None

-- #2154: the IMPORTER-side spine arm — the peer of definerShadowSpineArgAt /
-- definerShadowSpineVarAt for an imported standalone shadowing a method whose
-- interface dispatches at argument k > 0.  Peels the spine's ultimate head with the
-- SAME test shadowStandaloneHead already applies to a bare head (so a marked
-- EMethodAt receiver and an unmarked EVar/EVarId receiver both fire, exactly as
-- shadowStandaloneHead's own two arms do), then gates on `shadowSpineNodesAt`, which
-- declines (`None`) for a bare head (k == 0, nodes == []) — the existing
-- shadowStandaloneHead / inferShadowApp path stays byte-identical.
shadowStandaloneSpineHeadAt : TcEnv ->
  Expr ->
  Option (String, List (Ref (Option Int)), List (Ref Route, Ref Inner), Expr, List Expr)
shadowStandaloneSpineHeadAt env f =
  match shadowStandaloneHead env (appSpineHead f)
    None => None
    Some (name, arityRefs, tagRefs) =>
      map
        (nodes => (name, arityRefs, tagRefs, appSpineHead f, nodes))
        (shadowSpineNodesAtImporter env.teDyn.dcModule name f)

-- a name that is BOTH a registered importer shadow (standaloneValuesRef), has a
-- stashed standalone scheme, and names a single-TYPARAM interface's method.
--
-- ⚠️ IMPORTER side ⇒ singleTyparamIfaceMethod, NOT ifaceMethodName (#54).  Fork 1 keeps
-- the per-receiver rule here, and that rule keys the impl query on the receiver's head
-- tycon standing at the interface's ONE typaram.  A multi-typaram interface has no such
-- correspondence to key on -- `FromEntries c e`'s `fromEntries : List e -> c` does not
-- even take its first typaram as an argument -- so the importer arms stay scoped to the
-- single-typaram case.  The DEFINER arms do not: under the S2 inversion they never query
-- the impl universe at all, so they are typaram-agnostic (ifaceMethodName).
isShadowStandalone : TcEnv -> String -> Bool
isShadowStandalone env name =
  omHasKey name env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.standaloneValuesRef.value
    && isSome (lookupImportedStandalone env name)
    && singleTyparamIfaceMethod env.teDyn.dcModule name

-- True iff [name]'s interface (in methodEntryHere) takes exactly ONE type
-- parameter -- the receiver-directed case the per-receiver IMPORTER rule (Fork 1) is
-- scoped to.  When two or more declarations are admitted it answers over the whole
-- set (every admitted interface takes one), never by the absence of a single winner:
-- `False` would skip the importer route and with it S2-DECL (d)'s cardinality
-- decision (`importerAdmittedVerdict`).
--
-- ⚠️ RENAMED from `singleParamIfaceMethod` (#54).  The old name said "single-PARAM
-- method" while the body counts interface TYPE PARAMS; it stated the opposite of what it
-- does and sent one agent down a wrong hypothesis (issue #54; SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md S8).
-- A two-PARAM method of a one-typaram interface (`comb : a -> a -> Int`, cell d7) passes
-- this predicate, and always did.
singleTyparamIfaceMethod : ModuleCtx -> String -> Bool
singleTyparamIfaceMethod mctx name = match methodEntryHere mctx name
  Some (_, typarams, _, _) => listLen typarams == 1
  None => match methodAdmittedHere mctx name
    [] => False
    ifs =>
      allList
        (r => match r.mrEntry
          (_, typarams, _, _) => listLen typarams == 1)
        (filterList
          (r =>
            let key = ifaceSortKey (methodRowIface r)
            anyList (ir => ifaceSortKey ir == key) ifs)
          (methodVisibleHere mctx name))

-- True iff [name] is a method of SOME visible interface, whatever its typaram arity --
-- the DEFINER-side gate (#54, closing S-3 / SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md row 26).
--
-- Under the S2 inversion a definer shadow denotes its module's own standalone
-- unconditionally: the impl universe is never consulted, so there is no receiver-to-
-- typaram correspondence to require, and gating the definer entry points on the typaram
-- COUNT only excused `interface Ix a i` from the machinery.  That excusal was the S-3
-- bug: d11 typed+emitted per-receiver (the OLD, pre-inversion semantics) while eval, which
-- has no route stamp to follow, resolved the bare name lexically to the standalone and
-- E-PANICked `unknown op '*'` on a `Box` -- an S7 path-agreement violation.
-- Two or more admitted declarations are each a method of a visible interface, so the
-- admitted set answers True as well.
ifaceMethodName : ModuleCtx -> String -> Bool
ifaceMethodName mctx name =
  isSome (methodEntryHere mctx name)
    || isNonEmptyL (methodAdmittedHere mctx name)

-- Bug C: type `toList m` for a no-impl receiver against the imported STANDALONE
-- scheme (giving the concrete result element type, e.g. `List (String, Int)`) and
-- stamp the route RLocal (when marked); if the receiver DOES have an impl (or its head
-- is not yet concrete) fall through to ordinary dispatch (typed against the method
-- scheme the env rebound the name to).
--
-- ✅ S1-RESIDUAL-B CLOSED (2026-07-14).  This function used to have NO groundShadowReceiver
-- call, unlike its definer peer inferDefinerShadowApp (which P0-20 gave one).  An UNGROUNDED
-- receiver — a bare `Num` LITERAL is the everyday case, it is `Num a => a`, not `Int` — so
-- never reached the standalone arm below (headTyconMono is None) and fell to the
-- ordinary-app arm, which types against the METHOD scheme the env rebound the name to.
--
--   -- lib/prov.mdk:  export isEmpty : Int -> Bool
--   import lib.prov.{isEmpty}
--   main = println (debug (isEmpty 0))     -- Type mismatch: Int literal vs Int Int
--
-- The `Int Int` in that message is the tell: the PRELUDE's `Foldable.isEmpty : t a -> Bool`
-- is higher-kinded, so unifying `t a` with the literal's tyvar solved `t := Int, a := Int`.
-- The user's imported `isEmpty : Int -> Bool` was never consulted.  (Filed as "under-applies
-- on run" for a CONSTRAINED standalone; the root is broader — it breaks an UNCONSTRAINED one
-- at `check` too, whenever the shadowed method is higher-kinded.)
--
-- Fix, exactly as filed: ground an ungrounded receiver to the IMPORTED standalone's declared
-- domain BEFORE asking the S2 impl question, so typecheck and the post-inference route
-- resolver ask it about the SAME head.  That symmetry is the whole P0-20 lesson — a decision
-- derived twice, at two different times, over a receiver that changed in between.
--
-- ⚠️ NOT affected by the S2 inversion: an IMPORTER shadow keeps the per-receiver rule
-- (Fork 1).  Grounding only decides WHICH head the rule is applied to; a grounded head with
-- a live impl still dispatches (`isEmpty [1, 2]` → `Foldable.isEmpty`, fixture i4).
inferShadowApp : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  List (Ref (Option Int)) ->
  List (Ref Route, Ref Inner) ->
  Expr ->
  Expr ->
  Mono
inferShadowApp env mname arityRefs tagRefs f x =
  -- the application's loc, so a domain mismatch localizes to the call site, not
  -- the argument.
  let dloc = appSpanLoc env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc (EApp f x)
  let tx = infer env x
  -- The dict-var carve-out (S5/Fork 2) applies to importer shadows too: a receiver that is
  -- the enclosing fn's `=>`-bound constraint var DISPATCHES through that dict, so it must
  -- NOT be ground to the standalone's domain (that would monomorphise the written signature).
  -- groundShadowReceiver is also inert on an already-grounded receiver, so i1/i3/i4 (all
  -- concrete receivers) are byte-identical.
  let _ =
    groundShadowReceiver
      env.teDyn
      (importerShadowDomain env mname)
      tx
      (definerReceiverIsDictVar env.teDyn mname tx)
      dloc
  -- #2188 / S2-DECL (d): the cardinality decision, asked BEFORE the single-winner impl
  -- question below.  Inert (`AdDefer`, and `groundAdmittedReceivers` a no-op) for every
  -- name with fewer than two admitted declarations — see `importerAdmittedVerdict`.
  let _ = groundAdmittedReceivers env mname [tx] dloc
  match (importerAdmittedVerdict
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
    mname
    [tx])
    AdReject ifs =>
      let _ =
        pushAmbiguousShadowDecl
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          mname
          ifs
          (orElseLoc (appSpineHeadLoc f) dloc)
      -- T-ERRORS-ACCUM: the diagnostic is the verdict; inference still has to produce a
      -- type for the occurrence, and the standalone is the only denotation this call has
      -- that no admitted declaration disputes the SHAPE of.
      inferShadowStandaloneArm env mname arityRefs tagRefs f x tx
    AdStandalone => inferShadowStandaloneArm env mname arityRefs tagRefs f x tx
    AdDefer => match headTyconMono tx
      -- ARCH B-2.1-g: the S2 impl question, off the GRAPH-GLOBAL substrate — see
      -- `ieImplExistsForHead`.  It used to read the cumulative topological PREFIX
      -- (`shadowKeyTableRef`), which made this answer depend on where in the module order
      -- the receiver's impl happened to sit.
      Some head =>
        if ieImplExistsForHead
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
          mname
          head then
          inferApp env (EApp f x) (inferShadowAppHead env f) tx
        else
          inferShadowStandaloneArm env mname arityRefs tagRefs f x tx
      None => inferApp env (EApp f x) (inferShadowAppHead env f) tx

-- The STANDALONE arm of `inferShadowApp`, factored out verbatim so S2-DECL (d)'s
-- `AdStandalone` and `AdReject` verdicts reach exactly the arm the impl-query miss
-- already reached — one arm, three callers, no second copy to drift.
inferShadowStandaloneArm : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  List (Ref (Option Int)) ->
  List (Ref Route, Ref Inner) ->
  Expr ->
  Expr ->
  Mono ->
  Mono
inferShadowStandaloneArm env mname arityRefs tagRefs f x tx =
  match lookupStandaloneValue env mname
    Some value =>
      let occurrence =
        instantiateStandaloneOccurrence
          env
          mname
          ""
          (orElseLoc (appSpineHeadLoc f) env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc)
          value
      let _ = recordStandaloneAt env.teDyn.dcModule mname f occurrence
      let smono = occurrence.svoInstance.mtiBody
      let _ = stampMethodArities arityRefs (funArity smono)
      let r = freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule ()
      -- At the call site, as `inferShadowApp`'s domain check.
      let eff =
        applicationRow
          (envAtIfSome (appSpanLoc env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc (EApp f x)) env)
          (EApp f x)
          smono
          tx
          r
      let _ =
        performEffect
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.curEffect
          eff
      let _ = stampRoutes (map fst tagRefs)
      -- S-1 (Fork D — the importer half): an IMPORTED constrained standalone shadowing
      -- a method breaks identically to a local one (its def is dict-passed in its own
      -- module; this call must supply the dicts).  Compute them off the head type we
      -- just unified, and defer the ROUTE stamp to resolveRLocalSites — stampRoutes
      -- above ran mid-inference, when the receiver is not yet solved, so it could only
      -- write `RLocal sym []`.  forceLocal=True: this arm has already committed the
      -- site's TYPE to the standalone, so its route is not open to re-derivation.
      let _ =
        recordSelectedStandaloneRoutes
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          mname
          occurrence.svoDicts
          tagRefs
          tx
      r
    None => inferApp env (EApp f x) (inferShadowAppHead env f) tx

-- #411: infer an IMPORTER-shadow application's head with `dcShadowHeadCtx` set, so
-- maybeStandaloneValueMono's new importer arm does not pin an APPLIED occurrence to the
-- standalone scheme (which would kill per-receiver dispatch — Fork 1 / i4).  The definer
-- path has always typed its head this way (inferDefinerShadowApp); this is the peer
-- the importer path was missing, and the reason it could be missing before is that
-- nothing pinned importer value positions at all — which IS the #411 bug.
inferShadowAppHead : TcEnv -> Expr -> Mono
inferShadowAppHead env f = infer (shadowHeadEnv env) f

-- [env] for typing a shadow occurrence that heads its own application.
shadowHeadEnv : TcEnv -> TcEnv
shadowHeadEnv env = { env | teDyn = { env.teDyn | dcShadowHeadCtx = True } }

-- #2154: the spine-generalized twin of inferShadowApp — the peer of
-- inferDefinerShadowAppAt for the IMPORTER path.  [hd] is the spine's ultimate head
-- ([f] itself at index 0, unreachable here since shadowStandaloneSpineHeadAt declines
-- at k == 0) and [nodes] the application nodes already applied to it; [pre] is those
-- nodes' inferred (node, mono) pairs in source order, exactly as inferDefinerShadowAppAt
-- computes them.  Performs the SAME S2 impl-exists-vs-standalone-scheme branch
-- inferShadowApp does, at the outer node, folding inferApp/unification over the whole
-- applied prefix via inferSpineArgs/inferAppNodes/unifySpineResult.
inferShadowAppAt : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  List (Ref (Option Int)) ->
  List (Ref Route, Ref Inner) ->
  Expr ->
  List Expr ->
  Expr ->
  Expr ->
  Mono
inferShadowAppAt env mname arityRefs tagRefs hd nodes f x =
  -- the application's loc, as in `inferShadowApp`.
  let dloc = appSpanLoc env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc (EApp f x)
  let pre = inferSpineArgs env nodes
  let k = listLen pre
  let tx = infer env x
  let _ =
    groundShadowReceiver
      env.teDyn
      (importerShadowDomainAt env mname k)
      tx
      (definerReceiverIsDictVar env.teDyn mname tx)
      dloc
  -- #2188 / S2-DECL (d): [ats] is every argument up to and including THIS node's, so at
  -- the OUTERMOST admitted dispatch index (`importerDispatchIdxOuter`, the index this arm
  -- is gated on) every admitted declaration's own receiver argument is in it — which is
  -- what makes (b)'s per-declaration pairs jointly evaluable here and nowhere else.
  let ats = map snd pre ++ [tx]
  let _ = groundAdmittedReceivers env mname ats dloc
  match (importerAdmittedVerdict
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
    mname
    ats)
    AdReject ifs =>
      let _ =
        pushAmbiguousShadowDecl
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          mname
          ifs
          (orElseLoc (appSpineHeadLoc f) dloc)
      inferShadowStandaloneArmAt env mname arityRefs tagRefs hd pre f x tx
    AdStandalone =>
      inferShadowStandaloneArmAt env mname arityRefs tagRefs hd pre f x tx
    AdDefer => match headTyconMono tx
      Some head =>
        if ieImplExistsForHead
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
          mname
          head then
          inferAppNodes
            env
            (inferShadowAppHead env hd)
            (pre ++ [(EApp f x, tx)])
        else
          inferShadowStandaloneArmAt env mname arityRefs tagRefs hd pre f x tx
      None =>
        inferAppNodes env (inferShadowAppHead env hd) (pre ++ [(EApp f x, tx)])

-- The STANDALONE arm of `inferShadowAppAt`, factored out verbatim — the peer of
-- `inferShadowStandaloneArm` at dispatch index k > 0, and reached from the same three
-- verdicts.
inferShadowStandaloneArmAt : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  List (Ref (Option Int)) ->
  List (Ref Route, Ref Inner) ->
  Expr ->
  List (Expr, Mono) ->
  Expr ->
  Expr ->
  Mono ->
  Mono
inferShadowStandaloneArmAt env mname arityRefs tagRefs hd pre f x tx =
  match lookupStandaloneValue env mname
    Some value =>
      let occurrence =
        instantiateStandaloneOccurrence
          env
          mname
          ""
          (orElseLoc (appSpineHeadLoc f) env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc)
          value
      let _ = recordStandaloneAt env.teDyn.dcModule mname hd occurrence
      let smono = occurrence.svoInstance.mtiBody
      let _ = stampMethodArities arityRefs (funArity smono)
      -- At the call site, as `inferShadowApp`'s domain check.
      let r =
        unifySpineResult
          (envAtIfSome (appSpanLoc env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc (EApp f x)) env)
          f
          smono
          (pre ++ [(x, tx)])
      let _ = stampRoutes (map fst tagRefs)
      let _ =
        recordSelectedStandaloneRoutes
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          mname
          occurrence.svoDicts
          tagRefs
          tx
      r
    None =>
      inferAppNodes env (inferShadowAppHead env hd) (pre ++ [(EApp f x, tx)])

-- S1-RESIDUAL-B: the IMPORTED standalone's declared domain — the first arrow domain of the
-- scheme retained by the lexical binding descriptor. The importer peer of
-- shadowDomainFor's mangled arm, and it must NOT
-- be `lookupVar env mname`: env1 rebound the bare name to the interface METHOD, which is the
-- very scheme whose higher-kinded domain caused the bug.
--
-- None (⇒ grounding is a no-op) when the name has no stashed standalone scheme, or when that
-- standalone's own first parameter is itself polymorphic (`f : a -> Bool`) — unifying a bare
-- tyvar domain with an ungrounded receiver leaves it ungrounded anyway, so the caller's
-- headTyconMono still says None and the old ordinary-app arm runs, byte-identically.
importerShadowDomain : TcEnv -> String -> Option Mono
importerShadowDomain env mname = match lookupStandaloneVar env mname
  None => None
  Some s => match normalize (instantiate env.teDyn.dcModule s)
    TFun a _ _ => Some a
    _ => None

-- #2154: as importerShadowDomain, but the standalone's k-th declared parameter — the
-- one the receiver occupies when the interface dispatches at argument k > 0.  Peer of
-- shadowDomainForAt / standaloneShadowDomainAt (#1815).  `k = 0` is importerShadowDomain
-- verbatim (nthFunDomain 0 on a TFun matches its first arm exactly).
importerShadowDomainAt : TcEnv -> String -> Int -> Option Mono
importerShadowDomainAt env mname k = match lookupStandaloneVar env mname
  None => None
  Some s => nthFunDomain k (instantiate env.teDyn.dcModule s)

-- S-1 (importer half): re-record each of the importer shadow's route refs as an
-- RLocalSite carrying the imported standalone's own constraint dicts, so
-- resolveRLocalSites re-stamps the ref post-inference with the dicts filled in.
-- forceLocal=True — inferShadowApp's standalone arm already committed the site's type.
-- Inert (no dicts, same RLocal stamp) for an unconstrained imported standalone.
recordSelectedStandaloneRoutes : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  ShadowDicts ->
  List (Ref Route, Ref Inner) ->
  Mono ->
  Unit
recordSelectedStandaloneRoutes mctx _ _ [] _ = ()
-- multi-line RHS: the indented `:=` form is legal but not seed-parseable yet (#1744)
-- lint-disable-next-line rule-prefer-assign-op
recordSelectedStandaloneRoutes mctx mname dicts ((r, inner) :: rest) tx =
  let _ =
    pushSiteGoal
      mctx.mcGraph
      GKRLocalSite
      inner
      (PendingEntry
        mname
        r
        tx
        mctx.mcCells.currentFn.value
        (SKRLocal
          (routeLocalSym !r)
          True
          dicts.sdMonos
          dicts.sdIfaces
          dicts.sdArgVecs)
        mctx.mcLoc
        (captureScope mctx ())
        (freshEvId mctx ()))
  recordSelectedStandaloneRoutes mctx mname dicts rest tx

-- P0-18: peel a single-argument application's head to a DEFINER-shadow interface-
-- method occurrence (the user's OWN top-level fn reuses a single-param interface
-- method name, e.g. this module's `size : Int -> Int` shadowing `Sizeable`'s
-- `size`).  Unlike importer shadows (shadowStandaloneHead / inferShadowApp), the
-- user's definition SHADOWS the method in scope, so the occurrence is typed against
-- the standalone scheme whose declared domain (`Int`) is NOT the actual receiver.
-- Returning the route ref lets inferDefinerShadowApp record the REAL argument mono
-- for per-receiver routing (`Box` has a `Sizeable` impl → method; `Int` → standalone).
-- P0-18 (importer residual): on the EMIT path a definer shadow's bare name is NOT
-- in definerShadowNamesRef when the standalone is IMPORTED from another module (that
-- ref is keyed on module-local funDefs).  But the mark pass ALREADY seeded such an
-- occurrence's route with the mangled standalone symbol (`RLocal <sym>`), so a
-- non-empty route symbol is an equally-good "this is a shadow" signal that works
-- cross-module.  Firing here routes the occurrence through inferDefinerShadowApp,
-- which types it against the standalone scheme and records the per-receiver mono —
-- so an importer shadow on a live-impl receiver dispatches to the impl, and one on a
-- no-impl receiver falls back to the standalone (RLocal <sym>), exactly like a
-- definer shadow.  On the un-mangled run/check path the route is RNone (sym ""), so
-- this branch is inert there and the ordinary definerShadowNames branch governs.
definerShadowArgHead : ModuleCtx ->
  Expr ->
  Option (String, Ref (Option Int), Ref Route, Ref (List Route), Ref Inner)
definerShadowArgHead mctx (ELoc _ f) = definerShadowArgHead mctx f
-- ⚠️ #54: the two disjuncts carry DIFFERENT gates, because they serve different shadow
-- KINDS — this predicate is a Fork-1 boundary, not an arity test.  `isDefinerShadow` is
-- typaram-agnostic; `importerShadowOnEmitPath` is scoped to single-typaram interfaces (see
-- its header).  Spelling the definer disjunct as `isDefinerShadow` — rather than inlining
-- its conjuncts here — is deliberate: that function is ALSO what resolveRLocalSite routes
-- on, and "the typing entry point and the route stamper must apply the same gate" is the
-- P0-20 invariant.  Sharing the symbol makes them impossible to drift.
definerShadowArgHead mctx (EMethodAt name _ ev) =
  definerShadowArgHeadCell mctx name (methodCellOf mctx.mcGraph ev)
definerShadowArgHead mctx _ = None

definerShadowArgHeadCell : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  EvCell ->
  Option (String, Ref (Option Int), Ref Route, Ref (List Route), Ref Inner)
definerShadowArgHeadCell mctx name c
  | isDefinerShadow mctx name
    || importerShadowOnEmitPath mctx name c.ecTag =
    Some (name, c.ecArity, c.ecTag, c.ecImpl, c.ecInner)
  | otherwise = None

-- L4 (xmod-identity #1351 spine, RUN-XMOD-022/026): the mark pass's own per-occurrence
-- verdict, named rather than left as an anonymous `routeLocalSym … /= ""` idiom.
-- `rewriteArgScoped`'s `sm` arm is the SOLE origin of a non-empty RLocal symbol on an
-- EMethodAt route (F8); every other RLocal stamp propagates that origin symbol
-- unchanged.  This is NOT a graph-wide fact and is NOT interchangeable with one: "The
-- signal is PER-OCCURRENCE, not graph-wide … keying on it (not on the whole-graph
-- standaloneValuesRef) is what keeps this from pinning the compiler's genuine
-- method-values and breaking dispatch" (this file, historically beside this site).
-- #2809: the seed is the BARE standalone name on every path now, so "non-empty" no
-- longer says "the mangler moved the name" — `recoveredShadowSym` is what does.
occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym : String -> Ref Route -> Bool
occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym name tagRef =
  recoveredShadowSym name tagRef /= ""

-- #54: the SECOND disjunct of definerShadowArgHead — the IMPORTER-on-emit signal, kept
-- separate because it carries a DIFFERENT gate from the definer one.  The mark pass seeds
-- an importer shadow's route with the provider's mangled standalone symbol, so a non-empty
-- route symbol says "this is a shadow" cross-module, where definerShadowNamesRef (keyed on
-- module-local funDefs) cannot.  It stays scoped to singleTyparamIfaceMethod because what
-- it feeds is Fork 1's per-receiver rule; the definer disjunct (isDefinerShadow) does not,
-- because the S2 inversion never queries the impl universe.  On the un-mangled run/check
-- path the route is RNone (sym ""), so this is inert there.
--
-- L4: this predicate now names its two conjuncts separately instead of conflating them in
-- one `routeLocalSym … /= ""` test.  `gctx.mangledFunDefsPresentRef.value`
-- (L3) is the GRAPH-level fact "this compile's decls carry mangled funDefs at all";
-- `occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym tagRef` is the mark pass's own PER-OCCURRENCE verdict
-- for THIS route.  The new graph-level conjunct is ADDED, not substituted for the
-- occurrence test — F7 (this file) forbids replacing the per-occurrence route test with a
-- graph-wide one: doing so would fire for occurrences the mark pass never marked, and
-- would pin genuine method-values, breaking dispatch.
--
-- 🚨 RUN-XMOD-045 CORRECTION (post-landing, slice-breaker finding) — REPLACES the
-- original "redundant-by-construction, F8" safety narrative below with the actual one.
-- F8's implication chain ("a non-empty route symbol implies the graph fact is True") is
-- still literally true, but it undersold what actually holds: `mangledFunDefsPresentRef`
-- is not merely implied True in that case, it is CONSTANT TRUE on every emit path,
-- unconditionally — see `graphCarriesMangledFunDefs`'s header for the mechanism
-- (`private_mangle.mdk:14-16` mangles core's own funDefs unconditionally, before this
-- flag is ever computed; measured ~70 `@mdk_<mid>__*` symbols in a feature-free build's
-- IR with zero shadows).  F8's phrasing hid its own precondition: it is only a
-- meaningful narrowing test if the flag CAN be False on some occurrence's compile, and
-- on the emit path it never is.  The actual safety property is therefore simpler and
-- stronger than "redundant, measured by a negative control": THE FLAG IS CONSTANT TRUE
-- THE MOMENT MANGLING RAN AT ALL, so its conjunct can never be what rejects an
-- occurrence the un-mangled reading of `occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym` would have
-- accepted — the predicate's real discriminator is still, and only, the
-- per-occurrence route symbol.
--
-- 🚨 THIS FACT CURRENTLY HAS NO DISCRIMINATING CONSUMER — L4's conjunct
-- (`mangledFunDefsPresentRef`) is constant-True on emit and its partner
-- (`occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym`) is always-empty off emit.  It is explicit
-- documentation of an implicit invariant, not a live condition.  Do not migrate a
-- reader onto it expecting it to select.  KEPT rather than reverted (owner ruling,
-- RUN-XMOD-045): provably zero-risk, and "this graph was mangled" is more readable
-- than the anonymous `routeLocalSym … /= ""` idiom it replaced, even though it cannot
-- currently narrow anything a build-time `medaka check`/`run`/`build` differential
-- could observe from outside the compiler.
importerShadowOnEmitPath : ModuleCtx -> String -> Ref Route -> Bool
importerShadowOnEmitPath mctx name tagRef =
  singleTyparamIfaceMethod mctx name
    && mctx.mcGraph.mangledFunDefsPresentRef.value
    && occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym name tagRef

-- P0-18: type `size (Box 3)` exactly as the ordinary path (against the standalone
-- scheme the env rebound `size` to, preserving program types), but record the
-- ACTUAL argument mono (`Box`) as this site's receiver so resolveRLocalSite routes
-- per-receiver: a receiver head WITH an impl of the shadowed interface dispatches to
-- the method (route left untouched → eval arg-tag / emit RKey), one WITHOUT an impl
-- stays the standalone (RLocal).  dcSuppressRLocalRecord stops recordRLocalSite from
-- ALSO pushing the standalone's declared domain (which would mis-route `Box`→`Int`).
inferDefinerShadowApp : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  Ref (Option Int) ->
  Ref Route ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Ref Inner ->
  Expr ->
  Expr ->
  Mono
inferDefinerShadowApp env name arityRef tagRef implRef innerRef f x =
  inferDefinerShadowAppAt env name arityRef tagRef implRef innerRef f [] f x

-- #1815: the marked twin at an arbitrary dispatch index — the peer of
-- inferDefinerShadowVarAppAt, and the two must still agree cell-for-cell (S7).  [hd] is
-- the spine's ultimate head ([f] itself at index 0) and [nodes] the application nodes
-- already applied to it.  BOTH decision layers move together here: the TYPE arm reads
-- the receiver at index k, and the ROUTE stamps (pendingRLocalSites / pendingArgStamps)
-- are pushed at THIS node with THAT receiver — "the route must follow the arm".
inferDefinerShadowAppAt : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  Ref (Option Int) ->
  Ref Route ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Ref Inner ->
  Expr ->
  List Expr ->
  Expr ->
  Expr ->
  Mono
inferDefinerShadowAppAt env name arityRef tagRef implRef innerRef hd nodes f x =
  -- #2809: the RECOVERED symbol, not the raw route seed — every use of [sym] below is
  -- a typing decision that presumes "the bare name no longer denotes the standalone"
  -- (see `recoveredShadowSym`).  The two `SKRLocal (routeLocalSym !tagRef)` stamps
  -- keep the raw seed: that is the route the emitter follows.
  let sym = recoveredShadowSym name tagRef
  -- P0-19: the application's location, so a standalone-domain mismatch reports at
  -- the call site.
  let dloc = appSpanLoc env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc (EApp f x)
  -- #1815: the arguments the spine already applied, inferred in source order (exactly
  -- the order the recursive walk visited them in before).
  let pre = inferSpineArgs env nodes
  let k = listLen pre
  -- P0-19 d8 (S2/S6): infer the argument FIRST so the head scheme is chosen PER
  -- RECEIVER.  A receiver with a VISIBLE impl of the shadowed interface (impl universe
  -- is GRAPH-GLOBAL: ARCH B-2.1-g reads `bodyImplEnvRef` via `ieImplExistsForHead`)
  -- DISPATCHES → type
  -- 🚨 This note used to say "shadowKeyTableRef spans local ∪ imported ∪ prelude", and
  -- BOTH halves were wrong.  `SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md:242-245` RETIRES that phrase — "'local
  -- ∪ imported ∪ prelude' is NOT a synonym for graph-global … an older wording of S2 used
  -- it as one anyway" — and the table was narrower still: on the Module arm
  -- `shadowKeyTableRef` was the CUMULATIVE TOPOLOGICAL PREFIX, so it did not even span
  -- "imported" once the impl sat in a topologically later module.  Do not re-derive the
  -- retired claim from the old wording.
  -- the head against the METHOD scheme; else it is the STANDALONE.  Without this the
  -- mangled emit path (sym /= "") ALWAYS typed against the standalone scheme
  -- (`Int -> Int`), so a definer shadow whose impl is IMPORTED (`size (Box 3)`, d8)
  -- rejected `Int vs Box` at build/run instead of dispatching to the imported impl.
  let xt = infer env x
  -- P0-19 (constrained-receiver arm): an ungrounded receiver that is a dict-bound
  -- constraint var dispatches through that dict — it must neither be typed against the
  -- standalone scheme nor stamped RLocal (which would send eval/emit to the standalone
  -- and, e.g., apply `sz n = n + 1` to a Bool).
  let isDictVar = definerReceiverIsDictVar env.teDyn name xt
  -- P0-20: ground an ungrounded receiver to the standalone's declared domain BEFORE the
  -- dispatch decision, so typecheck asks the impl question about the SAME head the
  -- post-inference route resolver will.  See groundShadowReceiver.
  let _ =
    groundShadowReceiver
      env.teDyn
      (shadowDomainForAt env name sym k)
      xt
      isDictVar
      dloc
  let dispatches = definerReceiverDispatches env.teDyn name xt
  -- A dispatching occurrence names the interface whose method it selects, as an
  -- ordinary method occurrence does (`inferMethodCandidateAt`); the standalone arm
  -- names none.
  let _ =
    if dispatches || isDictVar then match spineHeadEv hd
      Some ev =>
        let cell = methodCellOf env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ev
        cell.ecIface := admittedIfaceWord env.teDyn.dcModule name
      None => ()
  -- The head is typed in `headEnv`: the two default pushes are suppressed, and, as an
  -- application head (marked EMethodAt on run/build, P0-19 d4b), it keeps the method
  -- scheme for per-receiver dispatch rather than the value-position standalone pin.
  let headEnv = { env |
    teDyn = { env.teDyn |
      dcSuppressRLocalRecord = True,
      dcSuppressArgStamp = True,
      dcShadowHeadCtx = True,
    },
  }
  -- P0-18: for the STANDALONE arm, type the head against the STANDALONE scheme.  On the
  -- un-mangled run/check path `infer env f` already resolves the bare name to the
  -- standalone (which shadows the method in scope).  On the EMIT path the bare name
  -- resolves to the interface METHOD scheme instead (the standalone was renamed to
  -- `<mid>__name`), whose result loses the concrete element type — e.g. Map's `toList`
  -- would type `List a` not `List (k, v)`, so a downstream `debug (toList m)` resolves
  -- the WRONG element dict and SIGSEGVs.  When we carry the mangled symbol, instantiate
  -- its (standalone) scheme directly so the impl-body types exactly as the run path
  -- does. For the DISPATCH arm, type against the METHOD scheme so a live-impl
  -- receiver unifies and the result comes from the method.
  -- DISPATCH arm: the interface METHOD scheme, fetched EXPLICITLY from
  -- methodEntryHere (which spans imported interfaces) — NOT `infer env f`, because
  -- on the multi-module path the env rebinds the bare method name to the LOCAL
  -- standalone (`Int -> Int`), so inferMethodAt's lookupVar would hand back `Int -> Int`
  -- and reject a live-impl receiver (`Box`).  STANDALONE arm: the standalone scheme
  -- (mangled sym on the emit path preserves the concrete result type).
  let selected =
    if dispatches then
      None
    else
      standaloneOccurrence headEnv name sym (orElseLoc (appSpineHeadLoc f) dloc)
  let ft =
    if dispatches then
      shadowVarHeadMethodScheme headEnv name hd
    else match selected
      Some occurrence =>
        let _ = recordStandaloneAt env.teDyn.dcModule name hd occurrence
        occurrence.svoInstance.mtiBody
      None => infer headEnv hd
  arityRef := Some (funArity ft)
  -- S-1: on the STANDALONE arm ONLY, compute that standalone's own `=>`-constraint
  -- dicts (and record its call obligations).  The DISPATCH arm typed `ft` against the
  -- interface METHOD scheme, whose dicts are the method's, not the standalone's — asking
  -- there would be meaningless.  A dict-var receiver dispatches through its dict and is
  -- likewise not the standalone.  ([], []) for an unconstrained standalone.
  let dicts =
    if dispatches || isDictVar then
      emptyShadowDicts
    else
      optionOr
        emptyShadowDicts
        (map (occurrence => occurrence.svoDicts) selected)
  -- Route by the ACTUAL argument type on BOTH the eval path (pendingRLocalSites,
  -- read by resolveRLocalSites) and the emit path (pendingArgStamps, read by
  -- resolveArgStamps — only recorded when this method arg-dispatches, i.e. on the
  -- build path).  xt grounds to the real receiver post-inference; the two default
  -- pushes (recordRLocalSite / recordArgStamp) that would carry the standalone's
  -- declared domain are suppressed above.
  -- ...EXCEPT for a dict-bound constraint-var receiver: resolveRLocalSite's ungrounded
  -- arm stamps RLocal unconditionally, which would route a genuine dict dispatch to the
  -- shadowing standalone.  Not recording the site leaves the route for ordinary dispatch
  -- (RNone → eval arg-tag / emit RKey via resolveArgStamps).
  -- P0-20: the route FOLLOWS THE ARM (`not dispatches` ⇒ forceLocal).  `ft` above has
  -- already committed this site's TYPE, so re-deriving its route from a receiver mono
  -- that may ground LATER (Num defaulting on an unsignatured standalone) is exactly how
  -- `check` and the binary came to disagree.  A dispatching receiver still re-derives
  -- (its head is already ground; RKey comes from resolveArgStamps on the emit path).
  let _ =
    if isDictVar then
      ()
    else
      pushSiteGoal
        env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
        GKRLocalSite
        innerRef
        (PendingEntry
          name
          tagRef
          xt
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn.value
          (SKRLocal
            (routeLocalSym !tagRef)
            (not dispatches)
            dicts.sdMonos
            dicts.sdIfaces
            dicts.sdArgVecs)
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
          (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
          (freshEvId env.teDyn.dcModule ()))
  let _ = match argDispatchOf env.teDyn.dcModule name
    -- #609: the SKArg full mono is the DISPATCH arm's method scheme (`ft`) — the
    -- only arm whose route this stamp decides.  On the STANDALONE arm `ft` is the
    -- standalone's own scheme, which is not an interface-method occurrence at all;
    -- pass the receiver mono `xt` so ifaceParamMonos fails its shape match and the
    -- selector falls back to the singleton goal, exactly as before #609.
    Some _ =>
      pushSiteGoal
        env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
        GKArgStamp
        innerRef
        (PendingEntry
          name
          tagRef
          xt
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn.value
          (SKArg implRef (if dispatches then ft else xt) [])
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
          (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
          (freshEvId env.teDyn.dcModule ()))
    None => ()
  -- P0-19: on the UN-MANGLED path (sym == "") `ft` is the permissive METHOD scheme
  -- (`a -> Int`), so `inferApp ft xt` would accept ANY receiver.  When this
  -- occurrence resolves to the STANDALONE — a grounded receiver head with no visible
  -- impl of the shadowed interface, or an ungrounded receiver (S5) — impose the
  -- standalone's DECLARED domain on the argument, so a domain mismatch (`size "hi"`,
  -- or a wrapper generalized over the shadow receiver then called at a live-impl type)
  -- becomes a located reject instead of build-time garbage.  A grounded receiver WITH
  -- an impl still dispatches (no enforcement) — that arm is untouched.  On the mangled
  -- emit path (sym /= "") `ft` is already the selected standalone instance,
  -- which enforces the domain itself, so this stays inert there.
  -- The STANDALONE arm with a written signature mirrors its unmarked twin
  -- (`inferDefinerStandaloneVarAppAt`'s `Some smono` branch): ONE unification of the
  -- standalone's type against the applied spine, at the call site.  Running the
  -- domain enforcement AND `inferApp` here raises the same mismatch twice (once at
  -- the call site, once at the receiver), and every driver reports from this arm
  -- now. `ft` IS the standalone's retained occurrence on this arm, so nothing is
  -- lost by not re-deriving it from the signature.
  match (if dispatches || isDictVar then
    None
  else
    standaloneSchemeFor env name sym)
    Some _ => unifySpineResult (envAtIfSome dloc env) f ft (pre ++ [(x, xt)])
    None =>
      let _ = if sym == "" then enforceStandaloneDomainAt env name xt dloc k
      inferAppNodes env ft (pre ++ [(EApp f x, xt)])

-- S1/S2 (THE INVERSION, 2026-07-14): is [name] a DEFINER shadow — a top-level fn defined in
-- THIS module that reuses a single-param interface method's name?  This is the exact
-- predicate that decides whether the inversion applies (Fork 1: definer-only).
--
-- ⚠️ It is NOT the same question as "did we reach inferDefinerShadowApp".  That entry point
-- (definerShadowArgHead) ALSO fires for an IMPORTER shadow on the mangled emit path, where
-- the mark pass seeded the route with the provider's mangled symbol (`routeLocalSym /= ""`)
-- — see its header.  Inverting on that signal would invert importer shadows too, which
-- Fork 1 forbids: it breaks the everyday `import map` pattern (`isEmpty [1,2]` must still
-- reach `Foldable.isEmpty`).  definerShadowNamesRef holds bare names on EVERY path — the
-- emit path recovers a mangled local funDef through the mangle map (buildDefinerShadows) —
-- and never holds an imported standalone, so it is the reliable definer/importer test.
--
-- The ifaceMethodName conjunct mirrors definerShadowVarHead / definerShadowArgHead's
-- definer disjunct verbatim, so every entry point agrees on which occurrences the
-- machinery owns.  ✅ S-3 / row 26 CLOSED (#54): a multi-TYPARAM interface
-- (`interface Ix a i`) is now IN scope.  The gate used to be singleParamIfaceMethod (a
-- typaram COUNT test), which excused `Ix a i` from every typing entry point and left its
-- occurrences to ordinary dispatch — check/build kept the pre-inversion per-receiver
-- answer while eval resolved the bare name lexically and E-PANICked (SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md
-- S8; the S7 violation d11 pinned).
isDefinerShadow : ModuleCtx -> String -> Bool
isDefinerShadow mctx name =
  ifaceMethodName mctx name
    && omHasKey name mctx.mcCells.definerShadowNamesRef.value

-- S2 (THE INVERSION, 2026-07-14; SHADOW-INVERSION-DESIGN.md): True iff the shadow [name]
-- applied to a receiver of type [xt] should DISPATCH to the interface method rather than
-- call the standalone.
--
-- ⚠️ FOR A DEFINER SHADOW THE IMPL UNIVERSE IS NO LONGER CONSULTED.  It used to be: a
-- receiver whose head tycon had a visible impl of the shadowed interface dispatched, and the
-- standalone was only a FALLBACK for a no-impl head.  That rule silently ERASED the user's
-- function —
--
--   eq : List Int -> List Int -> Bool
--   eq a b = True
--   main = println (debug (eq [1] [2]))   -- printed False: `impl Eq List` won
--
-- — and `check --types` did not even report the user's signature.  Since the prelude declares
-- ~49 method names over every common type (`map`, `filter`, `length`, `compare`, `eq`, `min`,
-- `empty`, `toList`, `display`, …), that made the most natural names in the language into
-- landmines.  A top-level name written in a module is now THAT MODULE'S NAME: a definer
-- shadow is the standalone, unconditionally, and the argument must type against the
-- standalone's declared domain (a mismatch is a located reject — S2/S3/S6).
--
-- The ONE carve-out (S5, Fork 2): a receiver that is a dict-bound `=>` constraint var of the
-- enclosing function still DISPATCHES.  Writing `Sz a => …` is an explicit, written-down
-- request to resolve through the interface, and there is currently no other way to name the
-- method inside a shadowing module (SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md §1.1).  A grounded head never
-- normalizes to a TVar, so it correctly answers False for every concrete receiver.
--
-- An IMPORTER shadow reaching here (via definerShadowArgHead's mangled-sym arm) keeps the
-- OLD per-receiver rule — Fork 1.
definerReceiverDispatches : DynCtx -> String -> Mono -> Bool
definerReceiverDispatches dyn name xt
  | isDefinerShadow dyn.dcModule name = definerReceiverIsDictVar dyn name xt
  | otherwise = match headTyconMono xt
    -- ARCH B-2.1-g: graph-global, off `bodyImplEnvRef` — see `ieImplExistsForHead`.
    -- The guard above means only the Fork-1 IMPORTER arm reaches here.
    Some head =>
      ieImplExistsForHead
        dyn.dcModule
        dyn.dcModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
        name
        head
    None => definerReceiverIsDictVar dyn name xt

-- P0-19 (constrained-receiver arm): True iff an UNGROUNDED definer-shadow receiver is
-- one of the ENCLOSING group's `=>`-constraint variables for the SHADOWED interface (or
-- a superinterface of it).  Such an occurrence dispatches through that dict — it is a
-- METHOD call, not the standalone — so it must be typed against the method scheme and
-- must NOT have the standalone's declared domain imposed on it.
--
-- Without this, ANY constrained function that calls the method on its own dict-bound
-- var, in a program where some top-level fn shadows that method's name, is silently
-- monomorphised to the shadow's domain.  That includes the PRELUDE's own bodies: on the
-- flat single-file path `prog` is core ++ user, so a user `eq : Int -> Int -> Int`
-- made core's `neq : Eq a => a -> a -> Bool` (`neq x y = not (eq x y)`) infer `eq x y :
-- Int` and reject with `Type mismatch: Bool vs Int` at the top of the user's file.
-- A higher-kinded receiver `t a` reads the written constraint on `t`.
definerReceiverIsDictVar : DynCtx -> String -> Mono -> Bool
definerReceiverIsDictVar dyn name xt = match headMonoNode xt
  TVar cell => match methodEntryHere dyn.dcModule name
    Some (mIface, _, _, _) =>
      dictVarSatisfiesIface
        dyn.dcModule
        mIface.irName
        (tyvarId cell)
        (groupMonos dyn)
    None => False
  _ => False

-- The enclosing group's constraint monos; empty outside a group (a tail body).
groupMonos : DynCtx -> List (String, Mono)
groupMonos dyn = match dyn.dcGroup
  None => []
  Some group => group.gcMonos

-- does any of the group's constraint vars BOTH normalize to tyvar [id] AND carry an
-- interface whose (self + transitive supers) closure includes [mIface]?
dictVarSatisfiesIface : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Bool
dictVarSatisfiesIface mctx _ _ [] = False
dictVarSatisfiesIface mctx mIface id ((cIface, cm) :: rest)
  | monoIsTyvarId cm id && contains mIface (ifaceSelfAndSupers mctx cIface) =
    True
  | otherwise = dictVarSatisfiesIface mctx mIface id rest

-- [iface] plus its transitive `requires` supers (a `Ord a =>` constraint also supplies
-- the `Eq` dict, which its dictionary carries).  Prelude and user super chains alike.
-- Its callers hold interface SPELLINGS (`gcMonos` carries no origin), so
-- the lookup is by spelling over `superDeclsRef`, first match; every other superclass
-- reader looks interfaces up by identity (`superLookup`).
ifaceSelfAndSupers : ModuleCtx -> String -> List String
ifaceSelfAndSupers mctx iface =
  map
    (n => n.superIface.irName)
    (superClosure
      (ir => ifaceSupersOf mctx.mcCells.superDeclsRef.value ir.irName)
      (_ _ _ => Some ())
      (ir _ => ir.irName)
      [(ifaceRefBare iface, ())])

-- P0-19: impose a definer-shadow standalone's declared domain on the actual argument
-- [xt] WHEN the occurrence resolves to the standalone (RLocal).  No declared signature ⇒
-- nothing to enforce (permissive fallback, unchanged).  [dloc] locates the check at the
-- application so a mismatch localizes to the call, not the argument.
--
-- S2 (THE INVERSION): a definer shadow now ALWAYS resolves to the standalone, so its domain
-- is ALWAYS enforced.  This used to skip enforcement whenever the receiver's grounded head
-- had a visible impl of the shadowed interface — that head dispatched, so no domain applied.
-- That skip is precisely what let `eq [1] [2]` sail through `check` against the PRELUDE's
-- `Eq.eq` while the user's `eq : List Int -> List Int -> Bool` was discarded.  The only
-- surviving exemption is the Fork-2 dict-var carve-out: imposing a concrete domain on the
-- enclosing group's `=>`-constraint var would monomorphise its written signature.
-- #1815: [k] is the interface's dispatch index, so the domain imposed on the receiver is
-- the standalone's k-th parameter.  `k = 0` is the pre-#1815 behavior verbatim (the
-- bare-head arms pass it, and both of this function's callers now name the index).
enforceStandaloneDomainAt : TcEnv -> String -> Mono -> Option Loc -> Int -> Unit
enforceStandaloneDomainAt env name xt dloc k =
  match standaloneShadowDomainAt env.teDyn.dcModule name k
    None => ()
    Some dom =>
      if definerReceiverIsDictVar env.teDyn name xt then
        ()
      else
        unifyStandaloneDomain env.teDyn dom xt dloc

-- P0-20 (SILENT WRONG ANSWER, `eq 1 2` → the binary printed 0): typecheck's
-- dispatch-vs-standalone decision and the POST-inference route resolver
-- (resolveRLocalSite) must ask the S2 impl question about the SAME receiver head.
--
-- They did not.  A definer-shadow receiver that is not yet grounded AT INFERENCE TIME —
-- a NUMERIC LITERAL is the everyday case, it is `Num a => a`, not `Int` — took the
-- ungrounded arm (S5 ⇒ standalone) and was typed against the standalone's scheme.  That
-- typing then UNIFIES the standalone's declared domain into the receiver, so by the time
-- resolveRLocalSite runs the receiver IS grounded — to `Int` — and `Int` has `impl Eq
-- Int`, so the route resolver left the site to DISPATCH.  Result: `check` typed
-- `eq 1 2 : Int` (the user's `eq : Int -> Int -> Int`) while eval/emit called the
-- interface method and produced a `Bool` — `run` panicked (`intToString: not an Int`)
-- and `build` SILENTLY PRINTED 0.  Only literal receivers were affected: `f k = eq k 1`
-- (k : Int, already grounded) dispatched consistently on all three paths.
--
-- Fix: perform S5's monomorphisation FIRST (it is the same unification the standalone
-- arm would have done, only earlier), then decide.  With the receiver grounded to `Int`,
-- S2 sees the impl and DISPATCHES on every path — check == run == build.  A grounded
-- receiver, a dict-bound one, and an unsignatured standalone (no domain to ground to)
-- are all untouched; so is a standalone whose domain head has NO impl of the shadowed
-- interface (`compiler/frontend/parser.mdk`'s `orElse : Parser a -> Parser a -> Parser a`
-- against `Alternative.orElse` — the compiler declares no `impl Alternative Parser`).
--
-- [dom] MUST come from shadowDomainFor, not standaloneShadowDomain: on the MANGLED emit
-- path the standalone was renamed `<mid>__eq`, so the bare-name sig table is empty there
-- and grounding would be silently inert — which is not a no-op, it flips the emit path to
-- the STANDALONE arm while check/run dispatch.  (Observed: `build` printed 3, `run`
-- printed False.)  Same bug, other direction.
groundShadowReceiver : DynCtx ->
  Option Mono ->
  Mono ->
  Bool ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
groundShadowReceiver dyn dom xt isDictVar dloc
  | isDictVar = ()
  | isSome (headTyconMono xt) = ()
  | otherwise = match dom
    None => ()
    Some d => unifyStandaloneDomain dyn d xt dloc

-- P0-20: the definer-shadow standalone's declared domain, resolved on EITHER path.
-- Un-mangled run/check (sym == ""): the module's own sig table, keyed by the bare name.
-- Mangled emit (sym /= ""): private_mangle renamed the standalone to `<mid>__name`, so
-- definerShadowSigsRef has no `name` entry — take the domain off the env binding for the
-- mangled symbol, whose value descriptor also supplies the selected occurrence.
-- #1815: [k] is the interface's dispatch index; `k = 0` is the pre-#1815 behavior.
shadowDomainForAt : TcEnv -> String -> String -> Int -> Option Mono
shadowDomainForAt env name "" k =
  standaloneShadowDomainAt env.teDyn.dcModule name k
shadowDomainForAt env _ sym k = match lookupVar env sym
  None => None
  Some s => nthFunDomain k (instantiate env.teDyn.dcModule s)

-- unify the standalone domain against the argument at the call's location.
unifyStandaloneDomain : DynCtx -> Mono -> Mono -> Option Loc -> Unit
unifyStandaloneDomain dyn dom xt dloc = unifyIn (dynAt dloc dyn) dom xt

-- a definer-shadow standalone's declared parameter type, freshly instantiated (so a
-- polymorphic standalone domain does not leak vars across sites).  None when there is
-- no top-level signature, or the signature is not a function type.
-- #1815: [k] is the interface's dispatch index — the standalone's k-th declared
-- parameter is the one the receiver occupies.  `k = 0` is the pre-#1815 behavior.
standaloneShadowDomainAt : ModuleCtx -> String -> Int -> Option Mono
standaloneShadowDomainAt mctx name k =
  match omLookup name mctx.mcCells.definerShadowSigsRef.value
    None => None
    Some ty => nthFunDomain k (instantiate mctx (sigToScheme mctx ty))

-- P0-19 d4b (S4): a definer-shadow occurrence in bare VALUE position (NOT the head of
-- its own application — dcShadowHeadCtx is False) denotes the STANDALONE.  Returns the
-- standalone's declared scheme freshly instantiated so a HOF sees `Int -> Int`, not the
-- permissive method scheme `a -> Int` — making `map size [Box …]` a located reject
-- (Box vs Int) while `map size [1,2,3]` still accepts.  Only fires for a single-param
-- interface-method name that is a module-local standalone WITH a declared signature;
-- everything else (app head, non-shadow, unsignatured standalone) returns None → the
-- ordinary env lookup / method scheme, unchanged.
-- #411 (row 21, S4): the IMPORTER half of the same cell.  S4 is not keyed on where the
-- standalone lives — a value-position shadow denotes the standalone whether this module
-- DEFINED it or IMPORTED it — so the definer arm below is followed by the importer arm,
-- reading the imported standalone's scheme from the lexical binding descriptor
-- (the same scheme inferShadowApp's standalone arm uses).
--
-- Fork 1 is not touched.  This arm is gated on dcShadowHeadCtx = False, i.e. bare
-- VALUE position only; every APPLIED importer occurrence goes through inferShadowApp,
-- which now flags its head (inferShadowAppHead) exactly as the definer path always did.
-- So per-receiver importer dispatch (i4's `isEmpty [1, 2]` → `Foldable.isEmpty`) is
-- unchanged — rows 15-20/22 do not move.
--
-- #54: the definer arm is gated on ifaceMethodName (typaram-agnostic) and the importer arm
-- on singleTyparamIfaceMethod (Fork 1's per-receiver scope) — the guards are now per-arm,
-- where they used to share one leading singleParamIfaceMethod test.
maybeStandaloneValueMono : TcEnv -> String -> Option Mono
maybeStandaloneValueMono env name =
  map
    (value =>
      let _ = rejectAdmittedValueOccurrence env.teDyn.dcModule name
      (instantiateStandaloneOccurrence
        env
        name
        ""
        env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
        value).svoInstance.mtiBody)
    (standaloneValueBinding env name)

-- S2-DECL (d) for a VALUE occurrence of an importer shadow (`ap2 mth`, `g = mth`,
-- `flip mth`): no argument is applied, so no admitted declaration's own receiver can be
-- evaluated, and with two or more admitted the declarations have not been shown to
-- agree.  That is the located reject, in every import order.  The standalone still
-- types the occurrence, as at the applied arms' reject.  A definer shadow denotes its
-- own module's standalone and is never ambiguous.
rejectAdmittedValueOccurrence : ModuleCtx -> String -> Unit
rejectAdmittedValueOccurrence mctx name
  | isDefinerShadow mctx name = ()
  | otherwise =
    let ifs = methodAdmittedHere mctx name
    if listLen ifs >= 2 then pushAmbiguousShadowDecl mctx name ifs mctx.mcLoc

instantiateStandaloneOccurrence : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Option Loc ->
  ValueScheme ->
  SelectedValueOccurrence
instantiateStandaloneOccurrence outer name sym origin value =
  let env = envAt origin outer
  let inst = instantiateValueTracked env.teDyn.dcModule name value.vsScheme
  let declared =
    declaredEffectsAt env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph inst value.vsDeclared
  let _ = match declared
    Some dc =>
      recordDeclaredBindingCall
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        dc
        inst.mtiSubstitution.misTypeSubst
    None =>
      recordShadowStandaloneObls env name inst.mtiSubstitution.misTypeSubst
  let key = if sym == "" then name else sym
  let dc = optionOr (shadowDeclaredFor env.teDyn.dcModule name key) declared
  SelectedValueOccurrence {
    svoScheme = value.vsScheme,
    svoInstance = inst,
    svoDicts =
      shadowStandaloneDictSlots
        env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
        dc.cdSlots
        dc.cdArgs
        inst.mtiSubstitution.misTypeSubst,
  }

standaloneValueBinding : TcEnv -> String -> Option ValueScheme
standaloneValueBinding env name
  | env.teDyn.dcShadowHeadCtx = None
  | ifaceMethodName env.teDyn.dcModule name
    && omHasKey name env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.definerShadowNamesRef.value =
    lookupStandaloneValue env name
  | not (singleTyparamIfaceMethod env.teDyn.dcModule name) = None
  | otherwise = lookupStandaloneValue env name

-- #410/#669 (S4, EMIT path only): the sym-recovering peer of maybeStandaloneValueMono,
-- for the marked (EMethodAt) value-position occurrence whose bare name maybeStandaloneValueMono
-- can no longer see because the mangler renamed the definer standalone's funDef to
