-- so guarding the stamp on RNone reproduces that do-nothing None arm exactly and never
-- clobbers an RLocal seed.  implRef is []-seeded everywhere, so []-over-[] needs no guard.
resolveSite sx rpNames name tagRef implRef resultMono fullMono encl origin scope =
  let (route, routes) =
    entail
      sx
      name
      resultMono
      encl
      scope
      (EKReturn fullMono (omHasKey name rpNames))
  let _ = match route
    RNone => ()
    _ => tagRef := route
  implRef := routes

-- An admitted-set occurrence's route, committed by `admittedSelection`, the function
-- that decides its verdict in the same drain (`runStampCtx`): the selected instance's
-- canonical key and prerequisites, and the selecting declaration's interface word on
-- the occurrence, which carried none while its spelling named two or more.  Any
-- other answer is rejected there, and the site keeps no route.
resolveAdmittedSite : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  Ref String ->
  Ref Route ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
resolveAdmittedSite sx name ifaceRef tagRef implRef fullMono encl scope =
  match (admittedSelection
    sx
    sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
    name
    fullMono)
    Selects iface row goals =>
      ifaceRef := ifaceWordOf iface.irOrigin iface.irName
      tagRef :=
        RKey
          (rowRouteKey row)
          []
          (selectedCallSupers sx name (Some row) encl scope goals)
      implRef := implDictRoutesForRow sx encl scope goals row
    _ => ()

resolveExactReturnSite : SiteCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  String ->
  Ref Route ->
  Ref (List Route) ->
  Mono ->
  MethodReturnRequest ->
  String ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
resolveExactReturnSite sx rpNames name tagRef implRef resultMono request encl origin scope =
  if methodReturnAmbiguousWithoutGiven sx.sxModule request then
    noteMethodReturnTrace sx.sxModule MRTStamped request None []
  else match methodReturnArgs sx.sxModule.mcGraph request
    None =>
      let _ = noteMethodReturnTrace sx.sxModule MRTStamped request None []
      resolveSite
        sx
        rpNames
        name
        tagRef
        implRef
        resultMono
        request.mrrOccurrence
        encl
        origin
        scope
    Some _ =>
      let resolution = solveExactReturnOnce sx request
      let _ =
        if methodReturnResolutionValid sx.sxModule request resolution then
          ()
        else
          panic "ordinary return route received invalid solver evidence"
      let (route, routes) =
        exactReturnRoutes sx name encl scope (omHasKey name rpNames) resolution
      let _ =
        noteMethodReturnTrace sx.sxModule MRTStamped request (Some route) routes
      let _ = match route
        RNone => ()
        _ => tagRef := route
      implRef := routes

exactReturnRoutes : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Bool ->
  MethodReturnResolution ->
  (Route, List Route)
exactReturnRoutes sx name encl scope isReturnPosition resolution = match (
  resolution.mrrOutcome,
  resolution.mrrSelectedRow,
)
  (Solved (GivenEvidence binder), None) => (
    givenRoute sx.sxModule.mcGraph isReturnPosition binder,
    [],
  )
  (Solved (SuperclassEvidence parent path), None) => (
    RProj (givenRoute sx.sxModule.mcGraph isReturnPosition parent) path,
    [],
  )
  (Solved (InstanceEvidence _ args prerequisites _), Some row) => (
    RKey
      (rowRouteKey row)
      []
      (selectedCallSupers sx name (Some row) encl scope args),
    methodReturnEvidenceRoutes sx encl scope prerequisites,
  )
  -- No instance was selected: the site keeps no route, never the occurrence's head
  -- tag, which names no instance.
  (Deferred _ _, None) => (RNone, [])
  (Insoluble _ _, None) => (RNone, [])
  _ => panic "ordinary return outcome and selected row disagree"

givenRoute : GraphCtx -> Bool -> EvidenceBinderId -> Route
givenRoute gctx isReturnPosition binder =
  if isReturnPosition then
    RDictFwd (renderEvidenceBinder gctx binder)
  else
    RDict (renderEvidenceBinder gctx binder)

methodReturnEvidenceRoutes : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List PrerequisiteEvidence ->
  List Route
methodReturnEvidenceRoutes sx encl scope prerequisites =
  map (methodReturnEvidenceRoute sx encl scope) prerequisites

methodReturnEvidenceRoute : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  PrerequisiteEvidence ->
  Route
methodReturnEvidenceRoute sx encl scope prerequisite =
  match prerequisite.prerequisiteArguments
    first :: more =>
      routeOfD
        sx
        prerequisite.prerequisiteInterface
        encl
        scope
        KeepNone
        first
        more
        (reqWalkStart ())
    [] => RNone

resolveNumLitSite : SiteCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  String ->
  Ref Route ->
  Mono ->
  Mono ->
  ClassPredicate ->
  String ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
resolveNumLitSite sx rpNames name tagRef resultMono fullMono predicate encl origin scope =
  let (route, routes) =
    entail
      sx
      name
      resultMono
      encl
      scope
      (EKNumReturn predicate fullMono (omHasKey name rpNames) origin)
  let _ = match route
    RNone => ()
    _ => tagRef := numericReturnRoute route routes
  ()

numericReturnRoute : Route -> List Route -> Route
numericReturnRoute (RKey key _ sups) routes = RKey key routes sups
numericReturnRoute route _ = route

-- Recover the FULL list of interface-type-parameter monos for a method occurrence,
-- ordered by the interface's typaram declaration.  Look up the method's interface
-- (methodEntryHere: iface, typarams, declared method Ty), match the declared Ty
-- against the occurrence's full mono to bind each typaram → its inferred mono, then
-- read them out in typaram order.  For `fromEntries : List e -> c` matched against the
-- occurrence `List Int -> Set _a`, this yields [Set _a, Int] (c then e) — the element
-- grounding (`e ↦ Int`) the result-only `resultMono` (= c = Set _a) had lost.  None
-- when the method has no registered interface (a plain `=>`-constrained fn) or the
-- declared/occurrence shapes do not match — resolveSite falls back to [resultMono].
ifaceParamMonos : ModuleCtx -> String -> Mono -> Option (List Mono)
ifaceParamMonos mctx name fullMono = occurrenceParamMonos mctx name fullMono []

-- `ifaceParamMonos` at an occurrence that posed its goal with [omitted]
-- (`methodOmittedVars`): a typaram the declared type never mentions reads the
-- goal's own variable, so the route selects on the vector §3 determined.
occurrenceParamMonos : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  Mono ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Option (List Mono)
occurrenceParamMonos mctx name fullMono omitted =
  match methodEntryHere mctx name
    None => None
    Some (_, typarams, mty, _) =>
      map
        (subst => map (paramMonoOf (subst ++ omitted)) typarams)
        (matchTyMono mty fullMono)

-- RIGID PRODUCER 2 of 2 (#1110): [tp] is an interface type-PARAMETER name, so
-- the fallback when the head match bound nothing for it is a rigid variable,
-- not a type constructor.  See `Mono.TRigid`.
paramMonoOf : List (String, Mono) -> String -> Mono
paramMonoOf subst tp = optionOr (TRigid tp) (lookupAssoc tp subst)

importerAdmittedVerdict : ModuleCtx ->
  ImplEnv ->
  String ->
  List Mono ->
  AdmittedVerdict
importerAdmittedVerdict mctx env name ats = match methodAdmittedHere mctx name
  [] => AdDefer
  ifs =>
    if listLen ifs < 2 then
      AdDefer
    else match admittedDeclHitters mctx env name ifs ats
      None => AdReject ifs
      Some hits => if isEmptyL hits then AdStandalone else AdReject ifs

-- The admitted declarations whose OWN (receiver argument, impl query) pair — S2-DECL
-- (b), both halves from the same declaration — HITS.  `None` if any declaration's pair
-- cannot be evaluated at all, which `importerAdmittedVerdict` reads as an ambiguity.
admittedDeclHitters : ModuleCtx ->
  ImplEnv ->
  String ->
  List IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option (List IfaceRef)
admittedDeclHitters mctx _ _ [] _ = Some []
admittedDeclHitters mctx env name (ir :: rest) ats =
  match admittedDeclHits mctx env name ir ats
    None => None
    Some hit =>
      map
        (hs => if hit then ir :: hs else hs)
        (admittedDeclHitters mctx env name rest ats)

-- S2-DECL (a)+(b) for ONE declaration: its receiver argument is the applied argument at
-- ITS OWN dispatch index (not the occurrence's first argument), and the impl query asks
-- about an impl of THAT interface at that receiver's head — over the unchanged
-- graph-global row set (`ieImplExistsForHeadOf` is `ieImplExistsForHead`'s own body).
admittedDeclHits : ModuleCtx ->
  ImplEnv ->
  String ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Bool
admittedDeclHits mctx env name ir ats = do
  k <- lookupIdxById ir name mctx.mcCells.methodDispatchIdxByIdRef.value
  at <- nthMono k ats
  hk <- headTyconMono at
  Some (ieImplExistsForHeadOf mctx env name hk (Some [ir]))

-- The OUTERMOST dispatch index over the admitted set — the spine node at which every
-- admitted declaration's receiver argument is already inferred, and therefore the only
-- node at which (b)'s per-declaration pairs can be evaluated JOINTLY.  Falls back to
-- `methodDispatchIdx` (the single-winner index) for every name with fewer than two
-- admitted declarations, i.e. for every program that exists today.
importerDispatchIdxOuter : ModuleCtx -> String -> Option Int
importerDispatchIdxOuter mctx name =
  match admittedIdxMax mctx name (methodAdmittedHere mctx name)
    Some k => Some k
    None => methodDispatchIdx mctx name

admittedIdxMax : ModuleCtx -> String -> List IfaceRef -> Option Int
admittedIdxMax mctx _ [] = None
admittedIdxMax mctx name (ir :: rest) =
  let here = lookupIdxById ir name mctx.mcCells.methodDispatchIdxByIdRef.value
  match admittedIdxMax mctx name rest
    None => here
    Some k => match here
      None => Some k
      Some j => Some (maxI j k)

-- Ground each admitted declaration's OWN receiver argument to the standalone's declared
-- domain at that index, before the impl queries are asked — the P0-20 symmetry rule
-- ("ask the impl question about the SAME head the route resolver will") applied once per
-- declaration instead of once per occurrence.  A no-op for every name with fewer than
-- two admitted declarations, since `methodAdmittedHere` answers `[]` there.
groundAdmittedReceivers : TcEnv -> String -> List Mono -> Option Loc -> Unit
groundAdmittedReceivers env mname ats dloc =
  groundAdmittedGo
    env
    mname
    (methodAdmittedHere env.teDyn.dcModule mname)
    ats
    dloc

groundAdmittedGo : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  List IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
groundAdmittedGo env _ [] _ _ = ()
groundAdmittedGo env mname (ir :: rest) ats dloc =
  let _ =
    match (lookupIdxById
      ir
      mname
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.methodDispatchIdxByIdRef.value)
      None => ()
      Some k => match nthMono k ats
        None => ()
        Some at =>
          groundShadowReceiver
            env.teDyn
            (importerShadowDomainAt env mname k)
            at
            (definerReceiverIsDictVar env.teDyn mname at)
            dloc
  groundAdmittedGo env mname rest ats dloc

-- ERROR-QUALITY: name the two things that collide, say what the collision costs, then
-- name the fixes.  Callers locate it at the occurrence's head (`appSpineHeadLoc`): an
-- application carries no location of its own, and the location current when the
-- occurrence is reached can belong to whichever module was checked last.  Phrased after `aliasAmbiguityMsg`, the nearest neighbour in this file.
-- The interface list is the SORTED admitted set, so the prose does not encode import
-- order any more than the verdict does (S2-DECL (e)).
pushAmbiguousShadowDecl : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List IfaceRef ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
pushAmbiguousShadowDecl mctx name ifs dloc =
  pushTypeErrorHelpFixAt
    mctx
    "T-AMBIGUOUS-SHADOW-DECL"
    dloc
    "`\{name}` is ambiguous here: \{joinWith " and " (map shadowIfaceLabel ifs)} each declare a method `\{name}` and are both in scope; \{ambiguousShadowHelp}"
    ambiguousShadowHelp
    None

-- The method-only sibling of `pushAmbiguousShadowDecl`: no standalone is in scope,
-- so the admitted declarations are the only candidates, and the occurrence decides
-- none of them (`admittedSelection`).  Same sorted interface list, same help.
pushAmbiguousMethod : ModuleCtx -> String -> List IfaceRef -> Option Loc -> Unit
pushAmbiguousMethod mctx name ifs loc =
  pushTypeErrorHelpFixAt
    mctx
    "T-AMBIGUOUS-METHOD"
    loc
    "`\{name}` is ambiguous here: \{joinWith " and " (map shadowIfaceLabel ifs)} each declare a method `\{name}`, and this use does not decide which one it means; bring only one of those interfaces into scope"
    ambiguousShadowHelp
    None

-- The admitted set's one selecting declaration [sel] has method-level constraints,
-- which an admitted-set occurrence records no dictionaries for (`routableSelection`).
-- Same code and help as `pushAmbiguousMethod`: the ambiguity of the spelling is
-- what withholds those dictionaries.
pushUnroutableAdmitted : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List IfaceRef ->
  IfaceRef ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
pushUnroutableAdmitted mctx name ifs sel loc =
  pushTypeErrorHelpFixAt
    mctx
    "T-AMBIGUOUS-METHOD"
    loc
    "`\{name}` names a method of more than one interface here (\{joinWith " and " (map shadowIfaceLabel ifs)}); the one this use selects, `\{sel.irName}.\{name}`, has method-level constraints, and a use of a name that more than one interface declares cannot supply their dictionaries; bring only one of those interfaces into scope"
    ambiguousShadowHelp
    None

-- C5: stamp RLocal on each recorded standalone-shadow arg-position site whose
-- receiver mono now grounds to a concrete head tycon with NO impl of the method.
-- The receiver HAS an impl (the genuine-method case, e.g. `toList (Some 7)`) → leave
-- the route untouched (RNone → eval arg-tag-dispatches to the real impl).  An
-- ungrounded receiver (still a tyvar) → leave it (polymorphic, deferred).
-- RLocal only when no impl exists.
-- S-1: the stamp calls routesOfMonosTop — a PURE
-- function of the (union-find-solved) constraint monos — to fill the standalone's own
-- dict routes IN PLACE.  Deliberately NOT routed through pendingDictApps: that list is
-- resolved by resolveDictApps, which runs AFTER this in `moduleStampOrder`, so the stamp
-- would read `[]`.  Resolving inside the stamp is ordering-immune.  An unconstrained
-- standalone has no monos ⇒ routesOfMonosTop returns [] immediately (it cannot even
-- reach its AmbiguousImpl arm) ⇒ `RLocal sym []` ⇒ byte-identical to the pre-S1 stamp.
-- #156 S3d — resolveRLocalSites is DELIBERATELY NOT routed through `entail`, and DICT-
-- SEMANTICS §3 conformance REQUIRES that, rather than merely permitting it.  This pass
-- implements §4 `(var)`'s FIRST premise — binding selection: does this occurrence denote the
-- module's own standalone `sym` or a shadowed interface method?  (Keyed on the solved receiver
-- mono, which is why it runs post-inference.)  That decision reads shadow facts — isDefinerShadow,
-- definerShadowNamesRef — that are NOT components of entailment's domain `(IE, CE, P, π)` (§3
-- resolution-determinism); they are facts about Γ.  Folding them into the one entailment function
-- would make it depend on inputs outside its spec-given domain — violating the very law a merge
-- would invoke.  The tell: the `Some tag` arm treats "a live impl exists" as DO-NOTHING (the name
-- is a genuine method, dispatched elsewhere) and emits RLocal for the NO-impl case — the inverse of
-- `entailInst`'s success condition.  "No π to discharge; the name denotes another binding" is not an
-- evidence statement.  §4 `(var)`'s SECOND premise — the chosen standalone's actual entailment
-- obligations — IS routed through the one engine: every RLocal payload is filled by routesOfMonosTop
-- → entail (EKNestedTop).  So the single-entailment-function law holds at 4-of-5 BY CONSTRUCTION; what
-- stays out is exactly the binding-selection axis §3 never claimed (cf. §8 I1: identity keyed by
-- binding, not bare name).  "Does an impl exist" and "which impl entails" must agree on ONE
-- impl table — a drift between them would be a real dispatch bug.  #415 item 2: that
-- agreement is STRUCTURAL, not a standing obligation.
-- Arch B-2.1-g rebased both reads, together, onto `ModuleCells.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef`, and the
-- sentence that stood here — "There is no second table in scope to drift TO" — WAS ALREADY
-- FALSE and is what licensed a bad scoping.  `bodyImplEnvRef` has been a second impl table,
-- in scope from anywhere, since B-2.1-a2, and B-2.1-b2 moved three SELECTION legs onto it
-- while this site's two reads stayed on the threaded prefix `[keyTable]`.  `B-2.1-c` then
-- moved the sibling SHADOW existence reads and deferred this one, which produced exactly the
-- drift this block claimed was unreachable: existence answered True off the whole graph while
-- `routesOfMonosTop … keyTable`, one line below, had no row to select — a located reject
-- became exit 0 printing a garbage pointer.  So the agreement is restored the only way it can
-- be, by moving BOTH: `ieImplExistsForHead …bodyImplEnvRef…` directly, and `keyForSite` (also
-- repointed onto `bodyImplEnvRef`) via routesOfMonosTop → routeOf → entail (EKNestedTop) →
-- entailInst.  ⚠️ THE INVARIANT IS UNCHANGED AND IS STILL THE ONE THAT MATTERS: these two
-- reads must name ONE population.  It is no longer enforced by a shared parameter, so it is
-- now enforced by a shared REF — and the check on any future edit here is "does the thing I
-- am reading answer over the same population `keyForSite` selects from?", not "am I using
-- [keyTable]?".  No impl list is threaded through this signature or through
-- `routesOfMonosTop`'s subtree any more.
-- (The inference-time existence reads in `inferShadowApp` / `definerReceiverDispatches` are
-- the same decision at an earlier PHASE and are now on the same ref for the same reason —
-- B-2.1-c's measurement is that a phase split of one decision is as fatal as a table split.
-- ⚠️ Do not re-derive the retired defence "GLOBAL by design — local ∪ imported ∪ prelude":
-- `SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md:242-245` retires that phrase as a false synonym for graph-global, and
-- `shadowKeyTableRef` was in fact the cumulative topological PREFIX on the Module arm.)
resolveRLocalSites : SiteCtx -> List PendingEntry -> Unit
resolveRLocalSites sx [] = ()
resolveRLocalSites sx ((PendingEntry name tagRef am encl kind loc scope _) :: rest) =
  let sx = { sx | sxSite = loc }
  let _ = match kind
    SKRLocal sym forceLocal monos ifaces argVecs =>
      if forceLocal then
        tagRef :=
          RLocal sym (routesOfMonosTopV sx encl scope monos ifaces argVecs)
      else
        resolveRLocalSite sx name tagRef am encl scope sym monos ifaces argVecs
    _ => ()
  resolveRLocalSites sx rest

-- C5: stamp RLocal on each recorded standalone-shadow arg-position site whose
-- receiver mono now grounds to a concrete head tycon with NO impl of the method.
-- The receiver HAS an impl (the genuine-method case, e.g. `toList (Some 7)`):
-- leave the route untouched — eval arg-tag-dispatches on RNone; emit already
-- stamped the correct RKey<receiverHead> via resolveArgStamps.
-- An ungrounded receiver (still a tyvar) → leave it.  The
-- RLocal-vs-ordinary-dispatch split keys the genuine case off the receiver.
resolveRLocalSite : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  Ref Route ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  String ->
  List Mono ->
  List IfaceRef ->
  List (List Mono) ->
  Unit
resolveRLocalSite sx name tagRef am encl scope sym monos ifaces argVecs =
  match headTyconMono am
    -- S2 (THE INVERSION): route by SHADOW KIND first, receiver second.
    --   * DEFINER shadow (the name is this module's own top-level fn) → the standalone,
    --     UNCONDITIONALLY.  The impl universe is not consulted; a grounded head with a live
    --     impl no longer steals the call.  (The APP path already forces this via the
    --     RLocalSite `forceLocal` flag; this arm is what carries the other recorders —
    --     notably the VALUE-position sites pushed by the generic recordRLocalSite, which is
    --     gated on standaloneValuesRef and that set holds definer AND importer shadows.)
    --   * IMPORTER shadow (Fork 1) → the OLD per-receiver rule, unchanged: a live impl at the
    --     receiver head dispatches, else the standalone.  An `import` is a SIBLING scope, not
    --     an inner one, so it does not shadow; inverting it too would break the everyday
    --     `import map` pattern (`isEmpty [1,2]` must still reach `Foldable.isEmpty`).
    -- am is the ACTUAL argument type (inferDefinerShadowApp records it), not the standalone's
    -- declared domain, so the importer arm's impl query is still meaningful.
    --
    -- ⚠️ isDefinerShadow — NOT a bare definerShadowNamesRef membership test.  It carries the
    -- SAME gate every typing entry point applies (ifaceMethodName, #54; it was the typaram-
    -- COUNT test singleParamIfaceMethod until S-3 / row 26 was closed).  Routing here on a
    -- gate the typing entry points do not share would route a site whose TYPE came from the
    -- dispatch path — route and type disagreeing is exactly the P0-20 bug class.  Keep the
    -- two gates identical.
    -- ARCH B-2.1-g: graph-global, off `bodyImplEnvRef` — see `ieImplExistsForHead`, and
    -- see the `#415 item 2` block above for why this read could only move TOGETHER with
    -- its sibling selection leg (`routesOfMonosTop … keyTable` → `keyForSite`, likewise
    -- repointed by this bite).  Both now read ONE table again, and it is the same table
    -- the emitter counts over.
    Some tag =>
      -- Route construction solves dictionary obligations. Do it only after
      -- committing to the standalone, never for a discarded method alternative.
      if not (isDefinerShadow sx.sxModule name)
        && ieImplExistsForHead
          sx.sxModule
          sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
          name
          tag then
        ()
      else
        tagRef :=
          RLocal sym (routesOfMonosTopV sx encl scope monos ifaces argVecs)
    -- An UNGROUNDED definer-shadow receiver keeps the old default (RLocal → standalone);
    -- other (importer) ungrounded sites stay untouched (deferred/polymorphic).
    None =>
      if omHasKey name sx.sxModule.mcCells.definerShadowNamesRef.value then
        tagRef :=
          RLocal sym (routesOfMonosTopV sx encl scope monos ifaces argVecs)

-- if [m] normalizes to a registered constraint variable, the dict parameter name
-- a method at that type reads.  A return-position method at a HIGHER-KINDED
-- constraint var (`pure : a -> m a`, so the result mono is `m Unit` = TApp (TVar
-- m) Unit) carries the dict var in the application HEAD, not at top level — recurse
-- through TApp to find it.  (A concrete head, e.g. `Option Unit` after unification,
-- is a TCon and falls through to None → RKey, unchanged.)
activeDictVarOf : GraphCtx -> Mono -> ScopeId -> Option EvidenceBinderId
activeDictVarOf gctx m useScope = match peelQual m
  TVar cell =>
    firstDictForEncl
      gctx
      (tyvarId cell)
      useScope
      gctx.graphRun.activeDictVars.value
  TApp a _ => activeDictVarOf gctx a useScope
  _ => None

-- The lexical active-dict lookup.  `registerImplRequires` registers every method
-- of an impl under the same impl tyvar id (`impl Ord (List a)` registers `a` once
-- per compare/lt/gt/min/max/…).  Each entry now carries the exact body scope that
-- owns its slot.  The occurrence's captured scope may read that owner or an
-- ancestor and rejects every sibling; generated dictionary spellings play no
-- part in selection, and neither does the enclosing declaration's name: a site in
-- a test or prop body, which has none, still sees the givens of a local binding it
-- sits in.
activeDictVarForEncl : GraphCtx -> Mono -> ScopeId -> Option EvidenceBinderId
activeDictVarForEncl gctx m useScope = match peelQual m
  TVar cell =>
    firstDictForEncl
      gctx
      (tyvarId cell)
      useScope
      gctx.graphRun.activeDictVars.value
  TApp a _ => activeDictVarForEncl gctx a useScope
  _ => None

-- The lexical active-dict lookup restricted to binders [answers] accepts: the
-- registry keeps every binder registered for the variable, most recent first.
activeDictVarAnswering : GraphCtx ->
  Mono ->
  ScopeId ->
  (EvidenceBinderId -> Bool) ->
  Option EvidenceBinderId
activeDictVarAnswering gctx m useScope answers = match peelQual m
  TVar cell =>
    find
      (b => answers b)
      (visibleDictsFor
        gctx
        (tyvarId cell)
        useScope
        gctx.graphRun.activeDictVars.value)
  TApp a _ => activeDictVarAnswering gctx a useScope answers
  _ => None

visibleDictsFor : GraphCtx ->
  Int ->
  ScopeId ->
  List (Int, EvidenceBinderId) ->
  List EvidenceBinderId
visibleDictsFor gctx _ _ [] = []
visibleDictsFor gctx id useScope ((eid, binder) :: rest)
  | eid == id
    && Scopes.givenVisibleFrom
      (currentScopeStore gctx ())
      useScope
      (Scopes.binderScope binder) =
    binder :: visibleDictsFor gctx id useScope rest
  | otherwise = visibleDictsFor gctx id useScope rest

firstDictForEncl : GraphCtx ->
  Int ->
  ScopeId ->
  List (Int, EvidenceBinderId) ->
  Option EvidenceBinderId
firstDictForEncl gctx _ _ [] = None
firstDictForEncl gctx id useScope ((eid, binder) :: rest)
  | eid == id
    && Scopes.givenVisibleFrom
      (currentScopeStore gctx ())
      useScope
      (Scopes.binderScope binder) = Some binder
  | otherwise = firstDictForEncl gctx id useScope rest

-- activeDictVarOf, but for a constraint var that is the ENCLOSING fn's OWN constraint
-- var, return [encl]'s in-scope dict param (the slot it sits at) rather than the
-- GLOBAL activeDictVars entry.  In a mutually-recursive group the constraint vars of
-- the siblings unify to one id; activeDictVars (global, uncleared) maps that id to
-- whichever sibling registered it LAST — so an arg-stamp inside `evenCat` would
-- forward `$dict_oddCat_0` (out of scope in evenCat's body).  Preferring encl's own
-- slot keeps the forwarded dict the one actually bound in the body.  A miss is None;
-- evidence owned by a different impl is not in scope here.
-- #1177: [goal] is the PREDICATE the use site has to discharge (its interface, and
-- the instantiated argument vector when the occurrence let one be recovered), NOT
-- just the constraint var — see `enclDictVarOf`.  `None` selects the legacy scalar
-- lookup, still bounded by the same lexical owner.
activeDictVarOfEncl : ModuleCtx ->
  Option PredicateRequest ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option AssumAnswer
activeDictVarOfEncl mctx None m encl useScope =
  map LegacyScalar (activeDictVarForEncl mctx.mcGraph m useScope)
activeDictVarOfEncl mctx (Some request) m encl useScope =
  -- A complete predicate request is terminal: a miss must not be overwritten by
  -- the scalar tyvar-id registry, whose key cannot distinguish declarations or
  -- complete argument vectors.  The None arm above is the legacy scalar control.
  orElseOpt
    (map LegacyScalar (enclDictVarOf mctx (Some request) m encl useScope))
    (implReqDictVarOf mctx.mcGraph (Some request) m useScope)

-- 🚨 #1154 RESIDUAL: AN IMPL-`requires` SITE IS RESOLVED BY ITS PREDICATE, NOT BY ITS
-- CONSTRAINT VAR'S ID — the same rule #1177 established for the SIGNATURE `=>` channel,
-- on the channel #1177 did not reach.  `registerReqSlots` opens one dict slot per
-- `requires` ENTRY but keys `activeDictVars` on the tyvar ids INSIDE the entry, so
-- `impl Sh (Box a) requires Ix a Char, Dbg2 a` registers `a`'s id TWICE — once per slot.
-- `firstDictForEncl` then scans a cons-list whose head is the LAST registration, so
-- EVERY method use in the body read the LAST slot: `ix x 'z'` read the `Dbg2` dict, its
-- route degraded, and first-declared-`impl Ix` won.  MEASURED on the typed Core IR dump
-- at this slice's base — `sh`'s body lowered to `CMethod "ix" (RDict "$dict_sh_1")` and
-- `CMethod "dbg2" (RDict "$dict_sh_1")`, with `$dict_sh_0` bound and never read — which
-- is why moving the `Ix` entry to the END of the `requires` list (a meaning-preserving
-- edit) moved the answer from 116 to the correct 227.
--
-- ⚠️ THIS IS NOT THE `argReqRoute`/`EKNestedTop` GOAL-VECTOR SEAM, AND THAT SEAM IS NOT
-- BROKEN.  The routes handed to the call site are already correct at every position
-- (`(RKey "Ix|Int Char|") (RKey "Int")`, in `requires` order); the loss is entirely on
-- the CONSUMPTION side, in which slot the impl BODY reads.  A fix aimed at the routing
-- ladder would have moved nothing.
--
-- A complete request uses one exact pass.  A miss is terminal at
-- `activeDictVarOfEncl`; only an explicit no-predicate route may consult scalar state.
--
-- #2547 unit 3: the scan is `firstPredForEnclAt` — the id-gated given lookup — not a
-- private `implReqPick`.  The two were term-for-term the same test over the same pair in
-- opposite tuple orders; one given environment leaves one of them.
implReqDictVarOf : GraphCtx ->
  Option PredicateRequest ->
  Mono ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option AssumAnswer
implReqDictVarOf gctx None _ _ = None
implReqDictVarOf gctx (Some request) m useScope = match peelQual m
  TVar cell =>
    firstPredForEnclAt
      gctx
      GSImplRequires
      (tyvarId cell)
      request
      useScope
      (givensForScope gctx useScope)
  TApp a _ => implReqDictVarOf gctx (Some request) a useScope
  _ => None

predicateSlotKnownArgs : PredicateSlotArgs -> List Mono
predicateSlotKnownArgs PSArgsUnknown = []
predicateSlotKnownArgs (PSArgsKnown args) = args

instantiateMethodPredicateTemplate : GraphCtx ->
  MethodPredicateTemplate ->
  MethodInstantiationSubst ->
  MethodPredicateTemplate
instantiateMethodPredicateTemplate gctx template subst = MethodPredicateTemplate {
  mptInterface = template.mptInterface,
  mptArguments =
    map (instantiateMethodPredicateArgument gctx subst) template.mptArguments,
}

instantiateMethodPredicateArgument : GraphCtx ->
  MethodInstantiationSubst ->
  Option Mono ->
  Option Mono
instantiateMethodPredicateArgument gctx subst argument =
  map
    (substMono gctx subst.misTypeSubst subst.misEffectSubst subst.misAuthSubst)
    argument

methodPredicateTemplateArgs : List (Option Mono) -> Option (List Mono)
methodPredicateTemplateArgs [] = Some []
methodPredicateTemplateArgs ((Some argument) :: rest) =
  map (argument :: _) (methodPredicateTemplateArgs rest)
methodPredicateTemplateArgs (None :: _) = None

uniqueMethodTemplateGiven : GraphCtx ->
  MethodPredicateTemplate ->
  ScopeId ->
  List GivenEntry ->
  Option GivenEntry
uniqueMethodTemplateGiven gctx template useScope givens =
  let chain = Scopes.visibleChain (currentScopeStore gctx ()) useScope
  match methodTemplateGivenScan template chain givens MethodTemplateGivenNone
    MethodTemplateGivenOne given => Some given
    _ => None

methodTemplateGivenScan : MethodPredicateTemplate ->
  List Int ->
  List GivenEntry ->
  MethodTemplateGivenResult ->
  MethodTemplateGivenResult
methodTemplateGivenScan _ _ [] result = result
methodTemplateGivenScan template chain (given :: rest) result =
  let result2 =
    if givenInScope GSPredicateOnly given
      && Scopes.visibleOnChain chain (Scopes.binderScope given.geBinder)
      && methodPredicateTemplateMatchesSlot
        template
        given.geSlot then match result
      MethodTemplateGivenNone => MethodTemplateGivenOne given
      _ => MethodTemplateGivenMany
    else
      result
  match result2
    MethodTemplateGivenMany => MethodTemplateGivenMany
    _ => methodTemplateGivenScan template chain rest result2

methodPredicateTemplateMatchesSlot : MethodPredicateTemplate ->
  PredicateSlot ->
  Bool
methodPredicateTemplateMatchesSlot template slot =
  sameIfaceDecl template.mptInterface slot.psIface
    && (match slot.psArgs
      PSArgsUnknown => False
      PSArgsKnown arguments =>
        methodPredicateTemplateArgumentsMatch template.mptArguments arguments)

methodPredicateTemplateArgumentsMatch : List (Option Mono) -> List Mono -> Bool
methodPredicateTemplateArgumentsMatch [] [] = True
methodPredicateTemplateArgumentsMatch ((Some expected) :: rest) (actual :: arguments) =
  monoSameGiven expected actual
    && methodPredicateTemplateArgumentsMatch rest arguments
methodPredicateTemplateArgumentsMatch (None :: rest) (_ :: arguments) =
  methodPredicateTemplateArgumentsMatch rest arguments
methodPredicateTemplateArgumentsMatch _ _ = False

-- 🚨 #1177: A USE SITE IS RESOLVED BY ITS PREDICATE, NOT BY ITS CONSTRAINT VAR'S ID.
-- `funConstraintsRef` is the SHATTERED per-tyvar slot table, so a context naming two
-- interfaces over ONE type variable — `useIx : (Dbg a, Ix a Char) => a -> Int` —
-- registers TWO slots carrying the SAME id.  The old body asked `indexOfId (tyvarId
-- cell) ids`, whose FIRST match is slot 0 whichever predicate the site belongs to, so
-- EVERY method use in the body read slot 0: `ix` read the `Dbg` dict, its route
-- degraded to the bare head tag, and first-declared-`impl` won.  Swapping the two
-- predicates — a meaning-preserving edit — moved the answer from 116 to the correct
-- 227, on both engines, at exit 0, with `check --json` clean.
--
-- `funPredicateSlotsRef` carries the authoritative slots in order, so this lookup
-- never has to reconstruct a predicate from parallel scalar tables.
enclDictVarOf : ModuleCtx ->
  Option PredicateRequest ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option EvidenceBinderId
enclDictVarOf mctx goal m encl useScope
  | encl == "" = None
  | otherwise = match peelQual m
    TVar cell =>
      map
        (Scopes.binderAt
          (Scopes.declarationScope
            (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
            useScope))
        (enclSlotIndex mctx goal (tyvarId cell) encl)
    TApp a _ => enclDictVarOf mctx goal a encl useScope
    _ => None

-- the slot index [target]'s dict param sits at in [encl]'s own constraint slots:
-- by PREDICATE when the goal supplies one and a slot answers it, else the historical
-- first-tyvar-id match.
enclSlotIndex : ModuleCtx ->
  Option PredicateRequest ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  Option Int
enclSlotIndex mctx None target encl = indexOfId target (enclSlotIds mctx encl)
enclSlotIndex mctx (Some request) target encl =
  indexOfPred target request (enclPreds mctx encl)

enclSlotIds : ModuleCtx -> String -> List Int
enclSlotIds mctx encl =
  predicateSlotIdsAt encl mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsIdxRef.value

-- [encl]'s own constraint slots as PREDICATES, in slot order: each slot's interface
-- and the argument vector its signature recorded, paired with every bound tyvar id.
enclPreds : ModuleCtx -> String -> List PredicateSlot
enclPreds mctx encl =
  optionOr
    []
    (lookupPredicateSlots encl mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsIdxRef.value)

-- Stable one-pass predicate lookup.  Known/Known vector disagreement cannot downgrade
-- to interface-only or scalar matching.
indexOfPred : Int -> PredicateRequest -> List PredicateSlot -> Option Int
indexOfPred target request preds = indexOfPredGo 0 target request preds

indexOfPredGo : Int ->
  Int ->
  PredicateRequest ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  Option Int
indexOfPredGo _ _ _ [] = None
indexOfPredGo i target request (sp :: rest)
  | containsI target sp.psBoundIds && predicateRequestMatchesSlot request sp =
    Some i
  | otherwise = indexOfPredGo (i + 1) target request rest

-- The single request/slot routing relation.  Declaration identity is complete and
-- fail-closed.  Known vectors compare recursively at every position; interface-only
-- compatibility is available only when at least one side explicitly says Unknown.
predicateRequestMatchesSlot : PredicateRequest -> PredicateSlot -> Bool
predicateRequestMatchesSlot request slot =
  request.prIface.irName /= ""
    && slot.psIface.irName /= ""
    && sameIfaceDecl request.prIface slot.psIface
    && predicateRequestArgsMatch request.prArgs slot.psArgs

predicateRequestArgsMatch : PredicateSlotArgs -> PredicateSlotArgs -> Bool
predicateRequestArgsMatch (PSArgsKnown requestArgs) (PSArgsKnown slotArgs) =
  monoVecSameGiven requestArgs slotArgs
predicateRequestArgsMatch _ _ = True

-- #1177: the predicate a METHOD occurrence discharges — the interface [name] is
-- declared by, plus its full instantiated type-parameter vector when [fullMono] lets
-- `ifaceParamMonos` recover one.  `None` for a non-method name (a top-level
-- constrained call), which is what keeps those sites on the tyvar-keyed lookup.
--
-- The interface is read from `methodIfaceHere` (#1182), so the goal carries the
-- declaration's identity rather than `OriginUnresolved`.  This predicate's only
-- consumers are `enclSlotIndex`/`indexOfPredGo` and `implReqDictVarOf`/
-- `firstPredForEnclAt`, both of which compare `sp.iface.irName == p.iface.irName` — a
-- NAME compare that cannot see an origin — so the identity selects nothing there yet;
-- it is the precondition for re-keying those two comparators onto `sameTyConHead`.
goalPredOf : ModuleCtx -> String -> Mono -> Option PredicateRequest
goalPredOf mctx name fullMono = occurrencePredOf mctx name fullMono []

-- `goalPredOf` at an occurrence that posed its goal with [omitted]: the request
-- reads the vector `occurrenceParamMonos` builds, the one `entailInst` selects the
-- impl row on, so a typaram the declared type never mentions compares as the goal's
-- own variable rather than as the interface's rigid parameter name.
occurrencePredOf : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  Mono ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Option PredicateRequest
occurrencePredOf mctx name fullMono omitted =
  let args = match occurrenceParamMonos mctx name fullMono omitted
    Some xs => PSArgsKnown xs
    None => PSArgsUnknown
  map
    (ifr => PredicateRequest { prIface = ifr, prArgs = args })
    (methodIfaceHere mctx name)

-- the operator/unop form: the node carries one operand mono, not a method occurrence,
-- so no argument vector is recoverable (`stampOpRouteVal` says the same).  Every
-- operator interface is single-param anyway, so the interface alone is the predicate.
-- Same SLICE-1 supply as `goalPredOf` above, same table, same reasoning.
goalPredOfOp : ModuleCtx -> String -> Option PredicateRequest
goalPredOfOp mctx name =
  map
    (ifr => PredicateRequest { prIface = ifr, prArgs = PSArgsUnknown })
    (methodIfaceHere mctx name)

-- Phase 151 / Gap G: stamp each comparison/equality OPERATOR site's EBinOp route
-- ref with the resolved Eq/Ord impl key (RKey) — but ONLY when the operand type
-- grounds to a NON-primitive head tycon.  Primitive (Int/Float/String/Bool/Char)
-- and ungroundable operands stay RNone → the structural-builtin EBinOp eval path
-- (so `eq a b = a == b` on Int never recurses).  Mirrors resolveSite's concrete
-- branch (head tycon → canonical key) minus the impl-dicts: the rewritten `eq`/`lt`
-- is arg-position, so it narrows by arg tag and needs no forwarded element dict.
binopPrimitiveHead : String -> Bool
binopPrimitiveHead h = contains h ["Int", "Float", "String", "Bool", "Char"]

-- Roadmap #18a: the heads a binop lowers to a BUILTIN for, and must therefore never
-- route to a typeclass method.  For the comparison operators that is exactly the
-- scalar primitives.  For `++` (→ Semigroup's `append`) it is those PLUS `List`:
-- `++` on a String/List is lowered structurally (eval's `appendVal`; the emitter's
-- `mdk_string_append`/`mdk_list_append`), and core.mdk's own builtin impls are
-- written in terms of the operator —
--     impl Semigroup (List a) where append xs ys = xs ++ ys
--     impl Semigroup String   where append s1 s2 = s1 ++ s2
-- — so routing a List/String `++` to `append` would make those bodies call
-- themselves unboundedly.  Every OTHER head still routes, which is precisely what
-- makes a user `impl Semigroup MyRope` reachable from `a ++ b`.
--
-- The fixed-width heads (`U8`/`U16`/`U32`/`U64`/`I32`/`I64`) are builtin for the
-- COMPARISON methods only.  The tagged ones share `Int`'s word, held in
-- `0 .. 2^n - 1` or, for `I32`, sign-extended, so the signed word compare is their
-- order; a `U64` or `I64` compares its boxed payloads, unsigned or signed
-- (`stampOpRouteVal`).  They are deliberately NOT in
-- `binopPrimitiveHead`, which the unary-minus path also reads: a builtin `-x` on a
-- `U8` would be `Int` negation and leave a negative word, so `negate` routes to
-- the type's own `Num` impl instead.
binopBuiltinHead : String -> String -> Bool
binopBuiltinHead "append" tag = binopPrimitiveHead tag || tag == "List"
binopBuiltinHead method tag =
  binopPrimitiveHead tag || isFixedIntHead tag && isCompareMethod method

-- After the module is inferred, classify each recorded arithmetic operand mono and
-- stamp the supported concrete scalar tag on the node's route. Grounded-only,
-- exactly like resolveBinopSite: a still-
-- polymorphic operand (headTyconMono None) is left untouched (RNone → dict path),
-- so polymorphic-Num arithmetic keeps routing through the runtime Num dict. Never
-- overwrite a route another pass already set (a comparison op has a different
-- node/ref; an arithmetic route starts RNone).
resolveArithSites : List (Ref Route, Mono) -> Unit
resolveArithSites [] = ()
resolveArithSites ((dref, m) :: rest) =
  let _ = resolveArithSite dref m
  resolveArithSites rest

resolveArithSite : Ref Route -> Mono -> Unit
resolveArithSite dref m = match !dref
  RNone => match arithmeticTag m
    Some tag => dref := RScalar tag
    None => ()
  _ => ()

-- EBinOp and EUnOp share ONE dict-route resolution family
-- (resolveOpSites/resolveOpSite/stampOpRouteVal/opDictVarOf), selected by an `isBinop`
-- flag (Roadmap #18c collapsed the binop/unop mirror pair — unopMethodApp already
-- reused binopRouteSplit, proving the shapes unify).  The two paths differ in exactly
-- two flag-keyed places: the dict-var-of policy (opDictVarOf) and the RKey stamp
-- (stampOpRouteVal — its builtin-head guard and Ord-style innerDefaultMethod reduction).
-- #156 S3c: resolveOpSite is now a thin adapter over `entail` (EKOp kind); the inst
-- route is stampOpRouteVal, a pure Route-returning extraction of the old stampOpRoute.
resolveOpSites : SiteCtx -> Bool -> List PendingEntry -> Unit
resolveOpSites sx _ [] = ()
resolveOpSites sx isBinop ((PendingEntry method tagRef operandMono encl kind loc scope _) :: rest) =
  let sx = { sx | sxSite = loc }
  let _ = match kind
    SKOp inImpl =>
      resolveOpSite sx isBinop method tagRef operandMono inImpl encl scope
    SKPredicateOp inImpl predicate =>
      resolvePredicateOpSite
        sx
        isBinop
        method
        tagRef
        operandMono
        inImpl
        predicate
        encl
        scope
    _ => ()
  resolveOpSites sx isBinop rest

-- G4: an `==`/`<`/… INSIDE an impl body ([inImpl]) whose operand is the enclosing
-- impl's abstract `requires`-constrained tyvar routes RDict that impl's element dict
-- (`activeDictVarOf` maps the operand's surviving tyvar id → `$dict_<method>_<slot>`,
-- registered by registerImplRequires after body inference; this deferred batch sees
-- the populated table).  binopMethodApp then rewrites it to a dict-dispatched
-- `eq x y` and `usesImplDict` prepends the matching param.  Without this the abstract
-- operand never grounds to a head tycon → the route stayed RNone → the SHALLOW
-- structural builtin (`mdk_value_eq` / pointer-eq), silently mis-comparing any non-Int
-- element (List → False, nested Box → False) and crashing once the dicts were threaded.
-- The [inImpl] gate is REQUIRED for the GLOBAL activeDictVars route: activeDictVars
-- is global + uncleared, so a TOP-LEVEL comparison's operand tyvar id can collide
-- with a stale impl element-var entry → a spurious RDict (this flipped the repl's
-- String-keyed `:browse` sort).  But a legitimately-constrained TOP-LEVEL operator
-- (`f x y = x == y` under `Eq a =>`) must STILL forward the enclosing fn's own class
-- dict, exactly as the direct `eq x y` arg-stamp path does.  enclDictVarOf draws that
-- line PRECISELY: it consults `funConstraintsRef[encl]` (the enclosing fn's OWN
-- declared constraint slots, keyed by fn name) — NOT the global activeDictVars — so
-- it fires ONLY when the operand var is genuinely one of encl's constraint vars, and
-- can never pick up a stale cross-impl element-var id.  A concrete operand (no active
-- dict var / not a constraint var, grounds to Some tag) keeps the existing RKey path.
--
-- Roadmap #18a RESIDUAL — `++`/`append` does NOT take the IN-IMPL element-dict route.
-- `binopDictVarOf` sends `append` to `enclDictVarOf` even when inImpl, so an operand
-- that is an impl's abstract `requires` tyvar stays RNone (the structural builtin)
-- instead of routing the impl's threaded element dict.
--
-- WHY (measured, not assumed).  Taking that route for `append` regresses
-- `test/eval_typed_modules_fixtures/impl_requires_nonfunctor_sibling`:
--     impl Applicative (VT e) requires Semigroup e where
--       pure a = VS a
--       ap (VF e1) (VF e2) = VF (e1 ++ e2)
-- Routing `e1 ++ e2` to `$dict_ap_0` makes `usesImplDict "ap"` true for the FIRST
-- time, so `implDictPassMethods` PREPENDS an impl-`requires` dict param to `ap` —
-- which shifts `ap`'s arg-position dispatch index by one.  The VTypedImpl's recorded
-- discriminating indices are NOT re-offset to match, so the impl then tag-checks its
-- leading DICT argument instead of its receiver, rejects it, and every candidate
-- falls through → `no matching impl for dispatch`.  (Before #18a that
-- `requires Semigroup e` was effectively DEAD — nothing in the body consumed it —
-- which is why the latent hole never fired.)  Fixing it properly means re-offsetting
-- arg-dispatch indices when impl-dict params are prepended: Phase 83/84 territory,
-- across ast/typecheck/dict_pass/eval, and deliberately NOT attempted here.
--
-- What still works (all gated): a GROUND non-builtin operand (`Rope "a" ++ Rope "b"`)
-- routes RKey to the user impl — the whole point of #18a, and the fix for the `build`
-- SIGSEGV; a TOP-LEVEL declared `Semigroup a => a -> a` routes RDict through
-- `enclDictVarOf` (the enclosing fn's OWN declared constraint slot, a different and
-- already-sound dict source); and String/List stay on the structural builtin.
-- What does NOT: `++` on an impl's abstract `requires`-bound tyvar — it keeps the
-- pre-#18a builtin behaviour exactly (correct for List/String, which is every such
-- site in the tree today), so this is a residual, not a regression.
-- BINOP path (`isBinop`): `append` → enclDictVarOf even when inImpl (Roadmap #18a
-- residual, above); any other method → activeDictVarOf when inImpl, else enclDictVarOf.
-- UNOP path (not `isBinop`): ALWAYS enclDictVarOf.  Roadmap #18a/#45 landmine (same
-- shape as the `append` residual): routing `-x` through activeDictVarOf can make
-- usesImplDict true for a method for the FIRST time, prepending a dict param that
-- shifts the impl's arg-dispatch index without re-offsetting the VTypedImpl's
-- discriminating indices — dispatch then tag-checks the dict instead of the receiver.
-- So `-x` on an impl's own abstract `requires`-bound tyvar stays on the structural
-- builtin (RNone) via a top-level fn's own declared constraint slot, never
-- activeDictVarOf — a residual, not a regression (mirrors the `++` residual exactly).
opDictVarOf : ModuleCtx ->
  Option PredicateRequest ->
  Bool ->
  String ->
  Mono ->
  Bool ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option AssumAnswer
opDictVarOf mctx request True "append" m _ encl useScope =
  map LegacyScalar (enclDictVarOf mctx request m encl useScope)
opDictVarOf mctx request True _ m inImpl encl useScope
  | inImpl = map LegacyScalar (activeDictVarOf mctx.mcGraph m useScope)
  | otherwise = map LegacyScalar (enclDictVarOf mctx request m encl useScope)
opDictVarOf mctx request False _ m _ encl useScope =
  map LegacyScalar (enclDictVarOf mctx request m encl useScope)

-- #156 S3c: a thin adapter over `entail` (EKOp kind).  `entail`'s ladder IS this
-- resolver's ladder: assum = opDictVarOf → RDict; inst = stampOpRouteVal (builtin head →
-- RNone; else RKey with the element reqs PACKED in, so `snd` is empty and no separate
-- implRef exists); fallback = RNone.  Op-site route cells are minted `RNone`-seeded
-- (`mintOpSite`), and the mark pass mints each site once, so the two do-nothing arms
-- (builtin-inst, fallback) both yield RNone and the RNone guard preserves that seed.
resolveOpSite : SiteCtx ->
  Bool ->
  String ->
  Ref Route ->
  Mono ->
  Bool ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
resolveOpSite sx isBinop method tagRef operandMono inImpl encl scope =
  match fst (entail sx method operandMono encl scope (EKOp isBinop inImpl))
    RNone => ()
    route => tagRef := route

resolvePredicateOpSite : SiteCtx ->
  Bool ->
  String ->
  Ref Route ->
  Mono ->
  Bool ->
  ClassPredicate ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
resolvePredicateOpSite sx isBinop method tagRef operandMono inImpl predicate encl scope =
  match (fst
    (entail
      sx
      method
      operandMono
      encl
      scope
      (EKPredicateOp isBinop inImpl predicate)))
    RNone => ()
    route => tagRef := route

-- Native Gap C: a tuple (or other parametric-with-requires) Eq/Ord impl carries
-- element `requires` dicts (Eq a, Eq b) that the rewritten `eq`/`compare` method body
-- reads.  Stamp them into the RKey route's reqs so binopMethodApp can forward them
-- as the EMethodAt impl-dict routes — exactly as resolveArgStamp does for a direct
-- `eq`/`compare` call.  A concrete non-parametric impl (user `Eq MyType`) has no
-- requires → empty reqs → the plain direct call, behaviour unchanged.
--
-- PARAMETRIC DEFAULT CASE (now routed RKey, gap closed 2026-06-12): a comparison
-- OPERATOR (`<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=` → `lt`/`gt`/`lte`/`gte`) whose method is NOT itself
-- impl'd at this head (an Ord interface DEFAULT reducing to inner `compare`) AND the
-- head's Ord impl HAS `requires` (parametric, e.g. tuple / `List a` / `Box a`).  This
-- stamps the RKey route with the SAME element-dict reqs as the `==`/`eq` path, but
-- keyed on the INNER same-interface `compare` (the relational method has no own impl
-- at this head, so `argImplDictRoutesForEncl` keyed on it would find nothing).
-- binopMethodApp forwards them as the EMethodAt impl-dicts; emitDefaultRKey passes
-- them as leading words to `@mdk_default_<op>_<tag>`, whose emitDefaultDefine
-- eta-PREPENDS the matching dict params and threads them into the inner
-- `@mdk_impl_<tag>_compare(dict.., a, b)` call.  Previously this case BACKED OFF to
-- RNone, which the backend lowered as a raw pointer `icmp` (silently WRONG result) /
-- SIGSEGV on the by-name `lt` path.  Concrete Ord (no requires) keeps empty reqs →
-- the plain `@mdk_default_<op>_<tag>(a, b)` direct call, unchanged.
-- Flag-keyed differences between the two paths:
--   * builtin-head guard — BINOP: `binopBuiltinHead method tag` (append also treats
--     List as builtin); UNOP: `binopPrimitiveHead tag` (a ground Int/Float stays on
--     evalUnop's VInt/VFloat fast path, the unop analogue of the comparison guard).
--   * dictMethod — BINOP reduces an Ord-style interface DEFAULT to its inner
--     same-interface `compare` (innerDefaultMethod) when the head does not impl the
--     method directly; UNOP has no interface-level default to reduce through (every
--     `impl Num`, including Int/Float's own `negate a = 0 - a`, defines `negate`
--     directly), so dictMethod is just `method`.
-- #156 S3c: the PURE op-site inst route (called from entailInst's EKOp arm).  A builtin
-- head → RNone (the do-nothing case the old `if isBuiltin then ()` arm expressed; the
-- adapter's RNone guard turns it back into a no-op that preserves the ref's RNone seed).
-- Else a concrete non-builtin head → `RKey key reqs` with the element `requires` dicts
-- PACKED into the primary route's reqs (binopRouteSplit later rips them onto the
-- EMethodAt impl-dict ref).  Byte-identical to the pre-S3c stampOpRoute stamper.
stampOpRouteVal : SiteCtx ->
  Bool ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  String ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  Route
stampOpRouteVal sx isBinop encl useScope method operandMono tag =
  let isBuiltin =
    if isBinop then binopBuiltinHead method tag else binopPrimitiveHead tag
  -- #2356: a builtin head is not a dispatch, but it is not nothing either.  A
  -- comparison whose operand GROUNDS to `Int` gets the positive scalar stamp
  -- `RScalar "Int"`, the same carrier resolveArithSite uses for Float, so the
  -- native emitter can compare the two tagged words inline instead of calling the
  -- opaque @mdk_value_eq/@mdk_value_lt runtime discriminators.  The stamp is the
  -- ONLY sound witness for that: the emitter's own `LTInt` is its default for an
  -- operand whose type it could not recover, so an `icmp` keyed on LTy would
  -- compare boxed String/Float POINTERS as integers.  Every other builtin head
  -- (Float/String/Bool/Char) and every ungrounded operand stay RNone, i.e. on the
  -- runtime-discriminated path they are on today.
  if isBuiltin then
    -- a tagged fixed-width comparison is the `Int` word compare (see
    -- binopBuiltinHead); a `U64` or `I64` one compares the two boxed cells'
    -- 64-bit payloads, unsigned or signed.
    if isBinop
      && (tag == "Int" || isTaggedFixedHead tag)
      && isCompareMethod method then
      RScalar "Int"
    else if isBinop && tag == "Char" && isCompareMethod method then
      RScalar "Char"
    else if isBinop && isBoxed64Head tag && isCompareMethod method then
      RScalar tag
    else
      RNone
  else
    -- #609: no interface param vector is recoverable at an operator site (the
    -- node carries one operand mono, not a method occurrence), so the goal is the
    -- singleton — entryHeadMatches then takes its arg-0 fallback, byte-identical
    -- to the pre-#609 scan.  Every operator interface (Eq/Ord/Num) is single-param
    -- anyway, where the singleton IS the full vector.
    let (siteKey, selected) = keyForSite sx method [operandMono]
    -- ARCH B-2.1-h: graph-global, off `bodyImplEnvRef` — see `ieDefinesReqMethodAt`.
    -- The head projection is `headTyconMono operandMono`, i.e. the `HeadKey` whose
    -- `headKeyName` IS the `tag` this arm was passed (`entail` derives both from the
    -- same mono, and on the nominal heads `TCon`/`TRigid` that carry a name the two
    -- classifiers agree; they differ only on `TFun`, which `headTyconMono` keys and
    -- `headTyconNameMono` does not), so the LOOKUP is the same question at the same
    -- key strength — only the POPULATION moved.
    let dictMethod =
      if isBinop then
        if ieDefinesReqMethodAt
          sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
          method
          (headTyconMono operandMono) then
          method
        else
          innerDefaultMethod method
      else
        method
    let reqs = argImplDictRoutesForEncl
      sx
      encl
      useScope
      dictMethod
      tag
      operandMono
      [operandMono]
    -- No row: the operand's type has no instance, and the site keeps its RNone seed.
    match siteKey
      Some key =>
        RKey
          key
          reqs
          (selectedCallSupers sx method selected encl useScope [operandMono])
      None => RNone

-- Exact Num arithmetic uses the predicate selected by the producer for both the
-- implementation word and its prerequisite routes. Supported solved primitive
-- heads bypass method dispatch; a user Num impl for any other head, including
-- String/Bool/Char, is selected through the exact interface identity.
stampPredicateOpRouteVal : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  String ->
  Mono ->
  ClassPredicate ->
  Route
stampPredicateOpRouteVal sx encl useScope method operandMono predicate =
  match predicateScalarRoute method operandMono
    Some route =>
      noteNumericPredicateTrace
        sx.sxModule.mcGraph
        NPTArithmetic
        predicate
        useScope
        sx.sxSite
        None
        (Some route)
        []
      route
    None =>
      let env = sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
      let goals = predicate.predicateArguments
      match ieSelectRowByIface sx env predicate.predicateInterface goals
        Some (row@(ImplRow _ _ selectedIface _ _ _ _)) =>
          let reqs = implDictRoutesForRow sx encl useScope goals row
          let key = rowRouteKey row
          let route =
            RKey
              key
              reqs
              (selectedCallSupers sx method (Some row) encl useScope goals)
          noteNumericPredicateTrace
            sx.sxModule.mcGraph
            NPTArithmetic
            predicate
            useScope
            sx.sxSite
            (Some selectedIface)
            (Some (RKey key [] []))
            reqs
          route
        None =>
          let route = RNone
          noteNumericPredicateTrace
            sx.sxModule.mcGraph
            NPTArithmetic
            predicate
            useScope
            sx.sxSite
            None
            (Some route)
            []
          route

predicateScalarRoute : String -> Mono -> Option Route
predicateScalarRoute method operandMono = match arithmeticTag operandMono
  -- Unary Int negation already has its dedicated primitive path and the unop
  -- carrier does not publish a scalar annotation.
  Some "Int" => Some (if method == "negate" then RNone else RScalar "Int")
  Some "Float" => Some (RScalar "Float")
  -- A fixed-width head's binary arithmetic is a builtin too, stamped with its
  -- own tag so every engine wraps the result at that width. Its unary negation
  -- takes the head's `Num` impl like any other instance.
  Some scalar => if method == "negate" then None else Some (RScalar scalar)
  None => None
-- Gap #21 (CLOSED): element reqs are now forwarded unconditionally on both eval and
-- emit paths.  The impl method `eq`/`compare` carries leading `$dict_*` params
-- (resolveArgStamps runs on both paths); emitter applies them; eval's methodAtNarrow
-- forwards dict reqs (like RDictFwd) truncated to the matched impl's reqCount.

-- The inner same-interface method an interface DEFAULT reduces to, supplying the
-- element `requires` dicts.  Ord's `lt`/`gt`/`lte`/`gte`/`min`/`max` defaults all
-- reduce to `compare`; any other relational/equality method has its own impl so the
-- `ieDefinesReqMethodAt` guard keeps it on `method`, never reaching here.
innerDefaultMethod : String -> String
innerDefaultMethod m =
  if contains m ["lt", "gt", "lte", "gte", "min", "max"] then "compare" else m

-- #2356: the five comparison OPERATOR methods (`==`/`/=` -> `eq`, `<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=`
-- -> `lt`/`gt`/`lte`/`gte`).  `min`/`max` are deliberately absent: they are Ord
-- methods but no operator records a site for them, so a name-only match on them
-- would stamp nothing and claim a reach this predicate does not have.
isCompareMethod : String -> Bool
isCompareMethod m = contains m ["eq", "lt", "gt", "lte", "gte"]

-- ── coherence check (TYPECHECK-AUDIT S3) ───────────────────────────────────
-- Phase 68: reject incoherent USER
-- impl sets at declaration time.  Two impls of the SAME interface whose head
-- types can match the same concrete type (impls_overlap) are unresolvable unless
-- one strictly specializes the other (most-specific-wins).  Genuinely incoherent:
--   • two overlapping impls that are NOT a strict specialization → OverlappingImpls.
-- (Named impls + `@Name` selection + `default impl` were removed 2026-07-11; the
-- newtype-wrapper approach is the answer for a second instance.)
-- Prelude/seeded impls are excluded entirely (the driver passes USER decls only):
-- user impls are meant to override prelude impls (e.g. single-file `impl Ord Int`),
-- so they must not pair with a prelude `impl Ord Int`.  At most ONE error is
-- emitted (mirrors the oracle raising Type_error on the first conflict).

-- 🪦 RETIRED 2026-08-12 (#1559 A-3.7 bite 3.7-9): `cohImplsOf` / `cohImplsOfMid` —
-- the decl-walking adapters that built `CohImpl`s straight off `DImpl` nodes, and
-- `cohCollectImpls` / `cohCollectModuleImpls`, their two list drivers.  Coherence's
-- input is now a projection of `IE`'s rows (`cohImplOfRow`), so both sweeps read the
-- registry the rest of stage K reads instead of re-walking decls.  Zero tree-wide
-- callers at deletion time (`grep -rn 'cohCollectImpls\|cohCollectModuleImpls\|
-- cohImplsOf' --include=*.mdk .` → definitions and comments only).  The `#414` span
-- derivation they carried is preserved below, because `cohImplOfRow` still calls
-- `firstTyLocList` on the row's head and inherits every word of it.
--
-- #414: the span to blame for an impl comes from its head types, via
-- `firstTyLocList` (`frontend/ast.mdk`), which folds `firstTyLoc` — that inner
-- walk is the one shared with resolve (`dupSigOf`); resolve does not call
-- `firstTyLocList` itself (issue 480).
-- A `DImpl` has no `Loc` of its own (`DUse` is the only `Decl` variant
-- carrying one inline) — but the parser stamps every `TyCon` leaf with its span
-- (`parser.mdk`'s parseTyAtom: `tyConUnresolved c (Some (locOfSpan s q))`), so the head's
-- own tycon IS the impl's location.  Pre-order, so `impl C (Pair a Int)` blames
-- `Pair` — the head — not the argument.  An alias head's expansion is located at
-- the alias occurrence (`locateTyAt`), so `impl C LB` still blames `LB`.
--
-- ⚠️ RESIDUAL (#414): only `TyCon` leaves carry spans, so a head with NO tycon —
-- the fully-parametric `impl Foo a` — still yields `None` and falls back to the
-- file-start caret.  That is the degenerate overlap case (`test/
-- typecheck_error_fixtures/overlapping_impls.mdk`).  Closing it needs a span on
-- `TyVar` (an ast.mdk change rippling through every `Ty` consumer) or the parser's
-- `DeclPos` side-table threaded into typecheck; both are out of proportion to an
-- S3 diagnostic-quality fix.  Every head naming a CONCRETE type is covered.
--
-- #1559 A-3.7 OCCURRENCE MINT, and the retirement above is the reason it worked:
-- the deleted adapter destructured `implOrigin` in the SAME record pattern as `iface`
-- and built the `IfaceRef` from that pair on the spot, using the identical expression
-- `implDeclFact` uses to build `ImplRow`'s interface half.  Because the two
-- constructions could not drift, replacing the adapter with a projection of `IE`'s
-- rows yields the same interface half by construction rather than by assertion.
--
-- the impl's head args → monos under ONE shared fresh-var map (so a var reused
-- across args, e.g. `Conv a a`, is the SAME fresh tyvar — the oracle shares one
-- tbl across the whole impl head; distinct impls get distinct ids).
cohFreshTys : ModuleCtx -> List Ty -> List Mono
cohFreshTys mctx tys = snd (implHeadMonos mctx tys)

-- An impl head's variables under their declared kinds: a name in an
-- `Authority`-kinded slot (`impl Eq (Handle p)`) is an authority binder, as
-- in a signature; every other bare name is a type variable.  One map is
-- shared across the head's arguments, so a name reused across them is one
-- variable.
implHeadMonos : ModuleCtx -> List Ty -> (List (String, Mono), List Mono)
implHeadMonos mctx tys =
  let _ = fold (_ ty => checkImplHeadIndices mctx ty) () tys
  let auths = dedupBinders (flatMap (authArgBindersIn mctx) tys) []
  let pats = flatMap (patternSlotNamesIn mctx) tys
  let tvMap =
    freshTvMap
      mctx
      (removeAllS (map fst auths) (dedup (flatMap tyVarNames tys)))
  let etbl =
    sigVarsWithAuths
      (map (b => freshAuthBinderRanged mctx (contains (fst b) pats) b) auths)
      emptySigVars
  (tvMap, map (fromAstTypeE mctx etbl tvMap) tys)

-- An instance is chosen by its head's type constructor and the index is
-- erased, so an impl covers every index of the head: an `Authority` slot of
-- an impl head takes a name, never a written term.
checkImplHeadIndices : ModuleCtx -> Ty -> Unit
checkImplHeadIndices mctx (TyApp a b) = match tyAppSpine (TyApp a b)
  (TyCon { tyConName = n, tyConOrigin = o }, args) =>
    match lookupTab (tyTabKey o n) mctx.mcCells.dataParamKindsRef.value
      Some kinds if listLen kinds == listLen args =>
        fold
          (_ ka => match ka
            (KAuth _ _, TyAuth ps loc) =>
              pushTypeErrorOncePerSite
                mctx
                "T-AUTHORITY-KIND"
                loc
                (implHeadIndexMsg n (ppTy (TyAuth ps loc)))
            _ => ())
          ()
          (zipL kinds args)
      _ => ()
  _ => ()
checkImplHeadIndices mctx _ = ()

-- #1559 A-3.7: THE `IE`→`CohImpl` ADAPTER — coherence's input, relocated off the decl
-- walk.  Every one of the four things coherence judges on comes out of the row:
--   * the interface half is `ieRowTriple`'s `IfaceRef` — the SAME value
--     `cohImplsOfMid` built by hand from `iface`+`implOrigin`, because `implDeclFact`
--     builds it with the identical expression.  That is why this relocation is not an
--     acceptance change: `cohSameIface` (3.7-4) sees the same pair of `IfaceRef`s.
--   * the head is `cohFreshTys` of the row's `List Ty`, the same call the decl
--     adapter made.  Effectful (fresh tyvars), exactly as the decl adapter was.
--     The head is already in alias normal form (`stampGraphDecls`), so
--     coherence compares the head selection reads, and `fromAstTypeE` finds no
--     alias left on it to expand with the checked module's alias table (the
--     wrong table for another module's head).
--   * the owner module id is `instRefMid` of the row's `InstRef` — this is where
--     `InstRef` acquires its FIRST judgment reader in this tree.
--   * the blame span is `firstTyLocList` of that same head.
-- ⚠️ `ieLoc` IS NOT OWED FOR THIS.  `ImplRow`'s "no location field" note argues from
-- `Decl` carrying no `Loc`, which is true and beside the point: the row carries the
-- head's `List Ty`, and the parser stamps every `TyCon` leaf with its span, so the span
-- coherence uses today is recoverable with no new field and no `DImpl` change.
cohImplOfRow : ModuleCtx -> ImplRow -> CohImpl
cohImplOfRow mctx r = match ieRowTriple r
  (ir, tys, _) =>
    CohImpl
      ir
      (cohFreshTys mctx tys)
      (instRefMid (ieRowInst r))
      (orElseLoc (firstTyLocList tys) (ieRowLoc r))

-- The prelude is ordinal 0 on the Module arm, structurally: `buildDeclEnvs` builds
-- `declEnvModulesFrom 0 (("core", coreDecls)::modules)`, so nothing else can be.
-- Coherence compares a program's impls with the prelude's (DICT-SEMANTICS §6.1), but
-- never the prelude's with itself: the prelude is trusted and cannot be edited.
cohPreludeOrd : Int
cohPreludeOrd = 0

-- the prelude's own rows: the second population of the per-module sweep.
cohPreludeRows : ImplEnv -> List ImplRow
cohPreludeRows env = ieRowsOwnedBy cohPreludeOrd env

-- every USER module's rows, for the whole-graph sweep.  The prelude is absent here
-- because a program-vs-prelude pair is owned by the per-module sweep (which sees the
-- prelude and reports with the impl's own span); the whole-graph sweep would report
-- the same pair a second time, span-less.
cohRowsOf : ImplEnv -> List ImplRow
cohRowsOf env = filterList (r => ieRowOrd r /= cohPreludeOrd) (ieRowsAll env)

-- the per-module sweep's own population.  The prelude module itself checks nothing:
-- its rows are the second population, never the first.
cohRowsOwnedBy : Int -> ImplEnv -> List ImplRow
cohRowsOwnedBy cur env
  | cur == cohPreludeOrd = []
  | otherwise = ieRowsOwnedBy cur env

-- subsumes ~general ~specific: is [specific] an instance of [general]?  Only the
-- general side's vars bind (consistently: a var bound twice must see structurally
-- equal types); the specific side's vars are rigid (match only the same id).
cohSubsumes : List Mono -> List Mono -> Bool
cohSubsumes general specific
  | listLen general == listLen specific =
    isSome (matchOneSided cohStep eqInt cohEqMono (zipL general specific) [])
  | otherwise = False

-- Mono-space step: normalize BOTH sides (chasing links), then classify the general
-- node.  Effect rows are row-blind (TEff/TEff ⇒ MOk; TFun's row slot ignored).
cohStep : Mono -> Mono -> MStep Int Mono Mono
cohStep g0 s0 =
  let g = peelQual (normalize g0)
  let s = peelQual (normalize s0)
  match g
    TVar c => MVar (tyvarId c)
    -- #1111 A-2.10 on the `TCon`/`TCon` pairing only (`sameTyConHead`); the
    -- cross-population arms stay name-only for the reason `cohGoR` gives.
    -- ⚠️ The cross-population ones are NOT SEPARATELY PROBED — armed
    -- because the pre-split arm answered them, and because a rigid and a real
    -- head CAN both spell `__tupleN__` (see `Mono.TRigid`).  Measured instances
    -- of that forgery: `unifyN`, `matchStep` (§8 I6.2(b), OWED-#1243).
    TCon a oa => match s
      TCon b ob => if sameTyConHead a oa b ob then MOk else MFail
      TRigid b => if a == b then MOk else MFail
      _ => MFail
    TRigid a => match s
      TRigid b => if a == b then MOk else MFail
      TCon b _ => if a == b then MOk else MFail
      _ => MFail
    TApp f1 a1 => match s
      TApp f2 a2 => MKids [(f1, f2), (a1, a2)]
      _ => MFail
    TFun a1 _ b1 => match s
      TFun a2 _ b2 => MKids [(a1, a2), (b1, b2)]
      _ => MFail
    TEff _ => match s
      TEff _ => MOk
      _ => MFail
    TAuth _ => match s
      TAuth _ => MOk
      _ => MFail

eqInt : Int -> Int -> Bool
eqInt a b = a == b

-- [a] strictly more specific than [b]: b subsumes a but not a subsumes b
cohStrictlyMoreSpecific : List Mono -> List Mono -> Bool
cohStrictlyMoreSpecific a b = cohSubsumes b a && not (cohSubsumes a b)

-- [impls] are paired with each other; each is also paired with every one of [fixed]
-- (the prelude's impls), which are never paired with one another.
cohScan : CohSweep -> List CohImpl -> List CohImpl -> CohScan
cohScan sweep impls fixed = cohScanOuter sweep impls fixed (CohScan None None)

cohScanOuter : CohSweep -> List CohImpl -> List CohImpl -> CohScan -> CohScan
cohScanOuter _ [] _ acc = acc
cohScanOuter sweep (e :: rest) fixed acc
  | cohScanDone acc = acc
  | otherwise =
    cohScanOuter
      sweep
      rest
      fixed
      (cohScanInner sweep e fixed (cohScanInner sweep e rest acc))

-- both classes already witnessed ⇒ nothing later can change what is reported.
cohScanDone : CohScan -> Bool
cohScanDone (CohScan (Some _) (Some _)) = True
cohScanDone _ = False

-- #1559 A-3.7: DO TWO IMPL OCCURRENCES NAME THE SAME INTERFACE?
--
-- 🚨 `sameTyConHead`, NEVER `ifaceIdMatches`, AND THE TWO ARE EXACT INVERSES.  This
-- is the whole substance of the bite, so the derivation is here rather than in a
-- ledger:
--   * `sameTyConHead n1 o1 n2 o2 = n1 == n2 && not (tyConIdsConflict o1 o2)`
--     (`frontend/ast.mdk`) — name equality, and an ABSENT origin makes NO CLAIM, so
--     it matches anything.
--   * `ifaceIdMatches a b = a /= "" && a == b` (`frontend/ast.mdk`) — absence NEVER
--     matches, not even itself.
-- `recordCandIsType`'s header states which to use when, and the rule is about the
-- QUESTION being asked, not about the table: `sameTyConHead` belongs where a false
-- REJECT would refuse a valid program (an ACCEPTANCE question); `ifaceIdMatches`
-- belongs where a false HIT is silent wrongness (a LOOKUP).
--
-- Coherence is an ACCEPTANCE question — it decides whether to reject a program — so
-- `sameTyConHead` is correct, and it is also the FAIL-LOUD direction here: an impl
-- whose `implOrigin` is still `OriginUnresolved` compares by name exactly as it did
-- before this unit, so no live rejection can silently vanish.  `ifaceIdMatches` in
-- this position would turn every unstamped-origin conflict into a SILENT ACCEPT,
-- which is a severity INCREASE and one no fixture in the tree would catch.
--
-- ⚠️ NOT a re-keying of the HEAD half.  Coherence's head comparison already routes
-- through `sameTyConHead` (`cohGoR`'s `TCon` arm, A-2.10) and is untouched, so the
-- #1317 T1 rule and closed S0 #1277 are not in scope for this unit.
cohSameIface : IfaceRef -> IfaceRef -> Bool
cohSameIface a b = sameTyConHead a.irName a.irOrigin b.irName b.irOrigin

cohScanInner : CohSweep -> CohImpl -> List CohImpl -> CohScan -> CohScan
cohScanInner _ _ [] acc = acc
cohScanInner sweep (e1@(CohImpl if1 xs mid1 _)) ((CohImpl if2 ys mid2 _) :: rest) acc
  | cohScanDone acc = acc
  | cohSameIface if1 if2 && cohOverlap xs ys =
    cohScanInner sweep e1 rest (cohClassify sweep e1 xs ys mid1 mid2 acc)
  | otherwise = cohScanInner sweep e1 rest acc

-- classify ONE overlapping pair.  A strict specialization either way is coherent
-- (most-specific-wins ranks it) and contributes nothing.  The remaining two cases
-- are exhaustive and disjoint: `cohStrictlyMoreSpecific a b = cohSubsumes b a && not
-- (cohSubsumes a b)`, so if neither direction is strict then `cohSubsumes` holds
-- BOTH ways (mutual ⇒ HARD) or NEITHER way (incomparable ⇒ SOFT).
-- Keep-first per class mirrors the old "first conflict wins" reporting.
--
-- ⚠️ WHY THE HARD ARM CANNOT SIMPLY MOVE TO THE GOAL SITE, stated because "then fix
-- it there" is the obvious review question and the answer is not "we didn't try".
-- The root is one level up from `entryCovers`: `entryCoversAllOthers` /
-- `findMostSpecificEntry` test for a ⊑-MINIMUM, where §6 C1 requires **at most one
-- ⊑-MINIMAL element**.  In a preorder that is not antisymmetric those two coincide
-- everywhere EXCEPT at α-equal heads — precisely this arm's class.  (`entryCovers`
-- itself is fine: with `S = tySubsumesV`, `tyHeadEqV a b || S b a` is exactly ⊑;
-- it does not conflate ⊒ with =.)  Tightening `entryCoversAllOthers` to demand
-- STRICT specificity was built and measured: it finds 6 true positives and then
-- breaks `stdlib/core.mdk`, which stops typechecking with "the goal `Num Int`
-- matches `impl Num Int` and `impl Num Int`" — checking core as a user program
-- registers the same instance twice, and deduping needs INSTANCE IDENTITY this tree
-- does not have (`bucketKeyEntriesFrom` restarts its numbering at 0 per module, so
-- two distinct impls in different modules share an index).  That is L2 / A-3 / B-2
-- work.  Until it exists, the declaration site is the only place this class is
-- caught at all.
--
-- A program impl α-equal to a PRELUDE impl is this arm's class too: the per-module
-- sweep pairs each program impl with the prelude's impls (DICT-SEMANTICS §6.1), so a
-- user `impl Display String` is rejected at the program's impl.  A strictly more
-- specific program impl is coherent and wins on every engine.
cohClassify : CohSweep ->
  CohImpl ->
  List Mono ->
  List Mono ->
  String ->
  String ->
  CohScan ->
  CohScan
cohClassify sweep e1 xs ys mid1 mid2 (CohScan hard soft)
  | cohStrictlyMoreSpecific xs ys = CohScan hard soft
  | cohStrictlyMoreSpecific ys xs = CohScan hard soft
  | cohMutuallySubsumes xs ys && cohHardInScope sweep mid1 mid2 =
    CohScan
      (cohKeepFirst hard (Some (cohHardMsg e1 xs ys mid1 mid2, cohImplLoc e1)))
      soft
  -- A mutually-subsuming pair the sweep does NOT own contributes nothing at all --
  -- it must not fall through to the soft arm below, because HARD and SOFT are
  -- disjoint classes (mutual subsumption is the exact complement of
  -- ⊑-incomparability here), and reporting it as `W-INCOMPARABLE-IMPLS`
  -- would be a wrong classification, not a quieter one.
  | cohMutuallySubsumes xs ys = CohScan hard soft
  | not (cohSoftInScope sweep mid1 mid2) = CohScan hard soft
  | otherwise =
    CohScan
      hard
      (cohKeepFirst
        soft
        (Some (
          cohIncomparableMsg (cohImplIfaceName e1) xs ys mid1 mid2,
          cohImplLoc e1,
        )))

-- Which sweep OWNS a soft (⊑-incomparable) pair.  Two sweeps run over overlapping
-- inputs: `checkCoherence` over ONE module's own impls and `globalCoherenceConflict`
-- over every user module's impls (real mids).  A pair
-- whose two impls live in the SAME module is seen by BOTH — the per-module one with a
-- real span, the global one span-less (#414) — so recording it in both makes
-- `run`/`build` print it TWICE where `check` prints it once.  The global sweep's
-- unique contribution is the pair that SPANS two modules, which no per-module sweep
-- can see; that is the only soft pair it should claim.
--
-- ⚠️ Scoped to the SOFT class deliberately.  The HARD class double-reports the same
-- way, and that is PRE-EXISTING — it did so as a `T-CONFLICTING-IMPL` error before
-- F-3d, on these same two paths — so narrowing it here would be an unrelated
-- behaviour change riding this one, and one that moves error goldens.
-- 🚨 #1559 A-3.7: SWEEP-SCOPED, NOT MID-SHAPE-SCOPED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS A
-- LOUD→SILENT REGRESSION THIS FUNCTION USED TO BE ONE COMMIT AWAY FROM.
-- The body was:
--     cohSoftInScope "" ""   = True
--     cohSoftInScope m1 m2   = cohIsCrossModule m1 m2
-- i.e. it asked "are both mids empty?" as a stand-in for "am I the per-module
-- sweep?".  That proxy held only because the per-module sweep's input came from
-- `cohImplsOf`, which had no module id to stamp and so stamped `""`.  Pointing that
-- sweep at `IE` gives every row a REAL id (`instRefMid`), so an intra-module pair
-- arrives as `(m, m)` with `m /= ""` — the first arm stops matching, `cohIsCrossModule
-- m m` is `False`, and EVERY intra-module `W-INCOMPARABLE-IMPLS` silently stops being
-- reported.  Diagnostic-only, so no value golden in this tree could see it.
--
-- The sweep tag says outright what the mid shapes were being read to infer:
--   * `CohSweepOwn` — the per-module sweep.  Its input is ONE module's own rows, so
--     every pair it sees is intra-module BY CONSTRUCTION and it owns all of them.
--     Answering `True` unconditionally is exactly what the old `"" ""` arm did for
--     the only input that sweep ever had.
--   * `CohSweepGlobal` — the whole-graph sweep.  It owns only the pair that SPANS two
--     modules; the intra-module ones already belong to the sweep above.  The `"" ""`
--     arm is retained HERE (and only here) because it is behaviour-preserving for a
--     degenerate global input in which both ids are blank — a shape this function
--     answered `True` for before A-3.7, and one this bite deliberately does not
--     re-adjudicate.
cohSoftInScope : CohSweep -> String -> String -> Bool
cohSoftInScope CohSweepOwn _ _ = True
cohSoftInScope CohSweepGlobal "" "" = True
cohSoftInScope CohSweepGlobal mid1 mid2 = cohIsCrossModule mid1 mid2

-- Which sweep OWNS a HARD (mutually-subsuming) pair.  #1449 / F8: the SAME rule as
-- `cohSoftInScope`, and it is a delegation rather than a copy so the two classes can
-- never drift apart silently.
--
-- 🚨 THIS IS THE NARROWING `cohSoftInScope`'s header DECLINED TO MAKE, now made
-- deliberately.  That header said, of the hard class: "The HARD class double-reports
-- the same way, and that is PRE-EXISTING … so narrowing it here would be an unrelated
-- behaviour change riding this one, and one that moves error goldens."  It is no
-- longer unrelated: the double report IS #1449's shape, and it is user-visible on the
-- most ordinary program there is.  Measured before this change, on a single file with
-- two `impl Foo Int`, `medaka check --json` emitted the identical
-- `T-CONFLICTING-IMPL` message TWICE — once with the declaration's real span (from the
-- per-module sweep, `checkCoherence` / `CohSweepOwn`) and once span-less (from this
-- whole-graph sweep, prepended by `attachCoherenceConflict`, which `driveGraphK` and
-- the keyed arm of `checkModulesDiagsChain` both call.  An IMPORT-BEARING two-module
-- program whose overlap is entry-module-local double-reports identically, so the
-- double report is not specific to one module.  Per-module sweep and whole-graph
-- sweep each report the pair: one with the declaration span, one without it.
--
