-- PARAMETER to a STATICALLY SELECTED impl — the wrong value, at exit 0, with no
-- diagnostic.  A selector call sitting on an `assum` or `fallback` arm is precisely how
-- that happens, which is why this is a placement rule and not a tidiness point.
--
-- 🚨 IT IS A REACHABILITY PROPERTY, NOT A COUNT — AND THE COUNT FORM IS FALSE ON A
-- CORRECT TREE.  There are legitimately TWO selector calls per `inst` arm: one for the
-- primary route word, one inside the element-route helper.  At `EKArg` and `EKOp` those
-- two deliberately ask about DIFFERENT methods — the element helper is keyed on the
-- `innerDefaultMethod`-reduced name when the head's impl does not itself define the
-- method (`ieDefinesReqMethodAt`).  Any *"one selector call per arm"* rule would license
-- collapsing them, which changes WHICH IMPL'S CONTEXT IS DISCHARGED (§6 C2).  Do not
-- restate this property in the count form.
--
-- ⚠️ AND A GREP OF `ieSelectRowBy*` IS NOT THE CHECK.  `concreteReqMatchByIface` is a
-- LEGITIMATE selector call outside this ladder — it is the obligation channel's evidence
-- check, not a routing decision — and is out of scope here.  An audit that greps the
-- selector names without excluding it reports a false violation.
-- 🚨 THE `inst` ARM PROJECTS THROUGH `headTyconMono`, THE DISPATCH-KEY PROJECTION,
-- NOT THROUGH THE `headTyconNameMono` RESIDUAL IT READ UNTIL #1617.  This is the
-- SAME repoint A-2.2b made at `goalHeadCon` and the three `implExistsForHead`
-- receiver sites, arriving one site late: `entail` is a ROUTING decision (its
-- result is stamped straight into a site's route ref by `resolveArgStamp`), so it
-- owes the goal-side dispatch key, and the name-only residual can no longer
-- express that argument now that the two answer differently at `TFun`.
--
-- MEASURED, this line alone is what kept #1617 open after both head projections
-- and both definition-side tags already agreed on `__fun__`: an arg-position
-- occurrence (`sz : a -> Int` dispatches on its ARGUMENT, so it is stamped here
-- and not by `resolveSites`) took the `None => entailFallback` arm, left the site
-- `RNone`, and the emitter arg-tag-dispatched over a closure.  The typed Core-IR
-- dump showed `CMethod "sz" RNone` beside two correctly-tagged
-- `CImplTagged "__fun__"` entries — impl side fixed, goal side fixed, route still
-- unstamped.
--
-- ⚠️ The name is projected INSIDE the arm, not with `map headKeyName` over the
-- `Option` — same reason `headTyconNameTy`/`headTyconNameMono` exist at all
-- (`compiler/AGENTS.md`): Medaka is strict, so the combinator spelling would
-- allocate a second `Option` on every entailment to throw it away.
entail : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  EntailKind ->
  (Route, List Route)
entail sx name m encl useScope kind =
  match entailAssum sx.sxModule m encl name useScope kind
    Some answer =>
      let _ = noteAssumption sx.sxModule.mcGraph useScope answer
      let result = (
        assumAnswerRoute sx.sxModule.mcGraph answer (goalIfaceOfKind
          sx.sxModule
          name
          kind) useScope (dname =>
          entailAssumRoute dname kind),
        [],
      )
      let _ =
        noteNumericEntailment sx kind useScope None (fst result) (snd result)
      result
    None => match headTyconMono m
      Some hk => entailInst sx name m encl useScope (headKeyTag hk) kind
      None => match entailRigidLead sx m encl useScope kind
        Some result => result
        None => match entailDetermined sx name encl useScope kind
          Some result => result
          None =>
            let result = (entailFallback sx encl useScope m kind, [])
            let _ =
              noteNumericEntailment
                sx
                kind
                useScope
                None
                (fst result)
                (snd result)
            result

-- An argument-position occurrence whose goal a boundary determined by its one
-- unifying instance (DICT-SEMANTICS §3 "Determination by the one unifying
-- instance") dispatches through that instance, though its lead position is still
-- a variable that selection by head cannot read.
entailDetermined : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  EntailKind ->
  Option (Route, List Route)
entailDetermined sx name encl useScope (EKArg fullMono omitted) = match (
  occurrenceParamMonos sx.sxModule name fullMono omitted,
  methodIfaceHere sx.sxModule name,
)
  (Some goals, Some iface) =>
    map
      (row => (
        RKey
          (rowRouteKey row)
          []
          (selectedCallSupers sx name (Some row) encl useScope goals),
        implDictRoutesForRow sx encl useScope goals row,
      ))
      (determinedGoalInstance sx.sxModule iface goals)
  _ => None
entailDetermined sx _ _ _ _ = None

-- `inst` for a nested/top goal whose lead position is a variable, when every variable
-- of the vector is one a closed binder declared (DICT-SEMANTICS §6.1 points 2-3, §3
-- W3-inst).  Such a goal is closed: its variables are rigid in the matcher, so an
-- instance reduces it when some position is constructed, and it selects min⊑ of the
-- matches.  A goal over variables alone is its own residual and is not reduced.  Only
-- an instance whose first head position is a variable can match a variable lead, so
-- the headless bucket is the whole candidate set.  The rung lives here rather than in
-- `ieSelectRowByIface`'s headless arm because rigidity is a property of the goal's
-- scope, which that selector's other callers do not share.
entailRigidLead : SiteCtx ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  EntailKind ->
  Option (Route, List Route)
entailRigidLead sx m encl useScope (EKNestedTop iface _ walk rest) =
  let goals = m :: rest
  let ids = flatMap monoUnboundIds goals
  let declared = sx.sxModule.mcCells.declaredSigVarIds.value
  if isEmptyL ids
    || anyList (i => not (omHasKey (intToString i) declared)) ids
    || allList isBareTyvarMono goals then
    None
  else
    let env = sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
    let picked =
      pickMostSpecificEntry
        sx
        goals
        (ieEntriesForIface (ieHeadRows None env) iface goals)
    map
      (row => (nestedRowRoute sx encl useScope m goals walk row, []))
      (ieRowOfEntry env picked)
entailRigidLead sx _ _ _ _ = None

noteNumericEntailment : SiteCtx ->
  EntailKind ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option IfaceRef ->
  Route ->
  List Route ->
  Unit
noteNumericEntailment sx (EKNumReturn predicate _ _ origin) scope selected route prereqs =
  noteNumericPredicateTrace
    sx.sxModule.mcGraph
    NPTReturn
    predicate
    scope
    origin
    selected
    (Some route)
    prereqs
noteNumericEntailment sx (EKPredicateOp _ _ predicate) scope selected route prereqs =
  noteNumericPredicateTrace
    sx.sxModule.mcGraph
    NPTArithmetic
    predicate
    scope
    sx.sxSite
    selected
    (Some route)
    prereqs
noteNumericEntailment sx _ _ _ _ _ = ()

-- #412: `assum`, both halves.  DICT-SEMANTICS §3 pins the precedence — `assum`/`super`
-- takes precedence over `inst`; a predicate already in scope is USED, and `inst` fires only
-- when no assumption matches (GHC's rule) — which is what makes :160's "sub-evidence is
-- never pre-baked at the instance declaration" realisable.  The tyvar-keyed registry runs
-- first and unchanged; the predicate-keyed one (registerPredGiven) then answers the
-- STRUCTURED given (`requires S (List a)`) that `activeDictVarOf` structurally cannot see,
-- because it recurses to the spine head and a structured subject has a TCon there.
-- Strictly additive: every goal the tyvar path already answers routes exactly as before.
entailAssum : ModuleCtx ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  EntailKind ->
  Option AssumAnswer
entailAssum mctx m encl name useScope kind =
  let request = goalRequestOfKind mctx name kind
  match entailAssumVar mctx request m encl name useScope kind
    Some answer => Some answer
    None => match request
      Some req => activeDictPredOf mctx.mcGraph req m useScope
      None => None

goalRequestOfKind : ModuleCtx -> String -> EntailKind -> Option PredicateRequest
goalRequestOfKind mctx name (EKReturn fullMono _) =
  goalPredOf mctx name fullMono
goalRequestOfKind mctx _ (EKNumReturn predicate _ _ _) = Some PredicateRequest {
  prIface = predicate.predicateInterface,
  prArgs = PSArgsKnown predicate.predicateArguments,
}
goalRequestOfKind mctx name (EKArg fullMono omitted) =
  occurrencePredOf mctx name fullMono omitted
goalRequestOfKind mctx name (EKOp _ _) = goalPredOfOp mctx name
goalRequestOfKind mctx _ (EKPredicateOp _ _ predicate) = Some PredicateRequest {
  prIface = predicate.predicateInterface,
  prArgs = PSArgsKnown predicate.predicateArguments,
}
goalRequestOfKind mctx _ (EKNestedTop _ _ _ _) = None

-- assum: which in-scope dict-param (if any) does [m]'s head constraint var read?  The
-- genuine/arg kinds prefer the enclosing method's own slot (activeDictVarOfEncl); the
-- nested/top kind uses the plain encl-aware lookup (activeDictVarForEncl); the op kind
-- routes through opDictVarOf (isBinop/inImpl-keyed, needs the method [name]).  [name] is
-- ignored by the non-op kinds.
entailAssumVar : ModuleCtx ->
  Option PredicateRequest ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  EntailKind ->
  Option AssumAnswer
-- #1177: the genuine/arg kinds now hand `activeDictVarOfEncl` the site's PREDICATE —
-- [name]'s interface plus the vector `ifaceParamMonos` recovers from the kind's own
-- full occurrence mono, the SAME vector `entailInst` selects the impl row on — so the
-- slot the body reads and the impl the site dispatches to answer one question.  The
-- nested/top kind keeps `activeDictVarForEncl` (no predicate: [name] there is a
-- constrained FUNCTION, not a method occurrence).
entailAssumVar mctx request m encl _ useScope (EKReturn _ _) =
  activeDictVarOfEncl mctx request m encl useScope
entailAssumVar mctx request m encl _ useScope (EKNumReturn _ _ _ _) =
  activeDictVarOfEncl mctx request m encl useScope
entailAssumVar mctx _ m encl _ useScope (EKNestedTop iface _ _ rest) =
  let request =
    PredicateRequest { prIface = iface, prArgs = PSArgsKnown (m :: rest) }
  match activeFunDictPredOf mctx.mcGraph request useScope
    Some answer => Some answer
    -- #1318 residual: EKNestedTop can still carry OriginUnresolved (#1507).  Preserve
    -- its pre-migration spelling fallback until that producer has declaration identity.
    None =>
      match (activeFunDictPredOfResidual
        mctx.mcGraph
        iface.irName
        (m :: rest)
        useScope)
        Some answer => Some answer
        -- An impl's `requires` givens are id-witnessed, so the predicate-only rungs above
        -- cannot see them; this rung matches them by predicate, as a method occurrence's
        -- does (#1154).  The tyvar-keyed registry that follows holds one entry per
        -- `requires` predicate on the variable, so it answers with the first binder
        -- whose interface is the goal's or reaches it through superclasses.
        None => match implReqDictVarOf mctx.mcGraph (Some request) m useScope
          Some answer => Some answer
          None =>
            map
              LegacyScalar
              (activeDictVarAnswering mctx.mcGraph m useScope (b =>
                scalarGivenAnswers mctx.mcGraph b iface useScope))
entailAssumVar mctx request m encl _ useScope (EKArg _ _) =
  activeDictVarOfEncl mctx request m encl useScope
entailAssumVar mctx request m encl name useScope (EKOp isBinop inImpl) =
  -- #1318: the in-impl non-append operator arm in opDictVarOf retains its scalar
  -- bypass pending a parameter-offset contract fix.
  opDictVarOf mctx request isBinop name m inImpl encl useScope
entailAssumVar mctx request m encl _ useScope (EKPredicateOp _ _ _) =
  activeDictVarOfEncl mctx request m encl useScope

-- The interface of the predicate a goal of [kind] discharges, when the kind knows it.
goalIfaceOfKind : ModuleCtx -> String -> EntailKind -> Option IfaceRef
goalIfaceOfKind mctx _ (EKNestedTop iface _ _ _) =
  if iface.irName == "" then None else Some iface
goalIfaceOfKind mctx _ (EKNumReturn predicate _ _ _) =
  Some predicate.predicateInterface
goalIfaceOfKind mctx _ (EKPredicateOp _ _ predicate) =
  Some predicate.predicateInterface
goalIfaceOfKind mctx name _ = methodIfaceHere mctx name

entailAssumRoute : String -> EntailKind -> Route
entailAssumRoute dname (EKReturn _ isRp) =
  if isRp then RDictFwd dname else RDict dname
entailAssumRoute dname (EKNumReturn _ _ isRp _) =
  if isRp then RDictFwd dname else RDict dname
entailAssumRoute dname (EKNestedTop _ _ _ _) = RDict dname
entailAssumRoute dname (EKArg _ _) = RDict dname
entailAssumRoute dname (EKOp _ _) = RDict dname
entailAssumRoute dname (EKPredicateOp _ _ _) = RDict dname

selectReturnRow : SiteCtx -> ImplEnv -> String -> List Mono -> Option ImplRow
selectReturnRow sx env name goals = match ieSelectRowByMethod sx env name goals
  Some row => Some row
  None => match methodIfaceHere sx.sxModule name
    Some iface => determinedGoalInstance sx.sxModule iface goals
    None => None

-- The instance a boundary's determination committed [iface]'s goal [goals] to
-- (`fileDeterminedRow`).  Selection by head constructor names nothing for a goal
-- whose first position is still a variable, such as one committed to a headless
-- instance; the commit is that goal's evidence.  The route reads the boundary's
-- decision rather than deciding again.
determinedGoalInstance : ModuleCtx -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Option ImplRow
determinedGoalInstance mctx _ [] = None
determinedGoalInstance mctx iface (first :: rest) = match normalize first
  TVar cell =>
    let goals = first :: rest
    let filed =
      optionOr
        []
        (IdMap.get (tyvarId cell) mctx.mcCells.determinedRowsRef.value)
    match filterList (entry => determinedEntryAnswers iface goals entry) filed
      (row, _) :: _ => Some row
      [] => None
  _ => None

-- inst: a concrete head [tag].  EKReturn → canonical full-type key + split element routes
-- (implRef-bound); EKNestedTop → the min⊑ winner's canonical key with requires PACKED
-- into the primary RKey (RNone when no row answers the vector);
-- EKArg → same canonical RKey primary as EKReturn but element routes keyed on the
-- (default-reduced) method via argImplDictRoutesForEncl; EKOp → stampOpRouteVal (builtin
-- head → RNone do-nothing, else RKey with reqs packed in, no separate element routes).
entailInst : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  String ->
  EntailKind ->
  (Route, List Route)
-- The exact arm selects on the interface's full instantiated parameter vector and
-- uses that same row and vector for both the route word and prerequisites.  A method
-- with no registered vector retains the legacy scalar result-head match.
entailInst sx name m encl useScope tag (EKReturn fullMono _) =
  let env = sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
  match ifaceParamMonos sx.sxModule name fullMono
    Some goals => match selectReturnRow sx env name goals
      Some row =>
        let routeKey = rowRouteKey row
        let routes = implDictRoutesForRow sx encl useScope goals row
        (
          RKey
            routeKey
            []
            (selectedCallSupers sx name (Some row) encl useScope goals),
          routes,
        )
      -- No row: the goal has no instance, and the site keeps no route.
      None => (RNone, [])
    -- A method without predicate-vector metadata retains the scalar result-head
    -- selection and substitution used by the compatibility path.
    None => match ieSelectRowByMethod sx env name [m]
      Some row =>
        let routeKey = rowRouteKey row
        let routes = legacyReturnReqRoutesForRow sx encl useScope m row
        (
          RKey
            routeKey
            []
            (selectedCallSupers sx name (Some row) encl useScope [m]),
          routes,
        )
      -- No vector and no row: the site keeps no route.  An occurrence of a spelling
      -- with two or more admitted declarations never reaches here: its route is
      -- `resolveAdmittedSite`'s, and its verdict `checkAdmittedOccObl`'s.
      None => (RNone, [])
entailInst sx name m encl useScope _ (kind@(EKNumReturn predicate _ _ _)) =
  let goals = predicate.predicateArguments
  let env = sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
  match ieSelectRowByIface sx env predicate.predicateInterface goals
    Some (row@(ImplRow _ _ selectedIface _ _ _ _)) =>
      let sups = selectedCallSupers sx name (Some row) encl useScope goals
      let route = RKey (rowRouteKey row) [] sups
      let routes = implDictRoutesForRow sx encl useScope goals row
      let _ =
        noteNumericEntailment sx kind useScope (Some selectedIface) route routes
      (route, routes)
    None =>
      let _ = noteNumericEntailment sx kind useScope None RNone []
      (RNone, [])
-- The primary route is the canonical key of the MOST-SPECIFIC impl (iface-keyed),
-- and every nested-`requires`/super-projection goal funnels through here, with
-- the packed requires coming from that same winner.
--
-- A nested/top `requires` goal is a PREDICATE: its goal is the predicate's whole
-- argument vector (§3 `match(IE, C τ̄)`), not its subject mono. [rest] is `[]` at
-- every caller with no goal vector, so those sites are unchanged.
--
-- The top-level `=>`-constrained-call leg also threads its own goal vector through
-- this arm, carrying the vector recorded at SIGNATURE REGISTRATION
-- (funConstraintArgsRef). Recording it beside `funConstraintsRef`, not inside it,
-- keeps per-tyvar dict slots — and hence emitted dict arity — exactly as they were.
-- #607 punch-list item 3 (dict slot = predicate, which would move arity) stays open.
entailInst sx _ m encl useScope _ (EKNestedTop iface _ walk rest) =
  -- Select the row once and hand that same value to both the route-word and
  -- prerequisite projections.  This makes §6 C2 structural: the dictionary names
  -- the same impl whose context it discharges.
  let goals = m :: rest
  let env = sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
  match ieSelectRowByIface sx env iface goals
    Some row => (nestedRowRoute sx encl useScope m goals walk row, [])
    -- No instance answers the vector (a call of `f : K x y => x -> String` leaves
    -- the constraint-only `y` undetermined): the dictionary keeps no route, and the
    -- evidence judgment rejects the call (`compiler/types/evidence_complete.mdk`).
    None => (RNone, [])
-- #609: select on the interface's FULL param vector (§5 — the dispatch type is the
-- instantiated vector `T̄`), not on the discriminating ARGUMENT's mono alone.
-- [goals] is bound ONCE and fed to BOTH arms: the method route (`routeKey`) and the
-- selected impl's own `requires`-context routes.  That is not a tidiness point — §6
-- C2 requires the impl dispatched to and the impl whose context is discharged to be
-- the SAME impl, and the first cut of this fix computed the vector here and then
-- handed the scalar `m` to argImplDictRoutesForEncl, so the two arms could select
-- differently at n≥2.  Sharing one binding makes them agree by construction.
entailInst sx name m encl useScope tag (EKArg fullMono omitted) =
  let goals =
    optionOr [m] (occurrenceParamMonos sx.sxModule name fullMono omitted)
  let (siteKey, selected) = keyForSite sx name goals
  -- ARCH B-2.1-h: graph-global, off `bodyImplEnvRef` — see `ieDefinesReqMethodAt`,
  -- which carries the measured repro.  The head is `headTyconMono m`, the `HeadKey`
  -- whose name IS this arm's `tag` (`entail` derives `tag` from the same `m` via
  -- `headTyconNameMono`), NOT `goalHeadCon goals` — this guard has always asked about
  -- the DISCRIMINATING mono's head, and re-aiming it at the vector's head would be a
  -- second, unrelated semantic change at n>=2.
  let dictName =
    if ieDefinesReqMethodAt
      sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
      name
      (headTyconMono m) then
      name
    else
      innerDefaultMethod name
  -- The selected impl's head is matched against the interface's first parameter,
  -- not the discriminating argument: `shL : List a -> …` dispatches on a `List a`
  -- argument, and at `a = List Int` matching `impl Sh (List b)` against that argument
  -- would bind `b` to `List Int` where the instance's `b` is `Int`.
  let subject = match goals
    g :: _ => g
    [] => m
  -- No instance answers the vector: the site keeps no route word, and its
  -- obligation is the verdict.  A standalone occurrence that reaches here is
  -- restamped `RLocal` (`resolveRLocalSites`).
  let word = match siteKey
    Some routeKey =>
      RKey routeKey [] (selectedCallSupers sx name selected encl useScope goals)
    None => RNone
  (word, argImplDictRoutesForEncl sx encl useScope dictName tag subject goals)
entailInst sx name m encl useScope tag (EKOp isBinop _) =
  (stampOpRouteVal sx isBinop encl useScope name m tag, [])
entailInst sx name m encl useScope _ (EKPredicateOp _ _ predicate) =
  (stampPredicateOpRouteVal sx encl useScope name m predicate, [])

-- A dictionary's super segment at the goal vector [goals]: one route per DIRECT
-- super of [iface], in declaration order, each solved at that same goal by the whole
-- ladder (DICT-SEMANTICS §2: supers are resolved per construction goal, `assum`
-- before `inst`).  [walk] is the walk that reached [goals], before [goals] itself was
-- entered: a super goal is entered beside it, not below it, and the declared super graph
-- is acyclic (W1), so it cannot recur on its own.
superRoutesAt : SiteCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List Mono ->
  ReqWalk ->
  List Route
superRoutesAt sx iface encl useScope goals walk =
  map
    (superRouteAt sx encl useScope walk)
    (directSuperGoals sx.sxModule.mcGraph iface goals)

superRouteAt : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  ReqWalk ->
  (IfaceRef, Option (List Mono)) ->
  Route
superRouteAt sx encl useScope walk (superIface, superArgs) = match superArgs
  Some (g0 :: gs) =>
    noteInnerRoute
      sx
      (routeOfD sx superIface encl useScope CommitSuper g0 gs walk)
  _ => noteInnerRoute sx RNone

-- The dictionary of a goal's selected instance [row]: the row's word, its `requires`
-- answered at [goals], and its own supers.  The word and the context are projections
-- of one row, so the dictionary names the impl whose context it discharges (§6 C2).
nestedRowRoute : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Mono ->
  List Mono ->
  ReqWalk ->
  ImplRow ->
  Route
nestedRowRoute sx encl useScope m goals walk (row@(ImplRow _ _ selectedIface _ _ _ _)) =
  RKey
    (rowRouteKey row)
    (argImplRequiresRoutesForRow sx encl useScope m goals walk row)
    (superRoutesAt sx selectedIface encl useScope goals walk)

-- A super goal no dictionary in scope answers and no head constructor selects for: a
-- goal over variables alone.  It is built from the instance the checker's super
-- judgment selected for it (`superGoalEntered`, `residualSelectionStable`), never
-- re-selected at the value: a variable a binder declared is rigid, so the instance is
-- the min⊑ of those matching the goal (DICT-SEMANTICS §6.1.3); a variable the binder
-- generalized reaches it here only when that selection is stable.
committedSuperRoute : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  IfaceRef ->
  ReqWalk ->
  List Mono ->
  Route
committedSuperRoute sx _ _ _ _ [] = RNone
committedSuperRoute sx encl useScope iface walk (goals@(m :: _)) =
  match stableGoalReach sx.sxModule [] iface goals
    ReachOne row if rowHeadMatches sx.sxModule goals row =>
      nestedRowRoute sx encl useScope m goals walk row
    _ => RNone

-- The super segment of a method-call primary `RKey`.  A call whose selected instance
-- supplies [name] only selects it, so the route carries none; a call whose instance
-- inherits [name]'s default hands that default the instance's dictionary itself (the
-- default's receiver), so the route carries the dictionary's supers, solved at the
-- goal like any dictionary's.
selectedCallSupers : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  Option ImplRow ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List Mono ->
  List Route
selectedCallSupers sx name (Some (ImplRow _ _ iface _ _ supplied _)) encl useScope goals =
  if contains name supplied then
    []
  else
    superRoutesAt sx iface encl useScope goals (reqWalkStart ())
selectedCallSupers sx _ None _ _ _ = []

entailFallback : SiteCtx -> String -> ScopeId -> Mono -> EntailKind -> Route
entailFallback sx _ _ _ (EKReturn _ _) = RNone
entailFallback sx _ _ _ (EKNumReturn _ _ _ _) = RNone
entailFallback sx encl scope m (EKNestedTop iface policy walk rest) =
  undeterminedRoute sx encl scope iface policy walk (m :: rest)
entailFallback sx _ _ _ (EKArg _ _) = RNone
entailFallback sx _ _ _ (EKOp _ _) = RNone
entailFallback sx _ _ _ (EKPredicateOp _ _ _) = RNone

-- ONE constrained-call-arg route resolver — collapses routeOfMono (encl="",
-- KeepNone) / routeOfMonoEncl (KeepNone) / routeOfMonoTop (encl="", CountImpls).
-- Only a non-empty [encl] can supply an active dict, and only from that owner's
-- constraint-var slots.  [policy] decides the undetermined arm (see Undetermined).
routeOf : SiteCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Undetermined ->
  Mono ->
  Route
routeOf sx iface encl useScope policy m =
  routeOfD sx iface encl useScope policy m [] (reqWalkStart ())

-- #217: the walk-carrying core of routeOf.  [walk] threads the shared `requires`
-- measure through the aware recursion (routeOfD → argImplRequiresRoutesForRow →
-- argImplReqRoutes → argReqRoute → routeOfD); the goal is entered in
-- argImplRequiresRoutesForRow, once per impl level.
-- #1154 (F-3a): [rest] carries the predicate's goal args past arg 0 (see EKNestedTop).
routeOfD : SiteCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Undetermined ->
  Mono ->
  List Mono ->
  ReqWalk ->
  Route
-- #156 S3b: a thin adapter over `entail` (EKNestedTop kind).  The nested/top ladder
-- packs its `requires` into the primary RKey, so `snd` is empty and only `fst` is read —
-- byte-identical to the pre-S3b arm-by-arm body.  The requires recursion still lands back
-- here via argImplRequiresRoutesForRow → argImplReqRoutes → argReqRoute → routeOfD, with the
-- walk threaded through the EKNestedTop payload.
routeOfD sx iface encl useScope policy m rest walk =
  fst (entail sx "" m encl useScope (EKNestedTop iface policy walk rest))

undeterminedRoute : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  IfaceRef ->
  Undetermined ->
  ReqWalk ->
  List Mono ->
  Route
undeterminedRoute sx _ _ _ KeepNone _ _ = RNone
undeterminedRoute sx _ scope _ (CountImpls iface) _ goal =
  routeUndeterminedTop sx scope iface goal
undeterminedRoute sx encl scope iface CommitSuper walk goal =
  committedSuperRoute sx encl scope iface walk goal

-- TOP-LEVEL constraint routes (a constrained-fn CALL site, e.g. `roundtrip 10`).
-- Like routesOfMonos but passes the CountImpls policy to routeOf, so the UNDETERMINED
-- case resolves via routeUndeterminedTop instead of the nested-recursion RNone (which
-- yields an empty dict → runtime `intToString: not an Int` / a null build dict): the
-- instances the slot's goal can still reach decide it:
--   • one, or a stable minimum → stamp that instance's RKey (deterministic
--                    dispatch on both run and build);
--   • two or more otherwise → genuinely ambiguous → `T-AMBIGUOUS-INSTANCE`, unless a
--                    scheme quantifies the goal (no route; the boundary verdict reports it);
--   • none         → keep RNone (existing no-impl behaviour/error).
-- #1161 (F-3a-ii): the vector-aware form.  Slot COUNT, slot ORDER and the number of
-- Routes produced are IDENTICAL to routesOfMonosTop's — the ONLY difference is the
-- GOAL each slot is selected with.  That is what keeps the change arity-neutral:
-- dictArityOf, dictPass, scopePredicateSlots, and the cross-module snapshot all read
-- the same predicate carrier, whose slot count this leaves untouched.
--
-- #1909 REWRITES THE INVARIANT THIS HEADER USED TO STATE.  It read: the widening is
-- "GATED ON `listLen v > 1` (topRouteV's two-cons pattern), so a 1-ary `=>` constraint —
-- which is every `=>` constraint in compiler + stdlib + sqlite — takes the SAME `routeOf`
-- call routesOfMonosTop makes, term for term.  The 1-ary path is therefore byte-identical
-- BY CONSTRUCTION."  That was the #1161 (F-3a-ii) gate, and #1909 is the case its own
-- closing caveat predicted: byte-identity held for the compiler's bare-tyvar constraints
-- and never held for a STRUCTURED single-subject one.
--
-- THE CORRECTED INVARIANT.  There is no length gate; `vectorGoal` declines only an EMPTY
-- vector or an unknown interface.  Byte-identity with routesOfMonosTop is now a property
-- of the VECTOR'S CONTENT, not of its length:
--   • vector `[m]` where the recorded argument IS the slot's own mono (every bare-tyvar
--     `=>` constraint — which is still every `=>` constraint in compiler + stdlib +
--     sqlite): `routeOfD … g0 [] 0 0` with `g0 == m` is `routeOf … m` term for term, so
--     those callers are byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION exactly as before;
--   • vector `[Wrap a]` against slot mono `a` (a structured single-subject predicate):
--     routes on `Wrap a`, which is the whole point — see `vectorGoal`;
--   • no vector at all: the `[]` arm below, still the untouched scalar router.
-- Slot COUNT, slot ORDER and the number of Routes produced are unchanged either way,
-- which is what still keeps this arity-neutral.  The self-compile fixpoint proves
-- absence-of-regression, never correctness of the new path — as before.
routesOfMonosTopV : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List Mono ->
  List IfaceRef ->
  List (List Mono) ->
  List Route
-- no vectors at all (a caller with nothing to offer) ⇒ the scalar router, unchanged.
routesOfMonosTopV sx encl useScope monos ifaces [] =
  routesOfMonosTop sx encl useScope monos ifaces
routesOfMonosTopV sx _ _ [] _ _ = []
routesOfMonosTopV sx encl useScope (m :: rest) [] (_ :: vs) =
  routeOf sx ifaceRefNone encl useScope (CountImpls ifaceRefNone) m
    :: routesOfMonosTopV sx encl useScope rest [] vs
routesOfMonosTopV sx encl useScope (m :: rest) (iface :: ifacesRest) (v :: vs) =
  topRouteV sx encl useScope iface m v
    :: routesOfMonosTopV sx encl useScope rest ifacesRest vs

-- one slot.  A multi-argument predicate hands `routeOfD` the goal TAIL (arg 0 stays in
-- `routeOfD`'s own `m`, exactly as EKNestedTop documents), so the selector sees
-- `Ix Int Char` instead of the shattered `Ix Int _` and `ieEntriesForIface`
-- returns a singleton.
-- ⚠️ The vector's arg 0 — NOT this slot's own mono — is the predicate head.  The two
-- differ whenever a predicate shatters into more than one slot (`Ix a b` gives the `b`
-- slot the mono of `b`, while the predicate's arg 0 is `a`'s): both slots are evidence
-- for the SAME predicate, so both must select on the same goal.  That is what
-- `vectorGoal` returning the head separately encodes; the scalar arm keeps [m].
topRouteV : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  IfaceRef ->
  Mono ->
  List Mono ->
  Route
topRouteV sx encl useScope iface m goals = match vectorGoal iface goals
  Some (g0, gs) =>
    routeOfD sx iface encl useScope (CountImpls iface) g0 gs (reqWalkStart ())
  None => routeOf sx iface encl useScope (CountImpls iface) m

-- `Some (arg0, tail)` exactly when the widening applies: a NON-EMPTY argument vector
-- under a KNOWN interface.  Everything else is None ⇒ the scalar route.
-- #1909: the length-1 declining clause (`vectorGoal _ [_] = None`) is GONE.  It made a
-- 1-ary predicate select on the SLOT's mono instead of on the vector's own argument —
-- byte-identical while the two coincide (`Shw a => …` records `[a]`, so arg 0 IS the
-- slot mono) and WRONG the moment they do not (`Tag (Wrap a) => …` records `[Wrap a]`
-- against slot mono `a`, so the call site keyed its dict on `Bool` where the predicate
-- is `Tag (Wrap Bool)`).  Arity is not what makes a vector meaningful; a recorded
-- argument that differs from the slot's own mono is.
-- `iface == ""` is pinned scalar deliberately: with no interface there is no arity
-- to give a vector meaning (#1168).  Dropping the length-1
-- clause does not touch that pin: it only widens WHICH non-empty vectors get past it.
vectorGoal : IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Option (Mono, List Mono)
vectorGoal _ [] = None
vectorGoal iface (g0 :: gs) = if iface.irName == "" then None else Some (g0, gs)

routesOfMonosTop : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List Mono ->
  List IfaceRef ->
  List Route
routesOfMonosTop sx _ _ [] _ = []
routesOfMonosTop sx encl useScope (m :: rest) [] =
  routeOf sx ifaceRefNone encl useScope (CountImpls ifaceRefNone) m
    :: routesOfMonosTop sx encl useScope rest []
routesOfMonosTop sx encl useScope (m :: rest) (iface :: ifacesRest) =
  routeOf sx iface encl useScope (CountImpls iface) m
    :: routesOfMonosTop sx encl useScope rest ifacesRest

-- The undetermined-constraint resolution (DICT-SEMANTICS §3): the instances the
-- goal [goal] can still reach, counted by `goalCandidates` and decided by
-- `goalReach` exactly as a boundary's verdict decides them.  None leaves the goal no
-- route; one, or a stable minimum, is its route; any other count is ambiguous.
routeUndeterminedTop : SiteCtx -> ScopeId -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Route
routeUndeterminedTop sx scope ifaceRef goal
  | ifaceRef.irName == "" = RNone
  | otherwise =
    match (goalReach
      sx.sxModule
      goal
      (goalCandidates
        sx.sxModule
        omEmpty
        goal
        (goalRows sx.sxModule ifaceRef goal)))
      ReachNone => RNone
      -- A goal on a scheme-quantified variable is the caller's: the one instance it
      -- reaches is not chosen for it.
      ReachOne _ if not (monoVectorClosed goal)
        && goalsClosed sx.sxModule goal => RNone
      ReachOne row => undeterminedRowRoute sx scope ifaceRef goal row
      -- No route and no diagnostic: the boundary verdict (`goalReach` at quiescence)
      -- owns an ambiguous goal and reports it once at its own site.
      ReachMany => RNone

-- The route of the one instance [row] an undetermined goal reaches: its canonical
-- word, its prerequisites answered at the goal, and each super of [ifaceRef], which
-- the goal leaves undetermined too, answered by the same rule.
undeterminedRowRoute : SiteCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  ImplRow ->
  Route
undeterminedRowRoute sx _ _ [] _ = RNone
undeterminedRowRoute sx scope ifaceRef (m :: rest) row =
  RKey
    (rowRouteKey row)
    (argImplRequiresRoutesForRow
      sx
      ""
      scope
      m
      (m :: rest)
      (reqWalkStart ())
      row)
    (map
      ((superIface, _) =>
        noteInnerRoute
          sx
          (routeUndeterminedTop sx scope superIface (m :: rest)))
      (directSuperGoals sx.sxModule.mcGraph ifaceRef []))

-- Native #54/#21 residual: the activeDictVar-AWARE requires recursion.  Recursing
-- via routeOf (not the removed blind reqRoute) keeps every nesting level
-- activeDictVar-aware: e.g. a `Debug (Map k v)` impl body's `debug (toList m)` arg-
-- stamps `List (k, v)` → RKey "List" recursing into the tuple `(k, v)` whose element
-- vars `k`/`v` ARE the enclosing impl's `requires Debug k, Debug v` dict params
-- (registered in activeDictVars), so they route RDict $dict_debug_<slot>, NOT RNone.
-- The emitted element-dict cell carries the live impl dicts instead of a null (0)
-- field — the null field was the SIGSEGV (the inner per-element debug/eq/compare
-- dispatched through a 0 dict).
-- #217: this is now the SOLE requires recursion — the return position
-- (implDictRoutesIn) routes through here too, no longer through a blind twin.  [encl]
-- threads the enclosing method so nested element dicts forward its own
-- `$dict_<encl>_<slot>` params (encl == "" recovers the global routing).
-- (#1154 folded away the depth-0 wrapper `argImplRequiresRoutesRec`: two names for one
-- body, one caller each.  Seed `reqWalkStart` at an entry point instead.)
--
-- Termination is the shared `requires` measure (`reqWalkEnter`, DICT §3 W2), the same
-- one every solving walk uses: a step to a strictly smaller goal is free, so a ground
-- chain like `impl Tag (Wrap a) requires Tag a` at `Wrap^34 Int` routes at any depth
-- its type needs (#1576); a non-shrinking step spends fuel; a repeated goal is a cycle.
-- This walk also enters each super of a goal beside it (`superRoutesAt`) and follows
-- that super instance's `requires`.  The solving walks follow the same goals under that
-- measure, the super goals included (`superGoalsEntered`, entered beside the goal the
-- same way), and reject a cycle or a spent walk at the goal's site, so this walk
-- reaches either outcome only on a rejected program (`requiresRouteWalkCut`).
--
-- The caller supplies the selected row, so the route word and the context it
-- discharges name the same impl (§6 C2) by construction.
argImplRequiresRoutesForRow : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Mono ->
  List Mono ->
  ReqWalk ->
  ImplRow ->
  List Route
argImplRequiresRoutesForRow sx encl useScope m goals walk row =
  match reqWalkEnter walk (ieRowIface row) goals
    ReqOn next => routeWalkMemoized
      sx
      encl
      useScope
      goals
      row
      next
      (walkSx => match ieRowHeadTriple (Some row)
        Some (headTy, itys, reqs) =>
          match headSubstWithParams sx.sxModule headTy itys m goals
            Some subst => argImplReqRoutes walkSx encl useScope subst reqs next
            None => []
        None => [])
    cut =>
      let _ = noteRouteWalkCut walk
      requiresRouteWalkCut sx.sxModule.mcGraph cut

-- A route walk that met a cycle or ran out of fuel.  The solving walks share its
-- measure and follow the same goals, a super instance's `requires` included
-- (`superGoalsEntered`), and reject the goal at its site, so this is reached only on a
-- program that already carries a type error, and its routes are never emitted.  With no error
-- recorded it is a compiler invariant failure, never a silent `[]` (#1910).
requiresRouteWalkCut : GraphCtx -> ReqStep -> List Route
requiresRouteWalkCut gctx _ =
  if typeErrorsArmed gctx () then
    []
  else
    panic "requires route walk reached a goal the solving walks did not accept"

-- ── D3b-1: arg-position element-dict routing ────────────────────────────────
-- The argument-position analogue of implDictRoutesFor.  Same impl-table match +
-- head-pattern unification against the discriminating-argument mono, but each
-- requires route is computed by routeOf (activeDictVar-aware): a recursive
-- element of the SAME parametric type (the impl's own element tyvar `a`, still a
-- registered constraint var) forwards the in-scope `$dict_<method>_<slot>` param
-- (RDict); a concrete element (`MyList Int`) materializes a static RKey.  #217: the
-- return position (implDictRoutesIn) now shares this same aware requires recursion — the
-- two chains were unified; this entry runs for emit-path arg stamps specifically.
-- #609: the operator route passes the singleton [mono] — and unlike the
-- deferred EKNestedTop case this is not a scope cut, it is EXACT: every interface
-- owning an operator method is single-param (`Eq a`, `Ord a`, `Num a`,
-- `Semigroup a`, `Monoid a` in stdlib/core.mdk), so `itys` has length 1, the
-- lengths agree, and the singleton IS the full vector — matchTyMonos [hty] [m]
-- reduces to matchTyMono hty m.  Should a multi-param interface ever own an
-- operator, entryHeadMatches degrades to the arg-0 fallback rather than
-- mis-selecting.
-- encl-aware variant: thread the ENCLOSING method [encl] so the recursively-routed
-- element dicts forward [encl]'s own `$dict_<encl>_<slot>` params (not whichever
-- method registered the shared impl tyvar id LAST — see activeDictVarForEncl).  An
-- empty [encl] has no lexical dict owner and therefore cannot forward one.
-- #203 (H): the arg/op-position element routes.  Was a FIRST-MATCH scan of the
-- ImplBuckets [tag] bucket (blind to no-requires siblings, see implDictRoutesForRow);
-- now selects the MOST-SPECIFIC matching impl over the graph-global impl universe (`IE`)
-- via the shared method-keyed selector (`ieSelectRowByMethod` since ARCH B-2.1-b2, which
-- replaced `matchedEntry`) and discharges THAT impl's OWN requires.  A
-- non-overlapping site (one match) selects the same impl the first-match scan did ⇒
-- byte-identical routes.
-- #609 (arg position): selects on the goal VECTOR [goals] and binds the subst from
-- the winner's FULL head types, as the return-position selected-row matcher does.
-- This is the SAME defect as #609 proper, one leg over:
-- selecting on `[mono]` length-mismatches a multi-param impl's `itys`, so
-- entryHeadMatches fell back to arg-0 and two siblings differing only past arg 0 both
-- matched.  They are genuinely disjoint, so coherence never rejected them and
-- entryCovers finds them incomparable ⇒ pickMostSpecificEntry took the FIRST-DECLARED,
-- and the impl whose `requires`-context was routed could differ from the impl
-- `routeKey` dispatched to — evidence for instance A attached to methods of instance
-- B (§2 "evidence is a tree"; §6 C2 coherence), order-dependently (§6 C3).
--
-- ⚠️ Only observable when the siblings' requires differ in COUNT.  The dict cell is a
-- TYPE tag (`@mdk_dc_0 = [1 x i64] [193460240]` — the `Int` tag, shared with
-- println's dict), and the routes are built from the subst, so two siblings whose
-- requires range over the SAME tyvar produce the SAME dict whichever is picked; the
-- interface is re-chosen at the use site by a method-specific dispatcher
-- (`@mdk_disp_bar_0_1`).  Differing COUNTS thread the wrong NUMBER of dicts, shifting
-- every later argument.  Regression:
-- test/eval_typed_fixtures/multiparam_impl_requires_arity{,_swapped}.mdk.
argImplDictRoutesForEncl : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Mono ->
  List Mono ->
  List Route
-- ARCH B-2.1-b2 (LEG 3b): the arg-position twin of leg 3a, repointed for the same
-- reason and in the same bite — the two legs select the SAME way at the same goal
-- and a split between them is the §6 C2 break the header describes.
argImplDictRoutesForEncl sx encl useScope name _tag mono goals =
  match (ieRowHeadTriple
    (ieSelectRowByMethod
      sx
      sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
      name
      goals))
    Some (headTy, implTys, reqs) =>
      match headSubstWithParams sx.sxModule headTy implTys mono goals
        Some subst =>
          argImplReqRoutes sx encl useScope subst reqs (reqWalkStart ())
        None => []
    None => []

-- #217: [walk] carries the shared `requires` measure through the aware recursion (see
-- argImplRequiresRoutesForRow, where each goal is entered).  An entry point seeds
-- `reqWalkStart`, or `reqWalkSeed` at the goal whose selected row's `requires` these are.
argImplReqRoutes : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List Require ->
  ReqWalk ->
  List Route
argImplReqRoutes sx _ _ _ [] _ = []
argImplReqRoutes sx encl useScope subst ((Require { requireHead = rIface, requireArgs = rargs, requireOrigin = ro }) :: rest) walk =
  let iface = IfaceRef { irName = rIface, irOrigin = ro }
  argReqRoute sx iface encl useScope subst rargs walk
    :: argImplReqRoutes sx encl useScope subst rest walk

-- [iface] is the requirement's resolved interface, origin included: two interfaces
-- spelled alike (`requires A.Sh a, B.Sh a`) select their impls by declaration, and a
-- bare spelling here selects whichever same-named row matches first (#3534).
argReqRoute : SiteCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List Ty ->
  ReqWalk ->
  Route
argReqRoute sx _ _ _ _ [] _ = noteInnerRoute sx RNone
-- #1154 (F-3a): `(arg::_)` USED TO DROP every argument past arg 0, so a multi-param
-- `requires Ix a Char` reached the selector as the singleton `[Int]` and matched every
-- `Ix Int _` impl.  Keep the whole vector; `routeOfD` threads the tail down the
-- EKNestedTop leg.  Single-param requires bind `more == []` ⇒ unchanged.
argReqRoute sx iface encl useScope subst (arg :: more) walk =
  noteInnerRoute
    sx
    (routeOfD
      sx
      iface
      encl
      useScope
      KeepNone
      (fromAstType sx.sxModule subst arg)
      (map (fromAstType sx.sxModule subst) more)
      walk)

-- Phase 69.x-e: fill each method occurrence's method-dicts ref — one route per
-- method-level constraint, from the instantiated constraint mono.  A concrete head
-- → RKey (eval supplies a literal VDict for the body's `empty`/… to read); a
-- constraint variable still (the caller is itself constrained) → RDict forwarding
-- the caller's dict.  Mirrors resolveDictApps; runs after inference.
resolveMethodDicts : SiteCtx -> List PendingMethodDict -> Unit
resolveMethodDicts sx [] = ()
resolveMethodDicts sx (pending :: rest) =
  pending.pmdRoutesRef :=
    methodPredicateRoutes sx pending.pmdEncl pending.pmdScope pending.pmdSlots
  resolveMethodDicts sx rest

methodPredicateRoutes : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  List Route
methodPredicateRoutes sx _ _ [] = []
methodPredicateRoutes sx encl scope (slot :: rest) =
  methodPredicateRoute sx encl scope slot
    :: methodPredicateRoutes sx encl scope rest

methodPredicateRoute : SiteCtx -> String -> ScopeId -> PredicateSlot -> Route
methodPredicateRoute sx encl scope slot = match slot.psArgs
  PSArgsKnown (g0 :: gs) =>
    routeOfD sx slot.psIface encl scope KeepNone g0 gs (reqWalkStart ())
  _ => RNone

-- ── recursive dict-app realization (self/mutual recursion) ──────────────────
-- A deferred recursive call records one route per the CALLEE's constraint slot
-- (matching the dict params dict_pass prepends to its def), each forwarding the
-- ENCLOSING fn's own dict param.  Run after inference, when funConstraintsRef is
-- fully populated.
realizeRecDictApps : SiteCtx -> List RecDictApp -> Unit
realizeRecDictApps sx [] = ()
realizeRecDictApps sx ((RecDictApp routesRef callee encl mono scope _) :: rest) =
  let slots =
    optionOr
      []
      (lookupPredicateSlots
        callee
        sx.sxModule.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsIdxRef.value)
  let routes = recRoutes sx encl scope mono slots
  routesRef := routes
  realizeRecDictApps sx rest

recRoutes : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Mono ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  List Route
recRoutes sx _ _ _ [] = []
recRoutes sx encl scope mono (slot :: rest) =
  recRoute sx encl scope mono slot :: recRoutes sx encl scope mono rest

-- For one of the callee's constraint ids, recover the live occurrence type from
-- [mono] (the var the body unified it to).  Concrete head → RKey; still a
-- constraint variable that is one of [encl]'s own → forward [encl]'s dict param
-- (RDict, the slot it sits at); otherwise leave the route unresolved.
recRoute : SiteCtx -> String -> ScopeId -> Mono -> PredicateSlot -> Route
recRoute sx encl scope mono slot =
  match recPredicateArgs sx.sxModule.mcGraph mono slot
    Some (g0 :: gs) =>
      routeOfD sx slot.psIface encl scope KeepNone g0 gs (reqWalkStart ())
    _ => match slot.psBoundIds
      id :: _ => match findTvarInMono mono id
        None => RNone
        Some m => resolveRecMono sx encl scope slot.psIface m
      [] => RNone

recPredicateArgs : GraphCtx -> Mono -> PredicateSlot -> Option (List Mono)
recPredicateArgs gctx mono slot = match slot.psArgs
  PSArgsUnknown => None
  PSArgsKnown args =>
    map
      (subst => map (substMono gctx subst [] []) args)
      (recSlotSubst mono slot.psBoundIds)

recSlotSubst : Mono -> List Int -> Option (List (Int, Mono))
recSlotSubst _ [] = Some []
recSlotSubst mono (id :: rest) = match findTvarInMono mono id
  None => None
  Some m => map ((id, m) :: _) (recSlotSubst mono rest)

resolveRecMono : SiteCtx -> String -> ScopeId -> IfaceRef -> Mono -> Route
resolveRecMono sx encl scope iface m = match headTyconMono m
  -- a rigid variable names no instance, so its spelled head is left as it was
  Some (hk@(HkRigid _)) =>
    RKey
      (headKeyTag hk)
      []
      (superRoutesAt sx iface encl scope [m] (reqWalkStart ()))
  -- a concrete head names an instance: select it like any other predicate goal, so
  -- the dictionary carries that instance's word and `requires`
  Some _ => routeOfD sx iface encl scope KeepNone m [] (reqWalkStart ())
  -- the enclosing slot is found by tyvar alone, so it may hold a SUB-interface of
  -- the callee's predicate: read the super out of it
  None => match enclSlot sx.sxModule encl m
    Some slot =>
      let binder =
        Scopes.binderAt
          (Scopes.declarationScope
            (currentScopeStore sx.sxModule.mcGraph ())
            scope)
          slot
      assumAnswerRoute
        sx.sxModule.mcGraph
        (LegacyScalar binder)
        (Some iface)
        scope
        RDict
    None => routeOf sx ifaceRefNone "" scope KeepNone m

-- the dict-param slot at which [m]'s tyvar sits among the enclosing fn's
-- constraint ids (its position in funConstraintsRef[encl] = the kept slot)
enclSlot : ModuleCtx -> String -> Mono -> Option Int
enclSlot mctx encl m = match normalize m
  TVar cell =>
    indexOfId
      (tyvarId cell)
      (predicateSlotIdsAt encl mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsIdxRef.value)
  _ => None

indexOfId : Int -> List Int -> Option Int
indexOfId target ids = indexOfIdGo 0 target ids

indexOfIdGo : Int -> Int -> List Int -> Option Int
indexOfIdGo _ _ [] = None
indexOfIdGo i target (x :: xs)
  | x == target = Some i
  | otherwise = indexOfIdGo (i + 1) target xs

-- ── dict_pass: prepend dict parameters to constrained function definitions ──
-- For each top-level def of a name in [dictNames], prepend one `$dict_<fn>_<slot>`
-- parameter per constraint (arity from funConstraintsRef, populated during
-- inference), matching the dicts EDictAt applies at call sites.  Multi-clause
-- functions are several DFunDef decls; each clause gets the same leading params.
-- ⚠️ #2189: [names] is the dict-passed set, which grows with the program, and this
-- maps over EVERY decl — so `contains n names` inside `dictPassDecl` was
-- O(decls x names).  Index it ONCE here; `dictPassDecl`/`dictPassLetBind` probe
-- with `omHasKey`.  Membership semantics unchanged.
dictPass : ModuleCtx ->
  EvIndex ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl
dictPass mctx idx mid names prog =
  let pe = PassEvidence idx (Ref omEmpty)
  map
    (dictPassDecl
      mctx
      pe
      (omFromNames names omEmpty)
      (returnPosMethodNames prog))
    (mapProg
      (e => rewriteLocalDictExpr mctx.mcGraph (rewriteBinopExpr mctx pe e))
      (grantPass mctx.mcGraph pe mid prog))

passIndex : PassEvidence -> EvIndex
passIndex (PassEvidence idx _) = idx

-- The entry published for method occurrence [ev].  A miss in both is the index's
-- miss.
passMethodOf : PassEvidence -> EvId -> PassMethod
passMethodOf (PassEvidence idx minted) ev =
  match evidenceLookup (Some idx) "method occurrence" ev
    Ok v => passMethodFacts v
    Err message => match omLookup (intToString (evOrdinal ev)) minted.value
      Some v => passMethodFacts v
      None => panic message

passMethodFacts : EvVal -> PassMethod
passMethodFacts (EvMethod iface _ tag impls meths) =
  PassMethod iface tag (impls ++ meths)
passMethodFacts _ =
  panic "evidence table: a method occurrence answered by another kind of entry"

-- ── grant passing: the authority analogue of the dictionary pass ─────────────
-- Runs before the dictionary rewrites of module [mid], so a binder's authority
-- parameters land after the dictionary parameters those rewrites prepend, and
-- each recorded use is applied to its grants while it still carries its id.
grantPass : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> String -> List Decl -> List Decl
grantPass gctx pe mid prog =
  let st = gctx.graphRun.grants
  let saved = st.gsPassingModule.value
  st.gsPassingModule := mid
  let result = map (grantDecl gctx pe mid) prog
  st.gsPassingModule := saved
  result

grantDecl : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> String -> Decl -> Decl
grantDecl gctx pe mid (DFunDef pub n pats body site bid) =
  DFunDef
    pub
    n
    (grantParamPats (topGrantIds gctx mid n) n ++ pats)
    (grantBody gctx pe body)
    site
    bid
grantDecl gctx pe mid (DLetGroup pub binds) =
  DLetGroup
    pub
    (map
      (b => match b
        LetBind n clauses site bid =>
          grantLetBind
            gctx
            pe
            (grantParamPats (topGrantIds gctx mid n) n)
            (LetBind n clauses site bid))
      binds)
grantDecl gctx pe _ (d@(DInterface { name, ifaceOrigin, methods, ... })) = DInterface { d |
  methods =
    map (grantIfaceMethod gctx pe (ifaceWordOf ifaceOrigin name)) methods,
}
grantDecl gctx pe _ (d@(DImpl { iface, implOrigin, methods, ... })) = DImpl { d |
  methods = map (grantImplMethod gctx pe (ifaceWordOf implOrigin iface)) methods,
}
grantDecl gctx pe _ (DProp pub name params body) =
  DProp pub name params (grantExpr gctx pe body)
grantDecl gctx pe _ (DTest pub name body) =
  DTest pub name (grantExpr gctx pe body)
grantDecl gctx pe mid (DAttrib attrs d) =
  DAttrib attrs (grantDecl gctx pe mid d)
-- a declaration with no expression body (data, signatures, imports, externs)
grantDecl gctx _ _ d = d

-- A method that takes grants declares them after its value arguments, so the
-- arity every backend reads off the declaration counts them.
grantIfaceMethod : GraphCtx ->
  PassEvidence ->
  String ->
  IfaceMethod ->
  IfaceMethod
grantIfaceMethod gctx pe word (IfaceMethod n ty def mloc) =
  match methodGrantOf gctx word n
    None =>
      IfaceMethod
        n
        ty
        (map
          (d => match d
            MethodDefault ps e => MethodDefault ps (grantBody gctx pe e))
          def)
        mloc
    Some mg =>
      IfaceMethod
        n
        (insertGrantArrows mg.mgArity (listLen mg.mgNames) ty)
        (map
          (d => match d
            MethodDefault ps e =>
              let (ps2, e2) =
                grantMethodParams gctx mg n ps (grantBody gctx pe e)
              MethodDefault ps2 e2)
          def)
        mloc

grantImplMethod : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> String -> ImplMethod -> ImplMethod
grantImplMethod gctx pe word (ImplMethod n ps e) =
  match methodGrantOf gctx word n
    None => ImplMethod n ps (grantBody gctx pe e)
    Some mg =>
      let (ps2, e2) = grantMethodParams gctx mg n ps (grantBody gctx pe e)
      ImplMethod n ps2 e2

-- A method clause's grant parameters, after its value parameters; a clause
-- written with fewer parameters than the method's arity takes the missing ones
-- first and applies its body to them.
grantMethodParams : GraphCtx ->
  MethodGrant ->
  String ->
  List Pat ->
  Expr ->
  (List Pat, Expr)
grantMethodParams gctx mg n ps body =
  let grants = grantParamPats mg.mgNames n
  let given = listLen ps
  if given >= mg.mgArity then
    (take mg.mgArity ps ++ grants ++ drop mg.mgArity ps, body)
  else
    let missing =
      map
        (_ => freshGrantName gctx.graphRun.grants ())
        (rangeFromCount given (mg.mgArity - given))
    (
      ps ++ map (x => PVar x (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId) missing ++ grants,
      applyExprs body (map EVar missing),
    )

-- [g] `List String` arguments after the first [k] arrows of a method's type.
insertGrantArrows : Int -> Int -> Ty -> Ty
insertGrantArrows k g (TyConstrained cs t) =
  TyConstrained cs (insertGrantArrows k g t)
insertGrantArrows k g (TyEffect effs tails t)
  | k > 0 = TyEffect effs tails (insertGrantArrows k g t)
insertGrantArrows k g (TyFun a b)
  | k > 0 = TyFun a (insertGrantArrows (k - 1) g b)
insertGrantArrows _ g t = grantArrows g t

grantArrows : Int -> Ty -> Ty
grantArrows g t
  | g <= 0 = t
  | otherwise =
    TyFun
      (TyApp (tyConBuiltin "List" None) (tyConBuiltin "String" None))
      (grantArrows (g - 1) t)

grantLetBind : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> List Pat -> LetBind -> LetBind
grantLetBind gctx pe params (LetBind n clauses site bid) =
  LetBind
    n
    (map
      (c => match c
        FunClause ps body => FunClause (params ++ ps) (grantBody gctx pe body))
      clauses)
    site
    bid

topGrantIds : GraphCtx -> String -> String -> List Int
topGrantIds gctx mid n =
  optionOr [] (omLookup (grantTopKey mid n) gctx.graphRun.grants.gsTopIds.value)

localGrantIds : GraphCtx -> String -> List Int
localGrantIds gctx n =
  optionOr [] (omLookup n gctx.graphRun.grants.gsLocalIds.value)

grantParamName : String -> Int -> String
grantParamName n i = "$auth_\{n}_\{intToString i}"

grantParamPats : List a -> String -> List Pat
grantParamPats ids n =
  map
    (i => PVar (grantParamName n i) (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId)
    (rangeFromCount 0 (listLen ids))

-- The top-down walk: a use of a file extern or a method is rebuilt with every
-- argument it takes, so it sees its whole application spine before its
-- arguments do.
grantExpr : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> Expr -> Expr
grantExpr gctx pe e =
  let inner = grantExprInner gctx pe e
  let st = gctx.graphRun.grants
  match st.gsValueBounds.value
    Tip => inner
    _ => match fileValueKey st.gsPassingModule.value e
      Some key =>
        let bounds = optionOr [] (omLookup key st.gsValueBounds.value)
        fold
          (result (ty, chain) => fileBoundValue gctx chain ty result)
          inner
          bounds
      None => inner

grantExprInner : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> Expr -> Expr
grantExprInner gctx pe (ELam pats body) = ELam pats (grantBody gctx pe body)
grantExprInner gctx pe (e@(EApp _ _)) = match grantSpine e []
  (EDictAt n ev, args) => match grantOccOf gctx ev
    Some occ => match occ.goTrailing
      Some arity =>
        saturateGrants
          gctx.graphRun.grants
          (EVar n)
          arity
          (grantTerms gctx occ)
          (map (grantExpr gctx pe) args)
      None => mapChildren (grantExpr gctx pe) e
    None => mapChildren (grantExpr gctx pe) e
  (EMethodAt n seed ev, args) => match methodGrantUse gctx pe n ev
    MethodGrants arity grants =>
      saturateGrants
        gctx.graphRun.grants
        (EMethodAt n seed ev)
        arity
        grants
        (map (grantExpr gctx pe) args)
    LeadingGrants _ grants =>
      applyExprs
        (applyExprs (EMethodAt n seed ev) grants)
        (map (grantExpr gctx pe) args)
    NoGrants => mapChildren (grantExpr gctx pe) e
  _ => mapChildren (grantExpr gctx pe) e
grantExprInner gctx _ (EDictAt n ev) = grantUse gctx n ev
grantExprInner gctx pe (EMethodAt n seed ev) = match methodGrantUse gctx pe n ev
  MethodGrants arity grants =>
    saturateGrants gctx.graphRun.grants (EMethodAt n seed ev) arity grants []
  LeadingGrants _ grants => applyExprs (EMethodAt n seed ev) grants
  NoGrants => EMethodAt n seed ev
grantExprInner gctx pe (ELet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e1 e2) =
  ELet
    m
    r
    (PVar x xloc bid)
    (grantLocalRhs gctx x (grantExpr gctx pe e1))
    (grantExpr gctx pe e2)
grantExprInner gctx pe (ELetGroup binds body) =
  ELetGroup
    (map
      (b => match b
        LetBind x clauses site bid =>
          grantLetBind
            gctx
            pe
            (grantParamPats (localGrantIds gctx x) x)
            (LetBind x clauses site bid))
      binds)
    (grantExpr gctx pe body)
grantExprInner gctx pe (EBlock stmts) = EBlock (map (grantStmt gctx pe) stmts)
-- every other node: its children, through the one traversal every pass shares
grantExprInner gctx pe e = mapChildren (grantExpr gctx pe) e

grantStmt : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> DoStmt -> DoStmt
grantStmt gctx pe (DoLet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e site) =
  DoLet m r (PVar x xloc bid) (grantLocalRhs gctx x (grantExpr gctx pe e)) site
grantStmt gctx pe (DoExpr e) = DoExpr (grantExpr gctx pe e)
grantStmt gctx pe (DoBind p e) = DoBind p (grantExpr gctx pe e)
grantStmt gctx pe (DoLet m r p e site) = DoLet m r p (grantExpr gctx pe e) site
grantStmt gctx pe (DoAssign x e) = DoAssign x (grantExpr gctx pe e)
grantStmt gctx pe (DoFieldAssign x fs e) =
  DoFieldAssign x fs (grantExpr gctx pe e)

-- A local that quantifies authorities takes them ahead of its own parameters.
grantLocalRhs : GraphCtx -> String -> Expr -> Expr
grantLocalRhs gctx x e = match localGrantIds gctx x
  [] => e
  ids =>
    prependLocalDicts
      (map (i => grantParamName x i) (rangeFromCount 0 (listLen ids)))
      e

-- An application spine's head and its arguments, through source-location
-- wrappers.
grantSpine : Expr -> List Expr -> (Expr, List Expr)
grantSpine (EApp f x) args = grantSpine f (x :: args)
grantSpine (ELoc _ e) args = grantSpine e args
-- any other node is the head
grantSpine e args = (e, args)

-- A use of a source binding: the head applied to its grants.  A grant-only use
-- of a binding that quantifies nothing is the plain variable it stood for.
grantUse : GraphCtx -> String -> EvId -> Expr
grantUse gctx n ev =
  let head = if isGrantOnlyEv gctx ev then EVar n else EDictAt n ev
  match grantOccOf gctx ev
    None => head
    Some occ => match occ.goTrailing
      Some arity =>
        saturateGrants
          gctx.graphRun.grants
          (EVar n)
          arity
          (grantTerms gctx occ)
          []
      None => applyExprs head (grantTerms gctx occ)

-- A method occurrence's grants.  One that dispatches passes the method's, after
-- the value arity its written type spells; a use that inference did not record
-- (its denotation was settled by a path that instantiates no method scheme) passes
-- the empty authority, so the method's arity still agrees with every body and the
-- use is refused rather than admitted.  One routed to the standalone its name
-- shadows passes that binding's grants, which inference recorded when it typed
-- the occurrence as the standalone; a grant-taking standalone reached without that
-- record has no grants to pass, and is a compile-time failure.  The occurrence's
-- published arity counts the grants, as the backends read it; the published table
-- is read out of the cells after the pass, so that count is written to the
-- occurrence's cell (`setOccurrenceArity`).
methodGrantUse : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> String -> EvId -> MethodGrantUse
methodGrantUse gctx pe n ev =
  let (PassMethod iface tag _) = passMethodOf pe ev
  let recorded = grantOccOf gctx ev
  let use = match tag
    RLocal sym _ => match standaloneOcc recorded
      Some (arity, occ) => LeadingGrants arity (grantTerms gctx occ)
      None =>
        if omHasKey
          (if sym == "" then n else sym)
          gctx.graphRun.grants.gsTakers.value then
          panic
            "grant pass: '\{n}' is routed to a standalone binding that takes authority grants, but inference did not type this use as that binding"
        else
          NoGrants
    _ => match methodGrantOf gctx iface n
      None => NoGrants
      Some mg => match recorded
        Some occ =>
          if occ.goStandalone then
            MethodGrants mg.mgArity (map (_ => bottomGrant) mg.mgNames)
          else
            MethodGrants mg.mgArity (methodTerms gctx n mg occ)
        None => MethodGrants mg.mgArity (map (_ => bottomGrant) mg.mgNames)
  let _ = match use
    MethodGrants arity grants =>
      setOccurrenceArity gctx pe ev (arity + listLen grants)
    LeadingGrants arity grants =>
      setOccurrenceArity gctx pe ev (arity + listLen grants)
    NoGrants => ()
  use

-- An occurrence in a module the drive served has no cell in this lineage: its
-- entry in the index takes the count (`setServedArity`).
setOccurrenceArity : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> EvId -> Int -> Unit
setOccurrenceArity gctx pe ev arity
  | evOrdinal ev < gctx.graphRun.evBase = setServedArity (passIndex pe) ev arity
  | otherwise =
    let cell = methodCellOf gctx ev
    cell.ecArity := Some arity

-- A use recorded as the standalone binding a method occurrence shadows, with its
-- value arity.
standaloneOcc : Option GrantOcc -> Option (Int, GrantOcc)
standaloneOcc (Some occ) = match (occ.goStandalone, occ.goTrailing)
  (True, Some arity) => Some (arity, occ)
  _ => None
standaloneOcc None = None

-- A recorded method use's grants, one per authority the method quantifies.
methodTerms : GraphCtx -> String -> MethodGrant -> GrantOcc -> List Expr
methodTerms gctx n mg occ =
  let terms = grantTerms gctx occ
  if listLen terms == listLen mg.mgNames then
    terms
  else
    panic
      "grant pass: a use of method '\{n}' instantiated \{intToString (listLen terms)} authorities, but the method takes \{intToString (listLen mg.mgNames)} grants"

-- The empty authority: a grant that admits no path.
bottomGrant : Expr
bottomGrant = EListLit [ELit (LString "")]

applyExprs : Expr -> List Expr -> Expr
applyExprs f args = fold (acc a => EApp acc a) f args

-- A head applied to all [arity] value arguments and then its grants.  A partial
-- or value use becomes a function of the arguments still missing; the arguments
-- it was given are bound first, so each is evaluated once, where the program
-- wrote it.
saturateGrants : GrantState -> Expr -> Int -> List Expr -> List Expr -> Expr
saturateGrants st head arity grants args =
  let given = listLen args
  if given >= arity then
    applyExprs (applyExprs head (take arity args ++ grants)) (drop arity args)
  else
    let bound = map (a => (freshGrantName st (), a)) args
    let missing =
      map (_ => freshGrantName st ()) (rangeFromCount given (arity - given))
    let call =
      applyExprs
        head
        (map (b => EVar (fst b)) bound ++ map EVar missing ++ grants)
    fold
      (body b =>
        ELet
          noDeclLoc
          False
          (PVar (fst b) (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId)
          (snd b)
          body)
      (ELam (map (x => PVar x (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId) missing) call)
      (reverseL bound)

freshGrantName : GrantState -> Unit -> String
freshGrantName st _ =
  let k = st.gsFresh.value
  st.gsFresh := k + 1
  "$grant_arg_\{intToString k}"

-- A declared file row bounds every operation performed while its body runs,
-- including operations in helpers and callbacks. The bound is checked in
-- addition to each extern's own grant; a statically named symlink can change
-- the physical order between the two authorities.
fileBoundKey : Loc -> String
fileBoundKey (Loc file line col endLine endCol) =
  "\{file}:\{intToString line}:\{intToString col}:\{intToString endLine}:\{intToString endCol}"

-- Some application and block roots carry locations only on their children.
-- Key the body by its first source node, and guard the whole body at its
-- binding/lambda seam, rather than guarding that child alone.
fileBodyLoc : Expr -> Option Loc
fileBodyLoc (ELoc l _) = Some l
fileBodyLoc e =
  let found = Ref None
  let _ =
    mapChildren
      (child =>
        let _ = match found.value
          None => found := fileBodyLoc child
          Some _ => ()
        child)
      e
  found.value

fileBoundSite : String -> Loc -> String
-- Parsed locations may have an empty file field; the module keeps equal
-- source spans in different modules from sharing a bound.
fileBoundSite mid loc =
  "\{intToString (stringLength mid)}:\{mid}:\{fileBoundKey loc}"

scopeFileBoundModule : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> String
scopeFileBoundModule mctx _ =
  (Scopes.scopeFrame
    (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
    (captureScope mctx ())).sfModuleId

fileValueKey : String -> Expr -> Option String
fileValueKey mid e =
  map (loc => "\{fileBoundSite mid loc}:\{fileValueShape e}") (fileBodyLoc e)

fileValueShape : Expr -> String
fileValueShape (ELoc _ _) = "loc"
fileValueShape (EApp f _) = "app" ++ intToString (appSpineArgCount f + 1)
fileValueShape (ELam _ _) = "lambda"
fileValueShape _ = "value"

finishFileValueScope : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> Unit
finishFileValueScope mctx _ = match mctx.mcCells.fileValueScopes.value
  saved :: rest =>
    mctx.mcCells.fileValueScopes := rest
    let flows = wWindow mctx.mcCells.fileValueFlows (snd saved)
    let _ = wRestore mctx.mcCells.fileValueFlows saved
    let _ =
      map
        (flow =>
          if isEmptyL rest || not (unsettledFileValueFlow flow) then
            checkFileValueFlow mctx flow)
        flows
    -- A local result can be shaped by a later use in its enclosing scope.
    -- Keep its producer evidence until that receiving type is determined.
    let _ = match rest
      [] => ()
      _ =>
        wPushAll
          mctx.mcCells.fileValueFlows
          (reverseL (filterList unsettledFileValueFlow flows))
    ()
  [] => ()

unsettledFileValueFlow : (Option Loc, Mono, Mono) -> Bool
unsettledFileValueFlow (_, upper, lower) =
  unsettledPackedFileBound False upper lower

unsettledPackedFileBound : Bool -> Mono -> Mono -> Bool
unsettledPackedFileBound packed upper lower = match (
  normalize upper,
  normalize lower,
)
  (TVar _, _) => True
  (_, TVar _) => True
  (TQual u _, l) => unsettledPackedFileBound packed u l
  (u, TQual l _) => unsettledPackedFileBound packed u l
  (TApp uf ux, TApp lf lx) =>
    unsettledPackedFileBound True uf lf || unsettledPackedFileBound True ux lx
  (TFun ud ur ux, TFun ld lr lx) =>
    packed && unsettledFileRow ur lr
      || unsettledPackedFileBound packed ld ud
      || unsettledPackedFileBound packed ux lx
  _ => False

unsettledFileRow : EffRow -> EffRow -> Bool
unsettledFileRow upper lower =
  let (ua, ut) = rowFlat upper
  let (la, lt) = rowFlat lower
  isNonEmptyL ut
    || isNonEmptyL lt
    || anyList (a => narrowFileAtom a && authHasVars (atomAuth a)) (ua ++ la)

checkFileValueFlow : ModuleCtx -> (Option Loc, Mono, Mono) -> Unit
checkFileValueFlow mctx (loc, upper, lower) =
  if changesPackedFileBound False upper lower then
    pushTypeErrorOncePerSite
      mctx
      "T-FILE-BOUND-VALUE"
      loc
      ("a function's file bound cannot change inside a container: "
        ++ ppMonosShared [lower, upper]
        ++ "; annotate the function with the container's FileRead or FileWrite bound before packing it")

changesPackedFileBound : Bool -> Mono -> Mono -> Bool
changesPackedFileBound packed upper lower = match (
  normalize upper,
  normalize lower,
)
  (TQual u _, l) => changesPackedFileBound packed u l
  (u, TQual l _) => changesPackedFileBound packed u l
  (TApp uf ux, TApp lf lx) =>
    changesPackedFileBound True uf lf || changesPackedFileBound True ux lx
  (TFun ud ur ux, TFun ld lr lx) =>
    packed && changesFileRow ur lr
      || changesPackedFileBound packed ld ud
      || changesPackedFileBound packed ux lx
  _ => False

changesFileRow : EffRow -> EffRow -> Bool
changesFileRow upper lower =
  let (ua, ut) = rowFlat upper
  let (la, lt) = rowFlat lower
  isEmptyL ut
    && anyList
      (u =>
        narrowFileAtom u
          && (isNonEmptyL lt
            || anyList
              (l =>
                atomKey l == atomKey u
                  && not
                    (authSub (atomAuth l) (atomAuth u)
                      && authSub (atomAuth u) (atomAuth l)))
              la))
      ua

hasFileBoundValue : Mono -> Bool
hasFileBoundValue t = match normalize t
  TFun _ row result =>
    let (atoms, tails) = rowFlat row
    isEmptyL tails && anyList narrowFileAtom atoms || hasFileBoundValue result
  TQual inner _ => hasFileBoundValue inner
  _ => False

recordValueFileBound : ModuleCtx -> Expr -> Mono -> Unit
recordValueFileBound mctx e ty =
  if hasFileBoundValue
    ty then match fileValueKey (scopeFileBoundModule mctx ()) e
    Some key =>
      let st = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.grants
      st.gsValueBounds :=
        omInsert
          key
          ((ty, grantChainAt mctx.mcGraph (captureScope mctx ()))
            :: optionOr [] (omLookup key st.gsValueBounds.value))
          st.gsValueBounds.value
    None => ()

-- Evaluate a function-valued expression once. Its bound becomes active on
-- application, and the returned function (if any) retains its own arrow rows.
fileBoundValue : GraphCtx -> List GrantBinder -> Mono -> Expr -> Expr
fileBoundValue gctx chain ty e =
  if hasFileBoundValue ty then match normalize ty
    TFun _ row result =>
      let fn = freshGrantName gctx.graphRun.grants ()
      let arg = freshGrantName gctx.graphRun.grants ()
      ELet
        noDeclLoc
        False
        (PVar fn (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId)
        e
        (ELam
          [PVar arg (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId]
          (fileBoundExpr
            gctx
            chain
            row
            (fileBoundValue gctx chain result (EApp (EVar fn) (EVar arg)))))
    TQual inner _ => fileBoundValue gctx chain inner e
    _ => e
  else
    e

recordFileBound : ModuleCtx -> Expr -> EffRow -> Unit
recordFileBound mctx body row =
  let (atoms, tails) = rowFlat row
  if isEmptyL tails && anyList narrowFileAtom atoms then match fileBodyLoc body
    None => ()
    Some loc =>
      let st = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.grants
      let key = fileBoundSite (scopeFileBoundModule mctx ()) loc
      st.gsBounds :=
        omInsert
          key
          ((row, grantChainAt mctx.mcGraph (captureScope mctx ()))
            :: optionOr [] (omLookup key st.gsBounds.value))
          st.gsBounds.value

grantBody : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> Expr -> Expr
grantBody gctx pe body =
  let inner = grantExpr gctx pe body
  match gctx.graphRun.grants.gsBounds.value
    Tip => inner
    boundsBySite =>
      let bounds = match fileBodyLoc body
        Some loc =>
          optionOr
            []
            (omLookup
              (fileBoundSite gctx.graphRun.grants.gsPassingModule.value loc)
              boundsBySite)
        None => []
      fold
        (result (row, chain) => fileBoundExpr gctx chain row result)
        inner
        bounds

narrowFileAtom : Atom -> Bool
narrowFileAtom atom = match atomLabelOf atom
  EffLabel label OriginBuiltin =>
    (label == "FileRead" || label == "FileWrite")
      && not (authIsTop (atomAuth atom))
  _ => False

recordClauseFileBound : ModuleCtx -> Expr -> Int -> Mono -> Unit
recordClauseFileBound mctx body arity ty
  | arity <= 0 = ()
  | otherwise = match normalize ty
    TFun _ row result =>
      if arity == 1 then
        recordFileBound mctx body row
      else
        recordClauseFileBound mctx body (arity - 1) result
    TQual inner _ => recordClauseFileBound mctx body arity inner
    _ => ()

fileBoundExpr : GraphCtx -> List GrantBinder -> EffRow -> Expr -> Expr
fileBoundExpr gctx chain row body =
  let (atoms, tails) = rowFlat row
  if isNonEmptyL tails then
    body
  else
    fold
      (result atom =>
        let label = atomLabel atom
        if narrowFileAtom atom then
          applyExprs (EVar ("$with" ++ label ++ "Bound")) [
            grantTerm gctx chain (atomAuth atom),
            ELam [PWild] result,
          ]
        else
          result)
      body
      atoms

-- The grant terms of one use, one per authority the callee quantifies.
grantTerms : GraphCtx -> GrantOcc -> List Expr
grantTerms gctx occ = match occ.goRecIds
  [] => map (grantTerm gctx occ.goChain) occ.goCells
  ids => map (i => grantIdTerm gctx occ.goChain i) ids

-- The whole domain is the empty list, the empty authority a list holding only the
-- empty element (it admits no path), and a set of elements joined with the
-- parameters of enclosing binders is their concatenation.  A variable is the
-- parameter of the innermost enclosing binder that quantifies it.  Two kinds of
-- variable have no caller to supply them, an opened existential and an instance
-- head's index (`markSourceless`), and each is the whole domain: the escape check
-- has held the declaration it reaches to its label's top.  Any other variable
-- whose binder is not found contributes the empty authority, so a lost binder is
-- a refusal at run time rather than an unconfined operation.
grantTerm : GraphCtx -> List GrantBinder -> Authority -> Expr
grantTerm gctx chain a = match authGrantShape a
  GrantTop => EListLit []
  GrantBottom => bottomGrant
  GrantParts elems vars => match grantVarParams gctx chain vars []
    None => EListLit []
    Some params =>
      let parts =
        (if isEmptyL elems then
            []
          else
            [EListLit (map (s => ELit (LString s)) elems)])
          ++ map EVar (dedup params)
      match parts
        [] => bottomGrant
        [p] => p
        p :: rest =>
          fold
            (acc param => topAbsorbs param acc)
            -- Generated after inference: the list identity supplies the operand
            -- representation that a hidden grant parameter alone cannot carry.
            (fold
              (acc q => EBinOp "++" acc q unminted)
              (EListLit [])
              (p :: rest))
            (dedup params)

-- The parameters a join's variables are, or None when one of them has no caller
-- to supply it and so makes the join the whole domain.  A variable whose binder
-- is not found contributes nothing.
grantVarParams : GraphCtx ->
  List GrantBinder ->
  List (Ref Authvar) ->
  List String ->
  Option (List String)
grantVarParams gctx _ [] acc = Some (reverseL acc)
grantVarParams gctx chain (v :: rest) acc =
  match grantParamFor gctx chain (authvarId v)
    Some p => grantVarParams gctx chain rest (p :: acc)
    None =>
      if isSourceless gctx (authvarId v) then
        None
      else
        grantVarParams gctx chain rest acc

-- A parameter holding the whole domain makes a join it is part of the whole
-- domain; concatenation alone would narrow it to the other parts.
topAbsorbs : String -> Expr -> Expr
topAbsorbs param join =
  EMatch (EVar param) [Arm (PList []) [] (EListLit []), Arm PWild [] join]

-- A recursive use forwards its enclosing binder's parameters; one whose binder is
-- not found is the empty authority, as in `grantTerm`.
grantIdTerm : GraphCtx -> List GrantBinder -> Int -> Expr
grantIdTerm gctx chain i = match grantParamFor gctx chain i
  Some p => EVar p
  None => bottomGrant

-- The parameter of the innermost enclosing binder that quantifies authority [i].
grantParamFor : GraphCtx -> List GrantBinder -> Int -> Option String
grantParamFor gctx [] _ = None
grantParamFor gctx (b :: rest) i =
  let (name, ids) = match b
    TopGrantBinder mid n => (n, topGrantIds gctx mid n)
    LocalGrantBinder n => (n, localGrantIds gctx n)
    BodyGrantBinder n bound => (n, bound)
  match indexOfId i ids
    Some k => Some (grantParamName name k)
    None => grantParamFor gctx rest i

-- Routed operators become method applications, including generic arithmetic.
-- Packed instance prerequisites move into EMethodAt's implementation-dictionary
-- routes. RNone and scalar routes preserve primitive operations, so primitive
-- Num method bodies do not recursively call their own dictionary methods.
rewriteBinopExpr : ModuleCtx -> PassEvidence -> Expr -> Expr
rewriteBinopExpr mctx pe (EBinOp op l r ev) =
  match evSiteRouteIn (passIndex pe) ev
    RNone => EBinOp op l r ev
    -- SHARED-FLOAT-RESIDUAL §3(C): an RScalar route is NOT a typeclass dispatch — it
    -- is the scalar-type tag typecheck stamped on a monomorphic binop
    -- (its primitive head on arithmetic, an allowed comparison tag on comparison).
    -- Lowering does not read the
    -- EBinOp's site id, so we carry the scalar type in a NODE by wrapping the binop
    -- in `EAnnot … (TyCon tag)`.  Eval ignores the
    -- annotation (`eval (EAnnot e _) = eval e`) and evaluates the binop dynamically
    -- (Float-correct); lowering reads the annotation to stamp CBinPrim's scalar tag so
    -- the native emitter picks that type's primitive without reading the operands'
    -- structure.  This is the dispatch route READ-OUT the design names, relocated
    -- from the (lost) ref cell to a (surviving) node.
    --
    -- #1110 (was a residual, DRAINED by the stamping PR): `tag` is a SCALAR-TYPE
    -- TAG this pass synthesises (never a head the user wrote), and this runs AFTER
    -- resolve, so nothing downstream would ever stamp it.  It takes the same
