  -- checkUndeterminedObligations as a SPURIOUS `Ambiguous instance` for any iface with
  -- >= 2 impls (it fired on every program the moment core's own parametric impls were
  -- inferred — the prelude snapshot).  So WINDOW the obligation channel across this
  -- pass and restore it afterward: the body-clash errors go through `typeErrors`, NOT
  -- the obligation channel, so windowing keeps the #781 reject while dropping the
  -- abstract-var false positives.
  --
  -- 🚨 #1114 (#792): THE ROLLBACK IS GROUND-PRESERVING, and it did not used to be.
  -- The two `wRestore`s below used to run bare, which threw away EVERY obligation the
  -- parametric pass recorded — including the GROUND ones, which are exactly the ones
  -- the abstract-var argument above does not cover.  `impl Foo (List a)` whose body
  -- calls `debug Bar` records a fully-ground `Debug Bar`; nothing about it is abstract,
  -- the gate would have rejected it on the spot, and the blanket rollback deleted it —
  -- so `check` exited 0 while `build` PANICKED (`no impl of method 'debug' for type
  -- 'Bar'`).  That is a `run_check_agreement` break, and the sentence this comment
  -- replaced ("stays deferred to `build` exactly as before — a residual, not a
  -- regression") named it as a known residual without naming its cost.
  --
  -- The policy is now written down: DICT-SEMANTICS §4.2 **D1** (a predicate the gate can
  -- decide where it is recorded is discharged there — no window may discard it) and
  -- **D6(b)** (a window that exists to suppress D3 false positives must filter by what is
  -- DECIDABLE, not discard wholesale).  So: window as before, then re-push exactly the
  -- obligations `uOblIsDecidableNow` accepts.  The abstract element tyvar of a parametric
  -- head is decidable by nothing, so every false positive the window was built to stop is
  -- still stopped.
  --
  -- ⚠️ The predicate is "the GATE can decide it now", NOT "it is ground" — those differ,
  -- and this site is where believing otherwise costs a verdict.  `uOblIsDecidableNow`
  -- carries the derivation and the counterexample (`Debug (Int -> Int)`); read it before
  -- touching either side.
  -- Re-pushed in `reverseL` order because `wWindow` yields newest-first (items are
  -- consed): reversing restores the original record order, which the gate reports in.
  let implOblsSnap = wSnapshot env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let callSnap = wSnapshot env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls
  let _ =
    inferImplBodies
      env
      rpNames
      ce
      cur
      (filterList (i => implHeadParametric (snd i)) impls)
  let keptImpl =
    filterList
      (uOblIsDecidableNow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph)
      (wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls (snd implOblsSnap))
  let keptCall =
    filterList
      (uOblIsDecidableNow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph)
      (wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls (snd callSnap))
  let _ = wRestore env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls implOblsSnap
  let _ = wRestore env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls callSnap
  let _ = wPushAll env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls (reverseL keptImpl)
  let _ = wPushAll env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls (reverseL keptCall)
  ()

-- True for a DImpl whose head types carry NO type variable (a monomorphic receiver like
-- `Eq Outer` / `Debug (List Int)`); False for a parametric head (`Eq (List a)`) and every
-- non-impl decl (which contributes no impl body regardless).
implHeadGround : Decl -> Bool
implHeadGround (DAttrib _ d) = implHeadGround d
implHeadGround (DImpl { tys, ... }) = isEmptyL (flatMap tyVarNames tys)
implHeadGround _ = False

-- True for a DImpl whose head types carry AT LEAST ONE type variable (a parametric
-- receiver like `Eq (List a)`); False for a ground head and every non-impl decl.  The
-- exact complement of implHeadGround over DImpl decls, so the two filters partition the
-- impls without double-inferring any (and both skip non-impl decls).
implHeadParametric : Decl -> Bool
implHeadParametric (DAttrib _ d) = implHeadParametric d
implHeadParametric (DImpl { tys, ... }) = isNonEmptyL (flatMap tyVarNames tys)
implHeadParametric _ = False

-- C8b: default-body type-checking runs UNCONDITIONALLY (checks
-- ALL default bodies regardless of whether they carry method-level constraints),
-- on every driver — a driver that skipped the unconstrained defaults
-- (Ord.lt/gt/min/max, Foldable.length/isEmpty, Filterable.filter, …) would
-- silently accept a bad default body.  The constrained branch still registers dict slots (needed
-- for the emit/dict path); the unconstrained branch only type-checks — safe on
-- the plain-check path (activeDictVars mutation is harmless; reset by `freshModuleCtx`).
inferDefaultBodiesIfEnabled : TcEnv -> List Decl -> Unit
inferDefaultBodiesIfEnabled env prog = inferDefaultBodies env prog

inferDefaultBodies : TcEnv -> List Decl -> Unit
inferDefaultBodies env [] = ()
inferDefaultBodies env (d :: rest) =
  let _ = inferOneIfaceDefaults env d
  inferDefaultBodies env rest

inferOneIfaceDefaults : TcEnv -> Decl -> Unit
inferOneIfaceDefaults env (DAttrib _ d) = inferOneIfaceDefaults env d
-- Type each default body against the
-- interface's OWN method scheme (built from [typarams]+[methods]), NOT
-- `lookupVar env mname`.  On the flat single-file check path a user top-level
-- funDef can SHADOW a method name (e.g. map.mdk's `isEmpty : Map k v -> Bool`
-- shadowing Foldable's `isEmpty`); looking the name up in env would instantiate
-- that Map-typed shadow and infer the default `isEmpty t = match toList t`
-- against it, grounding the default body's container var to `Map` — so a default
-- every `Foldable` shares would be typed for ONE container.  The interface scheme is
-- shadow-free.  (Until #2769 gave `Map` a real `impl Foldable`, that grounding also
-- raised a spurious `No impl of Foldable for Map`; the mis-typing is the part that
-- does not depend on which impls happen to exist.)
-- Also extend env with these schemes so PEER-method refs in a default body
-- resolve to the interface methods (oracle's env_with_methods), not user shadows.
inferOneIfaceDefaults env (DInterface { name, typarams, typaramKinds, methods, ifaceOrigin, ... }) =
  -- #822: derived from THIS declaration, not from a name key (declGradedScope), and
  -- threaded down so the default bodies see the same Row slots the schemes were built
  -- with.  Computed ONCE per interface rather than per method.
  let dscope =
    declGradedScope env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph typarams typaramKinds methods
  let ifaceSchemes = methodSchemesPure env.teDyn.dcModule dscope methods
  let iface = IfaceRef { irName = name, irOrigin = ifaceOrigin }
  inferDefaultMethods
    (extendVars env ifaceSchemes)
    iface
    dscope
    typarams
    methods
inferOneIfaceDefaults env _ = ()

inferDefaultMethods : TcEnv ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  List String ->
  List IfaceMethod ->
  Unit
inferDefaultMethods env _ _ _ [] = ()
inferDefaultMethods env iface dscope typarams (m :: rest) =
  let _ = inferDefaultMethod env iface dscope typarams m
  inferDefaultMethods env iface dscope typarams rest

-- C8b: every interface default body is type-checked, constrained or not, by the
-- one method-body driver, against the interface's own signature for the method.
inferDefaultMethod : TcEnv ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  List String ->
  IfaceMethod ->
  Unit
inferDefaultMethod env iface dscope typarams (IfaceMethod mname mty (Some (MethodDefault pats body)) _) =
  inferMethodBody env iface DefaultBody (typarams, mty, dscope) mname pats body
inferDefaultMethod env _ _ _ _ = ()

methodLevelPredicateSlots : ModuleCtx ->
  List String ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List PredicateSlot
methodLevelPredicateSlots mctx typarams (TyConstrained cs t) tvMap =
  flatMap (methodLevelPredicateSlot mctx typarams tvMap) cs
    ++ methodLevelPredicateSlots mctx typarams t tvMap
methodLevelPredicateSlots mctx typarams (TyEffect _ _ t) tvMap =
  methodLevelPredicateSlots mctx typarams t tvMap
methodLevelPredicateSlots mctx _ _ _ = []

methodLevelPredicateSlot : ModuleCtx ->
  List String ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Constraint ->
  List PredicateSlot
methodLevelPredicateSlot mctx typarams tvMap c
  | not (constraintIsMethodLevel typarams c) = []
  | otherwise =
    let args = map (fromAstType mctx tvMap) c.constraintArgs
    [
      PredicateSlot {
        psIface = IfaceRef {
          irName = constraintIface c,
          irOrigin = c.constraintOrigin,
        },
        psArgs = PSArgsKnown args,
        psBoundIds = dedupI (flatMap monoTyvarIds args),
      },
    ]

-- ── PR3 keyed lookups (replace implMatches / implMatchesReceiver / findMatchingImplReqs /
-- implCountForIface).  Each first scans the concrete "iface|tag" bucket, then the iface's
-- headless bucket.  implMatchesU / bucketRecvMatch are EXISTENCE tests, so the
-- concrete-then-headless order is byte-identical to the old flat scan.  findMatchingImplReqsU
-- is first-MATCH and DOES depend on that order — a deliberate soundness/conformance fix,
-- documented on it below. ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- does SOME impl of [iface] match the concrete dispatch monos [args]? (existence)
implMatchesU : ModuleCtx -> ImplUniverse -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Bool
implMatchesU mctx _ _ [] = False
implMatchesU mctx univ iface (a0 :: rest) =
  bucketArgsMatch
      mctx
      (univConcreteBucket univ iface (headTyconMono a0))
      (a0 :: rest)
    || bucketArgsMatch mctx (univHeadless univ iface) (a0 :: rest)

bucketArgsMatch : ModuleCtx -> List (List Ty, List Require) -> List Mono -> Bool
bucketArgsMatch mctx [] _ = False
bucketArgsMatch mctx ((tys, _) :: rest) args =
  implHeadMatchesArgs mctx tys args || bucketArgsMatch mctx rest args

-- does some impl in the bucket have a RECEIVER (first head type) matching the single
-- dispatch mono [dm]?  (the call-obligation path carries only the receiver mono.)
bucketRecvMatch : List (List Ty, List Require) -> Mono -> Bool
bucketRecvMatch [] _ = False
bucketRecvMatch ((tys, _) :: rest) dm = match tys
  recv :: _ => match matchTyMono recv dm
    Some _ => True
    None => bucketRecvMatch rest dm
  [] => bucketRecvMatch rest dm

-- the impl of [iface] whose `requires` we must check at a dispatch to [args] (the
-- receiver-head mono [args[0]]), with its (subst, reqs) — the impl checkNestedReqs
-- then discharges.  The concrete RECEIVER-head bucket is consulted BEFORE the iface's
-- headless bucket, so a specific impl always outranks a `impl Foo a` catch-all.
--
-- ⚠️ Coherence ACCEPTS a specific-vs-general overlap (`impl Foo Int` + `impl Foo a`,
-- most-specific-wins), so TWO impls can match one concrete mono.  Selecting the WRONG
-- one's requires is a soundness hole: parametric `impl Foo a` (no reqs) first + concrete
-- `impl Foo Int requires Bar Int` (no `impl Bar`) → an ACCEPT then a runtime null-dict
-- crash, because `foo (3:Int)` dispatches to the MOST-SPECIFIC `impl Foo Int`.
--
-- #326: the within-bucket winner is chosen by the SHARED min⊑ selector — the SAME
-- registry, and the SAME selector, the dispatch ROUTER stamps with (PR #319 fixed the
-- router, this makes the CHECKER agree).  ⚠️ ARCH B-2.1-b2 moved BOTH sides at once:
-- that registry is now `ieSelectRowByIface` over the graph-global `IE`
-- (`bodyImplEnvRef`), not `selectImplEntryByIface` over the topological-prefix
-- `shadowKeyTableRef`.  The checker-agrees-with-router property is what forced the two
-- to move in one bite — see the `B-2.1-b2` block's three-leg header.  It returns the most-specific impl's
-- OWN requires — [] for a no-requires specific `impl Foo (List Int)` sibling declared
-- ALONGSIDE a `impl Foo (List a) requires Show a`, both in the same `List` head bucket —
-- never the general sibling's.  The prior concrete-then-headless first-match ranked
-- concrete-vs-headless correctly but took DECLARATION-ORDER first-match WITHIN a shared
-- head bucket, so `Foo (List Int)` could inherit `List a`'s `Show a` requirement (a false
-- reject/accept).  A non-overlapping receiver head has exactly one match, which
-- pickMostSpecificEntry returns unchanged ⇒ byte-identical to the old first-match.
-- ⚠️ #1128 (F-3b) CORRECTION.  This said "Headless impls carry no head tycon and so
-- are absent from KeyBuckets — the headless bucket fallback (still over the
-- ImplUniverse) covers them."  They are no longer absent: `keyEntryOf` registers a
-- bare-TyVar head under `noneHeadTag` and the candidate scan unions it into every
-- goal-head lookup (`candidateBucket` then; `ieCandidatesForIface`/`…ForMethod` since
-- B-2.1-b2, the former deleted by B-2.1-d), so a HEADLESS winner can be returned
-- directly.  That does not change which impl's requires get discharged — the union
-- goes through the same min⊑ selector, and concrete ⊑ headless strictly at every
-- single-param head, so a concrete match still outranks the catch-all exactly as the
-- "concrete bucket before headless bucket" ordering below did.  What it changes is
-- WHERE the headless answer comes from: the `firstReqMatch (univHeadless …)` fallback
-- is now reached only when the KeyBuckets union has no match at all (e.g. an empty
-- arg list, the arm above).  The fallback is retained rather than deleted because
-- `ImplUniverse` and `KeyBuckets` are populated from different decl sets and this
-- stage is a bug fix, not a registry merge.  ⚠️ `keyEntryOf` and `KeyBuckets` (this whole
-- paragraph's subject) were later deleted outright by `S-keytable-payoff` (`75f4148f`);
-- `findMatchingImplReqsU` below reads `ImplUniverse` only.  This paragraph is kept as the
-- historical record of the #1128 fix it documents, not as a description of the current
-- table.  Regression:
-- test/typecheck_error_fixtures/overlap_specific_req_wins.mdk (concrete-vs-headless) and
-- overlap_same_head_req_wins{,_swapped}.mdk (#326 within-bucket min⊑).
findMatchingImplReqsU : SiteCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option (List (String, Mono), List Require)
findMatchingImplReqsU sx univ iface [] =
  firstReqMatch sx.sxModule (univHeadless univ iface) []
-- 🚨 B-4b-ii SUPPLIES THE IDENTITY HERE — B-4b-i's `ifaceRefBare iface.irName`
-- wrapper is DELETED, and this is the behaviour change that bite deferred.
--
-- WHY THIS SOURCE IS TRUSTWORTHY, stated as a derivation rather than an assertion:
-- `iface` reaches this function from `reqObligationsFor` and `residualPredsOf`, whose
-- own `IfaceRef` is minted by `reqToObligation` off `Require.requireHead` +
-- `Require.requireOrigin` — a carrier `resolve.fillIfaceOccOrigin` stamps from the
-- DECLARING module's `iface:`-tagged scope, under the immunity rule (an occurrence
-- that already carries identity is never re-stamped).  It is NOT taken from
-- `methodEntryHere`, the bare-method-name-keyed table whose own S0s are open;
-- nothing on this path consults it.
--
-- ⚠️ THE TWO LEGS OF THIS FUNCTION DISAGREED, AND THAT IS WHAT THIS FIXES.  The
-- HEADLESS fallback one line below has ALWAYS been identity-keyed — `univHeadless`
-- looks the bucket up through `oblIfaceKey`, i.e. `tabKeyOf NsIface ir.irOrigin
-- ir.irName`, which is `TkIdent` for an origin-bearing interface — while the CONCRETE
-- leg re-minted the query bare and asked a SPELLING question over the same population.
-- One function, two keyings, and the concrete leg is the one tried first.
--
-- MEASURED false reject this removes (hand-derived first, then run): two unrelated
-- modules each declaring `interface Same a`, each with `impl Same (Box a)` — one plain,
-- one `requires Eq a`.  A use of the PLAIN one's method at `Box Opaque` was rejected
-- with *"No impl of Eq for Opaque"*, because the spelling scan reached the OTHER
-- module's row and imposed ITS `requires`.  Swapping the two modules' names made the
-- same program compile: the answer depended on declaration order, which is the
-- signature of a spelling-keyed selection. See `test/dict_fixtures/b4bii-*`.
--
-- ⚠️ ABSENCE IS STILL A WILDCARD, and that is what keeps the flat drivers alive:
-- `sameTyConHead`'s `tyConIdsConflict` answers True only when BOTH origins are
-- identities and they differ, so a single-file `check`/lsp/repl/doc run — which stamps
-- nothing — is unaffected, term for term.  This is NOT `ifaceIdMatches`; see
-- `ieRowIfaceMatches`.
findMatchingImplReqsU sx univ iface (a0 :: rest) =
  match concreteReqMatchByIface sx iface (a0 :: rest)
    Some r => Some r
    None => firstReqMatch sx.sxModule (univHeadless univ iface) (a0 :: rest)

-- #326: the concrete-receiver-head requires match, routed through the shared min⊑
-- selector over the all-impls KeyBuckets registry (the router's `ieSelectRowByIface`
-- selects the SAME entry the SAME way).  Bind the winning
-- impl's typaram vars by matching its FULL head types against [args] (multi-param subst
-- preserved), then hand back that impl's OWN requires.  A selected entry whose full head
-- fails to match [args] yields None, so findMatchingImplReqsU falls through to the
-- headless bucket, mirroring the old scan.
-- #609: select on [args] — the FULL head-mono vector this function already matches
-- the winner's `itys` against two lines down.  Selecting on the receiver alone while
-- substituting against the whole vector was the same split #609 names: the checker
-- saw the vector, the selector saw arg 0.  With one goal for both, a selected entry
-- can no longer fail the subst for a reason the selector could have seen.
concreteReqMatchByIface : SiteCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option (List (String, Mono), List Require)
-- Use `bodyImplEnvRef`, not `shadowKeyTableRef`: the latter is a topological PREFIX,
-- so an impl in a later module contributes no `requires` and the goal reads as
-- unroutable. This is LEG 1 of ARCH B-2.1-b2's coordinated three-leg change; moving
-- only this function alone produces an S0.
concreteReqMatchByIface sx iface args =
  match (ieSelectRowByIface
    sx
    sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
    iface
    args)
    Some row => selectedRowReqMatch sx.sxModule args row
    None => None

firstReqMatch : ModuleCtx ->
  List (List Ty, List Require) ->
  List Mono ->
  Option (List (String, Mono), List Require)
firstReqMatch mctx [] _ = None
firstReqMatch mctx ((tys, reqs) :: rest) args =
  match implHeadSubst mctx tys args
    Some sub => Some (sub, reqs)
    None => firstReqMatch mctx rest args

-- the concrete "iface|tag" bucket (empty when the tag is None / no such impl).
-- A-2.2 (#1111): the GOAL-side head arrives as a `HeadKey` that CAN carry
-- identity — this is the row the concrete bucket's `"<iface>|<tag>"` key is
-- built from, on both sides (`insertUnivImpl` is the impl side; the bucket used to
-- be cited as `obUnivConcreteRef`, retired by #1112 A-3.4 PR2).  The tag is
-- still that key's bare NAME, so every bucket lookup answers exactly as before.
-- A-2.2b (#1111): the `"\{iface}|\{tag}"` string splice is gone — this is a
-- structured two-component key (`RegKey`), so a `|` inside either half can no
-- longer forge the other, and each half carries its namespace.  Both halves are
-- still keyed by SPELLING; `dispHeadTab` derives why.
univConcreteBucket : ImplUniverse ->
  IfaceRef ->
  Option HeadKey ->
  List (List Ty, List Require)
univConcreteBucket (ImplUniverse conc _) iface (Some hk) =
  mregLookupK (regKeyNTab [oblIfaceKey iface, dispHeadTab hk]) conc
univConcreteBucket _ _ None = []

univHeadless : ImplUniverse -> IfaceRef -> List (List Ty, List Require)
univHeadless (ImplUniverse _ hl) iface =
  mregLookupK (regKeyOfTab (oblIfaceKey iface)) hl

-- ── Error-path B4: missing-impl dispatch-obligation check ──────────────────
-- The `No impl of … for …` reject.  For each recorded interface-method occurrence, recover the types the
-- interface params resolved to at this site (dispatchMonosOf), and — ONLY when
-- they are all CONCRETE (a resolved head tycon, no remaining polymorphic var, so
-- a constrained-generic `Ord a =>` site whose receiver is still `a` is correctly
-- deferred to the caller) — verify the program declares a matching impl.  None →
-- `No impl of <iface> for <args>`.
-- #838 I4: the second obligation checker (checkImplObligations/checkImplObligationsU/
-- checkOneImplObligation) is RETIRED — impl obligations now route through the unified
-- checkOneCallObligation (so a rule lands ONCE).
-- #991: the `implOblToU` bridge that used to project a surviving
-- `pendingImplObligations` 5-tuple onto `UObligation` is GONE — both channels store
-- `UObligation` directly.  The projection it performed still happens at CHECK time and
-- in the same place: `uOblArgs`, via the `OpMethodOcc` arm (NOT `oblDispatchMonos`,
-- which special-cases Num → [] and would drop a numeric literal's operand).
-- Improvement, determination and defaulting at each group's close run BEFORE the gate
-- and ground the shared mono cells, so a determined multi-param goal's projected args
-- are already ground here.

-- #11 soundness (native obligation hole): check each constrained-fn CALL site's
-- instantiated obligation.  When `f : C a => …` is applied (`g = f "hello"`),
-- inferDictAtFound recorded (iface, the instantiated constraint mono) here.  After
-- inference the mono is ground: a CONCRETE-head mono (`String`) with no matching impl
-- is an ERROR; a still-polymorphic head (`a`, the obligation propagated to a further-
-- out caller — `id x = x; y = id 5`) is DEFERRED.  Exactly the accept/reject decision
-- of checkOneImplObligation's tail: it checks fun_constraints instantiated at the call.
-- #838 I1: takes `List UObligation` (the ported call channel) instead of the old bare
-- tuple.  Deferral is BYTE-IDENTICAL to before the port — checkOneCallObligation still
-- reads (iface, occs, loc) exactly as it did; only the storage/read shape changed.
-- #838 I4: [deferNonGround] selects the ONE rule that genuinely differs between the two
-- obligation channels this single checker now serves (all GROUND rules — no-prelude-Num,
-- unimplementable-head, function-reject, accept/nested-reqs, reportNumOrNoImpl reframe —
-- are shared, which is the payoff).  False = the CALL channel: a non-ground obligation
-- runs checkUndeterminedObligations (the undetermined-goal verdict).  True = the retired IMPL
-- channel's semantics: a non-ground impl obligation DEFERS unconditionally (old
-- checkOneImplObligation step 7).  This is NOT a mode fork on elaboration — it is the
-- same fact the two checkers always encoded: the impl channel's genuinely-ambiguous
-- subset is caught out-of-band by registerAmbiguousConstraintsOwnedBy (which re-records the
-- escaped-unanchored var as a PCallSlot call obligation → the undetermined-goal verdict), so applying that verdict
-- to the impl channel directly would ALSO reject the benign non-ground impl obligations
-- (prelude interface-method occurrences: a bare receiver var recorded outside any
-- generalized-group-close window, so in neither deferrableVarIds nor the RETPOS pass) —
-- a spurious `Ambiguous instance` on essentially every program.  Adding those vars to
-- deferrableVarIds instead is UNSOUND: it is shared with the call channel's scheme exemption, and
-- the RETPOS-registered ambiguous var must stay OUT of it or the genuine ambiguity would
-- defer too.  So the disposition is per-channel, byte-identical to each retired checker.
-- #838 I4 (S0 fix, PR #863 review): a CHECK-level [dedup] flag used to be the SECOND
-- per-channel fact here — the CALL channel skipped a repeat of an already-checked
-- (iface, every-arg-head-tycon) key, because the SAME call obligation is recorded by
-- more than one path (EVar + EDictAt).  That CHECK-level skip was itself the #1330 S0:
-- a tuple's head tycon is `__tuple2__` regardless of element types, so `Debug (Color,3)`
-- and `Debug (1,2)` shared a key, and skipping the second (a different-verdict sibling)
-- meant its checkNestedReqs `No impl Debug Color` reject never ran → check-green,
-- run-CRASH.  #1330 fixed it by running `checkOneCallObligation` on EVERY obligation on
-- both channels — the flag, the `seen` accumulator threaded to carry it, and the
-- `oblDedupKey` call that fed `seen` were left in place but unread (#1925: removed).
-- The ONLY dedup left is at EMISSION: `checkOneCallObligation`'s `pushTypeErrorOnceAt`
-- collapses two IDENTICAL rendered messages to one report — DICT-SEMANTICS §4.2 OD5.
-- #1925: the CHECK-level dedup key that used to be minted here (`oblDedupKey`,
-- A-2.2b #1111's identity-keyed encoding through `dispKeyRender`/`regKeyNTabAt`) fed
-- only a `seen` accumulator that #1330 (above) left unread — every obligation is
-- checked now, so there is nothing left to key.  Removed along with `oblKeyParts`
-- (its sole helper).  `dispKeyRender`/`dispHeadTab`/`regKeyNTabAt` stay — they are
-- general `types/registry.mdk` machinery with other callers.
checkCallObligationsU : ModuleCtx ->
  Bool ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  List UObligation ->
  Unit
checkCallObligationsU mctx _ _ [] = ()
checkCallObligationsU mctx deferNonGround univ (o :: rest) =
  let iface = o.pred.iface
  -- `uOblArgs`, NOT `o.pred.args`: an impl-channel obligation carries an EMPTY
  -- `pred.args` and projects its dispatch vector at CHECK time (see `OblProjection`).
  -- Reading the field directly makes every method-occurrence obligation inert here —
  -- `checkOneCallObligation` returns on `isEmptyL args` — which is SILENT.  Measured:
  -- with this line reading the field, `test/dict_fixtures/s6-2-t3-closed-goal-reported`
  -- flipped from its `T-AMBIGUOUS-INSTANCE` reject to an ACCEPT printing an
  -- order-decided 1-or-2, and `diff_compiler_dict_semantics_permute`'s
  -- differential was the only thing in the tree that caught it.
  let occs = uOblArgs mctx.mcGraph o
  let loc = o.loc
  let _ = match o.oblProj
    -- The ambiguity rule reads the present positions before the omitted
    -- variables can complete the goal.
    OpExactReturn request =>
      let _ =
        if methodReturnAmbiguousWithoutGiven mctx request then
          pushAmbiguityAt
            mctx
            False
            loc
            (ambiguousImplMsg request.mrrIface.irName)
        else match methodReturnWanted mctx request
          Some _ =>
            consumeExactReturnOutcome
              mctx
              univ
              request
              (solveExactReturnOnce (siteFor mctx) request)
          None =>
            checkOneCallObligation
              mctx
              deferNonGround
              univ
              iface
              occs
              loc
              o.uoScope
      noteMethodReturnTrace mctx MRTChecked request None []
    _ =>
      checkOneCallObligation mctx deferNonGround univ iface occs loc o.uoScope
  let _ = noteNumericObligationChecked mctx.mcGraph o occs
  checkCallObligationsU mctx deferNonGround univ rest

-- The sole production decision for a complete ordinary return.  The request keeps
-- the result so checking and route publication cannot observe different selections.
solveExactReturnOnce : SiteCtx -> MethodReturnRequest -> MethodReturnResolution
solveExactReturnOnce sx request = match request.mrrResolution.value
  Some resolution => resolution
  None =>
    let resolution = solveExactReturn sx request
    request.mrrResolution := Some resolution
    resolution

methodReturnAmbiguousWithoutGiven : ModuleCtx -> MethodReturnRequest -> Bool
methodReturnAmbiguousWithoutGiven mctx request =
  methodPredicateTemplateHasAbsent request.mrrPredicateTemplate
    && isNone
      (uniqueMethodTemplateGiven
        mctx.mcGraph
        request.mrrPredicateTemplate
        request.mrrScope
        (givensForScope mctx.mcGraph request.mrrScope))
    && methodPredicateTemplateCandidateCount
        request.mrrPredicateTemplate
        (ieRowsAll mctx.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value)
        0
      >= 2

methodPredicateTemplateHasAbsent : MethodPredicateTemplate -> Bool
methodPredicateTemplateHasAbsent template =
  anyListM isNone template.mptArguments

methodPredicateTemplateCandidateCount : MethodPredicateTemplate ->
  List ImplRow ->
  Int ->
  Int
methodPredicateTemplateCandidateCount _ _ count
  | count >= 2 = count
methodPredicateTemplateCandidateCount _ [] count = count
methodPredicateTemplateCandidateCount template (row :: rest) count = methodPredicateTemplateCandidateCount
  template
  rest
  (if methodPredicateTemplateMatchesRow template row then count + 1 else count)

methodPredicateTemplateMatchesRow : MethodPredicateTemplate -> ImplRow -> Bool
methodPredicateTemplateMatchesRow template (ImplRow _ _ iface tys _ _ _) =
  sameIfaceDecl template.mptInterface iface
    && (match methodPredicateTemplateHeadPairs template.mptArguments tys
      Some pairs =>
        let subst = Ref []
        isSome (matchOneSided matchStep eqStr (matchEqMono subst) pairs [])
      None => False)

methodPredicateTemplateHeadPairs : List (Option Mono) ->
  List Ty ->
  Option (List (Ty, Mono))
methodPredicateTemplateHeadPairs [] [] = Some []
methodPredicateTemplateHeadPairs ((Some argument) :: rest) (head :: heads) =
  map ((head, argument) :: _) (methodPredicateTemplateHeadPairs rest heads)
methodPredicateTemplateHeadPairs (None :: rest) (_ :: heads) =
  methodPredicateTemplateHeadPairs rest heads
methodPredicateTemplateHeadPairs _ _ = None

solveExactReturn : SiteCtx -> MethodReturnRequest -> MethodReturnResolution
solveExactReturn sx request = match methodReturnWanted sx.sxModule request
  None => panic "complete return solver received a legacy request"
  Some wanted =>
    let predicate = wanted.predicate
    let args = map normalize predicate.predicateArguments
    let predRequest = PredicateRequest {
      prIface = predicate.predicateInterface,
      prArgs = PSArgsKnown args,
    }
    let resultMono = stripArrows request.mrrOccurrence
    let given =
      orElseOpt
        (activeDictVarOfEncl
          sx.sxModule
          (Some predRequest)
          resultMono
          request.mrrEnclosing
          wanted.scope)
        (activeDictPredOf
          sx.sxModule.mcGraph
          predRequest
          resultMono
          wanted.scope)
    match given
      Some answer =>
        let _ = noteAssumption sx.sxModule.mcGraph wanted.scope answer
        MethodReturnResolution {
          mrrWanted = wanted,
          mrrOutcome = Solved (assumAnswerEvidence answer),
          mrrSelectedRow = None,
        }
      None => solveExactReturnInstance sx request wanted args

solveExactReturnInstance : SiteCtx ->
  MethodReturnRequest ->
  Wanted ->
  List Mono ->
  MethodReturnResolution
solveExactReturnInstance sx request wanted [] = MethodReturnResolution {
  mrrWanted = wanted,
  mrrOutcome = Deferred wanted [BlockingFinalization],
  mrrSelectedRow = None,
}
solveExactReturnInstance sx request wanted args =
  let env = sx.sxModule.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
  let iface = wanted.predicate.predicateInterface
  let selected =
    orElseOpt
      (ieSelectRowByIface sx env iface args)
      (determinedGoalInstance sx.sxModule iface args)
  match selected
    Some (row@(ImplRow _ inst selectedIface _ _ _ _)) =>
      let prerequisites = methodReturnPrerequisites sx.sxModule args row
      MethodReturnResolution {
        mrrWanted = wanted,
        mrrOutcome =
          Solved
            (InstanceEvidence
              (RequestInstanceId (instRefSeq inst))
              args
              prerequisites
              (instanceSuperEvidence sx.sxModule.mcGraph selectedIface args)),
        mrrSelectedRow = Some row,
      }
    None =>
      let outcome =
        if exactReturnDefers sx.sxModule wanted args then
          Deferred wanted (exactReturnBlockers args)
        else
          Insoluble wanted MissingInstance
      MethodReturnResolution {
        mrrWanted = wanted,
        mrrOutcome = outcome,
        mrrSelectedRow = None,
      }

exactReturnDefers : ModuleCtx -> Wanted -> List Mono -> Bool
exactReturnDefers mctx wanted args =
  wanted.predicate.predicateInterface.irName == "Num"
      && not (builtinClassPresent mctx.mcGraph BNum)
    || not (allConcreteHeads args)
    || goalDefersOpenWorld
      mctx
      wanted.scope
      wanted.predicate.predicateInterface
      args

exactReturnBlockers : List Mono -> List SolverBlocker
exactReturnBlockers args =
  map BlockingTypeVariable (flatMap monoUnboundIds args)

methodReturnPrerequisites : ModuleCtx ->
  List Mono ->
  ImplRow ->
  List PrerequisiteEvidence
methodReturnPrerequisites mctx args row =
  match selectedRowReqMatch mctx args row
    Some (subst, reqs) =>
      map prerequisiteEvidence (map (reqToObligation mctx subst) reqs)
    None => []

-- The direct supers of [iface] at [args], as the predicates a dictionary for that
-- goal carries in its super segment (declaration order).
instanceSuperEvidence : GraphCtx -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> List SuperEvidence
instanceSuperEvidence gctx iface args =
  map
    ((superIface, superArgs) => SuperEvidence {
      superInterface = superIface,
      superArguments = optionOr [] superArgs,
    })
    (directSuperGoals gctx iface args)

-- Each direct super of [iface] at the goal vector [goals], in declaration order, with
-- its argument vector — `None` when a super parameter does not resolve against the
-- goal (a shorter-than-declared vector).  One entry per declared super, always, so
-- a super's position in this list is its index in every dictionary of [iface].
directSuperGoals : GraphCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  List (IfaceRef, Option (List Mono))
directSuperGoals gctx iface goals = match superLookup gctx iface
  None => []
  Some (typarams, supers) =>
    map
      (sup => (
        superIfaceRef sup,
        if listLen goals == listLen typarams then
          mapAll (p => lookupPos p typarams goals) (superParamsOf sup)
        else
          None,
      ))
      supers

superParamsOf : Super -> List String
superParamsOf (Super { superParams = params, ... }) = params

prerequisiteEvidence : (IfaceRef, List Mono) -> PrerequisiteEvidence
prerequisiteEvidence (iface, args) = PrerequisiteEvidence {
  prerequisiteInterface = iface,
  prerequisiteArguments = args,
}

consumeExactReturnOutcome : ModuleCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  MethodReturnRequest ->
  MethodReturnResolution ->
  Unit
consumeExactReturnOutcome mctx univ request resolution =
  if not (methodReturnResolutionValid mctx request resolution) then
    panic "ordinary return solver outcome failed validation"
  else match resolution.mrrOutcome
    Solved (GivenEvidence _) => ()
    Solved (InstanceEvidence _ _ prerequisites _) =>
      checkReqObligations
        (siteFor mctx)
        univ
        (reqWalkSeed
          resolution.mrrWanted.predicate.predicateInterface
          resolution.mrrWanted.predicate.predicateArguments)
        request.mrrLoc
        request.mrrScope
        (map prerequisiteObligation prerequisites)
    Solved (SuperclassEvidence _ _) => ()
    Deferred _ _ => ()
    Insoluble wanted MissingInstance =>
      pushNoImplError
        mctx
        wanted.predicate.predicateInterface.irName
        request.mrrLoc
        wanted.predicate.predicateArguments
    Insoluble _ (AmbiguousInstances _) =>
      panic "ordinary return solver produced an unrendered ambiguity"
    Insoluble _ (ResolutionCycle _) =>
      panic "ordinary return solver produced an unrendered cycle"

prerequisiteObligation : PrerequisiteEvidence -> (IfaceRef, List Mono)
prerequisiteObligation prerequisite = (
  prerequisite.prerequisiteInterface,
  prerequisite.prerequisiteArguments,
)

methodReturnResolutionValid : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodReturnRequest ->
  MethodReturnResolution ->
  Bool
methodReturnResolutionValid mctx request resolution =
  methodReturnWantedMatches mctx request resolution.mrrWanted
    && (match (resolution.mrrOutcome, resolution.mrrSelectedRow)
      (Solved (GivenEvidence _), None) => True
      (Solved (SuperclassEvidence parent path), None) =>
        match projectedGivenOf mctx.mcGraph parent path
          Some g =>
            predicateRequestMatchesSlot
              PredicateRequest {
                prIface = resolution.mrrWanted.predicate.predicateInterface,
                prArgs =
                  PSArgsKnown resolution.mrrWanted.predicate.predicateArguments,
              }
              g.geSlot
          None => False
      (Solved (InstanceEvidence identity args prerequisites _), Some row) =>
        methodReturnInstanceMatches identity row
          && monoVecSameGiven
            args
            resolution.mrrWanted.predicate.predicateArguments
          && methodReturnPrerequisitesMatch
            prerequisites
            (methodReturnPrerequisites mctx args row)
      (Deferred wanted _, None) => wantedMatches wanted resolution.mrrWanted
      (Insoluble wanted _, None) => wantedMatches wanted resolution.mrrWanted
      _ => False)

methodReturnWantedMatches : ModuleCtx -> MethodReturnRequest -> Wanted -> Bool
methodReturnWantedMatches mctx request wanted =
  match methodReturnWanted mctx request
    Some carried => wantedMatches carried wanted
    None => False

wantedMatches : Wanted -> Wanted -> Bool
wantedMatches left right =
  left.id == right.id
    && sameTraceEvId left.destination right.destination
    && left.scope == right.scope
    && sameIfaceDecl
      left.predicate.predicateInterface
      right.predicate.predicateInterface
    && monoVecSameGiven
      left.predicate.predicateArguments
      right.predicate.predicateArguments

methodReturnInstanceMatches : RequestInstanceId -> ImplRow -> Bool
methodReturnInstanceMatches (RequestInstanceId identity) (ImplRow _ inst _ _ _ _ _) =
  identity == instRefSeq inst

methodReturnPrerequisitesMatch : List PrerequisiteEvidence ->
  List PrerequisiteEvidence ->
  Bool
methodReturnPrerequisitesMatch [] [] = True
methodReturnPrerequisitesMatch (left :: ls) (right :: rs) =
  sameIfaceDecl left.prerequisiteInterface right.prerequisiteInterface
    && monoVecSameGiven left.prerequisiteArguments right.prerequisiteArguments
    && methodReturnPrerequisitesMatch ls rs
methodReturnPrerequisitesMatch _ _ = False

noteNumericObligationChecked : GraphCtx -> UObligation -> List Mono -> Unit
noteNumericObligationChecked gctx o occs =
  if not (numericPredicateTraceOn gctx ()) then
    ()
  else match (o.prov, o.oblProj)
    (_, OpNumLit _) =>
      noteNumericPredicateTrace
        gctx
        NPTChecked
        ClassPredicate {
          predicateInterface = o.pred.iface,
          predicateArguments = o.pred.args,
        }
        o.uoScope
        o.loc
        None
        None
        []
    (POperator, _) =>
      let predicate = ClassPredicate {
        predicateInterface = o.pred.iface,
        predicateArguments = occs,
      }
      if sameIfaceDecl
        predicate.predicateInterface
        (builtinIfaceRef gctx BNum) then
        noteNumericPredicateTrace
          gctx
          NPTChecked
          predicate
          o.uoScope
          o.loc
          None
          None
          []
    _ => ()

-- [occs] is the predicate's whole argument vector.  At arity 1 the match test stays
-- receiver-only (`oblCallVerdict`, byte-identical to the pre-#607 behaviour: for a 1-param
-- interface the receiver IS the vector).  At arity >= 2 it is implMatchesU, which
-- matches the FULL head vector — the difference between "is there an impl of Ix whose
-- receiver is String" (yes-ish, vacuously) and "is there an impl of Ix for
-- (String, Bool)" (no).
checkOneCallObligation : ModuleCtx ->
  Bool ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
checkOneCallObligation mctx deferNonGround univ iface occs loc scope =
  let args = map normalize occs
  if isEmptyL args then
    ()
  else if iface.irName == "Num" && anyListM numUnimplementableHead args then
    -- ⚠️ P1 (#1446): the three `Num` tests in this checker and in
    -- `undeterminedGoalExempt` stay SPELLING tests, not identity tests against
    -- `builtinIfaceRef BNum`.  They select a DIAGNOSTIC/defaulting policy for the numeric
    -- class, and an identity test would change which programs take these arms the moment a
    -- second `Num` can exist — a behaviour change §7.1 U1 owns, not this re-key.  Today the
    -- two cannot differ: a user redeclaration of a prelude interface name is rejected
    -- outright (`Duplicate interface: Num`).

    pushNoImplError mctx iface.irName loc args
  else if iface.irName == "Num"
    && not (builtinClassPresent mctx.mcGraph BNum) then
    -- #838 I4 (was checkOneImplObligation step 4): no-prelude Num skip.  A grounded
    -- `Num Int` literal in a prelude-free program (bare-HM oracle, the prelude's `Num`
    -- absent) has no `impl Num Int`; without this guard the ground path below reports a
    -- spurious `No impl of Num for Int`, breaking `typecheck_main`/tc_probe oracle parity.
    -- #1539: the PRESENCE half is now `builtinClassPresent BNum` (was `ifaceRegistered
    -- "Num"`), per DICT §8 I7 qualification 4 — see `recordIfaceObligation`.  The SPELLING
    -- half (`iface.irName == "Num"`) deliberately stays a spelling test, exactly as the
    -- ⚠️ note above requires: the two halves ask different questions, and only the
    -- presence half is what #1539 owns.
    ()
  else if not (allConcreteHeads args) then
    -- #838 I4: the ONE per-channel branch (see checkCallObligations).  IMPL channel
    -- (deferNonGround) defers a non-ground obligation unconditionally; the signed-body
    -- coverage census below verifies that its complete predicate is declared.  CALL
    -- channel gives the goal the undetermined-goal verdict.

    if deferNonGround then
      ()
    else
      checkUndeterminedObligations mctx iface args loc scope
  else match oblCallVerdict mctx univ iface args
    -- 🚨 #1867 (S1): A TRUNCATED GOAL IS UNDER-DETERMINED, NOT DECIDABLE HERE.
    -- `recordCallObligations` records one obligation per SHATTERED per-tyvar dict slot,
    -- so a call to `useIx : (Ix a Char, Ix a Bool) => a -> Int` records the 1-ary goal
    -- `Ix Int` — the SECOND parameter of a two-parameter predicate is simply dropped.
    -- Its own header says this is deliberate ("widening this to a joint vector … moves
    -- emitted arity"), and it is: the JOINT obligation for the same predicate is recorded
    -- separately by `declaredSchemeOblsFor`/`declaredOblMixed` and reaches this checker
    -- with the full vector (`Ix Int Bool`, `Ix Int Char`), where it decides correctly.
    -- What was NOT safe is letting the truncated goal ALSO decide.  Below,
    -- `oblCallVerdict` at arity 1 matches on the receiver alone (`bucketRecvMatch`),
    -- so `Ix Int` matches BOTH `impl Ix Int Char` and `impl Ix Int Bool`;
    -- `checkNestedReqs` then poses that 1-ary goal to the min⊑ selector
    -- (`reqObligationsFor` → `findMatchingImplReqsU` → `pickMostSpecificEntry`), which
    -- finds two ⊑-incomparable candidates and reports `T-AMBIGUOUS-INSTANCE`.  MEASURED:
    -- that reject is the whole of #1867 — trace order at the base was
    -- `RECOBL Ix ×2` → `CHKOBL Ix nargs=1 args=Int` → `AMBIGOVERLAP-FIRE ngoals=1 ncands=2`
    -- → `RECERR T-AMBIGUOUS-INSTANCE`, with the correct 2-ary goals checked separately and
    -- silently accepting.  `medaka check` never surfaced it and `run`/`build` rejected the
    -- program unlocated (the #1812 surface).
    -- ⚠️ THE GATE IS "SOME IMPL OF THIS INTERFACE DECLARES MORE HEAD TYPES THAN THE GOAL
    -- CARRIES", not "arity 1".  A genuine 1-parameter interface has no impl head longer
    -- than 1, so this arm cannot fire for it and every existing 1-ary verdict is
    -- byte-identical.  [W-QUIETER] check: nothing goes silent that was decidable here —
    -- the truncated goal was never decidable (it cannot see the dropped argument), and
    -- the joint goal that CAN decide is checked on the same channel.  Negative controls,
    -- all still rejected with a located diagnostic: an unsatisfiable declared context
    -- (`No impl of Ix for Int Bool`), the same with the constraint INFERRED rather than
    -- declared, and a conditional two-parameter instance whose `requires` fails
    -- (`No impl of Tag for Color`, i.e. `checkNestedReqs` still runs — via the joint goal).
    -- Measured firings across `stdlib/list.mdk` and `compiler/driver/medaka_cli.mdk`: 0.
    -- Regression: test/dict_fixtures/s-nary-truncated-goal-not-ambiguous (accept) and
    -- s-nary-truncated-goal-joint-rejects (reject).
    -- ⚡ PERF (#1974): the truncation gate and the match test below read THE SAME two
    -- buckets, so they are answered from ONE pair of lookups (`oblCallVerdict`) rather
    -- than one pair per question.  Each `mregLookupK` is a full tree walk over the
    -- bucket map, and the doubled lookups cost ~70 MB of extra garbage at N=400 modules and ~22% of the whole
    -- `typecheck` stage on `diff_compiler_perf_scaling.sh`'s `modules` shape — enough to
    -- push its TIME arm over the gate's 3.0x-per-doubling ceiling (measured 1.63 s -> 1.28 s
    -- at N=400 with the gate stubbed out).  The VERDICTS are byte-identical: same buckets,
    -- same concrete-then-headless order, same two tests, truncation still asked FIRST and
    -- over BOTH buckets.

    -- truncated goal — defer to the joint obligation (see the block above).
    None => ()
    -- Recurse into a matched CONDITIONAL instance's `requires` (`impl Display (a, b)
    -- requires Display a, Display b`) so an unsatisfied element constraint surfaces
    -- (`main = (Red, 5)` → `No impl of Display for Color`) instead of the head-only
    -- match silently accepting (→ null element dict → SIGSEGV at runtime).
    Some True =>
      checkNestedReqs (siteFor mctx) univ (reqWalkStart ()) iface args loc scope
    Some False => checkOneCallObligationNoImpl mctx iface args loc scope

-- the no-impl tail of `checkOneCallObligation` — reached when the goal is neither a
-- truncation nor matched by any impl.  Extracted verbatim so `oblCallVerdict`'s three
-- verdicts can be a `match` without duplicating it; the two arms below are unchanged.
checkOneCallObligationNoImpl : ModuleCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
checkOneCallObligationNoImpl mctx iface args loc scope =
  -- 🚨 #1939 / #1938 (OPEN WORLD): `allConcreteHeads` IS NOT GROUNDNESS, AND ONLY
  -- GROUNDNESS LICENSES A REJECT HERE.  It asks whether every argument has a head
  -- TYCON, which `Wrap a` satisfies while still carrying a variable — so a goal like
  -- `Tag (Wrap a)` walks past the defer gate above and is refuted against the impls of
  -- THIS load graph, which never contains the module's dependents.  This is the SAME
  -- closed-world reading `residualRefutableNow` carries, reached by the other channel,
  -- and it owns the SINGLE-PARAMETER half of both issues (a 1-ary goal is discharged
  -- here; the mixed/n-ary vector goes out as a residual).  MEASURED at slice 1's head
  -- `7941e5fe` with `residualRefutableNow` already fixed:
  --   * `f : Tag (Wrap a) => Wrap a -> String ; f x = tag x` — declared, never called,
  --     legal — still rejected at its own definition.
  --   * `medaka check lib.mdk`, where `lib` infers `Tag (Wrap α)` for
  --     `describe x = tag (Wrap x)` and the satisfying `impl Tag (Wrap Int)` lives in a
  --     module that IMPORTS `lib` — still rejected.
  -- ⚠️ THE GATE IS FIVE CONJUNCTS AND EACH ONE IS PAID FOR.  Bare openness is not
  -- enough.  The three below are slice 2's; the LANDING-SITE pair the fix round added
  -- (review S0-1 / S0-2 / S2-5) is derived on `goalDefersOpenWorld`'s own header, where
  -- the three exit-0 type-confused-dict programs they refuse are written out:
  --   * `monoVectorClosed` — a closed goal cannot instantiate further, so its verdict
  --     is the one the use site would reach anyway.  Keep rejecting those.
  --   * `monoHeadIsDecl` — §8 I6.1's rigid-variable forgery.  `headTyconMono` hands a
  --     bare `TRigid n` out as `HkRigid n`, so `allConcreteHeads` reads `Q zzz` (an
  --     UNDECLARED data-field variable, quantified by nothing) as concrete.  Without
  --     this conjunct that program becomes a SILENT ACCEPT — MEASURED: `check` exit 0,
  --     0 errors, on `test/typecheck_error_fixtures/rigid_mono_head_key.mdk`, whose
  --     golden is exactly this reject.  [W-QUIETER]: that is a severity INCREASE, not
  --     a fix, and it is the reason this arm is not the one-line `not
  --     (monoVectorClosed args)`.
  --   * `deferrableVarIds` — the scheme exemption's own test, one arm up in
  --     `undeterminedGoalExempt`: a goal whose variables NO enclosing scheme
  --     quantifies has nowhere to defer TO, and dropping it would green a program the
  --     emitter builds a null dict for.  ⚠️ A DECLARED CONTEXT'S VARIABLES ARE NOT
  --     `TRigid` AT THIS SITE — MEASURED: `g : Tag (Wrap a) => …` reaches here carrying
  --     `Tag (Wrap TVar#736)`, an ordinary unbound cell, so this test is a REAL one for
  --     the declared channel and passes because the id genuinely is deferrable.  (The
  --     end-of-sprint review's S0-2 asserted the opposite and called this conjunct
  --     vacuous for a declared context; it is vacuous only for a goal whose openness is
  --     ALL rigid — S2-5's nested-rigid shape, which conjunct 3 now covers.)
  if goalDefersOpenWorld mctx scope iface args then
    ()
  else if anyIn
    (flatMap monoUnboundIds args)
    mctx.mcCells.poisonedVars.value then
    -- A variable of the goal is one an earlier diagnostic explained.
    ()
  else
    -- #838 I4 (was checkOneImplObligation step 9): reportNumOrNoImpl is a strict superset
    -- of pushNoImplError — it reframes a ground `Num`-obligation tracing to a numeric
    -- LITERAL (loc-keyed `numlitReframeLoc`, not prov-keyed) into `T-TYPE-MISMATCH`, and
    -- degrades to pushNoImplError verbatim for any non-literal (every call obligation) —
    -- so this restores the impl channel's literal-mismatch diagnostic quality byte-for-byte.

    reportNumOrNoImpl mctx iface.irName args loc

-- #1867 + PERF (#1974): the ONE call-obligation verdict, answered from ONE pair of
-- bucket lookups.  It fuses two questions over THE SAME buckets, the truncation test
-- and the match test, which asked separately would each re-mint (and re-RENDER, see
-- `insertUnivImplAt`) its registry key:
--   `None`       — the goal is a TRUNCATION of a k-parameter predicate, k > its own
--                  arity: some impl of [iface] this goal could reach declares more head
--                  types than the goal carries.  Scoped to arity 1 because that is the
--                  only truncation any producer mints — `recordCallObligations` shatters
--                  a predicate into ONE obligation per dict slot, each carrying a single
--                  mono; every other goal on this channel is a whole vector.  See
--                  `checkOneCallObligation`'s block for the verdict this decides and why
--                  deferring is not a [W-QUIETER] regression.
--   `Some True`  — some impl matches (receiver-only at arity 1, full head vector above).
--   `Some False` — no impl matches.
-- ⚠️ ORDER IS SEMANTIC AND UNCHANGED.  The truncation question is still asked FIRST and
-- over BOTH buckets (concrete receiver-head bucket, then the iface's headless bucket) —
-- a goal that is truncated defers even when the concrete bucket would have matched it.
-- The headless bucket is still read only when the concrete one did not already answer
-- "truncated", exactly as the old `||` short-circuited; it is then REUSED by the match
-- test instead of being looked up again.  No third universe, no new registry read.
oblCallVerdict : ModuleCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Bool
oblCallVerdict mctx univ iface [a0] =
  let cb = univConcreteBucket univ iface (headTyconMono a0)
  if bucketAnyLonger cb 1 then
    None
  else
    let hb = univHeadless univ iface
    if bucketAnyLonger hb 1 then
      None
    else
      Some (bucketRecvMatch cb a0 || bucketRecvMatch hb a0)
oblCallVerdict mctx univ iface args = Some (implMatchesU mctx univ iface args)

bucketAnyLonger : List (List Ty, List Require) -> Int -> Bool
bucketAnyLonger [] _ = False
bucketAnyLonger ((tys, _) :: rest) n = listLen tys > n || bucketAnyLonger rest n

-- The verdict on a call-channel goal still open when the module's obligations are
-- checked: the same candidates and the same verdict a boundary gives
-- (`rejectUndeterminedVectors`), for every arity, the module's declared signature
-- variables held rigid.  A goal that the boundary judged reaches the same verdict
-- here, and the diagnostic folds on its span; a goal no boundary's window held
-- gets it here.  No impl of the interface that unifies with the goal is
-- `T-NO-IMPL`; one is the instance; two or more with no stable minimum is
-- `T-AMBIGUOUS-INSTANCE`.  That verdict depends on the goal alone, not on whether
-- the callee's body reads the dictionary.
checkUndeterminedObligations : ModuleCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
checkUndeterminedObligations mctx iface args loc scope =
  let rigidIds = mctx.mcCells.declaredSigVarIds.value
  if not (undeterminedGoalExempt mctx iface args scope)
    && isEmptyL (sigCellsOf rigidIds (flatMap monoVarCells args)) then
    reportUndeterminedGoal
      mctx
      rigidIds
      (goalWindowOf mctx.mcGraph [])
      iface
      args
      loc

-- PLAN.md #11: after HM + defaulting every source integer literal's type var is
-- ground (or a genuine `Num a` survivor).  Decide each literal's runtime rep
-- (3-way):
--   • ground Float ⇒ stamp the float cell + CLEAR the fromInt route (dref RNone) ⇒
--     dictPass emits `ELit (LFloat f)` (eval is value-tagged; eval_arith rejects
--     mixed int/float tags, so a Float literal must carry a real float).
--   • ground Int (incl. via ambiguous→Int defaulting) ⇒ clear both cells ⇒
--     `ELit (LInt n)`, no dict dispatch.
--   • NOT a primitive head (a still-polymorphic `Num a` — the soundness case, `1`
--     in `inc x = x + 1` — or an exotic user numeric type) ⇒ leave [dref]'s
--     resolveSites-stamped route in place ⇒ dictPass emits
--     `EApp (EMethodAt "fromInt" …) (ELit (LInt n))` so the literal dispatches
--     through the runtime Num dict (Int→identity, Float→intToFloat).  A dref left
--     RNone (route never filled, e.g. unreachable position) falls to Int below.
-- Reads numlitRefs (populated by inferNumLit during THIS run/module's inference).
setNumlitFloatsGo : List (Mono, Ref (Option Float), Int, Ref Route) -> Unit
setNumlitFloatsGo [] = ()
setNumlitFloatsGo ((var, fref, n, dref) :: rest) =
  let _ = match normalize var
    TCon "Float" _ =>
      fref := Some (intToFloat n)
      dref := RNone
    TCon "Int" _ => dref := RNone
    _ => ()
  setNumlitFloatsGo rest

-- Impl-based improvement (DICT-SEMANTICS §3 "Improvement by the one matching
-- instance"): when the head matcher (`implHeadSubst`) accepts a goal by binding
-- the goal's own free variables through a repeated head variable, and that
-- instance is the only one of the interface whose head unifies with the goal,
-- the binding is committed, so selection sees the goal the instance determined.
-- `Pick (List t) (List Int) (List Int)` against the only instance `impl Pick a a a`
-- fixes `t = Int`.  A second instance that unifies with the goal (an overlap,
-- including one a later binding of a goal variable would make match) or none
-- leaves the goal as it is.
--
-- It runs at a top-level binding group's close (`processSCC`) and at a method
-- body's (`inferMethodBody`), before that boundary's Num defaulting and once more
-- after it, each time ahead of
-- `determineByUniqueInstance`, which commits a goal to its one unifying instance
-- even where no repeated head variable ties the goal to itself.  A local boundary
-- runs it once, before its Num defaulting (`improveLocalGoals`).
--
-- [sigIds] are the group's declared-signature variables still free at its close
-- (at a method body, its instance head's and declared signature's variables).
-- The commit never binds one: they take part as constants, and a goal that would
-- need one bound is left as it is, for `checkSigsTooGeneral` has already run.
improveByUniqueImpl : DynCtx -> OrdMap Unit -> List UObligation -> Unit
improveByUniqueImpl dyn _ [] = ()
improveByUniqueImpl dyn sigIds (o :: rest) =
  let _ =
    improveGoal
      dyn
      sigIds
      o.pred.iface
      (map normalize (uOblArgs dyn.dcModule.mcGraph o))
  improveByUniqueImpl dyn sigIds rest

-- Determination by the unique unifying instance (DICT-SEMANTICS §3, the settle
-- sequence's second step).  A goal of any arity that is not closed is unified with
-- a fresh instance of the one instance head that unifies with it, every variable in
-- [rigidIds] held rigid.  [rigidIds] are the variables the boundary does not own:
-- at a group, the declared signatures' variables and the variables in an argument
-- position of a member's type; at a method body, the instance head's and declared
-- signature's.  Any other variable of the goal is the boundary's, and the unique
-- instance is the only type the program can have there.
--
-- The candidates are `goalCandidates`', kept only if a commit leaves every sibling
-- goal on a variable it binds satisfiable: a sibling the commit closes must have an
-- instance in the table.  A projection of a wider goal is not determined: the
-- positions it drops can still tell its candidates apart.
--
-- Sweeps repeat until one commits nothing, so a goal that another goal's commit
-- makes unique is determined in the same pass whatever order the window lists
-- them in.  What stays open gets its verdict from `rejectUndeterminedVectors`.
determineByUniqueInstance : ModuleCtx -> OrdMap Unit -> List UObligation -> Unit
determineByUniqueInstance mctx rigidIds obls =
  if isNonEmptyL obls then
    determineSweeps
      mctx
      rigidIds
      (goalWindowOf mctx.mcGraph obls)
      (listLen obls + 1)

-- The fuel only bounds the loop: every sweep but the last changes some goal's
-- shape.
determineSweeps : ModuleCtx -> OrdMap Unit -> GoalWindow -> Int -> Unit
determineSweeps mctx rigidIds window fuel =
  if fuel > 0
    && determineByUniqueInstanceGo
      mctx
      rigidIds
      window
      False
      window.gwGoals then
    determineSweeps mctx rigidIds window (fuel - 1)

-- One sweep over the window; True when some goal took its instance's shape.
determineByUniqueInstanceGo : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  GoalWindow ->
  Bool ->
  List (Int, UObligation) ->
  Bool
determineByUniqueInstanceGo mctx _ _ changed [] = changed
determineByUniqueInstanceGo mctx rigidIds window changed ((_, o) :: rest) =
  let args = map normalize (uOblArgs mctx.mcGraph o)
  let now = determineGoal mctx rigidIds window o args
  determineByUniqueInstanceGo mctx rigidIds window (now || changed) rest

-- True when the commit changed the goal's shape.  A commit that only renames the
-- goal's variables to the instance's fresh ones leaves the goal's size and its
-- count of distinct variables as they were; the window is re-filed either way,
-- since the goal's variables are no longer the ones it was filed under.
determineGoal : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  GoalWindow ->
  UObligation ->
  List Mono ->
  Bool
determineGoal mctx rigidIds0 window o args =
  let rigidIds = withDeclaredVars mctx rigidIds0 args
  determineHeldGoal mctx rigidIds window o args

-- [rigidIds] plus each variable of [args] a closed binder declared: determination
-- commits a binding, and a declared variable is rigid in every matcher that does.
withDeclaredVars : ModuleCtx -> OrdMap Unit -> List Mono -> OrdMap Unit
withDeclaredVars mctx rigidIds args =
  let declared = mctx.mcCells.declaredSigVarIds.value
  omFromNames
    (filterList
      (k => omHasKey k declared)
      (map intToString (flatMap monoUnboundIds args)))
    rigidIds

determineHeldGoal : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  GoalWindow ->
  UObligation ->
  List Mono ->
  Bool
determineHeldGoal mctx rigidIds window o args
  | monoVectorClosed args || goalVarsAllHeld rigidIds args = False
  | otherwise =
    let rows = goalRows mctx o.pred.iface args
    let unifying =
      if goalIsProjection args rows then
        []
      else
        goalCandidates mctx rigidIds args rows
    match determinationCandidates mctx window args unifying
      [(row, _)] =>
        let oldIds = dedupI (flatMap monoUnboundIds args)
        let sizeBefore = monoSizes args
        -- Minted inside the boundary's level: a goal variable unified with one
        -- of these keeps its level and still generalizes.
        let _ = enterLevel mctx ()
        let heads = freshRowHeads mctx row
        let _ = exitLevel mctx ()
        let _ = commitImprovement (dynFor mctx) rigidIds (zipL args heads)
        let _ = fileDeterminedRow mctx row args
        let _ = refileGoals mctx.mcGraph window oldIds
        monoSizes args /= sizeBefore
          || listLen (dedupI (flatMap monoUnboundIds args)) /= listLen oldIds
      _ => False

determinedEntryAnswers : IfaceRef -> List Mono -> (ImplRow, List Mono) -> Bool
determinedEntryAnswers iface goals (row, committed) =
  ieRowOfIface iface row
    && listLen committed == listLen goals
    && allList (pair => cohEqMono (fst pair) (snd pair)) (zipL committed goals)

-- Files a commit's instance under the variable heading the committed goal, the
-- one `determinedGoalInstance` reads when selection by head finds nothing.
fileDeterminedRow : ModuleCtx -> ImplRow -> List Mono -> Unit
fileDeterminedRow mctx _ [] = ()
fileDeterminedRow mctx row (first :: rest) = match normalize first
  TVar cell =>
    let table = mctx.mcCells.determinedRowsRef.value
    let filed = optionOr [] (IdMap.get (tyvarId cell) table)
    let entry = (row, map normalize (first :: rest))
    mctx.mcCells.determinedRowsRef :=
      IdMap.set (tyvarId cell) (entry :: filed) table
  _ => ()

-- Files every commit again under the variable now heading its goal.  A later group
-- or module that unified the committed variable moved its representative, and a
-- lookup reads the representative.  Called where the lookups run: the module's end
-- and each module's stamping in the drain.
refileDeterminedRows : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> Unit
refileDeterminedRows mctx _ =
  let table = mctx.mcCells.determinedRowsRef.value
  if not (IdMap.isEmpty table) then
    let entries = reverseL (flatMap identity (IdMap.values table))
    mctx.mcCells.determinedRowsRef := Tip
    fold (_ entry => fileDeterminedRow mctx (fst entry) (snd entry)) () entries

-- Every variable of the goal is one the boundary holds rigid, so a commit could
-- bind none of them.
goalVarsAllHeld : OrdMap Unit -> List Mono -> Bool
goalVarsAllHeld rigidIds args =
  allList
    (c => omHasKey (intToString (tyvarId c)) rigidIds)
    (flatMap monoVarCells args)

-- The rows of [iface] a goal can unify with: those filed under the goal's first
-- head constructor or under none, or every row of [iface] when the goal's first
-- position is a variable.
goalRows : ModuleCtx -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> List ImplRow
goalRows mctx iface args =
  let env = mctx.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
  let pool = match goalHeadCon args
    Some hk => ieHeadRows (Some hk) env ++ ieHeadRows None env
    None => ieRowsAll env
  filterList (ieRowOfIface iface) pool

-- A goal with fewer positions than some head of its interface is the projection
-- of a wider goal onto its first positions: a per-slot goal `recordCallObligations`
-- shatters a predicate into, or the receiver position of a method occurrence.
goalIsProjection : List Mono -> List ImplRow -> Bool
goalIsProjection args rows =
  anyList (row => listLen (ieRowTys row) > listLen args) rows

-- The instances an undetermined goal can still reach (DICT-SEMANTICS §3): the rows
-- of [rows] whose heads unify with [args], every variable in [rigidIds] held rigid
-- and the instance's variables fresh, each with the substitution that unifies it.
-- Every head shape is unified by its structure: data, tuple, arrow, qualified and
-- variable heads alike.  A projection is unified with each head's first positions,
-- and heads that agree there reach it as one candidate.
goalCandidates : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List Mono ->
  List ImplRow ->
  List (ImplRow, List (Int, Mono))
goalCandidates mctx rigidIds args rows =
  let unifying =
    flatMap
      (row => match rowPrefixSubstRigid mctx rigidIds args row
        Some subst => [(row, subst)]
        None => [])
      rows
  if goalIsProjection args rows then
    distinctPrefixes (listLen args) unifying []
  else
    unifying

-- [row]'s first `listLen args` heads, freshened, unified with [args] in a scratch
-- substitution with every variable in [rigidIds] held rigid.
rowPrefixSubstRigid : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List Mono ->
  ImplRow ->
  Option (List (Int, Mono))
rowPrefixSubstRigid mctx rigidIds args row =
  map
    (scratch => !scratch)
    (headsUnifier mctx.mcGraph rigidIds args (freshRowHeads mctx row))

distinctPrefixes : Int ->
  List (ImplRow, List (Int, Mono)) ->
  List (ImplRow, List (Int, Mono)) ->
  List (ImplRow, List (Int, Mono))
distinctPrefixes _ [] kept = reverseL kept
distinctPrefixes k (cand :: rest) kept =
  let prefix = take k (ieRowTys (fst cand))
  if anyList (seen => tyHeadEqV prefix (take k (ieRowTys (fst seen)))) kept then
    distinctPrefixes k rest kept
  else
    distinctPrefixes k rest (cand :: kept)

-- The candidates that count toward a commitment or an ambiguity: `rowCountsFor`'s,
-- each kept only if its commit leaves every sibling goal on a variable it binds
-- satisfiable.
determinationCandidates : ModuleCtx ->
  GoalWindow ->
  List Mono ->
  List (ImplRow, List (Int, Mono)) ->
  List (ImplRow, List (Int, Mono))
determinationCandidates mctx window args unifying =
  filterList
    (cand =>
      rowCountsFor args (fst cand)
        && siblingsStaySatisfiable mctx window (snd cand))
    unifying

-- The candidates an undetermined goal's verdict counts: `determinationCandidates`,
-- or, when a sibling refutes every one of them, every candidate `rowCountsFor`
-- keeps.  Such a goal has no type that satisfies the boundary's goals together,
-- and its verdict is the one its candidates alone give.
verdictCandidates : ModuleCtx ->
  GoalWindow ->
  List Mono ->
  List (ImplRow, List (Int, Mono)) ->
  List (ImplRow, List (Int, Mono))
verdictCandidates mctx window args unifying =
  match determinationCandidates mctx window args unifying
    [] => filterList (cand => rowCountsFor args (fst cand)) unifying
    counted => counted

goalReach : ModuleCtx ->
  List Mono ->
  List (ImplRow, List (Int, Mono)) ->
  GoalReach
goalReach mctx _ [] = ReachNone
goalReach mctx _ [(row, _)] = ReachOne row
goalReach mctx args cands =
  let rows = map fst cands
  match filterList (row => stableMinimum mctx args rows row) rows
    row :: _ => ReachOne row
    [] => ReachMany

stableMinimum : ModuleCtx -> List Mono -> List ImplRow -> ImplRow -> Bool
stableMinimum mctx args rows row =
  rowHeadMatches mctx args row
    && allList (other => tySubsumesV (ieRowTys other) (ieRowTys row)) rows

-- An undetermined goal no verdict is owed for.  A `Num` goal belongs to literal
-- defaulting (a spelling test, see `checkOneCallObligation`).  A closed goal is
-- the obligation gate's.  A goal whose variable a primary mismatch already
-- explained is not reported twice.  A goal generalization abstracts is the
-- caller's: every free variable in it is quantified by a scheme, the test residual
-- selection admits a predicate into a scheme by (`declaredOblArgOk`).  A goal each
-- argument of which is a forwarded enclosing dictionary's variable, or that a
-- given answers, is answered.
undeterminedGoalExempt : ModuleCtx -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> ScopeId -> Bool
undeterminedGoalExempt mctx iface args scope =
  iface.irName == "Num"
    || monoVectorClosed args
    || anyIn (flatMap monoUnboundIds args) mctx.mcCells.poisonedVars.value
    || allList
      (declaredOblArgOk (i => IdMap.has i mctx.mcCells.deferrableVarIds.value))
      args
    || allList (a => isSome (activeDictVarOf mctx.mcGraph a scope)) args
    || goalGivenAt mctx.mcGraph iface args scope

-- The verdict on an undetermined goal (DICT-SEMANTICS §3, §4.2 OD3).  No unifying
-- instance is `T-NO-IMPL`: no later binding can satisfy it.  Two or more counted
-- candidates with no stable minimum is `T-AMBIGUOUS-INSTANCE`: the goal has no
-- type to choose its dictionary by.  One candidate, or a stable minimum,
-- determines the goal.
reportUndeterminedGoal : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  GoalWindow ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
reportUndeterminedGoal mctx rigidIds window iface args loc =
  match goalCandidates mctx rigidIds args (goalRows mctx iface args)
    [] => reportUndeterminedNoImpl mctx iface args loc
    unifying =>
      match goalReach mctx args (verdictCandidates mctx window args unifying)
        ReachMany =>
          pushBoundaryAmbiguity
            mctx
            rigidIds
            args
            loc
            (ambiguousImplMsg iface.irName)
        _ => ()

-- DIAGNOSTIC-CODES-DESIGN `T-NO-IMPL` for an undetermined goal.  A one-position
-- goal names its interface by its declaring module, so the diagnostic says which
-- of two same-spelled declarations lacks an impl; a vector renders each variable
-- as `_`.
reportUndeterminedNoImpl : ModuleCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
reportUndeterminedNoImpl mctx iface [a] loc =
  pushNoImplError mctx (qualifiedIfaceLabel iface) loc [a]
reportUndeterminedNoImpl mctx iface args loc =
  pushTypeErrorOnceAt
    mctx
    "T-NO-IMPL"
    loc
    (undeterminedNoImplMsg mctx.mcGraph iface.irName args)

-- The verdict on a boundary's goals that determination left open, once the
-- group's schemes are registered.  A goal is this boundary's to judge when it has a
-- variable nothing outside the boundary can bind: not held rigid ([rigidIds], the
-- enclosing scope's), not quantified by a scheme (the caller's), and not in the
-- type of a non-generalized member ([liveIds], which a later group can still
-- ground, §6.2 T2).  Such a goal is judged by `reportUndeterminedGoal` in full,
-- whether a constrained call posed it ([callObls]) or an interface method's own
-- occurrence did ([implObls]): nothing left can give it a type (§6.2 T4).
rejectUndeterminedVectors : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List UObligation ->
  List UObligation ->
  Unit
rejectUndeterminedVectors mctx rigidIds liveIds implObls callObls =
  let obls = implObls ++ callObls
  if isNonEmptyL obls then
    let window = goalWindowOf mctx.mcGraph obls
    fold
      (_ o => undeterminedVectorVerdict mctx rigidIds liveIds window o)
      ()
      obls

-- [window] is the boundary's goal window.  A goal on a live variable waits for
-- quiescence (`judgeQuiescentGoals`) with the boundary's [rigidIds] and [window].
-- So does one whose only open variables the boundary holds, when one of them is live
-- (an argument position of a non-generalized member): no group of the module owns it,
-- and only the graph can still ground it (`judgeLiveGoals`).
undeterminedVectorVerdict : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  GoalWindow ->
  UObligation ->
  Unit
undeterminedVectorVerdict mctx rigidIds liveIds window o =
  let args = map normalize (uOblArgs mctx.mcGraph o)
  let ids = flatMap monoUnboundIds args
  let isLive = i => omHasKey (intToString i) liveIds
  if undeterminedGoalExempt mctx o.pred.iface args o.uoScope then
    ()
  else if anyList (i => boundaryOwnsOpen mctx rigidIds i) ids then
    if anyList isLive ids then
      mctx.mcCells.quiescentGoalsRef :=
        (rigidIds, window, o) :: mctx.mcCells.quiescentGoalsRef.value
    else if isEmptyL (sigCellsOf rigidIds (flatMap monoVarCells args)) then
      reportUndeterminedGoal mctx rigidIds window o.pred.iface args o.loc
    else
      reportMixedGoalAmbiguity mctx rigidIds window o.pred.iface args o.loc
  else if anyList isLive ids then
    mctx.mcCells.heldLiveGoalsRef :=
      (rigidIds, window, o) :: mctx.mcCells.heldLiveGoalsRef.value

-- Records, at the module's end, the variables its non-generalized members still
-- leave open, for the graph-end drain (`GraphRun.liveRoots`).
recordLiveRoots : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> Unit
recordLiveRoots mctx _ =
  let members = mctx.mcCells.liveMemberMonosRef.value
  let liveIds = dedupI (flatMap (liveVarIdsOf mctx) members)
  if isNonEmptyL liveIds then
    let goals =
      mctx.mcCells.implObls.items.value ++ mctx.mcCells.obls.items.value
    let numObls =
      mctx.mcCells.implObls.items.value
        ++ numCallObls mctx.mcGraph mctx.mcCells.obls.items.value
    let numIds =
      filterList (i => containsI i liveIds) (numConstrainedIds numObls)
    let numRoots = filterMap (i => liveNumVarGo i numObls) (dedupI numIds)
    let g = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun
    g.liveRoots :=
      filterMap (findTvarInMonos members) liveIds ++ g.liveRoots.value
    g.liveGoals := reverseL (liveGoalsOf mctx members) ++ g.liveGoals.value
    if isNonEmptyL numRoots then
      g.liveNumRoots := numRoots ++ g.liveNumRoots.value
      g.liveNumGoals :=
        filterList
            (o =>
              anyIn (flatMap monoUnboundIds (uOblArgs mctx.mcGraph o)) numIds)
            goals
          ++ g.liveNumGoals.value

-- The module's held goals that a live root still leaves open, in the order they
-- were held, each under the first of [members] whose type mentions one of its live
-- variables.  A goal a later group grounded is the module's obligation check's.
liveGoalsOf : ModuleCtx -> List Mono -> List LiveGoal
liveGoalsOf mctx members =
  let mid = mctx.mcCells.currentModuleRef.value
  let owners = memberOfIds mctx members
  filterMap
    ((rigidIds, window, o) =>
      let ids = flatMap monoUnboundIds (uOblArgs mctx.mcGraph o)
      map
        (k => LiveGoal {
          lgModule = mid,
          lgBinding = k,
          lgRigidIds =
            fold
              (acc i =>
                if IdMap.has i owners then
                  omDelete (intToString i) acc
                else
                  acc)
              rigidIds
              ids,
          lgWindow = window,
          lgGoal = o,
        })
        (findMap (i => IdMap.get i owners) ids))
    (reverseL mctx.mcCells.heldLiveGoalsRef.value)

-- Each live variable of [members] under the index of the first member whose type
-- mentions it.
memberOfIds : ModuleCtx -> List Mono -> Map Int Int
memberOfIds mctx members =
  fst
    (fold
      ((owners, k) m => (
        fold
          (acc i => if IdMap.has i acc then acc else IdMap.set i k acc)
          owners
          (liveVarIdsOf mctx m),
        k + 1,
      ))
      (Tip, 0)
      members)

-- The verdict on the goals boundaries held for live roots, at the drain, after the
-- live `Num` roots are defaulted: every module has closed, so nothing is left to
-- ground them, and each is judged as its boundary would have judged it had it owned
-- the live variables (DICT-SEMANTICS §6.2 T4, R-SC3), in its own module's context.
-- A binding gets one verdict: the first of its goals that draws one.
judgeLiveGoals : ModuleCtx -> List StampCtx -> List DrainFinding
judgeLiveGoals saved ctxs =
  let g = saved.mcGraph.graphRun
  let goals = reverseL g.liveGoals.value
  g.liveGoals := []
  if isEmptyL goals then
    []
  else
    let byModule = omFromPairs (map (c => (c.scModule, c)) ctxs) omEmpty
    reverseL (fst (fold (judgeLiveGoal saved byModule) ([], omEmpty) goals))

-- [saved] is the record the drain began with, which each entered stamp context takes
-- its drain tables from (`enterStampCtx`).
judgeLiveGoal : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap StampCtx ->
  (List DrainFinding, OrdMap Unit) ->
  LiveGoal ->
  (List DrainFinding, OrdMap Unit)
judgeLiveGoal saved byModule (found, judged) lg =
  let binding = "\{lg.lgModule}\t\{intToString lg.lgBinding}"
  match (omHasKey binding judged, omLookup lg.lgModule byModule)
    (False, Some ctx) =>
      let stamp = enterStampCtx saved ctx
      let rigidIds = lg.lgRigidIds
      let diags = captureTypeErrors stamp (_ =>
        fold
          (_ o =>
            undeterminedVectorVerdict stamp rigidIds omEmpty lg.lgWindow o)
          ()
          (lg.lgGoal :: nestedRequireGoals stamp rigidIds omEmpty [lg.lgGoal]))
      match diags
        [] => (found, judged)
        _ => (
          reverseL (map (verdictFinding lg.lgModule True) diags) ++ found,
          omInsert binding () judged,
        )
    _ => (found, judged)

-- Quiescence defaulting (DICT-SEMANTICS §6.3 D1, §6.2 T4): a live `Num` root no
-- module of the graph grounded defaults to `Int`, unless D3 clause 3 withholds it.
-- Every group of every module has closed, so no channel is left to determine it.
defaultLiveNumRoots : ModuleCtx -> Unit
defaultLiveNumRoots mctx =
  let g = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun
  let roots = g.liveNumRoots.value
  if isNonEmptyL roots then
    let guard = armNumGuard mctx.mcGraph NumGuard {
      ngGoals = g.liveNumGoals.value,
      ngRigidIds = omEmpty,
      ngOuterBelow = None,
    }
    fold
      (_ m => match normalize m
        TVar cell => groundOrWithhold (dynFor mctx) guard (tyvarId cell) m
        _ => ())
      ()
      roots
  g.liveRoots := []
  g.liveNumRoots := []
  g.liveNumGoals := []

-- The verdict on the goals boundaries left to quiescence, once every group of the
-- module has closed: no later group is left to ground their variables, so each is
-- judged as its boundary would have judged it, and so are the prerequisites its
-- boundary left to this point (`nestedRequireGoals`).
judgeQuiescentGoals : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> Unit
judgeQuiescentGoals mctx _ =
  let goals = reverseL mctx.mcCells.quiescentGoalsRef.value
  mctx.mcCells.quiescentGoalsRef := []
  fold
    (_ (rigidIds, window, o) =>
      fold
        (_ g => undeterminedVectorVerdict mctx rigidIds omEmpty window g)
        ()
        (o :: nestedRequireGoals mctx rigidIds omEmpty [o]))
    ()
    goals

-- A goal that mentions both a rigid variable and one only this boundary could have
-- fixed.  Whatever the enclosing scope instantiates the rigid variable to, the
-- other stays open, so two or more instances reachable under some instantiation
-- with no stable minimum is `T-AMBIGUOUS-INSTANCE` (§6.2 T4).  Fewer is left
-- unjudged here: whether the rigid variable can take that instance's type is the
-- impl-body and signature checks' question.
reportMixedGoalAmbiguity : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  GoalWindow ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
reportMixedGoalAmbiguity mctx rigidIds window iface args loc =
  let unifying = goalCandidates mctx omEmpty args (goalRows mctx iface args)
  match goalReach mctx args (verdictCandidates mctx window args unifying)
    ReachMany =>
      pushBoundaryAmbiguity
        mctx
        rigidIds
        args
        loc
        (ambiguousImplMsg iface.irName)
    _ => ()

-- The variables a later group can still ground (§6.2 T2): those no scheme
-- quantifies in the types of this group's members [monos] and of every earlier
-- top-level member of the module.  The members that still carry one are kept for
-- the groups after this one; a member grounded since is dropped.
liveMemberIds : ModuleCtx -> List Mono -> OrdMap Unit
liveMemberIds mctx monos =
  let open =
    filterList
      (m => isNonEmptyL (liveVarIdsOf mctx m))
      (monos ++ mctx.mcCells.liveMemberMonosRef.value)
  mctx.mcCells.liveMemberMonosRef := open
  omFromNames
    (map intToString (dedupI (flatMap (liveVarIdsOf mctx) open)))
    omEmpty

liveVarIdsOf : ModuleCtx -> Mono -> List Int
liveVarIdsOf mctx m =
  filterList
