    (i => not (IdMap.has i mctx.mcCells.deferrableVarIds.value))
    (monoUnboundIds m)

-- The prerequisites of the instances [obls]' goals select, as goals of the same
-- boundary at their parents' sites (DICT-SEMANTICS §3).  An instance answers a goal
-- only once its `requires` is answered too, so a prerequisite left open is judged
-- like a goal the boundary posed itself.  It is not determined: an open sibling
-- refutes no candidate, so a commit through a prerequisite could choose a
-- structural instance whose open sibling no instance meets (`Num (MyList ?m)`).
-- A goal a given
-- answers whole selects no instance; a goal every variable of which is held rigid
-- leaves its prerequisites to the enclosing scope; a closed goal's are closed, and
-- the obligation gate's.  A goal whose verdict waits for quiescence, on a variable
-- of [liveIds], is walked there with it (`judgeQuiescentGoals`), after a later
-- group could ground that variable.  Each prerequisite continues its parent's walk
-- under the shared `requires` measure (`reqWalkEnter`), which bounds a chain that does
-- not shrink; a repeated or out-of-fuel prerequisite is reported at its site.
-- The goals come level by level, in the order the walk reaches them.  A goal one
-- seed's walk reaches again, at the same fuel, after following it cleanly is the same
-- goal with the same prerequisites, so it is kept and followed once (`wmFollowed`).
-- That pass reports nothing; when a step of it repeats a goal or runs out of fuel,
-- the goals come from a second pass that follows every path and reports each such
-- step, because the walk's path then decides what is reported.
nestedRequireGoals : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List UObligation ->
  List UObligation
nestedRequireGoals mctx rigidIds liveIds obls =
  let seeds = requireGoalSeeds mctx.mcGraph obls
  let goals =
    nestedRequireGoalsOnce
      mctx
      rigidIds
      liveIds
      (flatMap (followRequireGoal mctx rigidIds liveIds) seeds)
  if anyList (s => (reqWalkMemo (snd s)).wmStopped.value) seeds then
    nestedRequireGoalsGo
      mctx
      rigidIds
      liveIds
      (requireGoalSeeds mctx.mcGraph obls)
  else
    goals

-- Each goal of [obls] as the seed of its own walk.
requireGoalSeeds : GraphCtx -> List UObligation -> List (UObligation, ReqWalk)
requireGoalSeeds gctx obls =
  map
    (o => (o, reqWalkSeed o.pred.iface (map normalize (uOblArgs gctx o))))
    obls

nestedRequireGoalsGo : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List (UObligation, ReqWalk) ->
  List UObligation
nestedRequireGoalsGo mctx rigidIds liveIds walks =
  match flatMap (selectedRequireGoals mctx rigidIds liveIds) walks
    [] => []
    derived =>
      map fst derived ++ nestedRequireGoalsGo mctx rigidIds liveIds derived

-- The goals from level [walks] down, each goal its walk has already followed left out.
nestedRequireGoalsOnce : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List (UObligation, ReqWalk) ->
  List UObligation
nestedRequireGoalsOnce mctx _ _ [] = []
nestedRequireGoalsOnce mctx rigidIds liveIds walks =
  let (kept, derived) = followRequireLevel mctx rigidIds liveIds walks [] []
  kept ++ nestedRequireGoalsOnce mctx rigidIds liveIds derived

-- One level, in order: a goal its walk has already followed is left out,
-- each other is kept and followed, and the goals it selects form the next level.
followRequireLevel : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List (UObligation, ReqWalk) ->
  List UObligation ->
  List (List (UObligation, ReqWalk)) ->
  (List UObligation, List (UObligation, ReqWalk))
followRequireLevel mctx _ _ [] kept derived =
  (reverseL kept, flatMap identity (reverseL derived))
followRequireLevel mctx rigidIds liveIds ((o, walk) :: rest) kept derived =
  if walkGoalFollowed walk o.pred.iface (uOblGoalArgs mctx.mcGraph o) then
    followRequireLevel mctx rigidIds liveIds rest kept derived
  else
    let below = followRequireGoal mctx rigidIds liveIds (o, walk)
    followRequireLevel mctx rigidIds liveIds rest (o :: kept) (below :: derived)

-- [o]'s prerequisites on the pass that reports nothing; [o] is recorded as followed
-- when selecting them detected no error and minted none of their variables
-- (`solvedCleanly`).
followRequireGoal : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  (UObligation, ReqWalk) ->
  List (UObligation, ReqWalk)
followRequireGoal mctx rigidIds liveIds (o, walk) =
  let (clean, below) =
    solvedCleanly
      mctx
      (goals => flatMap (g => uOblArgs mctx.mcGraph (fst g)) goals)
      (_ => requireGoalsBelow mctx prerequisiteUnreported rigidIds liveIds (
        o,
        walk,
      ))
  let _ =
    if clean then
      noteWalkGoalFollowed walk o.pred.iface (uOblGoalArgs mctx.mcGraph o)
  below

uOblGoalArgs : GraphCtx -> UObligation -> List Mono
uOblGoalArgs gctx o = map normalize (uOblArgs gctx o)

-- [o]'s prerequisites under the one instance its goal selects as it stands, each
-- with the walk that reaches it from [o]'s.
selectedRequireGoals : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  (UObligation, ReqWalk) ->
  List (UObligation, ReqWalk)
selectedRequireGoals mctx rigidIds liveIds walk =
  requireGoalsBelow mctx (prerequisiteOnWalk mctx) rigidIds liveIds walk

-- [o]'s prerequisites, each entered on [o]'s walk by [enter].
requireGoalsBelow : ModuleCtx ->
  (ReqWalk -> UObligation -> List (UObligation, ReqWalk)) ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  (UObligation, ReqWalk) ->
  List (UObligation, ReqWalk)
requireGoalsBelow mctx enter rigidIds liveIds (o, walk) =
  let args = map normalize (uOblArgs mctx.mcGraph o)
  let iface = o.pred.iface
  let parentIds = flatMap monoUnboundIds args
  if isEmptyL args
    || monoVectorClosed args
    || goalVarsAllHeld rigidIds args
    || goalGivenAt mctx.mcGraph iface args o.uoScope
    || anyList (i => omHasKey (intToString i) liveIds) parentIds
      && not (undeterminedGoalExempt mctx iface args o.uoScope) then
    []
  else
    let rows = goalRows mctx iface args
    let reach =
      if goalIsProjection args rows then
        ReachMany
      else
        goalReach mctx args (goalCandidates mctx rigidIds args rows)
    match reach
      ReachOne row =>
        let goalsOf =
          ids subst reqs =>
            flatMap
              (req =>
                flatMap
                  (enter walk)
                  (requireGoalAt o ids (reqToObligation mctx subst req)))
              reqs
        match selectedRowReqMatch mctx args row
          Some (subst, reqs) => goalsOf parentIds subst reqs
          None => match unifiedRowReqs mctx rigidIds args row
            Some (subst, fresh, reqs) => goalsOf (parentIds ++ fresh) subst reqs
            None => []
      _ => []

-- A prerequisite entered on its parent's walk; a repeated or out-of-fuel one is
-- reported at its site and is not a goal of the boundary.
prerequisiteOnWalk : ModuleCtx ->
  ReqWalk ->
  UObligation ->
  List (UObligation, ReqWalk)
prerequisiteOnWalk mctx walk g =
  let step = reqWalkEnter walk g.pred.iface (map normalize g.pred.args)
  match reqWalkReported mctx g.loc step
    Some next => [(g, next)]
    None => []

-- A prerequisite entered on its parent's walk without a report: a repeated or
-- out-of-fuel one stops the walk (`wmStopped`), which `nestedRequireGoals` then runs
-- again with `prerequisiteOnWalk`.
prerequisiteUnreported : ReqWalk -> UObligation -> List (UObligation, ReqWalk)
prerequisiteUnreported walk g =
  match reqWalkEnter walk g.pred.iface (map normalize g.pred.args)
    ReqOn next => [(g, next)]
    _ =>
      let memo = reqWalkMemo walk
      memo.wmStopped := True
      []

-- The prerequisites of [row] under the unifier of its heads with [args] (every
-- variable in [rigidIds] held rigid), for a goal the row's head determines without
-- matching it as it stands (`B ?a` under `impl B (List b)`).  The unifier is not
-- committed, so the head variable it introduces (`?b` in `?a := List ?b`) stands
-- for a part of the goal's variable only while nothing outside the boundary can
-- still bind that variable: every goal variable it binds must be the boundary's.
-- One a scheme quantifies makes the goal the caller's, and the caller walks it on
-- its own variables.  The substitution keeps the goal's own variables where the
-- unifier held them rigid, and the variables it introduces are returned beside it.
unifiedRowReqs : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List Mono ->
  ImplRow ->
  Option (List (String, Mono), List Int, List Require)
unifiedRowReqs mctx rigidIds args (row@(ImplRow _ _ _ _ reqs _ _)) =
  let (tvs, heads) = freshRowHeadsTvs mctx row
  let goalIds = flatMap monoUnboundIds args
  match headsUnifier mctx.mcGraph rigidIds args heads
    Some scratch =>
      if allList
        (b =>
          not (containsI (fst b) goalIds)
            || boundaryOwnsOpen mctx rigidIds (fst b))
        !scratch then
        let sigCells = sigCellsOf rigidIds (flatMap monoVarCells args)
        let bound =
          map
            (nv => (fst nv, unrigidSig sigCells (cohApply scratch (snd nv))))
            tvs
        Some (bound, flatMap (nv => monoUnboundIds (snd nv)) bound, reqs)
      else
        None
    None => None

-- A prerequisite as a goal at [o]'s site.  One that mentions a variable the
-- instance's head does not fix is left to the module's obligation check.
requireGoalAt : UObligation ->
  List Int ->
  (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  List UObligation
requireGoalAt o parentIds (iface, args)
  | not (allList (i => containsI i parentIds) (flatMap monoUnboundIds args)) =
    []
  | otherwise = [
    UObligation {
      pred = Predicate { iface = iface, args = args },
      originId = o.originId,
      prov = o.prov,
      loc = o.loc,
      uoScope = o.uoScope,
      oblProj = OpProjected,
    },
  ]

-- The verdict on the goals on a variable D3 clause 3 withheld, once the second
-- determination has run.  The boundary owns that variable and nothing after it
-- can choose it, so a goal on it that two or more candidates still unify with is
-- `T-AMBIGUOUS-INSTANCE`, even when it also mentions a rigid variable: the
-- candidates are counted with [rigidIds] held rigid, and an instantiation of a
-- rigid variable can only add candidates, never remove one.  Zero candidates is
-- left to `rejectUndeterminedVectors`, whose `T-NO-IMPL` keeps the rigid
-- exemption.
rejectWithheldAmbiguity : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List Mono ->
  List UObligation ->
  Unit
rejectWithheldAmbiguity mctx _ [] _ = ()
rejectWithheldAmbiguity mctx rigidIds withheld obls =
  match withheldGoals mctx.mcGraph withheld obls
    [] => ()
    held =>
      let window = goalWindowOf mctx.mcGraph obls
      fold (_ o => withheldVectorVerdict mctx rigidIds window o) () held

-- The goals of [obls] that mention a still-open variable of [withheld].
withheldGoals : GraphCtx -> List Mono -> List UObligation -> List UObligation
withheldGoals gctx withheld obls =
  let heldIds = idSetOf (flatMap monoUnboundIds withheld) Tip
  filterList
    (o =>
      anyList
        (i => IdMap.has i heldIds)
        (flatMap monoUnboundIds (uOblArgs gctx o)))
    obls

withheldVectorVerdict : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  GoalWindow ->
  UObligation ->
  Unit
withheldVectorVerdict mctx rigidIds window o =
  let args = map normalize (uOblArgs mctx.mcGraph o)
  let iface = o.pred.iface
  if not (undeterminedGoalExempt mctx iface args o.uoScope) then
    let unifying = goalCandidates mctx rigidIds args (goalRows mctx iface args)
    match goalReach mctx args (verdictCandidates mctx window args unifying)
      ReachMany =>
        pushBoundaryAmbiguity
          mctx
          rigidIds
          args
          o.loc
          (ambiguousImplMsg iface.irName)
      _ => ()

hasVectorArgs : GraphCtx -> UObligation -> Bool
hasVectorArgs gctx o = listLen (uOblArgs gctx o) >= 2

goalWindowOf : GraphCtx -> List UObligation -> GoalWindow
goalWindowOf gctx obls =
  let goals = indexed obls
  GoalWindow {
    gwGoals = goals,
    gwByIndex = fold (m (i, o) => IdMap.set i o m) Tip goals,
    gwByVar = Ref (fold (m (i, o) => fileGoal gctx i o m) Tip goals),
  }

fileGoal : GraphCtx ->
  Int ->
  UObligation ->
  Map Int (List Int) ->
  Map Int (List Int)
fileGoal gctx i o byVar =
  fold
    (m id => IdMap.set id (i :: optionOr [] (IdMap.get id m)) m)
    byVar
    (dedupI (flatMap monoUnboundIds (uOblArgs gctx o)))

goalsOnVar : GoalWindow -> Int -> List Int
goalsOnVar window id = optionOr [] (IdMap.get id window.gwByVar.value)

-- A commit binds only variables of the committed goal and of the instance's fresh
-- head, so the goals whose variables it can change are the ones filed under the
-- committed goal's variables.
refileGoals : GraphCtx -> GoalWindow -> List Int -> Unit
refileGoals gctx window oldIds =
  window.gwByVar :=
    fold
      (acc i => match IdMap.get i window.gwByIndex
        Some g => fileGoal gctx i g acc
        None => acc)
      window.gwByVar.value
      (dedupI (flatMap (goalsOnVar window) oldIds))

-- [row]'s head, freshened, unified with [args] in a scratch substitution with
-- every variable in [rigidIds] held rigid; the substitution, or None.
rowHeadSubstRigid : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List Mono ->
  ImplRow ->
  Option (List (Int, Mono))
rowHeadSubstRigid mctx rigidIds args row =
  let heads = freshRowHeads mctx row
  let scratch = Ref []
  if listLen heads == listLen args
    && cohOverlapGo
      scratch
      (rigidSigPairs mctx.mcGraph rigidIds (zipL args heads)) then
    Some !scratch
  else
    None

-- A candidate does not count when its first head unifies with the goal only by
-- peeling a qualifier: `<Stdout> Int` elaborates to `Int`, and the head matcher
-- reads through a constraint or authority qualifier the same way, so against a
-- goal whose first position is already `Int` such an instance is not a second
-- type the goal could have (`test/engine_fixtures/fun_head_impl_bystander.mdk`).
-- A goal whose first position is a variable binds it to the qualified head
-- without peeling anything, so there the instance counts.  An arrow-, tuple- or
-- variable-headed instance unifies by its structure and counts.
rowCountsFor : List Mono -> ImplRow -> Bool
rowCountsFor args row = match ieRowTys row
  headTy :: _ =>
    not (tyIsQualified (headTySpineNode headTy)) || goalFirstIsVariable args
  [] => False

goalFirstIsVariable : List Mono -> Bool
goalFirstIsVariable (a :: _) = match normalize a
  TVar _ => True
  _ => False
goalFirstIsVariable [] = False

tyIsQualified : Ty -> Bool
tyIsQualified (TyEffect _ _ _) = True
tyIsQualified (TyConstrained _ _) = True
tyIsQualified (TyQual _ _ _) = True
tyIsQualified _ = False

siblingsStaySatisfiable : ModuleCtx -> GoalWindow -> List (Int, Mono) -> Bool
siblingsStaySatisfiable mctx window subst =
  let bound = map fst subst
  let scratch = Ref subst
  allList
    (i => match IdMap.get i window.gwByIndex
      Some s => siblingStaysSatisfiable mctx scratch bound s
      None => True)
    (dedupI (flatMap (goalsOnVar window) bound))

-- A sibling the commit leaves open stays satisfiable, and a closed one needs an
-- instance whose head matches it.  A sibling with fewer arguments than some
-- instance of its interface has heads is a truncation, the projection of a wider
-- goal onto its first positions (a per-slot goal `recordCallObligations` shatters
-- a predicate into), so matching rows cannot refute it and it stays satisfiable.
siblingStaysSatisfiable : ModuleCtx ->
  Ref (List (Int, Mono)) ->
  List Int ->
  UObligation ->
  Bool
siblingStaysSatisfiable mctx scratch bound s =
  let args = map normalize (uOblArgs mctx.mcGraph s)
  if not (anyIn (flatMap monoUnboundIds args) bound) then
    True
  else
    let after = map (cohApply scratch) args
    not (monoVectorClosed after)
      || anyList
        (row =>
          listLen (ieRowTys row) > listLen after
            || rowHeadMatches mctx after row)
        (filterList (ieRowOfIface s.pred.iface) (improvementPool mctx after))

freshRowHeads : ModuleCtx -> ImplRow -> List Mono
freshRowHeads mctx row = snd (freshRowHeadsTvs mctx row)

-- [row]'s heads with each of its variables fresh, and the name each fresh variable
-- stands for.
freshRowHeadsTvs : ModuleCtx -> ImplRow -> (List (String, Mono), List Mono)
freshRowHeadsTvs mctx row =
  let tys = ieRowTys row
  let tvs = freshTvMap mctx (dedup (flatMap tyVarNames tys))
  (tvs, map (fromAstType mctx tvs) tys)

-- DIAGNOSTIC-CODES-DESIGN `T-NO-IMPL`, undetermined vector: each variable renders
-- as `_`, since a letter would read as a name the program wrote.
undeterminedNoImplMsg : GraphCtx -> String -> List Mono -> String
undeterminedNoImplMsg gctx iface args =
  let holes = map (c => (tyvarId c, TRigid "_")) (flatMap monoVarCells args)
  let shown = map (substMono gctx holes [] []) args
  let positions = indexed args
  let fixed = filterList (p => monoClosed (snd p)) positions
  let open = filterList (p => not (monoClosed (snd p))) positions
  let head = "no impl of \{iface} for \{ppPredArgsShared shown}"
  if isNonEmptyL fixed && allList (p => isBareTyvarMono (snd p)) open then
    let has =
      joinWith
        " and "
        (map
          (p =>
            "`\{ppMonosShared [snd p]}` in its \{ordinalWord (fst p)} position")
          fixed)
    let free = joinWith " and " (map (p => ordinalWord (fst p)) open)
    let noun = if listLen open == 1 then "position" else "positions"
    "\{head}; no impl of `\{iface}` has \{has}, so no type for the \{free} \{noun} can satisfy it"
  else
    "\{head}; no impl of `\{iface}` has that shape, so no type for `_` can satisfy it"

improveGoal : DynCtx -> OrdMap Unit -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Unit
improveGoal dyn sigIds iface args
  | isEmptyL args || monoVectorClosed args = ()
  | otherwise =
    let rows =
      filterList (ieRowOfIface iface) (improvementPool dyn.dcModule args)
    match filterList (rowHeadMatches dyn.dcModule args) rows
      [row] => match repeatedGoalPairs (ieRowTys row) args
        [] => ()
        pairs =>
          if listLen (filterList (rowHeadUnifies dyn.dcModule args) rows)
            == 1 then
            commitImprovement dyn sigIds pairs
      _ => ()

-- Solve [pairs] in a scratch substitution with every signature variable held
-- rigid, then bind each variable that substitution solved, in the direction it
-- solved it: `unify (TVar cell) m` links `cell`, so a fresh variable is linked
-- to a signature variable and never the other way round.
commitImprovement : DynCtx -> OrdMap Unit -> List (Mono, Mono) -> Unit
commitImprovement dyn sigIds pairs =
  let cells = flatMap (p => monoVarCells (fst p) ++ monoVarCells (snd p)) pairs
  let sigCells = sigCellsOf sigIds cells
  let scratch = Ref []
  let rigidPairs = rigidSigPairs dyn.dcModule.mcGraph sigIds pairs
  let cellsById = map (c => (tyvarId c, c)) cells
  if cohOverlapGo scratch rigidPairs then
    fold
      (_ binding => match lookupAssocI (fst binding) cellsById
        Some cell => unifyIn dyn (TVar cell) (unrigidSig sigCells (snd binding))
        None => ())
      ()
      (reverseL !scratch)

-- DICT-SEMANTICS §3: a declared variable is rigid in every matcher.  A goal that an
-- instance head accepts only by binding one needs it to be a specific type, which
-- the caller chooses, so the goal is rejected at its site unless the declared
-- context gives it.  The head matcher with [sigIds] free (`rowHeadMatches` on
-- [args]) and the same matcher with them rigid disagree on exactly such a goal.
-- A binder runs it at its close over the goals recorded inside it, while its
-- declared variables are still free cells: a top-level group after improvement and
-- defaulting (`sccProtectedSignatureIds`), a method body after its own (the
-- method signature's variables), an expression annotation once the annotated
-- expression has met its written type.  A generalized local declares nothing a
-- programmer wrote, so it runs no check of its own: its goals are improved before
-- it generalizes (`improveLocalGoals`), its quantified variables turn rigid at
-- generalization (`declareRigidVars`), each goal improvement leaves on them stays in
-- its scheme, and each use poses that goal to the binder enclosing the use.
checkSigVarGoals : ModuleCtx ->
  DeclaringBinder ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  List UObligation ->
  Unit
checkSigVarGoals mctx binder sigIds sigTvMaps obls
  | omSize sigIds == 0 = ()
  | otherwise =
    fold (_ o => checkSigVarGoal mctx binder sigIds sigTvMaps o) () obls

checkSigVarGoal : ModuleCtx ->
  DeclaringBinder ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  UObligation ->
  Unit
checkSigVarGoal mctx binder sigIds sigTvMaps o =
  let args = map normalize (uOblArgs mctx.mcGraph o)
  let cells = flatMap monoVarCells args
  match sigCellsOf sigIds cells
    [] => ()
    own =>
      let iface = o.pred.iface
      let rows = filterList (ieRowOfIface iface) (improvementPool mctx args)
      let rigidArgs =
        map (substMono mctx.mcGraph (sigRigidBindings sigIds cells) [] []) args
      if anyList (rowHeadMatches mctx args) rows
        && not (anyList (rowHeadMatches mctx rigidArgs) rows)
        && not (goalGivenAt mctx.mcGraph iface args o.uoScope) then
        let _ =
          pushTypeErrorOnceAt
            mctx
            "T-MISSING-CONSTRAINT"
            o.loc
            (sigVarGoalMsg binder sigTvMaps (map tyvarId own) iface args)
        -- The goal's other variables are explained by this report, so no later
        -- verdict on a goal over them reports it again.
        let ownIds = map tyvarId own
        mctx.mcCells.poisonedVars :=
          filterList
              (i => not (containsI i ownIds))
              (flatMap monoUnboundIds args)
            ++ mctx.mcCells.poisonedVars.value

-- A binder's declared variables join the set every instance-head matcher holds
-- rigid (`matchEqPairs`), from the binder's close on.
declareRigidVars : ModuleCtx -> List String -> Unit
declareRigidVars mctx [] = ()
declareRigidVars mctx keys =
  mctx.mcCells.declaredSigVarIds :=
    omFromNames keys mctx.mcCells.declaredSigVarIds.value

goalGivenAt : GraphCtx -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> ScopeId -> Bool
goalGivenAt gctx iface args scope =
  isSome
      (activeFunDictPredOf
        gctx
        PredicateRequest { prIface = iface, prArgs = PSArgsKnown args }
        scope)
    || goalMatchesGiven gctx scope iface args

-- [t] with the rigid stand-in of each of [sigCells] replaced by that variable.
unrigidSig : List (Ref Tyvar) -> Mono -> Mono
unrigidSig sigCells t = match normalize t
  TRigid n => match filterList (c => sigStandIn c == n) sigCells
    c :: _ => TVar c
    [] => TRigid n
  TApp a b => TApp (unrigidSig sigCells a) (unrigidSig sigCells b)
  TFun a eff b => TFun (unrigidSig sigCells a) eff (unrigidSig sigCells b)
  TQual a q => TQual (unrigidSig sigCells a) q
  other => other

-- Every row that can unify with [args]: the graph-global `IE` rows route selection
-- reads (`ieSelectRowByIface`).  A goal whose first position has a head constructor
-- is unified only by rows filed under that head or under none; a multi-position
-- goal whose first position is a variable, by any row.  A one-position goal that
-- is a bare variable binds no repeated head variable, so it gets no candidates.
improvementPool : ModuleCtx -> List Mono -> List ImplRow
improvementPool mctx args =
  let env = mctx.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
  match goalHeadCon args
    Some hk => ieHeadRows (Some hk) env ++ ieHeadRows None env
    None => if listLen args > 1 then ieRowsAll env else []

rowHeadMatches : ModuleCtx -> List Mono -> ImplRow -> Bool
rowHeadMatches mctx args row = isSome (implHeadSubst mctx (ieRowTys row) args)

-- Coherence's overlap question (`cohOverlap`), asked of the row's head, freshened,
-- and the goal: both sides' variables are wildcards, nothing is committed.
rowHeadUnifies : ModuleCtx -> List Mono -> ImplRow -> Bool
rowHeadUnifies mctx args row =
  let tys = ieRowTys row
  let tvs = freshTvMap mctx (dedup (flatMap tyVarNames tys))
  cohOverlap (map (fromAstType mctx tvs) tys) args

-- The pairs a repeated head variable binds, each of which the matcher found
-- unifiable in its scratch `cohOverlapGo`.
repeatedGoalPairs : List Ty -> List Mono -> List (Mono, Mono)
repeatedGoalPairs tys args = match positionBindings tys args []
  Some binds => repeatedBindings binds []
  None => []

-- After the impl head for (iface, args) matched, a CONDITIONAL instance's
-- `requires` constraints must ALSO be satisfied (`impl Display (a, b) requires
-- Display a, Display b`).  Recover the impl's typaram bindings from the head match
-- and check each substituted requirement recursively — so `main = (Red, 5)` (Red
-- has no Display) surfaces `No impl of Display for Color` at the deepest failing
-- leaf, exactly like the bare `main = Red`, instead of the head-only match silently
-- accepting the unsatisfiable element constraint (→ null element dict → SIGSEGV).
-- A satisfied requirement (`Display Int`, `Display String`) recurses into ITS own
-- (empty) requires and accepts, so `(5, "hi")` / `[1,2,3]` still build.
-- The recursion is bounded by the shared `requires` measure: [walk] is the path that
-- reached (iface, args), and a repeated or non-shrinking-past-fuel goal is reported at
-- [loc] (#1575, #2120).  The goal's dictionary also carries its supers', so each super
-- instance's `requires` is checked too (`superGoalsEntered`).
checkNestedReqs : SiteCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  ReqWalk ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
checkNestedReqs sx univ walk iface args loc scope =
  match reqWalkReported sx.sxModule loc (reqWalkEnter walk iface args)
    None => ()
    -- A goal this walk already checked clean is not checked again (`WalkMemo`): every
    -- diagnostic below it is pushed at the walk's one [loc], so a repeat can only
    -- repeat a push.
    Some next if walkGoalDischarged next iface args => ()
    Some next =>
      let (erred, _) = erredDuring sx.sxModule (_ =>
        let _ = checkEnteredReqs sx univ next iface args loc scope
        fold
          (_ e =>
            checkEnteredReqs sx univ e.sgWalk e.sgIface e.sgArgs loc scope)
          ()
          (superGoalsEntered sx.sxModule univ walk loc [] iface args))
      if erred then () else noteWalkGoalDischarged next iface args

-- R-SUPER-CARRY (DICT-SEMANTICS §6.1.4 point 4).  A dictionary for a goal carries one
-- for each of its interface's supers at the same arguments, transitively, each built
-- by the instance that super goal selects, so that instance's `requires` is part of
-- the goal's residual at every walk that reduces the goal: the end-of-body checker
-- (`checkNestedReqs`), a generalizing or signed binder (`residualPredsOf`) and an impl
-- body (`implGoalResiduals`).  The declaration entails the context of the super
-- instance its head selects (`checkImplSuperContexts`), so only a strictly more
-- specific super instance adds a goal.  A super goal is entered beside the goal, on the
-- walk that reached it, as the route walk enters it (`superRoutesAt`), a cycle or
-- spent fuel reported at [loc].  A super goal [answered] gives, itself or through its
-- supers, is not entered: the construction's ladder tries `assum` before `inst`.  Any
-- other super goal is a selection, whatever its arguments are (constructed, arrows or
-- variables alone), and is entered when an instance matches it.  One no instance
-- matches is the impl declaration's error (`checkImplSuperContexts`): the
-- declaration's existence match (`superHeadCovers`) holds the head variables rigid and
-- binds a repeated impl variable consistently, as `implMatchesU` does here.
superGoalsEntered : ModuleCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  ReqWalk ->
  Option Loc ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  List SuperGoalEntry
superGoalsEntered mctx univ walk loc answered iface args =
  flatMap
    (sg => superGoalEntered mctx univ walk loc answered (fst sg) (snd sg))
    (superGoalClosure mctx.mcGraph iface args)

superGoalEntered : ModuleCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  ReqWalk ->
  Option Loc ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  List SuperGoalEntry
superGoalEntered mctx univ walk loc answered sup supArgs
  | not (implMatchesU mctx univ sup supArgs) = []
  | goalAnsweredBy mctx.mcGraph answered sup supArgs = []
  | otherwise = match reqWalkReported mctx loc (reqWalkEnter walk sup supArgs)
    Some next =>
      [SuperGoalEntry { sgWalk = next, sgIface = sup, sgArgs = supArgs }]
    None => []

-- Whether one of [answered], or one of its supers at its arguments, is the goal.
goalAnsweredBy : GraphCtx ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Bool
goalAnsweredBy gctx answered iface args =
  anyList
    (g =>
      walkGoalSame (fst g) (snd g) iface args
        || anyList
          (s => walkGoalSame (fst s) (snd s) iface args)
          (superGoalClosure gctx (fst g) (snd g)))
    answered

-- The goals a goal's super instances leave beyond [own], the residuals its own
-- instance's context left: one [own] answers is not new.
superCarriedResiduals : GraphCtx ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
superCarriedResiduals gctx own carried =
  own ++ filterList (g => not (goalAnsweredBy gctx own (fst g) (snd g))) carried

-- The goals of [iface]'s supers at [args], transitively, each interface once, so a
-- cyclic super graph (rejected by W1) still ends.
superGoalClosure : GraphCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
superGoalClosure gctx iface args =
  superGoalClosureGo gctx [(iface, args)] [iface] []

superGoalClosureGo : GraphCtx ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  List IfaceRef ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
superGoalClosureGo gctx [] _ acc = reverseL acc
superGoalClosureGo gctx ((iface, args) :: rest) seen acc =
  let step =
    st sg => match sg
      (sup, Some supArgs) if not (anyList (sameIfaceDecl sup) (fst st)) =>
        (sup :: fst st, (sup, supArgs) :: snd st)
      _ => st
  let (seen2, found) = fold step (seen, []) (directSuperGoals gctx iface args)
  let fresh = reverseL found
  superGoalClosureGo gctx (rest ++ fresh) seen2 (found ++ acc)

-- `checkNestedReqs` below a goal [walk] has just entered.
checkEnteredReqs : SiteCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  ReqWalk ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
checkEnteredReqs sx univ walk iface args loc scope =
  -- #1155: `reqObligationsFor` asks the min⊑ selector WHICH impl matched, so this
  -- is the one goal-posing site that reaches `pickMostSpecificEntry` from OUTSIDE
  -- the five resolver drains — publish the obligation's own snapshotted span so
  -- the ambiguity reject lands on the use site; outside the drains no construct
  -- is live.
  let sx = { sx | sxSite = loc }
  let reqs = reqObligationsFor sx univ iface args
  checkReqObligations sx univ walk loc scope reqs

-- The substituted requirement obligations of the impl of [iface] whose head
-- matches [args]: bind the impl's typaram vars from the head match, then apply that
-- binding to each `Require`'s type args.  No matching impl / no reqs → [].
-- #154 PR3: the FIRST-match impl lookup is now the keyed `findMatchingImplReqsU`
-- (bucket by iface|tag, headless fallback) instead of a flat scan over every impl.
-- ⚠️ THE `None` ARM IS NOT "NOTHING TO CHECK" — it is Door 4's `None` arm, one
-- consumer over.  See `unroutedGroundReqs` directly below for why it rejects.
reqObligationsFor : SiteCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
reqObligationsFor sx univ iface args =
  match findMatchingImplReqsU sx univ iface args
    None => unroutedGroundReqs sx univ iface args
    Some (subst, reqs) => map (reqToObligation sx.sxModule subst) reqs

-- ── SA-1 / "Door 4b": the GROUND goal's un-plumbed case is a LOUD reject too ──
-- Door 4 (`unroutedResidual`, on `residualPredsOf`'s `None` arm) made the
-- two-registry disagreement loud for a DEFERRED goal.  It has exactly one call site,
-- and a goal that never becomes a residual predicate never reaches it: a GROUND goal
-- (`Tag (Wrap Int)` — from a type signature, or from literal defaulting on a nullary
-- binding) is discharged here instead, by the end-of-body obligation checker
-- (`checkOneCallObligation` -> `checkNestedReqs` -> this function), which has the SAME
-- split.  `oblCallVerdict` accepts over the graph-global `IE` while
-- `findMatchingImplReqsU`'s evidence legs could not recover the requires.  ⚠️ ARCH
-- B-2.1-b2/-d: this sentence used to name the CONCRETE leg
-- (`concreteReqMatchByIface`) reading `shadowKeyTableRef`, the CUMULATIVE
-- `universeKeyBucketsRef` prefix.  That leg is graph-global now and both refs are
-- deleted; the surviving prefix read is the HEADLESS fallback `firstReqMatch
-- (univHeadless univ iface)` over `residualUnivRef` — see Door 4's block for the full
-- narrowing.  The split is narrower, not closed — so the impl's
-- `requires` are never recovered, no dict is built, and the emitted call is one
-- argument short of the impl it dispatches to.
-- MEASURED at `0b953165` on #1564's own four files with `export nest : Int -> String`
-- added to `nest.mdk` and NOTHING else changed: `check` exit 0 (`main : Unit`),
-- `run` exit 1 `E-PANIC: putStrLn: not a String`, `build` exit 0, and the built binary
-- exit **139** (segmentation fault); the control (the two import lines swapped) is
-- clean on all four arms and prints `wrap(int)`.  Same defect, same mechanism, one
-- signature away from the reproduction Door 4 was verified against.
-- 🚨 REJECT, DO NOT ROUTE.  Handing this arm the `requires` from `univ` would be
-- "move only the checker's leg" — `TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md:1814-1815` defers
-- both the re-key and the reader move to B-2 BY NAME, and the tree has already MEASURED
-- that desynchronizing the checker from the router yields an `argReqRoute` of `RNone`
-- and a binary that still faults (#1560).  So this reads
-- `univ` for a yes/no REJECT PREDICATE only: no obligation is discharged from it, no
-- scheme and no route changes, and both arms still return `[]`.
-- ⚠️ WHY THE TEST IS THIS ONE.  It shipped NARROWER than Door 4's, which fired on
-- `implMatchesU` alone and so did not ask whether the matched impl HAS a `requires`.
-- 🪦 THAT ASYMMETRY IS GONE: SA-4 (owner ruling RUN-055) moved `unroutedResidual` onto
-- this same predicate, so both guards now read `implMatchesWithReqsU`.  This site could
-- never have afforded the bare twin: EVERY ground obligation in every
-- program reaches here, including a no-`requires` impl whose evidence is a bare route
-- word and needs no dict at all (MEASURED by R5: `define i64 @mdk_nest__nest(i64
-- %arg0)`, arity 1, no dict) — rejecting those would be a false reject on programs that
-- run correctly.  So the predicate is "some impl that MATCHES these args carries a
-- non-empty `requires`", i.e. exactly "a dictionary would have to be passed here".
-- The disjunctive form (ANY matching impl, not the selected one) is the LOUD fail
-- direction: the selector that would name the winner is the registry that just failed.
-- 🚨 THE MESSAGE IS `requiresUnroutedMsg` — DOOR 4'S OWN, VERBATIM, AND THAT SHARING IS
-- LOAD-BEARING, NOT LAZINESS.  A DEFERRED goal reaches BOTH guards (this checker runs on
-- `Tag (Wrap a)` too — `allConcreteHeads` is about head TYCONS, so a partially-free
-- vector still gets here), so a second, differently-worded message would DOUBLE-REPORT
-- the same defect at the same span.  MEASURED: with a bespoke ground-shaped message,
-- `check --json` on #1564's own `main.mdk` emitted TWO `T-REQUIRES-UNROUTED`
-- diagnostics at range 2:16-2:21 and the must-fail pin flipped to DRAINED on a live
-- bug.  `pushTypeErrorOnceAt` dedups on the MESSAGE, so identical text collapses the
-- pair to one report by construction.  ⚠️ Consequence for SA-5 / item 4: the wording
-- now serves two sites, and its *"the module where this binding is generalized"* clause
-- is inaccurate on THIS one (nothing is generalized at a ground use site).  Reword it
-- for both, and do not fix that by re-splitting the text.
unroutedGroundReqs : SiteCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
unroutedGroundReqs sx univ iface args
  | implMatchesWithReqsU sx.sxModule univ iface args =
    let _ =
      pushTypeErrorOnceAt
        sx.sxModule
        "T-REQUIRES-UNROUTED"
        sx.sxSite
        (requiresUnroutedMsg iface args)
    []
  | otherwise = []

-- does SOME impl of [iface] matching [args] carry a non-empty `requires`?  The
-- reqs-aware twin of `implMatchesU`: same buckets, same concrete-then-headless order,
-- same `implHeadMatchesArgs` success condition, so True-here-with-`findMatchingImplReqsU`-None
-- isolates precisely the two-registry disagreement on a goal that needs a dict.
-- ⚠️ TWO CALLERS, and they must stay the same predicate: `unroutedGroundReqs` (the ground
-- obligation site, SA-1) and `unroutedResidual` (Door 4's residual site, moved here by
-- SA-4 / RUN-055).  They share `requiresUnroutedMsg` verbatim because
-- `pushTypeErrorOnceAt` dedups on message text and a deferred goal reaches BOTH; if the
-- two guards ever disagree about what counts as a match, one of them starts reporting a
-- defect the other has already ruled out.
implMatchesWithReqsU : ModuleCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Bool
implMatchesWithReqsU mctx _ _ [] = False
implMatchesWithReqsU mctx univ iface (a0 :: rest) =
  bucketArgsMatchReqs
      mctx
      (univConcreteBucket univ iface (headTyconMono a0))
      (a0 :: rest)
    || bucketArgsMatchReqs mctx (univHeadless univ iface) (a0 :: rest)

bucketArgsMatchReqs : ModuleCtx ->
  List (List Ty, List Require) ->
  List Mono ->
  Bool
bucketArgsMatchReqs mctx [] _ = False
bucketArgsMatchReqs mctx ((tys, reqs) :: rest) args =
  isNonEmptyL reqs && implHeadMatchesArgs mctx tys args
    || bucketArgsMatchReqs mctx rest args

reqToObligation : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Require ->
  (IfaceRef, List Mono)
reqToObligation mctx subst (Require { requireHead = ifaceR, requireArgs = tysR, requireOrigin = o }) = (
  IfaceRef { irName = ifaceR, irOrigin = o },
  map (reqTyToMono mctx subst) tysR,
)

-- Check each substituted requirement with the SAME accept/reject logic as a
-- top-level obligation, recursing into a satisfied conditional impl's own reqs.
-- [walk] is the `requires` walk that posed them (`reqWalkEnter`).
checkReqObligations : SiteCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  ReqWalk ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  Unit
checkReqObligations sx _ _ _ _ [] = ()
checkReqObligations sx univ walk loc scope ((ifaceR, monoArgs) :: rest) =
  let _ = checkReqOne sx univ walk ifaceR monoArgs loc scope
  checkReqObligations sx univ walk loc scope rest

-- One nested `requires` goal, judged as `checkOneCallObligation` judges a top-level one.
-- An arrow is a constructed head, so a ground `requires Ord k` at k = (Int -> Int) —
-- `Map { f => 1 }` selecting `FromEntries (Map k v) (k, v) requires Ord k` — is decided
-- here and rejected (P0-18), and a ground arrow goal some impl matches has that impl's
-- own `requires` walked by `checkNestedReqs`.
checkReqOne : SiteCtx ->
  ImplUniverse ->
  ReqWalk ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
checkReqOne sx univ walk iface args loc scope
  -- An open prerequisite is judged at its boundary (`nestedRequireGoals`), where the
  -- impl-head and signature variables it may mention are known to be rigid.
  | not (allConcreteHeads args) = ()
  | implMatchesU sx.sxModule univ iface args =
    checkNestedReqs sx univ walk iface args loc scope
  -- #1939 / #1938 (OPEN WORLD): the nested-`requires` twin of
  -- `checkOneCallObligation`'s open-world defer, and it moves WITH it by the same
  -- argument this header already makes about the function-typed reject — the two
  -- checkers share their accept/reject logic, so a rule landing in one and not the
  -- other refutes or defers the same goal according to whether it arrived as a
  -- top-level obligation or as a conditional impl's `requires`.  `residualPredsOf`
  -- reduces through `requires` too, so a deferred sub-goal reaches the enclosing scheme
  -- by the route the top-level one takes and is adjudicated where it grounds.
  | goalDefersOpenWorld sx.sxModule scope iface args = ()
  | otherwise = pushNoImplError sx.sxModule iface.irName loc args

-- A mono no `Num` impl can ever match: an application whose spine head is still an
-- unbound tyvar (a literal forced into `m a` monad position).  An arrow is not one: it is
-- a constructed head that a declared `impl Num (Int -> Int)` matches.
numUnimplementableHead : Mono -> Bool
numUnimplementableHead m = match normalize m
  TApp a b => isBareTyvarMono (spineHeadMono (TApp a b))
  _ => False

-- Chunk D (Num mis-framing reframe): at the final no-impl branch, a `Num`
-- obligation forced to a fully-ground concrete non-Num head (`args` already passed
-- allConcreteHeads + failed implMatches) is reframed to a structural type mismatch
-- WHEN it traces to a bare numeric LITERAL (`numlitReframeLoc`: recorded at this
-- loc, and NOT an arithmetic operand).  An operator-sourced `Num` failure
-- (`x + 1`, `1 + x`) keeps `No impl of Num for T` — the `+` is the real culprit.
reportNumOrNoImpl : ModuleCtx -> String -> List Mono -> Option Loc -> Unit
reportNumOrNoImpl mctx iface args loc
  | iface == "Num" && numlitReframeLoc mctx loc =
    numlitMismatchPush mctx args loc
  | otherwise = pushNoImplError mctx iface loc args

numlitMismatchPush : ModuleCtx -> List Mono -> Option Loc -> Unit
numlitMismatchPush mctx args loc =
  let hint = numlitMismatchHint mctx loc args
  let msg = numlitMismatchMsg mctx loc args
  pushTypeErrorHelpFixAt
    mctx
    "T-TYPE-MISMATCH"
    loc
    (if hint == "" then msg else "\{msg}; \{hint}")
    hint
    None

-- True iff [loc] is a literal-sourced Num obligation eligible for reframe: some
-- literal was recorded at [loc] and that loc was NOT operator-tainted.
numlitReframeLoc : ModuleCtx -> Option Loc -> Bool
numlitReframeLoc mctx (Some l) =
  anyList (p => locEq (snd p) l) mctx.mcCells.numlitVarLocs.value
    && not (anyList (ol => locEq ol l) mctx.mcCells.numlitOpLocs.value)
numlitReframeLoc mctx None = False

-- site-specific reframe wording (if / list / cons) when the context is known, else
-- a bare literal-vs-type mismatch.  `Int` is the numeric default the literal takes.
numlitMismatchMsg : ModuleCtx -> Option Loc -> List Mono -> String
numlitMismatchMsg mctx loc args = match numlitCtxKind mctx loc
  Some JoinIf =>
    "`if` branches have different types: Int vs \{ppMonosShared args}"
  Some JoinList =>
    "list elements have different types: Int vs \{ppMonosShared args}"
  Some JoinCons => "`::` head is Int but the list holds \{ppMonosShared args}"
  _ => "type mismatch: Int literal vs \{ppMonosShared args}"

-- Hint appended to `numlitMismatchMsg`.  Only the else-less `if` has a remedy
-- the message itself does not already state; the if/list/cons joins name both
-- types, so a "make them the same" hint would only repeat the fault.
numlitMismatchHint : ModuleCtx -> Option Loc -> List Mono -> String
numlitMismatchHint mctx loc _ = match numlitCtxKind mctx loc
  Some JoinElselessIf => elselessIfHelp
  _ => ""

numlitCtxKind : ModuleCtx -> Option Loc -> Option JoinContext
numlitCtxKind mctx (Some l) = lookupCtxKind l mctx.mcCells.numlitCtxTags.value
numlitCtxKind mctx None = None

lookupCtxKind : Loc -> List (Loc, JoinContext) -> Option JoinContext
lookupCtxKind _ [] = None
lookupCtxKind l ((l2, k) :: rest) =
  if locEq l l2 then Some k else lookupCtxKind l rest

-- the dispatch (interface-param) monos at one occurrence: parallel-walk the
-- declared method type against the normalized occurrence mono; wherever the
-- declared type is a bare interface-param tyvar, read the corresponding sub-mono.
-- Returns one entry per interface param, in typaram order (deduplicated by name).
-- An empty result means the walk found no iface-param position (shadowed method /
-- shape mismatch) — the caller then skips, so a shadow never produces a false
-- reject.
dispatchMonosOf : List String -> Ty -> Mono -> List Mono
dispatchMonosOf typarams mty occ =
  let pairs = walkDispatch typarams (stripTyConstraints mty) occ
  collectByParam typarams pairs

-- `dispatchMonosOf` over a method occurrence's whole interface vector: a typaram
-- the declared type never mentions reads the occurrence's own variable for it
-- ([omitted]), so the goal keeps every position (DICT-SEMANTICS §5).
occurrenceDispatchMonos : List String ->
  Ty ->
  Mono ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List Mono
occurrenceDispatchMonos typarams mty occ omitted =
  collectByParam
    typarams
    (walkDispatch typarams (stripTyConstraints mty) occ ++ omitted)

-- One fresh variable per interface parameter [mty] never mentions.  DICT-SEMANTICS
-- §5: the dispatch vector is fixed by the use site's instantiation of the whole
-- interface, wherever (or whether) a parameter appears in the method's type, so the
-- occurrence poses that position at a variable of its own for §3 to determine.
omittedParamVars : ModuleCtx -> List String -> Ty -> List (String, Mono)
omittedParamVars mctx typarams mty =
  let named = tyVarNames (stripTyConstraints mty)
  map
    (tp => (tp, freshVar mctx ()))
    (filterList (tp => not (contains tp named)) typarams)

-- `omittedParamVars` for the method [name] resolves to here, when it dispatches on
-- an argument.  None for a name with no single declaring interface, nor for a
-- return-dispatched method, whose occurrence mints its own beside its predicate
-- template (`methodReturnRequest`).
methodOmittedVars : ModuleCtx -> String -> List (String, Mono)
methodOmittedVars mctx name = match (
  argDispatchOf mctx name,
  methodEntryHere mctx name,
)
  (Some _, Some (_, typarams, mty, _)) => omittedParamVars mctx typarams mty
  _ => []

-- parallel structural walk collecting (paramName, mono) wherever the declared
-- type is a bare iface-param tyvar.  Other positions recurse; a shape mismatch
-- (declared has structure the occurrence lacks) simply stops that branch.
walkDispatch : List String -> Ty -> Mono -> List (String, Mono)
walkDispatch typarams (TyVar n) m
  | contains n typarams = [(n, normalize m)]
  | otherwise = []
walkDispatch typarams (TyFun a b) m = match peelQual m
  TFun ma _ mb =>
    walkDispatch typarams (stripTyConstraints a) ma
      ++ walkDispatch typarams (stripTyConstraints b) mb
  _ => []
walkDispatch typarams (TyApp a b) m = match peelQual m
  TApp ma mb => walkDispatch typarams a ma ++ walkDispatch typarams b mb
  _ => []
walkDispatch typarams (TyTuple ts) m = match tupleSpine m
  Some ms => flatMap (p => walkDispatch typarams (fst p) (snd p)) (zipL ts ms)
  _ => []
walkDispatch _ _ _ = []

-- one mono per interface param, in declaration order; if ANY param has no
-- recovered binding the whole obligation is abandoned (return [] → caller skips).
collectByParam : List String -> List (String, Mono) -> List Mono
collectByParam typarams pairs = match collectByParamGo typarams pairs
  None => []
  Some ms => ms

collectByParamGo : List String -> List (String, Mono) -> Option (List Mono)
collectByParamGo [] _ = Some []
collectByParamGo (p :: rest) pairs = match lookupAssoc p pairs
  None => None
  Some m => map (m :: _) (collectByParamGo rest pairs)

-- #154 PR3: implMatches / implMatchesReceiver (flat whole-universe scans) are replaced
-- by the keyed implMatchesU / bucketRecvMatch above.  implHeadMatchesArgs (used by
-- both the keyed matcher and matchTyMono callers) stays: each head-arg type pattern is
-- matched against the corresponding mono via matchTyMono (a TyVar in the head is a
-- wildcard; a parametric impl `impl Eq (List a)` thus matches `List Int`), and a
-- variable the head repeats must be bound consistently across positions
-- (`implHeadSubst`).
implHeadMatchesArgs : ModuleCtx -> List Ty -> List Mono -> Bool
implHeadMatchesArgs mctx tys args = isSome (implHeadSubst mctx tys args)

-- register, per slot, the default body's constraint var id → `$dict_<method>_<slot>`
-- in activeDictVars, so an in-body method ref unified to that var routes RDict.
-- Run AFTER body inference so the id is the SURVIVING (normalized) union-find root —
-- the same id the in-body site normalizes to (mirrors registerImplRequires).
registerMethodDictSlots : GraphCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  Int ->
  List Int ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  Unit
registerMethodDictSlots gctx _ _ [] _ = ()
registerMethodDictSlots gctx scope slot (id :: rest) subst =
  let _ = registerOneMethodDict gctx scope slot id subst
  registerMethodDictSlots gctx scope (slot + 1) rest subst

registerOneMethodDict : GraphCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  Unit
registerOneMethodDict gctx scope slot id subst = match lookupAssocI id subst
  None => ()
  Some m => match normalize m
    TVar cell =>
      gctx.graphRun.activeDictVars :=
        (tyvarId cell, Scopes.binderAt scope slot)
          :: gctx.graphRun.activeDictVars.value
    _ => ()

-- infer each impl-with-`requires`' return-position method bodies; the interface
-- method declarations come from the identity-keyed ClassEnv row at [cur].
-- Each impl is inferred at the span `locatedImpls` paired it with.
inferImplBodies : TcEnv ->
  List String ->
  ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  List (Option Loc, Decl) ->
  Unit
inferImplBodies env _ _ _ [] = ()
inferImplBodies env rpNames ce cur ((loc, d) :: rest) =
  let _ = inferOneImpl (envAtIfSome loc env) rpNames ce cur d
  inferImplBodies env rpNames ce cur rest

-- The impls of [decls], each with the span a check in it that names no construct
-- takes: the impl's interface name, or for an impl `deriving` generated (it has
-- none), the name of the type declared before it (`expandDecl` places a type's
-- derived impls right after it).
locatedImpls : Option Loc -> List Decl -> List (Option Loc, Decl)
locatedImpls _ [] = []
locatedImpls derivedFrom (d :: rest) = match implDeclLoc d
  Some here => (orElseLoc here derivedFrom, d) :: locatedImpls derivedFrom rest
  None => locatedImpls (derivingTypeLoc d) rest

-- `Some` for an impl, holding its interface name's span.
implDeclLoc : Decl -> Option (Option Loc)
implDeclLoc (DAttrib _ d) = implDeclLoc d
implDeclLoc (DImpl { implIfaceLoc, ... }) = Some implIfaceLoc
implDeclLoc _ = None

derivingTypeLoc : Decl -> Option Loc
derivingTypeLoc (DAttrib _ d) = derivingTypeLoc d
derivingTypeLoc (DData { dataNameLoc, ... }) = dataNameLoc
derivingTypeLoc (DNewtype { newtypeNameLoc, ... }) = newtypeNameLoc
derivingTypeLoc _ = None

inferOneImpl : TcEnv -> List String -> ClassEnv -> Int -> Decl -> Unit
inferOneImpl env rpNames ce cur (DAttrib _ d) =
  inferOneImpl env rpNames ce cur d
-- #1647 (S1): [implOrigin] is bound here, NOT dropped by the `...`.  The impl-body
-- signature lookup below used to receive the interface's
-- bare SPELLING, so two modules each declaring an interface spelled `Speak` sent
-- every impl body of either one to whichever `DInterface` the joint decl list
-- happened to list FIRST — attributing module B's body to module A's declared
-- method type, per import order.  DICT-SEMANTICS §8 I4: an interface is a
-- (module, name) pair, so the lookup takes the IDENTITY the `impl` head already
-- carries.  Same construction as `implDeclFact`, from the same two fields.
inferOneImpl env rpNames ce cur (DImpl { iface, tys, reqs, methods, implOrigin, ... }) =
  let iref = IfaceRef { irName = iface, irOrigin = implOrigin }
  match reqs
    [] => inferPlainImpl env ce cur iref tys methods
    _ => inferRequiresImpl env rpNames ce cur iref tys reqs methods
inferOneImpl env _ _ _ _ = ()

-- D3a: a NON-`requires` impl body, inferred on every path (single elaboration mode)
-- so its ARG-position method occurrences (e.g. `display` of a String field inside a
-- `Display`/`Debug` impl — the 19 `display@String` sites) reach inferMethodAt and
-- get stamped.  Mirrors inferRequiresImpl's head-mono substitution but with no
-- requires to register (an unconstrained impl threads no element dict).
inferPlainImpl : TcEnv ->
  ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Ty ->
  List ImplMethod ->
  Unit
inferPlainImpl env ce cur iface tys methods =
  let (implTvMap, headMonos) = implHeadMonos env.teDyn.dcModule tys
  inferImplMethods
    env
    ce
    cur
    iface
    implTvMap
    headMonos
    []
    (scopeImplMethods
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
      methods)

-- one impl `impl Iface (List a) requires Iface a where …`: build ONE tyvar map
-- shared between the head (`List a`) and the requires (`Iface a`) so the body's
-- inner method ref unifies its discriminating var to the head's `a`; infer each
-- method body against the method type instantiated at the head; THEN register the
-- requires' post-unification ids in activeDictVars keyed to `$dict_<method>_<slot>`.
inferRequiresImpl : TcEnv ->
  List String ->
  ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Ty ->
  List Require ->
  List ImplMethod ->
  Unit
inferRequiresImpl env rpNames ce cur iface tys reqs methods =
  let (implTvMap, headMonos) = implHeadMonos env.teDyn.dcModule tys
  let scopedMethods =
    scopeImplMethods
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
      methods
  let _ =
    inferImplMethods env ce cur iface implTvMap headMonos reqs scopedMethods
  registerImplRequires
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    ce
    cur
    iface
    implTvMap
    rpNames
    reqs
    scopedMethods

scopeImplMethods : ModuleCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  List ImplMethod ->
  List ScopedImplMethod
scopeImplMethods mctx _ [] = []
scopeImplMethods mctx parent (method :: rest) =
  let name = implMethodName method
  let scope =
    Scopes.freshScope
      (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
      (Some parent)
      mctx.mcCells.currentLevel.value
      (Scopes.scopeFrame (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ()) parent).sfModuleId
      (BindingOwner name)
  ScopedImplMethod { simMethod = method, simScope = scope }
    :: scopeImplMethods mctx parent rest

inferImplMethods : TcEnv ->
  ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List Mono ->
  List Require ->
  List ScopedImplMethod ->
  Unit
inferImplMethods env _ _ _ _ _ _ [] = ()
inferImplMethods env ce cur iface implTvMap headMonos reqs (m :: rest) =
  let _ = inferImplMethod env ce cur iface implTvMap headMonos reqs m
  inferImplMethods env ce cur iface implTvMap headMonos reqs rest

inferImplMethod : TcEnv ->
  ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List Mono ->
  List Require ->
  ScopedImplMethod ->
  Unit
inferImplMethod env ce cur iface implTvMap headMonos reqs scoped =
  match scoped.simMethod
    ImplMethod mname pats body => match ceMethodTyAt iface mname cur ce
      None => ()
      Some sig =>
        inferMethodBody
          env
          iface
          (ImplBody ImplBodySite {
            ibImplTvMap = implTvMap,
            ibHeadMonos = headMonos,
            ibRequires = reqs,
            ibScope = scoped.simScope,
          })
          sig
          mname
          pats
          body

-- The one method-body judgment: an impl method body, or an interface default
-- body, checked against the method's declared signature [sig] (the interface
-- params, the method type, and the graded scope the method's own scheme was built
-- under).  Both kinds instantiate the signature, infer the body against it under
-- one effect contract, query the launder trail, check W3 rigidity, run the
-- body-local numeric boundary and publish the method-level givens.  Each step at
-- which the kinds differ reads [kind] explicitly, and no flag governs two
-- unrelated steps.  In order:
--   * scope and currentFn: `openMethodBodyScope`; an impl body also sets
--     currentImplBody and resets currentFn to "" afterwards, where a default body
--     restores the caller's.
--   * instantiation: `instantiateMethodBody`.  A default body's rigidity reads the
--     same instantiation as its body and forcing row; a second signature would
--     disconnect force-only variables from the body being checked (guard fixture:
--     test/run_check_agreement_fixtures/reject_offspine_closed_row_launder_crossmodule.mdk).
--   * cascade suppression: `gatesBodyCascade`, default bodies only.
--   * where the forcing row is checked and the effect contract closes, and the
--     launder message: `checkMethodBodyAgainst`.
--   * effect-variable rigidity: one call, `checkMethodEffVarRigidity`.  An impl body
--     runs it after the type-variable half, with the launder query's verdict and its
--     index-only variables; a default body runs it before, with False and [], and
--     skips it when the body erred.  The two halves' diagnostics print in the order
--     they are pushed.
--   * the numeric channel: an impl body intersects the head and declared-dictionary
--     roots and checks its head's numeric prerequisites; a default body's surviving
--     roots are its declared type's.
--   * givens: `registerMethodBodyGivens`.
inferMethodBody : TcEnv ->
  IfaceRef ->
  MethodBodyKind ->
  (List String, Ty, List (String, List Kind)) ->
  String ->
  List Pat ->
  Expr ->
  Unit
inferMethodBody outer iface kind (params, mty, gscope) mname pats body =
  -- The body's own checks (its rigidity, its effect contract) are located at
  -- the body; its type meets the signature at the value it returns.
  let env = envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc body) outer
  let _ = enterLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let bodyLevel = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value
  let bodyScope = openMethodBodyScope env.teDyn.dcModule iface mname kind
  let savedCurrentFn = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn.value
  -- currentFn = the method name (NOT "") so arg-/return-position sites in THIS
  -- body record `encl = mname`.  registerImplRequires keys every method of an impl
  -- under the SAME impl tyvar id (`impl Ord (List a)` registers `a` once per
  -- compare/lt/min/max/…), so the global first-match route resolution returns the
  -- LAST-registered method's `$dict_<m>_<slot>` for ALL bodies — corrupting e.g.
  -- compare's element dispatch to `$dict_max_0` (unbound in compare's scope).  With
  -- encl = mname, activeDictVarOfEncl/argImplDictRoutesForEncl prefer THIS method's
  -- own `$dict_<mname>_<slot>`.  Pre-specialization each Ord impl defined only
  -- compare so there was no collision; universal default specialization exposes it.
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn := mname
  let _ = match kind
    ImplBody _ => env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentImplBody := True
    DefaultBody => ()
  -- #518: window this body's newly-added obligations, exactly as processLetGroup /
  -- `checkBodyImpl` does for a let-group, so the Num defaulting below is scoped to
  -- THIS method and can never touch an already-generalized outer var.
  let oblN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let callN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls
  let dictN0 = goalsMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ()
  let inst = instantiateMethodBody env.teDyn.dcModule kind params mty gscope
  let headBefore = match kind
    ImplBody site => implHeadVarRoots site.ibImplTvMap
    DefaultBody => []
  let _ =
    registerMethodBodyGrants
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
      iface
      mname
      (methodBodyHeadMonos kind)
      inst
      bodyScope
  let _ =
    recordClauseFileBound
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      body
      (listLen pats)
      inst.mbiExpected
  let loc = orElseLoc (implBodyLoc body) (firstTyLoc mty)
  let subject = methodBodySubject kind iface.irName mname
  -- #821: the method's effect variables are RIGID for the body — two of them
  -- meeting in an ambient row join rather than being identified.
  let contract =
    beginEffectContract
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      inst.mbiContractForce
      inst.mbiExpected
  -- issue 1146: "did the body DETECT an error" is a CONTROL judgment, so it is read
  -- off the occurrence counter, not off `listLen typeErrors`.  The region is the
  -- whole body check, which also pushes T-EFFECT-LAUNDER and contains its own gated
  -- unify, so no unify-level failure signal could answer it.
  let (bodyErred, check) = erredDuring env.teDyn.dcModule (_ =>
    checkMethodBodyAgainst
      env
      iface
      kind
      mname
      mty
      gscope
      inst
      contract
      loc
      pats
      body)
  let headMonos = methodBodyHeadMonos kind
  -- The launder query's verdict silences the atom half of an impl body's
  -- effect-variable check (same defect, one report).  A default body passes False,
  -- so a default body that launders can be reported by both.
  let launderFlagged = match kind
    ImplBody _ => check.mbcLaunderFlagged
    DefaultBody => False
  let effVarRigidity =
    _ =>
      checkMethodEffVarRigidity
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        subject
        headMonos
        gscope
        mty
        inst.mbiEffVars
        launderFlagged
        check.mbcEagerIndexed
        (orElseLoc loc check.mbcPerformedAt)
  -- Cascade gate S1 (ERROR-QUALITY.md §6): a default body that detected an error
  -- skips its effect-variable check.
  let _ = match kind
    DefaultBody => if bodyErred then () else effVarRigidity ()
    ImplBody _ => ()
  -- #814 (S0): W3 method-scheme fidelity (DICT-SEMANTICS §3).  The method's
  -- non-head quantified variables — type AND effect — belong to the CALLER
  -- (every use site re-instantiates them freshly), so the body must be checked
  -- at full generality.  [mbiSurvivors]/[mbiEffVars] were fresh flexible vars for
  -- the unify; verifying they SURVIVED unification as distinct unbound
  -- variables (types) / atom-free rows with distinct tails (effects) is
  -- equivalent to having checked the body against skolems, at the cost of one
  -- post-unify inspection (the same discipline as checkAnnotTooGeneral's C3).
  -- Without it a body can pin `b` in `mk : a -> b` — to Int (caller
  -- instantiates b := String, evaluation crashes) or to an effect-bearing
  -- arrow, alone or nested in a tuple/data arg (caller pins b to the pure
  -- arrow: a certified-pure value performs IO — the #814 laundering vein the
  -- per-arrow #803 walk is structurally blind to).  Runs BEFORE body-local
  -- defaulting so a Num default can never mask a pin.
  -- [addedObls] (this body's obligation window, also fed to the numeric boundary
  -- below) carries the CONSTRAINT axis: a body whose pin is a *constrained
  -- var* rather than a constructed type (`mk d = 42` pins b to a Num-obligated
  -- var, still a TVar) escapes the distinctness check, but its obligation on a
  -- caller-owned var is the same lie — gen-sig's `Q_sig ⊩ P'` on the impl side.
  let addedObls = wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls oblN0
  -- ALSO the CALL-obligation window: a predicate reaching a scheme var through
  -- a constrained HELPER call (`hh : Num x => x -> x`; body `meth d x = hh x`)
  -- is recorded by recordCallObligations, never by recordImplObligation — the
  -- adversarial review's break 2: without this window the Num rides a channel
  -- the survivor check never read, and `check` stayed green on a program whose
  -- built binary printed garbage.
  let addedCallObls = callOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0
  -- The settle sequence at the method-body boundary (DICT-SEMANTICS §3).  The body
  -- owns neither the instance head's variables nor its declared signature's: a
  -- construction site instantiates both, so both are held rigid, and every other
  -- variable of a goal is the body's.  An impl body's head monos and method type
  -- carry them; a default body has no head, and its method type carries the
  -- receiver's variables too.  It runs before the rigidity and head-prerequisite
  -- checks so that a predicate determination moves onto a head variable is read
  -- by them, and before the surviving roots are snapshotted.
  let bodyRigidIds =
    monoRootIdSet (headMonos ++ [inst.mbiExpected] ++ map snd inst.mbiNamedVars)
  let bodyObls = addedObls ++ callUOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0
  let _ = improveByUniqueImpl env.teDyn bodyRigidIds bodyObls
  let _ = determineByUniqueInstance env.teDyn.dcModule bodyRigidIds bodyObls
  let _ =
    checkMethodRigidityCore
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      subject
      iface.irName
      mty
      headMonos
      inst.mbiSurvivors
      (methodBodyOwnTyparams kind params)
      addedObls
      addedCallObls
      loc
  let _ = match kind
    ImplBody site =>
      checkImplHeadRigidity
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        subject
        iface.irName
        site
        headBefore
        (orElseLoc (firstExprLoc body) loc)
    DefaultBody => ()
  let _ = match kind
    ImplBody _ => effVarRigidity ()
    DefaultBody => ()
  -- The rigidity read above can normalize/alias union-find roots. Snapshot
  -- channels only afterward so this set and every obligation use the same
  -- final root identities.
  let survivingNumIds = match kind
    ImplBody site =>
      numChannelRootSet
        addedObls
        (site.ibHeadMonos
          ++ methodLevelConstraintMonos params mty inst.mbiNamedVars)
    DefaultBody => monoRootIdSet [inst.mbiExpected]
  let _ = match kind
    ImplBody site =>
      checkImplHeadNumObligations
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        subject
        site.ibImplTvMap
        site.ibRequires
        survivingNumIds
        addedObls
    DefaultBody => ()
  let _ = match kind
    ImplBody site =>
      checkImplHeadPrerequisites
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        subject
        iface
        site
        inst.mbiNamedVars
        mty
        addedObls
        addedCallObls
    DefaultBody => ()
  let _ = exitLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  -- #518 (S0, silent wrongness): PLAN.md #11 Num defaulting NEVER RAN over a method
  -- body — this path is not a let-group, so nothing grounded its ambiguous
  -- Num vars.  A literal consumed entirely inside the body (`t _ = s [1, 2]`) left
  -- its element var UNBOUND, so the receiver the route resolver saw was `List _a`,
  -- not `List Int` — and `List _a` matches only the GENERAL `impl S (List a)`, never
  -- the specific `impl S (List Int)`.  The min⊑ selector was never at fault: with one
  -- match there is nothing to select between.  It resolved to the general impl and
  -- routed its `requires S a` to RNone (a null dict) — hence `build` silently printing
  -- the general instance's answer and `run` panicking E-NOT-A-FUNCTION.
  -- The same expression at TOP LEVEL was always correct precisely because
  -- group defaulting grounded the var to Int first.  #873: a default body is inferred
  -- once and every inheriting instance reuses its routes, so it grounds here too, or
  -- module placement would decide which impl a body-local literal dispatches to.
  --
  -- MUST run AFTER the body's unify, when root identities are final. The
  -- surviving set is the intersection of this body's Num roots with head roots and
  -- declared method-dictionary roots. A return-position method variable (`lift :
  -- Num b => a -> Box b`) survives through the latter; `b` in `impl Mk (Acc b)`
  -- survives through the former and the rigidity owner above requires its impl-level
  -- prerequisite. An unrelated body-local root remains outside both and grounds.
  -- Group defaulting is still the wrong policy here: its arg-position-only filter
  -- measurably traded #518's S0 for a new one.
  --
  -- The just-exited method-body level owns both body-local defaulting and the
  -- ambiguity registration that follows it. Roots carried by the impl head or
  -- declared method dictionaries survive through [survivingNumIds]/[mbiExpected];
  -- deeper generalized locals remain outside this boundary by level.  A variable a
  -- multi-parameter goal ties to the head (`e` of `Index (Array a) k e`) is not in
  -- that set: D3 clause 3 withholds it when grounding it would leave the goal no
  -- instance, and the second determination below settles it.
  let withheld = finalizeNumBoundary
    env.teDyn
    NumBoundary {
      nbDisposition = NumBoundaryOwnedMethodBody bodyLevel,
      nbMembers = [inst.mbiExpected],
      nbSurvivingIds = survivingNumIds,
      nbDefaultObls =
        addedObls ++ calleeNumObls env.teDyn.dcModule callN0 dictN0,
      nbAmbiguityObls = addedObls,
      nbGuard = NumGuard {
        ngGoals = bodyObls,
        ngRigidIds = bodyRigidIds,
        ngOuterBelow = None,
      },
    }
  -- Defaulting is a substitution like any other, so the goals it changed are
  -- improved and determined once more.
  let _ = improveByUniqueImpl env.teDyn bodyRigidIds bodyObls
  let _ = determineByUniqueInstance env.teDyn.dcModule bodyRigidIds bodyObls
  -- The method signature's own variables are held at the body's close as a
  -- top-level signature's are at its group's.  A goal that fixes a head variable is
  -- W3-inst's (`checkImplHeadPrerequisites`), so only these are held.  The method's
  -- own `=>` context is given in the body's scope, with its supers, before they are
  -- (`publishMethodPredGivens`), so the check reads it through `goalGivenAt`.  They
  -- do not join `declaredSigVarIds`: the module-end verdict on a default body's
  -- open goal reads the instances its receiver variables reach
  -- (`test/dict_fixtures/undetermined-method-goal-default-body.mdk`).
  let methodSig = [(mname, mty, inst.mbiSurvivors)]
  let methodVarIds = sccProtectedSignatureIds methodSig
  let _ = publishMethodPredGivens env.teDyn.dcModule params mty inst bodyScope
  let _ =
    checkSigVarGoals
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      DeclaredBySignature
      methodVarIds
      methodSig
      bodyObls
  let _ =
    rejectUndeterminedVectors
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      bodyRigidIds
      omEmpty
      addedObls
      (callUOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0
        ++ nestedRequireGoals env.teDyn.dcModule bodyRigidIds omEmpty bodyObls)
  let _ =
    rejectWithheldAmbiguity env.teDyn.dcModule bodyRigidIds withheld bodyObls
  let _ =
    registerMethodBodyGivens
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
      iface
      kind
      params
      mty
      inst
      bodyScope
  let _ = match kind
    ImplBody _ => env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentImplBody := False
    DefaultBody => ()
  let restoredFn = match kind
    ImplBody _ => ""
    DefaultBody => savedCurrentFn
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn := restoredFn
  closeScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()

-- An impl body's scope was minted beside its siblings' before any body ran; a
-- default body mints its own, owned by its (interface, method) identity, at the
-- level just entered.
openMethodBodyScope : ModuleCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  String ->
  MethodBodyKind ->
  ScopeId
openMethodBodyScope mctx _ _ (ImplBody site) =
  let _ = openScope mctx site.ibScope
  site.ibScope
openMethodBodyScope mctx iface mname DefaultBody =
  let parentScope = captureScope mctx ()
  let owner = DefaultBodyIdentity { dbiIface = iface, dbiMethod = mname }
  let bodyScope =
    Scopes.freshScope
      (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
      (Some parentScope)
      mctx.mcCells.currentLevel.value
      (Scopes.scopeFrame
        (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
        parentScope).sfModuleId
      (DefaultBodyOwner owner)
  let _ = openScope mctx bodyScope
  bodyScope

-- Instantiate the declared method type for one body.
instantiateMethodBody : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodBodyKind ->
  List String ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  MethodBodyInstance
-- An impl body: the interface params are the head monos, every other signature
-- variable is fresh.  The tv map is built explicitly (instead of
-- expectedMethodType, which hides it) so the method's OWN method-level constraint
-- vars (`Thenable m => …`) can be registered after the body.
instantiateMethodBody mctx (ImplBody site) ifaceParams mty gscope =
  let baseMap = zipL ifaceParams site.ibHeadMonos
  -- #822: subtract rowArgNames too — the same split sigToSchemeTvs and
  -- astTypeFreshTbl already make.  A name sitting in a KRow type-app slot (`f e a`
  -- under a graded interface) is an EFFECT variable: it belongs to [effMap] below,
  -- and minting a TYPE var for it as well puts an entry in [extraMap] that
  -- [expected] never mentions.  Without the subtraction the graded fixtures still
  -- check, run and build identically, because the stray entry survives unification
  -- as an unbound, distinct var and so passes checkMethodRigidityCore's
  -- pinned/dup/head-disjointness tests vacuously; a survivor set containing a
  -- variable the method type does not mention would still be a false positive for
  -- the first rule that quantifies over all survivors.
  let extraMap =
    freshTvMap
      mctx
      (removeAllS
        ifaceParams
        (removeAllS (rowArgNamesIn mctx gscope mty) (dedup (tyVarNames mty))))
  -- #782/#784: build the method type's effect table the way sigToSchemeTvs does,
  -- so a free return-position effect var (`speak : a -> <e> String`) becomes a
  -- FRESH OPEN effvar that the impl body's actual effect instantiates (effect
  -- polymorphism: `Speak Dog`'s <Stdout> body sets e := <Stdout>), rather than
  -- collapsing to a CLOSED empty `<>` (fromAstType's empty etbl) and firing a
  -- spurious T-EFFECT-LEAK against a bound the method never declared.  A CONCRETE
  -- (`<Stdout>`) or PURE (`<>`) declared row still yields a closed row, so a genuine
  -- impl-body effect leak past a non-var bound is still enforced (#782).
  let effMap =
    sigVarsFor
      mctx
      mty
      (dedup (effTailNames mty ++ rowArgNamesIn mctx gscope mty))
  let mtvs = baseMap ++ extraMap
  let expected = fromAstTypeE mctx effMap mtvs mty
  let contractForce = bindingForceFromAst mctx effMap mtvs mty
  MethodBodyInstance {
    mbiExpected = expected,
    mbiContractForce = contractForce,
    mbiCheckedForce = _ => bindingForceFromAst mctx effMap mtvs mty,
    mbiEffVars = effMap.svRows,
    mbiSurvivors = extraMap,
    mbiNamedVars = mtvs,
    mbiDictSlots = [],
    mbiTypeSubst = [],
  }
-- A default body: the interface's own scheme for the method, instantiated once.
-- #822: [dscope] is the declaration-derived graded scope the method's scheme was
-- built under (inferOneIfaceDefaults → methodSchemesPure), so a default body of a
-- graded method sees its Row slots as rows, not as tyvars.
-- The constraint slot ids AND the instantiation MUST come from the SAME
-- sigToSchemeTvs build of this method's type.  Reading the ids from
-- methodPredicateSlotsRef (filled by a separate method-row build with its own
-- fresh tyvar ids) and instantiating an unrelated methodSchemesPure scheme gave ids
-- that did not appear in the instantiation subst → registerOneMethodDict's
-- `lookupAssocI id subst` returned None → activeDictVars got no entry → the in-body
-- `empty`/`++` routed RNone → eval's `++` saw a non-monoid acc and panicked
-- ('++' requires Semigroup).
-- The effect variables are read off the same substitution: sigToSchemeTvsIn
-- allocates its quantified rows in this name order, and the instantiation
-- preserves that order.
instantiateMethodBody mctx DefaultBody typarams mty dscope =
  let st = sigToSchemeTvsIn mctx dscope mty
  let descriptor = instantiateMethodTracked mctx (fst st)
  let subst = descriptor.mtiSubstitution.misTypeSubst
  MethodBodyInstance {
    mbiExpected = descriptor.mtiBody,
    mbiContractForce = descriptor.mtiForce,
    mbiCheckedForce = _ => effrowNorm descriptor.mtiForce,
    mbiEffVars =
      zipL
        (dedup (effTailNames mty ++ rowArgNamesIn mctx dscope mty))
        (map snd descriptor.mtiSubstitution.misEffectSubst),
    mbiSurvivors = defaultSurvivorMap (snd st) subst,
    mbiNamedVars = instantiateNamedMonos mctx.mcGraph (snd st) subst,
    mbiDictSlots = methodConstraintSlotIds typarams mty (snd st),
    mbiTypeSubst = subst,
  }

-- A default body has no instance head: the head-disjointness and head-row alias
-- tests then have nothing to compare against.
methodBodyHeadMonos : MethodBodyKind -> List Mono
methodBodyHeadMonos (ImplBody site) = site.ibHeadMonos
methodBodyHeadMonos DefaultBody = []

-- An obligation on a receiver typaram is entailed by the interface itself on a
-- default body; an impl body's receiver is its head, so it has none.
methodBodyOwnTyparams : MethodBodyKind -> List String -> List String
methodBodyOwnTyparams (ImplBody _) _ = []
methodBodyOwnTyparams DefaultBody typarams = typarams

-- The cascade gates of ERROR-QUALITY.md §6 (dim R: one root cause, no cascade; dim
-- X: one diagnostic per root cause), which a default body is checked under: S1
-- skips its effect-variable check when the body erred, S2 skips the method-boundary
-- unify and the launder query when inferring the body erred, and S3 drops the
-- body's own obligations when that unify fails.
gatesBodyCascade : MethodBodyKind -> Bool
gatesBodyCascade (ImplBody _) = False
gatesBodyCascade DefaultBody = True

-- Infer a method body against its declared type and query the launder trail.
--
-- The clause parameters are CHECKED against the declared domains (#821/#825,
-- Phase 73's peel) rather than inferred fresh, so a callback's row IS the
-- method's rigid `e` inside the body.  Performing it under a pure stored arrow
-- then meets `<>` as a rigid leftover — the #825 launder becomes a mismatch — and
-- two rigid rows performed together JOIN.
--
-- #803 (S0): the body's latent effect on EVERY arrow down to the method's declared
-- return is bounded by the effect the method declares at that same arrow.  An
-- effect a body legitimately performs by USING an argument (applying a callback
-- `a -> <e> b`, running a row-kinded `Async e` arg) enters the body row as that
-- argument's effect VARIABLE.  An INTRINSIC effect — `putStr`, or a call to a
-- concrete-effect helper, sourced from NO argument — instead lands as a CONCRETE
-- ATOM on whichever arrow evaluates it.  So per arrow, the body's concrete atoms
-- must be a subset of the method's declared concrete atoms; anything more
-- launders to pure at the call site.  Covering ALL declared arrows (not just the
-- `pats` count) is load-bearing: a curried / eta-reduced body (`speak d k = u =>
-- putStr …`) writes FEWER patterns and performs its intrinsic effect on a
-- RETURNED-lambda arrow BEYOND its pattern count — the arrow the declared return
-- still covers.
--
-- #839 2b: this is a POST-unify QUERY over the absorption event trail.  `unify`
-- merges an intrinsic atom into the shared open tail (both-open arm, runs no
-- effectLeakCheck), after which effrowLabels can no longer see it; the trail
-- records that merge.  So: snapshot the declared AND body arrow rows + MARK the
-- trail BEFORE the unify, run the unify (which RECORDS each absorbed atom against
-- the surviving tail), then query the window per arrow.  An OPEN body arrow's
-- absorbed atom is recovered from the trail; a CLOSED body arrow (a type
-- ANNOTATION or a point-free body) is checked directionally by `unifyInto` at the
-- seam itself — see launderEscapeFromLog.
--
-- Where the two kinds differ:
--   * an impl body checks its forcing row before the launder window opens and
--     closes the effect contract before the launder query; a default body checks
--     its forcing row inside the unify's error region and closes the contract
--     last.  Either order moves absorption events and diagnostics relative to the
--     other kind's, so each keeps its own.
--   * D-3 (#1095): an impl body reads its index-only effect variables BEFORE the
--     unify closes the declared-pure arrows.
--   * cascade gates S2/S3 (`gatesBodyCascade`), on a default body: when inferring
