--     the body detected an error, the unify and the launder query are skipped, so
--     one root cause is not reported again as the shape mismatch it induces at the
--     method boundary.  The unify runs with `dcMethodMismatch = Some mname`, so
--     a leaf TypeMismatch reports the specialized line `Method '<mname>': expected
--     type <e> but got <a>` (dims C and J).  When that unify detects a mismatch,
--     the body's own added impl obligations are TRUNCATED back to the pre-body
--     snapshot: the method's type is already known wrong, so its body's induced
--     obligations (e.g. `(5 : Bool)` ⇒ `Num Bool`) are cascade victims.  All three
--     read `ModuleCells.mcCells.errorsDetected` via `erredDuring`, never the diagnostic list
--     (issue 1146).  The leaf mismatch the unify region expects is pushed
--     NON-deduped: `dcMethodMismatch` is `Some mname` across the whole region,
--     which selects typeMismatchReport's first arm.
checkMethodBodyAgainst : TcEnv ->
  IfaceRef ->
  MethodBodyKind ->
  String ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  MethodBodyInstance ->
  (Map Int Unit, Map Int Unit) ->
  Option Loc ->
  List Pat ->
  Expr ->
  MethodBodyCheck
checkMethodBodyAgainst env iface kind mname mty gscope inst contract loc pats body =
  let oblSnapshot = wSnapshot env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let indexOnly = match kind
    ImplBody _ => indexOnlyEffVars env.teDyn.dcModule gscope mty
    DefaultBody => []
  -- A graded impl body collects the calls that run an effect variable, so the
  -- effect checks below can name the call rather than the whole body.
  let sites = if isEmptyL indexOnly then None else Some (Ref [])
  let (inferErred, inferred) = erredDuring env.teDyn.dcModule (_ =>
    inferBindingChecked
      { env | teDyn = { env.teDyn | dcPerformSites = sites } }
      (Some (normalize inst.mbiExpected))
      pats
      body)
  let actual = fst inferred
  let check =
    if inferErred && gatesBodyCascade kind then
      MethodBodyCheck {
        mbcLaunderFlagged = False,
        mbcEagerIndexed = [],
        mbcPerformedAt = None,
      }
    else
      let _ = match kind
        ImplBody _ =>
          rowInto
            env.teDyn
            True
            (inst.mbiCheckedForce ())
            (effrowNorm (snd inferred))
        DefaultBody => ()
      let launderMark = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.absorptions
      let declArrows = allArrowEffs inst.mbiExpected
      let actualArrows = allArrowEffs actual
      let eager =
        eagerIndexOnlyVars
          indexOnly
          inst.mbiEffVars
          actualArrows
          inst.mbiExpected
          actual
      -- A body that runs, at call time, a variable its signature charges only in
      -- a result index is judged against its signature at the call that ran it.
      let performedAt =
        if isEmptyL eager then None else performSiteIn sites actual
      let bodyDyn = match kind
        DefaultBody => { env.teDyn | dcMethodMismatch = Some mname }
        ImplBody _ => env.teDyn
      -- The body's type meets the signature at the value the body returns.
      let valueDyn = dynAtIfSome (valueSpanLoc body) bodyDyn
      let unifyDyn = match kind
        DefaultBody => valueDyn
        ImplBody _ => dynAtIfSome performedAt valueDyn
      let unifyErred =
        fst
          (erredDuring env.teDyn.dcModule (_ =>
            let _ = match kind
              DefaultBody =>
                rowInto
                  bodyDyn
                  True
                  (inst.mbiCheckedForce ())
                  (effrowNorm (snd inferred))
              ImplBody _ => ()
            unifyInto unifyDyn True inst.mbiExpected actual))
      let _ = match kind
        DefaultBody => ()
        ImplBody _ => finishEffectContract env.teDyn contract
      let escaping =
        launderEscapeFromLog
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
          declArrows
          actualArrows
          (wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.absorptions launderMark)
      -- `.irName`: a DIAGNOSTIC wants the spelling, not the identity (#1446 P1's
      -- rule — `irName` is kept alongside `irOrigin` for exactly this).
      let _ = match escaping
        [] => ()
        _ =>
          pushTypeErrorOnceAt
            env.teDyn.dcModule
            "T-EFFECT-LAUNDER"
            loc
            (methodBodyLaunderMsg kind iface.irName mname escaping)
      let _ =
        if unifyErred && gatesBodyCascade kind then
          wRestore env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls oblSnapshot
      MethodBodyCheck {
        mbcLaunderFlagged = isNonEmptyL escaping,
        mbcEagerIndexed = eager,
        mbcPerformedAt = performedAt,
      }
  let _ = match kind
    DefaultBody => finishEffectContract env.teDyn contract
    ImplBody _ => ()
  check

-- The method's own `=>` context, given in the body's scope with its supers.
publishMethodPredGivens : ModuleCtx ->
  List String ->
  Ty ->
  MethodBodyInstance ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
publishMethodPredGivens mctx params mty inst scope =
  registerSlotPredGivens
    mctx.mcGraph
    scope
    0
    (methodLevelPredicateSlots mctx params mty inst.mbiNamedVars)

-- Publish the method-level dictionary givens after body inference, so each
-- constraint var's id is its SURVIVING (normalized) union-find root — the same id
-- an in-body return-position site (`pure []`, `empty`, `++`) normalizes to
-- (activeDictVarOf reads that root).  Registering BEFORE inference recorded the
-- pre-unification id, the in-body site could become the surviving root instead,
-- and the route fell to RNone.  Mirrors registerImplRequires's ordering.
--   * the scalar slots: an impl body registers them by name over its tv map
--     (registerImplMethodDicts), a default body by slot id over its instantiation
--     (registerMethodDictSlots);
--   * the predicate-keyed twin, from this very instantiation, into the lexical
--     given registry before route resolution — a complete request miss is
--     terminal, so this carrier is not optional.  `inferMethodBody` publishes it
--     earlier, once the body's goals are settled (`publishMethodPredGivens`);
--   * a default body's receiver: the body answers for whichever instance inherits
--     it, so a sibling or superclass call inside it is discharged by the
--     receiver's evidence (directly, or projected onto a super) instead of being
--     left for an engine to select.  The binder is no parameter of the body — see
--     `defaultReceiverDict`.
registerMethodBodyGivens : GraphCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  MethodBodyKind ->
  List String ->
  Ty ->
  MethodBodyInstance ->
  ScopeId ->
  Unit
registerMethodBodyGivens gctx iface kind params mty inst scope =
  let _ = match kind
    ImplBody _ =>
      registerImplMethodDicts gctx scope params mty inst.mbiNamedVars
    DefaultBody =>
      registerMethodDictSlots gctx scope 0 inst.mbiDictSlots inst.mbiTypeSubst
  match kind
    DefaultBody =>
      let receiverArgs =
        map
          (tp => optionOr (TRigid tp) (lookupAssoc tp inst.mbiNamedVars))
          params
      registerFunPredGiven
        gctx
        PredicateSlot {
          psIface = iface,
          psArgs = PSArgsKnown receiverArgs,
          psBoundIds = dedupI (flatMap monoTyvarIds receiverArgs),
        }
        (Scopes.binderAt scope defaultReceiverOrdinal)
    ImplBody _ => ()

-- G4: mark binop sites recorded while inferring this impl body so resolveBinopSite
-- routes their element dict (RDict) — and ONLY theirs, not top-level operators.

-- #803 (S0, silent wrongness): the impl-body effect-LAUNDER check.  Sound rule, per
-- arrow of the method's DECLARED type down to its final return:
--
--     ∀ arrow i ≤ methodArity.  atoms(body_arrow_effect_i) ⊆ atoms(declared_effect_i)
--
-- i.e. the impl's concrete latent atoms at each arrow must be bounded by the method's
-- declared concrete atoms at that same arrow (the general form of
-- `body_latent ⊆ decl(φ) ∪ argContributable`).  Argument-contributed effects are free
-- and exact: at impl-check every parameter is still a fresh variable, so an effect the
-- body performs by USING an argument (applying a callback, running a row-kinded `Async e`
-- arg) appears as that VARIABLE — never a concrete atom — at every arrow.  Hence the
-- body's *concrete atoms* on any arrow are exactly the INTRINSIC effects, and per-arrow
-- `atomsEscape` against the declared row (IO-expanded via the same expandIoInBound the
-- binding-boundary check uses) is precisely the laundered set — a variable is
-- caller-visible and cannot lie, so only a concrete atom can launder.
--
-- #839 2b: sourced from the absorption event trail (increment 2a), POST-unify, rather
-- than arrowLaunderEscape's pre-unify walk over [expected]/[actual] arrow rows.  The
-- pre-unify walk existed only because `unify` then merges an intrinsic atom into the
-- shared open tail (both-open arm, no effectLeakCheck), after which effrowLabels can no
-- longer see it; 2a records that merge, so a post-unify query recovers it.
--
-- [declArrows]/[actualArrows] = the declared method type's and the inferred body's arrow
-- effect rows, BOTH captured PRE-unify and zipped (same spine, bounded at the shorter —
-- the methodArity bound arrowLaunderEscape had).  [evts] = the events `unify expected
-- actual` recorded in this body's trail window.  The per-arrow residual is
-- `atomsEscape (actual atoms) (declared WRITTEN atoms)`, recovered by two DISJOINT routes
-- keyed on whether the ACTUAL arrow is OPEN or CLOSED:
--
--  * OPEN actual arrow (the common inferred case): an intrinsic atom is ABSORBED at unify
--    (both-open / same-tail arm merges it into a shared tail, no effectLeakCheck), so
--    effrowLabels can no longer see it — recover it from the TRAIL.  Resolve the declared
--    arrow's tail LIVE (post-unify the fresh cell has ELinked into a shared v3 — a record-
--    time id names the old cell, not its current representative), gather atoms absorbed into that same
--    live tail (the per-cell key — risk 3, recovering arrowLaunderEscape's which-arrow
--    precision), and `atomsEscape` them against the declared row.  For a CLOSED declared
--    arrow met by an OPEN actual, the guarded closed~open arm already fired effectLeakCheck
--    (T-EFFECT-LEAK) during the SAME unify, so the trail route yields nothing and the leak
--    line stands alone (the pre-unify walk only ever DOUBLE-reported there).
--    WHY the trail equals the walk here: the both-open arm records the SYMMETRIC diff
--    (actual\declared ++ declared\actual) against the shared v3 both tails link to;
--    `atomsEscape absorbed declared` drops the declared\actual side (⊆ declared) and any
--    IO-covered atom, leaving actual \ expandIo(declared) — arrowLaunderEscape's residual.
--
--  * CLOSED actual arrow (a body type ANNOTATION — `(f : Unit -> <Stdout> Unit)` — or
--    a point-free body): nothing to recover here.  The seam's `unifyInto` checks a
--    closed~closed pair directionally as it meets it (T-EFFECT-LEAK when the actual's
--    atoms escape the declared row, nothing when the impl is PURER than declared), so
--    the query yields nothing for it and the one report stands alone.  (An annotated
--    closed actual met by an OPEN declared arrow lands in the open~closed arm and
--    reports the same launder the #816 effect-var rigidity check would — one report, via
--    launderFlagged suppression — matching the pre-unify walk.)
launderEscapeFromLog : GraphCtx ->
  List EffRow ->
  List EffRow ->
  List AbsorptionEvent ->
  List Atom
launderEscapeFromLog gctx [] _ _ = []
launderEscapeFromLog gctx _ [] _ = []
launderEscapeFromLog gctx (der :: dRest) (aer :: aRest) evts =
  let here = match aer
    EffRow _ None => []
    EffRow _ (Some _) => launderOpenActualArrow gctx der evts
  here ++ launderEscapeFromLog gctx dRest aRest evts

-- OPEN actual arrow: recover the absorbed launder atom from the trail, keyed on an OPEN
-- declared arrow's live tail; a CLOSED declared arrow's leak was already reported by the
-- closed~open arm's effectLeakCheck during the unify, so yield nothing.
launderOpenActualArrow : GraphCtx -> EffRow -> List AbsorptionEvent -> List Atom
launderOpenActualArrow gctx (EffRow declAtoms (Some cell)) evts =
  let tid = liveTailId cell
  if tid == 0 - 1 then
    []
  else
    atomsEscape gctx (atomsAbsorbedInto tid evts) declAtoms
launderOpenActualArrow gctx (EffRow _ None) _ = []

-- the concrete atoms the window recorded as absorbed into the live tail [tid]
-- (resolving each event's stored cell live, per risk 2).
atomsAbsorbedInto : Int -> List AbsorptionEvent -> List Atom
atomsAbsorbedInto _ [] = []
atomsAbsorbedInto tid (ev :: rest) =
  if liveTailId ev.cell == tid then
    ev.atom :: atomsAbsorbedInto tid rest
  else
    atomsAbsorbedInto tid rest

-- resolve an absorbing tail CELL to its live effvar id (post-unify the cell has ELinked
-- into a shared tail); -1 for a cell that resolved to a CLOSED row (no live tail).  Same
-- idiom as effVarTailIds.
liveTailId : Ref Effvar -> Int
liveTailId cell = match effrowNorm (EffRow [] (Some cell))
  EffRow _ (Some t) => effvarId t
  EffRow _ None => 0 - 1

-- the first source span inside an impl-method body, for locating T-EFFECT-LAUNDER
-- at the offending body rather than the shared interface signature.  Peels the
-- let-chain a `let _ = putStr …; body` body desugars to (a partial mirror of
-- resolve.mdk's firstExprLoc, which is not exported); falls back at the call site
-- to the method-signature loc when the body carries no span.
implBodyLoc : Expr -> Option Loc
implBodyLoc (ELoc l _) = Some l
implBodyLoc (ELam _ b) = implBodyLoc b
implBodyLoc (ELet _ _ _ e1 e2) = orElseLoc (implBodyLoc e1) (implBodyLoc e2)
implBodyLoc (ELetGroup _ b) = implBodyLoc b
implBodyLoc _ = None

-- #814 (S0): W3 method-scheme fidelity — the post-unify rigidity check, type-variable
-- and constraint axes (the effect axis is `checkMethodEffVarRigidity`).  The method
-- scheme's non-head quantifiers are re-instantiated freshly by every caller, so the
-- body may not constrain them.  Having unified the body against fresh flexible vars,
-- rigidity holds iff each survived untouched: every [extraMap] type var still
-- normalizes to a TVar (not pinned to a constructed type), and all their ids are
-- pairwise distinct and disjoint from the impl-head vars' ids (not identified with
-- each other or with a head variable).
-- Union-find bindings are monotone, so a var unbound-and-distinct AFTER unify
-- was never constrained DURING it: this is observationally the skolem check.
-- All lists here are the handful of quantified vars of one method signature.
-- One core for both kinds of method body; the per-kind values are parameters:
--   * [subject]      implSubject vs defaultSubject.
--   * [headMonos]    the instance-head monos of an impl body; a default body has no
--                    instance head and passes [], so the head-disjointness disjunct
--                    is vacuous (anyContainsI _ [] = False).
--   * [extraMap]     the survivor set: an impl body's non-head vars, every
--                    signature var of a default body (`defaultSurvivorMap`).
--   * [ownTyparams]  [] on an impl body, the interface typarams on a default body:
--                    a receiver-typaram obligation is self-entailed there.
checkMethodRigidityCore : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Ty ->
  List Mono ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List String ->
  List UObligation ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
checkMethodRigidityCore mctx subject iface mty headMonos extraMap ownTyparams addedObls addedCallObls loc =
  let pinned = map fst (filterList (p => not (isUnboundTvar (snd p))) extraMap)
  let _ =
    if isNonEmptyL pinned then
      pushTypeErrorOnceAt
        mctx
        "T-IMPL-TOO-SPECIFIC"
        loc
        (pinsTyvarMsg subject mty pinned)
    else
      let survivors = sigTvarIds (map snd extraMap)
      if hasDupI survivors
        || anyContainsI survivors (flatMap monoTyvarIds headMonos) then
        pushTypeErrorOnceAt
          mctx
          "T-IMPL-TOO-SPECIFIC"
          loc
          (collapsesTyvarsMsg subject mty)
  let _ =
    checkSurvivorObligations
      mctx
      subject
      iface
      ownTyparams
      mty
      extraMap
      addedObls
      loc
  checkSurvivorCallObligations
    mctx
    subject
    iface
    ownTyparams
    mty
    extraMap
    addedCallObls
    loc

-- The effect axis of W3 rigidity, one call shape for both kinds of method body:
-- every [effVars] effect var's row carries no concrete atom beyond what the
-- declared row at EVERY occurrence of that var in [mty] already covers
-- (IO-expanded, as the §5 escape check) — an atom unification poured into the var
-- from a position whose declared row lacks it is an intrinsic effect the caller
-- erases by instantiating the var to <> — and the vars' tails are pairwise
-- distinct; see checkImplEffVarRigidity.
-- #817 carve-out RETIRED (#823): a method effect variable may no longer alias an
-- INSTANCE-HEAD row parameter (`impl Mappable (Async e)`, whose `Suspend` arm
-- stored the callback and forced method `e'` ~ head `e`, charging the effect at
-- build time and performing it at force time).  With the `Deferred*` family the
-- head is the bare constructor and the callback row rides the index, so the
-- identification is never needed; the type-variable half never had the exception.
-- A default body has no instance head and passes [] for [headMonos].
checkMethodEffVarRigidity : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List Mono ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, Ref Effvar) ->
  Bool ->
  List String ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
checkMethodEffVarRigidity mctx subject headMonos gscope mty effVars launderFlagged eager loc =
  let _ =
    if anyContainsI
      (effVarTailIds effVars)
      (flatMap monoIndexEffvarIds headMonos) then
      pushTypeErrorOnceAt
        mctx
        "T-IMPL-TOO-SPECIFIC"
        loc
        (aliasesHeadRowMsg subject mty)
  checkImplEffVarRigidity
    mctx
    subject
    gscope
    mty
    effVars
    launderFlagged
    eager
    loc

-- A default body's survivor set: [tvs] is sigToSchemeTvs' name→scheme-var map and
-- [subst] instantiateTracked's scheme-var-id→fresh-mono subst; crossing them
-- recovers each declared name's post-unify mono, the shape an impl body's
-- non-head tv map already has.
defaultSurvivorMap : List (String, Mono) ->
  List (Int, Mono) ->
  List (String, Mono)
defaultSurvivorMap [] _ = []
defaultSurvivorMap ((name, m) :: rest) subst =
  match lookupAssocI (monoTyvarId m) subst
    Some fm => (name, fm) :: defaultSurvivorMap rest subst
    None => defaultSurvivorMap rest subst

-- the constraint axis of W3: a predicate the body records on a method-scheme
-- var must be entailed by a DECLARED method-level constraint on that var,
-- closed under `requires` (`foldMap : Monoid m => …` whose body's `++` infers
-- `Semigroup m` is entailed; `mk : a -> b` whose body's `42` infers `Num b` is
-- not — a caller instantiates b to a type with no Num impl and evaluation
-- dispatches into nothing).  Obligations on non-scheme vars (body-local
-- literals, impl-head `requires` vars, ground receivers) are skipped — the
-- existing checkImplObligations/defaulting machinery owns those.  [ownTyparams]
-- is non-empty only on the default path: an obligation on one of those
-- (receiver) vars is entailed by the interface itself + requires-closure.
checkSurvivorObligations : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List UObligation ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
checkSurvivorObligations mctx _ _ _ _ _ [] _ = ()
checkSurvivorObligations mctx subject ownIface ownTyparams mty extraMap (o :: rest) loc =
  -- the obligation's occurrence mono is the FULL instantiated occurrence type (`Int -> a`
  -- for a literal's `fromInt`); the constrained position is extracted by the
  -- same declared-type walk checkImplObligations uses.  Dispatch (receiver)
  -- typarams only, per the F0 stance: a non-receiver typaram is impl-determined.
  let _ = match o.oblProj
    OpProjected => ()
    OpMethodOcc otyparams omty occ _ =>
      checkSurvivorDispatchMonos
        mctx
        subject
        ownIface
        ownTyparams
        mty
        extraMap
        o.pred.iface.irName
        (dispatchMonosOf (dispatchTyparams otyparams) omty occ)
        loc
    OpExactReturn request =>
      checkSurvivorDispatchMonos
        mctx
        subject
        ownIface
        ownTyparams
        mty
        extraMap
        request.mrrIface.irName
        (dispatchMonosOf
          (dispatchTyparams request.mrrTyparams)
          request.mrrType
          request.mrrOccurrence)
        loc
    OpNumLit _ =>
      checkSurvivorDispatchMonos
        mctx
        subject
        ownIface
        ownTyparams
        mty
        extraMap
        o.pred.iface.irName
        o.pred.args
        loc
  checkSurvivorObligations
    mctx
    subject
    ownIface
    ownTyparams
    mty
    extraMap
    rest
    loc

-- #563's narrow instance-head prerequisite check. This reads the SAME protected
-- root set that body-local Num defaulting consumes, then asks only whether a root
-- carried by [implTvMap] has declared evidence in this impl's `requires`. Pinning is
-- `checkImplHeadRigidity`'s, and every other predicate on a head variable is
-- `checkImplHeadPrerequisites`'s, which renders a Num residual with this same
-- message, so the two report it once.
checkImplHeadNumObligations : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List Require ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List UObligation ->
  Unit
checkImplHeadNumObligations mctx _ _ _ _ [] = ()
checkImplHeadNumObligations mctx subject implTvMap reqs survivingIds (o :: rest) =
  let _ =
    checkImplHeadNumIds
      mctx
      subject
      implTvMap
      reqs
      survivingIds
      o.loc
      (dedupI (numObligIds o))
  checkImplHeadNumObligations mctx subject implTvMap reqs survivingIds rest

checkImplHeadNumIds : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List Require ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  Option Loc ->
  List Int ->
  Unit
checkImplHeadNumIds mctx _ _ _ _ _ [] = ()
checkImplHeadNumIds mctx subject implTvMap reqs survivingIds loc (id :: rest) =
  let _ = match survivorNameOfId id implTvMap
    Some vname =>
      if omHasKey (intToString id) survivingIds
        && not (implRequiresRoot mctx "Num" id implTvMap reqs) then
        pushTypeErrorOnceAt
          mctx
          "T-IMPL-MISSING-REQUIRES"
          loc
          (undeclaredImplPrerequisiteMsg subject "Num" vname)
    None => ()
  checkImplHeadNumIds mctx subject implTvMap reqs survivingIds loc rest

implRequiresRoot : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List Require ->
  Bool
implRequiresRoot mctx _ _ _ [] = False
implRequiresRoot mctx wanted id implTvMap ((Require { requireHead = iface, requireArgs = args, ... }) :: rest) =
  contains wanted (ifaceSelfAndSupers mctx iface)
      && requireArgsAreRoot id implTvMap args
    || implRequiresRoot mctx wanted id implTvMap rest

requireArgsAreRoot : Int -> List (String, Mono) -> List Ty -> Bool
requireArgsAreRoot id implTvMap [TyVar name] = match lookupAssoc name implTvMap
  Some m => match normalize m
    TVar cell => tyvarId cell == id
    _ => False
  None => False
requireArgsAreRoot _ _ _ = False

implHeadVarRoots : List (String, Mono) -> List (String, HeadVarRoot)
implHeadVarRoots implTvMap =
  flatMap
    (p => match headVarRootOf (snd p)
      Some root => [(fst p, root)]
      None => [])
    implTvMap

-- The head variables that are still type variables, by tyvar root.
implHeadTypeVarRoots : List (String, Mono) -> List (String, Int)
implHeadTypeVarRoots implTvMap =
  flatMap
    (p => match snd p
      TypeVarRoot id => [(fst p, id)]
      RowVarRoot _ => [])
    (implHeadVarRoots implTvMap)

-- The head variables this body narrowed: each one that was a variable before the
-- body and is now fixed to a constructed type or a row with atoms or a closed
-- tail, or now shares its root with another
-- head variable that was distinct before.  A variable an earlier sibling body
-- narrowed is not in [before], so it is reported once, by that body.
headVarsNarrowedBy : List (String, HeadVarRoot) ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List String
headVarsNarrowedBy before implTvMap =
  let after = implHeadVarRoots implTvMap
  map fst (filterList (headVarNarrowed before after) before)

headVarNarrowed : List (String, HeadVarRoot) ->
  List (String, HeadVarRoot) ->
  (String, HeadVarRoot) ->
  Bool
headVarNarrowed before after (name, root0) = match lookupAssoc name after
  None => True
  Some root =>
    anyList
      (other =>
        snd other /= root0 && lookupAssoc (fst other) after == Some root)
      before

-- A body that fixes a head variable holds only for the narrower head it implies,
-- yet the instance is registered for the written one, so a receiver the written
-- head admits and the body does not reaches the body with a value of another type.
checkImplHeadRigidity : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  String ->
  ImplBodySite ->
  List (String, HeadVarRoot) ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
checkImplHeadRigidity mctx subject iface site before loc =
  match headVarsNarrowedBy before site.ibImplTvMap
    [] => ()
    narrowed =>
      pushTypeErrorOnceAt
        mctx
        "T-IMPL-TOO-SPECIFIC"
        loc
        (narrowsImplHeadMsg subject narrowed (narrowedImplHead iface site))

-- The head the body actually supports, each still-free head variable under its
-- written name.
narrowedImplHead : String -> ImplBodySite -> String
narrowedImplHead iface site =
  let named = map (p => (snd p, fst p)) (implHeadTypeVarRoots site.ibImplTvMap)
  joinWith
    " "
    ("impl" :: iface :: ppEach (Ref named) (Ref 0) 3 site.ibHeadMonos)

-- The constraint axis of W3-inst: every predicate this body leaves on head variables
-- must be given by the impl.  Each goal mentioning a head variable is reduced through
-- the instances (§3 `inst`), a goal the impl gives ending the reduction (§3 `assum`
-- before `inst`), and a residual over head variables alone that no given answers is
-- reported at the goal's site.  The givens are the impl's own head, its `requires`
-- with their superinterfaces, and the method signature's own `=>` context.
-- A residual that an instance answers only by binding a head variable is reported
-- too, whatever other variables it mentions.  A goal no instance can answer even
-- with the head variables free is left to the obligation gate's no-impl verdict only
-- when the gate decides it (`allConcreteHeads`, as `uOblIsDecidableNow` asks).  A
-- vector the gate defers is a residual here: the head variable it waits on is rigid
-- for the body and never binds, so no later reader judges it.
checkImplHeadPrerequisites : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  IfaceRef ->
  ImplBodySite ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Ty ->
  List UObligation ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  Unit
checkImplHeadPrerequisites mctx subject iface site methodTvs mty addedObls addedCallObls =
  match implHeadTypeVarRoots site.ibImplTvMap
    [] => ()
    roots =>
      let givens = implBodyGivens mctx iface site methodTvs mty
      let goals =
        flatMap (oblPredOf mctx.mcGraph) addedObls
          ++ flatMap callPredOf addedCallObls
      fold
        (_ g => checkImplHeadGoal (siteFor mctx) subject roots givens g)
        ()
        goals

checkImplHeadGoal : SiteCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  Unit
checkImplHeadGoal sx subject roots givens (iface, ds, loc) =
  let args = map normalize ds
  if anyIn (flatMap monoUnboundIds args) (map snd roots) then
    let headIds = omFromNames (map (r => intToString (snd r)) roots) omEmpty
    let leaves =
      implGoalResiduals
        { sx | sxSite = loc }
        (reqWalkStart ())
        headIds
        givens
        iface
        args
    fold
      (_ leaf => reportImplHeadResidual sx.sxModule subject roots loc leaf)
      ()
      leaves

-- The head variables are matched as constants, the representation a declared
-- signature's variables have in every instance matcher (`sigRigidBindings`): an
-- instance that accepts the goal only by fixing a head variable does not reduce
-- it, and the goal itself is the residual.  A goal whose arguments are all type
-- variables is its own residual, as in a signature's body: no instance reduces it,
-- a blanket one included.  A reduced goal's super instances contribute their context
-- too, as in `residualPredsOf`.  The walk is bounded by the shared `requires` measure
-- and solves each goal once (`solvedOnWalk`), as in `residualPredsOf`; [headIds] and
-- [givens] are fixed for the walk `checkImplHeadGoal` starts.
implGoalResiduals : SiteCtx ->
  ReqWalk ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
implGoalResiduals sx walk headIds givens iface args
  | anyList (givenAnswers iface args) givens = []
  | not (anyConcreteHead args) = [(iface, args)]
  | otherwise =
    match reqWalkReported sx.sxModule sx.sxSite (reqWalkEnter walk iface args)
      None => []
      Some next => solvedOnWalk sx.sxModule next iface args (_ =>
        let univ = sx.sxModule.mcCells.residualUnivRef.value
        let cells = sigCellsOf headIds (flatMap monoVarCells args)
        let toRigid = sigRigidBindings headIds cells
        match (findMatchingImplReqsU
          sx
          univ
          iface
          (map (substMono sx.sxModule.mcGraph toRigid [] []) args))
          None =>
            if implMatchesU sx.sxModule univ iface args
              || answeredOnlyByBindingHead sx.sxModule headIds iface args
              || not (allConcreteHeads args) then
              [(iface, args)]
            else
              []
          Some (subst, reqs) =>
            let own =
              flatMap
                (r =>
                  implGoalResiduals
                    sx
                    next
                    headIds
                    givens
                    (fst r)
                    (map (unrigidSig cells) (snd r)))
                (map (reqToObligation sx.sxModule subst) reqs)
            superCarriedResiduals
              sx.sxModule.mcGraph
              own
              (flatMap
                (e =>
                  flatMap
                    (g =>
                      implGoalResiduals
                        sx
                        e.sgWalk
                        headIds
                        givens
                        (fst g)
                        (snd g))
                    (optionOr
                      []
                      (rigidHeadInstanceContext sx headIds e.sgIface e.sgArgs)))
                (superGoalsEntered
                  sx.sxModule
                  univ
                  walk
                  sx.sxSite
                  own
                  iface
                  args)))

-- An instance answers the goal only by fixing a head variable: some instance head
-- unifies with it while the head variables are free, and none does while they are
-- held rigid.  Unification rather than matching, because the instance may need the
-- goal's other variables bound as well (`Conv a String` against
-- `impl Conv Int String`, `Get (Box (List t)) b` against `impl Get (Box a) a`).
answeredOnlyByBindingHead : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Bool
answeredOnlyByBindingHead mctx headIds iface args =
  let rows = filterList (ieRowOfIface iface) (improvementPool mctx args)
  anyList (rowHeadUnifies mctx args) rows
    && not
      (anyList (row => isSome (rowHeadSubstRigid mctx headIds args row)) rows)

givenAnswers : IfaceRef -> List Mono -> PredicateSlot -> Bool
givenAnswers iface args slot =
  sameIfaceDecl slot.psIface iface
    && (match slot.psArgs
      PSArgsKnown gargs => monoVecSameGiven gargs args
      PSArgsUnknown => False)

-- The impl's own head is given as written: its superinterfaces are separate
-- instances whose own contexts must hold, so they are not given with it.
implBodyGivens : ModuleCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  ImplBodySite ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Ty ->
  List PredicateSlot
implBodyGivens mctx iface site methodTvs mty =
  let declared =
    map (requirePredicateSlot mctx site.ibImplTvMap) site.ibRequires
      ++ map (constraintPredicateSlot mctx methodTvs) (sigConstraintsOf mty)
  knownPredicateSlot iface site.ibHeadMonos
    :: declared
      ++ flatMap
        (s => map fst (predicateSlotKnownSupers mctx.mcGraph s))
        declared

requirePredicateSlot : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Require ->
  PredicateSlot
requirePredicateSlot mctx implTvMap (Require { requireHead = h, requireArgs = rargs, requireOrigin = o }) =
  knownPredicateSlot
    IfaceRef { irName = h, irOrigin = o }
    (map (fromAstType mctx implTvMap) rargs)

constraintPredicateSlot : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Constraint ->
  PredicateSlot
constraintPredicateSlot mctx tvs (Constraint { constraintHead = h, constraintArgs = cargs, constraintOrigin = o }) =
  knownPredicateSlot
    IfaceRef { irName = h, irOrigin = o }
    (map (fromAstType mctx tvs) cargs)

knownPredicateSlot : IfaceRef -> List Mono -> PredicateSlot
knownPredicateSlot iface args = PredicateSlot {
  psIface = iface,
  psArgs = PSArgsKnown args,
  psBoundIds = dedupI (flatMap monoTyvarIds args),
}

-- A residual over head variables alone names the `requires` to add.  One that also
-- mentions a variable of the body's own has no `requires` to name, so it is
-- reported when an instance answers it only by fixing a head variable, and as
-- `T-NO-IMPL` when no instance unifies with it at all: the head variable is rigid,
-- so no later binding can give it an instance.
reportImplHeadResidual : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  Option Loc ->
  (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  Unit
reportImplHeadResidual mctx subject roots loc (iface, args) =
  let ids = flatMap monoUnboundIds args
  let headIds = map snd roots
  let named = map (p => (snd p, fst p)) roots
  let rendered = ppEach (Ref named) (Ref 0) 3 args
  let pred = "\{iface.irName} \{joinWith " " rendered}"
  if isEmptyL ids || not (anyList (i => containsI i headIds) ids) then
    ()
  else if allList (i => containsI i headIds) ids then
    let msg = match (map normalize args, rendered)
      ([TVar _], [vname]) =>
        undeclaredImplPrerequisiteMsg subject iface.irName vname
      _ => undeclaredImplPredicateMsg subject pred
    pushTypeErrorOnceAt mctx "T-IMPL-MISSING-REQUIRES" loc msg
  else if answeredOnlyByBindingHead
    mctx
    (omFromNames (map (r => intToString (snd r)) roots) omEmpty)
    iface
    args then
    let fixed =
      dedup (flatMap (r => if containsI (snd r) ids then [fst r] else []) roots)
    pushTypeErrorOnceAt
      mctx
      "T-IMPL-MISSING-REQUIRES"
      loc
      (implGoalFixesHeadMsg subject pred fixed)
  else if isEmptyL
    (goalCandidates mctx omEmpty args (goalRows mctx iface args)) then
    reportUndeterminedNoImpl mctx iface args loc

-- the CALL-obligation half of the constraint axis: recordCallObligations pushes
-- (iface, [constraint-var mono], loc) for each dict slot a constrained CALLEE
-- discharges at a call site, so the monos here are the dispatch monos directly
-- (no declared-type walk needed).  Same rule as checkSurvivorObligations: a
-- predicate landing on a method-scheme var must be entailed by a declared
-- method-level constraint under requires-closure.
checkSurvivorCallObligations : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
checkSurvivorCallObligations mctx _ _ _ _ _ [] _ = ()
checkSurvivorCallObligations mctx subject ownIface ownTyparams mty extraMap ((oiface, monos, _) :: rest) loc =
  let _ =
    checkSurvivorDispatchMonos
      mctx
      subject
      ownIface
      ownTyparams
      mty
      extraMap
      oiface.irName
      monos
      loc
  checkSurvivorCallObligations
    mctx
    subject
    ownIface
    ownTyparams
    mty
    extraMap
    rest
    loc

checkSurvivorDispatchMonos : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  String ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
checkSurvivorDispatchMonos mctx _ _ _ _ _ _ [] _ = ()
checkSurvivorDispatchMonos mctx subject ownIface ownTyparams mty extraMap oiface (dm :: rest) loc =
  let _ = match survivorNameOf dm extraMap
    Some vname =>
      if survivorObligationEntailed
        mctx
        ownIface
        ownTyparams
        oiface
        vname
        mty then
        ()
      else
        pushTypeErrorOnceAt
          mctx
          "T-IMPL-TOO-SPECIFIC"
          loc
          (undeclaredConstraintMsg subject mty oiface vname)
    None => ()
  checkSurvivorDispatchMonos
    mctx
    subject
    ownIface
    ownTyparams
    mty
    extraMap
    oiface
    rest
    loc

-- entailment base per var kind: a RECEIVER typaram (default path only) is
-- entailed by the owning interface itself + requires-closure, and by the method's
-- declared `=>` constraints on it; a method-level var by its declared `=>`
-- constraints + requires-closure.
survivorObligationEntailed : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Ty ->
  Bool
survivorObligationEntailed mctx ownIface ownTyparams oiface vname mty
  | contains vname ownTyparams =
    contains oiface (ifaceSelfAndSupers mctx ownIface)
      || entailedByDeclared mctx oiface vname mty
  | otherwise = entailedByDeclared mctx oiface vname mty

-- the method-scheme var name whose post-unify root [omono] resolves to, if any
survivorNameOf : Mono -> List (String, Mono) -> Option String
survivorNameOf omono extraMap = match normalize omono
  TVar cell => survivorNameOfId (tyvarId cell) extraMap
  _ => None

survivorNameOfId : Int -> List (String, Mono) -> Option String
survivorNameOfId _ [] = None
survivorNameOfId id ((n, m) :: rest) = match normalize m
  TVar cell => if tyvarId cell == id then Some n else survivorNameOfId id rest
  _ => survivorNameOfId id rest

-- is [oiface] within the `requires`-closure of the method-level constraints
-- declared on var [vname] in [mty]?  ifaceSelfAndSupers — NOT expandSupersPairs,
-- whose WS-1b user-iface guard deliberately skips prelude chains (a dict-SLOT
-- policy), while entailment here must see them (`Monoid m =>` entails the
-- prelude `Semigroup m`).
entailedByDeclared : ModuleCtx -> String -> String -> Ty -> Bool
entailedByDeclared mctx oiface vname mty =
  contains
    oiface
    (flatMap (ifaceSelfAndSupers mctx) (declaredIfacesOn vname mty))

-- the interfaces the method's own signature constrains [vname] with
declaredIfacesOn : String -> Ty -> List String
declaredIfacesOn vname (TyConstrained cs t) =
  map
      constraintIface
      (filterList (c => contains vname (constraintVarNames c)) cs)
    ++ declaredIfacesOn vname t
declaredIfacesOn vname (TyEffect _ _ t) = declaredIfacesOn vname t
declaredIfacesOn _ _ = []

-- any member of [xs] present in [ys] (tiny per-method var lists)
anyContainsI : List Int -> List Int -> Bool
anyContainsI [] _ = False
anyContainsI (x :: xs) ys = containsI x ys || anyContainsI xs ys

-- the effect half of the rigidity check: atom containment per declared
-- occurrence, then tail distinctness among the METHOD's own effect vars.
-- A method effect var aliasing an INSTANCE-HEAD row parameter is REJECTED, not
-- admitted: `checkMethodRigidityCore` pushes `T-IMPL-TOO-SPECIFIC` when a
-- method effect var's tail is among `monoIndexEffvarIds` of the head monos,
-- before it calls this function.  What used to need the exception was Async
-- v1's `impl Mappable (Async e)`, whose `Suspend` arm stored the callback and
-- so forced method `e'` ~ head `e`; with the `Deferred*` family the head is the
-- bare constructor and the callback row rides the index, so no legal impl needs
-- that identification.  This function's own dup set is therefore the METHOD's
-- own effect vars only — impl-head row tails never enter it.  (The TYPE-var
-- half never had an exception either: a method type var may never alias an
-- impl-head type var.)
checkImplEffVarRigidity : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, Ref Effvar) ->
  Bool ->
  List String ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
checkImplEffVarRigidity mctx subject scope mty effMap launderFlagged eager loc =
  let occs =
    effVarOccAtoms mctx.mcGraph mty
      ++ map (n => (n, [])) (rowArgNamesIn mctx scope mty)
  let _ =
    if launderFlagged then () else checkEffVarAtoms mctx subject occs effMap loc
  let _ = checkIndexOnlyEffVarsOpen mctx subject effMap loc eager
  -- ⚠️ DEFERRED-PERFORMANCE residual (round-2 break 4; tracked, NOT enforced):
  -- a method effect var forced CLOSED post-unify is in truth a PIN — an impl
  -- that applies its <e>-callback inside a value whose declared row is pure
  -- (`act d k = (u => k ())` under `-> <e> (Unit -> Unit)`) closes e := <>,
  -- and a caller's effectful callback then runs inside a pure-typed thunk.
  -- Rejecting it here is CORRECT but outlaws the compiler's own Parser monad
  -- (`impl Mappable Parser` stores the callback under Parser's pure arrows —
  -- the identical shape, latent because the compiler only passes pure
  -- callbacks) and every pure-container deferred-application impl with it.
  -- Like #817, the honest result type needs grading (`Parser e a`, #820), so
  -- the channel is admitted for now and owned by #825 (pinned).
  if hasDupI (effVarTailIds effMap) then
    pushTypeErrorOnceAt
      mctx
      "T-IMPL-TOO-SPECIFIC"
      loc
      (collapsesEffvarsMsg subject mty)

-- ── D-3 (#1095): a result-INDEX occurrence is a PROMISE, not a CHARGE ──────
-- `checkArgEffVarCoverage` lets a row-kinded occurrence in the method's RESULT
-- (`f e b`) discharge the argument-only obligation the callback's `<e>` raises.
-- That is right for the DECLARATION — `f e b` says "performs <e> when forced"
-- — but it says nothing about the CALL, so an impl that APPLIES its callback
-- (`gmap g (Done a) = Done (g a)`) performs <e> at call time on an arrow the
-- signature declares pure, and nothing charges it: `check` is green and a
-- value typed `Int` prints (both engines).  The declaration cannot see it
-- (the caller sees only the index) and the #803 per-arrow bound cannot see it
-- (applying the callback contributes the VARIABLE `e`, never an atom).  The
-- seam with the information intact is the IMPL BODY: under a signature whose
-- only non-argument occurrences of `e` are indices, the body must leave `e`
-- OPEN.  Performing it — or forcing an `e`-indexed argument — meets the
-- declared-pure arrow and CLOSES `e := <>`, which is exactly the pin
-- `effVarTailIds` documents as "the safe direction" for a var the method's
-- own arrow charges, and is a launder for one it does not.  Storing the
-- callback (`Susp (u => g a)`) unifies `e` with the container's own thunk row
-- and leaves it open, so the deferred arm the spec requires stays legal.
--
-- Scoped to INDEX-ONLY variables on purpose: a var the method's own arrow
-- charges (`map : (a -> <e> b) -> f a -> <e> f b`) may still close — the
-- compiler's own `impl Mappable Parser` stores its callback under a pure
-- arrow and does, which is #825's channel, out of scope here and pinned.
-- ⚠️ CLOSED ALONE IS NOT THE SIGNAL.  An index-only variable can also close
-- through an INDEX unification with no effect performed: `deferAp mf ma =
-- deferThen mf (g => deferMap g ma)` maps a PURE `g` (from `f e (a -> b)`,
-- whose arrow is `<>`), so `deferMap g ma : f <> b` meets the result `f e b`
-- and pins `e := <>` — honest, and sound (the value built carries `mf`'s real
-- row).  What distinguishes the eager arm is that the body PERFORMS `e` on one
-- of the method's own arrows.  So [eager] is computed at the impl seam from the
-- body's arrow rows BEFORE they are unified with the declared (pure) arrows —
-- the same pre-unify snapshot the #803 launder query takes — and only a var in
-- that set is reported here.  (An interface DEFAULT body has no such snapshot
-- available at its rigidity read and passes `[]`: a residual, not a rule.)
checkIndexOnlyEffVarsOpen : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Ref Effvar) ->
  Option Loc ->
  List String ->
  Unit
checkIndexOnlyEffVarsOpen mctx subject effMap loc eager =
  checkIndexOnlyGo mctx subject effMap loc eager

-- the index-only vars of [mty] that some body arrow row (pre-unify) carries as
-- its tail — i.e. the body performs them at call time.
-- ⚠️ THE BODY'S CELLS ARE NOT THE SIGNATURE'S CELLS.  At the impl seam the
-- clause parameters are inferred fresh (`g : a -> <ρ> b`), and `ρ` is only
-- identified with the declared `<e>` by the final `unify expected actual`.
-- So the pre-unify arrow rows carry `ρ` (or whatever it has been linked to
-- meanwhile), never `e` itself.  [expected]/[actual] are walked in parallel
-- to pair each declared row cell with the actual cell at the same position
-- (`pairRowCells`), and the scan asks whether any of a var's actual
-- counterparts is a tail of some body arrow row.
eagerIndexOnlyVars : List String ->
  List (String, Ref Effvar) ->
  List EffRow ->
  Mono ->
  Mono ->
  List String
eagerIndexOnlyVars [] _ _ _ _ = []
eagerIndexOnlyVars idx effMap actualArrows expected actual =
  let tails = flatMap rowTailId actualArrows
  let pairs = pairRowCells expected actual
  filterList (v => effVarCellPerformed v effMap pairs tails) idx

-- (declared cell id, actual cell id) for every row found at the same
-- structural position of the two types — arrow latent rows and index rows,
-- under applications and arrows.  Ids are read AFTER normalization, so a cell
-- already linked during body inference reports its live representative.
pairRowCells : Mono -> Mono -> List (Int, Int)
pairRowCells d a = match peelQual d
  TFun d1 dr d2 => match peelQual a
    TFun a1 ar a2 => pairRows dr ar ++ pairRowCells d1 a1 ++ pairRowCells d2 a2
    _ => []
  TApp d1 d2 => match peelQual a
    TApp a1 a2 => pairRowCells d1 a1 ++ pairRowCells d2 a2
    _ => []
  TEff dr => match peelQual a
    TEff ar => pairRows dr ar
    _ => []
  _ => []

pairRows : EffRow -> EffRow -> List (Int, Int)
pairRows dr ar = match rowTailId dr
  [did] => map (aid => (did, aid)) (rowTailId ar)
  _ => []

effVarCellPerformed : String ->
  List (String, Ref Effvar) ->
  List (Int, Int) ->
  List Int ->
  Bool
effVarCellPerformed v effMap pairs tails = match lookupAssoc v effMap
  Some cell =>
    -- Compare live representatives, not the stable identity of an earlier
    -- linked cell: pairs/tails were recorded through normalization.
    let dids = rowTailId (EffRow [] (Some cell))
    anyList
      (did =>
        containsI did tails
          || anyList (p => fst p == did && containsI (snd p) tails) pairs)
      dids
  None => False

checkIndexOnlyGo : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Ref Effvar) ->
  Option Loc ->
  List String ->
  Unit
checkIndexOnlyGo mctx _ _ _ [] = ()
checkIndexOnlyGo mctx subject effMap loc (v :: rest) =
  -- [eager] already holds only the vars the body performed on a method arrow
  -- (`eagerIndexOnlyVars`); whether the cell then closed (the pre-#821 unify)
  -- or the ambient became a join (#821) is not the signal, the performing is.
  let _ =
    pushTypeErrorOnceAt
      mctx
      "T-EFFECT-INDEX-EAGER"
      loc
      (indexEagerMsg subject v)
  checkIndexOnlyGo mctx subject effMap loc rest

-- The earliest collected call that ran a variable now on one of [actual]'s arrows.
performSiteIn : Option (Ref (List (Ref Effvar, Option Loc))) ->
  Mono ->
  Option Loc
performSiteIn None _ = None
performSiteIn (Some sites) actual =
  let tails = flatMap rowTailId (allArrowEffs actual)
  findMap
    (site =>
      if anyList
        (id => containsI id tails)
        (rowTailId (EffRow [] (Some (fst site)))) then
        snd site
      else
        None)
    (reverseL sites.value)

-- the method effect vars that ride an ARGUMENT (a callback row or a row-kinded
-- argument) and occur on NO row the method's own type charges — every
-- non-argument occurrence is a result index.
indexOnlyEffVars : ModuleCtx -> List (String, List Kind) -> Ty -> List String
indexOnlyEffVars mctx scope mty =
  let argNames = dedup (map fst (methodEffArgOccs mctx scope mty))
  let charged = map fst (methodEffChargedOccs mctx.mcGraph mty)
  filterList (v => not (contains v charged)) argNames

-- effect-var occurrences on rows the method's type CHARGES: each spine arrow's
-- own latent row, and every arrow row written inside the final return type.
-- The `effVarOccAtoms` half of `methodEffRetOccs` minus the two INDEX forms —
-- the row-kinded-slot padding (`rowArgAtomsIn`) and a bare row written in a
-- slot (`TyRow`, `Box <Stdout | e> Unit`) — which promise rather than charge.
methodEffChargedOccs : GraphCtx -> Ty -> List (String, List Atom)
methodEffChargedOccs gctx (TyConstrained _ t) = methodEffChargedOccs gctx t
methodEffChargedOccs gctx (TyEffect labels tails t) =
  occsOfTails gctx tails labels ++ methodEffChargedOccs gctx t
methodEffChargedOccs gctx (TyFun _ b) = methodEffChargedOccs gctx b
methodEffChargedOccs gctx t = effVarChargedOccs gctx t

effVarChargedOccs : GraphCtx -> Ty -> List (String, List Atom)
effVarChargedOccs gctx (TyEffect labels tails t) =
  occsOfTails gctx tails labels ++ effVarChargedOccs gctx t
effVarChargedOccs gctx (TyApp a b) =
  effVarChargedOccs gctx a ++ effVarChargedOccs gctx b
effVarChargedOccs gctx (TyFun a b) =
  effVarChargedOccs gctx a ++ effVarChargedOccs gctx b
effVarChargedOccs gctx (TyTuple ts) = flatMap (effVarChargedOccs gctx) ts
effVarChargedOccs gctx (TyConstrained _ t) = effVarChargedOccs gctx t
effVarChargedOccs gctx _ = []

checkEffVarAtoms : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, List Atom) ->
  List (String, Ref Effvar) ->
  Option Loc ->
  Unit
checkEffVarAtoms mctx _ _ [] _ = ()
checkEffVarAtoms mctx subject occs ((n, cell) :: rest) loc =
  let esc =
    effVarOccEscape mctx.mcGraph n (effrowLabels (EffRow [] (Some cell))) occs
  let _ =
    if isNonEmptyL esc then
      pushTypeErrorOnceAt
        mctx
        "T-EFFECT-LAUNDER"
        loc
        (effVarLaunderMsg subject n esc)
  checkEffVarAtoms mctx subject occs rest loc

-- the first occurrence of var [n] whose declared atoms fail to cover
-- [instAtoms]: laundering demands EVERY occurrence cover the instantiation,
-- since the caller reads the var's row at each of them independently.
effVarOccEscape : GraphCtx ->
  String ->
  List Atom ->
  List (String, List Atom) ->
  List Atom
effVarOccEscape gctx _ [] _ = []
effVarOccEscape gctx _ _ [] = []
effVarOccEscape gctx n instAtoms ((m, declAtoms) :: rest) =
  if m == n && isNonEmptyL (atomsEscape gctx instAtoms declAtoms) then
    atomsEscape gctx instAtoms declAtoms
  else
    effVarOccEscape gctx n instAtoms rest

-- (name, written atoms) for each named-tail row occurrence in a method's AST
-- type — every TyEffect node, on the arrow spine or nested (tuples, callback
-- rows, data-arg rows).  Bare row-kinded ctor-arg slots (`Async e a`) carry no
-- written atoms and are contributed by rowArgNames at the call site.
effVarOccAtoms : GraphCtx -> Ty -> List (String, List Atom)
effVarOccAtoms gctx (TyEffect labels tails t) =
  occsOfTails gctx tails labels ++ effVarOccAtoms gctx t
-- A bare row atom (#997) is a named-tail row occurrence exactly like
-- `TyEffect` above, just with no wrapped type. Without this arm, a KRow
-- ctor-arg written as `Box <Stdout | e> Int` was invisible to
-- `checkImplEffVarRigidity`'s coverage set, so the impl-body T-EFFECT-LAUNDER
-- check over-fired ("not sourced from any argument") on an argument that
-- demonstrably DOES declare the atom.
effVarOccAtoms gctx (TyRow labels tails _) = occsOfTails gctx tails labels
effVarOccAtoms gctx (TyApp a b) = effVarOccAtoms gctx a ++ effVarOccAtoms gctx b
effVarOccAtoms gctx (TyFun a b) = effVarOccAtoms gctx a ++ effVarOccAtoms gctx b
effVarOccAtoms gctx (TyTuple ts) = flatMap (effVarOccAtoms gctx) ts
effVarOccAtoms gctx (TyConstrained _ t) = effVarOccAtoms gctx t
effVarOccAtoms gctx _ = []

-- the still-open tail id of each method effect var's row, post-unify (a closed
-- row contributes nothing: closing a var to the empty row performs LESS than
-- any caller instantiation — the safe direction, not a pin).
effVarTailIds : List (String, Ref Effvar) -> List Int
effVarTailIds [] = []
effVarTailIds ((_, cell) :: rest) = match effrowNorm (EffRow [] (Some cell))
  -- #821: a var whose cell became a JOIN is still its own (unidentified)
  -- variable; only a plain single surviving tail counts toward the dup set.
  EffRow _ (Some t) =>
    if isJoinCell t then
      effVarTailIds rest
    else
      effvarId t :: effVarTailIds rest
  EffRow _ None => effVarTailIds rest

-- Register an impl method's OWN method-level constraints (`Thenable m => …`) into
-- activeDictVars, one slot per constraint, so a return-position method in the impl
-- body whose result type is the constraint var routes RDictFwd $dict_<mname>_<slot>.
-- [tvMap] maps the method type's tyvar names → the monos expected/the body unified
-- against; normalize each to its surviving root before registering.  Slot numbering
-- matches methodConstraintSlotIds (same flatMap order), so it lines up with
-- implDictPassMethods' prepended params and the call-site methodRoutes
-- resolveMethodDicts fills.
registerImplMethodDicts : GraphCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  List String ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Unit
registerImplMethodDicts gctx scope ifaceParams mty tvMap =
  registerImplMethodDictsGo
    gctx
    scope
    0
    (methodLevelConstraintVarNames ifaceParams mty)
    tvMap

registerImplMethodDictsGo : GraphCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Unit
registerImplMethodDictsGo gctx _ _ [] _ = ()
registerImplMethodDictsGo gctx scope slot (vname :: rest) tvMap =
  let _ = registerImplMethodDictOne gctx scope slot vname tvMap
  registerImplMethodDictsGo gctx scope (slot + 1) rest tvMap

registerImplMethodDictOne : GraphCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Unit
registerImplMethodDictOne gctx scope slot vname tvMap =
  match lookupAssoc vname tvMap
    None => ()
    Some m => match normalize m
      TVar cell =>
        gctx.graphRun.activeDictVars :=
          (tyvarId cell, Scopes.binderAt scope slot)
            :: gctx.graphRun.activeDictVars.value
      -- A slot over a structured head (`Show2 (Pair b)` in `impl Desc (Pair b)`) has
      -- no single var to key by id; publishMethodPredGivens's predicate-keyed given
      -- for the same slot answers the body's goal instead.
      _ => ()

methodLevelConstraintMonos : List String ->
  Ty ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List Mono
methodLevelConstraintMonos ifaceParams mty tvMap =
  flatMap
    (name => match lookupAssoc name tvMap
      Some m => [m]
      None => [])
    (methodLevelConstraintVarNames ifaceParams mty)

-- #818 (#838 I3): the method-level `=>` constraints, one per slot, in the declaration
-- order methodLevelConstraintVarNames enumerates.  recordMethodLevelObls poses each as
-- its own obligation; the slot's interface identity is the `Constraint` occurrence's
-- resolve stamp (`constraintOrigin`, #1110, P1 #1446).
methodLevelConstraintSlots : List String -> Ty -> List Constraint
methodLevelConstraintSlots typarams (TyConstrained cs t) =
  filterList (constraintIsMethodLevel typarams) cs
    ++ methodLevelConstraintSlots typarams t
methodLevelConstraintSlots typarams (TyEffect _ _ t) =
  methodLevelConstraintSlots typarams t
methodLevelConstraintSlots _ _ = []

-- #818 (#838 I3): strip the leading `=>`/effect wrappers off a method's declared type,
-- leaving the bare function spine so matchTyMono can align it against a constraint-free
-- occurrence mono (mirrors the TyConstrained/TyEffect peel in methodLevelConstraintVarNames).
stripLeadingMethodConstraints : Ty -> Ty
stripLeadingMethodConstraints (TyConstrained _ t) =
  stripLeadingMethodConstraints t
stripLeadingMethodConstraints (TyEffect _ _ t) = stripLeadingMethodConstraints t
stripLeadingMethodConstraints t = t

-- AFTER body inference: for each method of the impl that dispatches the element
-- (return-position OR, on the emit path, argument-position), register the requires'
-- surviving (normalized) tyvar ids → its `$dict_<method>_<slot>` param, so the
-- inner ref's pendingSite/pendingArgStamp (also normalizing to that id) routes
-- RDict.  D3b-1: arg-position methods (`eq`/`compare`/`debug`/… on the element)
-- register whenever argDispatchOf finds a dispatch index (single elaboration mode;
-- return-position-only methods are unaffected).  (The element tyvar is shared
-- across an impl's methods, so per-method dict names only disambiguate for
-- single-method interfaces — exactly the D3b-1 targets Eq/Ord/Debug/Display/Hashable.)
registerImplRequires : ModuleCtx ->
  ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List String ->
  List Require ->
  List ScopedImplMethod ->
  Unit
registerImplRequires mctx _ _ _ _ _ _ [] = ()
registerImplRequires mctx ce cur iface implTvMap rpNames reqs (scoped :: rest)
  | registersElementDict mctx mname rpNames =
    let methodArity = methodDictArityInClassEnv mctx ce cur iface mname
    let _ = registerReqSlots mctx scoped.simScope implTvMap methodArity reqs
    registerImplRequires mctx ce cur iface implTvMap rpNames reqs rest
  | otherwise =
    registerImplRequires mctx ce cur iface implTvMap rpNames reqs rest
  where
    mname = implMethodName scoped.simMethod

methodDictArityInClassEnv : ModuleCtx ->
  ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  IfaceRef ->
  String ->
  Int
methodDictArityInClassEnv mctx ce cur iface method =
  match ceMethodTyAt iface method cur ce
    Some (typarams, ty, _) =>
      listLen (methodLevelConstraintVarNames typarams ty)
    None => methodDictArityOf mctx (methodSlotKey iface method)

-- a method registers an element dict if it is return-position (rpNames) or — on
-- the emit path only — an arg-position dispatch method (argDispatchOf is Some).
registersElementDict : ModuleCtx -> String -> List String -> Bool
registersElementDict mctx mname rpNames =
  contains mname rpNames || isSome (argDispatchOf mctx mname)

-- One dict parameter per declared `requires` predicate, starting at [base].  Each is
-- direct evidence; the predicate's transitive supers are projections of that same
-- parameter (the dictionary carries them), registered beside it exactly as a
-- signature slot's are (`registerFunPredGivenSlots`).
registerReqSlots : ModuleCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Int ->
  List Require ->
  Unit
registerReqSlots mctx _ _ _ [] = ()
registerReqSlots mctx scope implTvMap slot ((Require { requireHead = iface, requireArgs = rargs, requireOrigin = ro }) :: rest) =
  let argMonos = map (a => fromAstType mctx implTvMap a) rargs
  let ids = flatMap monoTyvarIds argMonos
  let binder = Scopes.binderAt scope slot
  let reqIface = IfaceRef { irName = iface, irOrigin = ro }
  let slotPred = PredicateSlot {
    psIface = reqIface,
    psArgs = PSArgsKnown argMonos,
    psBoundIds = ids,
  }
  let _ = registerEachActive mctx.mcGraph ids binder
  let _ = registerPredGiven mctx.mcGraph reqIface argMonos binder
  -- #1154 RESIDUAL: record the WHOLE predicate beside the ids, in the SAME op that
  -- registers them, so the two can never be written apart (`setFunConstraintEntry`'s
  -- rule, one channel over).  `registerPredGiven` above cannot serve this: it is
  -- single-subject and STRUCTURED-only, so `requires Ix a Char` registers nothing there.
  let _ = pushGiven mctx.mcGraph GMIdWitnessed DirectGiven slotPred binder
  let _ =
    registerFunPredGivenSlots
      mctx.mcGraph
      (predicateSlotKnownSupers mctx.mcGraph slotPred)
      binder
  registerReqSlots mctx scope implTvMap (slot + 1) rest

-- #412: the PREDICATE-keyed half of the given registry.  `activeDictVars` above is keyed
-- by TYVAR ID, which cannot express a STRUCTURED given: `requires S (List a)` registers
-- only `a`'s id (monoTyvarIds descends to the leaves), and the goal `S (List a)` looks up
-- through `activeDictVarOf`, which recurses to the SPINE HEAD (`TCon "List"`) and finds no
-- tyvar — so `assum` was unreachable by construction and `entail` fell through to
-- `entailInst`, statically committing the body to the GENERAL instance and discarding the
-- most-specific dict the construction site had correctly built and passed.  DICT-SEMANTICS
-- §3 (assum before inst) + :155-166 (sub-evidence is never pre-baked at the declaration).
-- Keyed by (iface, WHOLE argument vector) so it is neither iface-blind nor
-- structure-blind, and matched by `monoVecSameGiven` — pointwise `monoSameGiven`,
-- structural, on rigid-tyvar IDENTITY, never unification.
--
-- 🚨 #1956 / #1937: THE KEY IS THE VECTOR, NOT THE LEAD ARGUMENT.  This arm used to
-- match `[subject]` and return `()` for any longer vector, so a MULTI-PARAMETER
-- declared context (`f : Conv (Wrap a) b => …`) had no consumption-side answer at all:
-- `entailAssum` could never see it, `entail` fell through to `entailInst`, and the body
-- was statically committed to whichever impl was most specific at ABSTRACTION time while
-- the caller's correctly-built dict went unread — so `f (Wrap 5) True` and `f (Wrap 'c')
-- 7` both took the SAME impl, and swapping the two `impl` blocks changed which one, at
-- exit 0 (DICT-SEMANTICS §3 forbids selection by declaration order outright).
-- ⚠️ THE ANSWER TO "when are two predicate argument vectors the same predicate?" IS
-- POINTWISE STRUCTURAL IDENTITY OVER THE VECTOR: equal length, and `monoSameGiven` at
-- every position, in order.  `goalMatchesGiven`/`goalSlotStillOpen` follow this shape
-- exactly, and must keep following it — see their own headers.
--
-- §6.1.3's rigid commit is preserved TWICE OVER, and the guard below is the load-bearing
-- one: `requires S a` is a bare-tyvar given, so this writer registers nothing for it, and
-- the body's goal `S (List a)` finds no assumption ⇒ `inst` fires on the rigid goal ⇒ the
-- general instance ⇒ 2, unchanged.  Even had it been registered, `monoSameGiven` compares
-- structurally and would not match subject `a` against goal `List a` — only unification
-- would, and this is deliberately not unification.  Pinned by
-- test/build_diff_fixtures/impl_requires_structured_rigid_control.mdk.
--
-- #2547 unit 3: the guard is a `GivenMatch` decision now, not an absence.  The
-- all-bare vector this arm refuses IS in `gGiven` — `registerReqSlots` pushes it as
-- `GMIdWitnessed` — and what preserves the paragraph above is that every reader keyed on
-- predicate identity alone scans `GSPredicateOnly` and so cannot see it.  Both halves must
-- move together: pushing an all-bare vector as `GMPredicate`, or widening a
-- `GSPredicateOnly` rung, re-opens exactly what this guard closes.  Function carriers have
-- a distinct Known-slot writer (`registerSlotPredGivens`) because their complete
-- multi-parameter identity is required by EKNestedTop.
--
-- ⚠️ #1956 WIDENS THAT SHARP EDGE TO MORE POSITIONS, and does not introduce a new one.
-- A vector like `[Wrap a, b]` is admitted because SOME position is structured, but its
-- SECOND position is a bare tyvar matched by raw id — the same `TVar`/`TVar` arm of
-- `monoSameGiven`, one position over.  The structured position still gates the whole
-- match (all positions must agree, so a stale-id coincidence at a bare position can only
-- matter for a goal that already agrees structurally elsewhere at the same interface),
-- which is why this is a widening of an existing hazard rather than a new one.  Removing
-- it is the same scoped-projection question `activeDictVarOf`'s `inImpl` gate answers,
-- and belongs with the key-side work (#1904), not here.
registerPredGiven : GraphCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  EvidenceBinderId ->
  Unit
registerPredGiven gctx _ [] _ = ()
registerPredGiven gctx iface args dname
  | allList isBareTyvarMono args = ()
  | otherwise =
    let slot = PredicateSlot {
      psIface = iface,
      psArgs = PSArgsKnown args,
      psBoundIds = dedupI (flatMap monoTyvarIds args),
    }
    pushGiven gctx GMPredicate DirectGiven slot dname

-- Assumption lookup over predicate-keyed givens.  The occurrence's captured
-- scope selects only its own or an ancestor's binder; generated dictionary names
-- and registration order across sibling bodies are irrelevant, and so is the
-- enclosing declaration's name.
activeDictPredOf : GraphCtx ->
  PredicateRequest ->
  Mono ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option AssumAnswer
activeDictPredOf gctx request targetMono useScope =
  let preds = givensForScope gctx useScope
  match request.prArgs
    PSArgsKnown _ => firstPredForEncl gctx request useScope preds
    PSArgsUnknown => match predicateTargetId targetMono
      Some target =>
        firstPredForEnclAt gctx GSPredicateOnly target request useScope preds
      None => None

predicateTargetId : Mono -> Option Int
predicateTargetId m = match peelQual m
  TVar cell => Some (tyvarId cell)
  TApp a _ => predicateTargetId a
  _ => None

-- Function-carrier predicate evidence is lexical: the occurrence's captured scope
-- reads only its own or an ancestor's givens, so a module's givens accumulating across
-- its functions cannot route evidence from a different body.
activeFunDictPredOf : GraphCtx ->
  PredicateRequest ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option AssumAnswer
activeFunDictPredOf gctx request useScope =
  firstPredForEncl gctx request useScope (givensForScope gctx useScope)

firstPredForEncl : GraphCtx ->
  PredicateRequest ->
  ScopeId ->
  List GivenEntry ->
  Option AssumAnswer
firstPredForEncl gctx request useScope givens =
  firstPredOnChain
    request
    (Scopes.visibleChain (currentScopeStore gctx ()) useScope)
    givens

firstPredOnChain : PredicateRequest ->
  List Int ->
  List GivenEntry ->
  Option AssumAnswer
firstPredOnChain _ _ [] = None
firstPredOnChain request chain (g :: rest)
  | givenInScope GSPredicateOnly g
    && Scopes.visibleOnChain chain (Scopes.binderScope g.geBinder)
    && predicateRequestMatchesSlot request g.geSlot =
    Some (givenAnswerForRequest request g)
  | otherwise = firstPredOnChain request chain rest

-- Semantic given evidence requires predicate-only eligibility, complete matched
-- vectors, and resolved declaration identities.  Id-witnessed, unknown-vector,
-- and unresolved-declaration paths keep their routing but remain legacy.
givenAnswerExact : GivenEntry -> AssumAnswer
givenAnswerExact g = match g.geProvenance
  DirectGiven => SemanticGiven (GivenEvidence g.geBinder)
  ProjectedGiven parent path => SemanticGiven (SuperclassEvidence parent path)

givenAnswerForRequest : PredicateRequest -> GivenEntry -> AssumAnswer
givenAnswerForRequest request g = match (
  request.prArgs,
  g.geSlot.psArgs,
  g.geMatch,
)
  (PSArgsKnown _, PSArgsKnown _, GMPredicate) => match (
    request.prIface.irOrigin,
    g.geSlot.psIface.irOrigin,
  )
    (OriginUnresolved, _) => givenAnswerResidual g
    (_, OriginUnresolved) => givenAnswerResidual g
    _ => givenAnswerExact g
  _ => givenAnswerResidual g

givenAnswerResidual : GivenEntry -> AssumAnswer
givenAnswerResidual g = match g.geProvenance
  DirectGiven => LegacyPredicate g.geBinder
  ProjectedGiven parent path => LegacyProjected parent path

-- The id-witnessed scan.  [scope] is the rung's own declaration of what it may read —
-- both rungs that reach here supply a tyvar-id witness, but only one of them is keyed on
-- the givens that REQUIRE it.  See `GivenScope`.
firstPredForEnclAt : GraphCtx ->
  GivenScope ->
  Int ->
  PredicateRequest ->
  ScopeId ->
  List GivenEntry ->
  Option AssumAnswer
firstPredForEnclAt gctx scope target request useScope givens =
  firstPredAtOnChain
    scope
    target
    request
    (Scopes.visibleChain (currentScopeStore gctx ()) useScope)
    givens

firstPredAtOnChain : GivenScope ->
  Int ->
  PredicateRequest ->
  List Int ->
  List GivenEntry ->
  Option AssumAnswer
firstPredAtOnChain _ _ _ _ [] = None
firstPredAtOnChain scope target request chain (g :: rest)
  | givenInScope scope g
    && containsI target g.geSlot.psBoundIds
    && Scopes.visibleOnChain chain (Scopes.binderScope g.geBinder)
    && predicateRequestMatchesSlot request g.geSlot =
    Some (givenAnswerForRequest request g)
  | otherwise = firstPredAtOnChain scope target request chain rest

-- Explicit #1318 EKNestedTop residual: this is the one spelling-keyed lookup retained
-- for a producer that can still supply OriginUnresolved.  Complete method requests do
-- not reach it.
activeFunDictPredOfResidual : GraphCtx ->
  String ->
  List Mono ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option AssumAnswer
activeFunDictPredOfResidual gctx iface args useScope =
  firstPredForEnclResidual
    gctx
    iface
    args
    useScope
    (givensForScope gctx useScope)

firstPredForEnclResidual : GraphCtx ->
  String ->
  List Mono ->
  ScopeId ->
  List GivenEntry ->
  Option AssumAnswer
firstPredForEnclResidual gctx _ _ _ [] = None
firstPredForEnclResidual gctx iface args useScope (g :: rest)
  | givenInScope GSPredicateOnly g
    && g.geSlot.psIface.irName == iface
    && Scopes.givenVisibleFrom
      (currentScopeStore gctx ())
      useScope
      (Scopes.binderScope g.geBinder)
    && predicateRequestArgsMatch (PSArgsKnown args) g.geSlot.psArgs =
    Some (givenAnswerResidual g)
  | otherwise = firstPredForEnclResidual gctx iface args useScope rest

registerEachActive : GraphCtx -> List Int -> EvidenceBinderId -> Unit
registerEachActive gctx [] _ = ()
registerEachActive gctx (id :: rest) dname =
  gctx.graphRun.activeDictVars :=
    (id, dname) :: gctx.graphRun.activeDictVars.value
  registerEachActive gctx rest dname

-- extern declarations become top-level schemes (like interface methods)
--
-- 🚨 #1280: THE STAMPING WALK IS PART OF THIS FUNCTION, NOT OF ITS CALLERS, AND
-- THAT IS THE FIX.  Every other tree that reaches typecheck has already been
-- through `stampTyOrigins` at a driver (`stampGraphTyOrigins` on the module arm,
-- the retired single-program stamping path).
-- `runtimeDecls` was the one tree that reached a `Scheme` without ever entering
-- that walk on EITHER arm, so every `Mono` `fromAstTypeE` built out of an extern's
-- declared type carried `OriginUnresolved` — the SUPPLY half of the dispatch-key
-- blocker recorded at `dispHeadTab`, and the absent head #1279 bridges two
-- distinct identities through.
--
-- The scope is a parameter and not a `List Decl` prelude on purpose: two
-- `List Decl` arguments are positionally interchangeable and `stampTyHead`'s
-- immunity rule makes a wrong first stamp PERMANENT (`stampFlatTyOrigins`'
-- comment in `frontend/resolve.mdk` records that hazard costing a defect once
-- already).  Build it with `externTyOriginScope`, which owns the derivation of
-- WHY one scope is right for this population on both arms.
--
-- ⚠️ `externTyOriginScope []` at a call site is not a shrug: it is the same
-- historical "prelude boundary unknown" answer from that path when its
-- `coreProg0` is `[]` — those callers have already FLATTENED the prelude into the
-- program they check, so the prelude's own `Option`/`Ordering`/`Result`
-- declarations are unstamped on that path too and the two sides stay symmetric.
-- The builtin layer is still supplied there, so it is strictly more identity than
-- before, never a claim the driver cannot justify.
--
-- 🚨 FILTER BEFORE STAMPING, AND THAT ORDER IS PERFORMANCE, NOT STYLE.  The first
-- cut here was `externSchemesGo (stampTyOrigins scope decls)`, which is a no-op
-- difference for `runtimeDecls` (every element IS a `DExtern`) and wrong-shaped at
-- the `checkBodyImpl` call site, where `decls` is the WHOLE MODULE.  Read the
-- chain rather than take this on trust: `stampTyOrigins` is `map
-- (stampDeclTyOrigins scope)`, and `stampDeclTyOrigins` is `mapOriginsInDecl`,
-- i.e. a full `mapTyInDecl` REBUILD of the decl — so that shape reconstructs every
-- declaration in the program and then discards all but the externs, in a stage
-- `compiler/AGENTS.md` calls GC-bound.  Filtering first makes the walk
-- proportional to the externs, which is all this function reads.
--
-- ⚠️ THE MECHANISM ABOVE IS READ OFF THE SOURCE; THE MAGNITUDE WAS NOT MEASURED.
-- No before/after allocation number was taken, so this is a shape argument, not a
-- perf result — do not cite it as one.  It needs no number to be the right shape:
-- rebuilding what you are about to throw away is never the cheaper branch.
externSchemes : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap TyConOrigin ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, Scheme)
externSchemes mctx scope decls =
  let ds = externDecls decls
  -- #2074: THIS function is the stdlib extern CATALOG builder — its eight call
  -- sites all pass `runtimeDecls`, and `userExternSchemes` (below) is the
  -- declaration-site sibling that handles the program under check.  So this is
  -- the one seam where the set of names the emitter's `isAnyExtern` ladder will
  -- answer for is known, and it is recorded here rather than re-derived.  See
  -- `ffiIsBuiltinExternName` for what reads it and why.
  let _ = noteBuiltinExternNames mctx.mcGraph ds
  externSchemesGo mctx (stampTyOrigins scope ds)

-- Union, never replace: a driver may build the catalog seed more than once per
-- process (`medaka test` runs several engines), and a later call carrying a
-- shorter list must not shrink the set a guard is reading.
--
-- Each row records the catalog's written signature and the positions of its
-- argument binders, which `ffiCheckExternsShadow` and
-- `ffiCheckExternsCatalogRow` (#2163) both read: one map, so the two rules about
-- the same declaration cannot read two tables that fell out of step.
--
-- The signature's rows stay as written labels, not `List Atom`.  `atomsOfWritten`
-- resolves each bare label against `GraphCtx.effectDomains`, and this seam can
-- run before that registry is populated, so both sides are lifted at the check
-- seam, where the registry is the same for both.
--
-- Union means a re-seed REWRITES an existing row rather than skipping it — the two
-- seeds are the same `runtimeDecls` list, so the value is the same pair either
-- way, and preferring the later write keeps the map's contents a function of the
-- last seed rather than of call order.
noteBuiltinExternNames : GraphCtx -> List Decl -> Unit
noteBuiltinExternNames gctx ds =
  gctx.builtinExternNamesRef :=
    externSigsToMap ds gctx.builtinExternNamesRef.value

-- #2072 (epic #2070, R2): the DECLARATION-site sibling of `externSchemes`.
--
-- The eight `externSchemes … runtimeDecls` call sites above build the STDLIB EXTERN
-- CATALOG's schemes: `stdlib/runtime.mdk`'s 138 `extern` lines (derived: `grep -c
-- '^extern ' stdlib/runtime.mdk`), whose written rows ARE the effect vocabulary.
-- They must stay byte-identical.
--
-- THIS one is the `checkBodyImpl` call, which processes whichever program is under
-- check — normally a USER file, where an `extern f : Int -> <> Int` used to type as
-- a pure `Int -> Int`: a one-line escape hatch through the whole effect system.
--
-- 🚨 THIS FUNCTION NO LONGER REWRITES A DECLARED ROW (F1, epic #2070).  Its
-- predecessor STAMPED `FFI` into the terminal row whenever the label was absent,
-- which meant the declared row was never checked against what is enforced —
-- `<Net "a.com/*">` silently became `<FFI, Net "a.com/*">` exactly as `<>`
-- silently became `<FFI>`.  A signature that says one thing and types as another
-- is the defect, not the missing atom.  The honesty requirement is now a CHECK
-- (`ffiCheckExternsLabelled`, run beside the crossable guard at the same
-- `checkBodyImpl` seam): a user extern's terminal row must ALREADY name `FFI`,
-- whatever else it names, or the declaration is a located type error.  The scheme
-- built here is the declaration verbatim.
--
-- `mode` is still taken because every caller has one and the sibling guards read
-- it; the ownership gate now lives entirely on those guards.
userExternSchemes : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap TyConOrigin ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, Scheme)
userExternSchemes mctx scope decls =
  externSchemesGo mctx (stampTyOrigins scope (externDecls decls))

-- ── canonical checked FFI rows for backend input (#2174/#2135) ─────────────
--
-- A typed emitter must not reinterpret the written heads of `DExtern`: the five
-- declaration guards above have already expanded aliases through the current
-- module's alias table, and accepting one shape while lowering another is exactly
-- #2174's check/build split.  These two exported producers reuse the SAME helper
-- body (`expandAliasHeadTyWith`) against the alias carrier that survives the
-- relevant typed path:
--
--   * flat typed probes derive one side-effect-free stage-K `DataEnv` from their
--     already-stamped declaration list;
--   * module emitters read `DeclEnvs.deData.deAliases`, projected at each module's
--     own ordinal by the same visibility machinery the live typecheck used.
--
-- The builtin subtraction is a lookup in the extern catalog `noteBuiltinExternNames`
-- seeds.  These producers run after their drive, so they read the catalog from the
-- interners, which hold the catalog of the graph record most recently minted or restored.  Lowering
-- therefore no longer independently scans `runtimeDecls` to decide whether a checked
-- declaration routes as a builtin.
-- Typed emitters use these canonical producers for checked extern facts.
export
checkedFfiExternTypeNames : List Decl ->
  List (String, (List (String, String), (List String, String)))
checkedFfiExternTypeNames decls =
  let denv = dataEnvFromDeclsGo 0 decls emptyDataEnv
  ffiExternTypeRowsWith
    interners.value.externCatalog.value
    (aliasOwnAt 0 denv.deAliases)
    decls

export
checkedFfiExternTypeNamesModules : DriveOutputs ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  List (String, (List (String, String), (List String, String)))
checkedFfiExternTypeNamesModules o modules =
  flatMap
    (checkedFfiExternTypeNamesModule interners.value.externCatalog.value o)
    modules

checkedFfiExternTypeNamesModule : OrdMap (Ty, List (String, Int)) ->
  DriveOutputs ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  List (String, (List (String, String), (List String, String)))
checkedFfiExternTypeNamesModule catalog o (mid, decls) =
  let cur = ordOfIndex mid o.doOrdIndex
  let aliases =
    aliasOwnAt cur o.doFfiAliases ++ aliasUniverseAt cur o.doFfiAliases
  ffiExternTypeRowsWith catalog aliases decls

-- The current module's aliases arrive in front of its imported alias universe in
-- `checkBodyImpl`.  `DataEnv.deAliases` is already reverse declaration order, so
-- this filter preserves the exact first-match lookup order without rebuilding a
-- second registry.
aliasOwnAt : Int -> List (TabKey, AliasDecl) -> List (TabKey, (List String, Ty))
aliasOwnAt _ [] = []
aliasOwnAt cur ((key, ad) :: rest)
  | ad.adOrd == cur = (key, (ad.adParams, ad.adRhs)) :: aliasOwnAt cur rest
  | otherwise = aliasOwnAt cur rest

-- The pre-#1280 body, unchanged, over the ORIGIN-STAMPED list.  It is split out
-- rather than folded into `externSchemes` so that the recursion cannot re-enter
-- the origin-stamping walk on its own tail — the shape that turns a one-pass `map`
-- into a quadratic, which is the defect class `compiler/AGENTS.md` opens with.
--
-- It took a `stamp : Bool` until F1 (epic #2070), selecting whether to rewrite the
-- declared type with an `FFI` atom.  Both call sites now pass the declaration
-- through verbatim — the stdlib catalog always did, and the user-declaration site
-- checks the row instead of rewriting it (`ffiCheckExternsLabelled`) — so the
