-- parameter is gone rather than left as a constant nobody may vary.
externSchemesGo : ModuleCtx -> List Decl -> List (String, Scheme)
externSchemesGo mctx decls =
  map ((n, ty) => (n, sigToScheme mctx ty)) (directExternSigs decls)

directExternSigs : List Decl -> List (String, Ty)
directExternSigs [] = []
directExternSigs ((DExtern (ExternDecl { edName = n, edTy = ty, ... })) :: rest) =
  (n, ty) :: directExternSigs rest
directExternSigs (_ :: rest) = directExternSigs rest

declExternNames : List Decl -> List String
declExternNames decls = map fst (directExternSigs decls)

-- ── #2157: the OBLIGATION half of the same anchor ───────────────────────────────
--
-- #259 (above) fixed WHICH SCHEME a numeric literal instantiates — by interface
-- identity, out of the prelude `Num` declaration.  It did not fix which INTERFACE the
-- literal's impl-coverage obligation is recorded against: `inferNumLitMethod` routed
-- that through `recordImplObligation`, whose `methodEntryHere x` is a
-- bare method-NAME lookup with no interface-identity input at all.  A user module
-- declaring `interface Buildable c where fromInt : Int -> c` registers a SECOND row
-- under the key `"fromInt"`, last-write-wins, and every numeric literal in that module
-- then demanded `Buildable` instead of `Num` — `No impl of Buildable for Int` on
-- `println (1 + 2)`, on a program with no shadow of any kind (#2157).
--
-- ⚠️ The defect's true scope is the whole MODULE, not the same-named method's own impl
-- body: the table is per-module and the literal path reads it at every literal, so the
-- misfire needs only the `interface` DECLARATION, no `impl` and no occurrence of the
-- user's own method.  See `test/shadow_fixtures/x9_*` / `x10_*`.
--
-- The selected row is the only source for the numeric occurrence's scheme,
-- declared type, interface identity, and method-level slots.  A second declaration
-- walk could pair those fields from different duplicate declarations.

-- DRIVER-COLLAPSE Phase 2: skip when [mname] is ALREADY registered in THIS pass.
-- The ids must be the SAME quantified ids the call-site instantiation maps through
-- its subst (see the method carrier doc).  The module path's checkModuleFullImpl
-- can construct method rows more than once per pass (env setup + Flat name discovery
-- inference re-resolving schemes), and a SECOND registration prepends DIFFERENT
-- freshly-instantiated carrier → first-match would select metadata from the wrong
-- scheme build.  Keeping the FIRST (env-setup) registration — whose scheme is the one
-- lookupVar returns at call sites — restores the flat path's single-registration
-- invariant.  `freshModuleCtx` clears methodPredicateSlotsRef between modules, so this only
-- de-dups WITHIN a pass.

methodConstraintSlotIds : List String -> Ty -> List (String, Mono) -> List Int
methodConstraintSlotIds typarams (TyConstrained cs t) tvs =
  flatMap (constraintSlotId typarams tvs) cs
    ++ methodConstraintSlotIds typarams t tvs
methodConstraintSlotIds typarams (TyEffect _ _ t) tvs =
  methodConstraintSlotIds typarams t tvs
methodConstraintSlotIds _ _ _ = []

-- one slot per method-level constraint: the id of its dispatch var
-- (constraintSlotDispatchVar), which the supplied dict narrows by.
constraintSlotId : List String -> List (String, Mono) -> Constraint -> List Int
constraintSlotId typarams tvs c = match constraintSlotDispatchVar typarams c
  [] => []
  n :: _ => match lookupAssoc n tvs
    Some m => [monoTyvarId m]
    None => []

sigsOf : List Decl -> List (String, Ty)
sigsOf [] = []
sigsOf ((DTypeSig _ n ty _) :: rest) = (n, ty) :: sigsOf rest
sigsOf ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) = sigsOf (d :: rest)
sigsOf (_ :: rest) = sigsOf rest

-- every variable reference in an expr, bound ones included (an over-approximation
-- of its free references); the dependency graph uses `freeEVars` instead
allEVars : Expr -> List String
allEVars (EVar x) = [x]
allEVars (EVarId x _) = [x]
allEVars (EMethodAt n _ _) = [n]
allEVars (EDictAt n _) = [n]
allEVars (ELit _) = []
allEVars (EApp f x) = allEVars f ++ allEVars x
allEVars (ELam _ b) = allEVars b
allEVars (ELet _ _ _ e1 e2) = allEVars e1 ++ allEVars e2
allEVars (ELetGroup binds body) = flatMap letBindEVars binds ++ allEVars body
allEVars (EMatch e arms) = allEVars e ++ flatMap armEVars arms
allEVars (EIf c t e) = allEVars c ++ allEVars t ++ allEVars e
allEVars (EBinOp _ l r _) = allEVars l ++ allEVars r
allEVars (EUnOp _ e _) = allEVars e
allEVars (EInfix op l r) = op :: allEVars l ++ allEVars r
allEVars (EFieldAccess e _ _) = allEVars e
allEVars (ETuple es) = flatMap allEVars es
allEVars (EListLit es) = flatMap allEVars es
allEVars (EArrayLit es) = flatMap allEVars es
allEVars (ERangeList a b _) = allEVars a ++ allEVars b
allEVars (ERangeArray a b _) = allEVars a ++ allEVars b
allEVars (ESlice e a b _) = allEVars e ++ allEVars a ++ allEVars b
allEVars (EIndex e i) = allEVars e ++ allEVars i
allEVars (EAnnot e _) = allEVars e
allEVars (EBlock stmts) = flatMap doStmtEVars stmts
allEVars (ERecordCreate _ fs) = flatMap fieldAssignEVars fs
allEVars (ERecordUpdate e fs _) = allEVars e ++ flatMap fieldAssignEVars fs
allEVars (EVariantUpdate _ e fs) = allEVars e ++ flatMap fieldAssignEVars fs
allEVars (ELoc _ e) = allEVars e
allEVars (EDoOrigin _ e) = allEVars e
allEVars (EHeadAnnot e _) = allEVars e
allEVars (EAsPat _ e) = allEVars e
allEVars (EMapLit _ kvs) = flatMap kvEVars kvs
allEVars (ESetLit _ es) = flatMap allEVars es
allEVars (EDo _ stmts) = flatMap doStmtEVars stmts
allEVars (EStringInterp parts) = flatMap interpEVars parts
allEVars (EGuards arms) = flatMap guardArmEVars arms
allEVars (ESection s) = sectionEVars s
-- The arms above mirror `rewriteArgScoped`'s traversal (children only, binders
-- ignored).  What is left for the catch-all, derived against `Expr`'s full
-- constructor set, is exactly four
-- constructors that carry no sub-`Expr` reachable here:
--   ENumLit, EDictApp  — leaves;
--   EMethodRef         — no production verb mints one (see `declRefNames` below);
--   EVarAt             — minted by `annotateProgram`, which runs after typecheck.
-- A new reference-bearing constructor therefore needs an arm above: falling to the
-- catch-all silently drops a dependency edge rather than erroring.
allEVars _ = []

kvEVars : (Expr, Expr) -> List String
kvEVars (k, v) = allEVars k ++ allEVars v

interpEVars : InterpPart -> List String
interpEVars (InterpStr _) = []
interpEVars (InterpExpr e) = allEVars e

guardArmEVars : GuardArm -> List String
guardArmEVars (GuardArm guards body) =
  flatMap guardEVars guards ++ allEVars body

sectionEVars : Section -> List String
sectionEVars (SecBare op) = [op]
sectionEVars (SecRight op e) = op :: allEVars e
sectionEVars (SecLeft e op) = op :: allEVars e

letBindEVars : LetBind -> List String
letBindEVars (LetBind _ clauses _ _) = flatMap funClauseEVars clauses

funClauseEVars : FunClause -> List String
funClauseEVars (FunClause _ body) = allEVars body

armEVars : Arm -> List String
armEVars (Arm _ guards body) = flatMap guardEVars guards ++ allEVars body

guardEVars : Guard -> List String
guardEVars (GBool e) = allEVars e
guardEVars (GBind _ e) = allEVars e

doStmtEVars : DoStmt -> List String
doStmtEVars (DoExpr e) = allEVars e
doStmtEVars (DoLet _ _ _ e _) = allEVars e
doStmtEVars (DoBind _ e) = allEVars e
doStmtEVars (DoAssign _ e) = allEVars e
doStmtEVars (DoFieldAssign _ _ e) = allEVars e

fieldAssignEVars : FieldAssign -> List String
fieldAssignEVars (FieldAssign _ e) = allEVars e

-- The names `e` reads that are not bound by a binder inside `e` or in `bound`:
-- `allEVars` with the binders subtracted, for the dependency graph (`clauseRefs`).
-- Scoping follows resolve's `stampExpr`, the walk that decides which binding an
-- occurrence names: a lambda's and a clause's params, a let's pattern (in its own
-- right-hand side too when recursive), a let group's names, an arm's pattern and
-- its `<-` guards, and a statement's pattern for the statements after it.  An
-- `EVarId` is read by its name: a local letrec's bodies are stamped before they
-- are grouped, and every local occurrence carries the same id 0.
-- A recursive `DoLet` and a recursive non-`PVar` `ELet` bind the pattern in their own
-- right-hand side here, wider than `stampExpr`; the worst case is a group split that
-- could have stayed merged.
freeEVars : OrdMap Unit -> Expr -> List String
freeEVars bound (EVar x) = freeName bound x
freeEVars bound (EVarId x _) = freeName bound x
freeEVars _ (EMethodAt n _ _) = [n]
freeEVars _ (EDictAt n _) = [n]
freeEVars bound (EApp f x) = freeEVars bound f ++ freeEVars bound x
freeEVars bound (ELam ps b) = freeEVars (namesToSet (patVarsListTc ps) bound) b
freeEVars bound (ELet _ r p e1 e2) =
  let after = namesToSet (patVarsTc p) bound
  freeEVars (if r then after else bound) e1 ++ freeEVars after e2
freeEVars bound (ELetGroup binds body) =
  let inner = namesToSet (map letBindName binds) bound
  flatMap (freeLetBindEVars inner) binds ++ freeEVars inner body
freeEVars bound (EMatch e arms) =
  freeEVars bound e ++ flatMap (freeArmEVars bound) arms
freeEVars bound (EIf c t e) =
  freeEVars bound c ++ freeEVars bound t ++ freeEVars bound e
freeEVars bound (EBinOp _ l r _) = freeEVars bound l ++ freeEVars bound r
freeEVars bound (EUnOp _ e _) = freeEVars bound e
freeEVars bound (EInfix op l r) =
  freeName bound op ++ freeEVars bound l ++ freeEVars bound r
freeEVars bound (EFieldAccess e _ _) = freeEVars bound e
freeEVars bound (ETuple es) = flatMap (freeEVars bound) es
freeEVars bound (EListLit es) = flatMap (freeEVars bound) es
freeEVars bound (EArrayLit es) = flatMap (freeEVars bound) es
freeEVars bound (ERangeList a b _) = freeEVars bound a ++ freeEVars bound b
freeEVars bound (ERangeArray a b _) = freeEVars bound a ++ freeEVars bound b
freeEVars bound (ESlice e a b _) =
  freeEVars bound e ++ freeEVars bound a ++ freeEVars bound b
freeEVars bound (EIndex e i) = freeEVars bound e ++ freeEVars bound i
freeEVars bound (EAnnot e _) = freeEVars bound e
freeEVars bound (EBlock stmts) = freeStmtsEVars bound stmts
freeEVars bound (ERecordCreate _ fs) = flatMap (freeFieldEVars bound) fs
freeEVars bound (ERecordUpdate e fs _) =
  freeEVars bound e ++ flatMap (freeFieldEVars bound) fs
freeEVars bound (EVariantUpdate _ e fs) =
  freeEVars bound e ++ flatMap (freeFieldEVars bound) fs
freeEVars bound (ELoc _ e) = freeEVars bound e
freeEVars bound (EDoOrigin _ e) = freeEVars bound e
freeEVars bound (EHeadAnnot e _) = freeEVars bound e
freeEVars bound (EAsPat _ e) = freeEVars bound e
freeEVars bound (EMapLit _ kvs) = flatMap (freeKvEVars bound) kvs
freeEVars bound (ESetLit _ es) = flatMap (freeEVars bound) es
freeEVars bound (EDo _ stmts) = freeStmtsEVars bound stmts
freeEVars bound (EStringInterp parts) = flatMap (freeInterpEVars bound) parts
freeEVars bound (EGuards arms) = flatMap (freeGuardArmEVars bound) arms
freeEVars bound (ESection (SecBare op)) = freeName bound op
freeEVars bound (ESection (SecRight op e)) =
  freeName bound op ++ freeEVars bound e
freeEVars bound (ESection (SecLeft e op)) =
  freeName bound op ++ freeEVars bound e
-- Leaves.  `EMethodRef` and `EVarAt` never reach the dependency graph (see
-- `allEVars`'s catch-all), and are not counted there either.
freeEVars _ (ELit _) = []
freeEVars _ (ENumLit _ _ _) = []
freeEVars _ (EWideLit _ _ _ _) = []
freeEVars _ (EDictApp _) = []
freeEVars _ (EMethodRef _) = []
freeEVars _ (EVarAt _ _) = []

freeKvEVars : OrdMap Unit -> (Expr, Expr) -> List String
freeKvEVars bound (k, v) = freeEVars bound k ++ freeEVars bound v

freeName : OrdMap Unit -> String -> List String
freeName bound x = if omHasKey x bound then [] else [x]

freeInterpEVars : OrdMap Unit -> InterpPart -> List String
freeInterpEVars _ (InterpStr _) = []
freeInterpEVars bound (InterpExpr e) = freeEVars bound e

freeFieldEVars : OrdMap Unit -> FieldAssign -> List String
freeFieldEVars bound (FieldAssign _ e) = freeEVars bound e

freeLetBindEVars : OrdMap Unit -> LetBind -> List String
freeLetBindEVars bound (LetBind _ clauses _ _) =
  flatMap (c => clauseRefsUnder bound (funClausePair c)) clauses

clauseRefsUnder : OrdMap Unit -> (List Pat, Expr) -> List String
clauseRefsUnder bound (ps, body) =
  freeEVars (namesToSet (patVarsListTc ps) bound) body

freeArmEVars : OrdMap Unit -> Arm -> List String
freeArmEVars bound (Arm p guards body) =
  freeGuardsEVars (namesToSet (patVarsTc p) bound) guards body

freeGuardArmEVars : OrdMap Unit -> GuardArm -> List String
freeGuardArmEVars bound (GuardArm guards body) =
  freeGuardsEVars bound guards body

-- guards left to right, a `p <- e` guard binding `p` for the guards after it and
-- for the body
freeGuardsEVars : OrdMap Unit -> List Guard -> Expr -> List String
freeGuardsEVars bound [] body = freeEVars bound body
freeGuardsEVars bound ((GBool e) :: rest) body =
  freeEVars bound e ++ freeGuardsEVars bound rest body
freeGuardsEVars bound ((GBind p e) :: rest) body =
  freeEVars bound e
    ++ freeGuardsEVars (namesToSet (patVarsTc p) bound) rest body

freeStmtsEVars : OrdMap Unit -> List DoStmt -> List String
freeStmtsEVars _ [] = []
freeStmtsEVars bound ((DoExpr e) :: rest) =
  freeEVars bound e ++ freeStmtsEVars bound rest
freeStmtsEVars bound ((DoLet _ r p e _) :: rest) =
  let after = namesToSet (patVarsTc p) bound
  freeEVars (if r then after else bound) e ++ freeStmtsEVars after rest
freeStmtsEVars bound ((DoBind p e) :: rest) =
  freeEVars bound e ++ freeStmtsEVars (namesToSet (patVarsTc p) bound) rest
freeStmtsEVars bound ((DoAssign x e) :: rest) =
  freeEVars bound e ++ freeStmtsEVars (namesToSet [x] bound) rest
freeStmtsEVars bound ((DoFieldAssign _ _ e) :: rest) =
  freeEVars bound e ++ freeStmtsEVars bound rest

-- The Module arm's import overlay, registered over [env] without elaborating a
-- second time what the populations already hold.  A public data declaration is
-- elaborated once, by `appendDataUniverse` at the end of its own module's arm, and
-- an importer reads that payload back by declaration identity.  The overlay's other
-- decls (aliases, newtypes, attributed or private data, a declaration with no
-- identity) are registered exactly as `registerAllData` registers them.
--
-- A served declaration skips `recordDeclKinds` and `registerVariants`' kind, atom
-- and variance rows: it is public data of an earlier module, so stage K's seed
-- (`declEnvSeedDataUniverse`) already holds those rows under the same identity keys.
-- Its field-owner keys are still added, as `registerRecordInfoKeyed` adds them.
-- The overlay is folded in list order, because its tables are last-write-wins and
-- its named rows come last (`importedCtorTypeDeclsLastWins`).
-- [prog] is the reading module's own declarations.
registerImportOverlay : TcEnv -> List Decl -> List Decl -> TcEnv
registerImportOverlay env prog overlay =
  let _ = seedParamPolarityFixpointScoped env.teDyn.dcModule overlay overlay
  let ctorPop = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph.crossRun.universeCtorPop.value
  let recordPop = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph.crossRun.universeRecordPop.value
  let served = map (d => (d, overlayCachedRows ctorPop recordPop d)) overlay
  let _ =
    fold
      (_ p => match snd p
        None => recordDeclKinds env.teDyn.dcModule (fst p)
        Some _ => ())
      ()
      served
  let env1 =
    fold
      (e p => if isAliasDecl (fst p) then registerData e (fst p) else e)
      env
      served
  -- Cycles out before any field elaborates, as in `registerDeclsAliasesFirst`.
  let _ = rejectCyclicAliases env.teDyn.dcModule prog
  fold
    (e p => match snd p
      None => if isAliasDecl (fst p) then e else registerData e (fst p)
      Some rows => registerCachedRows e rows)
    env1
    served

-- The cached constructor schemes and record infos of [d], in variant order, when
-- every one of its constructors has a population row under its own identity; any
-- miss declines for the whole declaration.  Only `DData` has rows to serve, and
-- declining is never wrong: a declined decl is registered by `registerData`,
-- which is where a new `Decl` constructor has to be decided, so the final
-- clause covers every other constructor rather than naming each.
overlayCachedRows : SpellingPop Scheme ->
  SpellingPop RecordInfo ->
  Decl ->
  Option (List (String, Scheme), List (String, RecordInfo))
overlayCachedRows ctorPop recordPop (DData { dataCtors, dataOrigin, ... }) =
  cachedVariantRows ctorPop recordPop dataOrigin dataCtors
overlayCachedRows _ _ _ = None

cachedVariantRows : SpellingPop Scheme ->
  SpellingPop RecordInfo ->
  TyConOrigin ->
  List Variant ->
  Option (List (String, Scheme), List (String, RecordInfo))
cachedVariantRows _ _ _ [] = Some ([], [])
cachedVariantRows ctorPop recordPop o ((Variant cn payload) :: rest) = do
  ident <- mkIdent NsCtor o cn
  s <- spLookupIdent ident cn ctorPop
  recs <- cachedRecordRow recordPop ident cn payload
  later <- cachedVariantRows ctorPop recordPop o rest
  Some ((cn, s) :: fst later, recs ++ snd later)

-- A named-field variant's cached `RecordInfo`, as a zero- or one-row list; a
-- positional variant has none to look up.
cachedRecordRow : SpellingPop RecordInfo ->
  Ident ->
  String ->
  ConPayload ->
  Option (List (String, RecordInfo))
cachedRecordRow recordPop ident cn (ConNamed _ _) =
  map (ri => [(cn, ri)]) (spLookupIdent ident cn recordPop)
cachedRecordRow _ _ _ _ = Some []

registerCachedRows : TcEnv ->
  (List (String, Scheme), List (String, RecordInfo)) ->
  TcEnv
registerCachedRows env (ctors, recs) =
  let _ =
    fold
      (_ r => registerCachedRecord env.teDyn.dcModule (fst r) (snd r))
      ()
      recs
  fold (e c => addCtor e (fst c) (snd c)) env ctors

registerCachedRecord : ModuleCtx -> String -> RecordInfo -> Unit
registerCachedRecord mctx key ri =
  mctx.mcCells.recordByNameRef :=
    omInsert key ri mctx.mcCells.recordByNameRef.value
  mctx.mcCells.fieldOwnersRef :=
    addFieldOwners key (recordFieldNames ri) mctx.mcCells.fieldOwnersRef.value

-- ── dependency-ordered, SCC-merged letrec processing ──────────────────────
-- The prelude has forward references and mutual recursion throughout, so groups
-- must be type-checked in dependency order (a callee generalized before its
-- callers instantiate it polymorphically) with mutually-recursive cycles merged
-- into one letrec group (generalized together).  Mirrors the reference's
-- order_groups_by_deps + process_letrec_group (Phase 136).

-- ── Tarjan strongly-connected components (O(V+E)) ─────────────────────────
-- Replaces the former all-pairs-reachability + mutual-reachability SCC + topo
-- sort, which was O(n^3) in a module's top-level binding count and dominated
-- the multi-module typecheck (check_modules).  Emits SCCs in dependency-first
-- order (a "sink" component — no outside dependencies — finishes and is emitted
-- first), exactly what processSCCs needs.  State is held in module-level refs,
-- reset at the start of each run (processTopGroups runs sequentially per module).

depGraphMap : List String ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  OrdMap (List String)
depGraphMap names grouped =
  buildAdj names (namesToSet names omEmpty) grouped omEmpty

-- defs grouped by name ONCE (name -> its clauses, in defs order), so `depsOf`
-- does an O(log n) lookup instead of re-scanning all defs per name (was
-- O(names·defs)). Built by prepend (O(1)); `clausesOf` reverses on read to
-- restore defs order — so the per-name clause list is identical to the old
-- `clausesFor name defs`, keeping dep lists / SCC order / output byte-identical.
groupClauses : List (String, (List Pat, Expr)) -> OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr))
groupClauses defs = groupClausesGo defs omEmpty
groupClausesGo : List (String, (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr))
groupClausesGo [] m = m
groupClausesGo ((n, c) :: rest) m =
  groupClausesGo rest (omInsert n (c :: clausesAt n m) m)

clausesAt : String -> OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) -> List (List Pat, Expr)
clausesAt n m = match omLookup n m
  Some xs => xs
  None => []

clausesOf : String -> OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) -> List (List Pat, Expr)
clausesOf n m = revClauses (clausesAt n m) []

revClauses : List (List Pat, Expr) ->
  List (List Pat, Expr) ->
  List (List Pat, Expr)
revClauses [] acc = acc
revClauses (x :: xs) acc = revClauses xs (x :: acc)

buildAdj : List String ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  OrdMap (List String) ->
  OrdMap (List String)
buildAdj [] _ _ m = m
buildAdj (n :: rest) nameSet cbn m =
  buildAdj rest nameSet cbn (omInsert n (depsOf n nameSet cbn) m)

-- sig-name presence set (which top-level names carry a type signature), set once
-- per module in `processTopGroups` so `memberPeelSource` does an
-- O(log n) presence check instead of an O(sigs) `lookupAssoc` scan per SCC member
-- (was O(members·sigs) over the whole compiler). Module-level ref, matching the
-- `currentFn`/`curEffect` idiom; processing is sequential per module.

sigNamesToSet : List (String, Ty) -> OrdMap Unit -> OrdMap Unit
sigNamesToSet [] m = m
sigNamesToSet ((n, _) :: rest) m = sigNamesToSet rest (omInsert n () m)

-- PERF: name → declared signature, the same `sigs` assoc list as an index.  Three
-- sites (preunifySigsEx, checkEffectEscape, checkSigConstraintOne) did
-- `lookupAssoc m sigs` — an O(N) scan of EVERY top-level signature, run per member
-- of every group, so O(N²) over a large file.  Companion to `sigNameSetRef`, seeded
-- from the same `sigs` in processTopGroups.
--
-- Built from the REVERSED list: `omFromPairs` is last-write-wins, while the
-- `lookupAssoc` it replaces was first-match-wins, so reversing preserves which
-- signature a duplicated name resolves to.

processTopGroups : TcEnv ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  List (String, (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List String ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  (List (String, Scheme), OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)))
processTopGroups env sigs defs names exported =
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.sigNameSetRef := sigNamesToSet sigs omEmpty
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.sigTyMapRef := omFromPairs (reverseL sigs) omEmpty
  let grouped = groupClauses defs
  let ordered = tarjanSCCs names (depGraphMap names grouped)
  let result = processSCCs env sigs grouped ordered
  let _ = resolvePendingJoins env.teDyn 0
  let failures =
    EffectSolver.closeRootAuthorities
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.effectSummaries
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef.value
      (exportedRootCells exported (fst result))
      (widenOpenedFor env.teDyn.dcModule)
  -- read again after the close: a cell the root solved no longer appears
  let unsolved = rootCellsOf exported (fst result)
  let unsolvedIds = fold (acc (_, ids) => IdMap.union acc ids) Tip unsolved
  let _ =
    reportEffectSummaryFailures
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      (filterList (f => not (failureMentions unsolvedIds f)) failures)
  let _ =
    fold
      (seen u => reportUnsolvedExport env.teDyn.dcModule grouped seen u)
      Tip
      unsolved
  result

-- The authority cells an exported binding's published type holds unquantified:
-- a binding the value restriction keeps monomorphic leaves its type's cells to
-- the module root.
exportedRootCells : OrdMap Unit -> List (String, Scheme) -> Map Int Unit
exportedRootCells exported schemes =
  fold (acc (_, ids) => IdMap.union acc ids) Tip (rootCellsOf exported schemes)

rootCellsOf : OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List (String, Map Int Unit)
rootCellsOf exported schemes =
  flatMap
    ((name, scheme) =>
      if omHasKey name exported then match unquantifiedAuthIds scheme
        Tip => []
        ids => [(name, ids)]
      else
        [])
    schemes

failureMentions : Map Int Unit -> SummaryFailure ObligationSite -> Bool
failureMentions Tip _ = False
failureMentions ids failure = match failure.esfAuthority
  Some (lo, hi) =>
    anyList (c => IdMap.has (authvarId c) ids) (authVars lo ++ authVars hi)
  None => False

-- An exported binding whose published type (or residual context) still holds
-- a cell after the root solved: nothing in its module bounds it below, and an
-- importer cannot supply it later.  Each cell is reported once, at the first
-- exported binding that holds it; the obligations over it are this failure,
-- not separate ones.  Located at the binding's first located expression.
reportUnsolvedExport : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  Map Int Unit ->
  (String, Map Int Unit) ->
  Map Int Unit
reportUnsolvedExport mctx grouped seen (name, ids) =
  if IdMap.foldlWithKey (acc id _ => acc && IdMap.has id seen) True ids then
    seen
  else
    let loc = match clausesOf name grouped
      (_, body) :: _ => firstExprLoc body
      [] => None
    let _ =
      pushTypeErrorAt
        mctx
        "T-EXPORT-UNSOLVED-AUTHORITY"
        loc
        "exported binding `\{name}` has an authority in its type that nothing in this module determines; give `\{name}`, or the value it uses, a type signature that names the authority"
    IdMap.union seen ids
-- per-name dependencies: the other group names a binding's bodies reference FREE.
-- Consumed by depGraphMap → Tarjan.  An over-approximated edge is not harmless:
-- it merges two bindings into one SCC, which infers them monomorphically together
-- and can leak one member's constraints into the other's scheme.  So a local
-- binder or parameter that shadows a group name must not count as a reference to
-- it (`clauseRefs` → `freeEVars`).
depsOf : String -> OrdMap Unit -> OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) -> List String
depsOf name nameSet cbn =
  filterNonSelf
    name
    (keepGroupNames nameSet (dedup (groupRefs (clausesOf name cbn))))

groupRefs : List (List Pat, Expr) -> List String
groupRefs clauses = flatMap clauseRefs clauses

clauseRefs : (List Pat, Expr) -> List String
clauseRefs clause = clauseRefsUnder omEmpty clause

keepGroupNames : OrdMap Unit -> List String -> List String
keepGroupNames nameSet refs = filterList (r => omHasKey r nameSet) refs

filterNonSelf : String -> List String -> List String
filterNonSelf name xs = filterList (/= name) xs

-- process each SCC as a letrec group in topological order.  The clause map is
-- threaded through and returned: a Module-arm group's clauses come back MARKED
-- (`processSCC`), and `checkBodyImpl` writes them back into the module's tree.
processSCCs : TcEnv ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List (List String) ->
  (List (String, Scheme), OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)))
processSCCs env _ grouped [] = ([], grouped)
processSCCs env sigs grouped (scc :: rest) =
  let (env2, schemes, grouped2) = processSCC env sigs grouped scc
  let (restSchemes, grouped3) = processSCCs env2 sigs grouped2 rest
  (schemes ++ restSchemes, grouped3)

-- The Num obligations of variables that reach a boundary only through a
-- constrained callee's instantiation (a where helper generalized as
-- `Num r => a -> r`, used as `debug (two ())`).  They are on the call and
-- dictionary-application windows, not the boundary's own (#23); a top-level
-- group and a method body default them like any other candidate.
calleeNumObls : ModuleCtx -> Int -> Int -> List UObligation
calleeNumObls mctx callN0 dictN0 =
  numCallObls mctx.mcGraph (callUOblsWindow mctx callN0)
    ++ numDictObls mctx.mcGraph (dictAppsSince mctx.mcGraph dictN0)

-- #23 support: synthesize impl-obligation-shaped Num entries from a group's
-- pendingCallObligations / pendingDictApps deltas.  The Num constraint of an
-- ambiguous var reaching a group ONLY through a constrained-callee instantiation
-- (`main = println (app2 (==))`) is recorded on those refs, never on
-- pendingImplObligations, so group-level Num defaulting (defaultGroupNumWith /
-- groundNumVarsWith, which both reads candidate ids AND finds the live var to ground
-- from impl-shaped entries) never saw it — leaving an ungrounded var whose Num dict
-- route resolves RNone → a NULL dict word → build-time SIGTRAP (run is correct).
-- Only field 0 (iface) and field 3 (the live operand mono) are read downstream;
-- the rest mirror inferNumLitBare's placeholder shape.
-- Num is 1-param, so its obligation vector is a singleton; a wider predicate can
-- never be "Num" and is filtered out anyway.
numCallObls : GraphCtx -> List UObligation -> List UObligation
numCallObls gctx [] = []
numCallObls gctx (o :: rest) = match (o.pred.iface.irName, uOblArgs gctx o)
  ("Num", [mono]) =>
    mkMethodOccObl
        (builtinIfaceRef gctx BNum)
        ["a"]
        (TyVar "a")
        mono
        []
        PNumLit
        o.loc
        o.uoScope
      :: numCallObls gctx rest
  _ => numCallObls gctx rest

numDictObls : GraphCtx -> List PendingDictApp -> List UObligation
-- #1155: the loc comes from the ENTRY's own snapshot.  This runs at a generalized
-- group close, well after inference left the call site, where the record's `mcLoc`
-- names no construct of the entry.
-- Behaviour-neutral by inspection rather than by hope: these synthetic entries feed
-- ONLY the Num-defaulting search (`NumBoundaryOwnedScc` →
-- `numConstrainedIds`/`groundNumVarsWith` → `numObligIds`/`liveNumVarGo`), and every one
-- of those readers destructures the 5th element as `_`.  Nothing renders it today;
-- the point is that the tuple stops carrying a span it knows to be wrong.
numDictObls gctx [] = []
-- B-4b-iii: SPELLING consumer of the widened route carrier — the `"Num"` test is a
-- name test against the prelude spelling, unchanged, so `.irName` is projected here.
numDictObls gctx (app :: rest) =
  flatMap
      (p =>
        if fst p == "Num" then
          [
            mkMethodOccObl
              (builtinIfaceRef gctx BNum)
              ["a"]
              (TyVar "a")
              (snd p)
              []
              PNumLit
              app.pdaLoc
              app.pdaScope,
          ]
        else
          [])
      (zipL (map (i => i.irName) app.pdaIfaces) app.pdaMonos)
    ++ numDictObls gctx rest

-- #23 (two-hop forward): the impl-obligation-shaped entries for EVERY iface (not
-- just Num) a group's constrained-callee instantiations recorded on the call/dict
-- deltas.  Unlike numCallObls/numDictObls (which feed only Num-defaulting), these
-- feed registerSchemeObligations so a constraint FORWARDED from a constrained callee
-- (`useApp g = app2 g`, whose Num lives on the call/dict deltas, never on
-- pendingImplObligations) is recorded in schemeObligationsRef — so a caller of the
-- forwarder (`main = println (useApp (==))`) re-instantiates it (instantiateVarTracked),
-- surfacing the constraint on the caller's own delta where group Num-defaulting can
-- ground the shared ambiguous var.  Without this the forwarded var never grounds on
-- the check path and a downstream Eq/Ord obligation on it is falsely ambiguous.
-- #23 two-hop forward, VECTOR-PRESERVING.  A constraint forwarded from a constrained
-- callee lives on the pendingCallObligations delta, never in addedObls, so a caller of
-- this group must re-instantiate it from schemeObligationsRef.
--
-- This used to detour through a SYNTHETIC addedObls entry (iface, ["a"], TyVar "a",
-- mono, loc) that schemeObligationOne re-read via dispatchMonosOf.  That entry
-- structurally carries ONE Mono, so a joint predicate could not pass through it: it was
-- flat-mapped per ARGUMENT, and because each 1-ary shard lands on a bound tyvar,
-- boundTyvarIds SUCCEEDED and FABRICATED `Ix a` + `Ix i` alongside the real `Ix a i`
-- (one violation reported three times; `(Ix a, Ix a b, Ix b) =>` displayed).
--
-- The detour was pure overhead: dispatchMonosOf ["a"] (TyVar "a") m is an IDENTITY —
-- walkDispatch hits `contains "a" ["a"]` giving [("a", normalize m)], and collectByParam
-- reads it straight back out as [normalize m].  A pendingCallObligations entry ALREADY
-- carries its joint `List Mono`, so map it to bound tyvar ids DIRECTLY and the vector
-- survives at every arity.  Identical at arity 1 (boundTyvarIds normalizes too), and it
-- closes the UNSIGNED forwarding hole, which the declared-context path cannot reach
-- (lookupSigTvMap is None for an unsigned binding).
-- #1549: both scheme-obligation channels now project their entry to a PREDICATE
-- (`callPredOf` / `oblPredOf`) and map it through the ONE `vecOblOfPred` — so the
-- residual reduction §4 `gen` requires cannot be present on one channel and absent
-- from the other (this file's signature failure mode).
forwardedVecObls : ModuleCtx ->
  Bool ->
  List Int ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List VecObl
forwardedVecObls mctx generalizing boundIds callObls =
  flatMap
    (vecOblOfPred mctx generalizing boundIds)
    (flatMap callPredOf callObls)

-- the (interface, argument-vector) predicate a constrained-callee call-delta entry
-- carries.  An entry whose interface name is unrecoverable contributes nothing: the
-- name is what a VecObl is keyed and displayed by.
callPredOf : (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc)
callPredOf (iface, monos, loc)
  | iface.irName == "" = []
  | otherwise = [(iface, monos, loc)]

processSCC : TcEnv ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List String ->
  (TcEnv, List (String, Scheme), OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)))
processSCC outer sigs grouped0 members =
  -- The group's own checks (generalization, defaulting, its signatures'
  -- coverage) are located at its members' clause bodies.
  let env = envAtIfSome (membersSpanLoc grouped0 members) outer
  -- Marking on the schedule (ARCH §E): a Module-arm group is marked HERE, after
  -- every group it depends on has generalized, with the dict-name set as it stands;
  -- inference reads the stamped twin of the marked clauses.  Flat (`None`): the
  -- caller marked and stamped the whole program, the map is used as given.
  let marking = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.markingRef.value
  let grouped = match marking
    Some mm => markGroupClauses mm env members grouped0
    None => grouped0
  let groupedStamped = match marking
    Some mm => stampGroupClauses mm members grouped
    None => grouped
  let _ = enterLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let _ = beginEffectSummaryScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let oblN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let callN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls
  let dictN0 = goalsMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ()
  let placeholders = map (m => (m, freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule ())) members
  let scopedMembers =
    scopeMembers
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
      groupedStamped
      placeholders
  let (regs, sigTvMaps) = preunifySigsEx env.teDyn.dcModule sigs scopedMembers
  let savedRigidEffects = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidEffvarsRef.value
  let savedRigidAuths = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef.value
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidEffvarsRef :=
    fold
      (roots member =>
        IdMap.foldlWithKey
          (acc id _ => IdMap.set id () acc)
          roots
          member.smDeclaredRoots.value)
      savedRigidEffects
      scopedMembers
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef :=
    fold
      (roots member =>
        IdMap.foldlWithKey
          (acc id _ => IdMap.set id () acc)
          roots
          member.smDeclaredAuths.value)
      savedRigidAuths
      scopedMembers
  let env2 = extendBindings env (map scopedMemberBinding scopedMembers)
  -- P0-19 (constrained-receiver arm): publish THIS group's `=>`-constraint vars for
  -- the duration of body inference, so a definer-shadow method occurrence on one of
  -- them (`neq x y = not (eq x y)` under `neq : Eq a => …`) is seen as a DISPATCH and
  -- not monomorphised to the shadowing standalone's declared domain.
  -- `gcMonos` answers a SPELLING question (`dictVarSatisfiesIface`
  -- compares interface NAMES), so U1b (#1482) projects back to the name here rather than
  -- widening a second ref for a reader that would only throw the identity away.
  let groupCtx = GroupCtx {
    gcMonos = flatMap (r => flatMap ifaceMonoName (regIfaceMonosOf r)) regs,
    gcPendingEscapes = Ref [],
  }
  let groupEnv = { env2 | teDyn = { env2.teDyn | dcGroup = Some groupCtx } }
  -- #837: the schemeObligationsRef snapshot/restore window is RETIRED.  It existed
  -- because registerLocalScheme entries were NAME-KEYED and body-scoped: a prelude
  -- where-helper named `g` (core's `find`) leaked obligations onto an unrelated
  -- top-level `g` in a later body (a phantom `Num a =>` on types/numlit_bidir's
  -- signed fn).  Registration/lookup now key by (name, binding-id), so a top-level
  -- `g`'s use keys (g, its-id) and can never match a where-helper `g`'s (g, 0) entry.
  let _ = inferMembers groupEnv sigs groupedStamped scopedMembers
  let _ =
    fold
      (_ member => checkRecursiveValue env.teDyn member.smOwned)
      ()
      scopedMembers
  let _ =
    resolvePendingJoins env.teDyn env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value
  let residuals =
    finishEffectSummaryScopeKeeping
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      (quantifiableAuthorities env2 groupedStamped scopedMembers)
      (fold (acc member => memberEffectRoots member acc) Tip scopedMembers)
      (fold
        (acc member =>
          borrowedEffectCells env.teDyn.dcModule member.smOwned.bsValue acc)
        Tip
        scopedMembers)
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidEffvarsRef := savedRigidEffects
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef := savedRigidAuths
  let _ = checkSigsTooGeneral env.teDyn.dcModule sigTvMaps
  let _ = checkSigsFixedByExpansive env2 groupedStamped scopedMembers sigTvMaps
  let _ = registerConstraintRegs env.teDyn.dcModule regs
  let _ = flushPendingEscapes env.teDyn.dcModule (Some groupCtx)
  let _ = exitLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  -- PLAN.md #11 (locked §0.2): GROUP-LEVEL + per-binding Num defaulting.  Ground
  -- every ambiguous Num-only var to Int before this group generalizes.  A live var
  -- carried by a declared signature stays caller-determined across both passes;
  -- an argument-reachable var also stays polymorphic.  Body-only vars (`n = tag [1,2,3]`) still ground.  Scoped to
  -- THIS group's newly-added obligations (prepended at the front) so an earlier
  -- group's already-generalized var is never touched.
  let protectedSigIds = sccProtectedSignatureIds sigTvMaps
  let addedObls = wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls oblN0
  let groupObls = addedObls ++ callUOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0
  -- Determination holds rigid exactly the variables this group does not own: the
  -- declared ones and those in an argument position of a member's type, which the
  -- caller supplies.  A result-position or body-local variable is the group's.
  let unownedIds =
    omFromNames
      (map intToString (flatMap monoArgUnboundIds (map snd placeholders)))
      protectedSigIds
  let _ = improveByUniqueImpl env.teDyn protectedSigIds addedObls
  let _ =
    improveByUniqueImpl
      env.teDyn
      protectedSigIds
      (callUOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0)
  let _ = determineByUniqueInstance env.teDyn.dcModule unownedIds groupObls
  -- #23: also ground an ambiguous Num var that reaches this group ONLY through a
  -- constrained-callee instantiation (its Num obligation lives on the call/dict deltas,
  -- not pendingImplObligations).  See numCallObls/numDictObls.  The synthetic entries
  -- feed ONLY the Num-defaulting search; addedObls alone still drives the
  -- ambiguous-constraint/scheme-obligation registration below.
  let defaultObls = addedObls ++ calleeNumObls env.teDyn.dcModule callN0 dictN0
  let sccGuard = NumGuard {
    ngGoals = groupObls,
    ngRigidIds = protectedSigIds,
    ngOuterBelow = None,
  }
  let withheld = finalizeNumBoundary
    env.teDyn
    NumBoundary {
      nbDisposition =
        NumBoundaryOwnedScc (env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value + 1),
      nbMembers = map snd placeholders,
      nbSurvivingIds =
        tiedSurvivors
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
          (map snd placeholders)
          sccGuard
          protectedSigIds,
      nbDefaultObls = defaultObls,
      nbAmbiguityObls = addedObls,
      nbGuard = sccGuard,
    }  -- RETPOS soundness
  -- Defaulting is a substitution like any other, so the goals it changed are
  -- improved and determined once more.
  let _ = improveByUniqueImpl env.teDyn protectedSigIds groupObls
  let _ = determineByUniqueInstance env.teDyn.dcModule unownedIds groupObls
  let _ =
    checkSigVarGoals
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      DeclaredBySignature
      protectedSigIds
      sigTvMaps
      groupObls
  let schemes =
    sccSchemes
      env2
      sigs
      groupedStamped
      (isLetrecGroup members)
      residuals
      0
      scopedMembers
  let scopedSchemes = alignScopedSchemes scopedMembers schemes
  let _ = checkSigsOverExpansive env2 groupedStamped sigTvMaps
  -- #23 two-hop forward: also record constraints FORWARDED from a constrained
  -- callee (living on the call delta, never in addedObls) into schemeObligationsRef,
  -- so a caller of this group re-instantiates them and its own group can ground the
  -- shared ambiguous var.
  -- The CALL delta is passed RAW (it already carries each predicate's joint `List
  -- Mono`); registerSchemeObligations maps it with forwardedVecObls so a multi-param
  -- predicate survives whole.  #838 I5: a constrained callee's DICT slot is forwarded
  -- through THIS same call delta — inferDictAtFound records it as a 1-ary PCallSlot
  -- obligation (recordCallObligations, beside pushDictApp), so the old `allDictObls`
  -- re-derivation off the dict delta was a redundant duplicate (deduped away) and is
  -- retired; addedObls now carries only the real pendingImplObligations delta.
  let callOblsDelta = callOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0
  let _ =
    registerSchemeObligations
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.schemeDefIdsRef.value
      sigTvMaps
      callOblsDelta
      addedObls
      schemes
  let liveIds = liveMemberIds env.teDyn.dcModule (map snd placeholders)
  let _ =
    rejectUndeterminedVectors
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      unownedIds
      liveIds
      addedObls
      (callUOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0
        ++ nestedRequireGoals env.teDyn.dcModule unownedIds liveIds groupObls)
  let _ =
    rejectWithheldAmbiguity env.teDyn.dcModule unownedIds withheld groupObls
  -- SIGNATURE CONSTRAINT SOUNDNESS: a signed member whose body induces an
  -- interface constraint on one of its own quantified vars that its declared `=>`
  -- context (superclass-closed) does NOT cover severs the constraint for callers
  -- → wrong-dictionary dispatch (a silent wrong answer).  Reject at the def-site.
  -- Runs on every path; the census over compiler+stdlib+sqlite was 0 new failures.
  let _ =
    checkSigConstraintCoverage
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      regs
      sigs
      sigTvMaps
      callOblsDelta
      addedObls
      schemes
  let _ =
    registerInferredConstraints
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      sigs
      callOblsDelta
      addedObls
      scopedSchemes
  -- From here on every instance-head matcher holds this group's declared variables
  -- rigid; the group's own generalization above reads them as free variables, so a
  -- goal `checkSigVarGoals` rejected is not reported a second time.
  let _ = declareRigidVars env.teDyn.dcModule (omKeys protectedSigIds)
  -- The group's own occurrences of the members it just promoted (see
  -- `markRecursiveOccurrences`); Flat marks nothing here.
  let groupedOut = match marking
    Some mm =>
      markRecursiveOccurrences
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        mm
        placeholders
        scopedMembers
        grouped
    None => grouped
  let _ = match marking
    Some _ =>
      recordTopGrants
        env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
        env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentModuleRef.value
        schemes
        groupedOut
    None => ()
  (extendTermBindings outer schemes, schemes, groupedOut)

-- A multi-member SCC is a mutually-recursive group (always a function group, like
-- the oracle's DLetGroup); a singleton is a plain binding gated on its RHS.  Self-
-- recursive singletons have had their self-edge stripped (filterNonSelf) so they
-- arrive as size-1 SCCs — strict evaluation rules out a self-recursive zero-arg
-- value, so gating them on the RHS is sound and matches the oracle's DFunDef path.
isLetrecGroup : List String -> Bool
isLetrecGroup [] = False
isLetrecGroup [_] = False
isLetrecGroup _ = True

scopedMemberBinding : ScopedMember -> (String, EnvBinding)
scopedMemberBinding member =
  let binding =
    optionOr
      (ordinaryEnvBinding
        (Forall
          []
          []
          []
          []
          (memberForce member)
          member.smOwned.bsRecursiveValue))
      member.smRecursive.value
  (
    member.smName,
    bindingWithStandalone binding (LocalStandalone, binding.ebValue),
  )

memberForce : ScopedMember -> EffRow
memberForce member =
  optionOr (optionOr pureRow member.smForce) member.smForceBound.value

memberEffectRoots : ScopedMember -> Map Int Unit -> Map Int Unit
memberEffectRoots member roots =
  let inputs =
    if member.smSigned.value then
      roots
    else
      effectRoots member.smOwned.bsValue roots
  IdMap.foldlWithKey
    (acc id _ => IdMap.set id () acc)
    inputs
    member.smDeclaredRoots.value

scopeMembers : ModuleCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List ScopedMember
scopeMembers mctx _ _ [] = []
scopeMembers mctx parent grouped ((name, mono) :: rest) =
  let sid =
    Scopes.freshScope
      (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
      (Some parent)
      mctx.mcCells.currentLevel.value
      (Scopes.scopeFrame (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ()) parent).sfModuleId
      (BindingOwner name)
  -- This is the evaluator's topGroupValue distinction: a singleton nullary
  -- clause is a thunk, including a thunk whose result happens to be a function.
  let clauses = clausesOf name grouped
  let arity = match clauses
    (pats, _) :: _ => listLen pats
    [] => 0
  let owned = newBindingSummary arity (freshVar mctx) (freshEffectSummary mctx)
  let force = match clauses
    [([], _)] => Some owned.bsForce
    _ => None
  ScopedMember {
      smName = name,
      smMono = mono,
      smOwned = owned,
      smDeclaredRoots = Ref Tip,
      smDeclaredAuths = Ref Tip,
      smSigned = Ref False,
      smRecursive = Ref None,
      smForce = force,
      smForceBound = Ref None,
      smScope = sid,
    }
    :: scopeMembers mctx parent grouped rest

alignScopedSchemes : List ScopedMember ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List ScopedScheme
alignScopedSchemes [] [] = []
alignScopedSchemes (member :: members) ((name, scheme) :: schemes)
  | member.smName == name =
    ScopedScheme {
        ssName = name,
        ssScheme = scheme,
        ssScope = member.smScope,
      }
      :: alignScopedSchemes members schemes
  | otherwise = panic "scope/member scheme alignment mismatch"
alignScopedSchemes _ _ = panic "scope/member scheme arity mismatch"

-- Extended Pass A: same as preunifySigs but also returns the tyvar maps (for
-- the signature-too-general check after body inference).  Returns a pair:
-- (constraintRegs, sigTvMaps) where sigTvMaps is [(name, sig_ast, tvs)] for
-- each signed member.
-- #1161 (F-3a-ii): each reg is now a TRIPLE — (name, slot-parallel (iface, mono) pairs,
-- slot-parallel predicate argument VECTORS).  The first two components are unchanged;
-- the third is carried alongside, never instead of, so nothing downstream that sizes or
-- orders dict slots can move.
preunifySigsEx : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  List ScopedMember ->
  (List ConstraintReg, List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)))
preunifySigsEx mctx _ [] = ([], [])
preunifySigsEx mctx sigs (member :: rest) =
  let m = member.smName
  let v = member.smMono
  let (restRegs, restTvs) = preunifySigsEx mctx sigs rest
  match omLookup m mctx.mcCells.sigTyMapRef.value
    Some ty =>
      member.smSigned := True
      let (signedMono, tvs, forceBound) = instantiateSigTracked mctx ty
      member.smDeclaredRoots :=
        effectRowRoots
          (optionOr pureRow forceBound)
          (effectRoots signedMono Tip)
      member.smDeclaredAuths :=
        authRowRoots (optionOr pureRow forceBound) (authRoots signedMono Tip)
      member.smForceBound := forceBound
      let (declaredScheme, declaredTvs) = sigToSchemeTvs mctx ty
      let (Forall ids eids aids _ declaredForce declaredValue) = declaredScheme
      let slots =
        declaredPredicateSlots
          (constraintVarIfaceMonos (sigConstraints ty) declaredTvs)
          (constraintVarArgMonos
            mctx
            (sigConstraints ty)
            (sigConstraintArgTys ty)
            declaredTvs)
      member.smRecursive := Some EnvBinding {
        ebValue = ValueScheme {
          vsScheme =
            Forall
              ids
              eids
              aids
              []
              (match forceBound
                Some _ => declaredForce
                None => optionOr pureRow member.smForce)
              declaredValue,
          vsDeclared = Some CDeclared {
            cdSlots = predicateSlotCSlots slots,
            cdPrefix =
              CDPLen (listLen (dedupSlotVecs (map predicateSlotView slots))),
            cdArgs = predicateSlotArgs slots,
          },
        },
        ebMethodRow = None,
        ebStandalone = None,
      }
      let _ = bindFrom (dynFor mctx) v signedMono
      let regs = [
        ConstraintReg {
          crName = m,
          crScope = member.smScope,
          crIfaceMonos = constraintVarIfaceMonos (sigConstraints ty) tvs,
          crArgVecs =
            constraintVarArgMonos
              mctx
              (sigConstraints ty)
              (sigConstraintArgTys ty)
              tvs,
        },
      ]
      (regs ++ restRegs, (m, ty, tvs) :: restTvs)
    None =>
      let _ = unify mctx v member.smOwned.bsValue
      (restRegs, restTvs)

sigTvMapUnboundIds : (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) -> List Int
sigTvMapUnboundIds (_, _, tvs) = flatMap (p => monoUnboundIds (snd p)) tvs

-- A declared signature variable is a caller-chosen universal, so Num defaulting
-- never grounds it, whatever the group's shape. Every recursive occurrence of a
-- signed member instantiates its written contract afresh (`preunifySigsEx` installs
-- the declared scheme as `smRecursive`), so a declared variable never appears in
-- another member's type: an unsigned sibling's copy is its own inference variable
-- and defaults or generalizes under the ordinary rules. The former "shared by every
-- generalizable member" bound assumed monomorphic recursion, under which the
-- declared variable and the sibling's copy were one cell; with fresh contracts that
-- bound protected nothing, and both members of a signed mutual group defaulted to
-- Int without any too-general diagnostic.
sccProtectedSignatureIds : List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) -> OrdMap Unit
sccProtectedSignatureIds sigTvMaps =
  omFromNames (map intToString (flatMap sigTvMapUnboundIds sigTvMaps)) omEmpty

-- 🚨 ONE ENTRY PER PREDICATE (S-dict-arity-contract, #1318/B-4) — the (iface, bare
-- tyvar NAMES) pairs of a signature's `=>` constraints, ONE per constraint that has at
-- least one bare type variable ANYWHERE in its argument types, direct or NESTED
-- (`tyVarArgNames`'s `dedup (flatMap tyVarNames tys)` walks into `TyApp`/`TyFun`/`TyTuple`
-- spines, not just top-level `TyVar` arguments — S-structured-predicate-carry). So a
-- STRUCTURED-only constraint (`Tag (Wrap a) =>`, no bare argument, `a` only reachable by
-- descending into `Wrap a`) DOES carry a dict slot now.  Only a constraint whose
-- arguments are entirely ground/closed — no bare type variable anywhere in them, nested
-- or not — carries no dict slot and contributes nothing.
--
-- This list IS the dict-param cardinality of a `=>`-constrained top-level fn: it feeds
-- `registerMemberSlots` → `funConstraintsRef`, which `dictArityOf` (define side) and
-- `inferDictAtFound` (call side) both size from.  It used to emit one entry per bare
-- tyvar ARGUMENT — `Ix a b =>` shattered into TWO dict params for ONE predicate, both
-- routed from the same single-argument goal — so the emitted convention disagreed with
-- the METHOD-level channel (`methodLevelConstraintVarNames`/`constraintSlotDispatchVar`,
-- one slot per constraint since #818) and with the impl-`requires` channel
-- (`registerReqSlots`, one slot per ENTRY).  All three channels now agree: one dict per
-- predicate.  ⚠️ The names are kept as a LIST, not collapsed to the first one here,
-- because WHICH of them is still an abstract tyvar after body inference is not knowable
-- until `registerMemberSlots` normalizes the instantiated monos — and every abstract one
-- must still reach `activeDictVars`, or a body use dispatching on the predicate's SECOND
-- variable loses its route.
sigConstraints : Ty -> List (IfaceRef, List String)
sigConstraints (TyConstrained cs _) = flatMap constraintTyVars cs
sigConstraints _ = []

-- U1b (#1482): carries `constraintOrigin` (the #1110 interface-occurrence identity)
-- alongside the spelling, so `registerMember`'s slot-parallel iface list — and hence
-- every obligation `recordCallObligations` later mints from it — is identity-carrying.
constraintTyVars : Constraint -> List (IfaceRef, List String)
constraintTyVars (Constraint { constraintHead = iface, constraintArgs = tys, constraintOrigin = co }) =
  match tyVarArgNames tys
    [] => []
    ns => [(IfaceRef { irName = iface, irOrigin = co }, ns)]

tyVarArgNames : List Ty -> List String
tyVarArgNames tys = dedup (flatMap tyVarNames tys)

-- #1161 (F-3a-ii): slot-parallel to `sigConstraints` — the WHOLE predicate's argument
-- type list, ONE per slot.  `Ix a Char` and `Ix a b` are each ONE slot carrying their
-- full argument list (`[TyVar a, TyCon Char]` / `[TyVar a, TyVar b]`) — evidence for one
-- predicate, so one goal.
-- Length-parallel to sigConstraints by construction: both are `flatMap … cs` over the
-- SAME constraint list, and both emit one element per constraint that has at least one
-- bare tyvar argument.
-- Matches sigConstraints' TOP-LEVEL-`TyConstrained`-only shape deliberately, so the two
-- cannot desynchronize on a nested-constraint spine.
sigConstraintArgTys : Ty -> List (List Ty)
sigConstraintArgTys (TyConstrained cs _) = flatMap constraintTyVarArgs cs
sigConstraintArgTys _ = []

constraintTyVarArgs : Constraint -> List (List Ty)
constraintTyVarArgs (Constraint { constraintArgs = tys }) =
  match tyVarArgNames tys
    [] => []
    _ => [tys]

-- like constraintVarMonos but KEEPS the iface name paired with each constraint var's
-- mono (slot order preserved), so registerMember can register call-obligation ifaces.
-- S-dict-arity-contract: the payload is now the predicate's WHOLE bare-tyvar mono list,
-- one entry per predicate.  An entry survives when AT LEAST ONE of its names is in
-- [tvMap] (the drop rule `constraintVarArgMonos` mirrors exactly); the monos of the
-- names that are absent are simply not carried, which is what the per-name walk did.
constraintVarIfaceMonos : List (IfaceRef, List String) ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
constraintVarIfaceMonos [] _ = []
constraintVarIfaceMonos ((iface, names) :: rest) tvMap =
  match constraintNameMonos names tvMap
    [] => constraintVarIfaceMonos rest tvMap
    monos => (iface, monos) :: constraintVarIfaceMonos rest tvMap

-- #1161 (F-3a-ii): as constraintVarIfaceMonos, but yields each kept slot's predicate
-- argument vector as MONOS at the signature instantiation.  Drops exactly the slots
-- constraintVarIfaceMonos drops (same `lookupAssoc name tvMap` test, same walk), so the
-- two lists stay slot-parallel.
-- ⚠️ Resolves arguments with `fromAstType tvMap`, NOT `constraintArgMonos` — the latter
-- returns `None` for any argument that is not a bare type variable, i.e. exactly the
-- concrete `Char` in `Ix a Char` that is the whole point of recording the vector.
-- Every tyvar NAME reachable inside an argument is in [tvMap]: instantiateSigTracked
-- builds it from `tyVarNamesWithConstraints`, whose constraint half
-- (`constraintArgVarNames`) is a full structural `tyVarNames` walk of each argument —
-- so the interior `b` of `List b` is mapped, and fromAstType's unmapped-var → `TCon n`
-- fallback is unreachable here.
constraintVarArgMonos : ModuleCtx ->
  List (IfaceRef, List String) ->
  List (List Ty) ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List (List Mono)
constraintVarArgMonos mctx [] _ _ = []
constraintVarArgMonos mctx _ [] _ = []
constraintVarArgMonos mctx ((_, names) :: rest) (args :: argsRest) tvMap =
  match constraintNameMonos names tvMap
    [] => constraintVarArgMonos mctx rest argsRest tvMap
    _ =>
      map (fromAstType mctx tvMap) args
        :: constraintVarArgMonos mctx rest argsRest tvMap

-- After body inference, register each member's constraint variables by their
-- *surviving* (normalized) tyvar id: in activeDictVars (id → dict param name, for
-- in-body RDict routing) and per-fn in funConstraintsRef (for call-site dict
-- application).  Done per group so a callee's constraints are known before its
-- (later-group) callers infer.
registerConstraintRegs : ModuleCtx -> List ConstraintReg -> Unit
registerConstraintRegs mctx [] = ()
registerConstraintRegs mctx (reg :: rest) =
  let _ =
    registerMember mctx reg.crName reg.crScope reg.crIfaceMonos reg.crArgVecs
  registerConstraintRegs mctx rest

-- #994 (B-3-a): THE per-entry write op for the fn-constraint tables.  `CSlot` (U1b,
-- #1482) stopped every CONSUMER of a callee's constraint slots from holding two parallel
-- lists; this stops the two PRODUCERS — `registerMember` and `registerInferredFor` —
-- from holding them either.  Both projections come off ONE `CSlot` list, so
-- `funConstraintsRef`'s ids and `funConstraintIfacesRef`'s ifaces are slot-parallel by
-- TYPE here, not by a filter each writer re-derives and keeps in step by hand.
--
-- ⚠️ [argsOpt] is `None` for a writer that registers no `funConstraintArgsRef` entry at
-- all — since S-inferred-vector-supply (#1869) that is `registerInferredFor` only when it
-- recovered NO vector for any slot (`inferredArgsOpt`), not unconditionally as before —
-- and that is why the arg vectors CANNOT join `CSlot`:
-- `keptConstraintArgs` stops when its vector list runs out, so the args payload is
-- legitimately a PREFIX of the slots, and folding it in per-slot would either truncate
-- the id list (a dict-ARITY change) or invent a vector.  Entry-ABSENCE is also
-- meaningful — an ids-only entry is a distinct state from an entry with empty args.
setFunConstraintEntry : ModuleCtx -> String -> List PredicateSlot -> Unit
-- multi-line RHS: the indented `:=` form is legal but not seed-parseable yet (#1744)
-- lint-disable-next-line rule-prefer-assign-op
setFunConstraintEntry mctx m slots =
  mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsRef :=
    (m, slots) :: mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsRef.value
  mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsIdxRef :=
    omInsert m slots mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsIdxRef.value
  -- B-2.2-f (#1113): the DECLARED-prefix sidecar, written in the SAME op as the ids it
  -- describes so the two can never be written apart.
  --
  -- 🚨 The DEDUPED length, not `listLen slots` — MEASURED, not defensive.  The expansion
  -- starts from the deduped declared slots, so a signature whose context names one
  -- interface twice on one tyvar (`twice : (Shw a, Shw a) => a -> Int`) contributes ONE
  -- slot where `slots` holds two.  Recording the unshrunk length would put `index < k` one
  -- slot past the real declared prefix and mark the first APPENDED super slot as declared —
  -- the unsafe direction, silently.
  -- 🚨 S-slot-key-vector (#1866): it must be the SAME dedup the expansion runs, and that
  -- is now `dedupSlotVecs` over the slots PAIRED WITH THEIR VECTORS.  Keeping the
  -- vector-free dedup that used to stand here (`dedupSlots`, now deleted — see
  -- `cslotKey`) would under-count `(Ix a Char, Ix a Bool) => …` (one
  -- where the expansion now yields two) and re-introduce the same off-by-one in the other
  -- direction.  [argsOpt] is the very prefix `expandSupersEntry` reads back out of
  -- `funConstraintArgsRef`, so the two dedups see identical input; `None` (no vector row
  -- at all) yields `[]` per slot, i.e. exactly the pre-widening count.
  let _ =
    setRef
      mctx.mcCells.funConstraintDeclaredRef
      ((m, CDPLen (listLen (dedupSlotVecs (map predicateSlotView slots))))
        :: mctx.mcCells.funConstraintDeclaredRef.value)
  ()

-- register a member's constraints: ids into funConstraintsRef + activeDictVars (the
-- kept/abstract slots), and the SLOT-ALIGNED iface names into funConstraintIfacesRef.
-- declaredPredicateSlots keeps a slot only when its mono is still an abstract TVar (a
-- body-forced-concrete constraint takes no dict slot); it emits the (iface, id) pair in
-- ONE traversal, so the iface list cannot be filtered differently from the id list.
registerMember : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  List (List Mono) ->
  Unit
-- An UNCONSTRAINED member (empty constraint list) gets NO funConstraintsRef /
-- funConstraintIfacesRef entry.  These refs are keyed by BARE NAME and accumulate
-- across the per-module elaboration; an unconstrained top-level fn that shares a
-- name with a constrained one in another module (e.g. array.mdk's `find : (a ->
-- Bool) -> Array a -> Option a` vs core.mdk's `find : Foldable t => …`) would
-- otherwise register a `(find, [])` entry that, prepended later, wins the
-- first-match lookup over core's `(find, [foldableId])`.  inferDictAt then reads 0
-- constraint ids → 0 dict args at the call site → `unbound identifier:
-- $dict_find_0` at eval.  An unconstrained fn is never marked EDictAt, so it needs
-- no entry (mirrors registerInferredFor's empty-ids guard).
registerMember mctx _ _ [] _ = ()
registerMember mctx m scope ifaceMonos argVecs =
  let slots = declaredPredicateSlots ifaceMonos argVecs
  let _ = registerPredicateSlotIds mctx.mcGraph scope 0 slots
  -- #1909: the PREDICATE-keyed half of the given, alongside the tyvar-id half
  -- `registerPredicateSlotIds` just wrote. Exactly `registerReqSlots`' pairing, one channel
  -- over — see `registerSlotPredGivens`.
  let _ = registerSlotPredGivens mctx.mcGraph scope 0 slots
  setFunConstraintEntry mctx m slots

-- #1161 (F-3a-ii): the argument vectors of the constraints declaredPredicateSlots KEEPS,
-- in the same slot order — the same `normalize`-is-a-TVar filter applied to the parallel
-- vector list, so funConstraintArgsRef stays slot-parallel to funConstraintsRef's ids.
-- ⚠️ It is a PREFIX, not a full parallel list, when [argVecs] is shorter than the
-- constraint list (`constraintVarArgMonos` drops constraints absent from the tvs map):
-- the second clause stops early.  That is why #994's fusion keeps this payload
-- entry-level and OPTIONAL instead of folding it into `CSlot` — see
-- `setFunConstraintEntry`.
-- A constraint variable forced concrete by the body takes no dict slot.
--
-- #994 (B-3-a): emits `CSlot`s, not a bare id list.  The iface half used to be recovered
-- by a SECOND traversal (`keptConstraintIfaces`, deleted) applying the identical
-- `normalize mono` is-a-`TVar` filter to the identical list; one traversal carrying the
-- pair makes "the iface list is filtered the same way" unrepresentable-otherwise instead
-- of a comment two functions apart.
-- S-dict-arity-contract: ONE slot per PREDICATE.  [monos] is NOT the predicate's own
-- argument-type list (that can be structured, e.g. `[Wrap a]` for `Tag (Wrap a)`) — it is
-- the instantiated monos of the bare tyvar NAMES `sigConstraints`/`tyVarArgNames` found
-- inside those argument types, direct or nested, one per name
-- (`constraintNameMonos`/`constraintVarArgMonos`).  Each entry of [monos] is therefore
-- always a `TVar` at the signature instantiation, never a structured mono, even when the
-- predicate's own argument was structured.  The slot survives when at
-- least one of them is still abstract after body inference (a predicate ALL of whose
-- variables the body forced concrete takes no dict, as before), and it is keyed on the
-- FIRST such id — the same "first dispatch variable" rule the method-level channel has
-- used since #818 (`constraintSlotDispatchVar`).
--
-- ⚠️ EVERY abstract id of the predicate is registered in `activeDictVars` against THAT
-- ONE slot, not just the lead: `Ix a b => …` binds one dict param, and a body use whose
-- dispatch variable is `b` must still find it.  `activeDictVarForEncl`'s id-keyed lookup
-- is what answers those sites (`enclSlotIndex`'s predicate/first-id rungs are keyed on
-- the slot's lead id and legitimately miss).  This mirrors `registerReqSlots`'
-- `registerEachActive`, which has keyed many ids onto one `requires` slot all along.
declaredPredicateSlots : List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  List (List Mono) ->
  List PredicateSlot
declaredPredicateSlots [] _ = []
declaredPredicateSlots ((iface, monos) :: rest) [] = match abstractSlotIds monos
  [] => declaredPredicateSlots rest []
  id :: more =>
    PredicateSlot {
        psIface = iface,
        psArgs = PSArgsUnknown,
        psBoundIds = id :: more,
      }
      :: declaredPredicateSlots rest []
declaredPredicateSlots ((iface, monos) :: rest) (args :: argRest) =
  match abstractSlotIds monos
    [] => declaredPredicateSlots rest argRest
    id :: more =>
      PredicateSlot {
          psIface = iface,
          psArgs = PSArgsKnown args,
          psBoundIds = id :: more,
        }
        :: declaredPredicateSlots rest argRest

registerPredicateSlotIds : GraphCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  Int ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  Unit
registerPredicateSlotIds gctx _ _ [] = ()
registerPredicateSlotIds gctx scope kept (slot :: rest) =
  let _ = registerEachActiveId gctx slot.psBoundIds (Scopes.binderAt scope kept)
  registerPredicateSlotIds gctx scope (kept + 1) rest

-- the ids of [monos] that are still ABSTRACT type variables, in order.  The filter
-- `declaredPredicateSlots` and `keptConstraintArgs` must agree on, factored so the two
-- cannot drift (they decide, respectively, whether a slot exists and whether its
-- argument vector is recorded — a disagreement desynchronizes `funConstraintArgsRef`
-- from `funConstraintsRef`).
abstractSlotIds : List Mono -> List Int
abstractSlotIds [] = []
abstractSlotIds (mono :: rest) = match normalize mono
  TVar cell => tyvarId cell :: abstractSlotIds rest
  _ => abstractSlotIds rest

registerEachActiveId : GraphCtx -> List Int -> EvidenceBinderId -> Unit
registerEachActiveId gctx [] _ = ()
registerEachActiveId gctx (id :: rest) dname =
  gctx.graphRun.activeDictVars :=
    (id, dname) :: gctx.graphRun.activeDictVars.value
  registerEachActiveId gctx rest dname

-- #1909: the SIGNATURE channel's `registerPredGiven` call — the one `registerReqSlots`
-- has made since #412 and this side never did.  `registerEachActiveId` above registers a
-- fn's declared `=>` given by TYVAR ID only, which cannot express a STRUCTURED given:
-- `Tag (Wrap a) => …` registers only `a`'s id, and the body's goal `Tag (Wrap a)` looks
-- up through `activeDictVarOf`, which recurses to the spine head (`TCon "Wrap"`) and
-- finds no tyvar — so `entailAssum` was unreachable by construction, `entail` fell to
-- `entailInst`, and the body was statically committed to whichever impl `entailInst`
-- picked against the ABSTRACTION-time goal, discarding the per-instantiation dict the
-- call site (`routesOfMonosTopV` → `pickMostSpecificEntry`) had already built correctly.
-- `registerPredGiven`'s header carries the same paragraph for the `requires` channel.
--
-- ⚠️ NO SELECTOR IS CALLED HERE, and none may be: `typecheck.mdk`'s assum-rung rule is
-- that no selector call may be reachable from `entailAssum`.  This restores an EARLIER
-- rung's ability to answer; it does not re-select.
--
-- [slot] counts dict params the way `registerMemberSlots`' `kept` does, so the nth kept
-- slot gets `dictParamName m n`.  The vector list is legitimately a PREFIX of the slots
-- (`keptConstraintArgs` stops when its input runs out — see `setFunConstraintEntry`), so
-- the second clause stops early rather than inventing a subject for a vectorless slot.
registerSlotPredGivens : GraphCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  Int ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  Unit
registerSlotPredGivens gctx _ _ [] = ()
registerSlotPredGivens gctx scope slot (s :: srest) =
  let _ = registerFunPredGiven gctx s (Scopes.binderAt scope slot)
  registerSlotPredGivens gctx scope (slot + 1) srest

registerFunPredGiven : GraphCtx -> PredicateSlot -> EvidenceBinderId -> Unit
registerFunPredGiven gctx slot binder
  | slot.psIface.irName == "" = ()
  | otherwise =
    let _ = pushGiven gctx GMPredicate DirectGiven slot binder
    registerFunPredGivenSlots gctx (predicateSlotKnownSupers gctx slot) binder

-- A signature slot's supers share its dict parameter: the dictionary it receives
-- carries them, and a super is answered by projecting it (`givenEvidenceBinder`).
registerFunPredGivenSlots : GraphCtx ->
  List (PredicateSlot, List Int) ->
  EvidenceBinderId ->
  Unit
registerFunPredGivenSlots gctx [] _ = ()
registerFunPredGivenSlots gctx ((slot, path) :: rest) binder =
  let _ = pushGiven gctx GMPredicate (ProjectedGiven binder path) slot binder
  registerFunPredGivenSlots gctx rest binder

-- A dictionary supplied for one predicate also supplies every transitive
-- superinterface.  The original predicate is registered separately as direct evidence;
-- all aliases retain the SAME dict parameter, so this does not alter dict arity.
-- Prelude chains (`Thenable` -> `Applicative` -> `Mappable`) are evidence exactly as
-- user ones are.  Unknown vectors stay direct-only:
-- projecting a superclass argument without the sub-predicate's positional vector would
-- invent identity.
predicateSlotKnownSupers : GraphCtx ->
  PredicateSlot ->
  List (PredicateSlot, List Int)
predicateSlotKnownSupers gctx slot = match slot.psArgs
  PSArgsUnknown => []
  PSArgsKnown args =>
    map
      (n => (predicateSlotOfNode n, drop 1 n.superPath))
      (filter
        (n => listLen n.superPath > 1)
        (superClosure (superLookup gctx) predicateSuperStep predicateNodeKey [
          (slot.psIface, args),
        ]))

-- One predicate by interface identity and structural argument vector.
predicateNodeKey : IfaceRef -> List Mono -> String
predicateNodeKey iface monos =
  "\{regKeyRender (regKeyOfTab (oblIfaceKey iface))}|\{joinWith "," (map oblArgKey monos)}"

predicateSuperStep : List String -> List Mono -> Super -> Option (List Mono)
predicateSuperStep typarams args (Super { superParams = params, ... })
  | listLen args /= listLen typarams = None
  | otherwise = mapAll (p => lookupPos p typarams args) params

predicateSlotOfNode : SuperNode (List Mono) -> PredicateSlot
predicateSlotOfNode n = PredicateSlot {
  psIface = n.superIface,
  psArgs = PSArgsKnown n.superPayload,
  psBoundIds = dedupI (flatMap monoTyvarIds n.superPayload),
}

-- Pass B: infer each member's clauses, unifying with its placeholder.
-- Phase 73 (bidirectional, signature-driven parameter typing): a member WITH a
-- signature peels its declared arrow types onto the clause parameter patterns
-- BEFORE inferring the body, so the body sees concrete parameter types (a
-- receiver-directed field access `f p = p.x` or a `String`-indexed `s.[0]`
-- resolves from the signature alone).  [peel] is Some(placeholder) for a signed
-- member, None otherwise; the placeholder already holds the sig instantiation
-- (preunifySigsEx unified it), and its shared tyvars accumulate unifications
-- across clauses exactly as the oracle's `sig_t` does.  Purely additive: the
-- per-clause `unify v arrow` below imposes the same equalities anyway.
inferMembers : TcEnv ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List ScopedMember ->
  Unit
inferMembers env _ _ [] = ()
inferMembers outer sigs grouped (member :: rest) =
  let m = member.smName
  -- A member's own checks (its signature against its value, its forcing
  -- bound, its effect escape) are located at its clauses' bodies.
  let env = envAtIfSome (membersSpanLoc grouped [m]) outer
  let v = member.smMono
  let _ = openScope env.teDyn.dcModule member.smScope
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn := m
  let peel = memberPeelSource env.teDyn.dcModule sigs m v
  let effs = inferMemberClauses env peel member.smOwned (clausesOf m grouped)
  -- The signature is checked against the value the clauses return.
  let _ =
    if member.smSigned.value then
      unifyInto
        (dynAtIfSome
          (joinLocs (clauseSpans valueSpanLoc grouped [m]))
          env.teDyn)
        True
        member.smMono
        member.smOwned.bsValue
  let _ = match member.smForceBound.value
    Some bound =>
      let _ =
        fold
          (_ cl => recordFileBound env.teDyn.dcModule (snd cl) bound)
          ()
          (clausesOf m grouped)
      rowInto
        env.teDyn
        True
        (effrowNorm bound)
        (effrowNorm (optionOr pureRow member.smForce))
    None => ()
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn := ""
  let _ = closeScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  -- A value signature constrains the returned value, not the cost of forcing
  -- its initializer. That cost travels on the binding and is checked at uses.
  let _ = match member.smForce
    None => checkEffectEscape env.teDyn sigs m effs
    Some _ => ()
  inferMembers outer sigs grouped rest

-- The span of the named members' clause bodies (`exprSpanLoc`), joined.
membersSpanLoc : OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) -> List String -> Option Loc
membersSpanLoc grouped names = joinLocs (clauseSpans exprSpanLoc grouped names)

-- [span] of each clause body of the named members.
clauseSpans : (Expr -> Option Loc) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List String ->
  List Loc
clauseSpans span grouped names =
  flatMap
    (m =>
      flatMap
        (cl => option [] (l => [l]) (span (snd cl)))
        (clausesOf m grouped))
    names

-- The span of the expression whose value [e] is: a `let … in`, which has no
-- span of its own, returns its body's value, and a block returns its last
-- statement's.
valueSpanLoc : Expr -> Option Loc
valueSpanLoc (ELoc l _) = Some l
valueSpanLoc (ELet _ _ _ _ body) = valueSpanLoc body
valueSpanLoc (ELetGroup _ body) = valueSpanLoc body
valueSpanLoc (EBlock stmts) = match last stmts
  Some (DoExpr e) => valueSpanLoc e
  _ => exprSpanLoc (EBlock stmts)
valueSpanLoc e = exprSpanLoc e

-- the peel source for a member: Some placeholder if it has a signature (peel the
-- declared arrow domains onto the clause params), None otherwise
memberPeelSource : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  String ->
  Mono ->
  Option Mono
memberPeelSource mctx sigs m v =
  map (_ => v) (omLookup m mctx.mcCells.sigNameSetRef.value)

-- zip-unify the equal-length prefix of param types and peeled sig domains; a
-- shorter [qs] (partial sig) pushes nothing past its end
-- Domains constrain the recursive placeholder as each clause is inferred.
-- Produced results join once after all alternatives are known: the first
-- clause must not fix a returned callback's row for its siblings.
inferMemberClauses : TcEnv ->
  Option Mono ->
  BindingSummary ->
  List (List Pat, Expr) ->
  List Atom
inferMemberClauses env _ _ [] = []
inferMemberClauses env peel owned clauses =
  let (values, effects) = inferClauseValues env peel owned clauses
  let _ = publishProducedResults env.teDyn owned values
  effrowLabels (collectRows (joinCellOf env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph) effects)

inferClauseValues : TcEnv ->
  Option Mono ->
  BindingSummary ->
  List (List Pat, Expr) ->
  (List (Option Loc, Mono), List EffRow)
inferClauseValues env _ _ [] = ([], [])
inferClauseValues env peel owned (cl :: rest) =
  let ce = inferClauseEff env peel cl
  -- A clause that does not fit the member's type is reported at the value it
  -- returns.
  let value = valueSpanLoc (snd cl)
  let _ =
    unifySourceDomains
      (dynAtIfSome value env.teDyn)
      (listLen (fst cl))
      owned.bsValue
      (fst ce)
  let _ = recordEffectBody env.teDyn.dcModule owned.bsBody (snd ce)
  let (values, effects) = inferClauseValues env peel owned rest
  ((value, fst ce) :: values, snd ce :: effects)

-- infer one clause, returning its arrow type AND the concrete effect labels its
-- body performs (captured in a fresh collection, then the ambient restored —
-- building a closure performs nothing).  Mirrors inferLam but exposes the effect.
-- Phase 73: when [peel] is Some(sig source) and the clause has params, peel the
-- signature's arrow domains and zip-unify them onto the clause param types BEFORE
-- inferring the body (bidirectional checking mode).
inferClauseEff : TcEnv -> Option Mono -> (List Pat, Expr) -> (Mono, EffRow)
inferClauseEff outer peel (pats, body) =
  -- The clause is located at its body: patterns carry no source Loc, so an
  -- over-applied-constructor / arity pattern error lands on this clause, and a
  -- body the parser leaves unwrapped (an application, an operator) is still
  -- located.  See the twin note in inferLam.
  let env = envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc body) outer
  let lits = takePatLits env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let pr = inferPats env pats
  let _ = peelOntoParams env.teDyn peel (fst pr) pats
  let scope =
    openExistentialScope
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      (takeOpenedExistentials env.teDyn.dcModule ())
  let _ = settlePatLits env.teDyn lits
  let _ = match peel
    Some src => recordClauseFileBound env.teDyn.dcModule body (listLen pats) src
    None => ()
  -- #2109: a signed clause's body is inferred AGAINST the signature's result
  -- type (result-first), so a fresh construction at a non-covariant slot meets
  -- the declaration while its own slot is still a metavariable.  See
  -- `inferExpected`.  An unsigned clause is byte-identical to before.
  let (bodyTy, bodyEff) = captureEffects
    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.curEffect
    (joinCellOf env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph)
    (_ => match peel
      Some src => match resultAfterArrows (listLen pats) src
        Some expected =>
          let bodyEnv = extendLocalVars env (snd pr)
          checkedInto
            bodyEnv
            body
            expected
            (inferExpected bodyEnv body expected)
        None => infer (extendLocalVars env (snd pr)) body
      None => infer (extendLocalVars env (snd pr)) body)
  let _ = closeExistentialScope env.teDyn.dcModule scope bodyTy (exprLoc body)
  (arrowsWithLastEffect (fst pr) bodyEff bodyTy, bodyEff)

-- Phase 73 peel: for a signed clause with params, zip-unify the peeled sig
-- domains onto the inferred param types.  No-op for an unsigned member, a value
-- binding (no params), or a sig with no remaining arrows.
peelOntoParams : DynCtx -> Option Mono -> List Mono -> List Pat -> Unit
peelOntoParams dyn None _ _ = ()
peelOntoParams dyn (Some _) _ [] = ()
peelOntoParams dyn (Some src) patTypes pats =
  zipBindFrom dyn patTypes (peelArrows (listLen pats) src)

-- a signatured binding's body must not perform a concrete effect its signature
-- doesn't declare; effect *variables* (polymorphic `<e>`) carry no labels and so
-- never escape (Phase 79e)
checkEffectEscape : DynCtx -> List (String, Ty) -> String -> List Atom -> Unit
checkEffectEscape dyn sigs m effs = match dyn.dcGroup
  None => ()
  Some group => checkEffectEscapeIn dyn.dcModule group sigs m effs

checkEffectEscapeIn : ModuleCtx ->
  GroupCtx ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  String ->
  List Atom ->
  Unit
checkEffectEscapeIn mctx group sigs m effs =
  match omLookup m mctx.mcCells.sigTyMapRef.value
    None => ()
    -- #797: a genuinely open declared row (free return-position tail var, no
    -- argument-side occurrence) has nothing to escape FROM — the row admits
