    -- whatever the body performs, which is what a free tail var MEANS.  Skipping
    -- here rather than widening `declaredEffects` keeps the CLOSED-row rejection
    -- (and its wording) byte-identical.
    Some written =>
      let ty = expandReturnSpine mctx written
      if declaredEffectsOpen mctx ty then
        ()
      else match (atomsEscape
        mctx.mcGraph
        (filterList concreteAtom effs)
        (declaredEffects mctx.mcGraph ty))
        -- An atom whose authority is still symbolic is the scoped solver's to
        -- decide once the binding's arguments have bounded it; comparing it
        -- here would report a variable a later solution resolves.

        [] => ()
        extras =>
          group.gcPendingEscapes :=
            (
                m,
                mctx.mcLoc,
                effectEscapeMsg
                  m
                  (declaredEffects mctx.mcGraph ty)
                  (declaredEffectTail ty)
                  extras,
              )
              :: group.gcPendingEscapes.value

-- After a group's solver scope has closed: report the walk's finding for a
-- member the solver said nothing about, and drop it for one it reported.
flushPendingEscapes : ModuleCtx -> Option GroupCtx -> Unit
flushPendingEscapes mctx None = ()
flushPendingEscapes mctx (Some group) =
  let pending = reverseL group.gcPendingEscapes.value
  group.gcPendingEscapes := []
  fold
    (_ entry =>
      let (m, loc, msg) = entry
      if omHasKey m mctx.mcCells.rowFailureReportedRef.value then
        ()
      else
        pushTypeErrorAt mctx "T-EFFECT-LEAK" loc msg)
    ()
    pending

concreteAtom : Atom -> Bool
concreteAtom a = not (authHasVars (atomAuth a))

-- generalize each member's (sig-and-body-unified) placeholder.  A signature was
-- already unified into the placeholder by preunifySigs, so generalizing the
-- result respects it AND any further specialization the body forces (e.g.
-- sum : t a -> a with body `fold (+) 0` reports a Int -> Int, not the raw sig).
-- Value restriction (DICT-SEMANTICS §4.1 G2): generalize a member only if it is
-- a syntactic *value* — every one of its clauses has params, or its zero-arg RHS
-- is non-expansive (`isNonexpansive`).  The decision is per MEMBER and purely
-- syntactic, on every group shape:
--   * a multi-member SCC gets no exemption (#2554): a zero-arg expansive member
--     such as `cell = Ref (helper 0)` inside a mutually-recursive group is a
--     polymorphic reference if generalized, and its siblings with params are
--     values on their own account, so "a group is always a function group" was
--     never the premise that made generalizing it safe;
--   * a signed binding gets no exemption from its type (#2556): the old
--     "post-unify type is an arrow" reading admitted `weird : a -> a ;
--     weird = mk ()`, whose RHS allocates a Ref before returning the arrow, so
--     one cell was read at two types.  A point-free binding is a value only
--     if G2 says so — write `maximum xs = fold step None xs`, not
--     `maximum = fold step None`.
-- A non-function expansive binding (`r = Ref []`) is value-restricted and stays
-- monomorphic whether or not it is signed.  The `isLetrec` argument is retained
-- for the (unchanged) caller signature; it no longer influences the decision.
sccSchemes : TcEnv ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  Bool ->
  List (Int, AuthResidual) ->
  Int ->
  List ScopedMember ->
  List (String, Scheme)
sccSchemes env _ _ _ _ _ [] = []
sccSchemes env sigs grouped isLetrec residuals index (member :: rest) =
  let m = member.smName
  let isVal = allList (memberClauseIsValue env) (clausesOf m grouped)
  (
      m,
      genBindingRestricted
        env.teDyn
        member.smDeclaredAuths.value
        (residualsOf index residuals)
        isVal
        (memberForce member)
        member.smMono,
    )
    :: sccSchemes env sigs grouped isLetrec residuals (index + 1) rest

-- The authority variables each member of a group will quantify, keyed to the
-- member's index: the argument-position authorities of an unsigned value
-- member (`qualifierAuthIds`, the ones publication keeps).  A variable two
-- members' types share is a recursive group's monomorphic link and is solved
-- as before; a signed member publishes its signature, so it keeps none.
quantifiableAuthorities : TcEnv ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List ScopedMember ->
  ScopeRoles
quantifiableAuthorities env grouped members =
  scopeRolesOf
    (map
      (member => (
        memberRole
          -- the presence set, not a scan of every signature: this runs once
          -- per binding group (`sigNameSetRef`)
          (omHasKey
            member.smName
            env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.sigNameSetRef.value)
          (allList (memberClauseIsValue env) (clausesOf member.smName grouped)),
        member.smMono,
      ))
      members)

memberRole : Bool -> Bool -> BindingRole
memberRole True _ = RoleDeclared
memberRole False True = RoleQuantifies
memberRole False False = RoleMonomorphic

-- A local binding carries no signature of its own.
localRole : Bool -> BindingRole
localRole True = RoleQuantifies
localRole False = RoleMonomorphic

-- [members] in group order, each with its role and type.  A quantifying
-- member's argument-position authorities are quantified (a variable two
-- members share is a recursive group's monomorphic link and is solved as
-- before); a monomorphic member hands every authority of its type outward.
scopeRolesOf : List (BindingRole, Mono) -> ScopeRoles
scopeRolesOf members =
  let owners =
    fold
      ((acc, index) (role, mono) =>
        let ids = match role
          RoleQuantifies => IdMap.keys (qualifierAuthIds mono Tip)
          _ => []
        (
          fold
            (m id => IdMap.set id (index :: optionOr [] (IdMap.get id m)) m)
            acc
            ids,
          index + 1,
        ))
      (Tip, 0)
      members
  ScopeRoles {
    rlQuantified =
      IdMap.foldlWithKey
        (acc id indices => match indices
          [index] => IdMap.set id index acc
          _ => acc)
        Tip
        (fst owners),
    rlOutward =
      fold
        (acc (role, mono) => match role
          RoleMonomorphic => authIdsIn mono acc
          _ => acc)
        Tip
        members,
    rlTyped = Some (fold (acc (_, mono) => authIdsIn mono acc) Tip members),
    rlMemberAuths = _ => map ((_, mono) => authIdsIn mono Tip) members,
  }

residualsOf : Int -> List (Int, AuthResidual) -> List AuthResidual
residualsOf index residuals =
  flatMap ((owner, r) => if owner == index then [r] else []) residuals

-- a top-level clause is a value if it has params (function) or a non-expansive RHS
memberClauseIsValue : TcEnv -> (List Pat, Expr) -> Bool
memberClauseIsValue env ([], rhs) = isNonexpansive env rhs
memberClauseIsValue env (_, _) = True

-- ── polymorphic signature over an expansive body ─────────────────────────────
-- HM-CORE-SEMANTICS §1 clause 4 / DICT-SEMANTICS §4.1 G2.  A signed member whose
-- signature quantifies a type variable but whose clauses are not syntactic values
-- cannot generalize to what it declares: `sccSchemes` keeps it monomorphic, and
-- the declared scheme would otherwise be exported over a body that carries no
-- dictionary parameter — `check` narrowed it silently to its first use while
-- `build` panicked on an unbound witness (the former "point-free constrained
-- CAF", `sumOf : (Foldable t, Num a) => t a -> a ; sumOf = fold (+) 0`).  Reject
-- at the definition and name the remedy.
checkSigsOverExpansive : TcEnv ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  Unit
checkSigsOverExpansive env _ [] = ()
checkSigsOverExpansive env grouped ((m, ty, tvs) :: rest) =
  let _ =
    if not (isEmpty tvs)
      && not (allList (memberClauseIsValue env) (clausesOf m grouped)) then
      pushTypeError
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        "T-SIG-OVER-EXPANSIVE"
        (sigOverExpansiveMsg m ty)
  checkSigsOverExpansive env grouped rest

-- ── signature-too-general check ──────────────────────────────────────────────
-- After body inference, the declared signature's type variables must map to
-- DISTINCT TVar refs.  If two declared tyvars (e.g. `a` and `b` in `a -> b`)
-- collapse to the SAME TVar or become a concrete type, the body is not universal.
-- Recursive calls instantiate the written contract, so silently narrowing its
-- definition can also change dictionary arity underneath those calls.
checkSigsTooGeneral : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  Unit
checkSigsTooGeneral mctx [] = ()
checkSigsTooGeneral mctx ((m, ty, tvs) :: rest) =
  let _ = checkSigTooGeneral mctx m ty tvs
  checkSigsTooGeneral mctx rest

checkSigTooGeneral : ModuleCtx -> String -> Ty -> List (String, Mono) -> Unit
checkSigTooGeneral mctx name ty tvs =
  let tvarIds = sigTvarIds (map snd tvs)
  match groundedSignatureVariable tvs
    Some (vname, actual) =>
      pushTypeErrorOnceAt
        mctx
        "T-TYPE-TOO-GENERAL"
        (firstTyLoc ty)
        "type variable `\{vname}` in the signature of `\{name}` must remain universal, but the body requires `\{ppMono actual}`; write that type in the signature or make the body work for every `\{vname}`"
    None =>
      if hasDupI tvarIds then
        pushTypeError mctx "T-TYPE-TOO-GENERAL" (sigTooGeneralMsg name ty)

groundedSignatureVariable : List (String, Mono) -> Option (String, Mono)
groundedSignatureVariable [] = None
groundedSignatureVariable ((name, mono) :: rest) = match normalize mono
  TVar _ => groundedSignatureVariable rest
  actual => Some (name, actual)

-- The third way a declared variable stops being universal: a value-restricted
-- sibling in the same group shares it.  `sccSchemes` keeps that sibling
-- monomorphic (it is evaluated once, so it has one type), which fixes the signed
-- member's declared variable to that one evaluation; the group can neither
-- generalize the variable for the sibling nor default it for the signed member,
-- and publishing the sibling with the variable free would let a later use pick
-- the type after the shared value already ran.  Reported at the signature, like
-- the grounded and collapsed forms, because the contract is what the body fails.
-- A signed expansive member is `checkSigsOverExpansive`'s case and is skipped here.
checkSigsFixedByExpansive : TcEnv ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List ScopedMember ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  Unit
checkSigsFixedByExpansive env grouped members sigTvMaps =
  let fixed =
    flatMap
      (member =>
        if member.smSigned.value
          || allList
            (memberClauseIsValue env)
            (clausesOf member.smName grouped) then
          []
        else
          map (id => (id, member.smName)) (monoUnboundIds member.smMono))
      members
  match fixed
    [] => ()
    _ => checkSigsFixedBy env.teDyn.dcModule fixed sigTvMaps

checkSigsFixedBy : ModuleCtx ->
  List (Int, String) ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  Unit
checkSigsFixedBy mctx _ [] = ()
checkSigsFixedBy mctx fixed ((name, ty, tvs) :: rest) =
  let _ = match sigVarFixedBy fixed tvs
    Some (vname, sibling) =>
      pushTypeErrorOnceAt
        mctx
        "T-TYPE-TOO-GENERAL"
        (firstTyLoc ty)
        "type variable `\{vname}` in the signature of `\{name}` must remain universal, but the zero-argument sibling `\{sibling}` shares it and is evaluated once; give `\{sibling}` a parameter or declare its monomorphic type"
    None => ()
  checkSigsFixedBy mctx fixed rest

sigVarFixedBy : List (Int, String) ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Option (String, String)
sigVarFixedBy _ [] = None
sigVarFixedBy fixed ((vname, mono) :: rest) = match normalize mono
  TVar cell => match fixedSibling (tyvarId cell) fixed
    Some sibling => Some (vname, sibling)
    None => sigVarFixedBy fixed rest
  _ => sigVarFixedBy fixed rest

fixedSibling : Int -> List (Int, String) -> Option String
fixedSibling _ [] = None
fixedSibling id ((i, sibling) :: rest)
  | i == id = Some sibling
  | otherwise = fixedSibling id rest

-- true if the list has any duplicate Int
hasDupI : List Int -> Bool
hasDupI [] = False
hasDupI (x :: xs) = containsI x xs || hasDupI xs

-- ── inferred-constraint promotion (unsignatured `=>` — the two-pass layer) ──
-- After a group is generalized, an UNSIGNATURED eligible member that uses a
-- return-position method (methodSiteFns) — or calls a constrained fn (dictAppFns)
-- — at one of its OWN quantified tyvars carries an INFERRED constraint.  Register
-- it exactly as a signatured one (funConstraintsRef + activeDictVars, keyed by the
-- *surviving* normalized id) so its body's method routes RDict and dict_pass
-- prepends a dict param; and record it in `promotedRef` so scheduled marking sees its
-- occurrences EDictAt on the next pass.  Signatured members are skipped (their
-- constraints came from preunifySigs); prelude fns are skipped (not eligible).
-- #1549: the deltas are threaded in so an inferred constraint that arrived as a
-- `requires` RESIDUAL (`nest x = tagOf (Wrap x)`) gets its dict parameter too.
-- `inferredConstraintIds` reads `methodSiteFns`/`dictAppFns`, which store a bare mono
-- with no interface attached, so a compound receiver (`Wrap t`) cannot be reduced
-- there; `residualInferredPreds` reduces the SAME predicates the scheme-obligation
-- channel just deferred.  Without this the scheme carries `Tag a` while the body
-- abstracts no dict — `check` would reject the bad call and an ORDINARY correct
-- program's binary would still read an unpassed dict word (issue 1549's second cell).
registerInferredConstraints : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List UObligation ->
  List ScopedScheme ->
  Unit
registerInferredConstraints mctx _ _ _ [] = ()
registerInferredConstraints mctx sigs callObls addedObls (scoped :: rest) =
  let _ =
    maybeInferConstraint
      mctx
      sigs
      callObls
      addedObls
      scoped.ssName
      scoped.ssScope
      scoped.ssScheme
  registerInferredConstraints mctx sigs callObls addedObls rest

maybeInferConstraint : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List UObligation ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Scheme ->
  Unit
maybeInferConstraint mctx sigs callObls addedObls m scope sch
  | not (omHasKey m mctx.mcGraph.dictEligibleSetRef.value) = ()
  | omHasKey m mctx.mcCells.sigNameSetRef.value = ()
  | otherwise =
    let boundIds = schemeIds sch
    -- Predicate vectors determine both slot existence and slot arguments. A recursive
    -- sibling can share a direct predicate without having its own occurrence trace.
    -- Residual reduction runs once, and both projections consume the same result.
    let preds =
      flatMap (oblPredOf mctx.mcGraph) addedObls ++ flatMap callPredOf callObls
    let residualPreds = residualInferredPreds mctx boundIds preds
    let vecs = directInferredPreds boundIds preds ++ residualPreds
    let ids =
      dedupI
        (inferredConstraintIds mctx m boundIds ++ map inferredPredLead vecs)
    registerInferredFor mctx m scope ids vecs

-- #11 soundness (ALWAYS-ON): for each generalized member, record the deferred impl
-- obligations it quantifies over — an addedObls entry whose discriminating mono is a
-- TVar among the member's scheme ids becomes (iface, that id).  A signed member's
-- declared `=>` constraints come from its sig instead (registered via funConstraints);
-- but recording the inferred obligation list here too is harmless (a satisfiable
-- concrete instantiation passes; an unsatisfiable one SHOULD error).  Runs on every
-- path (NOT gated on dictEligibleSetRef), so the plain check path catches the hole.
-- SOURCING (#619 DECLARED-ONLY; supersedes the #607/#610 UNION): the predicates a
-- binding abstracts are its PRINCIPAL context, and per DICT-SEMANTICS §4 `gen`/`var`
-- an ASCRIBED signature IS that context — a contract the body must satisfy, not a
-- floor it can raise (Jones; Hall-Peyton-Jones-Wadler; Haskell).  So:
--   • SIGNED binding   → obligations come SOLELY from the declared `=>` context
--       (declaredSchemeOblsFor).  The body's inferred obligations
--       (schemeObligationsOf / forwardedVecObls) are NOT merged in — they are
--       CHECKED as entailed by the declared context (checkSigConstraintCoverage);
--       a body that genuinely needs MORE than the signature declares is a def-site
--       type error (T-MISSING-CONSTRAINT), not a silent widening.
--   • UNSIGNED binding → no declared context exists, so the inferred principal
--       context stands: direct body dispatch (schemeObligationsOf) plus any
--       constraint forwarded from a constrained callee (forwardedVecObls).  Its
--       inferred constraints are promoted, not checked (see checkSigConstraintOne).
-- #610 stays satisfied: a declared constraint the body never dispatches on
-- (`sz2 : Sz a => a -> Int; sz2 x = 9`) is still sourced from declaredSchemeOblsFor,
-- so the scheme keeps `Sz a` and every caller discharges it.  #619 additionally drops
-- the union's redundant superclass display — `when : Thenable m => …` whose body's
-- `pure` infers Applicative now renders just `Thenable a =>` (Applicative is entailed
-- by `Thenable requires Applicative`, so it is checked-and-dropped, not merged).
-- #837: [memberDefIds] carries each TOP-LEVEL member's binding id (processSCC passes
-- schemeDefIdsRef); the local/where call sites pass omEmpty so their members key under
-- the sentinel id 0.  A member absent from [memberDefIds] is a local/where binder → 0.
registerSchemeObligations : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap Int ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List UObligation ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  Unit
registerSchemeObligations mctx _ _ _ _ [] = ()
registerSchemeObligations mctx memberDefIds sigTvMaps callObls addedObls ((m, sch) :: rest) =
  -- #838 I2 / #827: record this binding's QUANTIFIED (generalized) var ids as
  -- caller-deferrable.  A var this binding ∀-quantifies is FORWARDED to its callers
  -- (each use re-instantiates it fresh), so an end-of-run call obligation carrying
  -- that exact id is this binding's own deferred predicate — undeterminedGoalExempt
  -- defers it into the scheme instead of a spurious `Ambiguous instance` reject.
  -- CRITICAL (S0 #855-review): this uses the POST-generalization `schemeIds`, NOT the
  -- pre-generalization member monos.  A value-restricted intermediate (`let x = mk n`,
  -- `mk : Int -> a`) does NOT quantify its var (`Forall []`), so an escaped ambiguous
  -- var never enters this set and the undetermined-goal verdict rejects it (a1_greet/a1_letleak).
  mctx.mcCells.deferrableVarIds :=
    idSetInsertAll (schemeIds sch) mctx.mcCells.deferrableVarIds.value
  let obs =
    dedupVecObls (schemeOblsForMember mctx sigTvMaps callObls addedObls m sch)
  let _ =
    if isEmptyL obs then
      ()
    else
      let defId = optionOr 0 (omLookup m memberDefIds)
      mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef :=
        ((m, defId), obs) :: mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value
  registerSchemeObligations mctx memberDefIds sigTvMaps callObls addedObls rest

-- #619: a SIGNED binding's scheme context is EXACTLY its declared `=>` predicates
-- (authoritative); an UNSIGNED binding's is its inferred principal context (direct
-- dispatch + forwarded).  Signedness is `lookupSigTvMap … = Some` — true for any
-- signed member, including a signed binding with an EMPTY `=>` (whose declared
-- context is correctly empty), which is what distinguishes it from an unsigned one.
schemeOblsForMember : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List UObligation ->
  String ->
  Scheme ->
  List VecObl
schemeOblsForMember mctx sigTvMaps callObls addedObls m sch =
  match lookupSigTvMap m sigTvMaps
    Some _ => declaredSchemeOblsFor mctx sigTvMaps m (schemeIds sch)
    None =>
      schemeObligationsOf mctx True (schemeIds sch) addedObls
        ++ forwardedVecObls mctx True (schemeIds sch) callObls

-- the DECLARED `=>` predicates of signed member [m], each as its argument vector of
-- scheme-quantified tyvar ids.  A predicate is kept only if EVERY argument is a plain
-- tyvar that instantiated to one of this scheme's quantified vars: a concrete-grounded
-- argument (`Sz Int =>`) carries no per-use obligation here, and a partial vector would
-- be a different predicate.  An unsigned member contributes nothing.
declaredSchemeOblsFor : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  String ->
  List Int ->
  List VecObl
declaredSchemeOblsFor mctx sigTvMaps m boundIds =
  match lookupSigTvMap m sigTvMaps
    None => []
    Some (ty, tvMap) =>
      flatMap (declaredOblOne mctx boundIds tvMap) (sigConstraintsOf ty)

declaredOblOne : ModuleCtx ->
  List Int ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  Constraint ->
  List VecObl
declaredOblOne mctx boundIds tvMap (Constraint { constraintHead = iface, constraintArgs = args, constraintOrigin = co }) =
  -- U1b (#1482): `constraintOrigin` is the #1110 interface-OCCURRENCE identity of the
  -- `=>` predicate as written in this module's scope — the same layer `DImpl.implOrigin`
  -- is stamped in, which is what makes the goal and the impl comparable.
  let ifref = IfaceRef { irName = iface, irOrigin = co }
  match constraintArgMonos args tvMap
    None => declaredOblMixed mctx boundIds ifref tvMap args
    Some monos => match boundTyvarIds boundIds monos
      Some ids => [VecObl { voIface = ifref, voIds = ids, voArgs = [] }]
      None => []

-- #1161 SYMPTOM 2: the predicate has an argument that is not a bare tyvar, so
-- `constraintArgMonos` answered `None` and the WHOLE predicate used to be discarded —
-- `Ix a Bool =>` with no `impl Ix _ Bool` anywhere reached neither the displayed scheme
-- nor any caller's obligation list, and `check` accepted it at exit 0 while the call
-- dispatched to an unrelated impl.  DICT-SEMANTICS §3 makes `match(IE, Ix Int Bool)`
-- empty and the goal a missing-instance rejection, so the predicate must survive the
-- channel: record its WHOLE argument vector in `voArgs`, and the ids of its bare-tyvar
-- positions in `voIds` (one dict slot per deferred variable, unchanged cardinality).
--
-- 🚨 THE ADMISSION TEST IS DELIBERATELY NARROW, AND EVERY CLAUSE OF IT IS LOAD-BEARING —
-- this is a NARROWING (programs that were accepted now reject), so an argument this
-- function admits without being able to instantiate CORRECTLY would substitute to a
-- wrong-but-CONCRETE goal, which is strictly worse than the missing one it replaces:
--   * a BARE tyvar bound by this scheme — `recordSchemeCallObligations` maps it through
--     the call's instantiation subst, exactly as the ids-only path always did;
--   * a GROUND argument (no tyvars anywhere, `monoTyvarIds` empty) — it needs no
--     substitution, so the signature's mono IS the call's mono;
--   * #1937: a STRUCTURED argument whose tyvar leaves are ALL bound by this scheme
--     (`Conv (Wrap a) b =>`) — `substOblArgs` now walks `TApp`/`TFun` structurally and
--     substitutes at each leaf, so the caller's goal is `Conv (Wrap Char) Bool`, not the
--     signature's own cell.  Before that walk existed this class HAD to be dropped, and
--     the two halves must stay together: admitting without the structural walk
--     substitutes to a wrong-but-CONCRETE goal;
--   * nothing else.  An unbound tyvar — bare, or as a leaf of a structured argument —
--     has no id to defer on and is dropped exactly as before.
-- At least one bare bound tyvar is REQUIRED: a fully ground declared context (`Sz Int =>`)
-- carries no per-use obligation on this channel and stays dropped, which keeps the
-- narrowing to the shape the issue is about.
declaredOblMixed : ModuleCtx ->
  List Int ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List Ty ->
  List VecObl
declaredOblMixed mctx boundIds ifref tvMap args =
  let monos = map (fromAstType mctx tvMap) args
  let ids = flatMap (declaredOblArgId boundIds) monos
  if isEmptyL ids
    || not (allList (declaredOblArgOk (i => containsI i boundIds)) monos) then
    []
  else
    [VecObl { voIface = ifref, voIds = ids, voArgs = monos }]

-- #1937: a STRUCTURED argument whose free ids are ALL scheme-bound now carries too.
-- The clause this replaces required a structured argument to be GROUND, because
-- `substOblArgs` substituted only at a top-level `TVar` and would have carried the
-- signature's own tyvar cell into the caller's goal.  That walk is now structural, so
-- the instantiation this admission promises is one the channel can actually perform;
-- the two halves are a single change (admitting without it substitutes to a
-- wrong-but-CONCRETE goal, strictly worse than the missing one it replaces).  An
-- UNBOUND tyvar anywhere in the argument is still refused — it has no id to defer on.
declaredOblArgOk : (Int -> Bool) -> Mono -> Bool
declaredOblArgOk isBound m = match normalize m
  TVar cell => isBound (tyvarId cell)
  _ => allList isBound (monoTyvarIds m)

-- the monos a predicate's arguments resolve to under a tyvar-name -> mono map, in
-- declaration order; None if ANY argument is not a plain tyvar or is absent from the
-- map (a partial vector is a DIFFERENT predicate, so the whole thing is dropped).
-- Shared by the declared-context sourcing and recordSigConstraintArgs.
constraintArgMonos : List Ty -> List (String, Mono) -> Option (List Mono)
constraintArgMonos [] _ = Some []
constraintArgMonos (a :: rest) tvMap = match constraintArgMono a tvMap
  None => None
  Some mono => map (mono :: _) (constraintArgMonos rest tvMap)

-- the mono ONE predicate argument resolves to: None unless it is a plain tyvar
-- present in [tvMap] (a concrete-grounded argument like `Sz Int =>` carries no
-- per-use obligation here).
constraintArgMono : Ty -> List (String, Mono) -> Option Mono
constraintArgMono a tvMap = match constraintArgVarName a
  None => None
  Some v => lookupAssoc v tvMap

lookupSigTvMap : String ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  Option (Ty, List (String, Mono))
lookupSigTvMap _ [] = None
lookupSigTvMap m ((n, ty, tvMap) :: rest)
  | m == n = Some (ty, tvMap)
  | otherwise = lookupSigTvMap m rest

-- #242: routed through the canonical O(n·log n) `support.util.dedupBy` (was a
-- private O(n²) `List`-as-a-set scan).  The iface name is length-prefixed and
-- the id VECTOR is comma-joined — ints carry no comma, so the encoding is
-- injective over both components.
-- ⚠️ Keyed on the SPELLING (`voIface.irName`), deliberately: this dedup decides what a
-- binding's DISPLAYED and re-instantiated scheme context is, and keying it on identity
-- would split one printed `Num a =>` into two.  U1b (#1482) carries identity through the
-- payload without changing what counts as the same entry.
dedupVecObls : List VecObl -> List VecObl
dedupVecObls xs = dedupBy vecOblKey xs

-- #1161: the GROUND half of the vector joins the key.  `(Ix a Bool, Ix a Char)` is two
-- predicates sharing one interface AND one id vector — without the ground positions the
-- dedup would collapse them into one, silently dropping half a declared context.  An
-- ids-only entry contributes a constant empty suffix, so its key is order-equivalent to
-- the pre-widening one.
-- S-nonlead-arg-identity (#1904) made `oblArgKey` structural and id-carrying.  On THIS
-- channel that is mostly redundant — `voIds` already carries every position's id — but
-- not entirely: `voIds` is a FLATTENED concatenation with no position boundaries, so
-- `Ix (Pair a b) (Pair c d)` and `Ix (Pair a c) (Pair b d)` shared both `voIds` and the
-- old head-name-only suffix.  The partition this key induces is strictly FINER than
-- before and identical on bare-tyvar vectors (the shape `dedupVecObls`' spelling caveat
-- above is about), so a printed `Num a =>` still does not split.
vecOblKey : VecObl -> String
vecOblKey o =
  "\{lenKey o.voIface.irName}\{joinWith "," (map intToString o.voIds)}|\{joinWith "," (map oblArgKey o.voArgs)}"

-- S-nonlead-arg-identity (#1904): ONE predicate-argument position, rendered as a
-- PREFIX-FREE PREORDER of the normalized mono, so the key REALISES the sprint's settled
-- notion of "same predicate" — pointwise `monoSameGiven` over the vector — rather than a
-- weaker local one.  Every arm below mirrors an arm of `monoSameGiven`:
--   * `TVar` keys on the tyvar's IDENTITY, not on its mere presence.  This is the whole
--     fix: the old encoding keyed EVERY tyvar position as the constant "*", so
--     `(Ix a b c, Ix a c b)` rendered `Ix|*,*,*` twice and `dedupSlotVecs` collapsed two
--     predicates into ONE dict slot (#1904, S0: `ix n x y + ix n y x` summed 333+333
--     instead of 333+111).  `vecOblKey` survived that only because `voIds` carries every
--     position's id in a SECOND component; `cslotVecKey` composes `cslotKey`, which
--     carries the LEAD id alone (`csId`), so it had no per-position id anywhere.
--   * `TCon`/`TRigid` fold to the same rendering because `monoSameGiven` equates them by
--     name across those two constructors.
--   * `TApp`/`TFun` recurse structurally, so the key sees the SPINE, not just the head —
--     `Ix (Pair a b) (Pair c d)` and `Ix (Pair a c) (Pair b d)` are now distinct, where a
--     head-name-plus-flattened-ids encoding (`xmodOblArgId`'s shape) would tie.
--   * `TEff` and `TAuth` (the remaining arms) key as the constant "*", realising
--     `monoSameGiven`'s erasure: it equates any two effect rows, and any two authorities.
-- One deliberate residual under-split: TYCON ORIGIN is dropped (name only, as
-- `headTyconNameMono` always did).  It cannot be folded into a key string at all:
-- `sameTyConHead`'s absent-origin arm is non-transitive, so no string equivalence can
-- realise it.
-- Injectivity: each arm emits a self-delimiting tag — "v"+digits+"." , "c"+`lenKey`, and
-- the fixed-arity "a"/"f" — so a preorder walk parses back uniquely and the joined vector
-- key is injective over the vector.
-- ⚠️ RAW TYVAR IDS IN A KEY STRING: safe HERE, and not by an "ids are unique" claim.
-- `cslotKey` already folds the raw lead `csId` into this same key, and the non-lead ids
-- come from the SAME predicate occurrence in the SAME signature, normalized together.
-- Both `dedupSlotVecs` call sites compare keys only WITHIN one binding's slot list
-- (a call's declared slots, `setFunConstraintEntry`'s declared prefix) and
-- `vecOblKey`'s `voIds` are equally raw — so this adds no exposure the lead id did not
-- already carry.  The G4 hazard at `registerPredGiven` is about `activeDictVars`, which
-- no key here consults.
oblArgKey : Mono -> String
oblArgKey m = match normalize m
  TVar cell => "v\{intToString (tyvarId cell)}."
  TCon name _ => "c\{lenKey name}"
  TRigid name => "c\{lenKey name}"
  TApp a b => "a\{oblArgKey a}\{oblArgKey b}"
  TFun a _ b => "f\{oblArgKey a}\{oblArgKey b}"
  TQual a _ => oblArgKey a
  _ => "*"

-- membership of ONE vector in the DECLARED set (reportUncoveredVec) — not a
-- dedup, and the declared set is a handful of entries, so it stays a scan.
containsVecObl : VecObl -> List VecObl -> Bool
containsVecObl _ [] = False
containsVecObl o (o2 :: rest) =
  sameIfaceDecl o.voIface o2.voIface && eqIntList o.voIds o2.voIds
    || containsVecObl o rest

eqIntList : List Int -> List Int -> Bool
eqIntList [] [] = True
eqIntList (a :: xs) (b :: ys) = a == b && eqIntList xs ys
eqIntList _ _ = False

-- the (iface, var-id VECTOR) entries of the obligations whose discriminating monos are
-- all quantified ids of this scheme.  Deduped on (iface, ids).
schemeObligationsOf : ModuleCtx ->
  Bool ->
  List Int ->
  List UObligation ->
  List VecObl
schemeObligationsOf mctx generalizing boundIds obls =
  flatMap
    (vecOblOfPred mctx generalizing boundIds)
    (flatMap (oblPredOf mctx.mcGraph) obls)

-- #991: the impl-channel arm only — a call-channel obligation is re-instantiated from
-- `schemeObligationsRef` by its own path and contributes nothing here.
-- U1b (#1482): forwards the whole `IfaceRef`, not `.irName` — the obligation already
-- carries its occurrence identity and this is the channel that hands it to every later
-- re-instantiation.  An EMPTY dispatch vector contributes nothing.
-- The obligation's own `loc` travels WITH the predicate — see `residualVecObls`, whose
-- reduction poses a goal to the min⊑ selector and must attribute it to the recording
-- site rather than to the construct around the group's close.
oblPredOf : GraphCtx -> UObligation -> List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc)
oblPredOf gctx o = match o.oblProj
  OpMethodOcc typarams mty occ omitted =>
    match occurrenceDispatchMonos typarams mty occ omitted
      [] => []
      ds => [(o.pred.iface, ds, o.loc)]
  OpExactReturn request => match methodReturnArgs gctx request
    Some ds => match ds
      [] => []
      _ => [(request.mrrIface, ds, request.mrrLoc)]
    None => []
  OpProjected => []
  OpNumLit _ => match o.pred.args
    [] => []
    ds => [(o.pred.iface, ds, o.loc)]

-- a single recorded predicate contributes ONE joint (iface, ids) entry iff EVERY one of
-- its dispatch monos is a bound tyvar of the scheme.  Before #607 the multi-mono case
-- fell into a `_ => []` wildcard and the obligation was DISCARDED — which is why an
-- unsatisfiable `Ix a i =>` reached neither the displayed scheme nor any caller's
-- obligation list, and `check` accepted it at exit 0 while the built binary did raw
-- pointer arithmetic.
-- #1549: a predicate whose argument vector is NOT all bare bound tyvars is no longer
-- simply discarded — it is first REDUCED by §3 entailment (`residualVecObls`), and the
-- residual that reduction leaves over this scheme's own quantified vars is deferred
-- here.  Dropping it outright is what severed `nest x = tagOf (Wrap x)` from its
-- `Tag a` (DICT-SEMANTICS §4 `gen` / §4.2 OD2).
vecOblOfPred : ModuleCtx ->
  Bool ->
  List Int ->
  (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List VecObl
vecOblOfPred mctx generalizing boundIds (iface, ds, loc) =
  match boundTyvarIds boundIds ds
    Some ids => [VecObl { voIface = iface, voIds = ids, voArgs = [] }]
    None => residualVecObls mctx generalizing boundIds iface ds loc

-- ── #1549: residual reduction at `gen` ──────────────────────────────────────
-- DICT-SEMANTICS §4 `gen` makes a binding's principal context `P'` = "the predicates
-- DEFERRED to this binding", and §4.2 OD2 says a non-ground predicate defers to the
-- binder that quantifies its variables.  A predicate like `Tag (Wrap t)` is neither
-- deferrable as written (its head is concrete, so it is not `P'`) nor dischargeable
-- (its `t` is generalizable): §3 `inst` reduces it against `impl Tag (Wrap a) requires
-- Tag a`, and the RESIDUAL `Tag t` is what defers.  Reducing here is what makes the
-- deferral OD2 already performs on the CHECK side (`undeterminedGoalExempt`
-- defers `Tag t` "to the caller") actually reach a caller: without the residual in the
-- scheme there is no context for `(var)` to discharge and no `λd̄.` for `gen` to
-- abstract, so `check` was silent, `run` fell back to declaration order, and the built
-- binary read a dict word that was never passed (issue 1549, S0).
--
-- Deliberately the FALLBACK arm only: when every argument is already a bound tyvar the
-- predicate IS its own residual and the direct path above owns it, so this returns []
-- for that case and the behaviour of every predicate that reached a VecObl before is
-- unchanged.  A predicate mentioning none of this scheme's quantified vars can have no
-- residual over them either (grounding is monotone), and is rejected by the cheap guard
-- before any impl lookup — that keeps the common ground obligation (`Display String`)
-- off the reduction path entirely.
--
-- 🚨 [loc] IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS NOT DECORATION — DROPPING IT MOVES A DIAGNOSTIC.
-- `residualPredsOf` reaches `findMatchingImplReqsU`, which asks the min⊑ selector WHICH
-- impl matched — so this is a SECOND goal-posing site outside the five resolver drains
-- (the first is `checkNestedReqs`, whose header says the same thing).  When the goal is
-- ambiguous the selector calls `reportAmbiguousOverlap`, which reads the context's `sxSite` and
-- falls back to the record's `mcLoc` when it is `None`.  At a generalized group's close
-- that is the construct around the close, not the site that recorded the
-- predicate; and because `pushTypeErrorOnceAt` dedups on the message, that badly-located
-- push WINS over the well-located one a later resolver drain would emit.
-- MEASURED on `test/dict_fixtures/s6-c1-rigid-goal-no-call-discriminator.mdk`
-- (`firstRow xss = index xss 0`): with the recorded loc dropped, the caret moved off the
-- `index` call at 29:15 onto the literal `0` at 29:25 — same code, same message, worse
-- span, and NO gate saw it because the dict-semantics gate asserted the code alone.
-- So hand the reduction a context whose `sxSite` is the obligation's OWN snapshotted span,
-- as `checkNestedReqs` does; a walk outside a drain gets no site and the selector falls
-- back rather than inheriting a stale span.
residualVecObls : ModuleCtx ->
  Bool ->
  List Int ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  List VecObl
residualVecObls mctx generalizing boundIds iface ds loc =
  map
    keepBoundResidual
    (residualBoundPreds (siteFor mctx) generalizing boundIds iface ds loc)

-- S-inferred-vector-supply: the reduction itself, factored out of `residualVecObls` so
-- the DICT-ABSTRACTION channel can read the residual predicate's ARGUMENT MONOS and not
-- only the ids `VecObl` keeps.  ⚠️ ONE run per group: `registerInferredFor`'s vectors and
-- its slot ids are both projections of this one call (see `maybeInferConstraint`), so the
-- §3 entailment — and the `sxSite`-scoped diagnostics it can emit — fire exactly as
-- often as they did before this slice, not twice.
-- Each entry is (interface, the residual's bare-tyvar ids IN ORDER, the residual's whole
-- argument vector); a residual not entirely over this scheme's own quantified vars is
-- dropped, exactly as `keepBoundResidual` always dropped it.
residualBoundPreds : SiteCtx ->
  Bool ->
  List Int ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Option Loc ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Int, List Mono)
residualBoundPreds sx generalizing boundIds iface ds loc
  | isSome (boundTyvarIds boundIds ds) = []
  | not (anyIn (flatMap monoUnboundIds ds) boundIds) = []
  | otherwise =
    -- A signed binder's variables are rigid in its body, so no use chooses them.
    let chosen = if generalizing then boundIds else []
    let preds =
      residualPredsOf { sx | sxSite = loc } chosen (reqWalkStart ()) iface ds
    flatMap (keepBoundResidualPred sx.sxModule boundIds) preds

keepBoundResidualPred : ModuleCtx ->
  List Int ->
  (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Int, List Mono)
keepBoundResidualPred mctx boundIds (iface, args) =
  match boundTyvarIds boundIds args
    Some ids => [(iface, ids, args)]
    None => residualMixedPred mctx boundIds iface args

-- ── #1905: the INFERRED twin of `declaredOblMixed` (#1161 SYMPTOM 2) ─────────────
-- A residual that is not ALL bare bound tyvars used to be dropped here, and that drop is
-- #1549's exact defect one shape over: `useIx x = ix x 'z'` leaves the residual
-- `Ix t Char`, `boundTyvarIds` answered `None` on the `Char`, and the predicate reached
-- neither `useIx`'s scheme nor its callers' obligation lists — `check` printed
-- `useIx : a -> Int`, and `main = println (useIx 'q')` was accepted on all four verbs,
-- printing `222` out of `impl Ix Int Char`.  §4.2 OD2 says a non-ground predicate defers
-- to the binder that quantifies its variables and is discharged at each USE SITE, and
-- `VecObl` has carried exactly this mixed shape since #1161 — ids for the bare-tyvar
-- positions, the whole vector in `voArgs`, instantiated per call by `substVecOblArgs`.
-- MEASURED that the declared half already does the right thing on the identical body:
-- with `useIx : Ix a Char => a -> Int` written out, `useIx 5` runs and prints `222`
-- while `useIx 'q'` is rejected on check/run/build with
-- `No impl of Ix for Char Char` at the call site.  This makes the INFERRED context
-- reach the same verdict, which is §4 `(gen)`'s whole claim (OD6(a): declared and
-- inferred contexts defer identically).
--
-- The ids are `declaredOblMixed`'s, read by the same `declaredOblArgId`, for the reason
-- `xmodVecObl`'s header states about ITS reuse of them: this is one fact about one
-- predicate recorded on three channels, and a channel admitting a wider argument class
-- than its siblings is a new divergence rather than a fix.  Since #1937 THREE argument
-- classes carry — a BARE tyvar bound by this scheme, a GROUND argument, and a STRUCTURED
-- argument all of whose tyvar leaves are bound by this scheme — and that third class
-- arrived on all three channels in one change, together with the structural
-- `substOblArgs` walk that makes it instantiable.
-- A residual of an inferred context can also mention a variable this scheme does not
-- quantify: one the binder shares with its enclosing scope (`v`'s type in
-- `g v = let f = i => v[i]; f 0`, or a literal's variable handed to the enclosing
-- boundary), or one no type of the binder mentions.  Such a variable is the same
-- variable at every use, and `substOblArg` keeps it as itself, so the residual is
-- admitted: no other channel carries the goal.  A variable another
-- binder declared (`declaredSigVarIds`: an inner local's quantified variable, in the
-- inner local's own goal) is not shared: that goal is the inner binder's, already in
-- its scheme, so it is not admitted here.  Neither other channel reaches this class: a
-- signature and an imported context quantify every variable they name.  At least one
-- bound tyvar is required: a residual over no quantified variable is not this
-- binder's to defer, and stays where it was recorded.
residualMixedPred : ModuleCtx ->
  List Int ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Int, List Mono)
residualMixedPred mctx boundIds iface args =
  let ids = flatMap (declaredOblArgId boundIds) args
  let declared = mctx.mcCells.declaredSigVarIds.value
  let foreign =
    i => not (containsI i boundIds) && omHasKey (intToString i) declared
  if isEmptyL ids || anyList foreign (flatMap monoUnboundIds args) then
    []
  else
    [(iface, ids, args)]

-- ⚠️ `voArgs` IS THE ids-only `[]` FOR AN ALL-BARE RESIDUAL AND THE WHOLE VECTOR FOR A
-- MIXED ONE — the same split `declaredOblOne` makes between its own arm and
-- `declaredOblMixed`, so the OBLIGATION channel's readers (`substVecOblArgs`,
-- `dedupVecObls`, `reportUncoveredVec`) see, for each shape, precisely the shape they
-- have always seen from the declared channel.  Every residual that reached a `VecObl`
-- before this change is all-bare by construction (it came through `boundTyvarIds`), so
-- its entry is byte-identical; the mixed entries are the ones #1905 adds.
-- The argument vector the DICT channel consumes (`funConstraintArgsRef`) is the third
-- component of the triple and is unaffected by this projection.
keepBoundResidual : (IfaceRef, List Int, List Mono) -> VecObl
keepBoundResidual (iface, ids, args) =
  VecObl { voIface = iface, voIds = ids, voArgs = residualOblArgs ids args }

-- 🚨 #1937: THIS TEST USED TO BE `listLen ids == listLen args`, AND THAT EQUIVALENCE DIED
-- WITH THE ADMISSION WIDENING.  It relied on `declaredOblArgId` contributing exactly one
-- id per BARE-tyvar position and none for anything else, so equal lengths meant "every
-- position is a bare tyvar".  Now that a STRUCTURED argument contributes its own bound
-- leaves, `Conv (Wrap a) b` has two ids for two arguments and would have taken the
-- ids-only `[]` arm — instantiating through `substMonos o.voIds` to the goal `Conv a b`,
-- i.e. silently DROPPING the `Wrap`.  Ask the structural question directly instead:
-- every position a bare tyvar, and each of them one of [ids] (a bare variable the
-- scheme does not quantify contributes no id, and the ids-only arm would drop it).
residualOblArgs : List Int -> List Mono -> List Mono
residualOblArgs ids args
  | allList isBareTyvarMono args && listLen ids == listLen args = []
  | otherwise = args

-- §3 `inst`, run for its residual rather than for a verdict (§4.2 OD2).  A goal with no
-- concrete-headed argument is its own residual and is not entered.  Any other goal,
-- including one that mixes a concrete head with a free variable (`Conv (Wrap t) u`), is
-- matched against the instances (`findMatchingImplReqsU`), whose matcher binds an
-- instance-head variable to whatever stands at its position but never binds a free
-- goal variable: an instance is selected only where it is generic exactly where the
-- goal is still free, so `impl Conv Int Bool` is never selected for `Conv (Wrap t) u`.
-- The selected instance's `requires`, under the match, are solved in turn, and so is
-- the context of each super instance the goal's construction selects, beyond what
-- those leave (`superGoalsEntered`).
-- - No instance matches: `unroutedResidual` decides between a reject at the goal's site
--   and keeping the goal as its own residual.
-- - The match, or the instance a super goal of its construction selects, is not the one
--   every use selects (`residualSelectionStable`, §6.1.3): the goal is kept as
--   written, so each use selects at its own instantiation, its supers included.  [chosen]
--   are the variables the binder's uses choose: the quantified variables of a
--   generalizing binder, and none at a signed binder, whose goal is reduced where it
--   stands.
-- The walk is bounded by the shared `requires` measure (`reqWalkEnter`, DICT §3 W2): a
-- cyclic instance is `T-REQUIRES-CYCLE` and a context that keeps growing its goal is
-- `T-REQUIRES-DEPTH`, both at `sxSite`, so a goal that leaves no residual because
-- the walk stopped is never a silent `[]`.  Each goal is solved once per walk
-- (`solvedOnWalk`) and the residuals come back deduplicated, so a goal the `requires`
-- reach along many paths costs one solve.  [chosen] and `sxSite` are fixed for
-- the walk `residualBoundPreds` starts, which is why they are not part of that key.
residualPredsOf : SiteCtx ->
  List Int ->
  ReqWalk ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
residualPredsOf sx chosen walk iface args
  | not (anyConcreteHead args) = [(iface, args)]
  | otherwise =
    match reqWalkReported sx.sxModule sx.sxSite (reqWalkEnter walk iface args)
      None => []
      Some next => solvedOnWalk sx.sxModule next iface args (_ =>
        let univ = sx.sxModule.mcCells.residualUnivRef.value
        match findMatchingImplReqsU sx univ iface args
          None => unroutedResidual sx iface args
          Some (subst, reqs) if not
            (residualSelectionStable
              sx.sxModule
              chosen
              (map (reqToObligation sx.sxModule subst) reqs)
              iface
              args) => [(iface, args)]
          Some (subst, reqs) =>
            let own =
              flatMap
                (r => residualPredsOf sx chosen next (fst r) (snd r))
                (map (reqToObligation sx.sxModule subst) reqs)
            superCarriedResiduals
              sx.sxModule.mcGraph
              own
              (flatMap
                (e =>
                  flatMap
                    (r => residualPredsOf sx chosen e.sgWalk (fst r) (snd r))
                    (reqObligationsFor sx univ e.sgIface e.sgArgs))
                (superGoalsEntered
                  sx.sxModule
                  univ
                  walk
                  sx.sxSite
                  own
                  iface
                  args)))

-- Whether every use of the binder builds the dictionary the goal's reduction builds
-- now (DICT-SEMANTICS §6.1.3): the goal mentions no variable the uses choose, or the
-- goal is stable (`goalSelectionStable`) and so is each of its super goals
-- (`superGoalClosure`) that selects.  [context] is the matched instance's context
-- at the goal; a super goal it answers (`goalAnsweredBy`) is built from that context,
-- not selected, and the context's goals are reduced under this same test.  Every
-- other super goal is a selection and is tested, whatever its arguments are
-- (constructed, arrows or variables alone): a super goal over variables alone that a
-- blanket instance answers now is unstable when a more specific instance unifies.
residualSelectionStable : ModuleCtx ->
  List Int ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Bool
residualSelectionStable mctx chosen context iface args
  | not (anyIn (flatMap monoUnboundIds args) chosen) = True
  | otherwise =
    goalSelectionStable mctx chosen iface args
      && allList
        (sg =>
          goalAnsweredBy mctx.mcGraph context (fst sg) (snd sg)
            || goalSelectionStable mctx chosen (fst sg) (snd sg))
        (superGoalClosure mctx.mcGraph iface args)

-- Whether every use of the binder selects the instance the goal matches now: the goal
-- mentions no variable the uses choose, or among the instance heads that unify with
-- it, one matches it and is ⊑ every other (`goalReach`'s stable minimum).  Only a
-- variable some binder declared (`declaredSigVarIds`) is held rigid in that
-- unification: an enclosing binder's variable that is not generalized yet can still
-- become a type another instance head needs.
goalSelectionStable : ModuleCtx -> List Int -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Bool
goalSelectionStable mctx chosen iface args =
  if not (anyIn (flatMap monoUnboundIds args) chosen) then
    True
  else match stableGoalReach mctx chosen iface args
    ReachMany => False
    ReachOne _ => True
    ReachNone => True

-- What the instance heads that unify with the goal decide (`goalReach`), with the
-- goal's variables that some binder declared (`declaredSigVarIds`) and [chosen] does
-- not name held rigid.
stableGoalReach : ModuleCtx -> List Int -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> GoalReach
stableGoalReach mctx chosen iface args =
  let declared = mctx.mcCells.declaredSigVarIds.value
  let rigidIds =
    omFromNames
      (map
        intToString
        (filterList
          (i => not (containsI i chosen) && omHasKey (intToString i) declared)
          (dedupI (flatMap monoUnboundIds args))))
      omEmpty
  goalReach
    mctx
    args
    (filterList
      (c => rowCountsFor args (fst c))
      (goalCandidates mctx rigidIds args (goalRows mctx iface args)))

-- ── #1564 / Stage A "Door 4": the un-plumbed case is a LOUD reject ────────────
-- `residualPredsOf`'s `None` arm conflates TWO facts, and since the instance axis went
-- graph-global (ARCH A-3.6, issue 1112) they are no longer the same fact:
--   (a) NO impl of this interface matches these arguments anywhere — the ordinary
--       "nothing to reduce against" terminal, owned by the call/req checkers (and, for
--       the partially-ground shape, still under-reported: issue 1578).  Unchanged: [].
--   (b) an impl DOES match — `implMatchesU` says so over the very same `ImplUniverse`
--       this arm just consulted — but `findMatchingImplReqsU` could not hand back its
--       `requires`.
--       ⚠️ ARCH B-2.1-b2/-d: THE CAUSE STATED HERE HAS NARROWED, AND THE OLD WORDING WAS
--       LEFT BEHIND BY TWO BITES.  It read: "its concrete leg
--       (`concreteReqMatchByIface`) does not read that universe at all: it reads
--       `shadowKeyTableRef`, copied per module from the CUMULATIVE
--       `universeKeyBucketsRef` accumulator."  That is no longer true on the CONCRETE
--       leg — B-2.1-b2 repointed `concreteReqMatchByIface` onto the graph-global
--       `bodyImplEnvRef`, and B-2.1-d deleted both refs.  What SURVIVES is the same
--       shape one leg over: `findMatchingImplReqsU`'s HEADLESS fallback is
--       `firstReqMatch (univHeadless univ iface)`, still read off `residualUnivRef` —
--       the `ImplUniverse` projected at THIS module's ordinal, i.e. still a topological
--       prefix.  So candidacy can still span the whole module graph while the evidence
--       registry does not, and a goal whose only matching impl is HEADLESS and declared
--       in a module that sorts LATER than the goal's own is admitted with no requires,
--       no residual, no `λd̄.` slot and no route dict.
--       🚨 DO NOT read this narrowing as "(b) is fixed" — it is not, and this arm must
--       still reject.  The prefix-read fallbacks are `B-2.1-b2`'s own Item 3 residual,
--       re-confirmed untouched by `B-2.1-g`, and no probe has yet reached them in a way
--       that DIVERGES; that is a negative result, not a clearance.
-- (b) used to be impossible: before A-3.6 the same import order that starved the
-- evidence registry also starved candidacy, so the program was REJECTED (that is
-- issue 1564's false reject).  Afterwards it was ACCEPTED and MISCOMPILED — MEASURED on
-- `test/must_fail_fixtures/1564-import-order-decides-conditional-impl-candidacy`:
-- `check` exit 0 (`main : Unit`), `run` exit 1 `E-PANIC: putStrLn: not a String`,
-- `build` exit 0, and the built binary exit **139**, because `@mdk_impl_Wrap_tagOf` is
-- emitted arity-2 and called arity-1: the value cell lands in the dict slot and the impl
-- loads a function pointer out of it.
-- 🚨 SO THIS ARM MUST NOT FALL THROUGH TO `[]`.  Returning "no residual" for (b) is
-- exactly issue 1549's drop and exactly issue 1562's cliff, one cause over — and the
-- precedent for the remedy is `T-REQUIRES-DEPTH` on this same function, whose own note
-- states the principle: only making the cliff LOUD removes the silent wrongness.
-- ⚠️ WHAT THIS IS NOT.  It does not route the evidence and it does not make
-- DICT-SEMANTICS C4/I2 true — C4 is a conjunction ("consult the same instance set AND
-- produce the same evidence"), and only the first conjunct is delivered.  ⚠️ BOTH
-- DEFERRALS NAMED HERE HAVE NOW BEEN CASHED, AND C4 STILL DOES NOT HOLD: B-2.1-b2
-- repointed the CONCRETE reader at `IE` and B-2.1-d deleted `universeKeyBucketsRef`
-- rather than re-keying it (`TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md`'s deferral row).  The
-- headless evidence leg is still prefix-read, so this arm still converts a segfault into
-- a located reject and nothing more; it drains when THAT leg moves, not before.
-- ⚠️ WHY THE TEST IS OVER THE SAME `univ`, and not a broader one: it is the EXISTENCE
-- twin of the matcher that just failed (same buckets, same
-- `implHeadMatchesArgs`/`implHeadSubst` success condition, same headless fallback), so
-- True-here-with-None-there isolates precisely the two-registry disagreement.  When both
-- registries agree that nothing matches, this is silent and (a)'s behaviour is
-- byte-identical to before.
--
-- ⚖️ RUN-055 (SA-4), owner ruling, 2026-08-12: THE TEST IS `implMatchesWithReqsU`, NOT
-- `implMatchesU`.  It shipped on the bare existence twin, which never asks whether the
-- matched impl HAS a `requires` — so it also converted the case where the correct answer
-- is `[]` on BOTH arms into a hard error.  MEASURED (R5-F2, and re-derived on this
-- change's own before/after arms): #1564's fixture with ONE variable changed — `impl Tag
-- (Wrap a)` carrying no `requires` — rejected with `T-REQUIRES-UNROUTED` while the
-- control order compiled to `define i64 @mdk_nest__nest(i64 %arg0)`, arity 1, with no
-- dict parameter anywhere.  For that shape the message's own claim ("accepting it would
-- build a program that reads a dictionary that was never passed") is simply false: no
-- dictionary is passed on either order.
-- 🚨 THIS IS AN ACCEPTANCE WIDENING and it RESTORES what BASE did — BASE never reached
-- this code at all.  Its could-not-pass-before fixture is leg 24 of
-- `test/diff_compiler_check_cli_modules.sh`.  The narrowing half is what must not move:
-- an impl that DOES carry `requires` still rejects (legs 24b/24c), and the disjunctive
-- form — ANY matching impl carries reqs, not the selected one — is the LOUD direction,
-- because the selector that would name the winner is the registry that just failed.
-- ⚠️ `implMatchesWithReqsU` is SA-1's, added at the sibling ground site
-- (`unroutedGroundReqs`) and reused verbatim here rather than re-derived: same buckets,
-- same concrete-then-headless order, same `implHeadMatchesArgs` success condition, one
-- extra `isNonEmptyL reqs` conjunct.  The two guards are now the SAME predicate, which is
-- also what keeps the shared message honest at both sites.
-- ── #1578 / #1905: case (a) REACHES A VERDICT, it no longer falls through to [] ──
-- The `| otherwise = []` this replaces was the silent half of the conflation the block
-- above names: "no impl matches" and "no residual" were one value, so the predicate
-- reached neither the binding's scheme, nor any channel's check, nor a diagnostic.  Both
-- measured shapes were exit-0 wrong answers (#1578 `h x y = conv (Wrap x) y` ran and
-- printed `int-bool` off `impl Conv Int Bool`; #1905 `useIx x = ix x 'z'` accepted
-- `useIx 'q'` on all four verbs and printed `222`).  DICT-SEMANTICS §4.2 gives exactly
-- two dispositions and this arm now picks between them rather than dropping the goal:
--   * OD1 — the goal is DECIDABLE here, so discharge it here.  `residualRefutableNow`
--     is the test, and it is the *structurally refutable* population OD1 enumerates,
--     not the *ground* one: the RECEIVER's head is a concrete tycon (hence stable —
--     grounding is monotone, no later substitution can move it) and NO impl of this
--     interface heads at that tycon or is headless, so `match(IE, π)` is empty now and
--     stays empty however the goal's remaining free arguments instantiate.  That is
--     #1578: `Conv (Wrap t) u` against a program whose only impl is `Conv Int Bool`.
--   * OD2 — otherwise the goal is its OWN residual and defers outward to the binder
--     that quantifies its variables, discharged at each use site by `(var)`.  That is
--     #1905: `Ix t Char` CAN still match `impl Ix Int Char` (`t := Int`), so rejecting
--     it here would be a false reject — MEASURED as a live accept, `useIx 5` prints
--     `222` and must keep doing so.  The verdict lands where it is decidable, at
--     `main`'s `useIx 'q'`.
-- ⚠️ THE OD1 ARM REPORTS THROUGH `T-NO-IMPL`, THE EXISTING CODE, AND MINTS NOTHING NEW.
-- `DIAGNOSTIC-CODES-DESIGN.md` draws the line at cause, and it already puts this arm on
-- that side: `T-NO-IMPL` is *"no instance matches"*, which both `T-REQUIRES-DEPTH`
-- ("instances matched all the way down and the chain did not bottom out") and
-- `T-REQUIRES-UNROUTED` ("exactly one instance matches and its evidence is unreachable")
-- are defined against.  A second code for the same fact reached one channel over would
-- be a taxonomy split, not a distinction — and `pushNoImplError` also carries the
-- derivable-iface / tuple-call hints, which apply here verbatim.
-- 🚨 THE OD2 ARM IS WHY `keepBoundResidualPred` HAD TO WIDEN IN THE SAME SLICE.  Handing
-- `[(iface, args)]` back here is necessary and NOT sufficient: `Ix t Char` is a MIXED
-- vector, and the ids-only `boundTyvarIds` filter one call up dropped every such
-- residual on the floor — the same drop, one shape over.  See `residualMixedPred`.
-- ⚠️ GUARD ORDER: the `implMatchesWithReqsU` arm stays FIRST and untouched (RUN-055 /
-- SA-4, above).  It is case (b) — an impl DOES match, its evidence cannot be routed —
-- and `residualRefutableNow` is False for it by construction (a matching impl is in one
-- of the two buckets the existence test reads), so the two arms cannot both fire.
unroutedResidual : SiteCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
unroutedResidual sx iface args
  | implMatchesWithReqsU
    sx.sxModule
    sx.sxModule.mcCells.residualUnivRef.value
    iface
    args =
    let _ =
      pushTypeErrorOnceAt
        sx.sxModule
        "T-REQUIRES-UNROUTED"
        sx.sxSite
        (requiresUnroutedMsg iface args)
    []
  | residualRefutableNow sx.sxModule iface args =
    let _ = pushNoImplError sx.sxModule iface.irName sx.sxSite args
    []
  | otherwise = [(iface, args)]

-- OD1's decidability test for this arm, and it is deliberately a CANDIDACY question
-- ("could any impl of this interface ever head-match this goal?") rather than the
-- MATCH question `findMatchingImplReqsU` just answered No to.  The difference is the
-- whole soundness of the reject: `Ix Int t` fails the match (a concrete impl-head
-- pattern against an unbound goal argument is `matchStep`'s `MFail`) while an
-- instantiation of `t` would satisfy it, so a reject keyed on the match would be a
-- false reject on every partially-free vector.  Candidacy keys on the RECEIVER head
-- alone, which is the one position `matchStep` can never recover by substitution once
-- it is a concrete tycon.
-- ⚠️ `goalHeadCon`'s `None` — a bare-tyvar receiver — is NOT refutable and must answer
-- False: that is #1905's own goal, and rejecting it is the false reject above.
-- 🚨 READ OVER `bodyImplEnvRef`, THE GRAPH-GLOBAL REGISTRY, NOT `residualUnivRef`.
-- Deliberate, and NOT a second selector: this is an existence read, the only decision it
-- makes is reject-vs-defer, and it is the twin of `ieCandidatesForIface` — same two
-- bucket reads (the goal head's own bucket plus the headless one), same
-- `ieRowIfaceMatches` comparator, minus the head-vector match candidacy must not apply.
-- `residualUnivRef` is the universe projected at THIS module's ordinal, i.e. a
-- topological PREFIX (Door 4's block above derives this at length); keying a REJECT on a
-- prefix would reject a program whose only matching impl is declared in a
-- later-sorting module — a false reject decided by module order, which is the exact
-- failure shape #1564 is.  Reading the graph-global registry fails toward DEFERRAL,
-- and a deferred goal still gets its verdict at the use site.
--
-- 🚨 #1939 / #1938 (OPEN WORLD): THE HEAD-CANDIDACY TEST IS NECESSARY BUT NOT
-- SUFFICIENT, AND ON ITS OWN IT REFUTES BY WHAT THE COMPILATION UNIT HAPPENS TO HAVE
-- LOADED.  The paragraph above argues candidacy is stable under substitution — true,
-- and it is the only thing the goal's OWN shape can make stable.  What it does NOT
-- establish is that `IE` is stable, and `IE` is not: the loaded module graph never
-- contains a module's DEPENDENTS, so `ieHeadCandidateExists` answering False means
-- *"no impl heads there IN THIS GRAPH"*, never *"no impl heads there"*.  For a goal
-- that is still open — any argument carrying a type VARIABLE, unification (`TVar`)
-- or declared-and-skolemized (`TRigid`) — that difference decides acceptance:
--   * #1939 shape (1): `f : Conv (Wrap a) b => Wrap a -> b -> String` with no `Conv`
--     impl in the file.  BASE rejected `f`'s DEFINITION (`No impl of Conv for Wrap a
--     b`) — a declared, never-called, perfectly legal constrained function.
--   * #1939 shape (2) / #1938: `medaka check <library module>`.  `a.mdk` infers `Conv
--     (Wrap α) β` for `h`; the satisfying `impl Conv (Wrap Int) Bool` lives in `b.mdk`,
--     which IMPORTS `a` and so is absent from `a`'s own load graph.  BASE rejected a
--     module that the whole project compiles fine.
-- ⇒ REFUTE ONLY A CLOSED GOAL.  A closed vector cannot instantiate further, so its
-- verdict is the one the use site would reach anyway and OD1 keeps its whole point
-- (`residualPredsOf` reaches here with ground `requires` vectors after a reduction
-- step, so this arm is not thereby dead).  An OPEN vector defers outward as OD2 —
-- `unroutedResidual`'s `otherwise` — and is adjudicated where it grounds, at the use
-- site, by `checkOneCallObligation`.  #1578 is exactly that: `Conv (Wrap α) β` now
-- defers out of `h`, and `main`'s `h 5 True` forces `Conv (Wrap Int) Bool`, which is
-- closed and still rejects.  The reject MOVED; it did not go away.
-- ⚠️ THIS IS AN ACCEPTANCE WIDENING ([W-QUIETER]) AND ITS NARROW HALF IS THE POINT:
-- the illegal siblings of both shapes still reject, one site further out.  Guarded in
-- both directions by `test/dict_fixtures/s-open-world-*`, plus the untouched #1578 /
-- #1905 rows whose REJECT verdicts are deliberately location-free.
residualRefutableNow : ModuleCtx -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Bool
residualRefutableNow mctx iface args = match goalHeadCon args
  None => False
  Some hk =>
    monoVectorClosed args
      && not (ieHeadCandidateExists mctx.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value iface hk)

-- The OPEN-WORLD defer test for the two OBLIGATION checkers (`checkOneCallObligation`,
-- `checkReqOne`), as opposed to `residualRefutableNow`'s bare `monoVectorClosed`.  The
-- residual site sits INSIDE a generalizing binding by construction — producing that
-- binding's context is its whole job — so an open goal there always has a scheme to
-- land on, and it never sees a bare-rigid receiver either (`goalHeadCon` is read for
-- candidacy, not for concreteness).  An obligation checker has neither guarantee, so it
-- asks all five questions.  Each conjunct's counterexample is on
-- `checkOneCallObligation`'s arm.
--
-- 🚨 CONJUNCTS 3 AND 5 ARE THE FIX-ROUND ADDITIONS (review S0-2 / S0-1 / S2-5), AND
-- THEY ASK THE ONE QUESTION THE THREE-CONJUNCT FORM NEVER DID: *does this goal have a
-- landing site that will actually be given a dict?*  "Defer" means "forward this
-- predicate outward to the binder that quantifies its variables, and let each use site
-- discharge it".  Where no such binder will carry it, "defer" means DROP, and a dropped
-- goal is a type-confused dict at exit 0 — MEASURED, three ways, all against the sprint
-- merge-base `0944ca9d` where every one of them was a located reject:
--   * S0-2 — `g : Tag (Wrap a) => a -> String ; g x = "…\{tagOf (Box x)}"`.  The goal
--     `Tag (Box a)` is NOT the declared context and a declared context cannot grow, so
--     it lands nowhere; HEAD printed `wrapChar|boxInt=123`, `Box Int`'s body applied to
--     a `Char`.  Conjunct 5.
--   * S0-1 — `f : Conv (Wrap a) Int => a -> String`.  The MULTI-PARAMETER goal has a
--     landing site (the declared context IS the goal) but no CONSUMPTION-side answer:
--     `registerPredGiven` matches `[subject]` only and registers nothing for a longer
--     vector, so `entailAssum` can never see it, `entail` falls to `entailInst`, and the
--     body is statically committed to whichever impl was most specific at ABSTRACTION
--     time while the caller's correct dict goes unread.  HEAD printed `T/T` for
--     `"\{f True}/\{f 41}"` (expected `T/n=42`), and swapping the two `impl` blocks
--     changed the answer to `intInt/intInt` — selection by declaration order, which
--     DICT-SEMANTICS §3 forbids outright.  Conjunct 5, via `goalMatchesGiven`, which is
--     deliberately `registerPredGiven`'s OWN shape: this gate admits exactly what that
--     registry can answer, so the two cannot drift into another silent accept.
--     ⚠️ SUPERSEDED AS A REJECT, NOT AS A RULE (#1956).  `registerPredGiven` is now keyed
--     on the WHOLE argument vector, so this exact program HAS a consumption-side answer:
--     `entailAssum` finds the declared context's dict and S0-1 is ACCEPTED, printing
--     `T/n=42` — the answer DICT-SEMANTICS §3 requires (assum before inst; the caller's
--     dict is used, not an abstraction-time commitment).  The invariant above is
--     unchanged and is what made the reject safe to lift: the gate still admits exactly
--     what the registry answers — the registry simply answers more.
--   * S2-5 — `data Bad = Bad zzz ; use (Bad v) = qq (Wrap v)`.  `zzz` is a `TRigid` no
--     scheme quantifies, so `monoUnboundIds` is empty and conjunct 4 passed VACUOUSLY —
--     the rigid-head forgery `monoHeadIsDecl` catches at the top level, leaking through
--     as soon as the rigid is NESTED inside a structure.  Conjunct 3 is the groundness
--     half made non-vacuous: a goal with no unbound variable at all has nothing for any
--     scheme to generalize, hence nowhere to defer TO.
--
-- ⚠️ CONJUNCT 5 FAILS OPEN ON PURPOSE, and that is what keeps #1939 shape (2) accepted.
-- `not (goalIdsClaimed …)` is the INFERRED-binding arm: `describe x = tag (Wrap x)` in a
-- library module reaches this gate BEFORE its own generalization has registered anything
-- (MEASURED on `test/dict_fixtures/s-open-world-library-dependent-impl/lib.mdk`: the
-- second check pass reaches the goal `Tag (Wrap α)` with an EMPTY given registry and no
-- `funConstraintArgsRef` row for `describe`), so its scheme is still open and the goal
-- is what will populate it.  A binding whose constraint set is already REGISTERED is
-- fixed — declared or inferred — and a goal claiming its variables must be in it.
--
-- ⚠️ MEASURED CORRECTION TO THE REVIEW'S STATED MECHANISM (report S0-2): a declared
-- context's variables are NOT `TRigid` at this site.  They are ordinary unbound `TVar`s
-- (`i2_unsound.mdk`'s `g` carries `Tag (Wrap TVar#736)` and its goal is
-- `Tag (Box TVar#736)` — the SAME cell), so conjunct 4 was never vacuous for S0-2; it
-- passed because the id genuinely IS deferrable.  The review's conclusion stands, its
-- mechanism does not, and conjunct 5 is keyed on the fact that was actually there.
goalDefersOpenWorld : ModuleCtx -> ScopeId -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Bool
goalDefersOpenWorld mctx scope iface args =
  not (monoVectorClosed args)
    && allList monoHeadIsDecl args
    && isNonEmptyL (flatMap monoUnboundIds args)
    && allList
      (i => IdMap.has i mctx.mcCells.deferrableVarIds.value)
      (flatMap monoUnboundIds args)
    && (goalMatchesGiven mctx.mcGraph scope iface args
      || goalSlotStillOpen mctx args)

-- is there an in-scope PREDICATE-keyed given that answers this goal exactly?
-- Deliberately `registerPredGiven`'s own shape — the WHOLE argument vector, structural,
-- matched by `monoVecSameGiven` (pointwise `monoSameGiven` on rigid/cell IDENTITY) rather
-- than by unification — because the question this gate asks is not "is the goal
-- plausible" but "will `entailAssum` be handed a dict for it".
-- 🚨 THIS SHAPE AND `registerPredGiven`'s MUST MOVE TOGETHER, AND #1956 IS WHY BOTH MOVED
-- IN ONE STEP.  Widening the registry alone would let this gate keep answering False for
-- a multi-parameter goal the registry can now answer (a needless reject); widening this
-- gate alone would re-open exactly the S0-1 hole FIX-1 closed — a goal admitted to defer
-- with no consumption-side answer, i.e. a dropped predicate and a type-confused dict at
-- exit 0.  The invariant is that this gate admits EXACTLY what that registry can answer.
-- #2547 unit 3: `GSPredicateOnly` is what still says so now that both registries share one
-- environment — it selects exactly the `GMPredicate` entries, which are exactly the ones
-- `registerPredGiven` / `registerFunPredGiven` write.
goalMatchesGiven : GraphCtx -> ScopeId -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Bool
goalMatchesGiven gctx _ _ [] = False
goalMatchesGiven gctx scope iface args =
  anyGivenMatches
    gctx
    PredicateRequest { prIface = iface, prArgs = PSArgsKnown args }
    scope
    (givensForScope gctx scope)

anyGivenMatches : GraphCtx ->
  PredicateRequest ->
  ScopeId ->
  List GivenEntry ->
  Bool
anyGivenMatches gctx request scope givens =
  anyGivenOnChain
    request
    (Scopes.visibleChain (currentScopeStore gctx ()) scope)
    givens

anyGivenOnChain : PredicateRequest -> List Int -> List GivenEntry -> Bool
anyGivenOnChain _ _ [] = False
anyGivenOnChain request chain (g :: rest) =
  givenInScope GSPredicateOnly g
      && Scopes.visibleOnChain chain (Scopes.binderScope g.geBinder)
      && predicateRequestMatchesSlot request g.geSlot
    || anyGivenOnChain request chain rest

isSemanticGivenAnswer : Option AssumAnswer -> Bool
isSemanticGivenAnswer (Some (SemanticGiven (GivenEvidence _))) = True
isSemanticGivenAnswer _ = False

isLegacyPredicateAnswer : Option AssumAnswer -> Bool
isLegacyPredicateAnswer (Some (LegacyPredicate _)) = True
isLegacyPredicateAnswer _ = False

-- Private service check for the selection half of the scope adapter.  It keeps
-- the full-vector and id-witness eligibility rules observable independently of
-- production examples, and its sibling query fails if lexical filtering is
-- removed from `anyGivenMatches`.
scopeGivenProbe : Unit -> List Bool
scopeGivenProbe _ =
  let gctx = probeGraphCtx ()
  let store = currentScopeStore gctx ()
  let root = Scopes.freshScope store None 0 "given-probe" ModuleOwner
  let owner =
    Scopes.freshScope store (Some root) 1 "given-probe" (BindingOwner "owner")
  let sibling =
    Scopes.freshScope store (Some root) 1 "given-probe" (BindingOwner "sibling")
  let iface =
    IfaceRef { irName = "PairGiven", irOrigin = OriginModule "given-probe" }
  let args = [tconBuiltin "Int", tconBuiltin "Bool"]
  let slot = PredicateSlot {
    psIface = iface,
    psArgs = PSArgsKnown args,
    psBoundIds = [41],
  }
  let _ = pushGiven gctx GMPredicate DirectGiven slot (Scopes.binderAt owner 0)
  let exact = PredicateRequest { prIface = iface, prArgs = PSArgsKnown args }
  let unknown = PredicateRequest { prIface = iface, prArgs = PSArgsUnknown }
  let truncated = PredicateRequest {
    prIface = iface,
    prArgs = PSArgsKnown [tconBuiltin "Int"],
  }
  let witnessIface = IfaceRef {
    irName = "WitnessGiven",
    irOrigin = OriginModule "given-probe",
  }
  let witnessSlot = PredicateSlot {
    psIface = witnessIface,
    psArgs = PSArgsKnown [tconBuiltin "Int"],
    psBoundIds = [73],
  }
  let witnessRequest = PredicateRequest {
    prIface = witnessIface,
    prArgs = PSArgsKnown [tconBuiltin "Int"],
  }
  let _ =
    pushGiven
      gctx
      GMIdWitnessed
      DirectGiven
      witnessSlot
      (Scopes.binderAt owner 1)
  let compatibleIface = IfaceRef {
    irName = "CompatibleGiven",
    irOrigin = OriginModule "given-probe",
  }
  let compatibleSlot = PredicateSlot {
    psIface = compatibleIface,
    psArgs = PSArgsUnknown,
    psBoundIds = [89],
  }
  let compatibleRequest = PredicateRequest {
    prIface = compatibleIface,
    prArgs = PSArgsKnown [tconBuiltin "Int"],
  }
  let _ =
    pushGiven
      gctx
      GMPredicate
      DirectGiven
      compatibleSlot
      (Scopes.binderAt owner 2)
  let givens = givensForScope gctx owner
  let result = [
    anyGivenMatches gctx exact owner givens,
    not (anyGivenMatches gctx exact sibling givens),
    not (anyGivenMatches gctx truncated owner givens),
    not (anyGivenMatches gctx witnessRequest owner givens),
    isSome
      (firstPredForEnclAt gctx GSImplRequires 73 witnessRequest owner givens),
    isNone
      (firstPredForEnclAt gctx GSImplRequires 74 witnessRequest owner givens),
    isSemanticGivenAnswer (firstPredForEncl gctx exact owner givens),
    isLegacyPredicateAnswer
      (firstPredForEnclAt gctx GSPredicateOnly 41 unknown owner givens),
    isLegacyPredicateAnswer
      (firstPredForEnclResidual gctx "PairGiven" args owner givens),
    isLegacyPredicateAnswer
      (firstPredForEncl gctx compatibleRequest owner givens),
  ]
  result

-- > scopeGivenProbe ()
-- [True, True, True, True, True, True, True, True, True, True]

firstMethodRow : List MethodSchemeRow -> MethodSchemeRow
firstMethodRow (row :: _) = row
firstMethodRow [] = panic "method-row observer expected a row"

methodSlotBoundIds : List MethodPredicateSlot -> List (List Int)
methodSlotBoundIds slots = map (slot => slot.mpsPredicate.psBoundIds) slots

methodSlotPositions : List MethodPredicateSlot -> List (List Int)
methodSlotPositions slots = map (slot => slot.mpsPositions) slots

methodSlotIdsAtPositions : List Int ->
  List MethodPredicateSlot ->
  List (List Int)
methodSlotIdsAtPositions ids slots =
  map (slot => map (pos => nthInt pos ids) slot.mpsPositions) slots

methodSlotArgumentIds : List MethodPredicateSlot -> List (List Int)
methodSlotArgumentIds slots = map methodSlotArgumentIdsOne slots

methodSlotArgumentIdsOne : MethodPredicateSlot -> List Int
methodSlotArgumentIdsOne slot = match slot.mpsPredicate.psArgs
  PSArgsUnknown => []
  PSArgsKnown args => flatMap monoTyvarIds args

methodRowRegistrySlotIds : ModuleCtx -> String -> List (List Int)
methodRowRegistrySlotIds mctx key =
  match (lookupMethodPredicateSlots
    key
    mctx.mcCells.methodPredicateSlotsRef.value)
    None => []
    Some slots => methodSlotBoundIds slots

observeMethodSchemeRowsForTest : Unit -> MethodRowTestObservation
observeMethodSchemeRowsForTest _ =
  let graph1 = probeGraphCtx ()

  let rows1 = initialModuleCtx graph1
  let constrainedRow =
    firstMethodRow (ifaceMethodSchemeRows rows1 [methodRowTestFoldMapDecl])
  let constrainedIds = schemeIds constrainedRow.msrScheme
  let constrainedSlots = constrainedRow.msrMethodSlots
  let constrainedBoundIds = methodSlotBoundIds constrainedSlots
  let constrainedPositions = methodSlotPositions constrainedSlots
  let constrainedIdsAtPositions =
    methodSlotIdsAtPositions constrainedIds constrainedSlots
  let constrainedArgumentIds = methodSlotArgumentIds constrainedSlots

  let graph2 = freshSubRecordsOf graph1
  let rows2 = carryModuleCtx graph2 rows1
  let counterBefore = graph2.graphRun.tyvarCounter.value
  let firstRow =
    firstMethodRow (ifaceMethodSchemeRows rows2 [methodRowTestFoldMapDecl])
  let counterAfterFirst = graph2.graphRun.tyvarCounter.value
  let secondRow =
    firstMethodRow (ifaceMethodSchemeRows rows2 [methodRowTestFoldMapDecl])
  let counterAfterSecond = graph2.graphRun.tyvarCounter.value
  let firstSchemeIds = schemeIds firstRow.msrScheme
  let secondSchemeIds = schemeIds secondRow.msrScheme
  let firstRowSlotIds = methodSlotBoundIds firstRow.msrMethodSlots
  let secondRowSlotIds = methodSlotBoundIds secondRow.msrMethodSlots
  let registryAfterSecondSlotIds =
    methodRowRegistrySlotIds rows2 (methodSlotKey firstRow.msrIface "foldMap")

  let graph3 = freshSubRecordsOf graph1
  let rows3 = carryModuleCtx graph3 rows2
  let sameNameForward =
    methodRowSameNameView
      (ifaceMethodSchemeRows rows3 [methodRowTestSameA, methodRowTestSameB])
  let graph4 = freshSubRecordsOf graph1
  let rows4 = carryModuleCtx graph4 rows3
  let sameNameReverse =
    methodRowSameNameView
      (ifaceMethodSchemeRows rows4 [methodRowTestSameB, methodRowTestSameA])

  let graph5 = freshSubRecordsOf graph1
  let rows5 = carryModuleCtx graph5 rows4
  let constantRows = ifaceMethodSchemeRows rows5 [methodRowTestConstantDecl]
  let constantRow = firstMethodRow constantRows
  let constantBodyIsFunction =
    match normalize (schemeBodyOf constantRow.msrScheme)
      TFun _ _ _ => True
      _ => False

  let graph6 = freshSubRecordsOf graph1
  let rows6 = carryModuleCtx graph6 rows5
  let attributed = DAttrib [] methodRowTestFoldMapDecl
  let attributedRows = ifaceMethodSchemeRows rows6 [attributed]
  let attributedMethods =
    methodEnvGo
      graph6
      [declEnvModule graph6 0 "foldable-test" [attributed]]
      emptyMethodEnv
  let (attributedParamIface, attributedParamTyparams) =
    match optionOr [] (omLookup "foldMap" attributedMethods.meByName)
      [] => ("", [])
      r :: _ => match r.mrEntry
        (iface, typarams, _, _) => (iface.irName, typarams)

  let directNum =
    methodRowTestNum
      "direct-num"
      (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "String" None) (TyVar "a"))
  let attributedNum =
    DAttrib
      []
      (methodRowTestNum
        "attributed-num"
        (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Int" None) (TyVar "a")))
  let builtinNum =
    methodRowTestNum "builtin-num" (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Int" None) (TyVar "a"))
  let numAnchors = [
    methodRowNumObservation rows6 "attrOnly" [attributedNum] [attributedNum],
    methodRowNumObservation rows6 "directOnly" [directNum] [directNum],
    methodRowNumObservation
      rows6
      "attrThenDirect"
