      [attributedNum, directNum]
      [attributedNum, directNum],
    methodRowNumObservation
      rows6
      "directThenAttr"
      [directNum, attributedNum]
      [directNum, attributedNum],
    methodRowNumObservation
      rows6
      "builtinThenUser"
      [builtinNum]
      [builtinNum, methodRowTestUserFromInt],
    methodRowNumObservation
      rows6
      "userThenBuiltin"
      [builtinNum]
      [methodRowTestUserFromInt, builtinNum],
  ]

  let observation = MethodRowTestObservation {
    mrtoSchemeIds = constrainedIds,
    mrtoSlotBoundIds = constrainedBoundIds,
    mrtoSlotPositions = constrainedPositions,
    mrtoSlotIdsAtPositions = constrainedIdsAtPositions,
    mrtoSlotArgumentIds = constrainedArgumentIds,
    mrtoCounterBefore = counterBefore,
    mrtoCounterAfterFirst = counterAfterFirst,
    mrtoCounterAfterSecond = counterAfterSecond,
    mrtoFirstSchemeIds = firstSchemeIds,
    mrtoSecondSchemeIds = secondSchemeIds,
    mrtoFirstRowSlotIds = firstRowSlotIds,
    mrtoSecondRowSlotIds = secondRowSlotIds,
    mrtoRegistryAfterSecondSlotIds = registryAfterSecondSlotIds,
    mrtoSameNameForward = sameNameForward,
    mrtoSameNameReverse = sameNameReverse,
    mrtoConstantRowCount = listLen constantRows,
    mrtoConstantSchemeIdCount = listLen (schemeIds constantRow.msrScheme),
    mrtoConstantBodyIsFunction = constantBodyIsFunction,
    mrtoConstantSlotCount = listLen constantRow.msrMethodSlots,
    mrtoAttributedRowCount = listLen attributedRows,
    mrtoAttributedParamIface = attributedParamIface,
    mrtoAttributedParamTyparams = attributedParamTyparams,
    mrtoNumAnchors = numAnchors,
  }
  observation

methodReturnProbeIface : String -> String -> Ty -> Decl
methodReturnProbeIface moduleId ifaceName methodTy =
  methodRowTestIface
    moduleId
    ifaceName
    ["a"]
    [IfaceMethod "make" methodTy None None]

methodReturnProbeImpl : String -> String -> Decl
methodReturnProbeImpl moduleId ifaceName = DImpl {
  pub = False,
  iface = ifaceName,
  tys = [tyConBuiltin "Int" None],
  reqs = [],
  methods = [ImplMethod "make" [] (ELit LUnit)],
  implOrigin = OriginModule moduleId,
  implIfaceLoc = None,
}

methodReturnProbeScope : ModuleCtx -> String -> ScopeId
methodReturnProbeScope mctx moduleId =
  let scope =
    Scopes.freshScope
      (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
      None
      0
      moduleId
      ModuleOwner
  let _ = openScope mctx scope
  scope

methodReturnProbeOccurrence : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  MethodTrackedInstantiation
methodReturnProbeOccurrence mctx row =
  let inst = instantiateMethodTracked mctx row.msrScheme
  let _ = unify mctx (stripArrows inst.mtiBody) (tconBuiltin "Int")
  inst

methodReturnProbeSpelling : ModuleCtx -> MethodSchemeRow -> Unit
methodReturnProbeSpelling mctx row =
  mctx.mcCells.methodAliasEntriesRef :=
    omInsert "make" (row.msrIface, row.msrTyparams, row.msrType, []) omEmpty

methodReturnProbeRequest : ModuleCtx -> MethodSchemeRow -> MethodReturnRequest
methodReturnProbeRequest mctx row =
  let inst = methodReturnProbeOccurrence mctx row
  methodReturnRequest
    mctx
    row
    inst.mtiBody
    inst.mtiSubstitution
    (Some (freshEvId mctx ()))

methodReturnVectorCompletenessProbe : Unit ->
  (Option (List String), Option (List String), Bool, Bool)
methodReturnVectorCompletenessProbe _ =
  let gctx = probeGraphCtx ()
  let mctx = initialModuleCtx gctx
  let _ = methodReturnProbeScope mctx "return-vector"
  let zeroRow =
    firstMethodRow
      (ifaceMethodSchemeRows mctx [
        methodRowTestIface "return-zero" "Zero" [] [
          IfaceMethod
            "make"
            (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (tyConBuiltin "Int" None))
            None
            None,
        ],
      ])
  let partialRow =
    firstMethodRow
      (ifaceMethodSchemeRows mctx [
        methodRowTestIface
          "return-partial"
          "Partial"
          ["a", "b"]
          [
            IfaceMethod
              "make"
              (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (TyVar "a"))
              None
              None,
          ],
      ])
  let zeroArgs =
    map
      (map ppMono)
      (methodReturnArgs gctx (methodReturnProbeRequest mctx zeroRow))
  let partialArgs =
    map
      (map ppMono)
      (methodReturnArgs gctx (methodReturnProbeRequest mctx partialRow))
  let observed = (
    zeroArgs,
    partialArgs,
    allMethodParamsMentioned zeroRow.msrTyparams zeroRow.msrType,
    allMethodParamsMentioned partialRow.msrTyparams partialRow.msrType,
  )
  observed

export
methodReturnTemplatePresenceProbe : Unit -> (List Bool, List Bool)
methodReturnTemplatePresenceProbe _ =
  let gctx = probeGraphCtx ()
  let mctx = initialModuleCtx gctx
  let present =
    firstMethodRow
      (ifaceMethodSchemeRows mctx [
        methodRowTestIface
          "return-template-present"
          "Present"
          ["a", "b"]
          [
            IfaceMethod
              "make"
              (TyFun
                (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None)
                (TyTuple [TyVar "a", TyVar "b"]))
              None
              None,
          ],
      ])
  let absent =
    firstMethodRow
      (ifaceMethodSchemeRows mctx [
        methodRowTestIface
          "return-template-absent"
          "Absent"
          ["a", "b"]
          [
            IfaceMethod
              "make"
              (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (TyVar "a"))
              None
              None,
          ],

-- Runs in a carry of [prev], the caller's record, in its graph record with a fresh
-- graph run, and returns it beside the codes: it is the record left current.
methodReturnProbeCodes : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  List Decl ->
  (List String, ModuleCtx)
methodReturnProbeCodes prev ownedRow impls =
  let gctx = GraphCtx { prev.mcGraph | graphRun = freshGraphRun () }
  let mctx = carryModuleCtx gctx prev
  let _ = methodReturnProbeScope mctx "return-owner-checker"
  let foreignRow =
    firstMethodRow
      (ifaceMethodSchemeRows mctx [
        methodReturnProbeIface
          "return-foreign"
          "Foreign"
          (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (TyVar "a")),
      ])
  let request = methodReturnProbeRequest mctx ownedRow
  let _ = methodReturnProbeSpelling mctx foreignRow
  let _ = recordExactMethodObligation mctx request
  let universe = buildImplUniverse impls
  mctx.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef := buildFlatImplEnv impls
  let _ = checkCallObligationsU mctx True universe (wAll mctx.mcCells.implObls)
  (map tcCode (reverseL mctx.mcCells.typeErrors.items.value), mctx)

methodReturnProbeRouteKey : Route -> String
methodReturnProbeRouteKey (RKey key _ _) = key
methodReturnProbeRouteKey _ = ""

-- Runs in a carry of [prev], the caller's record, in its graph record with a fresh
-- graph run.
methodReturnProbeStamp : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  List Decl ->
  (String, String, String)
methodReturnProbeStamp prev ownedRow foreignRow impls =
  let gctx = GraphCtx { prev.mcGraph | graphRun = freshGraphRun () }
  let mctx = carryModuleCtx gctx prev
  let scope = methodReturnProbeScope mctx "return-owner-stamper"
  let request = methodReturnProbeRequest mctx ownedRow
  let _ = methodReturnProbeSpelling mctx foreignRow
  let env = buildFlatImplEnv impls
  mctx.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef := env
  let tagRef = Ref RNone
  let implRef = Ref []
  let resultMono = stripArrows request.mrrOccurrence
  let _ =
    resolveExactReturnSite
      (siteFor mctx)
      omEmpty
      "make"
      tagRef
      implRef
      resultMono
      request
      ""
      None
      scope
  let goals = optionOr [] (methodReturnArgs gctx request)
  let ownedKey =
    match ieSelectRowByIface (siteFor mctx) env ownedRow.msrIface goals
      Some selected => rowRouteKey selected
      None => ""
  let foreignKey =
    match ieSelectRowByIface (siteFor mctx) env foreignRow.msrIface goals
      Some selected => rowRouteKey selected
      None => ""
  (methodReturnProbeRouteKey tagRef.value, ownedKey, foreignKey)

-- The request is created before the spelling table is pointed at Foreign.  The checker
-- must still reject a graph containing only Foreign's impl, its positive control must
-- accept Owner's impl, and the stamper must select Owner's distinct route.
methodReturnOwnershipProbe : Unit -> (List String, List String, Bool, Bool)
methodReturnOwnershipProbe _ =
  let ownedGraph = probeGraphCtx ()
  let ownedDecl =
    methodReturnProbeIface
      "return-owner"
      "Owner"
      (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (TyVar "a"))
  let foreignDecl =
    methodReturnProbeIface
      "return-foreign"
      "Foreign"
      (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (TyVar "a"))
  let ownedCtx = initialModuleCtx ownedGraph
  let ownedRow = firstMethodRow (ifaceMethodSchemeRows ownedCtx [ownedDecl])
  let foreignGraph = GraphCtx { ownedGraph | graphRun = freshGraphRun () }
  let foreignCtx = carryModuleCtx foreignGraph ownedCtx
  let foreignRow =
    firstMethodRow (ifaceMethodSchemeRows foreignCtx [foreignDecl])
  let ownedImpl = methodReturnProbeImpl "return-owner" "Owner"
  let foreignImpl = methodReturnProbeImpl "return-foreign" "Foreign"
  let (rejected, rejectedCtx) =
    methodReturnProbeCodes foreignCtx ownedRow [foreignImpl]
  let (accepted, acceptedCtx) =
    methodReturnProbeCodes rejectedCtx ownedRow [foreignImpl, ownedImpl]
  let (actualKey, ownedKey, foreignKey) = methodReturnProbeStamp
    acceptedCtx
    ownedRow
    foreignRow
    [foreignImpl, ownedImpl]
  let observed = (
    rejected,
    accepted,
    actualKey == ownedKey,
    actualKey /= foreignKey,
  )
  observed

-- > methodReturnOwnershipProbe ()
-- (["T-NO-IMPL"], [], True, True)

export
methodReturnResolutionMutationProbe : Unit -> (Bool, Bool, Bool, Bool)
methodReturnResolutionMutationProbe _ =
  let gctx = probeGraphCtx ()
  let mctx = initialModuleCtx gctx
  let _ = methodReturnProbeScope mctx "return-outcome-validation"
  let ownedDecl =
    methodReturnProbeIface
      "return-owner"
      "Owner"
      (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (TyVar "a"))
  let ownedRow = firstMethodRow (ifaceMethodSchemeRows mctx [ownedDecl])
  let ownedImpl = methodReturnProbeImpl "return-owner" "Owner"
  mctx.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef := buildFlatImplEnv [ownedImpl]
  let request = methodReturnProbeRequest mctx ownedRow
  let resolution = solveExactReturnOnce (siteFor mctx) request
  let valid = methodReturnResolutionValid mctx request resolution
  let (wrongSelection, wrongPrerequisites) = match resolution.mrrOutcome
    Solved (InstanceEvidence _ args prerequisites supers) => (
      MethodReturnResolution {
        mrrWanted = resolution.mrrWanted,
        mrrOutcome =
          Solved
            (InstanceEvidence
              (RequestInstanceId (-1))
              args
              prerequisites
              supers),
        mrrSelectedRow = resolution.mrrSelectedRow,
      },
      MethodReturnResolution {
        mrrWanted = resolution.mrrWanted,
        mrrOutcome =
          Solved
            (InstanceEvidence
              (RequestInstanceId (methodReturnSelectedIdentity resolution))
              args
              (PrerequisiteEvidence {
                  prerequisiteInterface =
                    resolution.mrrWanted.predicate.predicateInterface,
                  prerequisiteArguments = args,
                }
                :: prerequisites)
              supers),
        mrrSelectedRow = resolution.mrrSelectedRow,
      },
    )
    _ => panic "ordinary return mutation probe expected instance evidence"
  let wanted = resolution.mrrWanted
  let wrongWanted = Wanted {
    id = wanted.id,
    predicate = wanted.predicate,
    origin = wanted.origin,
    scope = ScopeId 999999,
    destination = wanted.destination,
  }
  let disagreement = MethodReturnResolution {
    mrrWanted = wrongWanted,
    mrrOutcome = resolution.mrrOutcome,
    mrrSelectedRow = resolution.mrrSelectedRow,
  }
  let observed = (
    valid,
    not (methodReturnResolutionValid mctx request wrongSelection),
    not (methodReturnResolutionValid mctx request wrongPrerequisites),
    not (methodReturnResolutionValid mctx request disagreement),
  )
  observed

methodReturnSelectedIdentity : MethodReturnResolution -> Int
methodReturnSelectedIdentity resolution = match resolution.mrrOutcome
  Solved (InstanceEvidence (RequestInstanceId identity) _ _ _) => identity
  _ => -1

methodReturnProbeSlotIfaces : List PredicateSlot -> List String
methodReturnProbeSlotIfaces slots = map (slot => slot.psIface.irName) slots

methodReturnProbeGoalIfaces : List Obligation -> List String
methodReturnProbeGoalIfaces [] = []
methodReturnProbeGoalIfaces (goal :: rest) = match goal.oPayload
  GPMethodDict pending =>
    methodReturnProbeSlotIfaces pending.pmdSlots
      ++ methodReturnProbeGoalIfaces rest
  _ => methodReturnProbeGoalIfaces rest

methodReturnProbeOblIfaces : List UObligation -> List String
methodReturnProbeOblIfaces [] = []
methodReturnProbeOblIfaces (obl :: rest) =
  let here = match obl.prov
    PMethodLevel => [obl.pred.iface.irName]
    _ => []
  here ++ methodReturnProbeOblIfaces rest

-- Runs in a carry of [prev], the caller's record, in its graph record with a fresh
-- graph run, and returns it beside the observation: it is the record left current.
methodReturnProbeSlotCase : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  Bool ->
  ((List String, List String), ModuleCtx)
methodReturnProbeSlotCase prev ownedRow foreignRow retainOwner =
  let gctx = GraphCtx { prev.mcGraph | graphRun = freshGraphRun () }
  let mctx = carryModuleCtx gctx prev
  let _ = methodReturnProbeScope mctx "return-owner-slots"
  mctx.mcCells.methodPredicateSlotsRef :=
    [(methodSlotKey foreignRow.msrIface "make", foreignRow.msrMethodSlots)]
  let _ = methodReturnProbeSpelling mctx foreignRow
  let env =
    if retainOwner then
      extendMethodRow (envFor mctx) "make" ownedRow
    else
      extendVar (envFor mctx) "make" ownedRow.msrScheme
  let inst = instantiateMethodTracked mctx ownedRow.msrScheme
  let _ =
    unify
      mctx
      (stripArrows inst.mtiBody)
      (tupleMono [tconBuiltin "Int", tconBuiltin "Int"])
  let _ =
    recordSite
      env
      "make"
      ownedRow.msrScheme
      (Ref "")
      (Ref RNone)
      (Ref [])
      (Ref [])
      (Ref innerNone)
      inst.mtiBody
      inst.mtiSubstitution
  (
    (
      methodReturnProbeOblIfaces (wAll mctx.mcCells.obls),
      methodReturnProbeGoalIfaces gctx.graphRun.goals.value,
    ),
    mctx,
  )

-- The retained row owns Seed, the same-name legacy table owns Decoy, and an empty
-- retained row is a known empty answer.  Only the missing-row compatibility control
-- may fall back to Decoy.
methodReturnSlotOwnershipProbe : Unit ->
  ((List String, List String), (List String, List String), (List String, List String))
methodReturnSlotOwnershipProbe _ =
  let ownedGraph = probeGraphCtx ()
  let ownedCtx = initialModuleCtx ownedGraph
  let ownedRow =
    firstMethodRow
      (ifaceMethodSchemeRows ownedCtx [
        methodReturnProbeIface
          "return-owner-slots"
          "OwnedSlots"
          (TyConstrained
            [methodRowTestConstraint "return-seed" "Seed" [TyVar "b"]]
            (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (TyTuple [TyVar "b", TyVar "a"]))),
      ])
  let emptyGraph = GraphCtx { ownedGraph | graphRun = freshGraphRun () }
  let emptyCtx = carryModuleCtx emptyGraph ownedCtx
  let emptyRow =
    firstMethodRow
      (ifaceMethodSchemeRows emptyCtx [
        methodReturnProbeIface
          "return-empty-slots"
          "EmptySlots"
          (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (TyVar "a")),
      ])
  let foreignGraph = GraphCtx { ownedGraph | graphRun = freshGraphRun () }
  let foreignCtx = carryModuleCtx foreignGraph emptyCtx
  let foreignRow =
    firstMethodRow
      (ifaceMethodSchemeRows foreignCtx [
        methodReturnProbeIface
          "return-foreign-slots"
          "ForeignSlots"
          (TyConstrained
            [methodRowTestConstraint "return-decoy" "Decoy" [TyVar "b"]]
            (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (TyTuple [TyVar "b", TyVar "a"]))),
      ])
  let (retained, retainedCtx) =
    methodReturnProbeSlotCase foreignCtx ownedRow foreignRow True
  let (emptied, emptiedCtx) =
    methodReturnProbeSlotCase retainedCtx emptyRow foreignRow True
  let (missing, _) =
    methodReturnProbeSlotCase emptiedCtx ownedRow foreignRow False
  let observed = (retained, emptied, missing)
  observed

-- > methodReturnSlotOwnershipProbe ()
-- ((["Seed"], ["Seed"]), ([], []), (["Decoy"], ["Decoy"]))

-- COULD a given for this goal still be registered, once the enclosing binding finishes
-- generalizing?  Both conditions are `registerPredGiven`'s own, because it is the only
-- writer that can ever answer a structured goal:
--   * NON-EMPTY.  It returns `()` for the empty vector and registers nothing, so an
--     empty goal can never acquire an answer.  (This used to read "ARITY 1", because the
--     registry matched `[subject]` only — #1956 replaced that narrowing with the whole
--     vector on all three channels (`requires`, declared, inferred), so a MULTI-PARAMETER
--     structured goal now DOES have a consumption-side answer and this arm no longer
--     withholds it.  The programs that pinned the old wording — `e1_inf_multi.mdk`
--     (`h x = conv (Wrap x) 0`, no signature) and its signatured twin `a2_twoarg.mdk` —
--     are re-measured against this widening, not assumed: see the S-nary-given report.)
--   * UNCLAIMED.  See below; this is the arm that keeps #1939 shape (2) accepted.
--     Asked of the vector's WHOLE unbound-id set, for the same reason the match above is
--     pointwise: a slot is open only if NO binding has already fixed a context claiming
--     any variable this predicate mentions, at any position.
goalSlotStillOpen : ModuleCtx -> List Mono -> Bool
goalSlotStillOpen mctx [] = False
goalSlotStillOpen mctx args =
  not (goalIdsClaimed mctx (flatMap monoUnboundIds args))

-- has some binding's constraint set ALREADY been registered against one of [ids]?  If
-- so that binding's context is fixed and this goal must be part of it; if not, the
-- binding is still generalizing and this goal is what will open its slot.  Reads
-- `funConstraintArgsRef`, which both channels write (`registerMember` for a declared
-- context, `registerInferredFor` for an inferred one), so the test does not distinguish
-- them — the fixedness, not the channel, is what decides.
goalIdsClaimed : ModuleCtx -> List Int -> Bool
goalIdsClaimed mctx [] = False
goalIdsClaimed mctx ids =
  anyClaimRow ids mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsRef.value

anyClaimRow : List Int -> List (String, List PredicateSlot) -> Bool
anyClaimRow _ [] = False
anyClaimRow ids ((_, slots) :: rest) =
  anyList
      (v => anyList (m => anyIn (monoTyvarIds m) ids) v)
      (predicateSlotArgs slots)
    || anyClaimRow ids rest

-- `T-REQUIRES-DEPTH` (issue 1562), worded in the user's vocabulary: the thing they wrote
-- is a `requires` clause.  It renders the goal reached when the fuel ran out, not the
-- goal originally posed, hence "still needed … after N steps".  Only a chain whose steps
-- do not shrink the goal reaches it (`reqWalkEnter`), so the remedy it offers is a
-- smaller `requires` or a direct impl, never less nesting at the call site.
requiresDepthMsg : IfaceRef -> List Mono -> String
requiresDepthMsg iface args =
  "cannot resolve this constraint: following the `requires` clauses of the matching impls still needed `\{iface.irName} \{ppPredArgsShared args}` after \{intToString requiresNonShrinkingFuel} steps that did not make the goal smaller, the limit; make the `requires` of the impls in this chain smaller than their heads, or add a direct `impl \{iface.irName} ...` for one of the types in the chain"

-- `T-REQUIRES-CYCLE`: following `requires` from a goal reached that same goal again, so
-- no finite chain resolves it.  It names the impl whose `requires` posed the repeat (the
-- one the selector picks for the parent goal), and the repeated goal.
requiresCycleMsg : ModuleCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  String
requiresCycleMsg mctx parentIface parentArgs iface args =
  "cannot resolve this constraint: the `requires` of \{requiringImplLabel mctx parentIface parentArgs} asks for `\{iface.irName} \{ppPredArgsShared args}`, which this chain of `requires` is already resolving, so it never ends; change that `requires` clause so it does not lead back to a goal it resolves"

-- The impl the selector picks for [iface] at [args], as written in its declaration.
requiringImplLabel : ModuleCtx -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> String
requiringImplLabel mctx iface args =
  match (ieSelectRowByIface
    (siteFor mctx)
    mctx.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef.value
    iface
    args)
    Some row =>
      "`impl \{iface.irName} \{joinWith " " (map ppTyAtom (ieRowTys row))}`"
    None => "the matching `impl \{iface.irName} ...`"

-- the residual predicates a group's recorded deltas leave over [boundIds], for the
-- DICT-ABSTRACTION channel (`registerInferredFor`). Reads the same two deltas through
-- the same two projections, so the scheme and evidence channels cannot see different
-- predicates. Each triple carries one COMPLETE predicate: its exact interface, its
-- lead id and its full argument vector. The producer below deduplicates and opens one
-- slot per such predicate; the lead is ordering/indexing information, not slot identity.
residualInferredPreds : ModuleCtx ->
  List Int ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List (IfaceRef, Int, List Mono)
residualInferredPreds mctx boundIds preds =
  flatMap (residualInferredPredOf mctx boundIds) preds

residualInferredPredOf : ModuleCtx ->
  List Int ->
  (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List (IfaceRef, Int, List Mono)
residualInferredPredOf mctx boundIds (iface, ds, loc) =
  flatMap
    leadInferredPred
    (residualBoundPreds (siteFor mctx) True boundIds iface ds loc)

-- the DIRECT arm's twin: a predicate every one of whose arguments is already a bound
-- tyvar IS its own residual (`residualVecObls` returns [] for it by design), so its own
-- monos supply the vector and its lead opens the slot. A recursive sibling can
-- inherit this predicate without a methodSiteFns/dictAppFns entry of its own.
directInferredPreds : List Int ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List (IfaceRef, Int, List Mono)
directInferredPreds boundIds preds =
  flatMap (directInferredPredOf boundIds) preds

directInferredPredOf : List Int ->
  (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List (IfaceRef, Int, List Mono)
directInferredPredOf boundIds (iface, ds, _) = match boundTyvarIds boundIds ds
  Some ids => leadInferredPred (iface, ids, ds)
  None => []

-- the receiver id of a deferred predicate — the one this scheme opens a dict slot for.
leadInferredPred : (IfaceRef, List Int, List Mono) ->
  List (IfaceRef, Int, List Mono)
leadInferredPred (iface, ids, args) = match ids
  id :: _ => [(iface, id, args)]
  [] => []

inferredPredLead : (IfaceRef, Int, List Mono) -> Int
inferredPredLead (_, id, _) = id

-- shatter vector obligations into (interface declaration, id) pairs — the currency of the
-- coverage subset test.  See checkSigConstraintCoverage's header.
-- A signed body's inferred predicate is covered only by the same interface declaration;
-- same spelling from a foreign module is not evidence.
pairsOfVecObls : List VecObl -> List (IfaceRef, Int)
pairsOfVecObls [] = []
pairsOfVecObls (o :: rest) =
  map (id => (o.voIface, id)) o.voIds ++ pairsOfVecObls rest

-- ── signature-constraint soundness check ─────────────────────────────────────
-- For each SIGNED member, the interface constraints its body INFERS on the
-- member's own quantified vars must be covered by the DECLARED `=>` context,
-- closed under the interface `requires` (superclass) graph.  An uncovered
-- inferred constraint ⇒ def-site type_error (the constraint analogue of
-- checkEffectEscape).  Under #619 DECLARED-ONLY this is the SOLE enforcement of the
-- body's inferred obligations: registerSchemeObligations no longer merges them into
-- the scheme, so a body needing more than its signature declares is caught HERE or
-- silently severed.  The inferred obligations are the UNION of the flat-path
-- (schemeObligationsOf over addedObls), the FORWARDED path (forwardedVecObls over the
-- constrained-callee call delta — #619: a signed forwarder that under-declares is no
-- longer backstopped by the union, so it must be checked here), and the marked-path
-- (inferredConstraintIds + ifaceForInferredId) sources — a return-position-method
-- constraint lands only in the last.
-- #607: the PAIR test runs in (iface, var-id) currency on both sides — a multi-param
-- predicate is shattered per argument before the subset test (pairsOfVecObls /
-- declaredPairsFor).  Shattering both sides is sound for a COVERAGE (subset) question
-- — declared `Ix a i` covers inferred `Ix a` and `Ix i` — and it makes the reject
-- direction live at n>=2.  On its own it UNDER-rejects the exotic cross-pairing
-- (declared `Ix a b, Ix c d` vs inferred `Ix a d`: all four pairs a,b,c,d are declared,
-- so pair coverage passes though the JOINT `Ix a d` is undeclared).
-- #619/#607 item 4: reportUncoveredVec closes that gap — an inferred JOINT vector
-- (arity >= 2) whose EXACT argument vector is not among the declared vectors
-- (vector-valued superclass closure, censusSuperCloseVec) is
-- uncovered, and is reported when the pair test did not already flag one of its args.
checkSigConstraintCoverage : ModuleCtx ->
  List ConstraintReg ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List UObligation ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  Unit
checkSigConstraintCoverage mctx _ _ _ _ _ [] = ()
checkSigConstraintCoverage mctx regs sigs sigTvMaps callObls addedObls ((m, sch) :: rest) =
  let _ =
    checkSigConstraintOne mctx regs sigs sigTvMaps callObls addedObls m sch
  checkSigConstraintCoverage mctx regs sigs sigTvMaps callObls addedObls rest

checkSigConstraintOne : ModuleCtx ->
  List ConstraintReg ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono, Option Loc) ->
  List UObligation ->
  String ->
  Scheme ->
  Unit
checkSigConstraintOne mctx regs sigs sigTvMaps callObls addedObls m sch =
  match omLookup m mctx.mcCells.sigTyMapRef.value
    None => ()  -- unsigned member: its inferred constraints are promoted, not checked
    Some _ =>
      let declaredPairs =
        censusSuperClose mctx.mcGraph (declaredPairsFor m regs)
      let boundIds = schemeIds sch
      let bodyVecs =
        quantifiedVecObls
          boundIds
          (schemeObligationsOf mctx False boundIds addedObls)
      let fwdVecs =
        quantifiedVecObls
          boundIds
          (forwardedVecObls mctx False boundIds callObls)
      let inferredB = inferredIfacePairs mctx m boundIds
      let inferred =
        dedupIfacePairs
          (pairsOfVecObls bodyVecs ++ pairsOfVecObls fwdVecs ++ inferredB)
      let _ = reportUncovered mctx m sigTvMaps declaredPairs inferred
      let declaredVecs =
        censusSuperCloseVec
          mctx.mcGraph
          (declaredSchemeOblsFor mctx sigTvMaps m boundIds)
      reportUncoveredVec
        mctx
        m
        sigTvMaps
        declaredPairs
        declaredVecs
        (bodyVecs ++ fwdVecs)

-- The vectors over [boundIds] alone.  A signature can declare no predicate on a
-- variable it does not quantify, so a residual that mentions one is never this
-- check's to cover: its verdict is the undetermined goal's, or `checkSigVarGoals`'.
quantifiedVecObls : List Int -> List VecObl -> List VecObl
quantifiedVecObls boundIds vecs =
  filterList
    (o =>
      allList (id => containsI id boundIds) (flatMap monoUnboundIds o.voArgs))
    vecs

-- inferred (iface, id) pairs from the marked path: each inferred constraint var id
-- paired with its recovered iface (skip an id whose iface can't be recovered).
inferredIfacePairs : ModuleCtx -> String -> List Int -> List (IfaceRef, Int)
inferredIfacePairs mctx m boundIds =
  flatMap (pairIface mctx m) (inferredConstraintIds mctx m boundIds)

pairIface : ModuleCtx -> String -> Int -> List (IfaceRef, Int)
pairIface mctx m id =
  let ir = ifaceForInferredId mctx m id
  match ir.irName
    "" => []
    _ => [(ir, id)]

-- the declared (iface, id) constraint pairs of member m: each declared constraint
-- mono normalized to its surviving tyvar id (single-param shape; concrete-grounded
-- constraints — no tyvar — carry no dict slot and are skipped).
declaredPairsFor : String -> List ConstraintReg -> List (IfaceRef, Int)
declaredPairsFor m regs = flatMap declaredPairOne (regIfaceMonosFor m regs)

-- #1161 (F-3a-ii): a reg is a triple, so its (iface, mono) component needs a named
-- accessor (`snd`/`lookupAssoc` no longer apply).  Both spellings — first-match by name,
-- and the whole-list projection — are exactly what the two consumers used before.
regIfaceMonosFor : String -> List ConstraintReg -> List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
regIfaceMonosFor _ [] = []
regIfaceMonosFor m (reg :: rest)
  | m == reg.crName = reg.crIfaceMonos
  | otherwise = regIfaceMonosFor m rest

regIfaceMonosOf : ConstraintReg -> List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
regIfaceMonosOf reg = reg.crIfaceMonos

-- U1b (#1482): project a reg's (interface occurrence, mono) pair back to the SPELLING
-- for `gcMonos`, whose only reader (`dictVarSatisfiesIface`) compares
-- interface NAMES.
-- ⚠️ S-dict-arity-contract: a reg entry is now ONE PREDICATE carrying ALL its bare-tyvar
-- monos, so this fans back out to one (name, mono) pair per variable.  Collapsing the
-- SLOT must not collapse the READ-ONLY census this and `declaredPairOne` feed: they
-- answer "is this variable declared at this interface", not "how many dicts", and
-- dropping `b` from `Ix a b =>` would make a body use at `b` UNCOVERED — an
-- over-rejection of a program that type-checks today.
ifaceMonoName : (IfaceRef, List Mono) -> List (String, Mono)
ifaceMonoName (ir, monos) = map (mono => (ir.irName, mono)) monos

declaredPairOne : (IfaceRef, List Mono) -> List (IfaceRef, Int)
declaredPairOne (iface, monos) = map (id => (iface, id)) (abstractSlotIds monos)

-- Superclass closure over declared (iface, id) slots, so prelude super chains
-- (Applicative requires Mappable, Thenable requires Applicative, …) are included.  It
-- only feeds the read-only subset test; no dict slot comes from it.
censusSuperClose : GraphCtx -> List (IfaceRef, Int) -> List (IfaceRef, Int)
censusSuperClose gctx declared =
  map
    (n => (n.superIface, n.superPayload))
    (superClosure
      (superLookup gctx)
      censusSuperStep
      (iface id => ifacePairKey (iface, id))
      declared)

-- A super shares the sub-predicate's lead id (0 for a nullary super) when every one of
-- its parameters is one of the sub's type parameters.
censusSuperStep : List String -> Int -> Super -> Option Int
censusSuperStep typarams id (Super { superParams = params, ... })
  | not (all (p => contains p typarams) params) = None
  | isEmptyL params = Some 0
  | otherwise = Some id

-- #619/#607 item 4: VECTOR-valued superclass closure over declared constraint vectors.
-- Unlike censusSuperClose (which collapses each predicate to per-arg pairs), this
-- preserves the whole argument vector, so an inferred JOINT predicate can be tested for
-- membership as a unit — the exotic cross-pairing `Ix a d` is NOT a member of
-- {`Ix a b`, `Ix c d`} even though every one of its args appears in some declared
-- predicate.  Ungated, like censusSuperClose.  The interface's type parameters map
-- POSITIONALLY onto a predicate's ids, so a multi-param super carries the right per-arg
-- ids; a super's ground argument positions are not recovered.
censusSuperCloseVec : GraphCtx -> List VecObl -> List VecObl
censusSuperCloseVec gctx declared =
  map
    vecOblOfNode
    (superClosure
      (superLookup gctx)
      censusVecSuperStep
      (iface payload =>
        vecOblKey
          (vecOblOfNode SuperNode {
            superPath = [],
            superIface = iface,
            superPayload = payload,
          }))
      (map (o => (o.voIface, (o.voIds, o.voArgs))) declared))

censusVecSuperStep : List String ->
  (List Int, List Mono) ->
  Super ->
  Option (List Int, List Mono)
censusVecSuperStep typarams (ids, _) (Super { superParams = params, ... }) =
  map (mapped => (mapped, [])) (mapAll (p => lookupPos p typarams ids) params)

vecOblOfNode : SuperNode (List Int, List Mono) -> VecObl
vecOblOfNode n =
  let (ids, args) = n.superPayload
  VecObl { voIface = n.superIface, voIds = ids, voArgs = args }

-- one type_error per inferred JOINT vector (arity >= 2) whose exact vector the declared
-- (super-closed) set does not contain.  Skipped when the pair test already flagged one
-- of the vector's args (allPairsIn False) — so a genuinely absent constraint reports
-- ONCE, via reportUncovered, and only the cross-pairing (all args present, joint
-- vector absent) reports here.  Arity < 2 is fully handled by the pair test.
reportUncoveredVec : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  List (IfaceRef, Int) ->
  List VecObl ->
  List VecObl ->
  Unit
reportUncoveredVec mctx _ _ _ _ [] = ()
reportUncoveredVec mctx m sigTvMaps declaredPairs declaredVecs (o :: rest) =
  let _ =
    if listLen o.voIds < 2 then
      ()
    else if containsVecObl o declaredVecs then
      ()
    else if not (allPairsIn o.voIface o.voIds declaredPairs) then
      ()
    else
      pushTypeError
        mctx
        "T-MISSING-CONSTRAINT"
        (missingConstraintVecMsg
          m
          o.voIface.irName
          (map (varNameForId sigTvMaps m) o.voIds))
  reportUncoveredVec mctx m sigTvMaps declaredPairs declaredVecs rest

allPairsIn : IfaceRef -> List Int -> List (IfaceRef, Int) -> Bool
allPairsIn iface ids declaredPairs =
  allList (id => containsIfacePair (iface, id) declaredPairs) ids

-- one type_error per inferred (iface, id) not covered by the declared-closed set.
reportUncovered : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)) ->
  List (IfaceRef, Int) ->
  List (IfaceRef, Int) ->
  Unit
reportUncovered mctx _ _ _ [] = ()
reportUncovered mctx m sigTvMaps declared ((iface, id) :: rest) =
  let _ =
    if containsIfacePair (iface, id) declared then
      ()
    else
      pushTypeError
        mctx
        "T-MISSING-CONSTRAINT"
        (missingConstraintMsg m iface.irName (varNameForId sigTvMaps m id))
  reportUncovered mctx m sigTvMaps declared rest

containsIfacePair : (IfaceRef, Int) -> List (IfaceRef, Int) -> Bool
containsIfacePair _ [] = False
containsIfacePair (i, d) ((i2, d2) :: rest) =
  sameIfaceDecl i i2 && d == d2 || containsIfacePair (i, d) rest

dedupIfacePairs : List (IfaceRef, Int) -> List (IfaceRef, Int)
dedupIfacePairs xs = dedupBy ifacePairKey xs

ifacePairKey : (IfaceRef, Int) -> String
ifacePairKey (iface, id) =
  regKeyRender (regKeyOfTab (oblIfaceKey iface)) ++ intToString id

-- the member's own quantified tyvar ids that a body method site / propagated
-- constrained-call sits at. This is the legacy trace/fallback supply; complete
-- predicates add their own leads before slot construction.
inferredConstraintIds : ModuleCtx -> String -> List Int -> List Int
inferredConstraintIds mctx m boundIds =
  dedupI
    (flatMap
        (boundTvarId boundIds)
        (sitesFor m mctx.mcCells.methodSiteFns.value)
      ++ flatMap
        (monosTvarIds boundIds)
        (sitesFor m mctx.mcCells.dictAppFns.value))

-- [vecs] carries every complete deferred predicate this binding recovered. Predicate
-- identity is the existing `cslotVecKey` (interface/lead plus the full argument vector),
-- so two predicates may share a lead and still open distinct slots. Trace-only ids with
-- no recovered predicate keep the historical scalar/PSArgsUnknown fallback.
registerInferredFor : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  List Int ->
  List (IfaceRef, Int, List Mono) ->
  Unit
registerInferredFor mctx m scope ids vecs =
  let slots = inferredPredicateSlots mctx m ids vecs
  if isEmptyL slots then
    ()
  else
    let _ = setFunConstraintEntry mctx m slots
    let _ = registerActiveDictVars mctx.mcGraph scope 0 slots
    -- #1909, the inferred twin of `registerMember`: complete predicate slots also
    -- register their structured givens. PSArgsUnknown fallbacks register nothing.
    let _ = registerSlotPredGivens mctx.mcGraph scope 0 slots
    mctx.mcCells.promotedRef := m :: mctx.mcCells.promotedRef.value

inferredPredicateSlots : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List Int ->
  List (IfaceRef, Int, List Mono) ->
  List PredicateSlot
inferredPredicateSlots mctx m ids vecs =
  let pairs = dedupSlotVecs (flatMap inferredPredicatePair vecs)
  let slots = map (predicateSlotFromExpanded omEmpty) pairs
  let buckets = inferredSlotBuckets (reverseL slots) omEmpty
  let covered = inferredSlotCoveredIds slots omEmpty
  inferredPredicateSlotsGo mctx m ids buckets covered []

-- An empty interface has no known vector. Its compatibility representation is the
-- trace-only PSArgsUnknown fallback.
inferredPredicatePair : (IfaceRef, Int, List Mono) -> List (CSlot, List Mono)
inferredPredicatePair (iface, id, args)
  | iface.irName == "" = []
  | otherwise = [(CSlot { csIface = iface, csId = id }, args)]

-- Build by cons over a reversed slot list so every lead bucket retains predicate order.
inferredSlotBuckets : List PredicateSlot ->
  OrdMap (List PredicateSlot) ->
  OrdMap (List PredicateSlot)
inferredSlotBuckets [] acc = acc
inferredSlotBuckets (slot :: rest) acc = match slot.psBoundIds
  [] => inferredSlotBuckets rest acc
  lead :: _ =>
    let key = intToString lead
    let bucket = optionOr [] (omLookup key acc)
    inferredSlotBuckets rest (omInsert key (slot :: bucket) acc)

inferredSlotCoveredIds : List PredicateSlot -> OrdMap Unit -> OrdMap Unit
inferredSlotCoveredIds [] acc = acc
inferredSlotCoveredIds (slot :: rest) acc =
  inferredSlotCoveredIds
    rest
    (omFromNames (map intToString slot.psBoundIds) acc)

-- [acc] is reversed. Each bucket is reversed onto it once, so total work is linear
-- in produced slots rather than repeatedly filtering the remaining id list.
inferredPredicateSlotsGo : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List Int ->
  OrdMap (List PredicateSlot) ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  List PredicateSlot
inferredPredicateSlotsGo mctx _ [] _ _ acc = reverseL acc
inferredPredicateSlotsGo mctx m (id :: rest) buckets covered acc =
  match omLookup (intToString id) buckets
    Some bucket =>
      inferredPredicateSlotsGo
        mctx
        m
        rest
        buckets
        covered
        (prependPredicateSlots bucket acc)
    None if omHasKey (intToString id) covered =>
      inferredPredicateSlotsGo mctx m rest buckets covered acc
    None =>
      let slot = PredicateSlot {
        psIface = ifaceForInferredId mctx m id,
        psArgs = PSArgsUnknown,
        psBoundIds = [id],
      }
      inferredPredicateSlotsGo mctx m rest buckets covered (slot :: acc)

prependPredicateSlots : List PredicateSlot ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  List PredicateSlot
prependPredicateSlots [] acc = acc
prependPredicateSlots (slot :: rest) acc =
  prependPredicateSlots rest (slot :: acc)

-- Private producer probe: same-lead predicates stay distinct, an exact duplicate
-- collapses, a multi-argument predicate owns one slot, a vector whose lead is another
-- predicate's non-lead survives, and a trace-only id retains PSArgsUnknown.
-- > inferredPredicateSlotsProbe (initialModuleCtx (probeGraphCtx ())) ()
-- [("Tweak", ["a", "Int"], ["a"]), ("Tweak", ["a", "Bool"], ["a"]), ("Ix", ["a", "b"], ["a", "b"]), ("Num", ["b"], ["b"]), ("", ["?"], ["c"])]
inferredPredicateSlotsProbe : ModuleCtx ->
  Unit ->
  List (String, List String, List String)
inferredPredicateSlotsProbe mctx _ =
  let a = freshVar mctx ()
  let b = freshVar mctx ()
  let c = freshVar mctx ()
  let aid = firstOrZero (monoTyvarIds a)
  let bid = firstOrZero (monoTyvarIds b)
  let cid = firstOrZero (monoTyvarIds c)
  let tweak = ifaceRefBare "Tweak"
  let slots =
    inferredPredicateSlots
      mctx
      "__inferred_predicate_slot_probe__"
      [aid, bid, cid]
      [
        (tweak, aid, [a, tconBuiltin "Int"]),
        (tweak, aid, [a, tconBuiltin "Bool"]),
        (tweak, aid, [a, tconBuiltin "Int"]),
        (ifaceRefBare "Ix", aid, [a, b]),
        (ifaceRefBare "Num", bid, [b]),
      ]
  map (inferredPredicateSlotProbeRow aid bid cid) slots

inferredPredicateSlotProbeRow : Int ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  PredicateSlot ->
  (String, List String, List String)
inferredPredicateSlotProbeRow aid bid cid slot = (
  slot.psIface.irName,
  match slot.psArgs
    PSArgsUnknown => ["?"]
    PSArgsKnown args => map (inferredPredicateSlotMonoTag aid bid cid) args,
  map (inferredPredicateSlotIdTag aid bid cid) slot.psBoundIds,
)

inferredPredicateSlotMonoTag : Int -> Int -> Int -> Mono -> String
inferredPredicateSlotMonoTag aid bid cid mono = match peelQual mono
  TVar cell => inferredPredicateSlotIdTag aid bid cid (tyvarId cell)
  TCon name _ => name
  _ => "_"

inferredPredicateSlotIdTag : Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> String
inferredPredicateSlotIdTag aid bid cid id
  | id == aid = "a"
  | id == bid = "b"
  | id == cid = "c"
  | otherwise = "_"

-- N5 (inherited, slice 1): entry ABSENCE means "no argument vector was recorded for this
-- callee at all", and every reader turns it into `(slot, [])` — the historical scalar
-- per-tyvar goal, byte for byte.  A row of all-empty vectors reads identically at every
-- reader, same-module and cross-module alike, so writing one would only ADD a
-- `funConstraintArgsRef` / `crossModuleFunConstraintArgsQualRef` row that says nothing.
-- Recover nothing ⇒ write nothing, exactly as before this slice.
-- #23: the iface name for an inferred constraint var.  `ifaceForConstraintId` only
-- recovers it from a pendingImplObligation whose `occ` is a BARE `TVar id`; a
-- constraint induced by a `fromInt`/method site records a COMPOUND occ (the whole
-- method type), so it returns "" — leaving the call site's dict route unkeyed
-- (`routeUndeterminedTop ""` → RNone → a NULL Num dict word → build SIGTRAP, while
-- `medaka run` is correct).  Two FALLBACKS recover the name when ifaceForConstraintId
-- returns "" (so existing non-"" routes stay byte-identical):
--   (1) `schemeObligationsRef` pairs each scheme var with its iface via
--       `dispatchMonosOf` (robust to compound occs); covers a fn whose own body has
--       the literal/method site (`app2 f = f 2 3`).
--   (2) a constraint FORWARDED from a constrained callee (`useApp g = app2 g`) never
--       lands in pendingImplObligations/schemeObligations — its iface lives in the
--       `pendingDictApps` entry the callee's inferDictAtFound recorded (slot-parallel
--       monos/ifaces).  Scan it for the var at a slot whose iface is now known.
-- Both run AFTER the callee's own constraints are registered (topological SCC order),
-- so the forwarded callee's ifaces are populated.
-- U1b (#1482): returns an `IfaceRef`, since `funConstraintIfacesRef` now stores one.
-- Every source carries the interface's declaration: `implObls` and
-- `schemeObligationsRef` hold the occurrence's, and a forwarded constraint takes the
-- callee slot's `pdaIfaces` entry.  Two same-spelled interfaces therefore stay two
-- slots here (#3679), which a name-only recovery would merge.  The scan is over the
-- CURRENT module's goals only: an earlier module's application of the same scheme var
-- id would be a stale read under the graph-wide counter.  `ifaceRefNone` is the "no
-- interface here" sentinel, which is a different fact from "identity unrecoverable".
ifaceForInferredId : ModuleCtx -> String -> Int -> IfaceRef
ifaceForInferredId mctx m id =
  let direct = ifaceForConstraintId mctx id
  if direct.irName /= "" then
    direct
  else match lookupSchemeIface m id mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value
    Some ir => ir
    None =>
      ifaceFromDictApps
        id
        (dictAppsSince mctx.mcGraph (currentModuleMarks mctx.mcGraph ()).mGoals)

-- #837: keyed by member NAME only (the id here is a SCHEME-VAR id, not a binding
-- id) — match the name component of the (name, binding-id) key, first match wins.
lookupSchemeIface : String ->
  Int ->
  List ((String, Int), List VecObl) ->
  Option IfaceRef
lookupSchemeIface _ _ [] = None
lookupSchemeIface m id (((m2, _), obs) :: rest)
  | m == m2 = match lookupIfaceById id obs
    Some iface => Some iface
    None => lookupSchemeIface m id rest
  | otherwise = lookupSchemeIface m id rest

-- the iface of the first recorded predicate whose ARGUMENT VECTOR mentions [id].
-- (#607: an obligation's ids became a vector; at arity 1 this is the old `id == oid`.)
-- This per-id recovery is inherently 1-ary — it answers "which interface constrains
-- this var", which for a multi-param predicate has no single right answer; it feeds
-- the dict-slot/route tables, whose per-tyvar shattering is punch-list item 3.
lookupIfaceById : Int -> List VecObl -> Option IfaceRef
lookupIfaceById _ [] = None
lookupIfaceById id (o :: rest)
  | containsI id o.voIds = Some o.voIface
  | otherwise = lookupIfaceById id rest

-- Scan pendingDictApps for [id] at a slot (bare-TVar mono) whose iface is non-empty,
-- returning that slot's interface with its declaration; `ifaceRefNone` when none does.
ifaceFromDictApps : Int -> List PendingDictApp -> IfaceRef
ifaceFromDictApps _ [] = ifaceRefNone
ifaceFromDictApps id (app :: rest) =
  match ifaceAtMonoId id app.pdaMonos app.pdaIfaces
    Some ir => ir
    None => ifaceFromDictApps id rest

ifaceAtMonoId : Int -> List Mono -> List IfaceRef -> Option IfaceRef
ifaceAtMonoId _ [] _ = None
ifaceAtMonoId _ _ [] = None
ifaceAtMonoId id (m :: ms) (i :: is) = match normalize m
  TVar cell =>
    if tyvarId cell == id && i.irName /= "" then
      Some i
    else
      ifaceAtMonoId id ms is
  _ => ifaceAtMonoId id ms is

-- recover the interface name of an INFERRED constraint var (unsignatured fn like
-- `f x = x + 1`): the var was recorded in a pendingImplObligation by the method
-- occurrence that induced the constraint (`+` → a `Num <thisvar>` entry).  Slot-
-- aligned with registerInferredFor's id list.  "" if unresolvable — recordCallObligations
-- still pairs it positionally, and checkOneCallObligation with an empty iface finds no
-- matching impl head ⇒ it only fires for a CONCRETE-head mono whose iface genuinely had
-- no impl, which for an inferred Num constraint is exactly the hole we close.  A still-
-- polymorphic head defers regardless of iface, so a blank iface never over-rejects.
ifaceForConstraintId : ModuleCtx -> Int -> IfaceRef
ifaceForConstraintId mctx id =
  ifaceForConstraintIdGo id mctx.mcCells.implObls.items.value

ifaceForConstraintIdGo : Int -> List UObligation -> IfaceRef
ifaceForConstraintIdGo _ [] = ifaceRefNone
ifaceForConstraintIdGo id (o :: rest) = match o.oblProj
  OpMethodOcc _ _ occ _ => match normalize occ
    TVar cell =>
      if tyvarId cell == id then
        o.pred.iface
      else
        ifaceForConstraintIdGo id rest
    _ => ifaceForConstraintIdGo id rest
  OpExactReturn request => match normalize request.mrrOccurrence
    TVar cell =>
      if tyvarId cell == id then
        request.mrrIface
      else
        ifaceForConstraintIdGo id rest
    _ => ifaceForConstraintIdGo id rest
  OpProjected => ifaceForConstraintIdGo id rest
  OpNumLit occ => match normalize occ
    TVar cell =>
      if tyvarId cell == id then
        o.pred.iface
      else
        ifaceForConstraintIdGo id rest
    _ => ifaceForConstraintIdGo id rest

registerActiveDictVars : GraphCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  Int ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  Unit
registerActiveDictVars gctx _ _ [] = ()
registerActiveDictVars gctx scope slot (s :: rest) =
  let _ = registerEachActiveId gctx s.psBoundIds (Scopes.binderAt scope slot)
  registerActiveDictVars gctx scope (slot + 1) rest

-- Render accumulated type errors as `TYPE ERROR: <msg>` lines (in order of
-- occurrence — typeErrors accumulates newest-first, so reverse).
typeErrorLines : List String -> List String
typeErrorLines [] = []
typeErrorLines (e :: rest) = "TYPE ERROR: " ++ e :: typeErrorLines rest

-- #415 item 1: the seeding PREAMBLE every runtime-seeded entry point runs before its
-- typecheck pass — the head half of the sandwich whose tail is `runFinalChecks`.
-- [oracleDecls] is the decl set the ctor oracle is built from: the ONE axis the callers
-- legitimately differ on (the flat paths pass `prog`; checkModuleFullDiags passes
-- `prog ++ accData` own-module-FIRST — see the P0-9 note there, that order is load-bearing).
-- The module's mint (`checkBodyImpl`) installs the seed: this oracle and an empty
-- warnings list.
seedCheckRun : List Decl -> CheckRunSeed
seedCheckRun oracleDecls = CheckRunSeed {
  crsOracle = buildOracle oracleDecls,
  crsWarnings = [],
}

-- #415 item 1: seed-and-run for the three FLAT runtime-seeded entry points
-- (the `checkOne*` wrappers). They
-- used to repeat this body verbatim under a "Mirrors checkToLinesWithRuntime's
-- side-effects EXACTLY" comment — a mirror obligation enforced only by that comment.
-- They now differ ONLY in what they HARVEST from the accumulators afterwards, so the
-- seeding+coherence they share has exactly one body and cannot drift.
-- ⚠️ trap #5, same as runFinalChecks: coherence sees the driver-staged USER decls only,
-- NEVER `prog`.  A user impl deliberately overrides a seeded prelude impl, so feeding
-- the seeded set to checkCoherence false-positives on the stdlib itself.
-- ── type-aware non-exhaustive-match check (the `check_match` driver) ────────
-- Run the full typecheck pass over [prog] (runtime externs seeded, NO prelude —
-- mirrors the reference's check_program_no_prelude oracle) and return one
-- `Warning: non-exhaustive match …` line per `match` that isn't exhaustive.
-- The oracle is built from the program's own data decls + the syntactic builtins
-- (same set check_match's env-backed oracle has in the no-prelude path).  Diffs
-- against `dev/diagdump.exe --check-match` (the harness sorts).
-- ── diagnostics entry point (compiler/driver/diagnostics.mdk bridge) ────────────
-- Run the full typecheck pass (runtime-seeded) over [prog] and return the
-- accumulated errors and non-exhaustive-match warnings as `TcDiag`s — each
-- carrying its own code, span (B.10.2b / S4), message, and optional help/fix —
-- so diagnostics.mdk maps them straight to structured `Diag` values.
-- ── multi-module typecheck (bootstrap front-end) ───────────────────────────
-- Threads per-module exports in dependency order.  The prelude (core) is checked
-- ONCE and ALL its schemes + ctors seed every module (it's implicitly visible);
-- each compiler module then contributes only its PUBLIC value schemes — private
-- helpers stay module-local, so same-named helpers across modules never collide
-- (the per-module-frame property, without a frame) — plus its public ctors.
-- Returns each module's OWN value schemes, in load order.

-- typecheck one program with seeded value schemes + accumulated data decls, as
-- the prelude's core pass.  Re-registers prior modules' public data declarations
-- (`accData ++ prog`) so imported constructors AND named-field-variant record
-- info (e.g. ast's DInterface) resolve.  The program's own impls are its impl
-- universe, as the tree arm's core pass (`elabModuleStamp`) has them: an impl
-- body's occurrence then routes through the impl's `requires` given on both arms.
-- Returns the module's own value schemes.  [prev] is the record current before the
-- pass, whose oracle and warnings the unseeded pass carries.
checkModuleFull : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (ModuleBindings, List Decl, ModuleCtx)
checkModuleFull prev seedVars accData prog =
  checkModuleFullImpl
    prev.mcGraph
    (checkRunResidue prev)
    ""
    (plainModuleSeed seedVars)
    accData
    prog
    prog

-- E5: like checkModuleFull but takes [implDecls] (core + every EARLIER module — NOT this
-- module: foldModules only grows the accumulator for LATER modules, so a module is never in
-- its own [implDecls]; a caller that needs this module's own decls too must fold [prog] in
-- itself, as the `superDecls` binding in checkBodyImpl does for #1457) as the impl-body
-- inference universe.  It ALSO infers THIS module's parametric impl
-- bodies, so their
-- ARG-position ELEMENT dispatch (`eq`/`compare`/… on the impl head tyvar) reaches
-- inferMethodAt and lands in pendingArgStamps, which elabModuleStamp's
-- resolveArgStamps then stamps RDict (via the requires dict registered by
-- registerImplRequires).  The stage-K ClassEnv gives body inference the interface
-- declarations, while [implDecls] lets a body dispatch against an earlier module's impl.
-- [gctx] and [runSeed] are the drive's graph record and the module's check-run seed,
-- passed to its mint (see `checkBodyImpl`), and the module's record is returned beside
-- its bindings.
checkModuleFullImpl : GraphCtx ->
  CheckRunSeed ->
  String ->
  ModuleSeed ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (ModuleBindings, List Decl, ModuleCtx)
checkModuleFullImpl gctx runSeed mid seedVars _accData implDecls prog =
  let (schemes, marked, mctx) =
    checkBodyImpl gctx runSeed seedVars mid implDecls prog
  -- #2705 (M2 phase 2): solving is not optional.  Every module a Module-arm driver
  -- checks — `check`, `run`, `build`, the LSP alike — cuts its stamping context
  -- here, at the point its stampers used to run, for the one graph-end drain
  -- (`drainStampQueue`, DICT §6.2 T4).  A driver that queues and never drains
  -- leaves the queue for the next driver entry, so every Module-arm driver ends
  -- with a drain (`driveGraphK`'s, or `checkGraphFinish` on a memo path).
  let _ = enqueueStampCtx mctx mid implDecls
  (schemes, marked, mctx)
-- C5: compute this module's standalone-shadow set BEFORE inference, so the
-- inferMethodAt arg-position record can gate on it (`freshModuleCtx` cleared it via
-- pendingRLocalSites, but standaloneValuesRef is set fresh here per module).
--
-- Two flavours of standalone-shadow, BOTH needing RLocal recording so a method
-- call on a no-impl receiver routes to the standalone instead of mis-dispatching:
--   • IMPORTER shadow (`importerShadows`): a name imported from a sibling that is
--     also an interface method (box importing map's `toList`).  Its scheme must be
--     REBOUND to the interface-method scheme (`shadowMethodSchemes`) so the call
--     site types polymorphically; RLocal then redirects the no-impl receiver back.
--   • DEFINER shadow (`definerShadows`): a name THIS module defines as a top-level
--     funDef that ALSO names an interface method (map-as-root's own `toList` /
--     `isEmpty`).  The MARK pass (`buildStandaloneShadowsGraph`) rewrites these to
--     `EMethodAt`, so without a matching RLocal record the route falls back to the
--     result-type `RKey` (e.g. `toList`'s `List` result), dispatching the method on
--     the WRONG impl (List's `toList = identity`) → `debug`/`display` recurse on the
--     unchanged receiver forever (Map Debug/Eq/Ord impl bodies call standalone
--     `toList`).  These must be RECORDED for RLocal but must NOT be rebound to the
--     method scheme — their local standalone scheme (`Map k v -> …`) is what the
--     impl body types against.

-- E6: re-install the cross-module constraint accumulator that `freshModuleCtx` just
-- wiped, so this module's `=>`-constrained call sites into EARLIER modules resolve.
-- Post-ARGSTAMP-UNIFY (Phase 4): eval and emit both thread dicts, so this runs
-- UNCONDITIONALLY on every path (single elaboration mode).

-- `methodEntryHere` answers from stage K's whole-graph `deMethods` (core, earlier
-- modules and this prog), so resolveSite's ifaceParamMonos can recover a multi-param
-- interface's full param monos (the element grounding `e` for `FromEntries c e`).
-- An empty table on the module path would make ifaceParamMonos return None → a
-- Set/Map-literal return-position `fromEntries` route drops its `Ord` element dict →
-- null dict → SIGSEGV.

-- C5: a standalone-shadow method name (box's `toList`/`isEmpty`) is bound in
-- seedVars to its imported MONOMORPHIC standalone scheme (`Box k v -> …`), which
-- would shadow the polymorphic interface-method scheme and mis-type a genuine
-- method call (`isEmpty [1,2,3]` unifying List with Box).  Re-bind those names to
-- the graph-wide METHOD scheme so the call site types against the method; RLocal then redirects only the no-impl receiver back to the standalone
-- at eval: the EApp method-head arm types against the
-- method scheme even when a standalone value holds the name.
-- DEFINER shadows are EXCLUDED here: the module's OWN funDef (map-root's `toList`)
-- must type against its local standalone scheme (`Map k v -> List (k, v)`), not the
-- imported method scheme — the impl bodies call it ON a Map.  Only IMPORTER shadows
-- (imported-from-sibling method names) get the method-scheme rebind.

-- E5: infer this module's parametric impl bodies (gated, emit path only), seeing
-- [implDecls] for interface method types + cross-module impl dispatch.  The sites
-- it records stay in pendingArgStamps/pendingSites for elabModuleStamp to resolve.

-- C8(b): also infer THIS module's interface DEFAULT bodies (gated identically to
-- the single-file path's inferDefaultBodiesIfEnabled) so a default body's type
-- error is caught on every path.

-- Phase 4.55: infer this
-- module's prop bodies so their prepass-marked EDictAt/EMethodAt routes resolve.
-- The multi-module test path (runPropsMulti) evaluates the ELABORATED prop body
-- against the dict-passed env, so the body's calls into the file's own promoted
-- `=>`-constrained fns (set's `wellFormed`/`fromList`) need their dict-arg routes
-- filled here — otherwise the call under-applies the dict-passed callee → not VBool
-- → every prop "fails".  funDefs ignores DProp, so without this the module path
-- never typed props at all.

-- E6: fold THIS module's freshly-registered fn-constraints into the cross-module
-- accumulator so a LATER module's call site finds them after its own reset.
-- Post-ARGSTAMP-UNIFY (Phase 4): unconditional on every path (single elaboration mode).

-- Shape A (gap #44): ground a container literal's free result-element var THROUGH
-- the unique impl's method type, so this module's pending sites/arg-stamps resolve
-- against the GROUNDED element (Set Int, not Set _a).  [implDecls] is the full impl
-- universe (core ++ earlier modules ++ prog), so the Set/Map impls are visible.

-- public top-level value names (the pub flag may sit on the sig, def, or extern).
-- C8(a): a PUBLIC interface ALSO exports its method names so an importer can see
-- their schemes — methods of an
-- `is_pub = true` interface are appended to the exported value schemes.
publicValNames : List Decl -> List String
publicValNames [] = []
publicValNames ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) =
  publicValNames [d] ++ publicValNames rest
publicValNames ((DFunDef True n _ _ _ _) :: rest) = n :: publicValNames rest
publicValNames ((DTypeSig True n _ _) :: rest) = n :: publicValNames rest
publicValNames ((DExtern (ExternDecl { edPub = True, edName = n, ... })) :: rest) =
  n :: publicValNames rest
publicValNames ((DInterface { pub = True, methods, ... }) :: rest) =
  ifaceMethodNames methods ++ publicValNames rest
publicValNames (_ :: rest) = publicValNames rest

-- C5: every interface method name declared anywhere in [decls] (unwrapping DAttrib).
allIfaceMethodNames : List Decl -> List String
allIfaceMethodNames [] = []
allIfaceMethodNames ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) =
  allIfaceMethodNames [d] ++ allIfaceMethodNames rest
allIfaceMethodNames ((DInterface { methods, ... }) :: rest) =
  ifaceMethodNames methods ++ allIfaceMethodNames rest
allIfaceMethodNames (_ :: rest) = allIfaceMethodNames rest

-- C5 (DEFINER shadow): the names THIS module declares as a top-level funDef that
-- ALSO name an interface method visible in [implDecls] (the imported prelude/core).
-- E.g. map-as-root defines `isEmpty`, which shadows Foldable's method of that name.
-- The
-- MARK pass (`buildStandaloneShadowsGraph`) rewrites occurrences of these to
-- `EMethodAt`, so they MUST be in `standaloneValuesRef` for `recordRLocalSite` to
-- record an RLocal candidate — otherwise the route falls back to the method's
-- RESULT-type RKey and the method dispatches on the WRONG impl.
-- Unlike importer shadows these keep their LOCAL standalone scheme (NOT rebound to the
-- method scheme), since the impl bodies apply them to the concrete receiver.
-- #154 PR1: fold THIS module's decls into the persistent universe accumulators
-- (declared in `CrossRun`).  Called from checkBodyImpl's Module arm BEFORE the shadow
-- reads, so this module's own decls are visible there — exactly as `fullUniverse` (which
-- appended prog0) was.
-- ⚠️ ARCH B-2.1-d REMOVED THE KEY-BUCKET LINE from this fold, with the
-- `universeKeyBucketsRef` cell it grew.  That line re-entered `bucketKeyEntries` once per
-- module with a NON-EMPTY accumulator, which is what duplicated declaration indices across
-- modules and left each module's slice descending; at the time, `buildKeyTable` was
-- `bucketKeyEntries`' sole caller and passed `omEmpty` (see `mergeByDeclIdx`).  Both
-- `buildKeyTable` and `bucketKeyEntries` (and the whole key-bucket table, `KeyBuckets`) were
-- deleted by `S-keytable-payoff`.  Do not re-add a cumulative key-bucket accumulator here:
-- impl EXISTENCE and impl SELECTION both read the graph-global `bodyImplEnvRef` now, and a
-- prefix-keyed second population is the shape B-2.1-c/-f/-g each measured an S0 out of.
-- BOTH SPELLINGS of the prelude's module id under `Module` mode, in one place.  The
-- export indexes (`meExports`, `deCtorExports`) key the prelude under `"core"`, but
-- the `mid` `graphPreamble` actually PASSES for the core pass is `""` on both output
-- selections (`GOutDiags`:
-- `checkCoreMemoized` → `checkModuleFull` → `checkModuleFullImpl ""`; `GOutTrees`:
-- `elabModuleStamp ""`).  A test of one spelling alone silently never fires on either
-- selection.  Two callers — `seedBuiltinClasses` and
-- `appendUniverseAccums` (below) — and they must not drift apart, since both ask the
-- same question: "is the unit being folded the implicit prelude?"
isPreludeMid : String -> Bool
isPreludeMid mid = mid == "core" || mid == ""

-- ⚠️ #1557 A-3.5a REMOVED THE COMPLETENESS LINE from this fold, with the
-- `universeIfaceRequiredRef` cell and its `insertIfaceRequired` writer.  The ordering
-- guarantee this comment records ("this module's own decls are visible at the read")
-- is no longer what impl-completeness depends on: it reads stage K's `CE`, whose rows
-- carry their declaring module's ordinal, and `declEnvVisibleAt cur o` (`o <= cur`)
-- admits the reader's OWN row — the same 0..cur-inclusive prefix the accumulator held
-- here.  Do not re-add a completeness accumulator to restore an ordering property that
-- has moved onto the ordinal predicate.
appendUniverseAccums : GraphCtx -> String -> List Decl -> Unit
appendUniverseAccums gctx mid prog =
  -- 🚨 SHADOW-SEMANTICS S1-PRELUDE (a), RULED 2026-08-10 (#1375 item 2, #1499 clause (b)):
  -- The prelude is not S1's left (standalone) operand.  The asymmetry with the shadow
  -- builders' interface-method test, `methodNameDeclaredAt`, which counts the prelude's
  -- interfaces at ordinal 0, is deliberate and is S1-PRELUDE's own
  -- (`SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md:225`): S1's INTERFACE operand is the wider "nameable in M",
  -- which INCLUDES the prelude, while its STANDALONE operand is pinned by the
  -- definer/importer kind partition — and a standalone reaching M only as an implicit
  -- prelude export is NEITHER kind, so it creates no shadow in M.
  -- This ref's ONE reader is the `importerShadows` binding in `checkBodyImpl`
  -- (`standaloneShadowsFromSet`'s `fnSet`), i.e. exactly that left operand; folding the
  -- prelude's own funDefs in admitted every prelude standalone as an IMPORTER shadow —
  -- the reading S1-PRELUDE names and REJECTS by consequence — so a user interface method
  -- colliding with `isEven`/`count` fell back to the prelude function at any receiver head
  -- carrying no impl, ACCEPTING at exit 0 where the ruling requires a located reject
  -- (`test/shadow_fixtures/x1_prelude_standalone_not_left_operand.mdk`, x2, matrix rows
  -- 46-48).  ⚠️ SUBTRACTING the prelude's names at the READ site instead would be WRONG:
  -- a name the prelude AND a real user module both define IS imported into M by the user
  -- module and DOES create a shadow there.  Not folding is what expresses "contributes
  -- nothing"; the union still carries the name via whichever user module defines it.
  let _ =
    if isPreludeMid mid then
      ()
    else
      gctx.crossRun.universeFunNamesRef :=
        namesToSet
          (map fst (funDefs prog))
          gctx.crossRun.universeFunNamesRef.value
  -- #154 PR-B: grow the dispatch-index accumulator by THIS module's interface indices.
  -- APPEND (universe first) so the accumulated list stays in the same core-first order the
  -- old `argDispatchIndices (accAll ++ prog)` flatMap produced.  #1351 L5 (CONTRACT) deleted
  -- the bare-name accumulator that used to be grown alongside this one: its only reader was
  -- `dispatchIdxScoped`'s fall-back arm, and the reader is now identity-keyed only, so a
  -- prior-module entry this module never names cannot be queried by spelling at all.
  gctx.crossRun.universeMethodDispatchIdxByIdRef :=
    gctx.crossRun.universeMethodDispatchIdxByIdRef.value
      ++ argDispatchIndicesById prog
  -- #1112 A-3.4 PR2: the #154 PR3 leg that grew the three `obUniv*` obligation-universe
  -- accumulators here is GONE.  Its consumer — the Module arm's `obUniv` — now projects
  -- stage K's `IE` at the reader's ordinal instead (`ieUniverseAt`), so this fold was
  -- building a second copy of a table nothing reads.  Note what that makes this function:
  -- it no longer answers "what impls exist" at all; every remaining line here is an
  -- interface/method/name-side accumulator.  Do not re-add an impl accumulator — the whole
  -- point of the flip is that `IE` is the one answer, and a second one is design law L1's
  -- divergence.
  ()

-- Takes this module's whole decl list, not a pre-filtered one.  The polarity
-- fixpoint runs over all of it (#2112), and filtering at the CALL SITE is what once let
-- the opaque-kind half go missing.
--
-- `fieldOwnersRef` arrives holding the K seed PLUS everything this module registered
-- during inference, and `registerAllDataScoped … pubDecls` below registers this module's
-- PUBLIC records a SECOND time.  `addFieldOwners` conses without dedupe, so every own
-- public record is DOUBLE-listed in `fieldOwnersRef` from that line until the next
-- `freshModuleCtx`.  Unobservable today only because nothing reads the multimap in between
-- (the two population walkers read `env2` and `recordByNameRef`).  A doubled owner key is
-- the shape `declEnvSeedChain`'s own-row note exists to prevent.  `fieldOwnerNames`
-- `sortUniqS`es on read, so the doubling does not move an answer; a new reader of
-- `fieldOwnersRef` after this point must de-duplicate first or restore a reset.
-- (`dataParamKindsRef` gets the same
-- doubling; it is inert there because `lookupTab` is first-match over identity-bearing
-- keys whose two copies are equal.)
appendDataUniverse : ModuleCtx -> String -> List Decl -> Unit
appendDataUniverse mctx mid prog0 =
  let pubDecls = publicDataDecls prog0
  -- The alias half of the reload is a stage-K projection, so it takes THIS module's
  -- ordinal, strictly BELOW-this-module (`aliasUniverseAt`'s `<`): the registration
  -- below is what puts this module's own aliases, public and private, in front.
  let _ =
    loadDataUniverse mctx (declEnvsOrdOf mid mctx.mcGraph.declEnvsRef.value)
  -- #2112: the polarity fixpoint sees the WHOLE module (`prog0`), the universe
  -- receives only the public keys — see `registerAllDataScoped`.
  let env2 =
    registerAllDataScoped
      (withCtors mctx (spFloor mctx.mcGraph.crossRun.universeCtorPop.value))
      (publicDataScopeDecls prog0)
      prog0
  -- Both walkers read the payloads this registration just made back out of `env2` and
  -- `recordByNameRef`, so each population row holds the very object its floor holds.
  mctx.mcGraph.crossRun.universeCtorPop :=
    insertCtorPop env2 pubDecls mctx.mcGraph.crossRun.universeCtorPop.value
  mctx.mcGraph.crossRun.universeRecordPop :=
    insertRecordPop mctx pubDecls mctx.mcGraph.crossRun.universeRecordPop.value
  mctx.mcCells.ownPopsRef :=
    (insertCtorPop env2 pubDecls spEmpty, insertRecordPop mctx pubDecls spEmpty)

-- What `appendDataUniverse` registers to elaborate a module's public data: the
-- public declarations plus every alias the module declares, private ones
-- included.  A public field may name a private alias, and the scheme it
-- elaborates to here is the one every importer reads back, so it expands under
-- the declaring module's aliases.  The private aliases reach only the working
-- alias table, which the next module's arm reloads; the populations take
-- `pubDecls` alone.
publicDataScopeDecls : List Decl -> List Decl
publicDataScopeDecls prog0 =
  filterList (d => publicDataDecl d || isAliasDecl d) prog0

-- #154 PR1: buildDefinerShadows with the `allIfaceMethodNames fullUniverse` scan
-- replaced by a membership test, `isMethod` (`methodNameDeclaredAt` at the module's
-- ordinal).  `direct` still filters THIS module's localNames in declaration order, so
-- `isMethod n` is a point-for-point substitute for `contains n methodNames` — same
-- set, same order, byte-identical output.
definerShadowsFromSet : GraphCtx -> (String -> Bool) -> List Decl -> List String
definerShadowsFromSet gctx isMethod prog =
  let localNames = dedup (map fst (funDefs prog))
  let direct = filter isMethod localNames
  let sm = gctx.mangledShadowMapRef.value
  let bares =
    flatMap
      (n => match lookupAssoc n sm
        Some bare => [bare]
        None => [])
      localNames
  removeAllS (localBoundNames prog) (dedup (direct ++ bares))

-- A name qualifies as an importer shadow when it is a universe fn, an interface
-- method, and NOT defined in this module; `not (contains n localNames)` drops this
-- module's own funDefs.  The `mangled` arm recovers the bare method name via
-- mangledShadowMapRef: on the EMIT path every funDef is mangled, so `direct` — which
-- intersects mangled universe-fn names against bare interface-method names — matches
-- nothing on its own, and without recovery the standalone/method dispatch decision
-- (Fork-1's importer rule) silently loses its site. Empty on the un-mangled run/check
-- path (the map is empty there) → `direct` alone → byte-identical. See
-- docs/spec/SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md § "2. Decision matrix (re-observed 2026-07-14,
-- post-`eb92cdff`; now GATED)" rows 21a/21b for the fixed bug and its fixtures.
standaloneShadowsFromSet : GraphCtx ->
  (String -> Bool) ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List Decl ->
  List String
standaloneShadowsFromSet gctx isMethod fnSet prog =
  -- Both probes below run once per GRAPH-WIDE fn name, so both of their tables are
  -- sets: a `contains` over the module's own names and a `lookupAssoc` over the
  -- definer-shadow map were each O(names x table) here.
  let localNames = namesToSet (map fst (funDefs prog)) omEmpty
  let direct =
    filter (n => isMethod n && not (omHasKey n localNames)) (omKeys fnSet)
  let sm = gctx.mangledShadowMapRef.value
  let mangled =
    flatMap
      (n => match lookupAssoc n sm
        Some bare => if omHasKey n localNames then [] else [bare]
        None => [])
      (omKeys fnSet)
  dedup (direct ++ mangled)

-- ── #1354 unit A (#1353): SHADOW-SEMANTICS S1's `nameable in M` interface operand ──
-- `docs/spec/SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md` S1 (SCOPE RULED 2026-08-06, #1375) intersects
-- funDef-names(standalones defined in or imported into `M`) with
-- iface-method-names(interfaces **nameable in `M`**).  `methodNameDeclaredAt` answers
-- for the method names of EVERY module at or before `M`'s ordinal, so the two builders
-- above implement the LEFT operand's scope (the `fnSet`/`localNames` guards) and give the
-- RIGHT one none: an interface reachable only transitively, through a module that
-- re-exports nothing, captured a standalone the occurrence's module had explicitly
-- imported (#1353, S0 — `7` instead of `99`, at exit 0, no diagnostic).
--
-- The remedy is a SUPPLY, not a re-scope: the membership test is correct and narrowing
-- it would answer a question nobody asks of it.  This is the missing predicate, applied to
-- the ALREADY-COMPUTED intersection rather than inside either operand's filter — the
-- intersection is single-digit in practice (over `compiler/**` + `stdlib/*` it is 3:
-- `toList`, `isEmpty`, `orElse`) while `fnSet` holds every top-level fn name in the graph,
-- so filtering the result is cheap and filtering the operand is not.
--
-- ⚠️ THE PREDICATE ASKS A TYPE-NAMESPACE QUESTION, and getting that wrong is how the first
-- cut of this fix shipped two defects at once — see `meIfaceExports` for both, measured.
-- §1.0's row says `nameable in M` qualifies **S1's INTERFACE operand**; asking instead
-- whether the METHOD NAME is exported along the import path is a different question that
-- answers differently in BOTH directions.
--
-- 🚨 IT FAILS OPEN, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT DIRECTION IS LOAD-BEARING.  Dropping shadow-hood
-- from an occurrence that IS one makes it dispatch unconditionally (`recordRLocalSite`'s
-- `standaloneValuesRef` guard declines, so no pending site exists for
-- `resolveRLocalSites` to stamp and the route stays the method's RKey) — the S4/#410
-- class, up to `no impl of method … for type …` on a valid program and a SIGSEGV variant.
-- Adding shadow-hood is the pre-existing behaviour.  So an ABSENT index answers True for
-- every name rather than False: `meIfaceExports` rides `declEnvsRef`, written
-- unconditionally at the one Module-mode driver entry, `graphPreamble`
-- (`checkModulesPreambleK` is its projection — the conjunction stated in full on
-- `meExports`, which shares that write), and a driver
-- that ever omits that write must degrade to today's graph-global answer, not to "nothing
-- is a shadow anywhere".
--
-- ⚠️ SCOPE, stated so it is not over-read.  The predicate is `nameable in M` as §1.0 defines
-- it, applied to S1's INTERFACE operand — so it covers BOTH failures S1 names, the
-- reachability one (#1353: no import path reaches the declaring module) and the one where a
-- path exists but does not carry the interface.  What it does NOT decide is #1302's axis:
-- `meIfaceExports` has no `pub` filter, so a module that imports a dependency BY NAME can
-- still be told about that dependency's PRIVATE interface.  That is the fail-open direction
-- and it is left exactly where #1302 and `declMethodIdentsOf`'s F3 already own it.
nameableIfaceShadows : GraphCtx -> List Decl -> List String -> List String
nameableIfaceShadows gctx _ [] = []
nameableIfaceShadows gctx prog names
  -- fail OPEN on an absent index — see the paragraph above; `names` unchanged is exactly
  -- the pre-#1353 graph-global answer.
  | omSize (ifaceExportsIndex gctx ()) == 0 = names
  | otherwise =
    let nameable = nameableIfaceMethodSet gctx prog
    filterList (n => omHasKey n nameable) names

-- The bare method names of every interface NAMEABLE in module [prog] — S1's three
-- nameable-in-`M` positions, built ONCE per module: the implicit prelude (`core`'s row),
-- this module's own interfaces, and, for each `DUse`, the interfaces THAT USE-PATH ADMITS
-- out of the dependency's row (which already carries what the dependency re-exports, at any
-- chain depth — S1-CHAIN, #1380).
--
-- 🚨 THE USE-PATH FILTER IS THE WHOLE POINT, and its absence was this fix's first defect.
-- Taking a dependency's WHOLE row on any import makes `import smod.{sf}` — one unrelated
-- function — enough to make `smod`'s interface "nameable", which it demonstrably is not:
-- `impl Sizeable Blob` in that module is rejected `Unknown interface: Sizeable`.  That left
-- #1353 narrowed rather than fixed (its own repro with the bridge hop removed still printed
-- the impl's value).  `selectIfaceRows` is shared with the re-export side so the import and
-- chain answers cannot drift apart.
--
-- Name-level rather than identity-level ON PURPOSE.  S1's intersection is over NAMES, so
-- when two interfaces declare `n` and only one is nameable here, `n` is a shadow either
-- way; which declaration an occurrence then means is `methodScopeAt`'s question
-- about a different table (`MethodEnv`'s rows), and answering it here would be
-- a second resolver free to disagree with that one.
--
-- 🔒 THIS IS S1's RIGHT OPERAND UNDER S1-NS (RULED 2026-08-08), and it is the ONLY predicate
-- in the compiler that answers it — `checkBodyImpl`'s shadow-hood and EVERY filter in the
-- mark pass read THIS set.  Named rather than counted, because a count rots silently and
-- this sentence already did (it said "all three" for a week after `rpNames` became the
-- fourth): `moduleMarkCtx` filters `rpNames`, `shadowNames` (through
-- `shadowBareName`), `argNames` and `shadowMap` — its own `otherwise` arm enumerates them
-- against what `rewriteArgScoped` can turn into an `EMethodAt`.  S1-NS (b) requires
-- shadow-hood to be a superset of dispatch
-- eligibility and rules two different predicates at the two sites non-conformant; one set
-- makes them equal, so the invariant holds by construction rather than by test.  Do not
-- introduce a second, wider set for marking: two earlier cuts of this unit did exactly that
-- and each shipped an S0 (a `run`-vs-built-binary split, and a `build`-only E-PANIC).
--
-- The per-METHOD union of the two namespaces lives in `selectIfaceRows`, applied on the
-- import arm here and on the re-export arm in `meIfaceExports`.
nameableIfaceMethodSet : GraphCtx -> List Decl -> OrdMap Unit
nameableIfaceMethodSet gctx prog =
  namesToSet (flatMap snd (nameableIfaceRows gctx prog)) omEmpty

-- The same operand ONE level less flattened: the (interface name, its method names)
-- ROWS, not just the union of their method names.  `nameableIfaceMethodSet` above is
-- defined as this list's flattening, so there is still exactly ONE derivation of S1's
-- right operand — a diagnostic that needs to name WHICH interface owns a colliding
-- method (#2738's `W-IMPORT-METHOD-SHADOW`) must not answer that from a second,
-- independently-scoped walk, which is what S1-NS (b) rules non-conformant.
--
-- `ifaceMethodRows prog` is `allIfaceMethodNames prog` grouped by declaration: both walk
-- `DAttrib`/`DInterface` in the same order and take `ifaceMethodNames methods`, so the
-- flattening above is the previous expression term for term.
nameableIfaceRows : GraphCtx -> List Decl -> List (String, List String)
nameableIfaceRows gctx prog =
  nameableIfaceRowsIn (ifaceExportsIndex gctx ()) prog

-- `nameableIfaceRows` over the interface-row index [idx].
nameableIfaceRowsIn : OrdMap (List (String, List String)) ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List String)
nameableIfaceRowsIn idx prog =
  optionOr [] (omLookup "core" idx)
    ++ ifaceMethodRows prog
    ++ importedIfaceRows idx prog

importedIfaceRows : OrdMap (List (String, List String)) ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List String)
importedIfaceRows _ [] = []
importedIfaceRows idx ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) =
  importedIfaceRows idx [d] ++ importedIfaceRows idx rest
importedIfaceRows idx ((DUse _ path _) :: rest) =
