  (match omLookup (useModId path) idx
      None => []
      Some src => selectIfaceRows path src)
    ++ importedIfaceRows idx rest
importedIfaceRows idx (_ :: rest) = importedIfaceRows idx rest

-- ── #2738: a selectively imported standalone displaced by a nameable method ──
-- The peer of `frontend/marker.mdk`'s `preludeStandaloneShadows` for the IMPORTER
-- direction, and it is sited here rather than beside it because the two operands it
-- needs live here: S1's right operand (`nameableIfaceRows`, the only predicate in the
-- compiler that answers `nameable in M`) and, through it, the interface a colliding
-- method name belongs to.  `compiler/frontend/marker.mdk` cannot reach either —
-- `types/typecheck.mdk` imports `frontend.marker`, so the edge does not run the other
-- way — and re-deriving the operand there is what S1-NS (b) rules non-conformant.
--
-- Yields one entry per DIFFERING-scheme collision, in declaration order:
--   (bound name, the interface declaring it, the standalone's declared signature,
--    the method's declared signature, the import member's own span).
-- The standalone signature is `None` when the defining module declares the function
-- without a signature: a scheme that cannot be read cannot be shown harmless, so it
-- counts as differing.  Identical (alpha-equivalent) signatures yield nothing, which is
-- what keeps the everyday `import m.{f}` silent.
--
-- SELECTIVE imports only (`UseGroup`).  A wildcard or bare import makes no statement
-- about the name, and a module alias binds a DOTTED local (`A.f`) that no bare method
-- name can collide with; the ruling is scoped to the explicit member list, which is the
-- strongest statement the language offers about which binding is meant.
--
-- Fails CLOSED on an absent index, the opposite of `nameableIfaceShadows` above and for
-- the opposite reason: that predicate decides resolution, where dropping shadow-hood
-- miscompiles, while this one only decides a warning, where a graph-global operand would
-- fire on collisions the module cannot name.
export
importedStandaloneShadows : DriveOutputs ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, String, Option Ty, Ty, Loc)
importedStandaloneShadows o graph prog =
  importedStandaloneShadowsIn o.doIfaceExports graph prog

-- `importedStandaloneShadows` over the interface-row index [idx], for a caller whose
-- index is not the last drive's: a single file analysed before its drive passes
-- `omEmpty`, which answers nothing.
export
importedStandaloneShadowsIn : OrdMap (List (String, List String)) ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, String, Option Ty, Ty, Loc)
importedStandaloneShadowsIn idx graph prog
  | omSize idx == 0 = []
  | otherwise =
    let rows = nameableIfaceRowsIn idx prog
    let nameable = namesToSet (flatMap snd rows) omEmpty
    let universe = flatMap snd graph ++ prog
    flatMap (importShadowsOfDecl graph rows nameable universe) prog

-- The catch-all arms here are exhaustive by construction, not by omission: a shadow can
-- only arise from an explicit member list, so every non-`DUse` declaration and every
-- non-`UseGroup` use path contributes nothing by the scoping rule stated above.
importShadowsOfDecl : List (String, List Decl) ->
  List (String, List String) ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List Decl ->
  Decl ->
  List (String, String, Option Ty, Ty, Loc)
importShadowsOfDecl graph rows nameable universe (DAttrib _ d) =
  importShadowsOfDecl graph rows nameable universe d
importShadowsOfDecl graph rows nameable universe (DUse _ path _) = match path
  UseGroup _ ms => match lookupAssoc (useModId path) graph
    None => []
    Some depDecls =>
      flatMap (importMemberShadow graph rows nameable universe depDecls) ms
  _ => []
importShadowsOfDecl _ _ _ _ _ = []

importMemberShadow : List (String, List Decl) ->
  List (String, List String) ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  UseMember ->
  List (String, String, Option Ty, Ty, Loc)
importMemberShadow graph rows nameable universe depDecls (UseMember origin _ mloc alias) =
  let local = match alias
    Some a => a
    None => origin
  if not (omHasKey local nameable) then
    []
  else match reachableStandaloneSig graph (listLen graph) depDecls origin
    None => []
    Some sty => match ifaceMethodSigFor local sty rows universe
      None => []
      Some (iface, mty) => [(local, iface, sty, mty, mloc)]

schemesAgree : Option Ty -> Ty -> Bool
schemesAgree None _ = False
schemesAgree (Some sty) mty = tyAlphaEq sty mty

-- A NAMEABLE interface declaring [name] whose signature differs from the standalone's
-- [sty], with that signature.  When two or more differ, the least by interface name and
-- then by rendered signature, so the warning reads the same in every import order
-- (S2-DECL (e)).  Rows whose declaration is not in [universe] are skipped rather than
-- guessed at.
ifaceMethodSigFor : String ->
  Option Ty ->
  List (String, List String) ->
  List Decl ->
  Option (String, Ty)
ifaceMethodSigFor _ _ [] _ = None
ifaceMethodSigFor name sty ((iface, ms) :: rest) universe =
  let later = ifaceMethodSigFor name sty rest universe
  if not (contains name ms) then
    later
  else match ifaceMethodTyIn iface name universe
    Some ty =>
      if schemesAgree sty ty then later else leastIfaceSig (iface, ty) later
    None => later

leastIfaceSig : (String, Ty) -> Option (String, Ty) -> Option (String, Ty)
leastIfaceSig a None = Some a
leastIfaceSig (a@(ia, ta)) (Some (b@(ib, tb)))
  | ia < ib = Some a
  | ib < ia = Some b
  | ppTy ta <= ppTy tb = Some a
  | otherwise = Some b

ifaceMethodTyIn : String -> String -> List Decl -> Option Ty
ifaceMethodTyIn _ _ [] = None
ifaceMethodTyIn iface name ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) =
  let inner = ifaceMethodTyIn iface name [d]
  match inner
    Some ty => Some ty
    None => ifaceMethodTyIn iface name rest
ifaceMethodTyIn iface name ((DInterface { name = n, methods, ... }) :: rest)
  | n == iface = match ifaceMethodTyOf name methods
    Some ty => Some ty
    None => ifaceMethodTyIn iface name rest
  | otherwise = ifaceMethodTyIn iface name rest
ifaceMethodTyIn iface name (_ :: rest) = ifaceMethodTyIn iface name rest

ifaceMethodTyOf : String -> List IfaceMethod -> Option Ty
ifaceMethodTyOf _ [] = None
ifaceMethodTyOf name ((IfaceMethod n ty _ _) :: rest)
  | n == name = Some ty
  | otherwise = ifaceMethodTyOf name rest

-- The standalone the imported member actually names, THROUGH `export import` hops:
-- `Some sig` when a module reachable from [decls] declares [name] as a top-level
-- function (`sig` being its declared signature, or `None` when it has none — a scheme
-- that cannot be read cannot be shown harmless, which is what `schemesAgree` then does
-- with it), and `None` when no such standalone exists at all.
--
-- The hop is not optional; it is what the spec asks for.  Reading only the DIRECTLY
-- imported module's own `DFunDef`s made the detector silent for a standalone that
-- reaches the importer through a re-exporter, which is the same silent displacement
-- #2738 names — `SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md`'s `nameable in M` row puts re-export chains in
-- scope (#1380) and S1-NS (a) rules the re-export arm SYMMETRIC with the import arm, so
-- a detector that answers only the direct case contradicts its own right operand, which
-- `meIfaceExports` already folds over chains of any depth.
--
-- The member list is followed the same way the re-export side follows it — through
-- `importedBindings`, the one place a use-path's (origin, local) bindings are derived —
-- so `export import m.{f as g}` re-exported as `g` looks `f` up in `m`, and a wildcard
-- re-export passes the name through unchanged.  A second walker keyed on a
-- hand-enumerated set of `UsePath` forms would drift from that one the first time a form
-- is added.
--
-- [fuel] bounds the chain at the number of modules in the compile, so a re-export cycle
-- terminates here rather than relying on the loader having rejected it upstream.
reachableStandaloneSig : List (String, List Decl) ->
  Int ->
  List Decl ->
  String ->
  Option (Option Ty)
reachableStandaloneSig graph fuel decls name
  | declaresStandalone name decls = Some (standaloneSigOf name decls)
  | fuel <= 0 = None
  | otherwise =
    reachableStandaloneSigGo graph (fuel - 1) (reexportedOrigins decls name)

reachableStandaloneSigGo : List (String, List Decl) ->
  Int ->
  List (String, String) ->
  Option (Option Ty)
reachableStandaloneSigGo _ _ [] = None
reachableStandaloneSigGo graph fuel ((mid, n) :: rest) =
  match lookupAssoc mid graph
    None => reachableStandaloneSigGo graph fuel rest
    Some ds => match reachableStandaloneSig graph fuel ds n
      Some sig => Some sig
      None => reachableStandaloneSigGo graph fuel rest

-- Every (dependency module id, name in THAT module) an `export import` in [decls] could
-- have re-exported [name] from.  A non-exporting `import` contributes nothing: it puts
-- no name into the re-exporter's own exports, so nothing downstream can reach through
-- it.
--
-- The catch-all arm is exhaustive by that rule rather than by omission — a re-export is
-- representable only as a `DUse True`, wrapped in `DAttrib` or not, so no other `Decl`
-- constructor can contribute a hop and a new one never will.  Its ledgered peer
-- `reexportedIfaceMethodsOf` (the interface-row half of the same walk) carries the same
-- two arms for the same reason.
reexportedOrigins : List Decl -> String -> List (String, String)
reexportedOrigins decls name = flatMap (d => reexportedOriginsOf d name) decls

reexportedOriginsOf : Decl -> String -> List (String, String)
reexportedOriginsOf (DAttrib _ d) name = reexportedOriginsOf d name
reexportedOriginsOf (DUse True path _) name = match importedBindings path
  None => [(useModId path, name)]
  Some bs =>
    map (b => (useModId path, fst b)) (filterList (b => snd b == name) bs)
reexportedOriginsOf _ _ = []

declaresStandalone : String -> List Decl -> Bool
declaresStandalone _ [] = False
declaresStandalone n ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) =
  declaresStandalone n [d] || declaresStandalone n rest
declaresStandalone n ((DFunDef _ m _ _ _ _) :: rest) =
  m == n || declaresStandalone n rest
declaresStandalone n (_ :: rest) = declaresStandalone n rest

standaloneSigOf : String -> List Decl -> Option Ty
standaloneSigOf _ [] = None
standaloneSigOf n ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) = match standaloneSigOf n [d]
  Some t => Some t
  None => standaloneSigOf n rest
standaloneSigOf n ((DTypeSig _ m ty _) :: rest)
  | m == n = Some ty
  | otherwise = standaloneSigOf n rest
standaloneSigOf n (_ :: rest) = standaloneSigOf n rest

-- Alpha-equivalence of two SURFACE signatures: equal up to a consistent renaming of
-- type variables, so `Box a -> a` and `Box b -> b` agree while `Box a -> (String, a)`
-- and `t a -> a` do not.  The bijection is carried both ways, so `a -> b` and `a -> a`
-- do not agree either.  Any shape not matched pairwise below is treated as DIFFERING,
-- which is the direction that warns, and every arm that IS matched pairwise compares
-- every field that can carry a type variable — a field skipped there errs toward
-- AGREEING, the silent direction, which is what a `listLen`-only `TyConstrained` arm did
-- (`Eq a => b -> a -> String` and `Debug a => t -> a -> String` compared equal, and the
-- displacement they name went unreported at exit 0).  The two fields deliberately not
-- compared are `TyCon`'s `tyConOrigin` and `TyRow`'s `Option Loc`: neither is part of the
-- written scheme, and `Constraint`'s `constraintOrigin` is skipped for the same reason.
export
tyAlphaEq : Ty -> Ty -> Bool
tyAlphaEq a b = match tyAlphaGo [] a b
  Some _ => True
  None => False

tyAlphaGo : List (String, String) -> Ty -> Ty -> Option (List (String, String))
tyAlphaGo m (TyVar x) (TyVar y) = bindTyName m x y
tyAlphaGo m (TyCon { tyConName = x }) (TyCon { tyConName = y })
  | x == y = Some m
  | otherwise = None
tyAlphaGo m (TyApp f x) (TyApp g y) = match tyAlphaGo m f g
  None => None
  Some m2 => tyAlphaGo m2 x y
tyAlphaGo m (TyFun a b) (TyFun c d) = match tyAlphaGo m a c
  None => None
  Some m2 => tyAlphaGo m2 b d
tyAlphaGo m (TyTuple xs) (TyTuple ys) = tyAlphaList m xs ys
tyAlphaGo m (TyEffect e1 t1 a) (TyEffect e2 t2 b)
  | sameWrittenAtoms e1 e2 && t1 == t2 = tyAlphaGo m a b
  | otherwise = None
-- BODY FIRST, then the constraints, and the order is load-bearing rather than
-- stylistic: the body is where a scheme's type variables are pinned, so matching it
-- first fixes the bijection the constraint comparison then only has to check.  The
-- reverse order has to GUESS which of two same-head constraints (`Eq a, Eq b => a -> b`
-- vs `Eq d, Eq c => c -> d`) pairs with which, and a wrong greedy guess reports a
-- false difference on two schemes that are the same.
tyAlphaGo m (TyConstrained c1 a) (TyConstrained c2 b)
  | listLen c1 /= listLen c2 = None
  | otherwise = match tyAlphaGo m a b
    None => None
    Some m2 => tyAlphaConstraints m2 c1 c2
tyAlphaGo m (TyRow e1 t1 _) (TyRow e2 t2 _)
  | sameWrittenAtoms e1 e2 && t1 == t2 = Some m
  | otherwise = None
tyAlphaGo _ _ _ = None

-- Two written rows agree when their atoms spell the same; the declaration
-- identity is not part of alpha-equivalence, which compares source shapes.
sameWrittenAtoms : List EffAtomTy -> List EffAtomTy -> Bool
sameWrittenAtoms e1 e2 =
  map (effAtomSurface escStr) e1 == map (effAtomSurface escStr) e2

tyAlphaList : List (String, String) ->
  List Ty ->
  List Ty ->
  Option (List (String, String))
tyAlphaList m [] [] = Some m
tyAlphaList m (x :: xs) (y :: ys) = match tyAlphaGo m x y
  None => None
  Some m2 => tyAlphaList m2 xs ys
tyAlphaList _ _ _ = None

-- A constraint SET, not a constraint list: `Eq a, Debug b =>` and `Debug b, Eq a =>`
-- are the same scheme, so a positional comparison would warn on two declarations that
-- differ only in the order the author wrote them — a false positive on correct code.
-- Each constraint of [c1] is therefore matched against any still-unconsumed member of
-- [c2].  The lists are equal-length at entry (the caller's guard), so consuming one per
-- step leaves nothing over.
tyAlphaConstraints : List (String, String) ->
  List Constraint ->
  List Constraint ->
  Option (List (String, String))
tyAlphaConstraints m [] _ = Some m
tyAlphaConstraints m (c :: rest) cs2 = match takeAlphaConstraint m c cs2 []
  None => None
  Some (m2, left) => tyAlphaConstraints m2 rest left

-- the first member of [cs] that matches [c], paired with the REMAINING members.  Their
-- order in that remainder is immaterial — this is a set comparison — so the rejected
-- prefix is simply appended back.
takeAlphaConstraint : List (String, String) ->
  Constraint ->
  List Constraint ->
  List Constraint ->
  Option (List (String, String), List Constraint)
takeAlphaConstraint _ _ [] _ = None
takeAlphaConstraint m c (d :: rest) tried = match tyAlphaConstraint m c d
  Some m2 => Some (m2, tried ++ rest)
  None => takeAlphaConstraint m c rest (d :: tried)

-- Same interface, and pairwise alpha-equal arguments under the map the body already
-- pinned.  `constraintOrigin` is identity metadata the surface signature does not carry
-- — the peer of `tyConOrigin`, skipped by the `TyCon` arm for the same reason.
tyAlphaConstraint : List (String, String) ->
  Constraint ->
  Constraint ->
  Option (List (String, String))
tyAlphaConstraint m (Constraint { constraintHead = h1, constraintArgs = as1, ... }) (Constraint { constraintHead = h2, constraintArgs = as2, ... })
  | h1 == h2 = tyAlphaList m as1 as2
  | otherwise = None

bindTyName : List (String, String) ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Option (List (String, String))
bindTyName m x y = match lookupAssoc x m
  Some y2 => if y2 == y then Some m else None
  None => if anyList (e => snd e == y) m then None else Some ((x, y) :: m)

-- C5: graph-wide standalone-shadow names — every top-level funDef name in [userDecls]
-- (the user modules, NOT core) that is also an interface method name anywhere in
-- [allDecls].  Used by the MARK pass to rewrite such occurrences to EMethodAt (so the
-- route ref exists for resolveRLocalSites to stamp).  Excludes core's own decls as the
-- funDef source so core's elaboration (no standalone shadows there) is untouched.
-- P0-18: recover, per (module, iface-method) pair, the mangled standalone symbol the
-- mangler produced for a definer-shadow funDef.  Forward-constructs `mangledName mid
-- method` (using the KNOWN mid — exact, not lossy prefix-stripping) and checks it
-- against the module's actual funDef names; a hit is a `(mangledSymbol ↦ bareMethod)`
-- entry.  On the un-mangled path no funDef matches → [] → every consumer unchanged.
computeMangledShadowMap : List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  List (String, String)
computeMangledShadowMap allDecls units =
  -- DEDUPED: `allIfaceMethodNames` walks every `DInterface` in the graph and a method
  -- name declared by two interfaces appears twice, so an undeduped list mints the SAME
  -- `(sym ↦ bare)` row twice per unit.  The rows are identical, so no reader's answer
  -- changes; what changes is the size of the table every reader below walks or indexes.
  let methodNames = dedup (allIfaceMethodNames allDecls)
  flatMap (unitMangledShadows methodNames) units

-- The unit's funDef names are an INDEX, not a list: this probes once per interface
-- method, so a `contains` here is O(methods x funDefs) — a shape where both grow
-- together (N interfaces beside N top-level bindings) makes it quadratic.  Same
-- treatment as `prePassDictArg`'s name sets (#2189).
-- #2809: THE BARE ROW.  Mangling now runs AFTER elaboration, so a definer shadow's
-- funDef carries the name its author wrote and the forward-constructed `<mid>__m` matches
-- nothing.  The row is what `rewriteArgScoped`'s `sm` arm reads to seed the occurrence
-- with its standalone SYMBOL, and that symbol is what the later rename moves
-- (`private_mangle`'s `EMethodAt` seed arm and `mangleRoute`) into the emitted direct
-- call.  Without it the route names the bare METHOD, whose define the rename has already
-- moved, and the emitter calls a symbol DCE pruned: `use of undefined value
-- '@mdk_orElse'`, on the compiler's own `frontend.parser`.
-- On the bare row `sym == bare`, so `moduleSpellsShadowBare`'s definer arm admits it in
-- the module that defines the standalone and its import arm in a module that spells the
-- bare name -- the same two admitting cases #1684 ruled for the mangled row.
-- THE PRELUDE UNIT CONTRIBUTES NO ROW: SHADOW-SEMANTICS S1-PRELUDE (a) puts the implicit
-- prelude in neither half of S1's standalone operand, so no `core.mdk` occurrence is a
-- user interface method's shadow -- the asymmetry `appendUniverseAccums` states, and the
-- direction #2153's `core__not ↦ not` incident was paid for.
unitMangledShadows : List String -> (String, List Decl) -> List (String, String)
unitMangledShadows methodNames (mid, decls) =
  let fns = omFromNames (map fst (funDefs decls)) omEmpty
  flatMap
    (m =>
      let sym = mangledName mid m
      if omHasKey sym fns then
        [(sym, m)]
      else if not (isPreludeMid mid) && omHasKey m fns then
        [(m, m)]
      else
        [])
    methodNames

-- L3 (xmod-identity #1351 spine, RUN-XMOD-022/026): the graph-level fact "this
-- compile's decls carry at least one top-level funDef with its own module's
-- mangle prefix" — the DENOTATION the new GraphCtx flag below actually
-- records (F12).  NOT literally "a mangler ran": a hand-written `m__foo` in
-- module `m` on the un-mangled (check/run) path also satisfies it, harmlessly
-- (see that flag's callers).  Reuses `isMangledFor` (F6) rather than a second
-- prefix test, and `funDefs` rather than a second decl walk.
-- Monomorphic, explicit-recursion, short-circuits on the first hit — do NOT
-- delegate to prelude `any`/`elem` here (AGENTS.md: costed +56% self-compile
-- on this file's hot helpers).
--
-- 🚨 RUN-XMOD-045 CORRECTION (post-landing, slice-breaker finding): on EVERY
-- emit path this flag is CONSTANT TRUE, not merely "true when some module
-- shadows an interface method."  `private_mangle.mdk:14-16` states the
-- mangler's actual scope: "EVERY top-level FUNCTION binding (in core + every
-- module) is renamed to a module-qualified unique symbol," unconditionally,
-- BEFORE `elaborateModules` (and therefore this function) ever runs.  So
-- `core`'s own funDefs already carry the `core__` prefix by the time this
-- walks them, and the very first unit checked (`("core", coreDecls)`, see
-- both call sites below) already satisfies `unitCarriesMangledFunDefs` —
-- MEASURED: a feature-free `main = println 1` build emits ~70 distinct
-- `@mdk_core__*`/`@mdk_<mid>__*` symbols in its own IR with zero user
-- modules, zero shadows, zero interfaces.  The ORIGINAL packet's inertness
-- argument (F8: "a non-empty route symbol implies this flag is True") is
-- still literally correct but was read as "this flag is sometimes False,"
-- which is false — it is NEVER False on the emit path, so F8's implication
-- is vacuously satisfied rather than doing narrowing work.  The precondition
-- F8's phrasing hid: BOTH writers (this flag AND the route-symbol conjunct
-- in `importerShadowOnEmitPath`) are stamped by the SAME compile, and on
-- that compile this flag is always True the moment mangling has run at all —
-- see `importerShadowOnEmitPath`'s own header for the consequence.
--
-- 🚨 THIS FACT CURRENTLY HAS NO DISCRIMINATING CONSUMER — L4's conjunct is
-- constant-True on emit and its partner (`occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym`)
-- is always-empty off emit.  It is explicit documentation of an implicit
-- invariant, not a live condition.  Do not migrate a reader onto it
-- expecting it to select.  KEPT (not reverted) by owner ruling because it is
-- provably zero-risk and reads better than the anonymous test it replaced —
-- see `importerShadowOnEmitPath`.
graphCarriesMangledFunDefs : List (String, List Decl) -> Bool
graphCarriesMangledFunDefs [] = False
graphCarriesMangledFunDefs ((mid, decls) :: rest) =
  if unitCarriesMangledFunDefs mid (funDefs decls) then
    True
  else
    graphCarriesMangledFunDefs rest

unitCarriesMangledFunDefs : String -> List (String, (List Pat, Expr)) -> Bool
unitCarriesMangledFunDefs mid [] = False
unitCarriesMangledFunDefs mid ((n, _) :: rest) =
  if isMangledFor mid n then True else unitCarriesMangledFunDefs mid rest

buildStandaloneShadowsGraph : List (String, String) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List String
buildStandaloneShadowsGraph sm allDecls userDecls =
  -- INDEX, not a list: this probes once per user funDef, so a `contains` over the
  -- interface-method names is O(funDefs x methods) — quadratic on a program whose
  -- interface count and top-level binding count grow together.
  let methodNames = omFromNames (allIfaceMethodNames allDecls) omEmpty
  let fns = dedup (map fst (funDefs userDecls))
  let direct = filter (n => omHasKey n methodNames) fns
  -- P0-18: written for the order where the EMIT path's funDef names were MANGLED
  -- (`<mid>__toList`), which the `direct` name-intersection misses; the map recovered
  -- them so the prePass marked their occurrences `EMethodAt`.
  -- #2809: no path reaches this with mangled funDefs any more, and the map is non-empty
  -- on ALL of them — the rows are `(name ↦ name)`, so this filter selects the funDef
  -- names `direct` already selected and the union is unchanged.  The header 25 lines up
  -- states that retirement; this line used to contradict it by claiming the map is empty
  -- off the emit path.  Kept rather than deleted because it is what would recover a
  -- genuinely mangled row if one appeared (a hand-written `<mid>__toList` mints one), and
  -- because `dedup` makes the redundancy free.
  let mangled = filter (n => isSome (lookupAssoc n sm)) fns
  dedup (direct ++ mangled)

-- WS-1a fix: every impl in scope, EXPORT OR NOT.  Instances are GLOBAL (coherence
-- + dispatch leak across module boundaries regardless of `export`), so the
-- superinterface existence query (checkSuperImpls/superImplExists) must see an
-- imported module's `impl Semigroup T` even when it isn't `export`-marked — else
-- `impl Monoid T` in an importer is falsely rejected for a "missing" super impl.
pickSchemes : List String -> OrdMap Scheme -> List (String, Scheme)
pickSchemes [] _ = []
pickSchemes (n :: ns) table = match omLookup n table
  Some s => (n, s) :: pickSchemes ns table
  None => pickSchemes ns table

-- Candidate spellings come from the same three binding sources the environment sees:
-- nameable bare methods (including the implicit core row), selective-import local
-- names, and module-alias-qualified names.  `lookupBinding` below remains the final
-- no-new-name gate, while this bounded list avoids walking every ordinary seed binding.
importedMethodBindingNames : GraphCtx ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, String) ->
  List String
importedMethodBindingNames gctx prog aliases =
  flatMap snd (nameableIfaceRows gctx prog)
    ++ importedMemberBindingNames prog
    ++ map fst aliases

plainModuleSeed : List (String, Scheme) -> ModuleSeed
plainModuleSeed schemes = ModuleSeed {
  msSchemes = schemes,
  msImportedValues = omEmpty,
  msImportedNames = omEmpty,
  msImportedExterns = omEmpty,
}

-- The ordinary winner and standalone alternative travel together through
-- import selection, aliases, re-exports, and graph memoization.
tagModuleExports : OrdMap Scheme ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List (String, ExportBinding)
tagModuleExports standalones schemes =
  map
    ((name, scheme) => (
      name,
      ExportBinding {
        xbScheme = scheme,
        xbStandalone = omLookup name standalones,
        xbExtern = False,
      },
    ))
    schemes

publicModuleExports : List Decl ->
  ModuleBindings ->
  List (String, ExportBinding)
publicModuleExports prog bindings =
  let standalones =
    omFromPairs
      (flatMap
        (name => match omLookup name bindings.mbStandaloneSchemes
          Some scheme => [(name, scheme)]
          None => [])
        (pubTopFnNames prog))
      omEmpty
  let externs =
    omFromNames (map fst (directExternSigs (externDecls prog))) omEmpty
  map
    ((name, binding) => (
      name,
      ExportBinding { binding | xbExtern = omHasKey name externs },
    ))
    (tagModuleExports
      standalones
      (pickSchemes
        (publicValNames prog)
        (omFromPairs (reverseL bindings.mbSchemes) omEmpty)))

-- The first row for a name wins, unless a second import supplies a different
-- declaration of the same name: then the occurrence is the ambiguity the
-- resolver reports as R-AMBIGUOUS-OCCURRENCE (`ambiguousSet`, keyed by
-- declaration through `importValueDecls`, whichever module each import names;
-- a local definition, which it exempts, shadows the seed here anyway).
-- Choosing either supplier would type the use against a definition the program
-- never named, and the cascade would change with the order the imports were
-- written.
importedBindingWinners : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, (Option String, ExportBinding)) ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, ExportBinding)
importedBindingWinners mctx [] _ _ = []
importedBindingWinners mctx ((name, (_, binding)) :: rest) seen ambiguous =
  if omHasKey name seen then
    importedBindingWinners mctx rest seen ambiguous
  else
    let chosen =
      if omHasKey name ambiguous then
        ambiguousImportBinding mctx ()
      else
        binding
    (name, chosen)
      :: importedBindingWinners mctx rest (omInsert name () seen) ambiguous

ambiguousImports : List (String, (Option String, a)) -> OrdMap Unit
ambiguousImports rows = ambiguousImportsGo rows omEmpty omEmpty

ambiguousImportsGo : List (String, (Option String, a)) ->
  OrdMap String ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit
ambiguousImportsGo [] _ acc = acc
ambiguousImportsGo ((_, (None, _)) :: rest) firstMid acc =
  ambiguousImportsGo rest firstMid acc
ambiguousImportsGo ((name, (Some mid, _)) :: rest) firstMid acc =
  match omLookup name firstMid
    None => ambiguousImportsGo rest (omInsert name mid firstMid) acc
    Some seen => ambiguousImportsGo rest firstMid (if seen == mid then
      acc
    else
      omInsert name () acc)

-- An ambiguous name types as a fresh, poisoned variable at every occurrence
-- (`freshSubst` recognises the reserved quantifier), so the resolver's
-- rejection stays the only diagnostic on the drivers that keep typechecking
-- after a resolve error (`check --json`, the LSP).
ambiguousImportBinding : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> ExportBinding
ambiguousImportBinding mctx _ =
  let cell =
    Ref (Unbound ambiguousImportTyvarId mctx.mcCells.currentLevel.value)
  ExportBinding {
    xbScheme = Forall [ambiguousImportTyvarId] [] [] [] pureRow (TVar cell),
    xbStandalone = None,
    xbExtern = False,
  }

moduleImportSeed : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List (String, (Option String, ExportBinding)) ->
  ModuleSeed
moduleImportSeed mctx base imported =
  let selected =
    importedBindingWinners mctx imported omEmpty (ambiguousImports imported)
  ModuleSeed {
    msSchemes =
      base ++ map ((name, binding) => (name, binding.xbScheme)) selected,
    msImportedValues =
      omFromPairs
        (flatMap
          ((name, binding) => match binding.xbStandalone
            Some scheme => [(name, scheme)]
            None => [])
          selected)
        omEmpty,
    msImportedNames = omFromNames (map fst selected) omEmpty,
    msImportedExterns =
      omFromNames
        (flatMap
          ((name, binding) => if binding.xbExtern then [name] else [])
          selected)
        omEmpty,
  }

-- `import m as A` binds EVERY value m exports under `A.name` — so it enumerates the
-- dependency's schemes rather than a fixed member list.
--
-- Same golden/mangled split as above: on the emit path the reference is already
-- `<definer>__name`, so the key must stay mangled; on the golden path the reference is
-- the flat `A.name` that desugar produced, so bind it under that.
--
-- #1337/#1427/#1472: the mangle test asks the LOADED MODULE-ID SET, not just the module
-- the importer spelled.  A key reached through `export import` is mangled for its
-- DEFINER, not for the re-exporter `m` that the importer named — so a spelled-mid-only
-- prefix test answered False for it and re-bound `lib_plain__g` as `A.lib_plain__g`,
-- while types/private_mangle (which chases re-exports to the definer) had already
-- rewritten the body's reference to the bare `lib_plain__g`.  The lookup then missed:
-- for a constrained callee that reaches inferDictAt's panic and `build` fails outright
-- (#1427); for an unconstrained one the enclosing prelude call's dict route resolves to
-- nothing, the emitter writes a null dict operand, and the BINARY segfaults (#1472).
--
-- Conservatism (the property this rests on): a BARE key — one no loaded module exports
-- under that exact name with that module's own mangle prefix — is still re-bound under
-- the alias.  That population is exactly the interface METHODS (publicValNames admits
-- them; private_mangle's rename map, built from unitDefNames/pubFnNames, never renames
-- them), which is the occurrence-carrier question #1276/#1386 own — deliberately NOT
-- moved here.  The only keys whose binding changes are those a DIFFERENT loaded module
-- actually exports under its mangled name, i.e. precisely the re-exported ones, i.e.
-- precisely the defect.
--
-- 🚨 THE TEST IS AN IDENTITY TEST, NOT A STRING-SHAPE TEST (RUN-XMOD-039 F2), and it
-- must stay one.  A first version asked only "does `k` carry SOME loaded module's mangle
-- prefix?" — a pure spelling question — and that regressed a program base accepted: with
-- a module `lib.plain` loaded, an unrelated module's ordinary exported binding literally
-- named `lib_plain__g` was misread as already-mangled and rejected `Unbound variable:
-- O.lib_plain__g` at exit 1.  That surface is UNBOUNDED AND GROWS WITH THE MODULE GRAPH
-- (every module `a.b` makes `a_b__x` a landmine), and a sprint whose thesis is "identity
-- must not be derived from spelling" cannot decide identity by spelling, even in a guard.
-- ⚠️ So do NOT repair a future false positive here by TIGHTENING THE PREFIX PATTERN — a
-- narrower heuristic has a smaller unbounded surface, not a bounded one.  The conjunct
-- below is what bounds it: `k` must be a name the candidate module ACTUALLY EXPORTS, so
-- a false positive now requires two modules to genuinely export the same symbol rather
-- than one identifier to merely look like a mangled one.
aliasSchemes : List (String, List (String, a)) ->
  String ->
  List (String, a) ->
  List (String, a)
aliasSchemes deps alias depSchemes =
  map (aliasSchemeEntry deps alias) depSchemes

aliasSchemeEntry : List (String, List (String, a)) ->
  String ->
  (String, a) ->
  (String, a)
aliasSchemeEntry deps alias (k, s) =
  if isMangledExportOfAny deps k then (k, s) else (qualifiedLocal alias k, s)

-- does `k` carry the `<sanitized mid>__` prefix the mangler would have given it?
isMangledFor : String -> String -> Bool
isMangledFor mid k =
  let pre = mangledName mid ""
  let lp = stringLength pre
  lp <= stringLength k && stringSlice 0 lp k == pre

-- is `k` a symbol some loaded module ACTUALLY EXPORTS under that module's own mangled
-- name?  Both halves are load-bearing and the ORDER is deliberate: the cheap spelling
-- test gates the assoc lookup, so the scan below runs only for the rare key that already
-- looks mangled.  Short-circuiting and monomorphic on purpose (a dict-passed `any` over
-- a closure is the measured anti-pattern here).
--
-- 🚨 THE HONEST RESIDUAL, RECORDED SO THE NEXT READER DOES NOT HAVE TO RE-DERIVE IT
-- (RUN-XMOD-042).  This is "SHAPE **AND** ACTUALLY-EXPORTED", **not** pure identity, and
-- the distinction matters if you are auditing it against the sprint's own thesis that
-- identity must not be derived from spelling.  `isMangledFor` is still a string test; it
-- has simply stopped being the *whole* decision.  What the `isSome (lookupAssoc k pubV)`
-- conjunct buys is that the surface becomes BOUNDED BY THE PROGRAM'S REAL EXPORT SET: a
-- false positive now needs a GENUINE SYMBOL COLLISION -- module `m` must actually export
-- something named exactly `k`, where `k` also carries `m`'s mangle prefix -- instead of
-- merely a similar-LOOKING name.  Before the conjunct, the surface grew with the module
-- graph (every module `a.b` made `a_b__x` a landmine, which is what regressed `core__foo`
-- and `lib_plain__g`); now it does not grow with the graph at all.
--
-- ⚠️ WHY NOT DROP THE SHAPE HALF AND MAKE IT PURE IDENTITY?  Because that is measurably
-- WRONG here, not merely purer: a re-exported interface METHOD key is also a key of its
-- declaring module's `pubV`, so "is `k` a key of some other loaded module?" alone answers
-- True for methods and would re-bind them -- moving the bare-key population that
-- #1276/#1386 own and that this slice must not touch.  The shape half is precisely what
-- holds methods out (a bare method name carries no `<mid>__` prefix).  So the two halves
-- are not redundant and neither may be removed on tidiness grounds.
--
-- ⚠️ The residual's true root is one level down and is NOT fixed here: private_mangle's
-- `(module, name) -> symbol` encoding is not injective -- a module `lib.plain` and a
-- module literally named `lib_plain` both yield `lib_plain__g`.  That is the common root
-- of both regressions above and is bigger than this function; do not try to repair it by
-- editing this test.
isMangledExportOfAny : List (String, List (String, a)) -> String -> Bool
isMangledExportOfAny [] _ = False
isMangledExportOfAny ((m, pubV) :: rest) k =
  isMangledFor m k && isSome (lookupAssoc k pubV) || isMangledExportOfAny rest k

-- the (key, scheme) pairs a single `import` form brings into scope, resolving each
-- member to its (possibly mangled) key in the dependency's schemes.  `deps` is the
-- loaded dependency environment — module id PLUS that module's public schemes, because
-- the alias arm's test needs the exported NAMES, not just the ids (see aliasSchemes).
-- The non-alias arms ignore it — their resolution is definer-agnostic by construction
-- (a `__<name>` SUFFIX test, and the wildcard form performs no mangle test at all).
--
-- Passing `depEnv` WHOLE is also what supplies the spelled `depId` itself: both callers
-- reach this only through a successful `lookupAssoc depId depEnv`, so the spelled module
-- is in the list by construction and needs no separate term.
--
-- 🚨 `"core"` IS DELIBERATELY **NOT** IN `mids`, AND MUST NOT BE ADDED BACK
-- (RUN-XMOD-039).  It was, briefly.  The argument for it reads well — `reexportSeed`'s
-- own comment records core as the one source NOT in depEnv, and private_mangle *does*
-- mangle core's exports to `core__<name>` — but it was DERIVED, never witnessed: a
-- `export import core.{…}` reached through an alias is green on every verb with or
-- without the term, because core's names are seeded via `baseSeed` and resolve before
-- the alias binding is ever consulted.  Meanwhile the term has a MEASURED cost: it made
-- `mangledName "core" "" == "core__"` a live prefix, so an ordinary user binding named
-- `core__foo` reached through an alias import was misread as already-mangled and left
-- un-rebound — `Unbound variable: O.core__foo`, exit 1, on a program that compiled and
-- printed correctly before.  Zero measured benefit, measured cost.
importFormSchemes : List (String, List (String, a)) ->
  UsePath ->
  List (String, a) ->
  List (String, a)
importFormSchemes deps (UseAlias _ alias) depSchemes =
  aliasSchemes deps alias depSchemes
importFormSchemes _ path depSchemes = importFormRows path depSchemes

-- ── import aliasing: re-key the dict-arity / dict-iface tables ───────────────────
-- Both tables (funConstraintsRef, funConstraintIfacesRef) are keyed by the name a CALL
-- SITE writes.  An alias makes that name differ from the definition's, so without this
-- an aliased constrained callee gets zero dict routes and under-applies.  Generic over
-- the payload so the arity table (List Int) and the iface table (List String) share it.
--
-- [qual] is the (definerMid, name)-keyed table, which is what makes this PRECISE: an
-- entry is copied only when its DEFINER is the very module the alias names.
-- #1114 (#845): THIS module's imported bindings' SCHEME CONTEXTS, keyed by the local
-- spelling the importer writes.  Structurally the sibling of `aliasConstraintEntries`
-- below — same `DUse` walk, same "copy an entry only when its DEFINER is the very module
-- this import names" precision, and the payload is likewise taken from the
-- `(definerMid, name)`-keyed qual table.
--
-- TWO deliberate differences from `aliasConstraintEntries`, both because that function
-- serves the DICT-ARITY tables on the emit path and this one serves the CHECK-time
-- obligation channel:
--   * it has a `UseWild` arm.  `aliasConstraintEntries` needs none — on the emit path a
--     wildcard-imported name keeps its own spelling and `funConstraintsRef` is re-seeded
--     from the bare `crossModuleFunConstraintsRef` accumulator, which already covers it.
--     The check path has no such bare re-seed (that ref is the emit path's), so without
--     this arm `import m.*` would be the one spelling that still dropped the obligation.
--   * it emits the UNALIASED member of a `UseGroup` too (`useMemberLocal`, not
--     `useMemberAlias`), because plain `import m.{f}` is the common spelling and is
--     exactly what #845 pins.
--
-- ⚠️ Kept SEPARATE from `aliasConstraintEntries` rather than generalizing it. Adding a
-- `UseWild` arm there would change what `funConstraintsRef` holds on the emit path, i.e.
-- dict-passing arity — a different judgment, with a different blast radius, reached from
-- here only by the coincidence that both read the same qual-table shape.
importedSchemeOblEntries : List Decl ->
  List ((String, String), List VecObl) ->
  List (String, List VecObl)
importedSchemeOblEntries [] _ = []
importedSchemeOblEntries ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) qual =
  importedSchemeOblEntries [d] qual ++ importedSchemeOblEntries rest qual
importedSchemeOblEntries ((DUse _ path _) :: rest) qual =
  schemeOblEntriesFor (importTableMid path) path qual
    ++ importedSchemeOblEntries rest qual
importedSchemeOblEntries (_ :: rest) qual = importedSchemeOblEntries rest qual

-- ── import aliasing of an interface/impl METHOD ─────────────────────────────────
-- A method is GLOBAL-BY-NAME.  Impl coalescing, dispatch routing, the emitter's method
-- tables and the METHOD-side dict-arity tables are every one of them keyed by the
-- method's own name, and there is exactly ONE cell per name — a method is deliberately
-- NOT a per-module binding (eval.mdk's globalCells / coalesceImpls).  So an alias of a
-- method is not a new binding at all: it is a second SPELLING of the same method.
--
-- No alias spelling is resolved here, module or member.  The alias spelling is what
-- makes the occurrence decidable.  Erasing `A.area` makes it the same name as an
-- unrelated imported standalone `area`, and the standalone shadow wins (#1386 Repro B);
-- erasing a member alias `import m.{area as computeArea}` makes `computeArea` and a bare
-- `area` one name, so the import's method captures an `area` that resolve bound to
-- another declaration (#3708).  Inference gets the spelling supplied to it
-- (`aliasQualifiedMethodEntries`, `moduleMarkCtx`, `originMethodName`) and
-- `resolveAliasMethodSpellings` puts the occurrence back under its origin name once
-- inference is done, so every stage after elaboration still sees an ordinary method
-- reference and needs no alias awareness.
--
-- That is also precisely why the METHOD-side predicate carrier and its qualified
-- scoped projection need no alias re-keying the
-- way funConstraintsRef did: by the time they are built, no aliased method name survives.
-- The standalone `=>`-constrained functions are the opposite case — they ARE per-module
-- bindings that keep their local name, which is why they needed the re-keying.
--
-- What this pass does rewrite is a module alias's `DUse`: it keeps its own non-method
-- values and an `import m.{…m's methods…}` is appended beside it, so the origin name is
-- in scope for the occurrence `resolveAliasMethodSpellings` resolves it to.  A member
-- alias's `DUse` is rewritten to its origin name by that same restore, after inference.
-- Beside the rewritten modules it returns each module's admissions, which the drive's
-- mint installs (`GraphCtx.graphAdmittedMethodsRef`, read by `admittedIn`).
renameAliasedMethods : List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  (OrdMap (List (String, String)), List (String, List Decl))
renameAliasedMethods coreDecls modules =
  let coreEntry = ("core", declMethodNames coreDecls)
  let methodsPerMid = coreEntry :: methodsPerMidGo [coreEntry] modules
  let admitted =
    omFromPairs
      (map
        ((mid, prog) => (mid, synthesizedAdmissions methodsPerMid prog))
        modules)
      omEmpty
  (admitted, map (renameAliasedMethodsIn methodsPerMid) modules)

admittedIn : GraphCtx -> String -> List (String, String)
admittedIn gctx mid =
  optionOr [] (omLookup mid gctx.graphAdmittedMethodsRef.value)

-- The method names `deAliasMethodImports` admits WITHOUT a binding the resolver
-- counted: every method of an alias-imported module.  `importSeed` reads this so
-- such a row never makes a bare name look supplied twice.
synthesizedAdmissions : List (String, List String) ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, String)
synthesizedAdmissions _ [] = []
synthesizedAdmissions mm ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) =
  synthesizedAdmissions mm (d :: rest)
synthesizedAdmissions mm ((DUse _ path _) :: rest) =
  let mid = useModId path
  let here = match lookupAssoc mid mm
    None => []
    Some methods => match path
      UseAlias _ _ => map (n => (mid, n)) methods
      _ => []
  here ++ synthesizedAdmissions mm rest
synthesizedAdmissions mm (_ :: rest) = synthesizedAdmissions mm rest

-- A module's method set is what it DECLARES *plus what it RE-EXPORTS*, folded in
-- dependency-first (loader) order so a re-export resolves against its source's
-- already-computed set (and a >1-hop chain still resolves).
--
-- The `++ reexportedMethodNames` half closes a run≠build divergence that predates
-- core re-exports and is NOT core-specific: with a module's set limited to its own
-- `declMethodNames`, a module that re-exports a method did not list it, so at an
-- importer's `import reExporter.{method as alias}` neither half of the rewrite fired
-- — the alias was not dropped from the DUse (b) and references were not renamed to the
-- origin (a).  `run` still worked (eval's import frame binds the alias to the origin's
-- cell), but a method is global-by-name with no per-module symbol, so EMIT had nothing
-- to bind `alias` to and died with `unbound variable '<alias>'`.  Observed on a pure
-- user-module chain (b defines `area`; c re-exports it; main imports `area as surface`
-- → run prints 16, build fails), and on `import list.{filter as f}` once
-- `export import core.{filter}` began re-exporting at all.
methodsPerMidGo : List (String, List String) ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  List (String, List String)
methodsPerMidGo _ [] = []
methodsPerMidGo acc ((mid, decls) :: rest) =
  let entry =
    (mid, dedup (declMethodNames decls ++ reexportedMethodNames acc decls))
  entry :: methodsPerMidGo (entry :: acc) rest

-- method names a module re-exports via `export import src.{…}` (`DUse True`), taken
-- from `acc` — the dependency's already-folded method set.
reexportedMethodNames : List (String, List String) -> List Decl -> List String
reexportedMethodNames acc decls = flatMap (reexportedMethodsOf acc) decls

reexportedMethodsOf : List (String, List String) -> Decl -> List String
reexportedMethodsOf acc (DAttrib _ d) = reexportedMethodsOf acc d
reexportedMethodsOf acc (DUse True path _) =
  match lookupAssoc (useModId path) acc
    None => []
    Some srcMethods => match importedBindings path
      -- `export import src.*` re-exports every one of src's methods
      None => srcMethods
      Some bs => filterList (n => contains n srcMethods) (map fst bs)
reexportedMethodsOf _ _ = []

-- Only a MODULE alias is rewritten before inference (`deAliasMethodImports`).  A
-- member alias reaches inference as written, so `import m.{mth as loc}` binds `loc`
-- and not `mth`; `resolveAliasMethodSpellings` restores the origin name afterwards.
-- The pass is a no-op on a module whose imports name no method.
renameAliasedMethodsIn : List (String, List String) ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  (String, List Decl)
renameAliasedMethodsIn methodsPerMid (mid, prog) =
  (mid, flatMap (deAliasMethodImports methodsPerMid) prog)

-- `import m as A` is kept (its non-method values are still `A.f`) and gains a sibling
-- `import m.{…m's methods…}`, the origin name `resolveAliasMethodSpellings` resolves
-- `A.area` to once inference is done.  The rewrite is recorded in
-- `graphAdmittedMethodsRef` (`synthesizedAdmissions`), because the resolver never saw
-- it.  The added import keeps the alias import's path and location, which is how the
-- method scope ladder tells it from a written one (`writtenImportsOf`).
deAliasMethodImports : List (String, List String) -> Decl -> List Decl
deAliasMethodImports mm (DAttrib attrs d) =
  map (DAttrib attrs) (deAliasMethodImports mm d)
deAliasMethodImports mm (d@(DUse pub path loc)) =
  match lookupAssoc (useModId path) mm
    None => [d]
    Some methods => match path
      UseAlias quals _ => match methodMembersOf methods loc
        [] => [d]
        mems => [d, DUse pub (UseGroup quals mems) loc]
      _ => [d]
deAliasMethodImports _ d = [d]

methodMembersOf : List String -> Loc -> List UseMember
methodMembersOf methods loc = map (n => UseMember n False loc None) methods

-- [qualified] holds the `A.mth` spellings: nothing but the method can be spelled that
-- way, so every occurrence moves.  [members] holds the member-alias locals no own
-- top-level value takes (`memberAliasCands`), which a local binder can still spell;
-- only a MARKED occurrence is the import's, since the marker leaves a locally-bound
-- name unmarked (`rewriteArgScoped`).
renameMethodVar : List (String, String) -> List (String, String) -> Expr -> Expr
renameMethodVar qualified _ (e@(EVar x)) = match lookupAssoc x qualified
  Some origin => EVar origin
  None => e
renameMethodVar qualified _ (e@(EVarId x _)) = match lookupAssoc x qualified
  Some origin => EVar origin
  None => e
-- A marked occurrence: `resolveAliasMethodSpellings` runs after inference, on a tree
-- the schedule has already marked.  Only the NAME moves — the route cell carries the
-- dispatch decision inference reached under the alias spelling.
renameMethodVar qualified members (e@(EMethodAt x sym ev)) =
  match lookupAssoc x qualified
    Some origin => EMethodAt origin sym ev
    None => match lookupAssoc x members
      Some origin => EMethodAt origin sym ev
      None => e
renameMethodVar _ _ e = e

-- ── #1386: the alias-qualified spelling, resolved AFTER inference ───────────────
-- `A.mth`, and a member alias `loc` from `import m.{mth as loc}`, reach inference
-- spelled as written, because that spelling is what makes the occurrence decidable:
-- rewriting either to a bare `mth` up front merges it with whatever else a bare `mth`
-- names in this module (`renameAliasedMethods`' header, #1386 Repro B, #3708).  Every
-- reader inference needs is supplied under that spelling — the obligation table, the
-- mark sets, the dispatch index — so the distinction survives exactly as long as it
-- decides something.
--
-- It must not survive further.  Everything DOWNSTREAM of elaboration keys a method by
-- its origin name and only its origin name: eval's coalesced method cells and its
-- per-(method, tag) `requires` counts (`methodReqCountRef`, whose miss would turn a
-- dispatch into the inherited-default path), the Core-IR interpreter's twin, and the
-- emitter's method tables.  Resolving the spelling here leaves all of them the tree
-- they get today, so the fix is a VERDICT change and nothing else.
resolveAliasMethodSpellings : GraphCtx ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  (String, List Decl)
resolveAliasMethodSpellings gctx (mid, prog) =
  let qualified = map aliasRowSpelling (useKeyCands (moduleAliasKeys gctx) prog)
  let members = map aliasRowSpelling (memberAliasCands gctx prog)
  match (qualified, members)
    ([], []) => (mid, prog)
    _ => (
      mid,
      mapProg
        (renameMethodVar qualified members)
        (map (deAliasMethodMembers members) prog),
    )

-- `import m.{mth as loc}` → `import m.{mth}`, once every `loc` occurrence carries `mth`:
-- downstream of elaboration a method is bound by its origin name only.  Only a
-- `DUse` names import members, so every other decl passes through unchanged.
deAliasMethodMembers : List (String, String) -> Decl -> Decl
deAliasMethodMembers rows (DAttrib attrs d) =
  DAttrib attrs (deAliasMethodMembers rows d)
deAliasMethodMembers rows (DUse pub (UseGroup quals ms) loc) =
  DUse pub (UseGroup quals (map (deAliasMethodMember rows) ms)) loc
deAliasMethodMembers _ d = d

deAliasMethodMember : List (String, String) -> UseMember -> UseMember
deAliasMethodMember rows (m@(UseMember n allCtors loc (Some local)))
  | containsPair (local, n) rows = UseMember n allCtors loc None
  | otherwise = m
deAliasMethodMember _ m = m

-- every interface/impl method name a decl list declares (interface methods with or
-- without a default, plus impl method names).
declMethodNames : List Decl -> List String
declMethodNames decls = dedup (flatMap declMethodNamesOf decls)

declMethodNamesOf : Decl -> List String
declMethodNamesOf (DAttrib _ d) = declMethodNamesOf d
declMethodNamesOf (DInterface { methods, ... }) = ifaceMethodNames methods
declMethodNamesOf (DImpl { methods, ... }) = map implMethodName methods
declMethodNamesOf _ = []

-- build THIS module's import-scoped seed: walk its DUse decls, and for each one
-- pick the imported names out of the named dependency's public schemes (held in
-- depEnv, keyed by the dotted module id that useModId yields == the loader's
-- mid).  `core` DUse decls are skipped — core is always seeded via baseSeed.
-- ── #1675: reject an import that admits a name with more than one denotation ──────
-- The hub `export import lib.pa.{g}` + `export import lib.pb.{g}` exports ONE spelling
-- `g` standing for TWO definitions.  Downstream, `resolveMemberRows`' `lookupAssoc`
-- took the first of them and every verb exited 0, so which function ran was decided by
-- the ORDER OF TWO `export import` LINES — a semantically null edit moving the printed
-- value from `2` to `10`.  This is the reject.
--
-- ⚠️ THE MECHANISM IS THE EXACT-KEY ARM, NOT THE `__<name>` SUFFIX FALLBACK, and the
-- distinction decides where the check can live.  #1675's body cites the suffix `filter`
-- ("cited, not instrumented", per its own pin's claim) — but `types/private_mangle`
-- runs ONLY in the emit drivers, so on `check`/`run` the hub's rows are keyed by the
-- BARE name, `lookupAssoc origin` HITS, and the fallback is never reached.  A guard
-- written on "the filter returned more than one candidate" is green on the whole repro.
-- The ambiguity is a property of the DEPENDENCY'S EXPORT TABLE, which is where
-- `deAmbigValues` records it, on both paths at once.
--
-- Reported at the IMPORT DECL (that is where the location points, and where the fix
-- belongs), but keyed on an OCCURRENCE: a name is rejected only if this module actually
-- WRITES it, in the spelling the form binds it under — bare for `import m.*` and for a
-- selective `{g}`, alias-qualified (`A.g`) for `import m as A`.  A hub may re-export a
-- hundred names under two denotations; an importer that never mentions any of them has
-- no ambiguity to resolve and must not be rejected.  This is the USE-SITE model taken
-- literally (#1070's reject-at-declaration stays superseded; the hub itself is still
-- legal).  It also keeps the verdict from depending on which definer came first: the
-- moment the name IS written, the import is rejected rather than silently resolved.
--
-- ⚠️ CORRECTED (sprint-review F2, from #1675's own landed behavior): the first cut
-- rejected at ADMISSION — `import lib.hub.*` / `import lib.hub as H` failed even when
-- the importer never mentioned the colliding name, while the selective form correctly
-- did not.  The precedent cited for that, `T-AMBIGUOUS-ALIAS-METHOD`, is a DIFFERENT
-- namespace: methods are dispatched by argument type, where "admitted into scope" and
-- "used" are hard to pull apart because having the method callable is often the point.
-- Whether the method side wants the same narrowing is a separate question, deliberately
-- not answered here.
--
-- ⚠️ THE CHAIN IS NOT WEAKENED by narrowing to an occurrence.  `reexportDefiners` takes
-- a wildcard `export import`'s rows WHOLESALE, so a module that re-exports an ambiguous
-- hub without mentioning the name carries the ambiguity into its OWN export table, and
-- the first module downstream that does write the name is rejected there.  Nothing is
-- laundered clean by passing through a silent hop.
--
-- Called from `checkBodyImpl`, after its module mint, and not from `importSeed`.
-- `importSeed` is where the member resolution lives and was the first home for this, but
-- the seed is computed in `foldModules` BEFORE the module's worker runs, and
-- `checkBodyImpl` opens with `freshModuleCtx` — which clears `typeErrors`.  MEASURED on
-- that version: `run` exited 1 with the unlocated "detected during elaboration … see
-- issue #1812" fallback (the sticky flag survives the reset, the diagnostic does not)
-- and `check`/`check --json` were both still SILENT at exit 0 on the whole repro.  A
-- diagnostic pushed while a seed is being built cannot be reported.  Everything this
-- needs is on the module's own `DUse` decls plus the graph table, so nothing is lost by
-- moving it inside the window; `checkBodyImpl` is the ONE body all four drivers share
-- (`checkModuleFullImpl` and `elabModuleStamp` both route through it), which is what
-- keeps `check` and the run/build elaboration pass answering alike.
reportAmbiguousImports : ModuleCtx -> List Decl -> Unit
reportAmbiguousImports mctx prog0 =
  reportAmbiguousImportsIn mctx (moduleRefNameSet prog0) prog0

-- every name this module's own decl bodies REFERENCE, as a set.  Parallels `groupRefs`'
-- collector (`freeEVars`, which skips locally bound names; `allEVars` here keeps every
-- occurrence) one level up, at the decl layer: the top-level clause bodies plus
-- the impl/default/prop/test bodies, which is every place a user program can spell
-- an imported value.  Alias-qualified references arrive here already flattened into a
-- single dotted `EVar "A.g"` by desugar's `rewriteAliasQual` (via `qualifiedLocal`), so
-- the alias spelling is a plain string lookup and needs no separate walk.
--
-- `allEVars` has no `EMethodRef` arm and does not need one: no production verb ever
-- constructs that node (it does carry `EMethodAt`/`EDictAt`, the shapes the elaborate
-- driver's dict pre-pass actually mints).  Independently of shape, the rows being filtered
-- come from `ambiguousExportRows` → `modulePubDefiners` → `pubTopFnNames`, i.e.
-- `declTopFnNames` ∩ exports — so an interface method name can never be in `amb` at all.
moduleRefNameSet : List Decl -> OrdMap Unit
moduleRefNameSet decls = namesToSet (flatMap declRefNames decls) omEmpty

declRefNames : Decl -> List String
declRefNames (DAttrib _ d) = declRefNames d
declRefNames (DFunDef _ _ _ body _ _) = allEVars body
declRefNames (DProp _ _ _ body) = allEVars body
declRefNames (DTest _ _ body) = allEVars body
declRefNames (DLetGroup _ binds) = flatMap letBindEVars binds
declRefNames (DImpl { methods, ... }) = flatMap implMethodEVars methods
declRefNames (DInterface { methods, ... }) = flatMap ifaceMethodEVars methods
declRefNames _ = []

implMethodEVars : ImplMethod -> List String
implMethodEVars (ImplMethod _ _ body) = allEVars body

ifaceMethodEVars : IfaceMethod -> List String
ifaceMethodEVars (IfaceMethod _ _ d _) = match d
  Some (MethodDefault _ body) => allEVars body
  None => []

-- `core` is never in `depEnv` (it is the implicit prelude — `reexportSeed`'s comment
-- carries the full reason), so it is passed separately as `coreV`, and it contributes
-- ONE thing: the keys an ALIAS introduces.  A plain `import core.{f}` still seeds
-- nothing, because `f` is already in `baseSeed` under that very spelling and seeding it
-- twice only adds a duplicate assoc entry — but `import core as C` and
-- `import core.{f as g}` ask for `C.f` / `g`, which `baseSeed` does not hold under any
-- spelling.  `resolve.mdk`'s `coreAliasNames` binds exactly the same two forms, and the
-- two must agree: a key bound in scope with no scheme here is a `T-UNBOUND` at the use
-- site, which is what #95 measured for six years.
-- Each row a use-path BINDS carries the declaration it denotes
-- (`importSupplierKey`), the same identity the resolver's value ambiguity check
-- keys on (`importValueDecls`), so `moduleImportSeed` can refuse to pick a winner
-- by import order for a name the resolver has already rejected, and still
-- accept one declaration reached through two imports. A row the form admits
-- without binding its name (a bare method row admitted for dispatch, a mangled
-- twin) carries no supplier, and core is exempt there as it is in the resolver.
-- The key is looked up by local name, so one member list binding a local twice
-- (`import m.{a as b, b}`) gives both rows one key and the first row wins here;
-- the resolver rejects that occurrence by declaration all the same.
importSeed : GraphCtx ->
  List (String, a) ->
  List (String, String) ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List (String, a)) ->
  List (String, (Option String, a))
importSeed gctx _ _ [] _ = []
importSeed gctx coreV admitted ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) depEnv =
  importSeed gctx coreV admitted (d :: rest) depEnv
importSeed gctx coreV admitted ((DUse _ path _) :: rest) depEnv =
  let depId = useModId path
  if depId == "core" then
    map (suppliedBy None) (coreAliasSchemes path coreV)
      ++ importSeed gctx coreV admitted rest depEnv
  else match lookupAssoc depId depEnv
    None => importSeed gctx coreV admitted rest depEnv
    Some depSchemes =>
      let bound = boundNames path
      let decls =
        omFromPairs
          (reverseL (importFormRows path (graphPubDefiners gctx depId)))
          omEmpty
      let methods =
        identKeysByName
          omEmpty
          (importFormRows
            path
            (match omLookup depId (methodExportsIndex gctx ())
              Some rows => rows
              None => []))
      map
          (row =>
            suppliedBy
              (if bindsName bound (fst row)
                && not (containsPair (depId, fst row) admitted) then
                Some (importSupplierKey depId decls methods (fst row))
              else
                None)
              row)
          (importFormSchemes depEnv path depSchemes)
        ++ importSeed gctx coreV admitted rest depEnv
importSeed gctx coreV admitted (_ :: rest) depEnv =
  importSeed gctx coreV admitted rest depEnv

-- The identity one import's binding of `name` is compared by: the declaration
-- it denotes.  A standalone value is `(defining module, name there)` from
-- `graphPubDefiners`, first row winning as it does there; an interface method
-- is the set of method declarations the import carries under that name
-- (`meExports`).  A driver without an import graph knows neither, so the
-- binding falls back to the importing module's id.  The three key shapes are
-- two, a multiple of four, and one netstring long, so no two can coincide.
importSupplierKey : String ->
  OrdMap (String, String) ->
  OrdMap (List String) ->
  String ->
  String
importSupplierKey depId decls methods name = match omLookup name decls
  Some (defMid, origin) => "\{lenKey defMid}\{lenKey origin}"
  None => match omLookup name methods
    Some keys => joinWith "" (sortUniqS keys)
    None => lenKey depId

identKeysByName : OrdMap (List String) ->
  List (String, Ident) ->
  OrdMap (List String)
identKeysByName acc [] = acc
identKeysByName acc ((n, ident) :: rest) =
  let seen = match omLookup n acc
    Some keys => keys
    None => []
  identKeysByName (omInsert n (identKey ident :: seen) acc) rest

suppliedBy : Option String -> (String, a) -> (String, (Option String, a))
suppliedBy mid (name, row) = (name, (mid, row))

containsPair : (String, String) -> List (String, String) -> Bool
containsPair _ [] = False
containsPair (a, b) ((x, y) :: rest) =
  a == x && b == y || containsPair (a, b) rest

-- The names an import form binds, as the resolver counts them
-- (`importedNamesMM`): a member list binds its locals, a single dotted name its
-- last component, an alias nothing bare, and a wildcard (`None`) every name it
-- reaches.
boundNames : UsePath -> Option (OrdMap Unit)
boundNames (UseGroup _ ms) = Some (omFromNames (map useMemberLocal ms) omEmpty)
boundNames (UseName ns) =
  Some (omFromNames (if listLen ns > 1 then [lastComponent ns] else []) omEmpty)
boundNames (UseWild _) = None
boundNames (UseAlias _ _) = Some omEmpty

bindsName : Option (OrdMap Unit) -> String -> Bool
bindsName None _ = True
bindsName (Some names) name = omHasKey name names

-- the schemes a `core` use-path binds under a spelling the prelude did not supply.
coreAliasSchemes : UsePath -> List (String, a) -> List (String, a)
coreAliasSchemes (UseAlias _ a) coreV = map (coreQualScheme a) coreV
coreAliasSchemes (UseGroup _ ms) coreV = flatMap (coreRenameScheme coreV) ms
coreAliasSchemes _ _ = []

coreQualScheme : String -> (String, a) -> (String, a)
coreQualScheme a (k, s) = (qualifiedLocal a k, s)

coreRenameScheme : List (String, a) -> UseMember -> List (String, a)
coreRenameScheme coreV m = match useMemberAlias m
  None => []
  Some local => match lookupAssoc (useMemberOrigin m) coreV
    None => []
    Some s => [(local, s)]

-- WS-2/D2: THIS module's imported value name → import-source module id, from its DUse
-- decls.  Mirrors importSeed's walk but records (localName, depId) for EXPLICIT imports
-- only (importedBindings = Some bindings); a wildcard `import mod.*` (None) is skipped —
-- it can't enumerate names here, so those names fall back to the bare arity table at the
-- call site.  `core` is skipped (core fns route via the prelude dict machinery, never the
-- cross-module qual tables).  depId == useModId == the loader mid == the qual
-- tables' definer key for a DIRECT import; a re-exported fn's depId is the intermediate
-- (≠ definer), so its qual lookup misses and it too falls back to bare (correct).
--
-- Keyed by the LOCAL name, because that is the name the CALL SITE writes: under a member
-- alias (`import m.{a as b}`) the call site says `b`, so `b` is what must map to m.
--
-- A whole-module alias (`import m as A`) contributes nothing, for the same reason a
-- wildcard doesn't: its locals are one-per-export and this walk has no depEnv to
-- enumerate them.  Those call sites take the same documented bare-table fallback as
-- every wildcard import does today.  The dict ARGS themselves are unaffected — they are
-- stamped from the callee's SCHEME, which importSeed binds under the alias local — so
-- this costs only the cross-module arity DISAMBIGUATION, and only when two modules
-- export same-named constrained fns of differing dict arity.
-- ── #674 / #1111 A-2.6: import-scoped constructor overlay ──────────────────
-- The `data`/`newtype` decls (from the surrounding universe `pool`) whose
-- CONSTRUCTORS this module binds by name, read from its own DUse decls.  They
-- OVERLAY the whole-universe ctor tables (the typecheck scheme table, the
-- record-info table AND the exhaust oracle) so a bare ctor / record name resolves
-- to the SPECIFIC module this unit imports it from — instead of the universe's
-- arbitrary load-order winner, the #674 root cause where the check side
-- (last-loaded-wins) and the native mangler (first-import-wins) DISAGREED.
--
-- A `UseGroup` member contributes its owning decl when EITHER
--   (a) it carries the `(..)` flag and names the decl's TYPE (`import m.{T(..)}`) —
--       the original #674 rule; or
--   (b) it NAMES ONE OF THE DECL'S CONSTRUCTORS (`import m.{T, C}` — and, because a
--       record's sole variant carries the type's own name, `import m.{Cfg}` for a
--       `data Cfg = { … }`).  #1111 A-2.6: (b) is the half that drains #1259 (the
--       ctor-scheme env) and #1256 (the record-info table).
--
-- ⚠️ Rule (b) is a CONSTRUCTOR-name test, not a "not a type name" test, and the
-- difference is observable.  A member spelled like a TYPE contributes nothing only when
-- no decl of `mid` happens to have a constructor of that spelling; if one does, the
-- member matches by rule (b) and that SIBLING decl is overlaid.  Measured: `pmod` with
-- `data Wrap = T Int`, `import pmod.{T, pf}`, and a local `data Loc = T String` —
-- pinned as `test/llvm_fixtures_modules/ctor_scope_type_only_sibling_decl/`.
-- (An earlier revision of this note claimed such a member "contributes NOTHING"; it was
-- measured false and the paragraph is rewritten rather than re-pointed.)
--
-- That contribution is harmless BECAUSE of the layering at the registration site
-- (`dataEnv`, `Module` arm): the overlay sits BELOW this module's own `prog0`, so a
-- sibling decl riding along can never clobber a locally-declared constructor.  What it
-- can still do is out-rank a ctor the unit names from a DIFFERENT module in an EARLIER
-- import clause, decided by source order — the residual this note used to claim was
-- prevented outright.  It is the pre-existing `(..)` hazard (#674's remainder) now also
-- reachable via (b), and it is order-dependent on `main` too.
--
-- 🚨 IT IS **#1284**, and that number is the point of this paragraph.  The note used to
-- end "it is tracked, not fixed here" while NOTHING tracked it — #1283 is the RE-EXPORT
-- spelling, #733 item 1a is marked FIXED and item 1c is wildcards only.  A declared-
-- but-unfiled residual is indistinguishable from an unnoticed one.  Pinned self-
-- drainingly by `test/must_fail_fixtures/1284-a26-overlay-sibling-ctor-beats-named-
-- import/`, whose CONTROL is the discriminator that dates it: the NON-sibling case is
-- rejected on `main` and accepted here, so A-2.6 repairs that one and leaves exactly
-- the sibling one.
--
-- 🚨 The pool lookup is IDENTITY-scoped, not bare-name.  The pool is the WHOLE
-- universe, so two modules declaring the same TYPE name (#1256's two `Cfg`s) made the
-- old bare-name first-match a LOAD-ORDER coin flip inside the very overlay that exists
-- to defeat load order.  The pool is appended in LOAD order and searched FIRST-match
-- while the tables it overlays are `omInsert` LAST-write-wins, so the two orders are
-- OPPOSITE: an unscoped lookup picks right only when the wanted module is loaded
-- FIRST, and `test/eval_typed_modules_fixtures/ctor_scope_load_order/` is the measured
-- counterexample (stubbing `declOwnedBy` to `True` regresses it to `7.0`, an answer
-- pristine `main` gets right).  `declOwnedBy` compares the decl's own identity against
-- `OriginModule <this import's module id>`; `useModId` yields exactly the loader
-- mid that `stampDeclOrigins` stamped with (see `aliasDictNamesOfPath`'s note, which
-- states the same equality for the qual tables).
--
-- ⚠️ PERF (issue #154) — THE REAL BOUND, stated for the WORK and not just the RESULT.
-- The RESULT is bounded by IMPORT COUNT x PER-MODULE PUBLIC DECL COUNT: at most one
-- overlay decl per UseGroup member, and — since `wildOverlayDecls` — the wildcard-named
-- module's whole published row per `UseWild`.  It is still a per-module VIEW (the row is
-- the envelope's own memoized `demPubDecls`, not a copy), never a per-module rebuild of
-- the global universe.  A module importing no constructors AND no wildcard overlays
-- NOTHING and stays byte-identical.  A bare `import mod` (UseName) still contributes no
-- overlay: the bare form binds no ctors at all, so no ctor occurrence in the reader can
-- mean that module's declaration by that import.  A wildcard `import mod.*` DOES
-- contribute, as of `wildOverlayDecls` below — it cannot name its owning type, but it
-- does not need to: every decl the module publishes is in scope by construction, and
-- leaving it to the universe-fallback made import-clause ORDER decide which declaration
-- a ctor occurrence meant, in both the spurious-warning and the lost-warning direction.
--
-- The WORK is NOT import-count bounded, and saying it is has already shipped a
-- regression.  `pool` is the WHOLE accumulated universe and it is SCANNED — so the cost
-- is O(members x |pool|) per module, i.e. O(modules x universe) across a run, the same
-- shape `main` has paid since #674 for its `(..)` members.  What keeps that acceptable
-- is entirely the CONSTANT, and the constant has exactly two load-bearing parts, both
-- enforced downstream and both measured:
--   * ONE traversal per member, not three (see `findOverlayDecl`/`overlayScan`); and
--   * ZERO allocation per visited decl (see `overlayNote` — name tests before the
--     identity mint).
-- Break either and the perf gate's `modules` shape goes superlinear: this comment
-- previously asserted the universe-independence outright, the first cut of A-2.6 broke
-- both parts, and the gate read typecheck TIME r2=3.24 (hard threshold 3.0) with net
-- allocation 306/744/2013 MB against `main`'s 242/491/1010.  A cheaper bound is
-- available if it is ever needed — index `pool` by owning module id, which would make
-- the owned passes O(log n) — but it does not exist today, so do not cite one.
--
-- 🚨 A-3.2b (#1512, absorbing #1319 unit 4): THE POOL IS NO LONGER A MATERIALISED
-- ACCUMULATOR.  It used to be `CrossRun.universeDataDecls` — a bare `List Decl`
-- grown by `appendDataUniverse` one module at a time, with NO record of which module
-- contributed what and no key at all beyond list position.  It is now the whole-graph
-- envelope (`DeclEnvs.deModules`, stage K) read at the READER'S OWN ORDINAL through
-- `declEnvRowVisible`, i.e. through `declEnvVisibleTo`'s two conjuncts.  `cur` is
-- `declEnvsOrdOf mid` for the module being checked — a LOADER-derived identity, not a
-- spelling re-derived from import syntax, which is what makes it survive the emit path
-- (see the call site in `checkBodyImpl`).
--
-- ⚠️ THE POPULATION IS NOT BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE OLD ACCUMULATOR, and the difference
-- is exactly one row: the READER'S OWN module.  The accumulator held only STRICTLY
-- EARLIER modules' public decls (`appendDataUniverse` runs at the END of a module's
-- own pass); `declEnvVisibleTo` admits the reader's own row too, privately, because
-- `entryOrd == cur` short-circuits the publicity conjunct.  That is the ruled
-- predicate and it is deliberately not special-cased away here.  Its reach is
-- bounded: `ownedType`/`ownedCtor` are scoped by `declOwnedBy mid` where `mid` comes
-- from a `DUse` path, and no module imports itself, so an own-module decl can only
-- ever fill the `bareType` fallback — LAST in a FIRST-wins walk, so it can only add a
-- candidate where every earlier row supplied none, never displace one.
-- 🚨 THE RESULT IS PARTITIONED: NAMED (`UseGroup`) ROWS AND WILDCARD (`UseWild`) ROWS
-- ARE TWO SEPARATE HALVES, and which half a consumer must see FIRST depends on that
-- consumer's own tie-break direction.  This is not a style choice; a single flat
-- source-ordered list shipped an S1.
--
-- WHY.  Before `wildOverlayDecls`, only `UseGroup` contributed, and every row was ONE
-- precisely-named decl.  A wildcard row is the module's WHOLE published set, so once
-- `UseWild` was enrolled the flat `flatMap` over the unit's decls in SOURCE ORDER made
-- import-clause order decide same-named-type collisions BETWEEN the two spellings: with
-- `import zzcol.*` written above `import aacol.{Red, Blue}`, a non-exhaustive match over
-- `aacol.Col` was reported as `Missing case: 'Green'` — a constructor of `zzcol.Col`,
-- the wrong type entirely — and the real missing case went unreported, so the program
-- then died at runtime on the case nobody warned about.  Swapping the two clauses fixed
-- it.  Measured on af6e0414 (broken) vs c7c879b7 (correct in BOTH orders).
--
-- THE RULE, and it is the ordinary scoping one: AN EXPLICITLY NAMED MEMBER OUTRANKS A
-- WILDCARD.  "You named this type" beats "you imported everything and it happened to be
-- in there", whichever clause is written first.
--
-- 🚨 THE TWO CONSUMERS TIE-BREAK IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, so they take opposite orders.
-- Enumerated, because a future edit that routes one of them through the other's wrapper
-- silently inverts the rule for that consumer with no diagnostic anywhere:
--   * `registerAllData` (the `dataEnv` overlay) folds the list LEFT and its bare-keyed
--     tables are `omInsert`, i.e. LAST-WRITE-WINS  -> named rows must come LAST
--     -> `importedCtorTypeDeclsLastWins`.
--   * `seedCheckRun` (the exhaustiveness ctor ORACLE) builds `oracleMap` =
--     `omFromPairs (reverseL …)`, i.e. FIRST-WINS   -> named rows must come FIRST
--     -> `importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins`.
-- Same rule, both sites; only the list order differs.  The big note at the `dataEnv`
-- call site enumerates the full set of order-observable structures — this pair is the
-- overlay's own contribution to it.
--
-- ⚠️ WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES **NOT** DECIDE: named-vs-named.  Two `UseGroup` clauses
-- each naming a same-spelled type from a different module are still resolved by
-- import-clause order, exactly as before this partition — within each half the walk is
-- the same `flatMap` over `unitDecls` in source order, and neither consumer's tie-break
-- direction moved.  That case is a SEPARATE, PRE-EXISTING defect (it reproduces on
-- c7c879b7, before the wildcard arm existed) and fixing it needs the overlay keyed by
-- RESOLVED DECLARATION IDENTITY rather than by bare type name — #1319/#1185 territory,
-- not an ordering change.  Do not "while you are here" it: an ordering answer for
-- named-vs-named would freeze a guess into the oracle.
--
-- ⚠️ PERF: the unit's decl list is walked TWICE (once per half) instead of once, but the
-- POOL — the expensive part, see `THE REAL BOUND` above — is scanned exactly as many
-- times as before: each clause yields its rows in whichever half claims it and `[]` in
-- the other, so the total member/wildcard lookups are unchanged.  The extra cost is one
-- linear pass over `unitDecls`, which is import-clause bounded, not universe bounded.
importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins : List Decl ->
  Int ->
  List DeclEnvModule ->
  List Decl
importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins unitDecls cur rows =
  overlayHalf False unitDecls cur rows ++ overlayHalf True unitDecls cur rows

importedCtorTypeDeclsLastWins : List Decl ->
  Int ->
  List DeclEnvModule ->
  List Decl
importedCtorTypeDeclsLastWins unitDecls cur rows =
  overlayHalf True unitDecls cur rows ++ overlayHalf False unitDecls cur rows

-- One half of the partition, in the unit's own source order.  `wildHalf` selects which:
-- True = `UseWild` rows only, False = `UseGroup` rows only.
overlayHalf : Bool -> List Decl -> Int -> List DeclEnvModule -> List Decl
overlayHalf wildHalf unitDecls cur rows =
  flatMap (importOverlayDecls wildHalf cur rows) unitDecls

importOverlayDecls : Bool -> Int -> List DeclEnvModule -> Decl -> List Decl
importOverlayDecls wildHalf cur rows (DAttrib _ d) =
  importOverlayDecls wildHalf cur rows d
importOverlayDecls wildHalf cur rows (DUse _ (p@(UseGroup _ ms)) _) =
  if wildHalf then [] else flatMap (memberOverlayDecl cur rows (useModId p)) ms
importOverlayDecls wildHalf cur rows (DUse _ (p@(UseWild _)) _) =
  if wildHalf then wildOverlayDecls cur rows (useModId p) else []
importOverlayDecls _ _ _ _ = []

-- The exhaustiveness oracle's import rows beyond `importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins`:
-- every decl a module ALIAS import's module publishes, and the declarations of the
-- constructors a wildcard or alias import reaches through that module's own
-- `export import`.  The oracle reads constructors by bare name (resolve strips `A.`
-- before inference), so without these rows a same-spelled constructor of a module
-- loaded earlier answers for them (#1185).  They follow both halves of
-- `importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins` because a bare occurrence means an unaliased
-- import's constructor.  Kept out of `importOverlayDecls`, whose other reader is the
-- `dataEnv` overlay.  A selective `import m.{…}` is already one of those rows, and no
-- decl other than a `DUse` imports anything, so `oracleImportDeclsOf` adds nothing for
-- either.
oracleImportDecls : GraphCtx ->
  List Decl ->
  Int ->
  List DeclEnvModule ->
  List Decl
oracleImportDecls gctx unitDecls cur rows =
  flatMap (oracleImportDeclsOf gctx cur rows) unitDecls

oracleImportDeclsOf : GraphCtx -> Int -> List DeclEnvModule -> Decl -> List Decl
oracleImportDeclsOf gctx cur rows (DAttrib _ d) =
  oracleImportDeclsOf gctx cur rows d
oracleImportDeclsOf gctx cur rows (DUse _ (p@(UseAlias _ _)) _) =
  let dep = useModId p
  wildOverlayDecls cur rows dep ++ reexportedCtorDecls gctx cur rows dep
oracleImportDeclsOf gctx cur rows (DUse _ (p@(UseWild _)) _) =
  reexportedCtorDecls gctx cur rows (useModId p)
oracleImportDeclsOf gctx _ _ _ = []

-- The decls declaring the constructors `dep` re-exports from other modules, found
-- through the graph's constructor export index, whose rows carry each constructor's
